title: Validate specs and pass one dry run through the lease runner
description:
## Background

Workstream acceptance from the plan's receipts section.

## Why

Proves specs are executable, not only well-formed.

## Scope

- Validate every spec; run one dry run (no measurement claim) through `run.py` on a worker.

## Out of scope

Measurements.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Validation output and dry-run journal entry recorded.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Load converter output in the manager and engine and check it against the reference
description:
## Background
Conversion tooling builds and verifies on its own (pinned container, FFHQ); its manager/engine load check joins integrated verification.

## Why
Converted chunks/manifests/descriptors must actually load and synthesize through the packages, not only pass converter self-checks.

## Scope
- Run the pinned container's acquire/convert/verify on the FFHQ checkpoint; host the output statically.
- Load through `browser-model-manager` into `stylegan-js`; compare raw synthesis with the converter's reference/parity report within the frozen tolerances.
- Manifest compatibility with the contracts.

## Out of scope
Non-face model (separate leaf).

## Considerations
- Container image digest recorded in the receipt.
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Raw synthesis from converted FFHQ within max RGB diff 1 / raw float 0.002 of the reference.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome) through the shared emitter from `build.event-log-core` (fm-bd03) and passes `scripts/check-event-log.ts`; the log is kept as a CI artifact, privacy-filtered like diagnostics; screenshots kept on failure.
- [ ] Each case is listed in this leaf's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix row IDs or defect numbers it grades.
- [ ] Ran against the named release-candidate artifact digest (the same digest the join report checks); a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded failed or untested, never passed.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes: Anchors: #conversion-tooling, #workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership (conversion row).

title: Paired not-worse workload on every device lane, with control/control noise
description:
## Goal
Build what the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27) runs on: one scripted visitor workload with fixed finish boundaries that runs the same way against the pinned candidate artifact (the control) and any build under test, in paired alternating order, on every platform-class lane the gate needs, iPhone included, and measure each lane's control/control noise. It runs and is accepted on the control alone (control against control), so the lanes and the noise margins exist before the monorepo release artifact does and the gate itself is a run, not a build project (PLAN.md "Strictly not worse than the candidate", operator 24 October 2026; its Owners line: workspace build carries the paired lanes, autoresearch re-homing supplies the paired ABBA harness and the device lease).

## Scope
- **Workload** `scripts/verify/not-worse/workload.ts` (strict TS). Fixed inputs: words and seeds from a committed list, a committed metadata-free one-face photo (the same file the integrated-verification harness uses), a two-face morph at the candidate's default length and resolution. Measures, each at a finish boundary both builds share:
  - time to a usable page (the first face field accepts text);
  - cold first face (fresh profile, empty storage, including model download, until the face's decoded pixels render), warm face (same profile, second visit) and the next face;
  - confirmed-photo encode where photo encoding is admitted on that lane (crop confirmation to the recovered face rendered);
  - complete morph: time to playable video (`canplaythrough`) and time per frame;
  - first and repeated Save (click to file ready);
  - no lockups while working (a real input gets a visible response within 1 s and the page never stops painting for more than 1 s; frame stutter itself is not measured);
  - bytes downloaded on the first and on a return visit (Resource Timing `transferSize`, CDP where available);
  - peak memory where the platform reports it (`performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory` or CDP); otherwise `unreported`, never estimated.
  Time the script spends waiting the way a person would (between a control appearing and the scripted click) is excluded from every measure, so a declared new step such as crop confirmation compares the same work.
- **Boundaries per build.** Where a declared UI change moved a control, a per-build selector map names the same semantic boundary for control and new build; a unit test fails if either map lacks a boundary.
- **Reliability capture** per run: whether the face, the photo face and the video were produced; page crash; tab reload (navigation count); out-of-memory (crash reason where the browser reports it); fallback (actual route differs from the requested one, read from the app's visible route explanation); uncaught page error.
- **Runner.** ABBA order with a discarded warmup, each run in a fresh browser context, reusing the shared device lease (`research.s1`, fm-zxj) and the paired runner of `migration.parity-harness` (fm-q007); no third implementation. At least 5 pairs per cell; the runner says when a cell's control/control spread needs more pairs and runs them.
- **Lanes** (each a workflow job; shared devices only under the device lease):
  - iOS Simulator: the existing `mobile-browser.yml` `ios` lane (`build.ci-mobile`, fm-hlv) gains a paired job.
  - Physical iPhone: a scheduled job on the self-hosted Mac the phone is connected to, driving Safari through `safaridriver` (WebDriver; Remote Automation enabled on the phone and `safaridriver --enable` run once on the Mac, both written in the lane's README). The device is setup, not an approval step: with no iPhone connected the job records the cell `untested` with that reason and exits.
  - Android: the emulator lane (`mobile-browser.yml` `android`) gains a paired job; the physical Huawei P30 Pro through `tools/device-lab/lab.py` (its `phone-webgpu` and `phone-cpu` cells, extended for ABBA pairs) under the lab lock; no second adb/Chrome loop.
  - Desktop: WebGPU on eris (RTX 2080 SUPER) and on the Mac (self-hosted, under the lease); CPU on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu.
- **Noise.** Control/control pairs per cell and measure give the noise margin the gate uses; re-measured whenever the cell's device, OS or browser version changes (recorded in the run).
- **Output.** One JSON file per run: cell (device, OS, browser and version, provider, cache state), build digest of each side, pair index and order, raw values per measure, reliability events. Logs name the cell, digest, pair index and order of every run; captures are privacy-filtered CI artifacts, traces and screenshots kept on failure.

## Out of scope
The comparison math, the verdict and the run against the release artifact (`verify.not-worse`). The real-visitor check (`verify.field-not-worse`). New optimization work.

## Notes
- Mobile safety: the workload uses only the routes the app itself admits on that device; it never forces WebGPU on a phone the app did not admit.
- Runs on development workers under the lease to save GitHub minutes. Adds scripts and workflow jobs only; edits no app source and none of the shared bridge/runtime/worker files.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#strictly-not-worse-than-the-candidate-operator-24-october-2026, #retained-performance-evidence-and-no-regression-checks, #development-workers-and-github-minute-use, #platform-ci-retention-and-performance-preservation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests: boundary detection for each measure on recorded fixture traces, with scripted waits excluded; both selector maps define every boundary; reliability classification of a crash, a reload, a fallback and an uncaught error from fixture events; ABBA order generation and warmup discard; run JSON validates against its schema.
- [ ] Control/control run (the control artifact on both sides, at least 5 ABBA pairs) completed on the iOS Simulator, the Android emulator, eris WebGPU, Mac WebGPU and Ubuntu CPU, with a noise margin per cell and measure in the run output; an unavailable hosted runner/simulator is recorded `untested` with its reason after a bounded attempt and does not permanently block. Physical iPhone measurement is optional, accurately labelled evidence; actual P30 Pro/eris release evidence remains required.
- [ ] A planted slowdown (a delay injected into one side's served artifact) shows in the raw paired values on at least one desktop and one phone cell; a planted crash shows as a reliability event.
- [ ] Every run's log names cell, build digest, pair index and order; failing runs keep traces and screenshots as CI artifacts.
- [ ] all platform-class lanes at close need fm-hlv (with fm-hlv). If fm-hlv has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-hlv (`br update fm-hlv --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-hlv
- [ ] GPU lane at close needs fm-wzy (with fm-wzy). If fm-wzy has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-wzy (`br update fm-wzy --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-wzy
notes:
24 Oct 2026: the physical Android cell exists and runs human-free: tools/device-lab/android (Huawei P30 Pro VOG-L29, Android 10, Chrome 150, on eris over USB). lab.py pauses and restores the p30pro Frigate camera (16-17 s, accessibility recovery service restored), drives real Chrome over CDP with OS taps verified by elementFromPoint and by the landed pointerdown target, keeps GA and changeover stats clean (GPC), recovers killed sessions, and holds a device lock. First candidate measurements: page usable 3.8 s; cold first face 72 s (CPU, incl. model download); warm face 17 s; peak Chrome PSS 4.35 GB; typedExactly=false (defect 5 reproduced on a real keyboard).
Operator, 25 October 2026 (fm-ajcf): reuse existing classic-style iOS Simulator inside the GitHub macOS runner and Android emulator CI alongside ordinary tests. Hosted runner/simulator unavailability is best effort: bounded attempt, explicit untested reason, no passing or physical-iPhone claim and no permanent release block. Actual available-lane failures require repair. Physical phone never runs in CI. Candidate handover needs no further approval and is incomplete until actual P30 Pro and eris CPU/WebGPU checks plus post-delivery-check pass against the deployed artifact. This supersedes older all-platform-availability and physical-iPhone release prerequisites; other product/performance requirements remain.

title: npm scope and publishing credentials
description:
## Goal
Three TypeScript packages publish to npm (the engine `stylegan-js`, `browser-model-manager`, `cloudflare-model-host`).
Publishing needs npm credentials for the chosen scope. This is an operator-supplied execution prerequisite for
`pkgdocs.release` (fm-oagi) and `delivery.packages` (fm-96v), not a decision gate.

## Scope
- The operator provides an npm account/scope they control and a publishing token.
- Store the token only as a CI secret of the publishing repository (organization `facemorph-me` after the rename);
  never in Git, logs or the tracker. Prefer a granular token limited to publishing the chosen packages in the chosen
  scope; note its type, scope and expiry date (never its value) so renewal is visible before it lapses.
- Each real package name and scope is chosen at publication by the registry availability check owned by
  `pkgdocs.engine` (fm-tohj; working names first, the operator-controlled scope as fallback). If that check moves the
  packages to the fallback scope, the token must cover that scope.

## Out of scope
Choosing package names (`pkgdocs.engine` name check). Publishing (`delivery.packages`).

## Notes
- Use the selected organization login `facemorph-me`; remotes say `check-face` until the rename.
- Assigned to `operator`, label `gate`; agents never claim or close it. Agents may write the verification CI job.
- The former receipt file is dropped (24 October cut); the CI job run is the evidence.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #independent-published-package-acceptance (what publishes),
  #workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership (package publication row).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Scope ownership verified (for example `npm access`/`npm org` listing shows the operator-controlled scope), noted without secret values.
- [ ] CI secret present in the publishing repository; a CI job using it runs `npm whoami` (prints the publishing account) and `npm access list packages <scope>` or `npm org ls <scope>` successfully, and `npm publish --dry-run` of one package succeeds; the job log shows no token value.
- [ ] Token type, scope and expiry date are noted in the close reason (no value).

title: Accept GPU startup and original behavior on a real NVIDIA worker
description:
## Background
Classic self-host today: `self-host/compose.yml`, `compose.gpu.yml`, `setup.py`, `Dockerfile`, `legacy-route-inventory.json`, `verify.sh`, pinned frontend `0abb215` in `self-host/frontend-overlay/source.json`, `torch 2.9.1+cu128`, NVlabs StyleGAN2-ADA commit `d72cc7d`. Current self-host work is on `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`; the remote default `master` publishes legacy production through Vercel. Planned CUDA cell: RTX 2080 SUPER (Turing) on the workstation (Docker 29.7.2, Compose 5.5.1, driver 610.57.04), under the shared device lease; nothing has run on it. TrueNAS GTX 1050 is Pascal, not expected to be supported by cu128 wheels (confirm) → CPU path only. GitHub-hosted runners have no GPU. `self-host/validation/2026-10-10/gpu.json` is historical (one GPU, synthetic inputs, source-only).

## Why
The CUDA claim rests on a real GPU run from empty volumes.

## Scope
- From empty images/volumes/build cache: build, download/verify, healthy; `/healthz` reports `"provider":"cuda"` and GPU name; `/api/face/?seed=0&dim=512` returns an image; frontend renders a face (`smoke_*` scripts); photo, morph and media endpoints; old seed/text semantics.
- `down`/`up` reuses volumes, healthy within a documented time.
- Measure first-run duration and disk use.
- CPU override run; host without NVIDIA runtime run (or container toolkit absent) fails clearly.
- Pascal cell attempt recorded.

## Out of scope
Pixel parity with historic production.

## Considerations
Acquire the device lease; record untested matrix cells.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each assertion above recorded with commit, driver, GPU, Docker/Compose versions.
- [ ] Untested cells listed.
- [ ] The run writes a structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, commit and image digests, host OS/Docker/Compose/driver/GPU, provider cuda|cpu, network requests by host class and bytes for weight downloads, container exit codes, outcome per assertion), retained as a CI artifact or committed evidence file, with every network/download claim asserted from the log.
- [ ] Receipt `docs/receipts/classic-gpu-acceptance.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime/model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] The classic harness writes its event log in the `e2e-event-log.v1` format from fm-ucl: a copy of the stdlib `scripts/evidence/event_log.py` is vendored into the distribution branch's validation tooling with its sha256 and source monorepo commit recorded (classic is frozen, so it never imports from the monorepo at run time), and each log passes the monorepo's `node scripts/check-event-log.ts <log>` before the receipt is written (polish r2).
notes: Plan anchors (PLAN.md): #classic-distribution, #frozen-classic-distribution, #classic-distribution-acceptance; receipts rule: #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance.

title: Operation-service interface with intents and stale-result rejection
description:
## Goal
Define the narrow, typed operation-service interface that the controller port's reducers call, with a bridge-backed implementation reproducing candidate semantics exactly so the port proceeds in parallel and the scheduler can later replace the bridge-backed behaviour without UI edits; and capture per-intent snapshots and input revisions so late results never replace newer input and approved scope never silently changes (candidate defect 17). The application operation controller bounds aggregate GPU/WASM/model memory, makes Morph a dependency-aware parent intent, rejects stale results and gives one honest whole-action progress bar, without moving scheduling into React; a single Busy/LastRun/Retry cannot represent independent slots, imports and downloads.

## Scope
- Typed interface (`apps/web/src/operations/service.ts`): request face (text/seed/name/photo/restored), request morph (ordered input revisions + settings), request import, cancel(slot|intent), retry(slot) with new attempt ID, subscribe to typed operation events (queued, admitted, progress, compute-ready, file-ready, failed with cause, cancelled, settled). Types from contracts milestone 1 (operation signatures); progress/tile types from milestone 2 are added in `opctl.progress`.
- Opaque request/input-revision/attempt IDs; actual provider in events; signals/callbacks stay caller-side; worker payloads cloneable.
- Bridge-backed implementation (`bridge-service.ts`) reproducing candidate semantics exactly (serial heavy execution, request order, morph blocked by photo decisions) so parity holds. It wraps (read-only classic sources) `src/Next/scheduler.mjs` `nextScheduled(jobs, {busy, blockedFaces, blockMorph})` (first eligible request, order preserved, morph waits for photo decisions) with `scheduler.test.mjs`; `product-bridge.mjs` `execute`, `cancel`, `queueFace`, `cancelQueuedFace`, `invalidateFace`, `invalidateMorph`, `subscribe`, `cancelPhotoRun`; it receives the descriptors and blocked-face list built by the ported `schedule` helper (`Product.fs` 388-399 at `b2d945a8`, ported in `migration.controller`).
- Intent snapshots (operator ruling 12 October): requested CPU/WebGPU route, permitted bounded failure-fallback scope, runtime/model identity, input revisions and request ID are captured at Start/download approval and stay with queued work; later selector changes apply to new jobs; new attempt ID per Retry; actual execution provider recorded.
- Typing/changing a source creates a new revision and invalidates old prepared file/morph immediately. Replacement commit points per the plan: keep the previous target through cancelled selection/rejected recovery where straightforward; never save the old face under a new name; never install a late result into a newer target.
- Defect 17 cases (candidate audit): removing a generating face does not stop its job; a saved-MP4 drop can leave Morph queued for good and replaces every face without asking; replacing a photo destroys the face before the new photo is checked; cancelling a queued re-generate can leave a broken image. Each becomes a stale-completion test with the fixed behaviour: remove while generating stops and releases the job; MP4 drop never leaves Morph queued forever and replaces faces only at the defined commit point; photo replacement checks the new photo before destroying the face; cancelling a queued re-generate leaves the previous verified image or an empty retryable target.

## Out of scope
- New scheduling semantics (`opctl.scheduler`); UI rendering of these states (face controls).
- Undo/history or transactional whole-project import (local staging/revision checks are enough).

## Notes
- Written in the same period as the controller port; the two never claim the same code. Consumers: face controls, morph pipeline, acquisition consent.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-migration (Controller port versus the operation layer); #application-operation-controller; #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts; #gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design; #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026 (defect 17); #operator-dispositions--12-october-2026.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Interface published as strict TS with type-level tests.
- [x] `bridge-service.test.ts` re-runs every `scheduler.test.mjs` case through the interface and passes.
- [x] Facade-harness run: a face and a morph complete through the bridge-backed service on CPU.
- [x] Named tests in `apps/web/src/operations/intents.test.ts`: `selector change after queueing keeps the queued snapshot`, `late completion for an old revision is discarded`, `remove while generating stops and releases the job`, `MP4 drop never leaves Morph queued forever`, `MP4 drop does not replace faces before its commit point`, `photo replacement checks the new photo before destroying the face`, `cancelling a queued re-generate leaves the previous verified image or an empty retryable target`, `Retry creates a new attempt ID`.
- [x] Unit tests listed in test discovery and pass locally with the CI command; CI verifies after push.
notes:
Correction (GLM review): the bridge-backed service takes job descriptors and the blocked-face list as caller-supplied arguments, built in its tests from `scheduler.test.mjs` cases; wiring the ported `schedule` helper and its test belongs to `migration.controller` (fm-v80g).
Implemented strict immutable operation snapshots, opaque IDs and type-level rejection checks; serial bridge service uses the retained nextScheduled seam, scoped provider/progress events, bounded file preparation and actual cancellation; local replacement commit tokens reject revision/new-slot races, retain prior verified identities, cancel dependent morph/import work and release terminal snapshots. Unit/discovery evidence: npm test -w apps/web 252/252 zero skips (15 operation cases), strict workspace typecheck and Vite build pass; /tmp/fm-next-operations-{web-tests-final,type-final,unit-final,discovery-final,build}.log. Real CPU service journey has passed twice with queued faces/morph, stale runtime identity refusal and cancellation/next-face success (/tmp/fm-next-operations-{cpu,cpu-final}.log); final full facade regression is running with removal delayed until actual route admission. Real GPU checks 3/3: both 7-canary paths within frozen tolerances; no-fallback scope refuses a planted real GPU canary failure with zero CPU synthesis requests (/tmp/fm-next-operations-gpu.log). Existing Auto fallback-to-CPU-once regression 1/1 (/tmp/fm-next-operations-fallback.log). No deployment or six-cell release claim.
Final local acceptance: real source-built CPU service 1/1 passes after fixing warm-runtime provider reporting (/tmp/fm-next-operations-cpu-warm-admission.log): queued faces/morph complete; changed runtime identity refused; remove after actual admission cancels and the next face completes without a late removed result. Earlier full facade regression passed its 9 direct-facade cases but caught the missing warm admission event in service (9 pass / 1 fail); repaired runtime now announces the existing qualified provider on warm real computation. title: Classic branch, pinned images and Python, vendored frontend
description:
## Goal
In `facemorph.me-classic`, put the frozen self-host distribution on its own branch (D4) with the pre-checks that make a later default-branch switch safe, and make its inputs reproducible: base images pinned by digest, Python dependencies hash-locked, the NVlabs fetch pinned by SHA, and the frontend shipped as a hash-pinned prebuilt bundle with vendored source, so the default build needs no .NET, Fable, npm or GitHub clone and floating inputs cannot rot silently. "Frozen" means these exact inputs build; no feature changes and no dependency bumps after qualification.

## Scope
- Starting point: `self-host/compose.yml`, `compose.gpu.yml`, `setup.py`, `Dockerfile`, `legacy-route-inventory.json`, `verify.sh`; frontend pin `0abb215` in `self-host/frontend-overlay/source.json`; `torch 2.9.1+cu128`; NVlabs StyleGAN2-ADA commit `d72cc7d`. Current self-host work is on `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`; the remote default `master` publishes legacy production through Vercel (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` runs `vercel --prod` on every push).
- **D4 branch.** Create branch `self-host` (implementation detail; no user-facing text names it) from the self-host work. Never merge into `master`.
- **Pre-checks for the later switch**: list workflows with `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch` on `master` and on the candidate branch (GitHub runs those only from the default branch's files) and confirm the rot check and GPU lanes exist on the new branch; check whether the Vercel project's Git settings follow the default branch; test, on a scratch repository with the same workflow shape (or by Vercel docs plus project settings), whether a default-branch switch fires a deploy. Outcome: the switch is safe, or the Vercel publisher must be retired first (the classic delivery reads this).
- **Pins (rot hazard 2).** Pin every base image by digest (`node:22-bookworm-slim` and `python:3.11-slim-bookworm` float today; `mongo:8.0.13` is by tag; only the .NET 5.0.408 SDK image is digest-pinned), resolved on the pin date. Hash-lock Python deps (`--require-hashes`) including the torch cu128 wheel index pins. Pin the NVlabs commit fetch by SHA. No version upgrades.
- **Frontend (rot hazard 1).** Remove the build-time `git clone` of this repository at an older commit (it breaks on rename/removal and builds a tree different from the cloned one). Default build uses a prebuilt `deploy-self-host/` bundle as a hash-pinned download (release asset or committed, chosen by measured size; the measurement is stated in the PR). Vendor the frontend source at `0abb215` with its npm lock, Fable tool pin and overlay; keep the .NET 5 stage as the documented opt-in from-source route (an EOL .NET 5/Fable stage inside the image is acceptable because it is digest-pinned; a .NET 8 attempt could not load the old Fable project).

## Out of scope
The default-branch switch (classic delivery); upgrading any version; changing frontend behaviour; API reconciliation and one-command start (next bead).

## Notes
- Development runs before the switch name the branch explicitly and are labelled development runs.
- The classic distribution is exempt from the dependency currency lane. Decisions D4–D7 settled 16 October; D4 branch plan simplified 17 October.
- 24 October rules: no receipt files; the pre-check outcome is stated in the merged PR.
- Plan: #classic-distribution, #frozen-classic-distribution, #classic-distribution-acceptance, #dependency-currency-and-the-frozen-self-host-guarantee--16-october-2026.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Branch `self-host` exists; nothing merged into `master`; pre-check results (workflow trigger list per branch, Vercel Git setting, scratch-repo switch test) are in the PR with commands and the switch-safe / retire-Vercel-first outcome.
- [x] Pin scan (`scripts/check-pins` over Dockerfiles and compose files) finds no floating tag; unit tests: a fixture with `FROM node:22-bookworm-slim` fails, one with `@sha256:` passes.
- [x] `pip install --require-hashes` succeeds in a clean build; the NVlabs fetch is by SHA.
- [x] Offline rebuild from the pins (after pulling the pinned digests and the pinned bundle) succeeds without network clone, npm or .NET.
- [x] Default build uses the hash-verified bundle with no network clone; a tampered bundle is rejected by hash; the opt-in source build produces a bundle whose file list matches (differences listed).
- [x] The frontend is vendored in the distribution (no clone of a repository at build time) and the node and python base images are pinned by digest.

Steps 2 and 3 of the external developer journey (convert, then host on infrastructure the developer controls) and the manager-loaded inference step must be followable from public docs with real copyable commands and no FaceMorph hostname, catalogue, alias or secret. This row writes the manager README and examples, the host package README with generic and Cloudflare static-hosting guides, and the converter's container docs for the tagged public release, each proven by a scripted verbatim run.

## Scope
**browser-model-manager**
- README: install; authorize-then-acquire flow (construction and status reads trigger no acquisition; the app or developer authorizes downloads); progress/abort; cache behaviour (OPFS, Cache Storage fallback, Safari worker sync handles); quota/eviction; reference-counted leases and typed invalidation; disposal; errors; troubleshooting; supported browsers. States plainly that no hidden network repair happens during engine operations.
- API reference from `.d.ts`; runnable example acquiring from a developer-hosted static origin and passing the capability to the engine.

**cloudflare-model-host (authored and then finalized here)**
- `packages/cloudflare-model-host/README.md`: staging/publication commands, inputs, manifest schema, required MIME/CORS/COEP/CORP/cache/digest headers, worker/WASM paths, COOP/COEP for threaded routes with usable single-thread behaviour, second-origin configuration (the `models.facemorph.me` Worker over R2 `facemorph-runtime-mirror` pattern) and the warm command.
- Generic HTTPS static-hosting guide and a Cloudflare-specific guide (Cloudflare tooling optional). Verified Cloudflare limits for the documented artifact sizes, with the check date; "free" tier claims only where verified against actual sizes and tier.
- API/CLI reference; runnable example publishing to a local static server.
- For publication: final package names and install commands from the name check (pkgdocs.engine), cross-links to the engine, manager and converter docs and the compatibility table, and the host -> manager -> engine quickstart.
- FaceMorph values (`models.facemorph.me`, `facemorph-runtime-mirror`) appear only inside a labelled example block.

**model-conv**
- `packages/model-conv/README.md`: clone at the tag, build, acquire (trusted checkpoint, terms; the pickle warning before the command), convert, verify; CPU and optional NVIDIA; validated OS/arch matrix; outputs and how they feed the host and manager; compatibility table link; licences and notices; no weights. Ships as the Dockerfile and opt-in Compose service at a tagged public release (base images pinned by digest), not an npm package or registry image.

## Out of scope
Engine docs (pkgdocs.engine). FaceMorph's own production promotion and tagging the release (delivery).

## Notes
- This row merges the former hosting-docs and host-finalization items, so the authoring/finalizing boundary between them no longer applies; the host README is written once here.
- Copyable commands only; no pseudocode quickstart.
- Edits no shared bridge/runtime/worker file.

title: Rewrite maintained research guides and protocol for this repository
description:
## Background

Maintained docs: guide (`README.md`), protocol (`program.md`), record standards (`records.md`), round and
append-only log-entry templates. Some guides still call classic facemorph.me or require browser/native
rotation. The targeted launch recipe today runs only in classic:
`python3 autoresearch/run.py --lane browser-gpu --device eris --state-dir autoresearch/state --timeout 1800 -- autoresearch/devices/eris/gpu-bench.sh "UNIQUE_RUN_LABEL" "QUALIFIED_ORIGIN" 6`.

## Why

No guide may tell an agent to start research in classic; one clearly named command entry point with new paths.

## Scope

- Maintained guide/protocol/records/templates updated (as new revisions; historical copies remain in Git
  history and in frozen trees where they are historical).
- One named entry point command documented with the absolute state directory per machine.
- Rules carried: lease before every heavy build/correctness run/warmup/measurement; control/control noise
  first; ABBA ×3 with discarded warmup; fresh confirmation separate from screening; append-only `log.md` at
  EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps; `results.tsv` 11-column header, evaluated outcomes
  only, corrections as new rows; opportunity reporting; native evidence stays historical.
- State this plan governs release scope over older guide text.

## Launch recipe and round template carried into the guide

- One named entry point: `autoresearch/run.py` invoked from this repository's root, documented as
  ```sh
  python3 autoresearch/run.py --lane <lane> --device <machine> \
    --state-dir "<absolute per-machine lease dir from research.runner-lease>" --timeout <s ≤ 3600> -- \
    <driver command with quoted arguments>
  ```
  with the existing GPU screen as the worked example (new paths, absolute state dir):
  `python3 autoresearch/run.py --lane browser-gpu --device eris --state-dir "<ABS_LEASE_DIR>" --timeout 1800 -- autoresearch/devices/eris/gpu-bench.sh "UNIQUE_RUN_LABEL" "QUALIFIED_ORIGIN" 6`.
  The guide states this GPU screen is not the chooser-overlap benchmark and that the evaluator/adapters do
  not exist merely because the wrapper exists.
- Round launch-recipe template (`autoresearch/templates/launch-recipe.md`), every field required:
  executable checkout and worker; dependency and artifact readiness checks; exact command and arguments
  (quoted); shared device identity; absolute lease-state directory; fixtures (metadata-free photos, no
  personal photos); browser profile handling (empty / retained / resident); durable output locations
  outside transient CI artifacts; fresh run label (`A–Z`, `a–z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output
  directory; budget (default 600 s, maximum 3600 s); busy handling (exit 75 or bounded `--wait`).
- Round template: dated round, named journey/bottleneck, exclusions, one falsifiable mechanism per
  candidate, resource/time budget, new candidate directory; control/control noise before candidate
  observation; discarded warmup + same-cell ABBA ×3; fresh confirmation separate from screening; record
  every screened candidate; cohorts (empty cache, cached files/new browser, live resident session, cached
  output, restored result); finish boundaries (decoded/drawn face, useful scrub frame, playable video,
  prepared file, Save/share handoff).
- Opportunity reporting fields: source/artifact, affected wait/journey/cache/device, bottleneck or
  hypothesis, mechanism, consent/asset/memory/cancellation costs, preserved invariants, platform cells,
  suitable worker, next refuting test; a proposal is not a ledger outcome or a tracker authorisation.
- Methodology boundaries kept from the 12 October check: no resets, no empty-ledger initialisation, no
  unbounded looping, no crash-as-zero metrics; a noisy minimum is not a gain.

## Out of scope

Driver changes (stage 2).

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A text scan finds no instruction to run research in classic and no relative `autoresearch/state` default in maintained guides.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] `autoresearch/templates/launch-recipe.md` exists with every listed field; a validator (or the workload spec validator) rejects a recipe missing the absolute lease dir, the run label or the durable output location.
- [ ] The maintained guide documents the single entry command with the absolute state dir and the worked GPU-screen example at the new paths; a text scan finds no instruction to start a round in classic.
- [ ] The launch-recipe validator also rejects: a timeout above 3600 s, missing busy handling, missing fixtures or browser-profile handling, a run label not matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`, and a run label whose output directory already exists (one fixture each).
- [ ] A link check over the re-homed research docs and the classic forward pointer resolves every link to this repository's plan and guides (including the replacement for classic's `PLAN.md` symlink) and fails on a dead link.

title: Freeze engine operation signatures, renderMorph and worker message rules
description:
## Background

The engine owns inference, numerical qualification, morph geometry (all current selector modes,
including linear and figure-eight), bounded frame production and computational image/media helpers.
The candidate's `video-worker.mjs` and `last-result.mjs` enforce a 4,096-frame path limit; the media
path is WebCodecs 1024→512 with FFmpeg 512 fallback, eight-frame raw segments and bounded codec queues.
Operations carry opaque request/input-revision/attempt IDs and actual providers.

## Why

The typed facade, compute extraction and morph pipeline need one frozen operation surface, and the
worker boundary rules prevent cloned-promise and late-result bugs.

## Scope

- Operation signatures: mapping, synthesis, encode, metadata/latent extraction, raw-pixel PNG and
  lossless WebP encode with recovery metadata, and `renderMorph` endpoints, settings, display
  callbacks and video result.
- Request/input-revision/attempt IDs on every operation; actual provider recorded on results.
- Cancellation/disposal settles pending operations; late results cannot replace newer input.
- Worker messages contain no promise/signal/callback objects; payloads are cloneable; signals and
  callbacks stay caller side. Status/capability reads start no acquisition.
- Buffer and device ownership; retained frame, resource, cancellation and evidence contracts
  (named numeric bounds, values in m2); sparse preview anchors cannot deadlock ordered video drain.
- Separate available pixels, file readiness, persistence, decoded display and playable video.
- Cover existing cache/raw/blob/sequential/retained-then-encode browser branches and endpoint reuse.
- Compute-ready versus default-file-complete milestones on results.

## Typed outputs (citable)

Draft first under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`, then moved by the milestone type-test bead to the module below. Exported names are stable: downstream beads cite them; a rename needs a contract revision and an update of the `contracts.md` export index.

- `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/operations.ts`: `OperationIds` (requestId, inputRevision, attemptId), `MappingRequest`/`MappingResult`, `SynthesisRequest`/`SynthesisResult`, `EncodeRequest`/`EncodeResult`, `ExtractMetadataRequest`/`ExtractMetadataResult`, `RawImageEncodeRequest` (`png` | `webp-lossless`, with `RecoveryMetadata`), `RenderMorphRequest` (endpoints, `MorphSettings` with `MorphPathMode` covering every current selector mode incl. linear and figure-eight, frame count, FPS, resolution), `RenderMorphResult`, `ResultMilestone` (`compute-ready` | `file-complete`), `OperationSettlement` (`completed` | `cancelled` | `superseded` | `failed`).
- `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/worker-messages.ts`: `EngineWorkerRequest` and `EngineWorkerResponse` unions (structured-clone safe; no functions, promises or AbortSignals).
- `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/recovery-metadata.ts`: `RecoveryMetadataV1` and `parseRecoveryMetadata(unknown)` result type (missing / damaged / incompatible distinguished).
- Constant `MAX_MORPH_FRAMES = 4096`.
- Consumers: `migration.facade-types`, `compute.*`, `morph.*`, `media.envelope-helpers`, `media.recovery-schema`.

## Out of scope

Application scheduler policy (m2). MP4 project import UI (deferred by operator).

## Considerations

- Packages must not import application policy; the app owns interaction, consent, input revisions,
  display URLs, session selection, slider preference and reporting transport.
- Shared-file note: the facade and compute extraction later edit `product-bridge.mjs`,
  `browser/runtime.mjs`, `browser/ort-worker.mjs`; this item only defines types.

## Polish r2 additions

- **Recovery parse result (engine level).** `parseRecoveryMetadata(bytes)` returns exactly one of
  `{kind: 'missing'}` (decodable image, no recovery chunk), `{kind: 'damaged', reason}` (chunk present
  but fails parse, integrity hash or bounds), `{kind: 'incompatible-schema', schemaVersion}` (valid
  envelope of a schema this build cannot read) or `{kind: 'parsed', metadata: RecoveryMetadataV1}`.
  Model comparison is the app's job: `contracts.app-batch-progress-types` maps `parsed` to
  `matching` / `incompatible-model` / `unknown-model`. The reader never fetches a URL found in
  metadata. Schema versioning for dynamic shapes is frozen with the descriptor in
  `contracts.model-descriptor-dev-journey`; V1 must not hard-code 18×512 in its type (shape comes

- **Five readiness states, not two (plan "separate available pixels, file readiness, persistence,
  decoded display and playable video").** `ResultMilestone` stays `compute-ready | file-complete`
  for the operation's own completion, and results additionally carry `ResultReadiness` =

  `not-applicable`), so persistence or display readiness is never implied by `file-complete`.
- **Media branch table.** The operations section has one row per existing browser branch: cached
  result, raw sparse preview anchors, blob stream, sequential, retained-then-encode, and endpoint
  reuse. Each row gives its callback/drain type, buffer owner, and the anchor-ordering rule that stops

title: stylegan-js package surface, caller-loaded example, capability table and the shared tarball content scan
description:
## Goal
Give `stylegan-js` a consumer-ready package surface, a caller-loaded example that needs no manager, a documented independent CPU/reference capability table, and the one shared tarball content scan every package, hosting and publication step runs. Split from `compute.app-rebind` (fm-fy2.6) in the 24 October final pass: this work needs only the engine package (`compute.synthesis`, `compute.photo-descriptor`) and none of the app, so it proceeds as soon as the engine package exists, alongside `compute.app-rebind`. `hosting.chunks`, `conversion.container`, `verify.consumers`, `pkgdocs.release` and `delivery.packages` reuse the scan unchanged.

## Scope
**Package surface and example**
- `package.json` exports map (main, types, worker entry points), emitted `.d.ts`, no workspace aliases, no React, `files` allowlist.
- `packages/stylegan-js/examples/caller-loaded/`: a minimal browser example that loads a model capability itself (no manager import), maps a seed, synthesizes, synthesizes a second face and one interpolated latent through the public `map`/`synthesize` API, and disposes, showing progress, abort and errors. (`renderMorph` does not exist yet; its example is written in `pkgdocs.engine` after `morph.render`.)
- Document and qualify the library's independent CPU/reference capabilities (providers, browsers, what is unqualified), distinct from the app's product routes; no native distribution requirement; Node/headless inference not implied.
- Package construction and status/capability reads start no acquisition.
- Detailed logging: the example and its test log load, map, synthesize and dispose timings, the actual provider and every intercepted request by host class.

**`package-tarball-content-scan` (created here, cited by name everywhere else; moved from `compute.app-rebind` in the 24 October final pass)**
- `scripts/packages/check-tarball-contents.mjs`: `node scripts/packages/check-tarball-contents.mjs --profile <stylegan-js|browser-model-manager|cloudflare-model-host|model-conv-context> --input <tarball.tgz | build-context dir> --report <out.json>`. Exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 usage error or unknown profile (never passes silently).
- All four profiles in `scripts/packages/tarball-profiles/<profile>.json`, created now from the stated package boundaries; a profile change is a reviewed diff with its self-test fixture.
- JSON report `{scanVersion, profile, input, inputSha256, files: [{path, bytes, sha256}], findings: [{rule, path, detail}], requiredMissing: [], outcome}`, kept as a CI artifact.
- Shared rules (lists `tar -tzf` or the directory) fail on: weights/model blobs (`.onnx`, `.ort`, `.bin`, `.pt`, `.pth`, `.pkl`, `.safetensors`, `.npy`, `.npz`, `.h5`, `.tflite`, and any file over a declared limit, default 5 MiB, not on a runtime-WASM allowlist); repository-only paths (`apps/`, `autoresearch/`, `docs/receipts/`, `docs/plans/`, `.beads/`, `deploy-next/`, `experiment/`, test fixtures, source maps pointing outside the package, absolute or sibling paths such as `/home/`, `../facemorph.me-classic`, `file://` inside emitted JS, `.d.ts` or `package.json`); secrets (`npm_` tokens, Cloudflare API tokens, `-----BEGIN` private keys, AWS-style keys, `.env`, `.npmrc` with auth); private provenance (FaceMorph production hostnames or R2 bucket names in engine/manager code; host package docs may name them only as an example origin).
- Required files: emitted JS, `.d.ts`, worker entry points named in `exports`, `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`, provenance record.
- Profile rules: `stylegan-js` no host URLs, OPFS/Cache Storage calls, DOM/UI imports or reporting transport; `browser-model-manager` no engine/inference code, FaceMorph catalogue or hostnames; `cloudflare-model-host` no weights, FaceMorph origins only in docs examples; `model-conv-context` no checkpoints, converted outputs, `.env` or credentials, and its `.dockerignore` excludes them.
- Runs in CI on every `npm pack` of each package and on the converter build context.

## Out of scope
App rebinding and product lanes (`compute.app-rebind`). Public README/API docs and quickstart (`pkgdocs.engine`). npm publication (delivery). Morph (`morph.render`).

## Notes
- Edits none of the shared bridge/runtime/worker files.
- If `hosting.chunks` or `conversion.container` needs the scan before this row lands, that row creates `scripts/packages/check-tarball-contents.mjs` with exactly the rules and profiles above and this row reuses it unchanged; there is never a second scanner.

title: Recovery envelope helpers and still-image recovery reader in stylegan-js
description:
## Goal
`stylegan-js` encodes raw pixels to PNG and lossless WebP carrying exact latent and model/provenance recovery metadata, and reads that metadata back with validation. On top of the helpers, a still-image recovery reader classifies every dropped, chosen or pasted file before any target is touched, so recovered and static results install without inference and damaged recovery never silently becomes a photo. Static names publish recovery-bearing WebPs through these helpers, so they can land early (the candidate code is already a valid producer).

## Scope
**Envelope helpers**
- Candidate sources: `src/Next/image-envelope.mjs` (~100 lines), `recovery-metadata.mjs` (~70 lines), `browser/png.mjs`, `image-encoder.mjs`/`image-encoder-worker.mjs`.
- Strict-TS `encodePng(pixels, recovery)`, `encodeLosslessWebp(pixels, recovery)`, `readRecovery(bytes)` with schema/version validation and typed rejection of unknown or damaged envelopes.
- Keep readers for schema-1 PNG and schema-2 PNG/WebP; the app's lossy WebP (quality 0.8) path keeps writing a valid envelope for its actual payload.
- Integrity hash over the actual new payload; re-encoding regenerates the envelope (never copy an obsolete hash).
- Metadata holds only latent, model/provenance and (for morphs) ordered controls/settings; never raw source photos, typed words, original filenames or diagnostics.
- No byte equality with the candidate's files is required; only exact recovery values and lossless pixel preservation. Keep the API stable once the first names catalogue publishes.

**Recovery reader**
- `inspectStill(file) -> {kind, image, latent?, modelIdentity?, reason}`, `kind` one of `matching`, `missing`, `damaged`, `incompatible-schema`, `incompatible-model`, `unknown-model`, with validated integrity; the one function the app's single-file entry, paste and multi-file batches call before any target replacement (late imports are rejected by the app's revision checks); the wiring into the app is `media.reader-wiring`.
- `missing`: decodable image with no recovery chunk; enters photo encoding only through an explicit Encode image / Use as photo action, never automatically.
- `damaged`: chunk present but fails parsing, integrity or bounds; never silently re-encoded (identity must not change); Use as photo offered only when the pixels decode, as an explicit action.
- `incompatible-schema`: well-formed envelope with a schema/version this build does not support; viewable and saveable, no latent use, reason names the version.
- `incompatible-model`: known identity different from the loaded model, including equal-shaped latents from another checkpoint (not combinable). `unknown-model`: identity this build does not know. Both: viewable and saveable with compute disabled.
- Model mismatch (all `incompatible-*` and `unknown-model`): image shown; Save/Share hands over the original bytes unchanged (no re-encode, envelope kept); the latent never reaches the engine; the face is excluded from morph inputs with a plain reason.
- `matching`: installs image and latent without model acquisition, detector or encoder.
- Never follow model URLs or any URL found in metadata.

## Out of scope
Dynamic-shape schema versioning and MP4 metadata (media.schema). Save/Share UI, batch UI, click order and keypoint insertion (face controls). App wiring (`media.reader-wiring`) and built-UI checks (`crop.ported-app`). MP4 project import (deferred).

## Notes
- `inspect-still.matching-dynamic-shape` is owned by media.schema and joins this suite when that schema lands; this row does not wait for it.
- This row edits none of the shared bridge/runtime/worker files: wiring the reader into the app's entry paths is `media.reader-wiring` and its built-UI checks are `crop.ported-app` (after `crop.queue`, split out in the 24 October final pass), so names generation can use the helpers early.
- Shared-file order (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October; revised in the 24 October final pass): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in one sequence enforced by needs edges, never concurrently: `provider.native` -> `provider.webgl` -> `provider.route-admission` -> `migration.project-json` (one-line ProjectJson import swap) -> typed facade (`migration.facade`) -> `compute.synthesis` -> `compute.photo-descriptor` -> `compute.app-rebind` -> `crop.fix` -> `crop.queue` -> `media.reader-wiring` -> `media.export` -> `media.schema` -> `morph.render` -> `morph.guards` -> `media.session` -> face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Rows that must not edit these files: `crop.repro`, `compute.blend`, `compute.package-surface`, `media.envelope`, `provider.admission` (evidence), `crop.ported-app` and `compute.ported-app` (acceptance on the ported app; a fix they need follows the out-of-turn rule below) and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept row; code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) until the bridge's own turn. A row that finds it must edit one of these files outside its turn adds a needs edge to the latest row in the sequence that edits it. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #media-and-recovery, #file-sharing-and-export-direction.

- [x] Helper unit tests in Node and a real browser: round-trip latent/model values exact; lossless decode of PNG and lossless WebP equals the supplied RGBA exactly; truncated, corrupt, oversized and unknown-schema inputs rejected.
- [x] Earlier candidate fixtures (schema-1 PNG, schema-2 PNG and WebP) decode to identical latent/model values.
- [x] Corruption fuzz (truncate, bit flip, wrong schema) never yields a silently accepted latent.
- [x] Named reader tests: `inspect-still.missing`, `.damaged-truncated`, `.damaged-bitflip`, `.damaged-oversized`, `.incompatible-schema`, `.incompatible-model`, `.unknown-model`, `.matching-schema1-png`, `.matching-schema2-png`, `.matching-schema2-webp`, `.mismatch-save-bytes-unchanged`, `.mismatch-latent-not-used` (engine spy receives nothing), `.no-metadata-url-fetch`.

title: Run destination JS and exact-artifact checks against the imported closure
description:
## Background
Import acceptance (PLAN.md "Candidate source import and bootstrap"): the destination's JS checks (unit, runtime and bridge-import) pass against the imported closure, and its local exact-artifact harness exercises the pinned control artifact with the selected runtime bytes, source identities and applicable functional/cancellation/resource checks; known planned-to-fix candidate behaviour is recorded separately; no remote publisher/domain change occurs.

Classic's list of these checks is `.github/workflows/next-site.yml` job `artifact` at the frozen revision (`6107f80` as read on 24 October): `scripts/check-tests-listed.mjs` (every test file is run), one `node --test` list of about 36 files under `src/Next/**`, `hosting/next-static/analytics.test.mjs`, `hosting/next-cloudflare/worker.test.mjs` and, since `6107f80`, `hosting/next-mirror/worker.test.mjs`; `scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs`; `scripts/check-progress-copy.mjs`; `src/Next/geometry/verify.mjs`; then `build:next`, the preview byte compare, `verify-fable.mjs` and `check-no-third-party.mjs deploy-next`.

## Why
Unblocks the typed facade and port milestones (via `ws:import`), and fixes the honest baseline: which classic checks run in the destination, which cannot yet and why.

## Scope
- Run in the destination, from `apps/web` / repo root as the development instructions name: `check-tests-listed` (adapted to the destination paths), the full `node --test` list at the frozen revision (minus tests whose files fm-hyw left in classic, each listed with its owner), `check-progress-copy`, `geometry/verify.mjs`.
- **Fable-dependent checks**: `check-bridge-imports.mjs` and `verify-fable.mjs` are recorded `not applicable until the port` with reason (no generated Fable output exists in the destination by rule) and successor (strict TS at `migration.facade-types` fm-pth3; ProjectJson goldens at `migration.ctl-projectjson` fm-dtmm). They are never reported as passed. In their place this bead runs `scripts/inventory/unresolved-imports.mjs`, whose only allowed entry is `product-bridge.mjs → ./ProjectJson.fs.js`.
- Run the local exact-artifact harness against the control artifact (`deploy-next/` from `npm run build:next`, labelled control) with functional, cancellation and resource checks, using runtime bytes acquired by `import.runtime-reuse`. Name the runtime identities (manifest digest, runtime bundle version) in the log. The second runtime origin is used only on `facemorph.me` / `*.facemorph.me` pages (`runtimeMirror()` in `src/Next/Assets/model-cache.mjs`, since `6107f80`), so a local harness run must show zero requests to `models.facemorph.me`; the log records the host class that served each runtime file and the run asserts that from the log.
- `check-no-third-party.mjs deploy-next` on the control output and the preview byte compare (`src/public/preview/hello-1024.webp` vs `deploy-next/preview/hello-1024.webp`).
- Record known planned-to-fix candidate behaviour separately (from the defect ledger, fm-pe0): a harness failure that matches a ledger row is reported as that row, not hidden and not counted as an import regression.

## Out of scope
Fixing candidate defects; operated UI acceptance (this is a harness run; by-name clicks are setup only).

## Considerations
A check that silently skips (zero files, zero tests) is a failure of this bead, not a pass: every check's log must show a non-zero count of what it checked, except the two recorded not-applicable checks.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] All applicable destination JS checks pass; each check's log line shows its non-zero count (tests run, files scanned); the run lists every classic check from `next-site.yml` with status passed / not applicable (reason, successor) / left in classic (owner).
- [ ] `check-bridge-imports.mjs` and `verify-fable.mjs` appear as `not applicable until the port`, not as passed; `unresolved-imports.mjs` passes with only the ProjectJson entry.
- [ ] Exact-artifact harness passes on the control with named runtime identities; functional, cancellation and resource checks listed with outcomes; `check-no-third-party` and the preview byte compare pass on the control output.
- [ ] Ledger-matching failures reported against their defect-ledger row ids.
- [ ] The end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, retains the log as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics), and every network claim is asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt `docs/receipts/import-checks.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime/model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Its structured event log is written with the emitter from `build.docs-decisions-receipts` (fm-ucl: `scripts/evidence/event-log.ts`, or `scripts/evidence/event_log.py` for Python harnesses) using the host classes in `scripts/evidence/host-classes.json`, and the log passes `node scripts/check-event-log.ts <log>`; the receipt passes `node scripts/check-receipts.ts` (polish r2).
notes: Plan anchors (PLAN.md): #candidate-source-import-and-bootstrap; receipts rule: #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance.

title: Import the candidate JS closure from Git objects with provenance
description:
## Background
`inventory.import-allowlist` (fm-hyw) commits, in `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/inventory.md`: the frozen committed import revision of classic (repo ID 295956585, branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`; `6107f80` as read on 24 October, four commits after the planning reference `b2d945a`), the reviewed delta from `b2d945a`, the allowlist and path map with sha256 digests, the exclusions, the destination collision list, and the **unresolved-import list** (expected to hold exactly `product-bridge.mjs → ./ProjectJson.fs.js`). `inventory.licenses` (fm-f7g) supplies the notices the import carries. Classic keeps its history and publisher; provenance stays available without copying `.git`, resetting or creating a worktree.

## Why
The monorepo needs the candidate's runnable code before the facade and port, as one checked revision that anyone can regenerate from Git objects.

## Scope
- Export allowlisted files from Git objects of the frozen commit (`git -C ../facemorph.me-classic archive <commit> <paths>` or `git show <commit>:<path>`; never copy from the working tree, which holds other sessions' uncommitted edits), write them under `apps/web` keeping the `src/Next` relative structure; temporary root paths for `desktop/runtime.mjs`, required `scripts/` and any `hosting/` files a closure test imports, each tracked in the inventory with its consumer.
- Record repo ID/commit, path map, digests and notices in `inventory.md`.
- Merge only required dependency settings into the destination `package.json`/lock.
- Review collisions first; protect `PLAN.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.beads/`.
- **Generated Fable output stays out.** `ProjectJson.fs.js` is not in Git (classic `.gitignore`: `*.fs.js`) and is not created, copied from a build, or replaced by a shim. `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` is imported byte-identical, including its line-9 import of `./ProjectJson.fs.js`, which stays unresolved until `migration.facade-types` (fm-pth3) swaps it for the TS module produced by `migration.ctl-projectjson` (fm-dtmm). Until then no destination step may load the bridge as an ES module or bundle it; the checks that touch it read it as text (see fm-hyw).
- **Later delta.** Files changed by the reviewed commits after `b2d945a` (`dce7f27` index/meta/og image, `bacd6e5` and `6107f80` `model-cache.mjs` retries and second-origin alternation, `6107f80` `reporting.mjs` network classification) are imported at their frozen-revision bytes. `hosting/next-mirror/` is imported only if fm-hyw's disposition says a closure test imports it; otherwise it remains in classic for `ws:hosting`/`ws:deploy` to take from the same frozen revision, and the receipt says which.
- **Check scripts** (committed under `scripts/import/`, unit-tested with fixture trees):
  - `verify-closure.mjs`: every imported file's sha256 equals the allowlist digest; every allowlisted file exists; no extra file.
  - `scan-exclusions.mjs`: no F# (`*.fs`, `*.fsproj`), no `*.fs.js`/`*.fs.js.map`, no `global.json`/`.config/dotnet-tools.json`, no Webpack config, no legacy Server/API file, no weights (by extension and size threshold), no `.wrangler/`, no credentials (secret-pattern scan).
  - `unresolved-imports.mjs` (shared with fm-hyw): output equals the committed unresolved-import list exactly; a new unresolved specifier fails.
  - Each prints one JSON line per finding and a summary line (`files`, `mismatches`, `excluded_hits`, `unresolved`), so the receipt quotes logs, not prose.

## Out of scope
F# build; native packages or release automation; moving temporary paths (later revisions); porting ProjectJson (fm-dtmm) or swapping the import (fm-pth3).

## Considerations
One checked revision. Temporary source paths leave only after their mapped consumers migrate. If the candidate branch moved after fm-hyw froze the revision, import the frozen revision anyway; newer commits are a later, separately reviewed delta, never pulled in silently.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `verify-closure.mjs` passes: imported tree digests equal the allowlist digests; zero missing, zero extra.
- [ ] `scan-exclusions.mjs` passes: no F#, no `*.fs.js`, no Server/API, weights, credentials or `.wrangler/`.
- [ ] `unresolved-imports.mjs` output equals the committed list (exactly `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs → ./ProjectJson.fs.js`, owner fm-dtmm, swap fm-pth3); `product-bridge.mjs` digest equals its frozen-revision digest (unchanged).
- [ ] Unit tests for the three scripts: digest mismatch detected; extra file detected; a planted `Foo.fs.js` and a planted `.wrangler/` dir each fail the exclusion scan; a planted second unresolved import fails; clean fixture passes.
- [ ] Provenance recorded (repo ID, frozen commit, reviewed delta from `b2d945a`, path map, notices); receipt states whether `hosting/next-mirror/` was imported or left for `ws:hosting`/`ws:deploy`.
- [ ] Receipt `docs/receipts/import-closure.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime/model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes: Plan anchors (PLAN.md): #candidate-source-import-and-bootstrap; receipts rule: #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance.

title: Check newer ORT bundles on iOS Simulator and Android emulator lanes
description:
## Background

The ORT WebGPU mapping is used on iPhone and Android in the existing Simulator and emulator lanes. The
design plan distinguishes bundles (`./webgpu`, `./jspi`) by async bridge; do not assume the native-EP
bundle runs where the JSEP one does. e4e WASM heap limit 268,435,456 bytes while 108 FP32 shards stream.

## Why

Phones are first-class; a runtime that breaks iOS WebKit or the e4e heap bound cannot be adopted for that route.

## Scope

- Run each staged set's mobile route checks in the iOS Simulator (WebKit) and Android emulator lanes.
- Measure e4e WASM heap peak against 268,435,456 bytes during streamed encode where the lane executes models.

## Out of scope

Physical-phone qualification (evidence gap remains).

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Per lane × set: load/canary result, heap peak where applicable, and named failures.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script involved emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform and provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, retains the log as a CI artifact, and any network claim is asserted from that log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Rows are per bundle (`./webgpu`, `./jspi`) × lane, the iOS row on WebKit in the Simulator; the e4e WASM heap peak over all 108 FP32 shards is pass/fail against 268,435,456 bytes, and exceeding it rejects that set for that route. The native-EP bundle is never assumed to run where the JSEP one does.

title: Tile action states, validation, paste and Encode image rename
description:
26 October operator correction: use the actual face card for file chooser/drop/paste, with no empty Encode source modal. Keep crop confirmation/adjustment for fresh photos. Generate/Cancel/Cancelling/Retry belongs inline beside the textbox; all validation, cancellation, stale-result, consent, recovery and batch guarantees remain. Placement/source-entry assertions below supersede conflicting historical wording; no behavioral acceptance is waived.

## Goal
Give each face tile one honest action slot whose state always matches what the face can do, accept text and seeds exactly as typed, make main-field paste and drop equivalent to choosing a file, rename photo entry to **Encode image**, and remove the duplicate filename caption and hold-to-compare. Fixes defects 5 (phone keyboard turns "hello" into "Hello", a different face, because `browser/identity.mjs` hashes the raw string), 8 (typed words with no picture leave the tile saying "Drop a photo, or tap to choose") and 20 (copy part).

## Scope
- **Slot state table** in the inline operation slot beside the textbox and `.next-tile-status` (one action slot per tile; Generate beside the textbox and Generate-becomes-Cancel are declared changes):

| state | slot |
|---|---|
| empty/invalid words or seed | no enabled Generate; concise field error |
| valid unfinished words/seed incl. display-only preview | Generate if admitted, else readable operation-specific reason + Help |
| verified result | result actions when file ready; no Generate |
| static selection pending | Loading, cancellable; Retry on fetch failure, never synthesis |
| queued/active compute or acquisition | Cancel for that operation |
| non-preemptible stopping | disabled Cancelling until settled, then Retry if input remains |
| failed/cancelled words/seed or confirmed photo with retry pixels | Retry, same input/slot, new attempt ID |
| interrupted photo without pixels | Encode image entry |
| pixels ready, file pending/failed | Preparing file / file-preparation Retry, pixels visible |

- Typing clears the displayed result and creates a new revision; eligibility = no valid result for the current revision. Retry works without another keystroke. Editing a queued/running tile cancels only that tile's job; late results for an old revision are rejected. Nothing is requested per keystroke.
- **Field**: `autocapitalize="off"`, `autocorrect="off"`, `spellcheck="false"`; never trim or normalize; Enter invokes the same Generate/Retry, respects IME composition, cannot duplicate an active job. Words reject empty/whitespace-only and enforce 512 UTF-8 bytes (`browser/identity.mjs`).
- **Seed**: 0 through 4,294,967,295 inclusive (`Product.fs` seed input, `image-envelope.mjs`); reject empty, negative, fractional and out-of-range with a field error; never strip digits into another seed.
- Typed word without an instant picture says "Press Generate to make this face"; photo entry stays in the mode menu and by drop (the empty-tile photo click cannot share Generate's click target).
- Blocked actions give the owning reason in the tile status, readable to keyboard/screen readers (no hover-only tooltip), before model/detector acquisition or photo preparation. One plain message per refused input; no raw runtime exception text as visitor copy; one message owner per failed action.
- Fix defect-20 copy: "about 1 seconds", "smaller than25 MB" and two more missing-space messages; seed placeholder "Just type anything".
- A historic initial preview is display-only: Morph may generate its unfinished text but cannot use preview pixels; Save waits for a verified result. No preview badge (defect 23 decision). Export-only Retry stays separate from inference Retry.
- **Encode image rename**: every photo-encoding label/entry reads **Encode image**; where photo encoding is unavailable the same entry reads **Open saved image** (recovery-only), no duplicate control.
- **Main-field paste**: image clipboard data wins over coincident text; a single image uses the same recovery-first/photo dispatch as the file chooser (same consent/crop/encoding flow); text-only paste unchanged; mixed/unsupported items give a contextual message with no unintended text replacement.
- **Drop**: on a face binds that stable target; background drop uses the first empty face or appends one. No new drop target or import toolbar.
- **File dispatch** inspects recovery metadata first: a valid matching still installs without models; missing/damaged/incompatible metadata are distinguished; damaged/incompatible never silently re-encodes (explicit Use as photo in the existing error area); external MP4 input is reported unsupported without replacing work.
- **Replacement commit points**: keep the previous result through a cancelled chooser or rejected recovery file; never install a late import into a newer target.
- Remove the separate filename caption (the field may show the filename). Remove hold-to-compare entirely: button, pointer/keyboard gesture, instructions and stale state; no replacement gesture.
- **Old text/seed links** (open operator question): until answered keep candidate behaviour: `?from_value=`, `?to_value=`, `?from_seed=`, `?to_seed=`, `?from_guid=`, `?to_guid=` (or a mix) open the ordinary empty page with no filled field, notice, request or error, and never reach exports or diagnostics. If the operator says "honour", fill faces 1 and 2 through normal validation with no auto-Generate; if "notice", one short dismissible line in the status area.

## Out of scope
Static-name fetch mechanics; photo Retry pixel ownership (face.batch); Share/Save (face.export); batch selection; the crop modal.

## Notes
- Edits the ported tile state table, field, menu, validation and arrival parsing in the TS controller and React tile; calls existing generate/cancel/cache-check and recovery-first import unchanged; edits no shared bridge/runtime/worker file. Removing hold-to-compare leaves bridge exports `rememberSourcePhoto`/`sourcePhotoUrl` unused: remove their facade entries and UI calls here; the next bridge-editing bead deletes the two exports.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design, #next-release-ui-and-photo-requirements, #clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation, #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026 (rows 5, 8, 20).
acceptance_criteria:
Operated rule: real pointer/touch at the visible position, `elementFromPoint` returns the control inside the named region; by-name only for setup; 390 px and 1,280 px with a screenshot per case.
- [ ] Each state row driven (the real operation service and real CPU inference in the built app); the slot control clicked/tapped at its visible position inline beside the textbox; resulting transition asserted.
- [x] Text: empty, whitespace-only, 512-byte and 513-byte UTF-8, very long pasted string, "Hello" vs "hello" (two identities), IME composition (Enter during composition does not submit); typed text reaches the generator byte-identical (identity hash).
- [x] Seed: 0, 4294967295, 4294967296, -1, 1.5, empty, pasted " 42 " -> field error, never a different seed.
- [x] Field attributes present in the DOM; iPhone emulation typing "hello" keeps lowercase.
- [x] Cancel during generation -> Cancelling -> Retry with no keystroke; one Generate per Enter; no duplicate job.
- [x] Typing in face 2 of 3 while it generates: only face 2 shows Cancelling then Generate for the new revision; faces 1 and 3 continue; old late result rejected.
- [ ] New words on a tile with a verified result: result clears on first keystroke, Generate appears inline beside the textbox; zero per-keystroke requests (intercepted).
- [x] Copy snapshot: no missing spaces or "1 seconds"; one plain message per refused input; no raw exception text.
- [ ] Paste via real clipboard events into the field: one PNG; image plus text (image wins); text only; two images / unsupported type (message, text unchanged); recovery-bearing WebP installs with zero model requests.
- [x] Drop on tile vs background (first empty, else append) with synthetic DataTransfer at the visible tile position.
- [ ] Encode image on every photo entry; with photo encoding genuinely refused (Chromium launched with WebGPU disabled and the encoder assets absent from the local artifact server) the entry reads Open saved image and a saved PNG opens and saves.
- [x] DOM scan: no hold-to-compare element, handler or copy; no duplicate filename caption.
- [x] Replacement commit points: cancelled chooser and damaged recovery file keep the previous result; a slow import settling after the target was edited is not installed; other faces unchanged.
- [x] Legacy query keys: arrival-parser unit tests ignore all six keys; a page load with them opens the empty page with zero parameter-caused requests and no parameters in exports or diagnostics (or the answered branch, tested the same way).
- [ ] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test`) and pass.
