title: Run numerical canaries on newer runtimes for CPU WASM and WebGPU
description:
## Background

Current tolerances: RGB difference at most 1, sampled raw-float error at most 0.002, e4e latent maximum absolute error 0.0001. A runtime that fails them is rejected regardless of speed.

## Why

Numerics first: no performance result counts for a runtime that is not numerically equivalent.

## Scope

- Run product canaries and the applicable reference suite for each staged set on CPU WASM and WebGPU
  (eris RTX 2080 SUPER under the lease; CPU on a capable worker).
- Record raw differences, not only pass/fail.

## Out of scope

Performance runs.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Per set × provider: max RGB diff, max sampled raw-float error, e4e latent error, with pass/fail against unchanged tolerances.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script involved emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform and provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, retains the log as a CI artifact, and any network claim is asserted from that log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Freeze synthesis numerical checks and export-quality rules
description:
## Background

Product synthesis canaries require maximum RGB difference 1 on 0–255 and maximum sampled raw-float
error 0.002; the e4e latent tolerance is maximum absolute error 0.0001. Research/reference suites
(full31 etc.) keep their own frozen coverage and tolerances. Exported images need no byte identity
between builds; lossy decoded pixels need no exact parity; lossless helpers must preserve supplied
pixels on decode; model/latent/provenance values stay exact. Cross-build encoded-image hashes are not
correctness gates. The retained quality policy is classic `autoresearch/reviews/2026-10-10/quality-policy.md`.

## Why

Every later workstream's numerical and export checks cite these rules. Freezing them prevents
tolerance widening or pixel-hash gates sneaking back in (operator ruling: exact pixel hash gates were
ditched as too strict).

## Scope

- Raw pre-compression synthesis vs the independent qualified reference for the same model, latent,
  noise, preprocessing and workload, across qualified CPU/WebGPU routes, at the tolerances above.
- e4e latent tolerance 0.0001; ordinary-vs-lab/CI scheduling retained (no encoder lab check per visitor).
- Export rules: dimensions, orientation, practical visual quality, valid format/playback, recovery
  behaviour; lossless helpers decode to supplied pixels; recovery envelope regenerated and validated
  when re-encoding changes a payload (never copy an obsolete integrity hash).
- Artifact/model/asset hashes bind inputs, manifests, packages and deployments; export-integrity hashes
  validate individual files only.
- Other models need their own references and declared tolerances before qualification.

## Typed outputs (citable)

Draft first under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`, then moved by the milestone type-test bead to the module below. Exported names are stable: downstream beads cite them; a rename needs a contract revision and an update of the `contracts.md` export index.

- `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/numerics.ts`: `PRODUCT_CANARY_TOLERANCE` (`maxRgbDiff: 1` on 0–255, `maxSampledRawFloatError: 0.002`), `E4E_LATENT_TOLERANCE` (`maxAbsError: 0.0001`), `NumericalCheckResult` (raw differences, not only pass/fail), `ExportQualityRule` list with `isGate` flags (dimensions, orientation, valid format/playback, lossless decode equals supplied pixels, recovery envelope regenerated on re-encode; encoded-byte identity and decoded-lossy equality are explicitly `isGate: false`).
- The constants file's digest is the input to `currency.tolerance-cell-guard`'s frozen manifest.
- Consumers: `compute.*`, `media.*`, `ortweb.numerics`, `currency.tolerance-cell-guard`, `build.check-migration-map` (image-hash mapping), `verify.flows-synthesis-export`.

## Out of scope

Running any canary. Choosing tolerances for non-face models (conversion/compute own that).

## Considerations

Never widen tolerances, change precision or replace numerical evidence with a visual spot-check.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts.md` numerics section states each tolerance with its source file in the candidate and the suite it applies to.
- [ ] The export rules list what is and is not a gate, and how inherited image-hash assertions map to them (input to the check-migration map).
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Every name listed under "Typed outputs (citable)" exists in the draft type file and has a row in the `contracts.md` export index naming its consumers.
notes: Anchors: PLAN.md#synthesis-correctness-and-export-quality; #package-and-operation-contracts.

title: Release-consistent asset sets: publication order, retention window, old-tab tests
description:
## Background
Tie-break: release-consistent asset sets, old-tab compatibility and retention window belong to model hosting (retention, publication order) with workspace build (identity).

## Why
An in-flight app uses one immutable manifest identity; publishing a new app must not switch its shard identities or preprocessors mid-operation.

## Scope
Stage immutable referenced assets before the app that uses them; keep referenced assets for the supported active-session/rollback window (window and storage cost named in domain handover's delivery inventory); garbage-collect only by a documented retention policy. Tests: old open tab while a new app/manifest is published, interrupted acquisition, mixed/incompatible catalogue assets, ordinary rollback; missing old assets yield a clear reload/recovery action.

## Out of scope
Service worker/offline install.

## Considerations
Model-cache eviction never deletes completed exports or recovery records.

## Concrete cases (polish r2)
- **Second origin.** `models.facemorph.me` keeps referenced immutable assets for the same active-session/rollback window as the site, and a rollback artifact's paths are confirmed held there (a HEAD list) before rollback is claimed.
- **Old open tab.** An old open tab keeps one manifest identity mid-operation after a new app/manifest is published. Its requests (from the event log) name only old-manifest digests. If an old asset has gone, it gets a clear reload/recovery action within a bounded number of requests: no unbounded retry loop and no silent switch to new digests.
- **Interrupted acquisition.** Kill the network mid-chunk and resume. Verified chunks are kept, and the resumed bytes equal the remaining bytes.
- **Mixed catalogue assets.** A catalogue whose assets come from an incompatible manifest is refused with a typed error, and nothing is half-applied.
- **Rollback.** After an ordinary rollback the previous app runs against its own manifest.
- **Retention never deletes user data.** Model-cache eviction and retention garbage collection never delete completed user exports or application recovery records. A storage spy shows no deletes outside model-cache keys.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Documented retention policy; E2E old-tab and rollback tests pass against the staging origin.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, and the log is retained as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics). Network claims are asserted from the log, never from screenshots.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/hosting/release-consistency.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] E2E against the staging origin: old-tab (only old digests requested; missing old asset -> reload/recovery action within a bounded request count), interrupted acquisition (resume bytes = remaining bytes), mixed/incompatible catalogue (typed refusal), rollback, and second-origin retention (rollback paths HEAD-200 on the test mirror); storage spy shows retention/eviction never touches exports or recovery records.
notes:
Plan anchors: PLAN.md#model-hosting-extraction; #cloudflare-model-host; #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts; PLAN.md#workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership.
Polish r2 (C): acceptance now covers every plan case (interrupted acquisition, mixed catalogue, missing-old-asset action, mirror retention).

title: Device check placement and estimate copy
description:
## Goal
Show the device check where the requesting action already reports status, cancellable and never in the way of static names, and turn checker/calibration evidence into honest range, unknown and slow-work copy for the consent modal and action areas. Fixes defect 20 (the candidate's cold-device estimate text can never appear) and stops historical single-device priors being presented as estimates.

## Scope
- **Placement.** A visible "Checking this device…" status with **Skip** (Cancel) in the guidance/status area of the requesting action (the owning tile status or the Morph status). It runs before the first acquisition modal when an action needs it; never an arrival wizard, overlay, estimate dashboard or first-visit panel.
- At the deadline the download decision stays usable with labelled unknown estimates.
- Skipping the timing check cannot bypass per-operation capability/resource admission and cannot disable supported phone/CPU work.
- Browsing, selecting and saving static names never wait for the check.
- **Range strings** for Generate (per face), Encode (per confirmed crop and batch), download time, and an optional compact Morph total beside Create Morph when reliable (including final video preparation, or labelling the missing cost).
- **Unknown copy**: "Download time depends on your connection"; "No reliable estimate for this device". No range is rendered without evidence.
- **Slow-work nudge** driven by the affected workload's range, never a phone label or user agent: "This may be slow here. For faster face generation and morphs, try a computer with WebGPU." with Continue/Cancel retained and **Using a computer** linking to Help at `#computer-requirements`; without a reliable range, only general Help advice. Photo encoding also depends on CPU, so WebGPU is no promise of faster e4e.
- **Interruption warnings**: switching apps/tabs may pause work; closing/reloading can lose unfinished photo inputs (Encode image modal status and Morph status).
- Relabel the historical priors in `route-priors.mjs`/`estimate.mjs`; never present `estimate.mjs` `encodeMs` (video export) as photo encoding.

## Out of scope
The checker itself (device.checker); calibration (device.calibration); consent modal structure (consent.modal); Help page content (provider workstream); the release summary's platform cells and tested browser/OS list (integrated verification).

## Notes
- Copy/estimate-string module plus rendering in the ported UI sources; edits none of the shared bridge/runtime/worker files.
- Needs the consent modal (`consent.modal`, fm-9kr8): its ranges and unknown labels render in that modal's rows and its acceptance operates the modal.
- Unknown or uncalibrated estimates are supported; consent copy does not wait for calibration; nothing here gates phone support.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#lightweight-device-check-and-pre-download-guidance, #ui-flow-matrix-and-open-journey-contracts (row "Run/skip/timeout device timing check"), #device-check-and-estimates. Audit row 20.
acceptance_criteria:
Operated rule: real pointer/touch input at the visible position with `elementFromPoint` asserting the control and its region; by-name clicks only for setup. Each case at 390 px and 1,280 px with a screenshot.
- [ ] Copy-builder unit tests: calibrated, comparable-device, uncalibrated and unknown inputs produce the specified strings; no range without evidence; the nudge triggers on range, not user agent; `encodeMs` never labelled as photo encoding.
- [ ] Operated **Skip** at its visible position inside the requesting action's status area (not an overlay): the consent modal opens with labelled unknown estimates; admission still enforced (an unsupported operation stays refused).
- [ ] Deadline and interruption: a sample throttled for real (CDP CPU throttling) settles at the real 5 s deadline to "No reliable estimate for this device" and the consent modal opens with labelled unknowns; hiding the tab (visibilitychange) cancels with the same outcome; request interception shows zero model/detector/runtime requests.
- [ ] Static names during the check: open the names picker from a face burger, select a name and Save the result while the check runs, with no wait (timestamps).
- [ ] Ranges render in the consent modal rows and the Morph status beside Create Morph; the nudge renders in the owning action's status with Continue/Cancel retained; an operated tap on **Using a computer** opens Help at `#computer-requirements`; the interruption warning is present in the Encode image modal status and the Morph status.
- [ ] Preflight, skip/timeout and prediction-error checks of PLAN.md#integrated-verification pass.
- [ ] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test`) and pass.

title: Blend view: button, #blend, copied slots, weights, blend run, result display, layout
description:
## Goal
Give the retired API's `num_multi` users a weighted multi-face blend in the visitor's browser, on the new engine, with no server, GPU host or install. A **Blend faces** button and the deep link `https://facemorph.me/#blend` open a second view of the same session: any number of slots built from the existing compact face tile, a weight per slot, one large result shown and exported like any other face, and **Add to morph**. The Synthetic Data Ltd tester has used `num_multi` since June 2023 through `multi-morph-test.vercel.app` to build a library of fictitious, straight-on, ID-photo-style faces; that page stops working when the API is retired, and this view also answers their self-hosting question. Operator, 21 October, revised 24 October: "a button and a deep link to switch to a more advanced UI for merging multiple faces at once", reusing existing elements and the established export paths; desktop first, phone welcome but not required.

This bead builds the view itself: entry and exit (button and `#blend`), the copied slot list, the weight controls, running a blend and showing its result, layout and capacity. The saved blend file with its recipe, reopening it, **Add to morph**, filling many slots from one batch and the `blend` job report are `face.blend-view.output`, which follows this bead.

## Scope
- **Entry and exit.** A **Blend faces** button in More options is the only main-page addition. `#blend` opens the app straight into the view: a plain hash that works on static hosting with no server routing, survives reload, and Back leaves the view. It carries no faces or results; result-sharing URLs stay retired. Only `#blend` selects a view: Help and footer anchors scroll to their target without changing the hash, and an open names picker or crop modal is closed by Back before the view is. **Back to morph** and browser Back (including after arriving by the deep link) return to the main page with the session intact.
- **One session, two views.** The view keeps its own ordered slot list in the same session as the morph faces, persisted and restored with the session (photo retry pixels stay tab-only). On first open, slots are seeded as copies of all morph faces that have or can get a latent, at equal weights. Slots are copies: editing a slot never changes a morph face, or the reverse. A newly added slot gets weight 1/N and other weights are left alone.
- **Slots reuse the compact face tile** from the many-face layout: words, seed, Browse names, Encode image with the confirmed-crop flow, Open saved image, Generate/Cancel/Retry, Remove, plus the slot's weight. Photo slots use the same consent, confirmed crop and bounded encode queue as the main page.
- **Result display.** The blended result is an ordinary face output shown like any other face, with no blend-specific size: the full model frame (1024 x 1024 for the face model) in the complete-output display, with the established export controls (Share primary, Save, compact WebP default quality 0.8 / PNG lossless, editable filename, prepared-file reuse) from the Share/Save bead. The old page's 500 px is not a target. What the saved file contains (suggested filename, recipe), reopening a saved blend and Add to morph are `face.blend-view.output`.
- **Running a blend.** The view submits the blend parent intent to the operation controller (which waits for each slot's latent: mapping for an unfinished word or seed, the confirmed encode for a photo, the catalogue latent for a name; not slot images or files) and the engine's `blend(latents, weights)` then runs one synthesis. Slots at weight 0 are skipped; all-zero weights are refused with one plain line. A newer weight change supersedes a pending blend (latest wins by input revision). Regenerate when a slider is released or a keyboard step is committed, not on every drag tick. While regenerating, the previous result stays visible marked "Updating…" with Share/Save off until the new pixels and file are ready. A missing generator model goes through the existing consent modal; failures offer Retry in the result's action area. Leaving the view cancels a pending blend synthesis; slot photo encodes keep running, as on the main page.
- **Weight control.** A slider 0 to 1 in steps of 0.05 (old 0.1 values stay reproducible), value shown as text, arrow keys step 0.05. The view never exposes values outside 0-1 (the engine accepts [-2, 2] for library callers). Show the weight sum. **Reset** sets every weight to 1/N (the API default). When the sum is outside 0.8-1.2 show one line, e.g. "Weights add up to 1.35. Faces usually look most natural at 1.", with a **Make it 1** action scaling every weight in proportion. (A sum below 1 pulls the face towards the origin of W, not towards the average face.)
- **Shuffle weights** (planned 24 October under the no-human-gates rule as a removable planner proposal): one button sets random weights adding up to 1, within 0-1; one regeneration per press. If the operator vetoes it before close, drop the button and its acceptance line.
- **Capacity: no fixed slot limit (operator, 24 October: only real constraints).** The old API's 16 was a server choice, not a hardware limit. A blend costs one weighted sum and one synthesis whatever N is; each slot holds one W+ latent (about 36 KB) and a thumbnail, and each photo slot costs one encode through the bounded queue. The real limits are memory for retained photo inputs (the existing byte budgets in the contracts) and screen space. A batch that would exceed the photo-input budget gets the existing actionable reduce-selection message, never silent truncation. Degrading nicely: past what fits on screen the slot grid scrolls inside its panel while the result stays in view; slots shrink to compact rows (thumbnail, field, weight); small weights stay usable through the sum line, Reset and Make it 1.
- **Layout.** Desktop: result large and kept in view on the right, slots in a grid of compact tiles (2-4 columns) on the left, each weight under its slot. Phone: result pinned at the top at a smaller size, slots in a single-column list of compact tiles. Phone polish not required, but the view passes the responsiveness sweep's no-clipping, no-overflow bars. Admission is per operation: generation on any admitted route including phone CPU, photo encoding where admitted; no phone-specific code path.

## Out of scope
The saved blend file's filename and recipe, reopening a saved blend (and restoring weights by latent digest), **Add to morph**, filling many slots from one multi-photo/saved-face batch, and the `blend` job report to the analytics and usage-statistics sinks (`face.blend-view.output`). Old GUIDs or links; a hosted endpoint; blending inside the morph video; automatic or batch generation of many blends; model training; new models, encoders, downloads, workers or hosting. The `blend` function and its fixture tests (compute.blend); the blend parent intent and supersession (operation controller, `opctl.scheduler` fm-in6a); the recipe format in saved files (media.schema); the `blend` entry in the shared diagnostics action list (diagnostics).

## Notes
- Split on 2026-10-24 for swarm size: `face.blend-view` (this ID, fm-2kse: view, deep link, slots, weights, running a blend, layout and capacity) and `face.blend-view.output` (saved blend file and recipe, reopen, Add to morph, filling many slots from one batch, the `blend` job report). The original estimate for the whole view was two to three days.
- **Conflict resolution.** The absorbed bead described the superseded "Advanced: blend faces" panel over the session's own faces (0.1 steps, weights in project export/import, entry disabled at 1 face, hint for "far from 1"). PLAN.md's rewritten section (24 October) wins: a separate view with copied slots, 0.05 steps, the recipe in saved files, no fixed slot limit (the 16-slot cap of the earlier 24 October text was removed the same day: only real constraints) and the 0.8-1.2 sum line with Make it 1.
- Ship before API retirement where practical (a preference, not a gate); the retirement notice (domain handover) points the tester to the view and link. Old GUIDs do not carry over.
- UI in the ported sources only; no shared bridge/runtime/worker file. Arithmetic context: `sum(weight_k * W+_k)` over W+ `[1,18,512]`, unnormalised; equals `num_multi` for photo slots (`LatentByMultiLerp`); word/seed slots deliberately differ from the API's Z-space handling. About 0.4 s warm on WebGPU in the tester's diagnostics (one device, not a promise).
- Missing-model consent uses the existing consent modal (`consent.modal`, fm-9kr8); per the 24 October parallelism pass that is a close-time integration check, not a start dependency.
- Anchor: PLAN.md#weighted-face-blend-advanced-mode.
acceptance_criteria:
Operated rule: real pointer/touch at the visible position with `elementFromPoint` returning the control in its region; by-name only for setup; screenshot per case.
- [ ] Unit tests in CI: `#blend` hash routing (enter, reload, Back; Help/footer anchors do not change the hash; Back closes an open picker or crop modal first); first-open seeding copies all latent-capable morph faces at equal weights (also from a 150-face morph row); slots are copies (edits do not cross views); a new slot gets 1/N and others unchanged; Reset gives 1/N; Make it 1 scales proportionally; sum-line shown only outside 0.8-1.2; 0.05 step and 0-1 range; all-zero refusal; weight-0 slots skipped; no slot count refusal; session persistence of slots and weights.
- [ ] Operated run at 1,280 px, and the same run at 390 px where admitted: open via the **Blend faces** button (More options) and via `#blend`; fill three slots (a word, a name, a confirmed photo).
- [ ] Drag weights: no synthesis during drag and exactly one blend synthesis per release or committed keyboard step; a newer change supersedes a pending one; previous result stays visible marked "Updating…" with Share/Save disabled until the new file is ready.
- [ ] Reset gives 1/N; sum shown; the sum line appears outside 0.8-1.2 and operated **Make it 1** brings the sum to 1.
- [ ] Slot counts 1, 2, 3, 8, 16, 40 and 100 at 1,280 px and 390 px: past what fits, the slot panel scrolls inside itself while the result stays in view (result box inside the viewport after scrolling to the last slot); slots use compact rows (thumbnail, field, weight); every slot's weight slider and Remove are hit by `elementFromPoint` at their centres after scrolling; the sum line, Reset and Make it 1 work at 100 slots; one blend synthesis per release at 100 slots; no horizontal page scroll.
- [ ] Reload in the view restores slots and weights; a footer Help link does not leave the view; Back with the names picker open closes only the picker.
- [ ] Missing generator model opens the existing consent modal; an injected failure offers Retry in the result's action area; leaving the view cancels a pending blend synthesis while slot photo encodes continue.
- [ ] Desktop layout keeps the result in view on the right with a 2-4 column slot grid; at phone width the result is pinned at the top with a single-column list; no horizontal page scroll and no clipped control at the sweep widths.
- [ ] Shuffle weights (planned 24 Oct, removable on veto): one button sets random weights adding up to 1; unit test checks sum and 0–1 range; the operated run presses it and sees exactly one regeneration.
- [ ] The blend view is exercised on phone-cpu at least once on a candidate build, with the run summary or screenshot recorded in this bead (blend journey lands via fm-ve73)
notes: Split 2026-10-24: saved blend file and recipe, reopen, Add to morph, batch slot fill and the blend job report moved to fm-gx4y (face.blend-view.output). The recipe input fm-fy2.7 moved with it.

title: Inventory native packaging and updater paths for retirement
description:
## Background
Native desktop packages are retired for this release. title: Contracts milestone 2: numeric ceilings, boundary vectors and validator fuzzing
description:
## Goal

Write the numeric count and byte ceilings that confirmed-crop, batch admission, acquisition consent, the scheduler, the device checker and media export cite, from the decode measurement, as a typed limits file with boundary vectors; and fuzz the validators for untrusted app payloads. Part of contracts milestone 2 (with `contracts.m2`, fm-fy2.2, for UI states, and `contracts.m2.walkthrough`, which closes the milestone); it does not need the UI state module and can proceed in parallel with it.

## Scope

**Numeric ceilings** — `apps/web/src/contracts/ceilings.ts`, `ceilings.vectors.json`, manager `budgets.ts`, engine `MemoryBoundName` table:
- `CEILINGS` with value, unit, route scope and measurement reference: per-route transient decode bounds (from the decode measurement file, kept beside the values), retained source, crop buffer, batch retained-input bytes, morph frame budget (derived per route from measured memory, storage and time; the classic 4,096-frame value stands until measured), stored-session size, a byte-size sanity bound for parsing untrusted project and session files (replacing classic `MaxControls = 64` and the 64-face session-restore check), image-preparation budget, file-encode budget, `PREPARED_FILE_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`; aggregate transfer/read-ahead/hash/write-buffer (`AcquisitionBudget`) and aggregate live-residency (`LiveResidencyLimit`); engine memory bounds.
- No unbounded default. A route with no measurement has no ceiling and is not admitted. Over-budget admission happens before any extra keypoint allocation, with an actionable reduce-selection/remove-retry-input message (no truncation or hidden eviction). Values revise only by contract revision. No face count or blend slot count ceiling (operator, 24 October: only real constraints).
- At-boundary and one-over vectors per ceiling for downstream tests.

**Validator fuzzing.** Runtime validators for app payloads (restored records, recovery metadata, worker messages, and the untrusted project/session files bounded by the byte-size sanity bound above) are fuzzed with a fixed seed and a recorded case count; every rejection is typed (no thrown strings, no silent default). Vector files (ceilings, export identity) validate against their types. Inputs: the decode measurement file from `fm-4cp`, the frozen app batch/progress/scheduler/preflight/export-identity types from `fm-s9n`, the recovery-metadata and descriptor types from `contracts.descriptor`. Strict TS: no broad `any`, unchecked casts or silent defaults; `unknown` validated at runtime.

## Out of scope

The UI state unions and transition tables (`contracts.m2`, fm-fy2.2); the typed flow walkthrough and milestone-2 export closure (`contracts.m2.walkthrough`); implementing admission checks (confirmed-crop, batch, scheduler and acquisition beads enforce these values); new measurements (a route with no measurement simply has no ceiling); model descriptor types (`contracts.descriptor`).

## Notes

- Downstream acceptance criteria that cite a ceiling (confirmed-crop at/over checks, batch admission, acquisition buffers, prepared-file cache bound, frame budget) are written against this bead's values after it merges; until then they report "measured, no threshold".
- Values are implementation contracts to qualify, not browser RSS control claims.
- Split on 2026-10-24 for swarm size into three beads: `contracts.m2` (this ID, fm-fy2.2: UI state unions and transition tables), `contracts.m2.ceilings` (numeric ceilings, vectors, validator fuzzing) and `contracts.m2.walkthrough` (typed flow walkthrough and the milestone-2 export closure, which completes milestone 2).
- Anchors: PLAN.md#external-developer-journey-and-non-face-models, #end-to-end-experience-and-design-fidelity-check, #ui-flow-matrix-and-open-journey-contracts, #supplied-ui-references, #package-and-operation-contracts.

- [x] Validator fuzzing for app payloads (restored records, recovery metadata, worker messages; fixed seed, recorded case count, typed rejection) passes locally with the workspace npm test command; CI verifies after push.

title: Consent, device-check and scheduler journeys asserted from intercepted requests
description:
## Goal
Network-start rules are privacy and cost commitments, and claims like "no model network before approval" must be
asserted from intercepted requests, not screenshots. Device guidance must not block names or eligible actions or fetch
models. Unit-level scheduler proofs do not show that the integrated bridge, manager and media behave together. This
bead runs the consent, device-check and composed-scheduler journeys on the built release artifact with cold, partial
and warm caches; its cases are part of sub-result 2 (platform and resource), collated by `verify.platform`.

## Scope
- **Consent (R01 network part, R15, R16 consent part, R22 refusal part, R24; defects 10, 19):** arrival, static names
  and recovered still open/save: zero model-host requests, no modal. Generate approval and Generate-and-encode
  approval with per-purpose missing bytes and optional photo costs; synthesis prerequisites first, detector promptly,
  encoder overlapped with photo choosing/crop review; seed generation before encoder completion; Cancel before
  approval; Cancel after approval (network/worker submissions stop within the declared bound); Cancel before and after
  crop OK; Escape/backdrop/Back; no late continuation; unknown cache status asks or settles with Retry, never starts
  acquisition; no model prompt for static names or valid cache hits; Cancel setup keeps verified chunks and missing
  assets need re-approval; download/cache/quota failure gives truthful bytes, a bounded explicit Retry and preserved
  completed work; detector refusal abandons only that acquisition and leaves local source access; revised
  material-cost decision; one figure per purpose in one unit, identical in toast, dialog and progress; the fallback
  video codec is inside consent (no 32 MB fetch outside it; unknown size never lets work start). Default modal copy at
  narrow widths keeps irrelevant operation rows and technical breakdowns out of the main decision. Responsive
  foreground work and bounded aggregate transfer buffers; unfinished optional preparation never blocks
  completed-result actions; recovered/static results satisfy requests without inference startup. Progress counts
  overlapping work once in one stable bar for the whole action. Zero requests from warming unless `consent.warming`
  shipped.
- **Cannot-keep case:** a real 1,000 MB browser storage quota (Chromium `Storage.overrideQuotaForOrigin` through CDP, enforced by the browser) with the 1,040 MB CPU package: the
  modal shows the re-download line with the byte figure; after approval, completion and reload, the package bytes are
  requested again and the modal shows the line again.
- **Prepare encoder:** operated Prepare encoder in the source step, approve, encoder requests start before any file is
  chosen; Cancel setup: no new encoder request after the declared bound; closing the source step abandons the
  pre-source owner.
- **Diagnostics events** added by consent are on the collector allowlist and named in the privacy text.
- **Device check (R13; defect 20 estimate-text part):** preflight with zero model-host requests; denied/skipped/
  timed-out checks; unknown calibration; context-specific photo/synthesis estimates; cold/warm overhead;
  material-cost change consent. Budgets: about two seconds of sampling, five-second UI deadline, 16 MiB scratch
  buffers, 100 KiB checker code; skip, timeout and GPU loss yield "no reliable estimate" and consent stays usable.
  Estimates never become admission proof or a phone gate: timing skip cannot bypass admission; viewport width/touch
  hints cannot suppress an eligible route. Prediction error against available paired measurements, uncalibrated
  cells recorded honestly, uncalibrated time fields honest, slow-work WebGPU-computer copy contextual; the cold-device
  estimate text appears when its condition holds.
- **Composed scheduler (R14 route-snapshot part, R35 one intent joins existing operations, R36 progress part):** photo
  then queued Morph; Morph auto-generation then explicit face request; capability loss while queued; Cancel at each
  dependency boundary. Requested route, fallback scope and model identity captured at approval stay with queued work.
  Shared-download ownership; whole-action progress through default file readiness (monotonic, never resets).
  Delay/fail face-file preparation while Morph consumes compute-ready inputs: bounded endpoint reuse, no duplicate
  inference, independent file-preparation Retry. Admission during provider/model loading and idle retained residency
  (idle encoder while generator loading), competing provider-load requests. frame budget (contracts ceilings); selected faces
  never truncated. One heavyweight operation per shared provider context; compute permit separate from residency;
  Morph yields its permit while waiting; completing inference does not imply memory reclaimed (check reservations
  until release).

## Out of scope
Warming (`consent.warming`, optional). Device-estimate calibration campaigns and physical-phone benchmarks.
Concurrency beyond one heavyweight operation. The degradation sweep (`verify.platform`).

## Notes
- Shared-file order (PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", 16 October; "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October): this
  bead adds test scripts only and edits none of `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` or
  `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (under `apps/web/src/Next/`). If it must, first add the ordering edge on
  `morph.guards` (fm-fy2.9) with `br dep add`.
- Prediction-error and estimate-budget thresholds are set in their device beads; until then "measured, no threshold".
  Calibration measurements feed the release summary's platform cells (`verify.join`).
- Capabilities are real (operator, 24 October): browsers launched with WebGPU disabled, real quotas, real devices, real server faults; a case no available browser or device can produce is reported untested, never mocked.
- Integrated verification checks the final integrated app (after the planned UI and package changes) against the Next baseline (`facemorph.me-classic` branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) plus the plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped. Not historic-API parity and not a shutdown-qualification campaign. Performance and reliability against the control, including control/control noise and the physical iPhone, are judged by the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27), not here. Correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found here are fixed in the owning bead and this bead re-runs. Wording says planned, experimental, implemented or deployed. No weights, secrets, photos or typed inputs in Git.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #consented-downloads-useful-overlap-and-cached-model-warming,
  #lightweight-device-check-and-pre-download-guidance, #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts,
  #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance (acquisition consent, device check, operation controller),
  #integrated-verification; defects 10, 19, 20.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Zero model-host requests before approval and after Cancel (within the declared bound); synthesis assets requested before encoder shards; zero warming requests unless warming shipped; each consent scenario above passes with assertions on requests by host class and bytes.
- [ ] Size figures compared across toast, dialog and progress: equal, one unit per purpose; the fallback codec fetch happens only inside consent.
- [ ] Narrow-width screenshots of the default modal.
- [ ] Cannot-keep case (1,000 MB quota, 1,040 MB CPU package) passes as described, including the re-request after reload.
- [ ] Prepare encoder path: encoder requests start before any file is chosen; none after Cancel setup's bound; closing the source step abandons the pre-source owner.
- [ ] Diagnostics events added by consent are listed on the allowlist and in the privacy text.
- [ ] Preflight shows zero model-host requests; skip/timeout/GPU-loss runs show "no reliable estimate" with consent usable; prediction-error table vs paired measurements recorded (or "measured, no threshold").
- [ ] Operation traces compared against expected traces for each composed scheduler case; no duplicate inference for a joined slot/revision; progress values monotonic in every run.
- [ ] Every UI step is operated through the `verify.harness` (fm-48bj) helpers: real pointer/touch at the control's visible position with an `elementFromPoint` assertion that the hit element is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role locators only for setup; phone-width and desktop-width screenshot per case.
- [ ] Every network or consent claim is asserted from intercepted requests by host class and bytes (the request-interception helper from `build.ci-site`, fm-aa8), never from a screenshot; traces and screenshots are kept on failure as privacy-filtered CI artifacts.
- [ ] Every case is listed in this bead's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix rows or defect numbers it grades; a case without a mapping fails manifest validation.
- [ ] All cases ran in the release-verification workflow against the named release artifact digest; a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded `failed` or `untested`, never `passed`.

title: Add per-slot Cancel/Retry, bounded encode queue and retry-pixel lifetime for confirmed batches
description:
## Background
After batch OK each slot holds a frozen confirmed crop and input revision. Contracts freeze per-slot Cancel, modal
Cancel as pre-commit batch cancellation, Retry as one existing slot with a new attempt ID, and reference-counted
pending/running/retryable pixel ownership.

## Why
PLAN.md#face-controls-and-modals lists these exact tests; slots must fail and recover independently.

## Scope
- Drive the bounded serial encode queue that `crop.batch-encode` (fm-gfut) provides (initially one e4e at a time);
  each crop's request/attempt identity, progress and result are shown in its own tile; a common acquisition/preparation
  prefix belongs to each slot's whole-action progress (from `opctl.progress`).
- Each queued/running tile shows its own Cancel in the face slot; no implicit batch-wide Cancel; queued siblings
  continue in frozen order; completed faces survive.
- Retry resumes only that slot with its frozen crop and a new attempt ID appended to the pending queue; Remove deletes
  only that slot; neither reopens crop nor allocates keypoints.
- Pixel ownership is implemented by fm-gfut (reference-counted tab-only source or immutable derived crop; success
  releases retry input; failed/cancelled keep only the minimum for Retry; Remove/replace/disposal release; a shared
  source is freed when no owner remains; never persisted to OPFS or session storage). This bead wires the tile actions
  (Remove, replace, Retry, app disposal) to those release calls and proves the lifetimes through the built UI. Lost
  pixels after reload -> the tile shows the Encode image entry, never Retry.
- Changing/removing a slot after OK invalidates only that slot's work and late results.

## Out of scope
Mixed recovered candidates; morph scheduling; the queue, attempt identities and reference counting themselves
(`crop.batch-encode`, fm-gfut).

## Boundary with `crop.batch-encode` (fm-gfut) (polish r2)
- **fm-gfut owns** the bridge-level encode path: the ordered list of frozen `ConfirmedCrop` records, bounded serial
  e4e, attempt IDs, pixel reference counting and the no-persistence rule, with its own unit/integration tests
  (`crop-queue.*`).
- **This bead owns** the tiles: per-slot Cancel/Retry controls in each tile's image-area action slot, per-slot status
  and progress rendering, the Encode image entry after a reload, focus and keyboard behaviour, and the operated built-UI
  acceptance below. It calls fm-gfut's queue and never reimplements it; it adds no second queue or ref-count.
- Shared tests are not duplicated: this bead's acceptance asserts the UI-visible effects (event-log order, ref counts
  read from fm-gfut's instrumentation, storage scan) on the built app.

## Considerations
Byte ceilings from contracts milestone 2 (phase2-numeric: report "measured, no threshold" until then).
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files**: the bridge-level queue is fm-gfut's (confirmed-crop position in the order); this bead is tile UI over it. It is ordered after the morph pipeline through fm-3peb. If it must edit one of the files, it adds the edge and conflict-list row first.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Operated-UI rule: each acceptance step acts with real pointer input (touch tap at phone widths) at the control's visible position, asserts `document.elementFromPoint` at that point returns the control (or a descendant) and that the point lies inside the region a person would look in (named per control below); by-name/by-role clicks are used only to set up state, never as the acceptance step.
- [ ] Every case is checked at a phone width (390 px) and a desktop width (1,280 px) with one screenshot per case kept as evidence.
- [ ] Cancel the first running face while later selections are queued: only that slot stops, siblings continue in order, completed faces survive (event log order asserted).
- [ ] Cancel a queued face: it never starts; others unaffected.
- [ ] Retry appends one existing slot without reallocating keypoints (keypoint IDs unchanged; no duplicate IDs).
- [ ] Cancel every slot, wait for all jobs to settle, retry one: no file reimport, no crop reopen.
- [ ] Mixed per-face failures (inject failure in slot 2 of 3) leave slots 1 and 3 complete.
- [ ] Pixel lifetime: instrumented ref counts reach zero after success, Remove, replacement and disposal; storage scan shows no source/crop in OPFS/sessionStorage; at and over the contract ceilings the admission refuses with the actionable message (phase2-numeric).
- [ ] Reload with a failed slot: Retry is replaced by the Encode image entry.
- [ ] Every new diagnostics event this item adds is listed with its allowlist entry and privacy-policy entry (the diagnostics consent control's event registry) before acceptance; no photos, latents, typed input or raw error strings.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic run in CI (`npm test` workspace target) and pass.
- [ ] Each end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Every network claim is asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Controls and regions: per-slot Cancel and Retry render in each tile's image-area action slot (inside the face image box); exercised with 1, 2, 3 and 8 confirmed slots, with `elementFromPoint` at each control centre returning that slot's control.
- [ ] Boundary check: the built app has one encode queue and one pixel ref-count implementation (fm-gfut's); a source scan finds no second queue or ref-count in the tile code, and the tile actions call fm-gfut's release functions (spies on Remove, replace, Retry and disposal).

title: Carry over the iOS Simulator product lanes (artifact and simulator jobs)
description:
## Background

Classic `mobile-browser.yml` jobs `ios-product-artifact` (Ubuntu 22.04 artifact build) and
`ios-product-simulator` (macOS 15, iPhone 16 Pro Simulator): product CPU face generation with real
inference, acquisition/admission, rendered bounds and resource checks. The current product build
shares source with the promoted bytes but is a rebuild, so its digest differs. Split out of
`build.ci-mobile-ios-lane` (fm-hlv) in polish round 2; fm-hlv keeps the `ios` component job.

## Why

This is the only retained lane that runs real inference on an iOS browser engine. Simulator results
are not physical-iPhone evidence, but losing the lane would leave no iOS product check at all.

## Scope

- Jobs in `.github/workflows/mobile-browser.yml`, IDs kept:
  - `ios-product-artifact` (`ubuntu-22.04`, any runner change recorded in the check-migration map):
    until `build.artifact-fanout` lands, builds the artifact under test and uploads
    `next-ios-artifact-<run_id>`; the receipt records "rebuilt, digest X" against the canonical
    digest. After fan-out it fetches and verifies the canonical `next-site-<sha>` through
    `.github/actions/fetch-artifact` instead (that switch is fan-out's acceptance).
  - `ios-product-simulator` (`macos-15`, 45-minute timeout): `python3 scripts/next-ios-sim.py
    --device 'iPhone 16 Pro' --evidence next-ios-evidence`, artifact `next-ios-simulator-<run_id>`,
    event log through `scripts/evidence/cdp_capture.py` or the Simulator's Web Inspector bridge;
    where Safari cannot report a field (cache hits, worker requests), the header lists it in
    `capture_limits` and claims on it are `untested`.
- Pass thresholds: product CPU face generated with real inference events; acquisition/admission
  checks pass; rendered bounds inside the viewport; resource checks pass; timings recorded as
  Simulator evidence only (retained reference: first full-1024 face 25287 ms, warm synthesis
  4741.2 ms on iOS 18.5 — a comparison point, not a limit).
- Triggers and path filters from `scripts/ci/path-filters.json` (`build.ci-artifact-lookup`), same as
  the `ios` job. Results are never labelled physical-iPhone evidence.

## Out of scope

The `ios` component job (fm-hlv). Physical-iPhone qualification.

## Considerations

- Record rebuild vs reuse in every receipt until fan-out; never present a rebuilt digest as the
  canonical one.
- Hosted macOS minutes are kept because they provide an otherwise unavailable environment; the job
  keeps classic's triggers and does not add new schedules.

A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Drive the control through every flow-matrix row and classify each row
description:
## Background
The plan's user-journey table (about 50 rows: first visit, return with retained work, phone/CPU route, words, seeds incl. zero and 0..4,294,967,295, Retry unchanged input, edit/remove queued tile, names open/pick/edit/close, device timing, CPU/WebGPU selection, consent approve/refuse, quota failure, photo replace/paste/drop/multi-file, crop confirm/adjust/no-face, add/remove, many faces, Undo/Start over, keyboard-only, identical neighbours, reload after morph, offline with cache, morph unfinished inputs, morph settings/cancel/retry, play/slider, Save/Share/rename/format, reopen still, report error, debug On/Off, remove down to one face, `?testing` bulk Generate, desktop-package link) mixes behaviour the control has with behaviour the plan adds. The 18 October operated check and candidate audit found defects 1-23 (Remove unclickable, >2 faces do not fit, no reset, Tab skips mode menu/names/file picker, autocapitalize, identical neighbours error, Add disabled at one face, wrong empty-tile hint, words lost on reload, inconsistent sizes, per-keystroke requests, report label, collector action list, names contrast, offline failure, stacked toasts, stale completions, 64-cap, consent gaps, typos, unlinked licence page, storage, preview badge).

## Why
Only rows that are present and unchanged gate the port. Without this freeze the port either copies defects or drifts without trace.

## Scope
- Drive the verified control artifact through every journey row (and the cold-model / model-cached / output-cached, narrow/intermediate/wide, keyboard/touch, unsupported/unknown capability, offline and changed-input variants where exercisable).
- Classify each row: **present and unchanged** (parity-graded), **present and changed by a declared UX change** (graded against the plan's specification after parity, citing the live requirement section: UI requirements table, flow matrix, known candidate defects, kept current by the inventory's defect ledger), or **absent** (new, specification-graded). Each candidate defect 1-23 is a **repair** row with its named owner, never parity.
- Commit the table keyed by journey, with the Playwright steps and a screenshot for each parity row. A row that cannot be exercised against the control is recorded untested, never passed.

## Out of scope
Fixing defects (owners: face controls, morph pipeline, media and recovery, acquisition consent, static names, diagnostics control, operation controller, provider Help).

## Considerations
Phase 2: the numeric/row-level parity acceptance of `ws:migration.parity` is set from this table. Steps that act on controls use real pointer/touch input (defect 1 shows by-name clicks hide unusable controls).

## Output format for downstream leaves (polish r1)
The machine-readable table `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/flow-matrix-freeze.json` has one record per journey row: `rowId` (stable slug, used as the golden directory name), plan row text, class (`parity` | `declared:<plan section>` | `absent` | `repair:<defect #>`), owner (workstream key) for non-parity rows, variants exercised, Playwright step file, screenshot paths (phone 390 px and desktop 1,280 px), control digest and `untested` reason where applicable. Each controller/rendering leaf names the rows it replays from this file; `migration.parity-run` reads its parity row list from it and `verify.flows-matrix` grades the rest against the plan specification.
Known declared-change rows to classify, not parity: WebGL entry in the Advanced selector (provider simplification), selector position above the first + (face controls `face.provider-selector`), names search/header/Show more (static names), Morph auto-generation of unfinished inputs (operation controller), bounded consent grant and copy (acquisition consent), native desktop links (provider simplification).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Committed table (e.g. `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/flow-matrix-freeze.md` + machine-readable JSON) has one entry per journey row with class, owner for non-parity rows, Playwright step file and screenshot for parity rows.
- [ ] Defects 1-23 each appear as a repair row with owner; none is classed parity.
- [ ] Untestable rows listed as untested with reason.
- [ ] UI acceptance is operated: real pointer/touch input at each control's visible position plus an `elementFromPoint` check that the element there is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role clicks only for setup; repeating controls exercised at 0 or 1, 2, 3, many and the cap; text inputs with empty, very long and pasted values; phone-width and desktop-width screenshot per case.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, and the log is retained as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics). Network claims are asserted from the log, never from screenshots.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/migration/flow-matrix-freeze.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Sub-result 1 (app flows): cancel/recovery, mixed batch, diagnostics, residual rows
description:
## Goal
Sub-result 1 of integrated verification: app flows. Cancellation, recovery and stale-result rejection are retained
candidate strengths and known defect areas; the mixed recovered-still/photo batch is a planned extension whose commit
mechanics need an integrated check; diagnostics behaviour is a declared UI change whose privacy claims need request
evidence; and some rows (keyboard-only, names modal, first visit, one-string defects) are covered by no other bead.
This bead runs those cases on the release artifact and emits the sub-result 1 output that combines its cases with
`verify.functional`'s, which the release summary (`verify.join`) reads.

## Scope
- **Cancel, retry, stale completion, recovery (R02, R06, R07, R17, R25, R33, R36, R43, R44; defects 9, 17):**
  cancel/fail text/seed generation, then Retry the unchanged revision without editing; edit/change mode/remove a
  queued or running tile: only that tile superseded, siblings preserved, late results rejected, Cancelling shown until
  settlement; cancel/retry one confirmed photo encode in the same slot without recrop or duplicate keypoints; Morph
  cancel at each boundary, partial animation never exported as complete, completed faces survive Morph failure;
  background/reload/close during unfinished work: truthful interruption, completed records retained, lost photo retry
  pixels after reload need source selection again; return with completed work: display/play/save without
  regeneration, late restore after user edits rejected, reload after morph restores faces and result (words restored
  if the defect-9 proposal ships, else `not-applicable-by-decision`); missing/damaged/incompatible still: no silent
  fresh encoding, explicit use-as-photo, model mismatch keeps media viewable/saveable with compute disabled,
  unsupported video reported without replacing work; export-only Retry after file-preparation failure keeps pixels
  visible. Replacement commit points (R17): replacing a face with a photo keeps the previous target through a
  cancelled picker, a cancelled crop and a rejected recovery; a failed replacement may leave a retryable or empty
  target while unrelated completed panels stay; the old face is never saved under a newly selected name; a late result
  never lands in a newer target. Morph settings (R36) snapshotted at start, duplicate starts disabled while one runs,
  Cancel and Retry keep completed faces, progress never goes backwards. Defect 17 cases (remove while generating,
  saved-MP4 drop leaving Morph queued or replacing every face without asking, photo replace destroying the face
  before the new photo is checked, cancelled queued re-generate leaving a broken image) each as a stale-completion
  case.
- **Mixed batch (R19, R23; defect 18):** drop/select several files containing several faces and recovery-bearing
  stills; select faces across files with one global click order. Before Cancel and OK: exact click order kept, ordered
  badges, Adjust Crop edits the focused candidate only. Cancel: no partial import. OK: atomic insertion in click order
  replacing the originating panel; unrelated panels untouched. Recovered stills enter without recovery re-encoding (no
  e4e request); per-slot error ownership and per-slot cancel/retry; slot/pixel budgets checked before insertion; batch
  pixel and frame limits have separate messages. No fixed face count (operator, 24 October; defect 18): all six entry
  paths (insertion "+", Add face, multi-file drop, batch OK, paste into a new face, background drop) go through
  one admission check against real budgets (retained photo-input bytes and stored-session size from the contracts ceilings, `apps/web/src/contracts/ceilings.ts`); a refusal names the limit reached in one plain
  message, identical on every path, with the existing reduce-selection option; no partial insertion, never silent
  truncation. A many-face morph over the frame budget gets the over-budget reason with the estimate before frame
  inference, so the generic project error never appears. Runs at 1, 2, 3 and many (30, 64, 150) selections and at
  each real budget's boundary.
- **Diagnostics (R31 no per-keystroke requests, R45, R48; defects 11, 12, 13, 16):** one-shot report stays one-shot and
  its label says so; standing opt-in explicit; Off-state report toast remains; no redundant opt-in toast while On.
  `Debug reports: Off/On` disclosure after Help/FAQ at `#debug-reporting`; FAQ/footer "Privacy & reports" links expand
  it and focus the checkbox. On/Off persists across reload; withdrawal aborts/discards unsent reports; persistence
  failure disclosed as tab-only. Typing sends nothing per keystroke; every outside request is named in the privacy
  text, as is what a saved file contains. Client and collector action lists agree (shared-list test against the
  deployed collector config). Only one prompt at a time and none covers an action. A forced failure at each typed
  stage (corrupt photo, refused route, storage full, broken download) yields the matching cause and stage; a scan
  finds no `unknown` without a counted defect.
- **Usage statistics (`diag.usage-stats`, fm-5yqq):** the **Usage statistics** switch beside the disclosure turns
  `/stats/v1` beacons off at once and the choice survives reload; GPC, Do Not Track and Save-Data keep it off; beacons go
  only to the same origin and hold only the closed vocabulary with `b: "monorepo"`; the privacy text and Help name
  what is counted. Graded under R48 and defect 11.
- **Keyboard-only (R29, defect 4):** every journey in the functional, result, cancel/recovery and mixed-batch sets by
  keyboard alone: every control reachable by Tab in visual order (focus order compared with element boxes), focus
  always visible, focus returned to the opener after every dialog (names, crop confirm, crop editor, consent, Undo
  notice), Enter activates Generate or Retry without duplicating an active job, IME composition does not trigger
  Generate, removed buttons leave no hidden focus targets.
- **Names modal (R12, defect 14):** open from each face's menu at counts 1, 2, 3, many; floating Back (touch) and Escape
  return to the same panel with work preserved; browser Back closes the modal without leaving the app; bounded scroll
  position restored on reopen; a stale selection after the face changed is rejected; name labels reach 4.5:1 contrast
  against their scrim or shadow on light and dark faces, measured from rendered pixels; a failed name list shows its
  error and Retry inside the dialog.
- **First visit (R01, defect 16):** cold profile; usable inputs and names; no model prompt and no model-host request on
  arrival; the initial preview is display-only (Generate prepares it, Morph may generate its unfinished text, Save
  waits for a verified current result, preview pixels are never a valid input); at most one prompt and none covering
  an action at 390 px and 1,280x800.
- **Defect 20:** no message with a missing space ("about 1 second", "smaller than 25 MB" and the other two); seed
  placeholder corrected; disabled Create morph visibly disabled (contrast and `aria-disabled` consistent); crop panel
  opaque in light mode. (Cold-device estimate text is checked in `verify.consent-device`.)
- **Defect 21:** the licence and notices page is linked from Help and the footer by operated clicks and states
  truthfully where the video codec is served from.
- **Defect 22 (planner proposal, removable):** if shipped, the Help line shows the stored size, Clear removes stored
  data (storage estimate before/after) and the faces store stays within its ceiling at 150 faces; if vetoed,
  `not-applicable-by-decision` citing the PLAN.md decision row.
- **Defect 23 (decided):** preview faces carry no badge and keep their screen-reader label.
- **Sub-result 1 output:** a machine-readable result (CI artifact of the release-verification workflow) naming the
  source commit and artifact digest, covering this bead's and `verify.functional`'s cases, every cell in the closed
  outcome set, `measured, no threshold` cells listed separately.

## Out of scope
Whole-project transactions and elaborate rollback (accepted limit; old-face rollback desirable, not mandatory).
External MP4 project opening. File-first sorting and direct face reordering. Collector retention and old-report
deletion (`diag.learnings`). Analytics policy changes. Changing the names picker design. Grading the full matrix
(`verify.join`).

## Notes
- Commit points are accepted behaviour for replacement.
- Integrated verification checks the final integrated app (after the planned UI and package changes) against the Next baseline (`facemorph.me-classic` branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) plus the plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped. Not historic-API parity and not a shutdown-qualification campaign. Performance and reliability against the control, including control/control noise and the physical iPhone, are judged by the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27), not here. Correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found here are fixed in the owning bead and this bead re-runs. Wording says planned, experimental, implemented or deployed. No weights, secrets, photos or typed inputs in Git.
- 24 October cut: the five sub-result/leaf receipts become one CI-generated sub-result output; the event-log field
  convention is dropped, the request assertions stay.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #integrated-verification (structure item 1, mixed batch paragraph),
  #ui-flow-matrix-and-open-journey-contracts, #debug-reporting-control-and-consent,
  #gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design,
  #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026 (defects 4, 9, 11-14, 16-18, 20-23).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Cancel/recovery cases scripted; requests show no inference after cancellation settles and no late result applied; each defect-17 case has a named passing case or a recorded failure.
- [ ] Mixed batch at 1, 2, 3 and many (30, 64, 150 faces) selections; no e4e request for recovered stills; each of the six entry paths adds a 65th and a 151st face; each path pushed one over a real budget (photo-input bytes; stored-session size) shows the same message text naming that limit and the face count is unchanged afterwards; a many-face morph over the frame budget shows the over-budget reason with zero inference, never the generic project error.
- [ ] A typing session shows zero requests per keystroke and only hosts listed in the privacy text; report sends show one-shot vs standing behaviour as labelled; the forced-failure run produces typed causes for every listed stage.
- [ ] Usage statistics: after operated Off no `/stats/v1` request in the session (intercepted) and the choice survives reload; with GPC set none is sent; an On session's beacon bodies hold only the closed vocabulary.
- [ ] Keyboard-only run exists for every journey in the functional, result, cancel/recovery and mixed-batch sets, with focus-order vs visual-order comparison and focus-return checks after each dialog.
- [ ] Names modal: Back, Escape and browser Back return to the same panel with work preserved; measured label contrast >= 4.5:1 on light and dark faces; a forced name-list failure shows its error and Retry inside the dialog.
- [ ] First visit: zero model-host requests on arrival; at most one prompt visible and none covering an action at 390 px and 1,280x800.
- [ ] Defects 20, 21, 22 and 23 each have an operated case with screenshots, or `not-applicable-by-decision` with the decision link (22 only).
- [ ] Repeating controls exercised at 0/1, 2, 3, many and, where a real budget exists, at that budget and its degraded state; text inputs empty, very long and pasted.
- [ ] The sub-result 1 output names the same source commit and artifact digest as the release identity record, uses only the closed outcome set and lists `measured, no threshold` cells separately.
- [ ] Every UI step is operated through the `verify.harness` (fm-48bj) helpers: real pointer/touch at the control's visible position with an `elementFromPoint` assertion that the hit element is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role locators only for setup; phone-width and desktop-width screenshot per case.
- [ ] Every network or consent claim is asserted from intercepted requests by host class and bytes (the request-interception helper from `build.ci-site`, fm-aa8), never from a screenshot; traces and screenshots are kept on failure as privacy-filtered CI artifacts.
- [ ] Every case is listed in this bead's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix rows or defect numbers it grades; a case without a mapping fails manifest validation.
- [ ] All cases ran in the release-verification workflow against the named release artifact digest; a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded `failed` or `untested`, never `passed`.

title: Verify result journeys: play/scrub, Share/Save/format/filename, repeat save and reopen
description:
## Background
The candidate's `next-e2e.yml` real-ui-cpu job covers playable and saved MP4 and face/video/slider restore. The
final app adds Share/Save with a compact format choice and an editable filename below each result (face controls
render; media and recovery implement export identity, filenames, collisions and the prepared-file cache by revision
and format). Split out of `verify.flows-functional` in polish round 1 so each leaf stays one coherent verification.
Numerical synthesis, export quality and exact recovery values are graded in `verify.flows-synthesis-export`; this
leaf grades the operated result journeys.

## Why
Result handling is where a person keeps their work; rows R37-R42 need operated evidence on the release artifact.

## Scope
Operate on the release artifact with real models (results produced through the UI):
- **Play/scrub (R37):** play the morph, switch to the slider, scrub; when scrub frames are absent the video stays
  playable and nothing regenerates.
- **Save (R38):** face WebP and PNG, morph MP4; the saved file's MIME type, extension and dimensions match what was
  chosen; when PNG fallback happens the MIME type and extension update.
- **Share (R39):** user-gesture share where the browser supports file sharing; a cancelled share keeps the prepared
  file and Save still works; without file-share capability Save is the primary action; an actual share failure falls
  back to saving the same file.
- **Repeat, rename, format, reload (R40):** repeat Save reuses the prepared bytes (same prepared-file identity, latency
  recorded); changing format prepares only that format; filenames are distinct and never overwrite (two faces with the
  same word, two saves of one face); editing the filename stays in the result action area; after reload, restored
  labels use the opened filename or a generic safe label when the original text is unavailable.
- **Reopen (R41):** open schema-1 PNG and schema-2 PNG/WebP stills from each face's file/menu entry without models
  (request log: zero model-host requests, no inference start); the latent restores without photo encoding; a
  model-mismatched still stays viewable and saveable with compute disabled.
- **External MP4 project open (R42):** deferred by the operator. Record `deferred`; check that MP4 metadata is
  readable through the internal readers and that same-origin session playback works.
- Counts: Save/Share exercised with 1, 2, 3, many faces and at the 64 cap; filenames empty, very long and pasted.

## Out of scope
Pixel/latent tolerances and export quality policy (synthesis-export). External MP4 project-open UI.

## Considerations
- Inspect the decoded full-size output and the rendered result box (all four corners), not only intrinsic sizes.
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each of R37-R42 has scripted operated cases; R42 recorded `deferred` with the internal-reader and session-playback check attached.
- [ ] Repeat Save shows the same prepared-file identity and records latency; a format change prepares only that format; no two saved files share a name.
- [ ] Reopen log shows zero model-host requests and no inference start; a model-mismatched still stays viewable and saveable with compute disabled.
- [ ] Cancelled share keeps the file and Save works afterwards; without share capability Save is primary.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome) through the shared emitter from `build.event-log-core` (fm-bd03) and passes `scripts/check-event-log.ts`; the log is kept as a CI artifact, privacy-filtered like diagnostics; screenshots kept on failure.
- [ ] Each case is listed in this leaf's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix row IDs or defect numbers it grades.
- [ ] UI steps are operated: real pointer/touch at the control's visible position with an `elementFromPoint` assertion that the hit element is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role clicks only for setup; repeating controls at 0/1, 2, 3, many and the cap; text inputs empty, very long and pasted; phone-width and desktop-width screenshot per case.
- [ ] Ran against the named release-candidate artifact digest (the same digest the join report checks); a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded failed or untested, never passed.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Make morph geometry descriptor-driven
description:
## Background
`geometry/latent-path.mjs` (`latent-path-v1`) accepts only Z/W `[512]` (rotating halves J(a,b)=(-b,a)) and W+ `[18,512]` (same rotation independently per layer, no layer mixing); other shapes are rejected. The external developer journey removes FFHQ's fixed 18 x 512 assumption from generic morph code.

## Why
Non-face checkpoints with other layer counts/latent sizes must morph through the same geometry with recorded algorithm version, or fail with an actionable error.

## Scope
- Geometry reads latent space/shape from the descriptor (any even width, any layer count the descriptor declares) with the same per-layer rotation rules; reject unsupported shapes with an actionable error.
- Keep `GEOMETRY_VERSION` semantics: never replace an imported version; unknown algorithms rejected; bump the version only if outputs change for existing shapes (they must not).
- Check with a qualified caller-loaded reference at a different output resolution/layer count.
- Existing `geometry/verify.mjs` checks keep passing for FFHQ shapes.

## Out of scope
Mapping/synthesis generalization (compute). Recovery schema (media).

## Considerations
- All five shape modes must survive unchanged for FFHQ.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.

- [ ] FFHQ geometry outputs byte-identical to `latent-path-v1` on the verify suite.
- [ ] Non-FFHQ descriptor produces valid paths for all modes; morph of that reference model renders and passes its own declared synthesis tolerance.
- [ ] Unsupported shapes rejected with typed actionable errors (unit tests).
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes: This leaf (morph.descriptor-geometry) is outside the shared-file sequence and must not edit the three shared files. Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. title: Add versioned overlap and warming adapters with explicit grants and timelines
description:
## Background

The existing auto-consent/file-injection driver cannot establish native chooser latency. Verified-cache warming (optional) ships only if a targeted round shows a foreground-safe benefit, and needs these adapters.

## Why

The overlap and warming campaigns need instrumentation that models consent and ownership honestly.

## Scope

- Adapters modelling the explicit bundle grant, ownership/request/attempt IDs, approved transfer timeline,
  stage timelines and independent confirmation; zero-speculative-network assertions from the event log.
- Built against the contract types; exercised against the app once acquisition consent exists.

## Out of scope

Running the campaigns.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.

  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;

- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
