title: Extract chunk staging and manifests; check Cloudflare limits
description:
## Goal
Extract the core reusable capability of `packages/cloudflare-model-host`: chunk staging, manifest generation, publication tooling and reconstruction verification, per the contracts milestone 1 host/converter manifest contract, and verify Cloudflare limits and cost against the exact artifacts so production publication never silently enables paid services. "Free" is a target to verify against actual asset sizes and service tier (CPU package about 1,040 MB, photo package, catalogue).

## Scope
- Chunking and manifest generation per contract (host/converter manifest compatibility; metadata schema/version rejection).
- Publication tooling, dry-run by default; publishes only with an explicit `--publish` and target.
- Reconstruction verification of every chunk against its declared asset digest; runtime pins; parity between qualified and published bytes.
- Tooling language per owner: Python tooling may remain inside the package, with an npm entry point as decided.
- Starting classic sources: `hosting/next-static/{stage.py,restage-runtime.py,mirror-runtime.py,promote.py,webgpu_contract.py}`, `hosting/next/prepare-runtime.py`, `src/Next/browser/stage-assets.py`, photo-runtime staging. Existing staging/promotion scripts are not moved wholesale; application promotion policy stays out of the package (deploy workstream).
- No weights in the package tarball; private source provenance never in published manifests.
- Pack content scan: the shared script `scripts/packages/check-tarball-contents.mjs` (test ID `package-tarball-content-scan`), rules as in `pkgdocs.release`: weights/extensions/size limits, repository-only paths, secret patterns, private hostnames, required files, a self-test with planted violations, and a JSON report. `compute.package-surface` creates it; if this bead lands first it creates the script with exactly those rules and `compute.package-surface` reuses it unchanged. Run it on the packed `cloudflare-model-host` tarball, adding the package rule that no private source provenance appears in published manifests.
- Limits and cost: state the chosen Cloudflare product/tier, total bytes and file count, per-file/chunk limits, request routing, storage/request/bandwidth allowances and the date of the limit documentation read, in the package hosting docs; check the actual staged artifact sizes against the per-file/chunk limits; validate model/source terms before publishing.

## Out of scope
- Serving headers, the mirror Worker and release consistency (`hosting.serving`).
- Purchasing.

## Notes
- If the qualified artifacts cannot meet the free tier, the limits table states the paid product, tier and expected monthly cost, the publication tooling refuses to enable a paid service unless the target configuration names it explicitly, and the figure goes into the delivery inventory read at the cutover decision; no work here waits for a decision (operator, 24 October: only the live cutover pushes need the operator).
- The classic server downloads upstream author weights; the browser chunk origin need not replace authors' download URLs.

title: Cross-file batch with ordered insertion and per-slot Cancel/Retry
description:
## Goal
Let a person pick faces from several files in one bounded batch proposal, in one global click order, and insert them atomically in that order; then let each confirmed slot encode, fail, cancel and retry independently. The candidate allocates one slot per dropped file and `selectPhoto` admits one source at a time, so a sequence like A1 -> B2 -> A2 is impossible. Ordered multi-selection across files is a settled operator extension (12 October).

## Scope
- **Proposal.** One bounded batch proposal with candidates from all supplied files, in the crop modal/grid visual language with minimal source grouping. A sole photo candidate keeps the single-crop default; multi-candidate starts empty and OK requires a choice (disabled at zero, with the reason exposed to screen readers).
- Accessible ordered selection badges; one global click sequence (not file, detector or completion order); deselect removes, reselect appends. The focused/last-selected candidate is identified. Each selected photo candidate has a proposed adjustable crop (face.crop-editor).
- A bad file is identified and can be omitted (omit control beside that file's group label) without shifting the target or losing valid selections.
- **OK.** Check source/target revision; reserve slot/pixel budget once (over budget -> actionable reduce-selection message, never truncation or hidden eviction); atomically assign the first selection to the originating keypoint and insert the rest immediately after it in order, keeping unrelated panels. No keypoints exist before OK. There is no face count limit (operator, 24 October): the slot/pixel budget reservation is the admission check, and its refusal names the limit reached.
- Before OK a changed/removed target invalidates the whole proposal; modal Cancel discards it.
- Single-input limits stay (`src/Next/photo/crop.mjs`: 64 MiB compressed, 120 x 1024² pixels, 20,000 px edge). Batch/revision/cancel/retry types and numeric source/crop/decode byte ceilings come from contracts milestone 2; until then at/over-boundary tests report "measured, no threshold".
- **After OK.** Each slot holds a frozen confirmed crop and input revision. Drive the bounded serial encode queue the crop workstream provides (initially one e4e at a time); each crop's request/attempt identity, progress and result show in its own tile; a common acquisition/preparation prefix belongs to each slot's whole-action progress.
- Each queued/running tile shows its own Cancel in the inline action slot beside the textbox; no implicit batch-wide Cancel; queued siblings continue in frozen order; completed faces survive. Modal Cancel is pre-commit batch cancellation.
- Retry resumes only that slot with its frozen crop and a new attempt ID appended to the pending queue; Remove deletes only that slot; neither reopens crop nor allocates keypoints. Changing/removing a slot after OK invalidates only that slot's work and late results.
- **Pixel lifetime.** Wire tile actions (Remove, replace, Retry, app disposal) to the crop queue's reference-counted release calls: success releases retry input; failed/cancelled keep only the minimum for Retry; a shared source is freed when no owner remains; never persisted to OPFS or session storage. Lost pixels after reload -> the tile shows the Encode image entry, never Retry.
- Any new diagnostics event gets its allowlist and privacy-policy entry; no photos, latents, typed input or raw error strings.

## Out of scope
Recovered candidates (face.mixed-batch); morph scheduling; the queue, attempt identities and reference counting themselves (crop workstream); post-insertion reorder UI (operator: no face reordering).

## Notes
- **Shared files.** Batch admission replaces the candidate's one-source `selectPhoto` composition in `photo-selection.mjs` and the bridge's photo entry, so this bead edits `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` and follows the morph pipeline (mandatory edge).
- **Boundary with the crop batch-encode bead**: it owns the bridge-level ordered list of frozen `ConfirmedCrop` records, bounded serial e4e, attempt IDs, pixel ref counting and the no-persistence rule with its own `crop-queue.*` tests. This bead owns tiles: controls, status/progress rendering, Encode image entry after reload, focus/keyboard and the operated built-UI acceptance. It adds no second queue or ref count.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#confirmed-crop-and-ordered-multi-selection-flow, #gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design (nested photo batches), #face-controls-and-modals, #package-and-operation-contracts.
acceptance_criteria:
Operated rule: real pointer/touch at the visible position with `elementFromPoint` returning the control in its region (badged candidate tiles in the proposal grid, OK footer right, CANCEL footer left, omit beside the group label, per-slot Cancel/Retry inside the face image box); by-name only for setup; 390 px and 1,280 px, screenshot per case.
- [ ] A1, B2, A2 across two files, omit a corrupt third file, OK: face-row order A1 (originating panel), B2, A2; unrelated panels unchanged (controller state and rendered order).
- [ ] Deselect/reselect: A1, B2, deselect A1, reselect A1 -> B2, A1.
- [ ] Zero selections: OK disabled with the reason exposed to screen readers.
- [ ] Click-order invariance: reversed file order and delayed detector completion give the same insertion order.
- [ ] Target removed while the proposal is open: proposal invalidated, no keypoints.
- [ ] Candidate counts 0, 1, 2, 3 and 12 across 3 files; selections taking the face row to 65 and to 150 faces are accepted when within the byte budgets (no count refusal).
- [ ] Budget at and one over the contract ceiling: reduce-selection message, no partial insertion ("measured, no threshold" until contracts milestone 2).
- [ ] Cancel the first running face while later ones are queued: only that slot stops, siblings continue in order, completed faces survive (event order).
- [ ] Cancel a queued face: it never starts; others unaffected.
- [ ] Retry appends one existing slot; keypoint IDs unchanged, no duplicates.
- [ ] Cancel every slot, let all settle, retry one: no file reimport, no crop reopen.
- [ ] Injected failure in slot 2 of 3 leaves slots 1 and 3 complete.
- [ ] Per-slot controls exercised with 1, 2, 3 and 8 confirmed slots; `elementFromPoint` at each centre returns that slot's control.
- [ ] Pixel lifetime: ref counts (crop queue instrumentation) reach zero after success, Remove, replacement and disposal; storage scan finds no source/crop in OPFS/sessionStorage; admission refuses at/over ceilings with the actionable message.
- [ ] Reload with a failed slot: Encode image entry replaces Retry.
- [ ] Boundary: source scan finds no second queue or ref count in tile code; spies show Remove, replace, Retry and disposal call the crop queue's release functions.
- [ ] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test`) and pass.
notes: 26 October operator reconfirmed multi-image/multi-face flow. Preserve global cross-file selection click order and atomic insertion after confirmation; the direct card chooser/inline Generate correction does not waive this acceptance. Current serial Photos queue and single-face DetectedDialog are partial predecessor behavior, not batch completion.

title: Clean consumers of the packed packages, and converter output in manager and engine
description:
## Goal
A package that only works through workspace aliases is not independently usable, and converted chunks, manifests and
descriptors must actually load and synthesize through the packages, not only pass converter self-checks. This bead
installs the packed packages into a clean external project and loads the pinned converter's FFHQ output through
`browser-model-manager` into `stylegan-js`, independently of package documentation's own smoke test. Its cases feed
sub-result 3 (`verify.packages`).

## Scope
- **Clean consumers:** run the package consumer gate from `build.m1` (fm-7ge: pack, install outside the workspace,
  strict TS against emitted declarations, every `exports` entry, worker assets through a bundler) on the release
  commit for `stylegan-js`, `browser-model-manager` and `cloudflare-model-host`, adding a Vite build to that gate if
  it lacks one; no second consumer project.
- Package construction and status reads fetch no weights, asserted from intercepted requests (zero `model-host`
  requests during construction and status) using the `build.ci-site` (fm-aa8) request helper.
- Retained lint/format/type checks and independent compute checks pass on the release commit.
- Source/licence/notice and weight-exclusion checks on the packed artifacts with the one named scanner
  `scripts/packages/check-tarball-contents.mjs` (test ID `package-tarball-content-scan`, created by
  `compute.app-rebind` fm-fy2.6, reused by `pkgdocs.release` fm-oagi): weight extensions and size limits,
  repository-only paths, secret patterns, private hostnames, required README/LICENSE/NOTICE. No second scanner; a
  missing rule is added to that script with a planted-violation self-test case.
- Record each tarball's integrity hash; the same hashes appear in the sub-result 3 output.
- **Converter output:** run the pinned `model-conv` container's acquire/convert/verify on the FFHQ checkpoint; host the
  output statically; load through `browser-model-manager` into `stylegan-js`; compare raw synthesis with the
  converter's reference/parity report within the frozen tolerances (max RGB difference 1 on 0-255, raw float 0.002);
  check manifest compatibility with the contracts. Record the container image digest.

## Out of scope
Registry publication and independent registry acceptance (`delivery.packages`, `pkgaccept.review`). The non-face
model (`verify.packages`).

## Notes
- Integrated verification checks the final integrated app (after the planned UI and package changes) against the Next baseline (`facemorph.me-classic` branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) plus the plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped. Not historic-API parity and not a shutdown-qualification campaign. Performance and reliability against the control, including control/control noise and the physical iPhone, are judged by the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27), not here. Correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found here are fixed in the owning bead and this bead re-runs. Wording says planned, experimental, implemented or deployed. No weights, secrets, photos or typed inputs in Git.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #integrated-verification (new architecture artifacts paragraph),
  #independent-published-package-acceptance (what publishes), #conversion-tooling.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] The clean consumer compiles (strict TS against emitted declarations) and bundles (Vite, worker/WASM assets) with all three packs; intercepted requests show no network at construction/status.
- [x] `package-tarball-content-scan` JSON report per tarball attached: zero weights, zero repository-only paths, zero secrets, licences/notices present; the scanner's planted-violation self-test fails on each planted file in the same run.
- [x] Each tarball's integrity hash is recorded and matches the hashes in the sub-result 3 output.
- [x] Raw synthesis from the converted FFHQ output, loaded through the manager into the engine, is within max RGB diff 1 / raw float 0.002 of the reference; manifests validate against the contracts; container image digest recorded.
- [x] Ran in the release-verification workflow on the named release commit and artifact digest; a check that did not run there, or missed its threshold, is recorded `failed` or `untested`.
- [x] close-check (conditional, from the parallelism pass): host-package install smoke at close should use fm-fy2.14's package if landed; tick once it holds or does not apply, saying which in the close reason

title: Real-bridge trace run asserting the operation event log
description:
## Background
Gate-style acceptance for this workstream: fake-clock tests plus one real-bridge run.

## Why
Proves the scheduler drives real runtime work in the expected order with correct settlement.

## Scope
Switch the operation-service implementation from bridge-backed to scheduler-backed; run in the facade harness on CPU: two faces (one word, one seed), a Morph with one unfinished input, cancel one face mid-run, retry it, file preparation; assert the emitted operation event log equals the expected trace (order, IDs, permits, reservations, terminal events).

## Out of scope
Integrated UI journeys (ws:verify).

## Considerations
Uses the shared device lease for any GPU cell; CPU is the required cell.

## Expected trace and log (polish r1)
The expected trace is a committed file `apps/web/test/harness/opctl-expected-trace.json`: ordered operation events with symbolic IDs (request, input revision, attempt), permit and reservation acquire/release, provider requested/actual, compute-ready, file-ready, cancelled, settled. The run compares the emitted event log to it ignoring timestamps and concrete IDs (mapped consistently). Scenario steps: two faces (one word, one seed), a Morph with one unfinished input, cancel one face mid-inference, Retry it (new attempt ID), file preparation for both and the MP4. The structured e2e log adds step IDs and network bytes by host class; a mismatch prints a diff of the first divergent event.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Trace assertion passes on CPU in CI; GPU cell run where a worker is available or recorded untested.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, and the log is retained as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics). Network claims are asserted from the log, never from screenshots.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/opctl/trace-run.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Expected-trace file committed; the run fails on a reordered permit/reservation event (negative test with a deliberately swapped trace).

title: Field lead: alignment is the longest photo wait and the top interruption point
description:
## Goal
Raise a performance lead from field evidence: alignment is the longest wait in the photo path and the stage where visitors most often walk away, so it is the first place a speed-up pays off. This bead only measures and proposes; it changes nothing unless a paired run shows a gain within the numerical tolerances. Source: `docs/findings/diagnostics-learnings-2026-10-18.md`, findings 1 and 2 (aggregates only).

## Background (field facts)
- Last stage before an interruption: alignment 11, asset acquisition 10, encoding 7, synthesis 7, synthesis-complete 7. Cancels cluster at synthesis (10 of 16).
- Alignment median 7.1 s on desktop WebGPU, 8.0 s on Android WebGPU, 24.6 s on desktop CPU; encoding 4.7 s, 5.6 s and 11.1 s on the same three.

## Scope
- Profile alignment per sub-stage (decode, detection, landmarks, warp) on the device lab cells under the lease, against the monorepo engine once `compute.photo-descriptor` (fm-dmlz) exists.
- Form hypotheses with the next test for each, run paired ABBA measurements against control/control noise, and report gains or none. A kept change goes through the strictly-not-worse rule.

## Out of scope
Changing numerical tolerances; UI copy for long waits (face controls own progress presentation).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Per-sub-stage alignment profile on each lab cell under the lease.
- [ ] Each hypothesis has a paired ABBA result against control/control noise; gains, none or inconclusive reported plainly; raw synthesis and e4e tolerances unchanged.
- [ ] landing any change needs fm-dmlz (with fm-dmlz). If fm-dmlz has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-dmlz (`br update fm-dmlz --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-dmlz

title: Name the independent reviewer, its input packet and review budget before publication
description:
## Background
Reviewer logistics (16 October cross-model review): before publication, name the independent-reviewer role (a person or an agent session that did not author the packages), decide what it is given (published package names, versions and public documents only) and set a bounded review budget in time and resources.

## Why
Independence and a fixed budget must be settled before anyone sees the packages, so the review cannot be steered by authors or cut short silently.

## Scope
- Decision entry in `docs/decisions/`: reviewer role and how independence is ensured (fresh agent session with no implementation conversation or private checkout, or a named non-author person), input packet contents, time/resource budget, the worker/browser environments available, and the rule that skipped journeys are recorded as unverified.
- Template for the acceptance report (registry versions/integrity, lockfile, identities, copied commands, outputs, friction log, verdict per capability).

## Out of scope
Running the review.

title: Integrated-verification harness: operated input, width sweep, artifact fixture, fixtures
description:
## Goal
The candidate's Playwright checks (`next-e2e.yml` real-ui-cpu, `next-matrix.yml`, `mobile-browser.yml`,
`scripts/next-matrix.mjs`) click controls by accessible name. That is how defect 1 passed CI: the Remove control sat
below the image, covered by the mode-menu button, and a real click at its position opened "Change mode" and removed
nothing (two faces at 1,280 px: control 32x32 at (201, 611), image 376x376 at (206, 229)). Every integrated journey
must drive the app the way a person does, bind its results to one artifact digest and map each case to the
flow-matrix row or candidate defect it grades. This bead builds the shared helpers so the verify beads stay
consistent and the release summary is mechanical.

## Scope
- **Artifact fixture:** serve or target one release artifact by digest (local static server over the canonical
  artifact, or the deployed staging URL with its digest verified from served identity). Every run is tagged with that
  digest; a digest mismatch aborts the run.
- **Host-class binding:** use the host classes and the versioned default map owned by the
  request-interception helper in `build.ci-site` (fm-aa8) unchanged (`app`, `model-host` including the
  `models.facemorph.me` second origin, `names-host`, `collector`, `third-party`, `local`); this bead only supplies the
  per-run override that binds the artifact's actual origins (local static server, staging or preview URL) to those
  classes. No new class. An unlisted origin is `third-party`; every verify case asserts zero `third-party` requests
  unless it says otherwise.
- **Journey assertions** on that helper's request primitives (never re-implemented): zero requests of a class within a
  step window; ordering such as synthesis assets before encoder shards; bytes per class; no request per keystroke (a
  typing helper that opens one step per keystroke and asserts each has no request).
- **Operated input:** `operatedClick` and `operatedTap` find the control's visible box, scroll it into view as a person
  would, assert `document.elementFromPoint` at the target point returns the control (or a descendant), assert the point
  lies inside the expected region (for example the image's top-right quadrant for Remove) and inside the viewport,
  then send a real pointer or touch event. By-name/by-role locators only for setup. Report the hit-target size (44 px
  comfortable touch size reported, not silently passed).
- **Device lab cells:** the same `operatedClick`/`operatedTap`/count/width contracts run on real hardware through
  `tools/device-lab/lab.py` on eris: OS-level taps on the USB Huawei P30 Pro (`phone-webgpu`, `phone-cpu`) and real mouse
  input in desktop Chromium (`eris-webgpu`, `eris-cpu`), with the same before/after hit checks, under the lab lock. Each
  verify case declares the lab cells and emulated widths it runs on; touch emulation never stands in for a phone cell
  when the case claims phone behaviour. Implementers use these runs for a bead's lab evidence (`lab.py qualify ... --bead`) and the release bead uses them in its full validation; the same helpers also run in the Linux browsers on eris (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) for local checks and in every CI lane of the browser matrix.
- **Step log:** every helper logs its step ID, the target control, the point used, the element actually hit and the
  per-host-class request counts and bytes for the step; the log is a CI artifact and is printed in full on failure.
- **Keyboard driver:** Tab and Shift+Tab walk with focus-visible checks, visual-order comparison against element boxes,
  and focus-return checks after dialogs close.
- **Count driver:** a repeating control at 0 or 1, 2, 3 and many (faces 30, 64, 150; blend slots 16, 40, 100) and, where a real resource budget exists, at that budget and its degraded state (the budget is forced for real, for example a real browser storage quota or a memory-constrained real device; there is no fixed face or slot count).
- **Text-input variants:** empty, whitespace only, very long (exactly 512 and 513 UTF-8 bytes, including multibyte
  characters), pasted, IME composition; numeric seed set 0, 4,294,967,295, 4,294,967,296, -1, 1.5 and pasted digits
  with spaces.
- **Width-sweep driver:** exported `SWEEP_WIDTHS` = 320, 360, 390, 480, 600, 768, 900, 1,024, 1,280, 1,920, 2,560 px
  (identical to `face.many`, fm-id4c) and `GRID_COUNTS` = 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 30, 64, 150; widths at or below the phone/tablet
  breakpoint run with touch emulation (`hasTouch`, `isMobile`). Plus each layout breakpoint read from the built CSS
  (media and container queries, em/rem converted) at +/-1 px; continuous resize through transitions;
  portrait/landscape; window-height changes; browser zoom and text enlargement; touch virtual-keyboard occlusion where
  supported. Screenshots at phone and desktop width per case and on every failure.
- **Case manifest:** each verify bead declares cases with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix
  row(s) or defect number(s) each grades; the matrix grader in `verify.join` reads these manifests.
- **Fixtures (with digests, no weights):** a metadata-free photo with one face; a photo with several faces; a photo
  with no detectable face; a rotated-EXIF photo; schema-1 PNG and schema-2 PNG/WebP recovery-bearing stills; a damaged
  still and a model-mismatched still; a saved project MP4; the defect-1 regression page (a control covered by another
  element, one clipped by its container, one off screen).
- **No mocks (operator, 24 October):** capability and failure cases are produced for real: a null adapter by launching the
  browser with WebGPU disabled, device loss by destroying the real GPU device, insufficient limits and a failed canary as plain
  inputs to the admission logic or on a real device that has them, and network failures from the local artifact server's fault
  switch (500, truncation, corrupt bytes). No in-browser request stubbing; interception only observes. A case nothing real can
  produce is `untested`.

## Out of scope
The request-interception helper, host-class map and network primitives (`build.ci-site`). Running the journeys (other
verify beads). CI lane carry-over and the device lease (`build.*`).

## Notes
- Reuse the build's lane runners and the shared device lease; no parallel CI system. Unit tests and the sample run use
  the workspace test command; captures are privacy-filtered CI artifacts.
- 24 October cut: the event-log line schema and per-bead receipt are dropped; network assertions and the digest
  binding stay. (Absorbed text pointed at the former event-log core bead, now `build.ci-site` (fm-aa8), and the dropped receipt/decision

- Integrated verification checks the final integrated app (after the planned UI and package changes) against the Next baseline (`facemorph.me-classic` branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) plus the plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped. Not historic-API parity and not a shutdown-qualification campaign. Performance and reliability against the control, including control/control noise and the physical iPhone, are judged by the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27), not here. Correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found here are fixed in the owning bead and this bead re-runs. Wording says planned, experimental, implemented or deployed. No weights, secrets, photos or typed inputs in Git.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance (network assertions; UI acceptance is operated),

title: Capture browser requests and console into the event log from Playwright and CDP, with the CI upload convention
description:
## Background

Split out of `build.docs-decisions-receipts` (fm-ucl) in polish round 2. `build.event-log-core`
defines the log, writers, validator and network primitives with no browser. This leaf connects them
to the browsers the retained harnesses drive: Playwright/Node (`scripts/next-matrix.mjs`) and
Python with `browser-harness==0.1.8` over CDP (`scripts/next-e2e-browser.py`,
`scripts/next-gpu-benchmark.py`, `scripts/next-ios-sim.py`, `tests/mobile/run.py`).

## Why

A network claim is only as good as the capture: requests from workers and service workers, cache
hits and console errors must reach the log in both languages, or "no model network before approval"
can pass by omission.

## Scope

- `scripts/evidence/playwright.ts` `attachPlaywright(pageOrContext, log)`: records page, dedicated
  worker and service-worker requests (`context.on('request'|'requestfinished'|'requestfailed')`,
  worker `page.on('worker')`), response bytes, `from_cache` where observable, and console errors;
  saves a screenshot on step failure through `log.screenshot`. Duck-typed, so it imports no
  Playwright package itself.
- `scripts/evidence/cdp_capture.py`: the same capture for the Python harnesses through
  `Network.*`, `Runtime.consoleAPICalled`, `Log.entryAdded` and `Target.setAutoAttach` (workers),
  with the browser-harness session object passed in.
- A fixture page `scripts/evidence/fixtures/journey/` (served locally) that issues one app request,
  one worker fetch, one cached request and one console error, then waits for an explicit "approve"
  click before one model-host request.
- CI convention, documented in `docs/receipts/README.md`: logs uploaded as artifact
  `e2e-log-<workflow>-<job>-<run_id>`, screenshots on failure as `e2e-shots-<workflow>-<job>-<run_id>`,
  retention 14 days (the classic `next-site` artifact retention) unless the lane states more; every
  lane runs `check-event-log` on its retained logs as a step after the journey.
- A reusable workflow step snippet (`.github/actions/event-log-upload/action.yml`) that runs
  `check-event-log` and uploads the log and screenshots with those names.

## Out of scope

The log format and network primitives (core). Operated input, width sweeps, journey assertions
(`verify.harness`).

## Considerations

- Capture limits are stated, not hidden: where a browser cannot report a cache hit or a
  service-worker request, the header records `capture_limits` and claims depending on that field are
  `untested`, never passed.
- Pinned Playwright comes from the workspace dev dependencies (`build.workspaces-ts`); browser-harness
  stays pinned at 0.1.8 until the currency lane bumps it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Cross-language check: the fixture journey logged once through `attachPlaywright` (Chromium) and once through `cdp_capture.py` (Chrome via browser-harness 0.1.8) both validate with `check-event-log`; both logs contain the worker request, the console error and a `model-host` request only after the approve step; `assertOrder(log, 'approve', first model-host request)` passes in both, and a variant that requests the model before approval fails `assertNoRequests` in both. Step-by-step output and both logs are kept as CI artifacts.
- [ ] Unit tests with recorded fixture events (no live browser) cover: worker and service-worker requests attributed to the right `initiator`; failed requests recorded with status; screenshot on step failure written and referenced from the log; `capture_limits` recorded when a field is unobservable and a dependent claim reported `untested`.
- [ ] The `event-log-upload` action runs `check-event-log` and uploads `e2e-log-<workflow>-<job>-<run_id>` and, on failure, `e2e-shots-...`; a recorded run with a deliberately failing step shows both artifacts.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Measure peak decode bytes per route
description:
## Goal

Measure the peak transient bytes of every supported image decode route on the available workers, so the milestone-2 byte ceilings are set from real measurement rather than guesses. No other workstream measures these, and a route that was not measured gets no ceiling and is therefore not admitted.

## Scope

- Routes: every supported decode route — browser image decode, any WASM or worker route, and the paths a phone uses (Android emulator and iOS Simulator lanes where available).
- Fixtures: maximum compressed size, maximum pixel count and maximum edge length at the existing single-input limits (64 MiB compressed, 120 × 1024² pixels, 20,000 px edge; `CROP_MAX_*` constants from the engine contracts, `contracts.engine`), plus a typical photo. Fixtures are generated or licensed and metadata-free; no personal photos in Git.
- Report peak allocation per representation (compressed, decoded, cropped, tensor) for each route × fixture, recording machine, browser and version, build digest and lease run ID.
- A re-runnable measurement script in this repository; every heavy step runs under the shared device lease (`autoresearch/run.py`) with the absolute per-machine state directory.
- Output: a machine-readable measurement file of raw rows (route, fixture, representation, peak bytes, machine, browser + version, build digest, lease run ID) placed beside the contract limits constants file, which the ceilings row reads; unmeasured routes listed explicitly as not admitted.

## Out of scope

Choosing the ceiling values (contracts milestone 2). Physical-phone qualification.

## Notes

- Depends on research stage 1 for the worker and lease runner (soft for milestone 1, hard for this task).
- Measurements are experimental evidence at their scope; they are not browser RSS control.
- PLAN.md (newer) has no `contracts.md`; the measurement file sits beside the limits constants file instead of a report beside `contracts.md`.
- Anchor: PLAN.md#package-and-operation-contracts (Decode-ceiling measurement protocol).

- [x] The measurement script runs end to end under the lease on the available workers and is re-runnable from a clean checkout with one documented command.
- [x] The measurement file lists every route × fixture (max compressed, max pixels, max edge, typical) × representation (compressed, decoded, cropped, tensor) with peak bytes, machine, browser + version, build digest and lease run ID.
- [x] Every route not measured is listed explicitly as not admitted.
- [x] Fixtures in Git contain no personal photos and no metadata; a test checks that.
- [x] Traces/screenshots of any browser-driven step are kept as CI artifacts on failure.

title: Wire still-recovery classification into file entry, drops and batches
description:
## Goal
Wire the still-image recovery reader (`inspectStill` from `media.envelope`) into the app's face file entry, drop targets and multi-file batches, so every chosen or dropped file is classified before any target is touched: recovered and static results install without inference, damaged recovery never silently becomes a photo, and a face from another model is shown and saved untouched but never computed with. Split from `media.envelope` in the 24 October final pass: the helpers and reader edit no shared file and must land early for static names, while this wiring edits `product-bridge.mjs` and therefore takes its turn after `crop.queue` in the shared-file sequence.

## Scope
- Call `inspectStill(file)` in the bridge's file-entry path (single file from the face menu, drop on a tile or the background) and once per file in multi-file drops, before any target replacement; late classifications for an old revision are discarded by the existing revision checks. Paste uses the same entry function when face controls adds it (`face.mixed-batch` / paste rows); no second classifier.
- Per kind, in the app:
  - `matching`: install image and latent with no model acquisition, detector or encoder.
  - `missing`: no automatic encoding; the face offers the explicit Encode image / Use as photo action, which enters the confirmed-crop flow.
  - `damaged`: never silently re-encoded (identity unchanged); Use as photo offered only when the pixels decode, as an explicit action; a plain reason names the damage class.
  - `incompatible-schema`: viewable and saveable, no latent use; the reason names the version.
  - `incompatible-model` / `unknown-model`: image shown; Save/Share hands over the original bytes unchanged (no re-encode, envelope kept); the latent never reaches the engine; the face is excluded from Morph inputs with a plain reason; compute disabled for that face.
- Never follow model URLs or any URL found in metadata.
- Reasons are data (`reasonKey`, plain sentence, Help anchor), like provider refusal reasons, so face controls renders them tied to the face.
- Detailed logging: each classification logs file index, byte size, kind, reason key and the target revision it applied to (never the file name or pixels).

## Out of scope
- Built-UI and operated checks on the ported app (`crop.ported-app`).
- The reader and envelope helpers themselves (`media.envelope`); dynamic-shape schema (`media.schema`); batch proposal UI, click order and keypoint insertion (face controls); MP4 project import (deferred).

## Notes
- Shared-file order: after `crop.queue`, before `media.export` (see the sequence note in `media.export`).
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#media-and-recovery (still-image UI re-import); #file-sharing-and-export-direction; #confirmed-crop-and-ordered-multi-selection-flow (mixed batches).

title: Operator cutover decision: facemorph.me promotion and API retirement
description:
## Goal
After execution begins, the one decision left to the operator is the explicit cutover: promotion to `facemorph.me` and retiring the old API (hosted Triton inference, encoder/legacy
API hosting, `api.facemorph.me`, `checkface.facemorph.me`): the pushes that change what live visitors get. These are
delivery actions with real lost capability (old result links and API clients stop working), so the operator chooses timing from a named
working artifact and its visible limitations. This bead is the gate node; it is not a workstream and not agent work.

## Scope
- Exactly these beads wait on it: `delivery.early-promotion` (fm-v0w, optional path), `delivery.promotion` (fm-fy2.12) and `delivery.api-retirement` (fm-9dz). The next.facemorph.me handover (`delivery.handover`, fm-s3o) does not wait on it (operator, 24 October
  2026: it deploys after full release validation). Package publication (`delivery.packages`,
  fm-96v) goes ahead without it (operator, 24 October; it needs only `gate.npm-creds` and the packed-tarball checks), as
  do the candidate edits and their merge, the legacy notice, classic publication and independent package acceptance.
- The decision is a dated row in PLAN.md "Operator decisions (dated)" stating: outcome; which actions are authorized
  (early promotion of the retained candidate, production promotion, API retirement); actions
  not authorized; the
  named artifact (repository ID, branch/commit, digest); the evidence considered with its visible limitations (the
  `verify.join` release summary for a new-monorepo release, including the strictly-not-worse gate's per-platform-class
  verdicts and, for a promotion after the handover, the latest real-visitor check (`verify.field-not-worse`), or the retained candidate's own functional/artifact
  evidence for an early promotion).
- One bead covers these three actions and the operator may authorize them at different times (for example early promotion of
  the retained candidate now, API retirement later). Closing this bead unblocks the delivery beads but does not
  authorize them: each delivery action, before running, must find its own action named as authorized in a dated
  decision row and cite that row in its close reason (the API retirement cites it in its receipt). An action not yet
  named waits for a later row.

## Out of scope
Performing any action (delivery beads). The next.facemorph.me handover (`delivery.handover`, fm-s3o) does not wait on it (operator, 24 October
  2026: it deploys after full release validation). Package publication, classic publication and independent package acceptance.

## Notes
- October 25 is aspirational; neither a date nor a test score triggers the decision. The operator may promote the
  existing working candidate before monorepo, package or research work finishes.
- No historic GUID/link preservation, old API parity, cross-domain storage migration, shutdown campaign or performance
  win is required. A monorepo build must be strictly no worse than the candidate (`verify.not-worse`, iPhone included),
  which the release summary shows; an early promotion of the retained candidate is the control itself.
- Assigned to `operator`, label `gate`. Agents do not make or infer this decision, never claim, perform or close this
  bead; no agent message is operator consent. It closes when the operator's dated decision row exists.
- Changed by the 24 October cut (this text wins over the absorbed text): the decision lives in the PLAN.md dated
  table, not a `docs/decisions/` entry; the evidence read is the CI-generated release summary, not a join receipt.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #delivery-and-publication, #remaining-choices-completion-and-cutover-authority,
  #integrated-verification (release summary).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A dated row in PLAN.md "Operator decisions (dated)" records the outcome, the authorized actions, the actions not authorized, and the named artifact (repository ID, commit, digest).
- [ ] The evidence considered is linked (the `verify.join` release summary, or the early-candidate evidence) with its visible limitations.
- [ ] Each delivery bead that relies on this gate cites the decision row naming its action, checked when that delivery bead closes, not inferred from this bead being closed.
notes: 24 Oct 2026 (operator): only the pushes that change what live visitors get need this decision. Package publication no longer waits on it (it needs only npm credentials and the packed-tarball checks); planner proposals go ahead.

title: Optional: exploratory WebNN EP probe
description:
## Background

The WebNN EP is a possible extra route, exploratory only.

## Why

Records whether a further route is worth a future research round.

## Scope

- Where a browser exposes WebNN on an available worker, run the numerics canaries and one timing screen.

## Out of scope

Adding a product route.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.

title: Route admission policy: pure per-operation admission, typed events and refusal reasons
description:
## Goal
Write the per-operation admission decision (Generate, photo encode, Morph) as a pure typed module over capability values, never phone/desktop labels, viewport or touch, with typed admission events and refusal reasons as data. fm-lt2p then wires it into the runtime and bridge.

## Scope
- Admission per operation/provider from capabilities, memory and qualified runtime/model evidence; generator admission does not establish encoder/codec support; absence/failure of an adapter selects the qualified CPU route; healthy slow GPU not demoted; bounded CPU fallback on GPU failure is a declared transition (`gpu-failure-to-cpu` with the stage); no native fallback.
- One typed event per admitted or refused operation: operation (face/photo-encode/morph), requested route (`auto`|`cpu`|`webgpu`), actual provider, fallback, refusal reason code, model/runtime identity and authorization scope. Keep `requestedProvider`/`provider`; add any new field to the reporting allowlist and privacy text list in the same revision.
- Refusal reasons are data: `reasonKey`, plain sentence (placeholder per key until `provider.copy` lands) and Help anchor; the type makes a reason mandatory whenever an action is disabled for a capability reason; raw runtime exception text never enters the reason field.
- Candidate facts to preserve: adapter probe before GPU acquisition (`navigator.gpu` alone once caused ~180 MiB of wasted Simulator downloads); `encoderStream.phoneAdmitted:true` with a 268,435,456-byte e4e WASM limit (scope `friends-and-family-candidate`).
- Keep quick product admission separate from full lab numerical checks.

## Rules
- This bead edits NONE of the shared files (`apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs`). Code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today until the bridge's own turn in the shared-file sequence; the bridge rewiring is the original bead's job.
- Tests run against real models, real browsers and real files where stated; no mocks, fixtures or captures stand in for live proof. The original bead's real-bridge/built-app checks still have to pass before the feature counts as done.
- Split from the original bead in the parallelism pass (operator, 24 October 2026: more parallel work from the start).
- Original bead: fm-lt2p (Per-operation route admission, typed admission events and refusal reasons); anchors as listed there.

The current separate iOS product rebuild is a cost and identity limitation, not a desired invariant.
Keep preview-deploy serialisation and qualified-artifact checks; never cancel a live publication halfway.

Exact-artifact identity across lanes and fewer hosted minutes.

## Scope

- One build job produces the canonical artifact with identity; site, e2e, matrix, Android, iOS

Changing which checks run.

- No worktrees, resets or cleans; preserve other sessions' uncommitted work.

title: Add build:next and deploy-next, and pass destination checks
description:
## Goal
Give the monorepo a root `build:next` compatibility wrapper and a written `deploy-next/` artifact contract populated from the pinned control artifact, then run the destination's JS checks and the local exact-artifact harness against the imported closure and the control. Exact-artifact checks, research drivers and deploy re-homing then work from day one without .NET, and the honest baseline is fixed: which classic checks run in the destination, which cannot yet and why. title: Restore typed words across reload; stored size with Clear and a bounded faces store (planner proposals)
description:
## Split (parallelism pass, 24 October 2026)
The package/core work of this bead moved to fm-udut (Session storage core: tab-scoped words, stored-size and Clear helpers, bounded faces store), which edits no shared file and starts as soon as its own inputs exist. This bead keeps: wiring restore into the word field and bridge, the Help line with stored size and Clear, the export/diagnostics byte scans, the operated checks and the removable clause. The scope text below is kept for context; where it describes work now owned by fm-udut, that bead owns and accepts it and this bead consumes the result.

## Goal
Two candidate defects found in the 18 October audit. Defect 9: after a reload the faces return but their words are gone (the field shows a disabled "Restored face"), which is confusing and loses the typed-name identity the person entered. Defect 22: nothing shows or clears what is stored on the device, and the faces store has no ceiling, a resource and privacy problem. Both fixes are planner proposals the operator may veto (PLAN.md "Planner proposals awaiting a veto", which also lists the rule for what Clear keeps); they proceed as written with no approval gate.

## Scope
**Words across reload (defect 9)**
- Store typed text/seed and a sanitized photo file name only in `sessionStorage`, keyed by the retained session record and face ID; restore them into the field on reload in the same tab when the record is compatible.
- Never in the IndexedDB session record (`last-generated-session-v2` in `checkface-originals-v1`, which outlives the tab and deliberately omits input strings), never in exported file metadata or diagnostics.
- `sessionStorage` is tab-scoped (survives a reload of that tab, not shared with other tabs, cleared when it closes), which keeps the rule "source photos/typed inputs stay tab-only".
- Abandon a late restore after any user edit; partial restore keeps valid faces.
- Best effort, not a promise: with empty or failing `sessionStorage` (new tab, reopened, private mode, quota or access error) faces restore with the accepted "Restored face" label; Help describes restoration as best effort and never promises original words or file names.
- Photo rules unchanged: source photos and retry crops are never written to OPFS, IndexedDB or session storage; reload loses unfinished photo retries; lost unfinished photo inputs point to Encode image, never Retry. A completed photo face restores from the session record as today, adding only its sanitized file name label.

**Stored size, Clear and bounded store (defect 22)**
- Current storage: IndexedDB `checkface-originals-v1` store `originals` (`browser/originals.mjs`): one record per generated result (image blob, latent, provenance) plus alias records, no ceiling; session record `last-generated-session-v2` capped by `MAX_SESSION_BYTES = 32 MiB` (faces, scrub frames, video kept only with headroom); `localStorage` `facemorph-slider-v1`; model caches belong to the manager.
- A Help line (below-fold `.next-explain`/Help area) showing stored result/session size and a **Clear** button. Clear removes the originals records, the session record and the tab-scoped words; it keeps the slider preference and model caches (the manager's own clear, if exposed, is separate and never deletes completed exports). The Help line states what Clear removes and keeps.
- Session restore checks the stored record by byte size (`MAX_SESSION_BYTES`), not face count: the port drops the `faces.length > 64` and `ids.length > 64` checks in `last-result.mjs` readSession (operator, 24 October: no fixed face count), and its 4,096 frame-array check follows the morph frame budget in the contracts ceilings (`apps/web/src/contracts/ceilings.ts`). A session over the byte bound is refused at save with one plain message naming stored-session size; faces are never dropped silently. Parsing keeps the byte-size sanity bound for untrusted records.
- Numeric ceiling for the faces store with oldest-first eviction by last use, never evicting a record referenced by the current session or a file being prepared. Measure record sizes over the standard journeys first and set the ceiling from that; until then report "measured, no threshold".

## Out of scope
Cross-tab or cross-device session transfer (ruled out). Embedding words in files. Model cache quota/eviction (manager).

## Notes
- If the operator vetoes either part (before or after implementation): remove that feature if it landed and keep the accepted limit wording in Help ("Restored face"; words and file names are not kept) for defect 9. If only the Clear scope is changed, change just the removed-store list and the Help sentence; the ceiling and eviction stand unless also vetoed. Rejected alternatives for Clear: also removing model caches (forces a re-download behind consent), or keeping the session record.
- Newer PLAN.md (24 October) wins over the earlier bead text: there is no separate decision log; the proposals are listed once in PLAN.md "Remaining choices", so no `docs/decisions/` entries are written.
- The session record path (`last-result.mjs` rememberSession/readSession, generateNameOrSeed) is called from `product-bridge.mjs`, so this row comes after `morph.guards` in the shared-file sequence (needs edge added in the 24 October final pass) and after the TS/React port; integrated verification waits on it rather than the media rows.
- Shared-file order (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October; revised in the 24 October final pass): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in one sequence enforced by needs edges, never concurrently: `provider.native` -> `provider.webgl` -> `provider.route-admission` -> `migration.project-json` (one-line ProjectJson import swap) -> typed facade (`migration.facade`) -> `compute.synthesis` -> `compute.photo-descriptor` -> `compute.app-rebind` -> `crop.fix` -> `crop.queue` -> `media.reader-wiring` -> `media.export` -> `media.schema` -> `morph.render` -> `morph.guards` -> `media.session` -> face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Rows that must not edit these files: `crop.repro`, `compute.blend`, `compute.package-surface`, `media.envelope`, `provider.admission` (evidence), `crop.ported-app` and `compute.ported-app` (acceptance on the ported app; a fix they need follows the out-of-turn rule below) and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept row; code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) until the bridge's own turn. A row that finds it must edit one of these files outside its turn adds a needs edge to the latest row in the sequence that edits it. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.
- Anchors: PLAN.md known candidate defects 9 and 22; #remaining-choices-completion-and-cutover-authority.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] fm-udut is closed; its modules are what this bead wires in (no second copy of the moved code left in the app).
- [ ] `session-words.photo-face-label-only` (no image bytes in any storage), `.unfinished-photo-points-to-encode-image`, `.no-words-in-exports-or-diagnostics` (byte scan of exported WebP/PNG/MP4 and captured diagnostics payloads) through the wired app.
- [ ] Storage scan: words, seeds and file names appear only in `sessionStorage`; no photo pixels stored anywhere.
- [ ] Operated check of the restored word field and of Clear: real pointer/touch at the control's visible position with `elementFromPoint` confirming the control and its expected region; by-name/role clicks only for setup; faces at 1, 2, 3, many (30, 64, 150) and at the stored-session size bound; word inputs empty, very long and pasted; 390 px and 1,280 px screenshots per case.
- [ ] Removable clause: if vetoed, the vetoed feature is absent from the artifact and Help keeps the accepted limit wording.

description:
## Goal
The self-hosted device lab (eris WebGPU/CPU, P30 Pro WebGPU/CPU) is in addition to hosted CI. Make the hosted platform lanes part of the gate before any monorepo deploy to next.facemorph.me (PLAN.md 'Device lab, deploy gates and CI policy').

- macOS desktop: WebKit, Firefox and Chrome. Windows desktop: Chrome and Edge (no Windows browser lane exists today; the old Windows lanes belonged to the retired native packages).
- Reuse the existing classic simulator/emulator approach; keep ordinary build/unit/browser tests. Attempt hosted lanes with bounded availability checks. A real test failure blocks; an unavailable/retired hosted runner or simulator is explicitly untested and does not permanently block. Physical phone/eris checks are local release work, not hosted phone CI.

LilacGlen (claimed), 26 Oct: root cause of the hosted android-emulator-chrome morph failure (runs 40274445309, 40259019211, 40187435942: 'Generation stopped responding' at about 483 s while frames still arrived 30–90 s apart). runtime.mjs startQualificationResume() sends qualify {resume:true} on the worker's background lane after the first face, with the default 300 s stall timer. The worker runs one operation at a time, so the morph's synthesize-frames preempts it. Frames reset only the morph's own timer, so the canary's timer (armed at about 183 s) fires at about 483 s and stop() kills a healthy morph.
Reproduced in runtime.test.mjs ('a morph longer than the stall window survives a preempted background canary; a silent worker still stops', stallMs 150, 8 frames 60 ms apart, the resume never answered). It fails in about 190 ms with exactly the hosted message.
Fix: any worker message resets every pending operation's timer (alive()). A stall is the worker being silent for the window, and a silent worker is still stopped (the same test). With the fix: runtime.test 25/25; mobile-runtime, confirmed-crop and runtime-manifest 50/50. Both changes are uncommitted: QuietCrane holds runtime.mjs (asked to release it or fold the fix in). runtime.mjs needs its import/allowlist ported record updated. title: Provider selector above the first +, Browse Names in each burger
description:
26 October operator clarification: optional early preparation belongs beside the top Auto/CPU/WebGPU selector, above the first +. No per-card Prepare encoder or blank Encode source modal. Skipping early preparation still automatically opens explanatory consent on Generate/Morph/fresh-photo preparation when prerequisites are missing, after recovery inspection and before model acquisition. One modal explains separate synthesis/encoder purposes, missing bytes and ranges/unknowns; only approved scopes download. Changing provider alone authorizes nothing. Page-level preparation is independently owned and survives cancelling an unrelated card chooser. This supersedes conflicting placement and source-modal lifecycle prose; existing behavioral acceptance remains.

## Goal
Move the Auto/CPU/WebGPU selector out of More options -> Advanced to a compact control above the first insertion +, and move Browse Names from a field adornment (`tabIndex=-1`, defect 4) into each face's burger menu bound to that face's stable ID. Both are declared changes; the plan earlier wrongly said the selector was already above the first + (18 October audit, section 3, found it only in Advanced with a WebGL option).

## Scope
- **Selector.** Compact Auto (default) / CPU / WebGPU above the first insertion +; remove the Advanced entry and any WebGL option. Preserve the candidate's recommendation text and saved choice and show the actual-route explanation beside it. The selection is captured for new work only (queued work keeps its approved scope; the controller snapshots it). Missing WebGPU leaves CPU selectable and usable. Optional **Using a computer** / **Supported browsers** links open below-page Help anchors (e.g. `#computer-requirements`). No installer, permanent support panel or device-label ban.
- **Boundary with provider simplification.** The selector changes no route semantics: it writes only the requested choice through the operation service and renders the requested/actual route data provider admission exposes (`requestedProvider`, `provider`, fallback/refusal reason). Auto's failure-only WebGPU -> CPU preference, explicit-choice meaning, bounded CPU fallback, WebGL preference migration and Help copy stay in the provider workstream, which never moves or restyles the selector. Until this lands, the ported Advanced selector shows Auto/CPU/WebGPU with the same semantics.
- **Browse Names.** Remove the field adornment from the `setpointField` replacement; add Browse Names to that face's existing burger/mode menu, keyboard reachable. Opening captures the face's stable ID and originating focus; picking returns to that tile; dismissing leaves it intact; a removed/revised target invalidates the pending selection. No page-wide selected-face mechanism, no first-empty fallback, no implicit new slot, no `/names` navigation. Uses `openNamesFocus`/`closeNamesFocus` (`photo-selection.mjs`). The entry may land before the refined names modal and opens the ported modal until then.
- Update the artifact harness (`scripts/check-next-artifact.sh` or its TS replacement): drop the field-adornment Browse names expectation (listed in `tests/retired.txt`) and assert Browse Names is reachable from each burger and that no adornment exists.

- **Early preparation placement.** Render the eligible optional Prepare encoder entry beside this top selector, above the first +, calling consent.modal; its approved status/Cancel setup stays in this compact area. Route selection alone neither opens automatic acquisition nor authorizes downloads. No per-card preparation control or permanent download panel. Consent owns policy, costs, grants and cancellation.

## Out of scope
Admission logic, WebGL removal and preference migration, Help copy (provider workstream); the names modal and static results (names.picker, names.static-result).

## Notes
- Historical `src/MorphForm.fs` is an additional field-menu reference. Edits only ported UI; no shared bridge/runtime/worker file.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#next-release-ui-and-photo-requirements, #clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation (provider row), #end-to-end-experience-and-design-fidelity-check, #workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership (names tie-break).

title: Application operation controller: scheduler, residency, intents, cancellation, progress
description:
## Background
The candidate serializes heavy work through `scheduler.mjs` `nextScheduled(jobs, {busy, blockedFaces, blockMorph})` (first eligible request, order preserved, morph waits for photo decisions) plus a single `Busy`/`JobId`/`LastRun` in `Product.fs` and `active`/`runtime.cancel()` in `product-bridge.mjs`. A single Busy/LastRun/Retry cannot represent independent slots, imports and downloads. No workstream owned the scheduler the contracts describe until 15 October.

## Why
Bounds aggregate GPU/WASM/model memory, makes Morph a dependency-aware parent intent, rejects stale results and gives one honest whole-action progress bar, without moving scheduling into React.

## Scope
Input revisions, request and attempt IDs, per-slot Cancel/Retry; one heavyweight operation per provider context with separate compute permits and residency reservations; Morph as a parent intent that yields its permit while awaiting dependencies; whole-action progress through default-file readiness; defects 15 (offline with cached models) and 17 (stale completions). Exposed through a narrow operation-service interface that the migration's reducers call.

## Out of scope
UI state machine (ws:migration); frame-budget check, frame production and MP4 probe (ws:morph); consent grant semantics (ws:consent); button/progress presentation (ws:face).

## Considerations
Written in the same period as the controller port; the two never claim the same code. Consumers: face controls, morph pipeline, acquisition consent. Operator rulings: no time boxes, no human approval gates, no fallbacks or backports to the old stack, no .NET/F#/Webpack in this repository. Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Fake-clock scheduler tests cover permit versus residency (`opctl.scheduler-core`), Morph yielding its permit (`opctl.morph-parent`), joining an existing operation (`opctl.morph-parent`), cancel at each boundary (`opctl.cancellation`) and no starvation (`opctl.scheduler-core`); each named test exists and passes in CI.
- [ ] One real-bridge run asserts the operation event log against the expected trace.
- [ ] The scheduler, dependency, cancellation and starvation cases named in face controls, morph pipeline and integrated verification are covered or explicitly delegated.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/opctl/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] The one real-bridge trace run (`opctl.trace-run`) passes on CPU in CI and its expected-trace file is committed.
notes: Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-operation-controller; #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts; #gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design; #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance. New workstream (no old record).

title: Carry over the self-hosted WebGPU lane under the shared device lease
description:
## Background

Classic `next-gpu-lane.yml` webgpu-benchmark: self-hosted TrueNAS `gpu-vulkan`, GTX 1050, pinned Chrome
for Testing 141.0.7390.54, actual WebGPU; scheduled/manual/path-triggered evidence, deliberately not a
promotion gate. The older `gpu-gtx1050` host config can use llvmpipe because the NVIDIA Vulkan ICD is
absent. The workflow's own concurrency group does not coordinate with local agents.

## Why

Hardware-GPU evidence is retained; the heavy command must share the device lease with local agents and research.

## Scope

- Destination workflow; wrap its heavy command in `autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's absolute state directory.
- Reject software adapters and name adapter failures.

- Artifact lookup, provenance (source repository ID, workflow, run, commit), digest verification,
  the shared path-filter list `scripts/ci/path-filters.json` (every new code root: `apps/web/**`,
  `packages/**`, `scripts/**`, relevant `hosting/**`, not only `src/Next`), concurrency and cache
  keys come from `build.ci-artifact-lookup` (`.github/actions/fetch-artifact`); inherited
  `context.repo` or a corrected org prefix is never used. This lane adapts its own paths, worker
  discovery and source assertions for `apps/web` and all four packages.
- Event log through `build.event-log-capture` (`cdp_capture.py` / `attachPlaywright`), validated by
  `check-event-log` and uploaded with `.github/actions/event-log-upload`.
- Retain the lane's protected behaviour, trigger coverage, required-check role and retained evidence;
  cancel superseded test builds; cache pinned dependencies and immutable runtime assets by identity.
- Every mapped check is listed in the check-migration map with its destination invocation.

## Destination workflow, platforms and pass thresholds

- File `.github/workflows/next-gpu-lane.yml` ("GPU lane benchmark"), job `webgpu-benchmark`,
  `runs-on: [self-hosted, truenas, gpu-vulkan]` (GTX 1050), pinned Chrome for Testing 141.0.7390.54
  (a pin change goes through the currency lane with a hold-back/bump record), `browser-harness==0.1.8`,
  driver `scripts/next-gpu-benchmark.py` under a 2100 s watchdog, artifact `next-gpu-benchmark-<run_id>`.
- Triggers kept: schedule `0 16 * * *`; workflow_dispatch with `url` (default: the staged/qualified origin,
  never assumed to be production) and `faces` (default 6, first face reported cold); push path filter on
  the WebGPU sources at their new paths (`packages/stylegan-js/**` WebGPU engine/fused-resample files,
  `apps/web/**` route-priors/route-selection/runtime, `scripts/next-gpu-benchmark.py`, the workflow file).
- Pass thresholds: the in-page adapter must be a hardware adapter (adapter info names the NVIDIA GPU);
  `llvmpipe`, SwiftShader or any software/fallback adapter is a named failure "software adapter", never a
  timing pass; `nvidia-smi` output recorded; synthesis canaries within RGB ≤ 1 / raw-float ≤ 0.002 before
  any timing is reported; per-face timings recorded as evidence, no absolute speed limit (not a promotion
  gate, not a required status).

## Out of scope

Making it a promotion gate.

## Considerations

- A workflow definition is not a passing result: record actual run outcomes, and do not advertise cells
  as passing that fail (the 7 October manual matrix run 37555426933 failed; recent GPU evidence failed
  adapter admission).
- Classic's publisher stays live until the explicit source handover; this repository's lanes must not
  publish `next.facemorph.me` (exactly one repository may publish a target at a time).
- Native-package retirement does not retire desktop-browser, mobile or hardware-GPU checks.
- Required statuses and branch-protection bindings come from the inventory, not workflow filenames.
- An installed GPU or runner label is not inference evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A recorded run shows the lease acquired (journal entry) and the real adapter identity, or a named adapter failure.
- [ ] A concurrent local leased run on the same machine is held off (busy exit 75 or bounded wait).
- [ ] Every end-to-end script involved emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform and provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, retains the log as a CI artifact, and any network claim is asserted from that log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] A run on a host exposing only a software adapter (llvmpipe/SwiftShader) ends with the named failure "software adapter" and reports no timings; a hardware run records adapter info, `nvidia-smi` output and canary results before timings.

title: Retirement inventory, handover action list, names-host plan and runbook dry run
description:
## Goal
Prepare everything the operator-controlled delivery actions execute so nothing is improvised at cutover: the list of every API-only process, binding and credential to remove versus shared resources to keep; a concise handover/retirement action list with verifiable preconditions, exact commands, a concretely named rollback target, one publisher per target and a proving check per action; the names-host redirect plan; and a dry run of every runbook command. The reusable post-delivery check script and the cutover annotation helper that every action ends with are `domain.actions.check`. Needs no monorepo build.

## Scope
- **Retirement inventory** (starting from the 15 October source scan of classic `b2d945a`): Triton/encoder/API processes and hosts, serving routes, tunnels/proxies, DNS records and Pages/Workers bindings for `api.facemorph.me` and `checkface.facemorph.me`, API-only credentials (names only). Each item remove or keep (shared) with reason and exact command. Keep: model chunks, names catalogue, preview/latent Workers (until the snapshot and static names replace their API dependency), diagnostics collector, `models.facemorph.me` with R2 `facemorph-runtime-mirror` and its credentials, the `/stats/v1` statistics Worker and its scrape token, `metrics.facemorph.me` Grafana and the triton Prometheus with its stored old-API counter series (the changeover statistics' "before" side, 5-year retention). The triton machine itself is kept as a development worker and Prometheus host; only its Triton inference/API processes, tunnels and API-only credentials are remove items. Dispositions for the source references: `hosting/gallery/materialize.py`/`name-catalogue.yml` (reads the snapshot); `src/Next/Product.fs` FAQ and `src/explain.md` linking `checkface.facemorph.me/api` (retirement copy); `src/Config.fs`, overlay `Config.fs`, `verify-config.mjs`, `verify-overlay.py` (historical/classic, unchanged; `apiAddr` never copied into the new app); `facemorph-names` grid (retired); external `multi-morph-test.vercel.app` (`api/face/?num_multi=N&guidK=…&amountK=…`; replaced by the weighted face blend).
- **Action list** `handover.md` (read by every delivery bead): early retained-candidate promotion; candidate-source handover (next.facemorph.me from classic `candidate/next-delivery-20260916` to the monorepo); production promotion (facemorph.me from legacy Vercel/`master` to the chosen on-device artifact); API retirement; names-host redirect; Vercel publisher retirement; reference to classic publication's default-branch switch pre-checks. Per action: verifiable preconditions, exact commands/console steps, rollback target (artifact digest or build id) and steps, owner, one-publisher enforcement step per target, and the exact `post-delivery-check` invocation (mode, hostname, expected digest, retired hosts). Stable repo IDs/URLs, chosen candidate source/artifact, current and future publishers and hosting owners recorded.
- Rollback after API retirement uses a retained working on-device artifact with its immutable runtime/model/catalogue assets and diagnostics configuration inside the declared retention window (from model hosting extraction); never restarting Triton/API or restoring historic production data. Distinguish candidate-source switch from production replacement.
- Second runtime origin: `models.facemorph.me` copies immutable runtime paths from `https://next.facemorph.me/` (hard-coded in classic `hosting/next-mirror/worker.mjs`) and pages on any `*.facemorph.me` host retry through it. Per action state what keeps it complete: after the candidate-source handover, an early-promoted candidate or rollback artifact relies on paths the copy already holds, so warm every runtime path of each live and rollback artifact before the handover, or re-point the copy's origin; verify by HEAD requests.
- Step to tell the `multi-morph-test.vercel.app` user (Synthetic Data Ltd tester) before API retirement that it stops and the on-device weighted blend replaces it (old GUIDs do not carry over; they re-add their photos).
- **Names host**: `names.facemorph.me` (sibling `facemorph-names`, Svelte grid calling the API) redirects (DNS/Worker redirect) to the API-independent main app with its fullscreen names modal; no names-only route, no old iframe/API messaging, no two-click or result-bearing URLs. Record the before state (DNS record or Worker route; status and body digest of `/`), redirect command, rollback command and `--mode redirect` check; `facemorph-names` disposition (archive notice text, history kept). What the names host may claim is decided at delivery after static names; the candidate picker still synthesizes, so a redirect to it does not establish inference-free selection.
- **Dry run of the runbook.** Every command in the retirement inventory and `handover.md` runs in the provider's dry-run or read-only form where one exists (`wrangler deploy --dry-run`, `wrangler ... list`/`get`, Cloudflare API GET of the record or route about to change, `gh api` GET, `vercel ls`/`inspect`); commands with no dry-run form are listed as such with the read-only probe that shows their target exists.
- Each action's post-delivery check invocation names the `scripts/delivery/post-delivery-check.mjs` mode, hostname, expected digest and retired hosts as that script defines them (`domain.actions.check`); visitor-changing actions also name their `annotate-cutover.mjs` call.

## Out of scope
Writing `post-delivery-check.mjs` and `annotate-cutover.mjs` (`domain.actions.check`). Executing any action; removing anything; production-data disposal or deleting personal records (a separate explicit operation); GUID archive, data migration or restore rehearsal; integrated verification journeys; package registry checks; re-archiving or rewriting `checkface`.

## Notes
- October 25 is aspirational; the operator chooses timing and order. No phone or shutdown-parity certification.
- 24 October rules: no per-action receipt paths; delivery evidence is each workflow's CI run with this check; only API retirement and old-report deletion keep receipts. No shared event-log emitter: network claims are asserted from intercepted requests by host class and bytes.
- Plan: #domain-handover-and-retirement-preparation, #retire-hosted-inference-and-the-old-api-completely, #known-active-references-to-the-retiring-hosts--source-scan-15-october-2026, #delivery-and-publication.
- Split on 2026-10-24 for swarm size: `domain.actions` (this ID, fm-5u9: retirement inventory, `handover.md` action list, names-host plan, runbook dry run) and `domain.actions.check` (`scripts/delivery/post-delivery-check.mjs` and `scripts/delivery/annotate-cutover.mjs`). The two can proceed in parallel; every delivery action needs both.

- [x] Retirement table: every item remove/keep with reason and command; every listed source reference has a disposition; secret scan finds no values; the keep list names the statistics Worker, `metrics.facemorph.me`, the triton Prometheus and its old-API series, and the triton machine as a worker.
- [x] Runbook dry run: every retirement-inventory and `handover.md` command runs in its provider dry-run/read-only form in CI (one JSON line per command: command, target, exit code, what it would change), or is listed as having no dry-run form with its read-only target probe; a command whose target does not exist fails the run.
- [x] `handover.md` has, per action, preconditions, commands, rollback target named concretely (digest or build id), owner, one-publisher step and its post-delivery check invocation; each rollback target's runtime paths are confirmed held by `models.facemorph.me` (HEAD list in CI output) or the action states how they will be.
- [x] Names-host entry names the before state (DNS/route, status, body digest), redirect and rollback commands and the `--mode redirect` invocation; `facemorph-names` archive notice text recorded.
