title: Generalize mapping and synthesis to the model descriptor
description:
## Background
Generic code currently assumes FFHQ: 1024 x 1024 output and W+ shape 18 x 512 (e.g. `geometry/latent-path.mjs` accepts only `[512]` and `[18,512]`; tensor sizes are fixed in runtime and media code). Contracts milestone 2 freezes the external developer journey and the model descriptor (latent/output shapes, layout/normalization, noise, truncation, optional class conditioning, resource requirements).

## Why
The packages must serve developers with non-face StyleGAN2 checkpoints at other resolutions; dimensional assumptions cannot remain implicit in generic APIs, and unsupported models must fail with an actionable error instead of being forced into FFHQ's shape.

## Scope
- Mapping and synthesis read every dimension from the descriptor carried by the loaded capability: Z/W size, W+ layer count, output resolution/channels, layout/normalization, noise, truncation and optional class conditioning.
- Descriptive rejection of unsupported descriptors/operator combinations (actionable error naming the unsupported field).
- Component check with a qualified caller-loaded reference model that has a different output resolution and latent layer count (the non-face fixture from conversion tooling when available; otherwise a test descriptor with an independent reference produced by the pinned reference implementation), using its own declared small tolerance.
- Non-face capabilities never load a face detector or FFHQ e4e.

## Out of scope
Descriptor-driven morph geometry (morph pipeline). Dynamic-shape recovery schema (media and recovery). Converter qualification of the non-face checkpoint (conversion tooling). The full external-developer journey (integrated verification).

## Considerations
- These component checks unblock media/application integration; they do not establish complete non-face package support, which closes only in integrated verification's joint proof.
- Other models' tolerances are their own; FFHQ values are not inherited.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] FFHQ outputs unchanged within the frozen tolerances after generalization.
- [ ] A different-resolution, different-layer-count reference passes mapping and synthesis within its own declared tolerance; its descriptor and reference provenance are recorded.
- [ ] Unit tests: each unsupported descriptor field yields a descriptive typed rejection; no code path reads a hardcoded 1024 or 18x512 (scripted source scan with an allowlist for FFHQ descriptor data).
- [ ] Non-face run's network log shows no detector or e4e asset request.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes: Position in the shared-file sequence: after compute.photo-orchestration, before compute.app-rebind. Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Leaves that must not edit these three files: ws:crop.repro (failing tests and the failure analysis only), crop.policy, media.envelope-helpers, media.recovery-schema, morph.descriptor-geometry, compute.consumer-example, compute.names-equality, and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept leaf. They keep the module export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) and move logic behind them into the package. If such a leaf finds it must edit one of the three files, it records the file in the check-migration map conflict list and adds a needs edge to the latest leaf in the sequence that edits it; it never edits concurrently. Each sequenced leaf lists every file it edits in the check-migration map conflict list at claim time.

title: Port the changeover statistics sink and add the Usage statistics switch
description:
## Goal
Carry the candidate's changeover statistics sink into the monorepo app with its meaning unchanged, add the visible **Usage statistics: On/Off** switch beside the debug-report disclosure, and label every beacon with the build that sent it, so the Grafana before/after view and the real-visitor not-worse check (`verify.field-not-worse`, fm-js8i) can tell candidate and monorepo traffic apart on any host (PLAN.md "Changeover statistics in Grafana", operator 24 October 2026). The Worker (`services/stats/`), the scrape job and the dashboard (`ops/grafana/`) already exist in this repository and are deployed; the candidate sink is candidate commit `551b607` on `candidate/next-delivery-20260916` and arrives with the candidate closure import.

## Scope
- **Port with the same semantics.** `src/Next/usage-stats.mjs` and its hooks in `analytics.mjs` (`setStatsSink` and the `stat()` calls in `start` (visit), `jobFinished` (job, plus morph frames), `modelsDownloaded` (model megabytes), `exported` and `milestone('generated-visible')` (time to first result)) become a typed module (`apps/web/src/analytics/usage-stats.ts`) wired by the ported controller/operation service through the facade instead of a bridge import. Keep every event definition as the candidate has it: closed vocabulary (actions face, photo, morph, names, blend; routes cpu, webgpu, auto; outcomes completed, cancelled, failed, with interrupted counted as cancelled; platform ios, android, desktop, unknown; visit first/returning; time-to-first-result cache `warm` meaning a returning visit; export kind image/video and method save/share); durations clamped at one hour; batching (flush at 150 events or 60 s, on `pagehide` and on hidden visibility; bodies of at most 3,800 bytes, split by halving); `navigator.sendBeacon` to same-origin `/stats/v1`; never throwing into the product. A changed definition would silently break the before/after comparison, so any change needs a new event kind and metric name, never a redefinition.
- **Opt-outs unchanged:** production hosts only; off for Global Privacy Control, Do Not Track, Save-Data and automation (`navigator.webdriver`); off when localStorage `facemorph-usage-stats` is `off`. The sink's production host list is `next.facemorph.me` and `facemorph.me` (the Worker already routes `facemorph.me/stats/*`); it is the sink's own rule, separate from where Google Analytics loads. `diag.rebinding` (fm-imm9) later folds this list into its production host map.
- **Build and host labels.** Each beacon carries `b: "monorepo"`. The Worker (`services/stats/worker.mjs`) accepts `b` only from the closed set `candidate`/`monorepo` (absent means `candidate`, which is what the candidate sends today) and adds the labels `build` and `host` (`next` or `production`, derived from the `Origin` header the Worker already checks, never from the body) to every `fm_web_*` series. Dashboard queries sum over the new labels so the existing panels show the same totals; a `build` variable is added. Deployed by the existing `stats-worker.yml`.
- **Switch.** One line **Usage statistics: On/Off** directly below the debug-report disclosure summary at `#debug-reporting` (that area only; nothing in face burgers, Morph options or output controls): a real checkbox with a label. Off writes `facemorph-usage-stats=off`, drops the in-memory queue and sends nothing more from that tab at once; On removes the key. If storage throws, the switch still works for the tab and says the choice could not be saved (the debug disclosure's wording pattern). When GPC, Do Not Track or Save-Data already turn it off, the switch shows Off, disabled, with that reason.
- **Help text.** One FAQ entry under privacy: what is counted (visits by platform class and first or returning visit; jobs by action, route and outcome, with durations; time to first result; morph frames; exports by kind and method; first-visit model megabytes); that only aggregate counters are kept, with no cookie, identifier, words, seeds, names, photos or file names; which opt-outs apply; where to switch it off. The privacy text (`diag.disclosure`, fm-szbf) names `/stats/v1` as a same-origin request.
- **Blend.** `blend` is already in the sink and Worker vocabulary; the blend view (`face.blend-view`, fm-2kse) reports its jobs through the same analytics call.

## Out of scope
The Worker's anti-abuse rules, scrape token and Grafana provisioning other than the label change (built in `services/stats/` and `ops/grafana/`); the real-visitor comparison (`verify.field-not-worse`); Google Analytics host policy (`diag.rebinding`).

## Notes
- The candidate wires the sink with a two-line import in `product-bridge.mjs` (`record as recordUsage`, `setStatsSink`). Wiring it from the ported controller replaces that through the facade, not a bridge edit; if a bridge edit turns out to be needed, add the `morph.guards` ordering edge first.
- The Worker drops obvious automation by user agent (its `BOT` pattern includes `playwright` and `headless`), so end-to-end checks assert beacons at the page's request interception and the Worker's behaviour through its unit tests.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#changeover-statistics-in-grafana, #strictly-not-worse-than-the-candidate-operator-24-october-2026 (after release, from real visitors), #debug-reporting-control-and-consent.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Sink unit tests: off under each of GPC, Do Not Track, Save-Data, `navigator.webdriver`, a non-production host and the localStorage switch; on for both production hosts; throwing storage leaves it on and never throws into the caller.
- [ ] Mapping unit tests: the candidate's `usage-stats.test.mjs` cases give the same events, plus `blend`, the `b: "monorepo"` field, interrupted counted as cancelled, durations clamped, malformed events dropped.
- [ ] Batching tests in a real browser with real time (the batching rule itself is a pure function given timestamps as plain values): flush at 150 events, at 60 s, on pagehide and on hidden visibility; a body over 3,800 bytes splits so every part fits; a throwing `sendBeacon` never reaches the product.
- [ ] Worker unit tests (`services/stats/worker.test.mjs`): `b` accepted only from the closed set and defaulted to `candidate`; `host` derived from `Origin` (`https://next.facemorph.me` gives `next`, `https://facemorph.me` gives `production`), never from the body; the existing vocabulary, size, count, origin, rate-limit and Prometheus-text tests still pass.
- [ ] Dashboard check: every pre-existing panel query returns the same totals on a real Prometheus scrape of generated test traffic with the new labels as on one without them.
- [ ] Operated check at 390 px and 1,280 px (real pointer/touch at the switch's visible position inside `#debug-reporting` with `elementFromPoint`; label click and Space): Off stops all further `/stats/v1` requests from that tab (intercepted, across a job and a page hide); On resumes; reload keeps the choice; with GPC set the switch shows Off, disabled, with its reason; storage throwing shows the tab-only line.
- [ ] End-to-end on a production-host test build (the automation opt-out cleared only through the test build's injected environment): one session (visit, a face, a morph, a Save) sends beacons that hold only closed-vocabulary events with `b: "monorepo"`, go only to same-origin `/stats/v1`, and no other new host is contacted (intercepted requests, logged per step).
- [ ] After the Worker deploy: the `stats-worker.yml` smoke check passes, the Prometheus target `facemorph_web` is up, and real candidate beacons appear with `build="candidate"` and `host="next"` within two scrapes.
- [ ] The FAQ entry and privacy text rendered at 390 px and 1,280 px name what is counted and the opt-outs.
- [ ] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test`) and pass.
- [ ] close-check (conditional, from the parallelism pass): switch placement next to the disclosure at close if fm-szbf landed; tick once it holds or does not apply, saying which in the close reason

Like-for-like timings (operator, 24 October 2026). Besides porting the candidate events unchanged, the sink sends three NEW event kinds (the Worker already accepts them; tests in services/stats/worker.test.mjs):
- `job_warm` {action, route, platform, ms}: request to visible result for jobs that ran with the models already loaded (not the first job that had to fetch/restore models). Metric fm_web_job_warm_seconds. Pairs with the old server's request_processing_seconds (face endpoint, server-side, no visitor network).
- `compute` {action, route, platform, ms}: model compute per image with models loaded (the synthesis-complete stage's elapsedMs per face; per photo encode for action photo). Metric fm_web_compute_seconds. Pairs with the old server's generator_network_seconds per generated image.

Acceptance adds: a unit test per new kind in the sink (only emitted when the condition holds, e.g. no job_warm for a job that loaded models), and the end-to-end run shows all three in one beacon. Dashboard panels 205, 206 and 301 read them.

title: Fill and publish the versioned support-and-evidence table
description:
## Background
Workspace build defines the table's schema (with the minimal declared browser matrix from the retained lanes); integrated verification fills it. Device check calibration supplies measurements. Help must provide a concise tested browser/OS support list plus evidence status.

## Why
Users and the operator need one versioned statement of what was tested, on what, with which outcome.

## Scope
- Use the schema from `build.support-table-schema` (fm-yqa) unchanged. Generate with `scripts/verify/support-table.ts` from the sub-result receipts, `collect-lane-results.ts` output and the device calibration receipt.
- One row per capability x platform/browser/provider cell: outcome from the same closed set the join uses (passed, failed, untested, unsupported, inconclusive, deferred, not-applicable-by-decision, measured, no threshold), artifact digest, run link. Generated from the sub-result receipts by script, not typed by hand.
- Small intended-feature matrix and which version was exercised.
- Calibration cells from device check, recorded honestly when uncalibrated.
- The ONNX Runtime Web evaluation decision (hold-back or adoption) noted if recorded.
- Physical iPhones listed as untested; Simulator speed does not fill that gap.

## Out of scope
Marketing claims; inferred cells.

## Considerations
- Unsupported/untested/inconclusive is never PASS.
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Table committed and versioned with the artifact; every cell carries an outcome and evidence link.
- [ ] Help support list generated from the same JSON; a test fails when Help text and table disagree.
- [ ] Unit tests for `support-table.ts`: a cell with no receipt is `untested`; an outcome outside the closed set is rejected; evidence from another digest is `untested`; physical-iPhone rows are always an evidence gap; the output validates against fm-yqa's schema.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Cancellation and settlement at every boundary
description:
## Background
Candidate action cancellation aborts the active controller and runtime (`active?.abort(); writer?.dispose(); runtime?.cancel()`); explicit prefetch has worker-stop/settlement primitives while its toast offers Hide.

## Why
Revision invalidation alone is not permission to keep running abandoned work; resources must settle before reuse.

## Scope
- Per-slot Cancel (actual abort/worker stop where supported), Cancelling state until settlement, then Retry if input remains.
- Shared fetch/acquisition stops when its final authorized consumer leaves; other explicit owners continue.
- Cancelling a morph never destroys a separately requested face job; Cancel is distinct from Hide.
- Removal invalidates and releases that slot without affecting unrelated completed faces.
- Network/worker submissions stop within the declared bound.

## Out of scope
Consent-dialog Cancel semantics (ws:consent) beyond releasing the intent's ownership.

## Considerations
Do not promise instant preemption of submitted GPU work; settle the in-flight unit.

## Named fake-clock tests (polish r1)
File `apps/web/src/operations/cancellation.test.ts`: one test per boundary (`cancel while queued`, `cancel during acquisition`, `cancel during runtime/session load`, `cancel during canary`, `cancel during inference (in-flight unit settles, no preemption promised)`, `cancel during file preparation`), each asserting: Cancelling state until settlement, exactly one terminal event, reservations and permits released, no late result installed, Retry available when input remains; plus `shared fetch continues for the remaining owner`, `last owner cancel stops transfer within the bound`, `morph cancel never cancels a separately requested face`, `remove releases only that slot`, `Cancel is distinct from Hide`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Fake-clock tests: cancel queued, cancel during acquisition, during load/canary, during inference, during file preparation; each settles, releases reservations and emits one terminal event.
- [ ] Shared-owner test: one of two owners cancels, transfer continues; last owner cancels, transfer stops.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic are listed in the destination test discovery (no unlisted test files) and pass in CI.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/opctl/cancellation.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes: Plan anchor: PLAN.md#application-operation-controller; #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts; #gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design (Operation/resource ownership; Separate Cancel from Hide).

title: Reconcile the self-host API and start with one command
description:
## Goal
Give the frozen classic distribution the original UI/API behaviour before it is frozen, by migrating only verified functionality missing from the PyTorch self-host relative to the archived legacy server, and make it start with the operator's one-command, README-executed quickstart: `git clone <canonical-url>` / `cd <repository>` / `ACCEPT_MODEL_TERMS=yes docker compose up`.

## Scope
- **API reconciliation.** Compare `self-host/legacy-route-inventory.json` with the archived `checkface/` server's routes and parameters (read-only; provenance only) using a re-runnable script. Migrate only missing verified functionality into the classic successor: seed/text semantics, photo reconstruction, morph/media endpoints, saved identities, health checks, persistent model/media volumes. Each gap is migrated with route tests or recorded as dropped with a reason.
- **One command (rot hazard 4).** Root `compose.yaml` that `include`s `self-host/compose.yml` (confirm the minimum Compose v2 version supporting `include`; this workstation has 5.5.1), so the quickstart needs no `cd` into a subdirectory. The old multi-step quickstart (clone, `cd`, export `COMPOSE_FILE`, build, separate setup run, `up`), the wrong `cd facemorph.me/self-host` and the feature-branch clone are removed.
- Setup service downloads and checksum-verifies the three author-hosted assets: dlib landmarks 64,040,097 B; StyleGAN2 checkpoint 381,673,535 B; e4e checkpoint 1,201,649,680 B on Google Drive (1.65 GB total). The API starts only after setup completes successfully and logs a clickable `http://localhost:8080` once healthy.
- Missing terms acknowledgement: stop with where the terms are and the exact command, exit non-zero, never hang; acceptance is never defaulted or silently injected.
- CUDA is the default through a documented CUDA Compose entry point (replacing the manual setup-profile step); CPU is an explicit documented override; no NVIDIA runtime gives a clear failure, never a CPU fallback.
- Interrupted setup recovers on the next `up`; a corrupt or partial asset is rejected by hash; verified files are reused.
- README quickstart block marked for extraction, with `<canonical-url>` as its one variable. Upstream weight hosts stated plainly.

## Out of scope
New features; historic pixel parity or production encoder parity; hosted API compatibility for the new app; mirrors, liveness jobs or overrides for weight hosts (D6); publishing a backend image (D5: the user builds it locally because it carries NVIDIA-licensed code and CUDA libraries).

## Notes
- Existing route tests establish neither production encoder parity nor byte-identical historical pixels.
- Runs before the default-branch switch name the branch explicitly and are development runs.
- Plan: #classic-distribution, #classic-distribution-acceptance, #frozen-classic-distribution (one-command contract, D5, D6).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Route comparison generated by a script reading `legacy-route-inventory.json` and the archived server's route table; each gap has route tests (request, status, content type, a decodable image where one is returned) or a recorded drop reason.
- [x] `setup.py` unit tests: wrong sha256 rejected; partial file resumed or replaced; verified file reused; missing acknowledgement exits non-zero with the terms location and exact command.
- [x] From a clean clone (development run, branch named) `ACCEPT_MODEL_TERMS=yes docker compose up` serves the frontend and API and logs `http://localhost:8080` once healthy.
- [x] Local runs show: missing terms fails fast with the instruction; a kill during setup recovers on the next `up`; a corrupted asset is rejected; restart reuses volumes with zero weight bytes downloaded (asserted from intercepted/recorded download bytes, not a screenshot).
- [x] No NVIDIA runtime: clear failure, no CPU fallback; the explicit CPU override starts.
- [x] The single-command path exists: root compose.yaml including self-host/compose.yml, ACCEPT_MODEL_TERMS handling (stops with the terms location and exact command, non-zero, never hangs), README quickstart is git clone; cd; ACCEPT_MODEL_TERMS=yes docker compose up (the current six-step README and its wrong cd path are replaced).

title: Model descriptor, recovery schema versioning and developer-journey types
description:
## Goal

Freeze the model descriptor and the external developer journey as exported TypeScript in `packages/stylegan-js`, so no generic API hides FFHQ's 1024 px / 18×512 assumptions: descriptor and latent schema types with an FFHQ 1024 and a hypothetical 512 px fixture, the compatibility table row type, dynamic-shape recovery schema versioning that keeps earlier candidate readers working, and the five-step developer journey as typed cases, checked by a declaration consumer. Split out of contracts milestone 2 in the 24 October final pass: it needs only milestone 1, so it runs in parallel with the app types and the decode measurement instead of waiting behind them, and milestone 2 stays reviewable in one sitting.

## Scope

**Model descriptor and developer journey** — `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/descriptor.ts`:
- `ModelDescriptor` (latent/output shapes, W/W+ layer count, layout/normalisation, noise, truncation, optional class conditioning, resource requirements, provider qualification, identity/digest), `LatentSchema`, `CompatibilityRow` (serialization variants, architecture, conditional, resolution/channels, Z/W dims, precision/operators, qualified providers, unsupported cells, conversion route, terms), `DescriptorQualification` (`qualified` | `unqualified: <blocker>`).
- Fixtures: FFHQ 1024 (18×512) and a hypothetical 512 px model; no hidden 1024/18×512 constants in generic signatures. Proposed non-face fixture is NVlabs AFHQ cat 512 px, not claimed supported; non-face support stays labelled unqualified with its named blocker until the joint proof passes.
- Dynamic-shape recovery schema versioning that keeps earlier candidate readers working; equal-shaped latents from different checkpoint identities cannot be combined; unknown models are viewable as media only.
- Five-step journey as typed contract cases: choose a checkpoint from the compatibility table; run the pinned conversion container; host on standard HTTPS static hosting; install packages in a clean project and authorise acquisition through the manager or load directly; export PNG/lossless WebP, reopen exact metadata, multi-input morph. Non-face generation never loads a face detector or FFHQ e4e.

**Tests.** Type-level tests per descriptor union; validator fuzzing (fixed seed, recorded case count, typed rejection) for descriptor-bearing recovery metadata; an emitted-declaration consumer outside the workspace graph for the descriptor types. Strict TS: no broad `any`, unchecked casts or silent defaults; `unknown` validated at runtime.

## Out of scope

Conversion and qualification of the non-face fixture (conversion tooling); descriptor-driven mapping and morph geometry implementations (compute extraction, morph pipeline); screen/state types and numeric ceilings (`contracts.m2`).

## Notes

- Consumers: compute extraction's descriptor generalization (`compute.photo-descriptor`), media and recovery's schema versioning, conversion tooling's compatibility table, package documentation and independent published-package acceptance (the non-face example and its support boundary).
- Non-face support stays labelled unqualified with its named blocker until the joint proof passes; a type walkthrough proves no runtime behaviour.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#external-developer-journey-and-non-face-models, #package-and-operation-contracts, #stylegan-js.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `descriptor.ts` FFHQ 1024 and 512 px fixtures express every field with no hidden constants; the five journey steps are typed test cases.
- [x] Recovery schema: candidate fixtures (schema 1 and 2, PNG and WebP) parse through `parseRecoveryMetadata` unchanged; a 512 px descriptor fixture with a different layer count round-trips; a morph request mixing equal-shaped latents from two `ModelIdentity` values is rejected with a typed error (type test plus validator vector).
- [x] The external consumer compiles against the packed descriptor declarations.
- [x] Type-level tests per descriptor union and validator fuzzing for descriptor-bearing metadata (fixed seed, recorded case count, typed rejection) pass in CI; a type test imports every descriptor export from the `stylegan-js` entry point and fails on a missing one; unit tests are listed in `check-tests-listed`.

title: Schedule approved acquisition synthesis-first and overlap it with photo choosing under aggregate buffers
description:
## Background
Candidate synthesis-first prefetch exists but pauses for foreground work; acquisition is delayed in parts of the photo
flow. The old two-chunk phone read-ahead is a per-worker bound and does not bound several overlapping workers.
Contracts freeze aggregate transfer/read-ahead/hash/write-buffer limits.

## Why
The operator's performance refinement: start approved acquisition before crop OK and overlap it with input work so
the post-confirmation wait shrinks.

## Scope
- Start the selected acquisition right after approval; prioritize synthesis prerequisites so seed/text generation is
  usable first; acquire the small detector/alignment prerequisite promptly; overlap remaining encoder transfer with
  local inspection, choosing faces and adjusting crops.
- Crop OK freezes input/order and queues encoding without waiting for downloads; the selected generator's readiness
  permits a face while encoder assets are in flight.
- Aggregate transfer budget with digest deduplication; acquisition holds no heavyweight compute permit while waiting;
  foreground-required assets outrank optional preparation; lower-priority work pauses when measured responsiveness or
  memory requires.
- Progress counts overlapping work once; setup progress sits in the crop/source modal status, then the owning tile.

## Out of scope
Warming (milestone); manager internals.

## Considerations
Overlapping downloads do not require simultaneous hydrated networks, all 108 encoder shards in RAM, or concurrent heavy
inference.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** Scheduling lives in the operation controller (ws:opctl) and the manager's acquisition queue (ws:manager). If implementation finds it must edit one of them after all, it first runs `br dep add fm-6fw9 fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph), adds the file to the conflict list in fm-bhw and records the change in its receipt (the plan's rule: an edge is added when an edit is discovered).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Fake-clock scheduler tests: synthesis assets complete before encoder assets under contention; a seed request during encoder transfer starts synthesis as soon as generator assets verify; aggregate buffer never exceeds the contract limit; no compute permit held by acquisition.
- [ ] Request-log run on the built app (cold profile): approval -> generator requests first; photo choose and crop happen while encoder bytes transfer; OK queues encode; first useful face timestamp precedes encoder completion.
- [ ] Foreground responsiveness: input latency during transfer recorded (measured, no threshold until contracts milestone 2).
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic run in CI (`npm test` workspace target) and pass.
- [ ] Each end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Every network claim is asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Exposed waits measured on the built app (cold and warm cache; desktop CPU, desktop WebGPU and one phone-class cell where available): approval -> first model byte, approval -> first useful face, crop OK -> encode start, encode end -> face file ready, and the complete choose -> generate/encode -> export journey, each recorded in the receipt as "measured, no threshold" with the event-log step IDs. Any overlap, warming or reuse opportunity found is recorded in the targeted research record (affected cache/device/workload, evidence or hypothesis, cost, next test) and raised to the operator/planner; it is not turned into a visitor setting.

title: Re-home promote.py and the deploy job; clean-clone deploy acceptance
description:
## Goal
Make promotion from this repository fail closed and re-home classic's `next-site.yml` deploy job (qualified-artifact preview deployment, live-byte checks, runtime-mirror deploy and warm) with the qualified-push cadence and a single-publisher guard, then prove the whole re-homed deploy path from a clean clone. Without this the monorepo cannot publish `next.facemorph.me` and classic cannot be wound down; delivery, diagnostics control, static names publication, the ONNX Runtime Web evaluation and classic wind-down build on it.

## Scope
- `hosting/next-static/promote.py` (candidate `6107f80`): arguments `--build-run`, `--qualification-run`, `--runtime`, `--catalogue`, `--work`, `--publish`, `--discard-after`. Line ~42 refuses a catalogue that differs from the one built into the qualified artifact; lines ~46-55 read `autoresearch/results.tsv` only `if ledger.exists()` and require a `keep` row for the runtime manifest's kernel `candidateId`, so a checkout without the ledger silently skips the research-backing check.
- Re-homed: read the canonical ledger re-homed by autoresearch stage 1; a missing ledger, missing kernel provenance (candidate ID and source hash in the runtime manifest) or missing qualified-artifact proof is an error. `--publish` explicit; non-publishing dry run against a qualified artifact.
- Deploy workflow in `.github/workflows/`, gated on the exact-artifact CPU/compiled-UI gates. Classic steps: verify artifact SHA256SUMS; restore/rebuild the runtime set (`mirror-runtime.py`); stage (`stage.py`); deploy the site (`npx -y wrangler@4.149.0 deploy --config hosting/next-static/wrangler.jsonc --assets public`); live checks (site serves this build, historic hello preview, every runtime file); deploy the runtime mirror; warm the mirror. Rollback from classic: `wrangler versions deploy <previous>@100`.
- Mirror deploy and warm call the model-host package commands from `hosting.serving`, after the site deploy and its live-byte checks. Warm semantics (classic `6107f80` lines ~215-220): every staged path matching `^runtime/(assets|chunks|manifests|photo|encoder-stream)/`, `curl -I --retry 3 --retry-all-errors` equivalent (retries only for transient errors), 8 in parallel, fail on any non-200, print `<n> runtime files held by <origin>`. The target origin comes from workflow target configuration; `models.facemorph.me` is not hard-coded, so a dry run warms a test mirror.
- Step definitions come from the same frozen import revision as `hosting/next-mirror/` (`inventory.import`, `6107f80` or later), so provenance is one commit.
- Single-publisher guard: a repository variable naming the targets this repository may publish, checked before any `wrangler deploy`, both site and mirror. The job stays disabled for `next.facemorph.me` and `facemorph.me` until delivery's candidate-source handover. Classic keeps publishing until then.
- Concurrency group that never cancels a publication in progress (`cancel-in-progress: false`).
- Clean-clone acceptance in one run: staging and a non-publishing promotion dry run against a qualified artifact reproduce classic's output fields; promotion refuses without the ledger; collector tests pass; catalogue pipeline dry run makes zero API-host requests; the deploy workflow dry run reaches a test target and a test mirror and warms it.

## Out of scope
- Running production promotion; turning the workflow on for `next.facemorph.me` or `facemorph.me` (delivery).
- Reusable chunk/manifest hosting (`hosting.*`); diagnostics consent UI and retention wording; names generator.

## Notes
- Exactly one repository's workflow may publish a target at a time; any publish is an explicit `--publish`.
- Optional matrix/GPU evidence is not silently made a promotion gate.
- Classic wind-down depends on this: the monorepo must deploy and warm `models.facemorph.me` itself before classic's workflow stops (`winddown.publishers`, `winddown.tree`). The mirror fills itself from the site, so an unwarmed mirror after handover holds only paths already there.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-deploy-and-collector-re-homing (Acceptance); #autoresearch-re-homing (promotion coupling); #candidate-preservation-comparison--12-october-2026 (delivery cadence).
Operator revision, 25 October 2026: physical phone validation is local, never CI. The release implementer runs the exact candidate on phone/eris locally before delivery and against the live site after delivery, keeping honest unavailable outcomes. Hosted Android/iOS/macOS/Windows lanes remain required release CI. Ordinary implementation slices close on executed relevant local tests and do not wait for CI; retain the full integrated deploy acceptance for this release capability.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Named tests: `missing ledger refuses`; `ledger without a keep row for the kernel candidate refuses`; `missing kernel provenance refuses`; `catalogue differing from the qualified artifact refuses`; `dry run without --publish publishes nothing` (intercepted requests show no publish host).
- [ ] Guard test: a publish attempt (site or mirror) to a classic-owned target is refused before any network call.
- [ ] Warm tests: a test mirror missing one path fails the job naming that path; all present prints the held count equal to the manifest's immutable runtime path count; the mirror origin comes from configuration (scan: no literal `models.facemorph.me` in the workflow).
- [ ] Concurrency test: two queued pushes, the second waits; no in-progress publication is cancelled.
- [ ] Workflow dry run on a test target exercises every step, including live-byte checks and mirror deploy and warm to a test mirror.
- [ ] One CI run from a clean clone: staging reproduces classic's output fields for the same artifact; non-publishing promotion dry run passes; promotion refuses without the ledger; collector tests pass; catalogue dry run shows zero API-host requests; deploy dry run reaches the test target and warms the test mirror, with every immutable runtime path checked and a non-200 failing the run.
- [ ] Unit tests listed in test discovery and pass locally with the CI command; CI verifies after push.
- [ ] The release implementer runs the four device-lab cells locally (`eris-webgpu`, `eris-cpu`, `phone-webgpu`, `phone-cpu`; physical phone never in CI) on the exact artifact digest before each deploy to next.facemorph.me and again against the live site after it (operator, 24 October): a real failure stops the deploy and passes the affected beads back; an unavailable device or runner is recorded as untested and never blocks.
- [ ] close-check (conditional, from the parallelism pass): clean-clone deploy acceptance at close should include the collector if fm-a0c1 landed; tick once it holds or does not apply, saying which in the close reason
- [ ] The deploy job calls .github/workflows/release-gate.yml (fm-5klw) for the artifact it publishes and needs its gate job, so any failed required hosted lane blocks the deploy; local device failures are repaired before release, unavailable physical cells are recorded honestly.

title: Confirmed-crop policy, byte ceilings and direct e4e without redetection
description:
## Split (parallelism pass, 24 October 2026)
The package/core work of this bead moved to fm-smdf (Confirmed-crop policy module: frozen ConfirmedCrop, single derivation and byte ceilings), which edits no shared file and starts as soon as its own inputs exist. This bead keeps: the direct-e4e bridge rewiring (detection only proposes before OK; zero detector/align/warp after `crop-confirmed`; one e4e attempt or one terminal error; no control flow keyed on detector error text) and the flipped crop.repro bridge tests. The scope text below is kept for context; where it describes work now owned by fm-smdf, that bead owns and accepts it and this bead consumes the result.

## Goal
Locked requirement (alignment-failure reference): an eligible confirmed crop proceeds to e4e without another successful detection or a repeated crop loop. This row adds the single frozen, versioned derivation from approved pixels to the encoder tensor (with a stable cache/provenance identity), enforces decode and crop byte ceilings before large allocations so constrained devices fail with an actionable message instead of crashing, and rewires the bridge so detection only proposes a crop before OK and never runs after it.

## Scope
**Preprocessing policy**
- Candidate: `photo/crop.mjs`, `photo/crop-view.mjs`, `photo/image-header.mjs` (EXIF), `photo/selection-worker.mjs`, photo-runtime local preprocessing (dlib/Pillow WASM, `photo-runtime/dist/photo-native.*`), e4e input `[1,3,256,256]`. Contracts milestone 1 freezes the policy.
- Eligibility: decodable supported pixels within declared limits, explicit orientation, alpha/color handling and the encoder's preprocessing requirements; not successful redetection.
- Frozen `ConfirmedCrop` record created at OK (readonly TS type plus `Object.freeze`): `{sourceRevision, sourceDigest, rect: {left, top, width, height} in oriented source pixels, rotationDegrees, exifOrientation (1-8) and whether applied, policyVersion, policyParams}`. Never edited; Adjust Crop or Encode image makes a new record with a new revision. Identity = SHA-256 over a canonical encoding of every field; it is the cache and provenance key.
- One path: `deriveEncoderInput(sourcePixels, confirmedCrop) -> {tensor: Float32Array [1,3,256,256], tensorDigest, policyVersion}` covering all eight EXIF orientations, rotation, crop, resize, color and normalization, run once per confirmed crop. Retry reuses retained derived pixels; re-derivation from a retained source must give the same `tensorDigest`.
- Guides (face guide, stencil, handles, grid) are display overlays only; derivation reads decoded source pixels, never a UI canvas; the policy module imports no DOM/canvas display code.
- Single-input limits preserved from candidate `src/Next/photo/crop.mjs`: `CROP_MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024` compressed ("Choose a photo smaller than 64 MB."), `CROP_MAX_PIXELS = 120 * 1024 * 1024`, `CROP_MAX_EDGE = 20000` px (both from `inspectImage` on the header, before full decode), `CROP_OUTPUT = 1024`, `PREVIEW_MAX_EDGE = 4096`. Changing them needs separate qualification; they are not browser memory bounds.
- 25 MB limit in `photo/align-photo.mjs`: limits only the detector proposal. Files between 25 MB and 64 MiB get no proposal, are labelled "detector not run" (never "no face found") and keep manual crop through to encoding. (Planner rule; see Notes.)

**Byte ceilings**
- The 120 × 1024² source limit can be 480 MiB for one RGBA buffer before decoder, canvas, crop and encoder copies. Contracts milestone 2 sets ceilings per decode route from measured peak transient bytes on named workers; an unmeasured route has no ceiling and is not admitted. Until then tests report "measured, no threshold".
- After header inspection and before any full-size decode or copy, check retained-source, crop-buffer and transient-decode ceilings separately; decode to a bounded working representation where supported while keeping the confirmed coordinates; otherwise an actionable size message. Ceilings may refuse inputs the single-input limits allow on a constrained route; they never relax them. Not a claim of browser RSS control.
- Over-budget batch admission gives a reduce-selection / remove-retry-input message before any keypoint allocation; no truncation or hidden eviction.

**Direct e4e**
- Before OK: detector-driven alignment/warping proposes a crop, shown to the person; multi-face selection precedes confirmation.
- After OK: only `deriveEncoderInput` on approved pixels, then e4e directly. Zero detector, `alignPhoto`, alignment or warp calls after `crop-confirmed`; optional validation may log (`crop.validate`) but cannot change `tensorDigest` or block.
- Remove the post-confirmation exactly-one-face requirement and the error-text-driven reopen (no control flow keyed on `No face was found|More than one face was found` in `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` or the runtime). Detector failure after OK (thrown, timeout, zero faces, several faces, not run) never reopens the prompt; only explicit Adjust Crop or Encode image does.
- Exactly one e4e attempt per eligible confirmed crop, ending in a result or one terminal error from a closed set (`unsupported-pixels`, `over-limit`, `encoder-unavailable`, `encoder-invalidated`, `cancelled`) with plain recovery text.
- A not-run detector (assets refused or absent) is not a detection failure; refusing detector assets keeps manual crop usable and starts no downloads.
- Preserve cancellation and input revisions; Cancel before OK abandons preparation without e4e or keypoints; stale results rejected. Flip the crop.repro tests to passing.
- e4e may reconstruct unaligned crops oddly; that does not forbid the direct route. Malformed/unsupported pixels still fail clearly.

## Out of scope
Crop modal/editor visuals and multi-selection UI (face controls). Consent modal (acquisition consent). Setting the ceiling values (contracts milestone 2). The batch queue (crop.queue).

## Notes
- The 25 MB detector-proposal-only rule was chosen during bead conversion and is listed in PLAN.md "Planner proposals awaiting a veto". Removable clause: if vetoed, the at/over-limit cases switch to the chosen alternative (reject over 25 MB at entry with a size message, or raise the detector limit to 64 MiB after a measured memory check); the "detector not run" label stays. No `docs/decisions/` entry (24 October rule: no separate decision log).
- The policy part edits no shared file; the bridge rewiring does.
- Shared-file order (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October; revised in the 24 October final pass): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in one sequence enforced by needs edges, never concurrently: `provider.native` -> `provider.webgl` -> `provider.route-admission` -> `migration.project-json` (one-line ProjectJson import swap) -> typed facade (`migration.facade`) -> `compute.synthesis` -> `compute.photo-descriptor` -> `compute.app-rebind` -> `crop.fix` -> `crop.queue` -> `media.reader-wiring` -> `media.export` -> `media.schema` -> `morph.render` -> `morph.guards` -> `media.session` -> face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Rows that must not edit these files: `crop.repro`, `compute.blend`, `compute.package-surface`, `media.envelope`, `provider.admission` (evidence), `crop.ported-app` and `compute.ported-app` (acceptance on the ported app; a fix they need follows the out-of-turn rule below) and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept row; code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) until the bridge's own turn. A row that finds it must edit one of these files outside its turn adds a needs edge to the latest row in the sequence that edits it. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #confirmed-crop-encoding, #confirmed-crop-and-ordered-multi-selection-flow, #crop-fidelity-and-export-flow-clarification, #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] fm-smdf is closed; its modules are what this bead wires in (no second copy of the moved code left in the app).
- [x] `crop-fix.no-redetect-after-ok`, `.one-attempt-or-error`, `.detector-failure-no-reopen` (one case per failure kind including not run), `.not-run-not-failure`, `.explicit-adjust-reopens`, `.cancel-before-ok` (zero e4e, zero keypoints), `.stale-revision`, plus the flipped crop.repro bridge-level tests and a real-bridge facade-harness run of the same case: forced failure after OK runs real e4e exactly once and finishes or shows one actionable terminal error (the built-UI flip runs in `crop.ported-app`).
- [x] Source scan: no control flow keyed on detector error text.
close_reason: All 3 acceptance items met: 7dc9c19 (+8e21a20 closure records). Confirmed crop -> deriveEncoderInput -> exactly one e4e, zero detection after OK; crop-repro bridge cases flipped (real e4e, 0 detection passes), facade crop-fix-after-ok green, confirmed-crop.test 8/8 named cases, source scan clean.

title: Freeze the engine loaded-capability and encoder ownership contract
description:
## Background

`stylegan-js` accepts a caller-supplied, already-loaded model capability with model identity,
dimensions, latent schema, mapping/synthesis and optional e4e support explicit. It never downloads
or manages model files: no model URLs, chunk downloader, OPFS cache, model-host dependency or
UI/reporting policy. Today the e4e encoder streams 108 sequential ORT sessions and may materialise
verified shards over HTTP during execution; moving network acquisition ahead of engine operations is
a deliberate boundary change.

## Why

Compute extraction and the manager cannot be built independently without a frozen handle shape and
ownership rules. This keeps the bounded stream viable on phones without loading the whole encoder.

## Scope

- Loaded handle types: ownership, asset digests, shapes, mapping, synthesis, encoder; actual
  provider, admission and validation state.
- Encoder baseline: the manager/provider adapter supplies an already-loaded encoder capability whose
  typed `encode` operation owns bounded sequential session creation/execution/release; it may read
  verified local shard storage lazily; no engine-originated network acquisition during execution.
  Loaded means ready for offline execution, not all sessions/weights resident in RAM.
- Consent-authorised acquisition and verification of the encoder's required shards finish before
  its admission; unrelated approved acquisition may proceed under its own budgets.
- The engine sees typed `encode`/`abort`/`dispose` operations only: no URLs, OPFS handles or
  `acquireBytes` callbacks. The existing network-repair-capable cache handle is never exposed as an
  offline loaded capability.
- Encoder-to-synthesis residency transition and memory bounds (named, numeric values in m2).
- Typed stage/timing hooks around real model work: await actual inference/readback completion
  (including GPU `mapAsync`); retain e4e verified read/session-create/run/total timings plus actual
  WASM/max-live-session facts. Not submission time, a mock or whole bridge-call duration. Engine
  events stay reporting-transport-free.
- Dependency injection for loaded capabilities; explicit unsupported capabilities; cleanup explicit.

## Typed outputs (citable)

Draft first under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`, then moved by the milestone type-test bead to the module below. Exported names are stable: downstream beads cite them; a rename needs a contract revision and an update of the `contracts.md` export index.

- `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/capability.ts`: `ModelIdentity`, `LoadedModelCapability` (mapping, synthesis, optional encoder; dimensions and latent schema explicit), `LoadedEncoderCapability` (`encode`, `abort`, `dispose` only), `ProviderState` (requested, actual, admission, validation), `UnsupportedCapability`, `ResidencyTransition` (encoder → synthesis), `MemoryBoundName` (named placeholders whose values `contracts.byte-ceilings-freeze` sets).
- `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/timing.ts`: `StageTimingEvent`, `StageCompletionBoundary` (`inference-complete` | `readback-complete` | `map-async-complete`), `E4eTimings` (verifiedReadMs, sessionCreateMs, runMs, totalMs, wasmHeapBytes, maxLiveSessions).
- Consumers: `compute.provider-adapters`, `compute.mapping-synthesis`, `manager.loaded-handles`, `migration.facade-types`, `crop.batch-encode`.

## Out of scope

Manager-side acquisition (contracts.manager-lifecycle-leases). Implementation.

## Considerations

- Any alternative ownership needs equivalent independent-consumer, memory and acquisition-boundary
  evidence before it replaces this baseline.
- Worker placement and GPU residency are measured implementation choices, not contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts.md` engine section and a draft `stylegan-js` capability type file record exact signatures, ownership, memory-bound names and the residency transition.
- [ ] A walkthrough traces seed→mapping→synthesis and confirmed crop→encode with a caller-loaded capability and no manager import, showing no network, URL or cache access from the engine.
- [ ] Stage/timing hook types name completion boundaries (readback, `mapAsync`) and e4e timing fields.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Every name listed under "Typed outputs (citable)" exists in the draft type file and has a row in the `contracts.md` export index naming its consumers.
notes: Anchors: PLAN.md#package-and-operation-contracts; PLAN.md#stylegan-js; #browser-model-manager.

title: Verify verified-cache warming if it ships
description:
## Background
Verified-cache warming is optional: it ships only if a targeted round shows a foreground-safe benefit within memory and mobile budgets. Local warming must issue zero model-network requests including repair.

## Why
If it ships, its zero-network and preemption guarantees need integrated evidence.

## Scope
- Warmup on eligible cached routes.
- Missing/corrupt/runtime-asset cases with zero speculative network.
- Immediate foreground preemption/settlement; warm ownership transfer; constrained phone encoder teardown (release generator warmth before e4e, rehydrate after).
- Static names and completed-result display never initialize inference.

## Out of scope
Measuring the benefit (research evaluator/targeted round).

## Considerations
- If warming does not ship, close this bead with a receipt stating 'not shipped' and record the request-log check that warming issues zero requests.
- Benefit threshold set at the warming milestone; until then 'measured, no threshold'.
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Request log shows zero model-host requests from warming in every case.
- [ ] Foreground job admitted after warm settlement without exceeding reservations.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome) through the shared emitter from `build.event-log-core` (fm-bd03) and passes `scripts/check-event-log.ts`; the log is kept as a CI artifact, privacy-filtered like diagnostics; screenshots kept on failure.
- [ ] Each case is listed in this leaf's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix row IDs or defect numbers it grades.
- [ ] Ran against the named release-candidate artifact digest (the same digest the join report checks); a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded failed or untested, never passed.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: After go-live: lasting usage and error insight for production; revamp or retire diagnostics
description:
## Goal
Reminder and cleanup bead for the end (operator, 24 October 2026). The diagnostics collector (hosting/next-cloudflare worker, R2 with KV fallback) is kept after go-live for a while, because it is how we understand usage and especially errors. Some time after facemorph.me promotion, design the lasting production approach and then revamp or retire the collector.

## Scope
- Review what the collector and GA showed in the weeks after go-live: which questions were answered, which errors mattered.
- Propose the ongoing analytics and error-reporting approach for production (respecting the current privacy rules: GPC/DNT, no cookie banner, opt-out), with options and costs; prefer what works without Cloudflare-specific services in case `ops.leave-cloudflare` happens.
- Implement it, then revamp or retire the old collector and its stored reports per the retention rules.
- next.facemorph.me stays up after go-live as the post-go-live test host; nothing here removes it.

## Out of scope
The changeover stats (ops.stats-retirement).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Written proposal in PLAN.md with the chosen approach, the operator informed.
- [ ] New approach live on facemorph.me and receiving real events/errors (shown in its own UI).
- [ ] Old collector revamped or removed; stored reports handled per the retention rules; privacy text updated.

title: Run the clean-consumer smoke test from packed tarballs with content scan
description:
## Background
Integrated verification's packages sub-result proves the non-face joint journey from local packs; this item is the publication-preparation smoke against the final docs and bound versions. A local `npm pack` is preflight, not independent acceptance.

## Why
Catches missing files, repository-only paths and doc steps that only work inside the monorepo before anything is published.

## Scope
- Fresh directory outside the monorepo, no workspace links: install the three packed tarballs, follow the quickstart verbatim (convert via container, host statically, manager-loaded inference and morph, PNG/lossless-WebP export and exact reopen, direct caller-loaded engine use, non-face example with no detector/e4e download).
- Content scan of each tarball: no weights, repository-only paths, secrets, private provenance; emitted JS/types/exports/worker assets present.
- Record every doc step that was missing or confusing and fix the docs before closing.

## Out of scope
Independent review of registry versions (`fm-fy2.21`).

## Considerations
- Author-run smoke never substitutes for the independent review.

## The joint journey, step by step (polish r1)
Run in a fresh directory outside the monorepo, from the final docs verbatim, with the three packed tarballs at their bound versions (no workspace links). Each step is a separate step ID in the structured event log:
1. **Trusted checkpoint acquisition**: follow the converter docs to acquire the documented non-face checkpoint; check its SHA-256 against the published value; the trusted-pickle warning appears before the command.
2. **Pinned container conversion**: clone the converter at the release-candidate tag, build the container (image digest recorded), convert, and run `verify`, whose upstream PyTorch reference check must pass the declared tolerance.
3. **Developer-controlled static hosting**: publish the outputs with the host package's documented commands to a local HTTPS static server under the test's control (no FaceMorph hostname, catalogue, alias or secret); check MIME, CORS, cache/digest headers.
4. **Manager-loaded inference**: authorize acquisition through `browser-model-manager`, load the capability, pass it to `stylegan-js`, map a seed and synthesize; raw output within the model's declared tolerance of the reference.
5. **Caller-loaded inference**: load the capability directly without importing the manager, same checks.
6. **Morphing**: a multi-input morph (at least 3 faces) with the same model; descriptor-driven geometry.
7. **PNG and lossless-WebP export and reopen**: export both, reopen, latent and model identity exact, decoded pixels equal the supplied pixels; a latent from another checkpoint with equal shape is refused for combination.
8. **Network assertions from the log**: zero requests at package construction and status reads; zero face detector or e4e requests anywhere in the non-face run.

## Named content-scan test
Runs `package-tarball-content-scan` (`scripts/packages/check-tarball-contents.mjs`), whose rules, four profiles, JSON report and self-test are defined and created by `compute.consumer-example` (fm-u38t, section "Citable contract"). This item runs it on the three tarballs at their bound versions (profiles `stylegan-js`, `browser-model-manager`, `cloudflare-model-host`) and on the converter build context (`model-conv-context`), keeps the JSON reports, and fixes any finding before closing. It adds no rules of its own; a missing rule found here is added to fm-u38t's profiles and self-test.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Smoke run passes from the docs verbatim; network log shows no requests at construction/status reads and no detector/e4e requests for non-face.
- [ ] Content scan passes for all tarballs.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots are kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Network claims are asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Each of the eight journey steps has its own step ID and outcome in the event log; network assertions (none at construction/status reads, no detector/e4e requests) are computed from that log.
- [ ] `package-tarball-content-scan` passes on all three tarballs and the converter build context, and its self-test proves each planted violation (weight file, repository-only path, fake secret, missing required file) fails the scan; the JSON report is retained.

title: Provider adapters on manager handles; mapping, synthesis and numerical gates in stylegan-js
description:
## Split (parallelism pass, 24 October 2026)
The package/core work of this bead moved to fm-3h3w (stylegan-js core: provider adapters, map/synthesize, canaries and numerical gates in the package), which edits no shared file and starts as soon as its own inputs exist. This bead keeps: switching `browser/runtime.mjs`, `browser/ort-worker.mjs` and the bridge to the package adapters and `map`/`synthesize`, deleting the moved app code, and proving it in the real-bridge harness. The scope text below is kept for context; where it describes work now owned by fm-3h3w, that bead owns and accepts it and this bead consumes the result.

## Goal
Move the core of the engine into `packages/stylegan-js` as strict TypeScript: engine-side adapters for every retained route that run on the browser model manager's verified-local loaded handles, plus `map` and `synthesize` with the canary set, admission receipts and numerical gates. The engine accepts a caller-supplied loaded capability (identity, dimensions, latent schema, mapping/synthesis, optional e4e) and never downloads or manages files. Raw output must stay within the frozen tolerances so published identity (for example static names) does not depend on which runtime produced it.

## Scope
**Provider adapters**
- Candidate sources: `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` (~400 lines), `browser/ort-worker.mjs` (~420 lines), direct WGSL engine `browser/webgpu-direct.mjs`/`webgpu-engine.mjs`, `fused-resample-v1.mjs`, `route-selection.mjs`, `route-priors.mjs`, `identity.mjs`, `originals.mjs`.
- Typed adapters for each retained route: ORT WASM CPU (bounded 1–4 threads when isolation/cores allow), ORT WebGPU (pinned 1.22.0, JSEP build), desktop direct WGSL engine with RGBA8 conversion/rounding, and mobile ORT WebGPU, consuming manager loaded handles through the contract-frozen signatures (contracts milestone 1). The manager owns shard reads and bounded session lifecycle.
- Explicit worker exports (no app aliases); worker payloads cloneable; no promise, signal or callback objects in worker messages.
- Typed invalidation passthrough: browser eviction, corruption, cross-tab deletion or device/worker loss settles affected operations with a typed error and releases resources, with no network repair.
- Preserve: adapter probing before GPU acquisition (an actual adapter, not `navigator.gpu` alone), failure-only route preference, `warmMapping()` overlap with loading on direct and ORT WebGPU (including eligible mobile GPU), sequential CPU loading, and the gating that keeps custom WGSL kernels off phone GPUs that cannot run them (mobile ORT WebGPU stays their route).
- `manifest.webgl` coefficients feed direct WebGPU and survive WebGL execution removal.
- Record the adapter surface so a later ORT runtime change (JSEP is being removed upstream) touches one place; adopt no new runtime here.

**Mapping, synthesis and gates**
- `map(seed | text latent)` and `synthesize(latent)` with abort/dispose, request/input-revision/attempt IDs and the actual provider identity in results.
- Move the canary set, content/provider/canary-set keyed admission receipts (`canary-qualification.mjs`) and numerical gate code into the package. Keep scheduling: a genuinely cold visitor runs one canary before the first face, the rest run one at a time behind foreground work and resume safely; compatible warm receipts skip canaries; CI `fullQualify` runs all.
- Preserve bounded GPU submit/readback overlap, RGBA8 direct output, `warmMapping()` overlap, bounded CPU threads, warm reuse and output-cache hits needing no inference.
- Typed stage/timing hooks (reporting-transport-free events) that await real completion, including GPU `mapAsync`, never submission time or whole-bridge duration.
- Frozen tolerances: product canaries max RGB difference 1 (0–255) and max sampled raw-float error 0.002 (alpha excluded); research/reference suites at their own frozen tolerances; e4e W+ 0.0001. Raw output before compression against the independent qualified reference, across CPU/WebGPU routes. Never widen, change precision or substitute a visual check to let a faster implementation pass.

## Out of scope
Manager acquisition, OPFS/Cache Storage, checksum repair (manager). WebGL execution (removed by provider simplification). Admission policy and copy (provider simplification, operation controller). ORT Web version changes (dependency currency). Descriptor generalization and e4e (compute.photo-descriptor). Morph frame production (morph.render). App rebinding (compute.app-rebind).

## Notes
- No new performance claim: architecture parity without faster timings is not a performance keep.
- Shared-file order (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October; revised in the 24 October final pass): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in one sequence enforced by needs edges, never concurrently: `provider.native` -> `provider.webgl` -> `provider.route-admission` -> `migration.project-json` (one-line ProjectJson import swap) -> typed facade (`migration.facade`) -> `compute.synthesis` -> `compute.photo-descriptor` -> `compute.app-rebind` -> `crop.fix` -> `crop.queue` -> `media.reader-wiring` -> `media.export` -> `media.schema` -> `morph.render` -> `morph.guards` -> `media.session` -> face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Rows that must not edit these files: `crop.repro`, `compute.blend`, `compute.package-surface`, `media.envelope`, `provider.admission` (evidence), `crop.ported-app` and `compute.ported-app` (acceptance on the ported app; a fix they need follows the out-of-turn rule below) and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept row; code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) until the bridge's own turn. A row that finds it must edit one of these files outside its turn adds a needs edge to the latest row in the sequence that edits it. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #compute-extraction, #stylegan-js, #synthesis-correctness-and-export-quality, #provider-simplification.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] fm-3h3w is closed; its modules are what this bead wires in (no second copy of the moved code left in the app).
- [x] Each retained route runs through the package adapter in the headless real-bridge harness; intercepted requests show zero engine-originated network requests.
- [x] Route selection through the app unchanged versus the control (route-priors, route-selection and mobile-runtime tests pass against the wired app).
- [x] Existing app tests touching runtime/ort-worker pass, adapted only where the code they assert moved.
- [x] package consumer gates (with fm-7ge). If fm-7ge has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-7ge (`br update fm-7ge --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-7ge
- [x] One ORT adapter surface: the manager's src/adapters/ort-generator.ts (fm-ffn7's port) is replaced by @facemorph/stylegan-js/engine loadCpuGenerator once the bundled app resolves the engine entry (with fm-3h3w)

title: Port one provider adapter from the candidate onto loaded handles
description:
## Background
The provider adapter owns shard reads and bounded session lifecycle. Candidate encoder: 108 sequential ORT sessions, streamed, single-threaded, bounded; generator: CPU/WebGPU ORT and direct WebGPU sessions.

## Why
Compute extraction consumes the manager's adapter and moves only engine-side orchestration, so the two workstreams never claim the same code.

## Scope

## Out of scope
Remaining adapters (follow under compute extraction or later manager leaves).

## Considerations
Typed stage/timing hooks await actual inference/readback completion (incl. GPU `mapAsync`), never submission time.

title: Build milestone 1: desktop matrix, package consumer gates, required statuses
description:
## Goal

Complete the build milestone that precedes the application port and provider simplification: carry over the desktop browser matrix lane with every cell, add the package consumer gates the extraction workstreams are accepted against (exports, worker entries, clean pack/install, no import side effects, package boundaries), and bind this repository's required status checks from classic's actual branch protection so no lane silently stops gating. With this bead merged, a clean clone runs the whole static, test and build chain.

## Scope

**Desktop matrix** — `.github/workflows/next-matrix.yml` ("New site browser matrix"), jobs `engines` and `summary`, `workflow_dispatch` against a deployed or staged origin input, `fail-fast: false`.
- Five cells, all kept: `ubuntu-24.04` × Chromium, Firefox, WebKit; `macos-14` × WebKit, Firefox. Runner from `scripts/matrix-tools` (pinned Playwright); driver `scripts/next-matrix.mjs <engine>` (repaired by the identity/retired-tests bead); summary `scripts/next-matrix-summary.py` into the step summary; artifacts `next-matrix-<os>-<engine>`, `next-matrix-summary`.
- Per cell, each stage reports pass/fail/incomplete-not-shipped with cause; the photo stage passes only with real encoder events from an independent metadata-free photo; the summary never shows a failed or incomplete cell as passing. macOS WebKit labelled "Playwright WebKit, not Safari"; Linux WebKit "not iOS". No dedicated Windows browser job exists.
- Shared lookup/provenance/path filters/concurrency/caches from the shared action; network claims through the interception helper; traces/screenshots on failure; lane paths adapted for `apps/web` and the four packages.

**Package consumer gates**
- Per package: pack, install into a temporary consumer outside the workspace, type-check against public declarations, resolve every `exports` entry, load emitted worker assets through at least one bundler, assert no repository-only path aliases in runtime imports. `stylegan-js` ships ESM JS plus generated `.d.ts`, explicit exports and explicit emitted worker entry points; consumers need no app Vite aliases or filesystem layout.
- Import side effects: importing each package in a sandbox touches no globals and performs no I/O (`browser-model-manager` import in particular).
- Boundaries (dependency-graph assertion): packages do not import app code; non-app packages do not import React; the engine has no network/cache imports.
- Runs in CI on every package edit.

**Required statuses**
- Read classic's branch protection/rulesets and required status names read-only (`gh api`), never inferred from workflow filenames. Configure equivalent required checks on this repository's default branch (this repository's settings only). Status names `<workflow name> / <job id>` stay identical where job IDs are kept.
- Classic workflow destinations to reconcile against: `next-site.yml` (artifact, compiled-ui, qualify → site lane; deploy → deploy workstream); `next-e2e.yml` real-ui-cpu; `next-matrix.yml` (manual, never required); `mobile-browser.yml` (android, ios, ios-product-artifact, ios-product-simulator); `next-gpu-lane.yml` (self-hosted, deliberately not required); `research-built-ui-media-v1.yml`, `research-rgba-screen-v1.yml` (research stage 2, experimental, never required); `name-catalogue.yml` (static names); `self-host-build.yml` (stays in classic as the distribution's rot check); `deploy.yml` (legacy .NET/Vercel, historical); `desktop-product.yml`, `desktop-native-inference.yml`, `desktop-candidates.yml` (retired with native retirement; shared browser/artifact/media checks re-homed, never substituted for a browser check).
- Non-required by design: manual matrix, GPU lane, research workflows, bleeding-edge lane.

## Out of scope

Real package content (extraction workstreams); publication docs; Windows or physical-phone qualification claims; changing classic's settings (classic wind-down).

## Notes

- A workflow definition is not a passing result (7 October manual matrix run 37555426933 failed; recent GPU evidence failed adapter admission). This repository must not publish `next.facemorph.me` before the source handover. Native-package retirement does not retire desktop-browser checks.
