title: Re-home the deploy job with qualified-push cadence and a single-publisher rule
description:
## Background
`next-site.yml` deploy job: qualified-artifact preview deployment and live-byte checks on every qualified candidate push (diagnostics stored in R2). Classic keeps publishing until the explicit candidate-source handover.

## Why
Keep the ordinary CI-driven preview cadence after handover without two repositories publishing the same target.

## Scope
Workflow in this repository gated on the exact-artifact CPU/compiled-UI gates; a publisher lock/guard so it is disabled for a target until delivery hands it over; live-byte checks; deploy warms the runtime mirror.

## Out of scope
Turning it on for `next.facemorph.me` or `facemorph.me` (ws:delivery).

## Considerations
Optional matrix/GPU evidence is not silently made a promotion gate.

## Classic job to re-home (candidate `6107f80` `next-site.yml` `deploy`)
Steps: verify artifact SHA256SUMS; restore/rebuild the runtime set (`mirror-runtime.py`); stage (`stage.py`); deploy the site (`npx -y wrangler@4.149.0 deploy --config hosting/next-static/wrangler.jsonc --assets public`); live checks (site serves this build, historic hello preview, every runtime file); deploy the runtime mirror (`wrangler deploy --config hosting/next-mirror/wrangler.jsonc`); warm the mirror with every immutable runtime file. Rollback note from classic: `wrangler versions deploy <previous>@100`. Here the mirror deploy and warm call the model-host package commands from `hosting.serving`, so this leaf depends on it. The job stays disabled for `next.facemorph.me` and `facemorph.me` until `delivery.candidate-source-handover`; the guard is a repository variable naming the targets this repository may publish, checked before any `wrangler deploy`.

## Mirror warm semantics to keep (polish r2)
Classic warm step (`next-site.yml` deploy job, `6107f80` lines ~215-220): select every staged path matching `^runtime/(assets|chunks|manifests|photo|encoder-stream)/`, request each from the mirror with `curl -I --retry 3 --retry-all-errors` (8 in parallel), fail the job on any non-200 and print `<n> runtime files held by models.facemorph.me`. Keep these semantics: every immutable runtime path, bounded parallelism, retries only for transient errors, the job fails if any path is missing, and the held count is printed and written to the receipt. The target origin comes from the workflow's target configuration. `models.facemorph.me` is not hard-coded, so a dry run warms a test mirror. The publisher guard is checked before the mirror deploy as well as before the site deploy.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Workflow dry run on a test target succeeds; guard prevents publishing to a target owned by classic.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/deploy/ci-workflow.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, and the log is retained as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics). Network claims are asserted from the log, never from screenshots.
- [ ] Dry run against a test target exercises every step including mirror deploy and warm (to a test mirror) and the live-byte checks; the guard test shows a publish attempt to a classic-owned target is refused before any network call.
- [ ] Warm step unit/dry-run tests: a test mirror missing one path fails the job naming that path; all paths present prints and records the held count equal to the manifest's immutable runtime path count; the target mirror origin is taken from configuration (no literal `models.facemorph.me` in the workflow); the publisher guard refuses a classic-owned mirror target before any network call.
- [ ] Deploy workflow uses a concurrency group that never cancels a publication in progress (cancel-in-progress: false); a test run with two queued pushes shows the second waits
notes:
Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-deploy-and-collector-re-homing; #candidate-preservation-comparison--12-october-2026 (delivery cadence).
Polish r2 (C): concrete warm semantics from classic; configurable mirror target; guard covers mirror deploy.

title: Controller port: replay all control goldens and retire Product.fs-reading checks
description:
## Background
Candidate photo/crop tests read `Product.fs` source text, bridge-import checks inspect generated `.fs.js`, and `scripts/check-progress-copy.mjs` asserts frame-only morph copy and old bridge source patterns.

## Why
The controller milestone is accepted on transition tests with goldens recorded by driving the control artifact; source-language assertions must become equivalent TS/schema/operation checks so coverage is not silently lost.

title: Optional verified-cache warming: round, then ship or drop
description:
## Goal
Optional and deferred. Find out whether eagerly hydrating the selected route's verified cached synthesis assets, session and mapping hides repeat-visit setup without hurting foreground work, and ship it only if a targeted research round shows a foreground-safe benefit within memory and mobile budgets. Today cache-only prefetch creates no session; eager warming is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated speedup. Consent and overlap do not wait on this bead.

## Scope
- **Round.** Targeted research row "Verified-cache runtime warming": cached files/new browser vs already-resident session; eager selected-generator preparation vs demand load; immediate next-face request; missing/corrupt shard and memory-constrained cases. Protected metrics: reload -> first/nth new face, CPU/GPU mapping/load/readback, peak live reservations, foreground wait, zero speculative network, recovery without inference. Run through the research evaluator's warming adapters under the shared device lease (discarded warmup, same-cell ABBA x3 initial paired design per the research protocol), desktop and phone-class cells where available, on a lease worker or a read-only clone (never a worktree). Benefit threshold comes from the round's protocol (phase2-numeric). Result rows go in the re-homed research ledger; the ship/drop outcome and threshold are stated in this bead's closing commit.
- **If it ships, implementation:** on a visible idle app for an eligible anticipated route, after boot/recovery, warm only the selected route's verified cached synthesis assets/session/mapping through low-priority scheduler admission and explicit residency reservations; reuse admission receipts; one product canary plus deferred checks when needed; never the full encoder lab gate.
- Zero model-network requests including repair: use the manager's verified-local-only access (e.g. `allowRepair:false` across OPFS and Cache Storage) with typed invalidation, because existing `model-cache.mjs` `acquire()` handles can fetch missing/corrupt assets through `bytes()`/`open()` and `readOnly`/`has()`/`peek()` do not enforce a local-only boundary. Required runtime/helper assets must be locally ready; skip on cache miss, corruption or eviction.
- Foreground work outranks warming: stop new warm submissions, settle the in-flight unit, release or transfer compatible resources (warm ownership transfers to the foreground job); count idle warm memory until release; never evict foreground resources. Do not promise instant preemption of submitted GPU work.
- Constrained iPhone/unknown-memory paths defer or release generator warmth before e4e and rehydrate after teardown.
- Static names and completed-result display/Save never initialize inference.
- Any new diagnostics event gets its allowlist and privacy-policy entry; no photos, latents, typed input or raw error strings.
- **If it drops:** close with the round's result and the request-log check that no warming requests are issued.

## Out of scope
Any consent or overlap behaviour; measuring benefit outside the targeted round.

## Notes
- Implementation edits shared runtime/worker files (`ort-worker.mjs` `warmMapping()`, session creation in `runtime.mjs`, or their `packages/stylegan-js` equivalents after compute extraction), so it follows the morph pipeline bead (ordering edge on `morph.guards`, fm-fy2.9). The round itself edits none of them.
- Integrated checks run on the final integrated app against the candidate baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`) plus declared changes. If warming ships, the release with warming on must still pass the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27) on every platform class, physical iPhone included. Fixes found land here and the check re-runs. Any further opportunity goes to the operator/planner with evidence and the next test.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#targeted-autoresearch-launch-and-preserved-history (warming row), #consented-downloads-useful-overlap-and-cached-model-warming, #workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership, #integrated-verification.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Round run with recorded cells, raw distributions and paired effects; zero speculative network asserted from intercepted requests; outcome (ship or drop) and threshold stated in the closing commit with ledger rows committed.
- [ ] If shipped, unit/integration tests: eligible cached route warms; missing/corrupt/runtime-asset cases warm nothing with zero network; a foreground request preempts and settles; warm ownership transfers to the foreground job; foreground job admitted after warm settlement without exceeding reservations; constrained phone encoder teardown releases generator warmth before e4e and rehydrates after.
- [ ] If shipped, built-app request-interception run on the release-candidate artifact: zero model-host requests from warming in every case; static names and completed-result display never initialize inference.
- [ ] If dropped: request-interception run shows warming issues zero requests.
- [ ] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test`) and pass.

title: Import the research tree byte-identical, with integrated-path dispositions
description:
## Goal

Move classic's whole tracked `autoresearch/` tree into this repository byte-identical from one frozen, digest-listed snapshot (changed 18 October: closed candidates, frozen reports, the 10 October round, the v2 campaign and native candidates move too, because classic's tree is cleaned at wind-down), and record for each integrated optimisation path where it came from and what destination check protects it, so the refactor cannot silently drop performance work. Classic wind-down removes classic's research tree only after this copy is verified.

## Scope

**Snapshot**
- Choose the snapshot commit in classic (read-only; never reset, clean or worktree). Source facts at `b2d945a`: 137 tracked files, about 9.7 MB (88 files / 8.8 MB historical `candidates/`); `results.tsv` 11-column header plus 69 rows (14 keep, 41 inconclusive, 5 proposed, 3 discard, 2 blocked, 2 baseline, 2 candidate); `state/` ignored and not imported; two research workflows and `hosting/next-static/promote.py` reference the tree. Re-check counts at the frozen revision (`git diff --stat b2d945a <frozen> -- autoresearch/`; the four commits after `b2d945a` touched no tracked `autoresearch/` file as of `6107f80`).
- Allowlist and source→destination path map (identity paths under `autoresearch/`) with SHA-256 of every tracked file, plus the consumer list; this digest list is the input to the import check and classic wind-down.
- Exclusions with reasons: the four uncommitted documents (`README.md`, `loop-v3-proposal.md`, `reviews/README.md`, `reviews/2026-10-10/next-directions.md`) are not imported (default decided 16 October) — if committed before the snapshot they come in with it, otherwise listed with content digests and adopted later only by explicit decision; any weight-bearing file.
- Weight/secret scan before import; no weights or fixtures containing weights enter Git.

**Import**
- Write every allowlisted file from Git objects (`git show <commit>:<path>` or archive); no `.git` copy, no working-tree overlay. Never edit an imported historical file. Never overwrite paths other sessions changed here; skip and report.
- Frozen trees added to Oxc ignore lists.
- `scripts/check-research-import.mjs` verifies every digest-list entry, count and bytes.

**Integrated-path dispositions** (in the provenance map beside the digest list)
- For each integrated optimisation path: current source, originating ledger row/report, retained behaviour, destination check, disposition (retained, deliberately replaced, historical, proposal, rejected, evidence unavailable). Families: morph-frame pipeline; WGSL/direct engine (`manifest.webgl` coefficients also feed direct WebGPU); OPFS shard cache; direct RGBA media; compressed session; photo runtime; current media/video worker; native CUDA.
- Each source invariant and phone-contract item maps to a destination check or a named gap owner: keyed synthesis admission receipts (cold visitor one canary first, others deferred, `fullQualify` runs all); `ort-worker.mjs` `warmMapping()` overlap in direct and ORT WebGPU incl. mobile GPU; CPU loading sequential; CPU synthesis 1–4 threads; streamed e4e bounded, unshared, single-threaded; dedicated cache-only worker; Firefox storage-permission timing; no-third-party gate; adapter probe before GPU acquisition (`navigator.gpu` alone wasted ~180 MiB in Simulator); failure-only preference; visible-time watchdogs; worker-start vs route failure; constrained worker teardown; 268,435,456-byte e4e WASM limit.
- Negative lessons as `rejected` with their ledger row/report and destination guard: no silent fp16 e4e or tolerance widening (currency tolerance guard), realtime WebCodecs encoder settings, PNG sub-filtering, IDB durability tuning, abandoned integrity-marker assumptions.

## Out of scope

Guides, lease, ledger handover and 69-row reference resolution (research stage 1); a new benchmark campaign; recovering missing historical raw reports.

## Notes

- When a later bead moves an integrated path and drops a test, it records the replacement in `tests/retired.txt`. Missing receipts constrain claims; not an automatic physical-phone cutover veto.
- Retained performance evidence and the no-regression protocol stay in PLAN.md#retained-performance-evidence-and-no-regression-checks.

title: Check that a phone without admitted WebGPU finishes a face on CPU; record download size and quota
description:
## Background
Consequence of the 17 October read: a phone-class device with no admitted WebGPU must finish a face on the CPU route, or the guidance must say plainly that it cannot. The findings note (18 October) shows every iOS storage check (143) reported a 1,000 MB quota and zero use, while the CPU package is 1,040 MB; the one cold iPhone attempt stopped at 678 MB.

## Why
The only case where WebGL helped was download size, so the CPU route's size and keepability decide phone usefulness.

## Scope
- Run a face to completion on CPU with WebGPU unavailable/not admitted on the iOS Simulator product lane and Android emulator (runtime harness before the port; repeated in the product by integrated verification).
- Record the CPU route's download size and the browser-reported quota (diagnostics already carry it); physical-iPhone measurement only when a device is at hand (evidence, not a gate).
- If the CPU package cannot be kept, specify the consent-text requirement (byte count; downloaded again each visit) for ws:consent to render; note a smaller phone CPU package as a later model-artifact option for conversion/hosting, not a release prerequisite.

## Out of scope
Physical-phone qualification; changing model artifacts.

## Considerations
Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a reason to downgrade phone support.

## Consumer (polish r1)
The consent requirement this leaf specifies is rendered by acquisition consent's modal, `consent.modal` (fm-9kr8): when the phone cannot keep the CPU package, the consent text states the byte count (from the actual provider/model manifest, one unit, same figure as progress per defect 10) and that it is downloaded again on each visit. This leaf writes that requirement into its receipt and into the decision log as a dated entry, with the measured quota and package bytes, so `consent.modal` can cite it. The rendering and its operated acceptance belong to `consent.modal`; this leaf does not change consent UI.

## Published figures for consent copy (polish r2)
Besides the markdown receipt, write `docs/receipts/provider/phone-cpu-check.json`, which the `consent.modal` (fm-9kr8) test fixtures import:
- `cpuPackageBytes` (integer, the sum of the CPU route's required assets from the actual provider/model manifest, with the manifest digest in `manifestDigest`) and `cpuPackageLabel`.
- `quotaBytes`, `usageBytes` (from `navigator.storage.estimate()` on each lane) and `quotaLabel`.
- `lane`, `browser`, `platform`, `measuredAt` (ISO date), `outcome` (`completed-on-cpu` / `guidance-shown`), `canKeep` (the same predicate consent uses: quota minus usage >= remaining package bytes).
The labels are produced by the app's single byte formatter, the one consent modal, progress and status all use (defect 10: one figure per purpose, one unit). Today's figures read "1,040 MB" (package) and "1,000 MB" (iOS quota). The JSON records which base that formatter uses. A unit test re-formats `cpuPackageBytes` and `quotaBytes` and requires the stored labels to match byte for byte, so consent copy, progress and this receipt cannot drift.

## Ordering (polish r2)
This check is evidence, not a shared-file edit. It gates `provider.acceptance`, `ws:provider` (and through it integrated verification) and `consent.modal`. It does not gate the typed facade.

- [ ] Simulator/emulator run completes a CPU face with WebGPU not admitted, or the guidance text is shown and asserted; download bytes and reported quota recorded.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, and the log is retained as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics). Network claims are asserted from the log, never from screenshots.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/provider/phone-cpu-check.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Receipt and `docs/decisions/` entry state the consent-text requirement (or that it is not needed) with the measured package bytes and reported quota, and name `consent.modal` (fm-9kr8) as the consumer.
- [ ] `docs/receipts/provider/phone-cpu-check.json` committed with `cpuPackageBytes`, `cpuPackageLabel`, `quotaBytes`, `quotaLabel`, `usageBytes`, `manifestDigest`, lane/browser/platform, `measuredAt`, `outcome`, `canKeep`; a unit test re-formats the byte values with the app's shared byte formatter and matches the stored labels exactly (e.g. "1,040 MB", "1,000 MB"); `consent.modal` fixtures read this file instead of literals.

title: Scheduled non-blocking bleeding-edge lane
description:
## Goal

Give qualified early warning on upcoming dependency versions (nightly/canary/dev/source builds) without risking the stable experience: a scheduled, non-blocking lane on a GPU worker under the shared device lease that records exact versions, numerical canaries and paired performance, and whose outputs never reach `deploy-next` or any publish path.

## Scope

- Scheduled workflow on a GPU worker (eris preferred) under the shared lease; not a required check.
- 16 October snapshot of lane tags: React canary `19.3.0-canary-098d2e87-20261015`, TypeScript `next` 7.1.0-dev.20261015.1, ONNX Runtime Web dev `1.31.0-dev.20260918-bc8e7ed75`, Playwright `1.65.0-alpha-2026-10-15`, PyTorch nightly `2.16.0.dev20261015` (conversion container only; that cell is added once the conversion container exists).
- Each run records exact version and integrity hash, numerical canaries, and paired-performance evidence through the research runner (raw per-run distributions and the paired effect against the pinned control).
- Durability: retention differs (npm keeps dev builds; PyTorch's nightly index held only 55 builds of the CUDA 13 Linux wheel), so any wheel or artifact a result depends on is copied to durable storage (URL plus integrity hash); source builds pin a commit SHA and mirror the built artifact.
- Isolation check: no build/deploy/publish job references a bleeding-edge artifact path or cache key.

## Out of scope

Adopting a nightly (only once it reaches a stable release, through the updater).

## Notes

- Hosted-minute economy: uses the self-hosted worker; never weakens a required check.
- Depends on the updater and the lease wrapper.
- Anchor: PLAN.md#dependency-currency-and-the-frozen-self-host-guarantee--16-october-2026.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] One recorded scheduled run with versions, integrity hashes, canary results, a paired-performance result against the pinned control and the lease journal entry; the job is not in the required-status list.
- [ ] Isolation check unit tests: a build/deploy job referencing a bleeding-edge artifact path or cache key fails; the check runs in CI on the real workflows and passes.
- [ ] A check fails a run whose result references an uncopied wheel/artifact or an unpinned source build; the recorded run's summary names each durable copy (URL + hash) and source-build SHA with its mirrored artifact.
- [ ] The ORT Web nightly cell records numerics (raw max RGB diff, sampled raw-float error, e4e latent error at the unchanged tolerances) and a paired desktop screen against the pinned control on eris, appended as non-shipping ledger rows; this is the nightly data point the ONNX Runtime Web evaluation (`ortweb.bump`, fm-qeh) cites.

title: Show stored size with a Clear action and bound the faces store (defect 22, planner proposal)
description:
## Background
Candidate defect 22 (source read, 18 October audit): nothing shows or clears what is stored on the device, and the faces store has no ceiling. Planner's proposal (operator may veto): a Help line with the size and a Clear button, and a bounded faces store.

## Why
Unbounded on-device storage and no way to clear it are resource and privacy problems.

## Scope
- A Help line (below-fold `.next-explain`/Help area) showing stored result/session size and a Clear button that removes app recovery records and retained results (model caches handled separately by the manager's own clear, if exposed, without deleting completed exports as collateral).
- A numeric ceiling for the faces store with oldest-first eviction of retained session records, never of a file the user is currently preparing.
- Unit tests for the ceiling and eviction order; operated UI test for Clear.

## Out of scope
Model cache quota/eviction (manager).

## Considerations
- Operator veto possible: if vetoed, record in `docs/decisions/` and close.
- The ceiling value is chosen from measured record sizes; until measured, report "measured, no threshold".

## Status: planner proposal, operator may veto (polish r1)
A planner's proposal (PLAN defect table row 22 and "Planner proposals awaiting a veto"), not an operator requirement. It proceeds without waiting for approval. If vetoed, record it in `docs/decisions/`, remove the feature if it landed and close as vetoed.

## Current candidate storage (to measure and bound)
- IndexedDB `checkface-originals-v1`, object store `originals` (`browser/originals.mjs`): one record per generated result (image blob, latent, provenance) plus alias records. No ceiling today: this is the unbounded faces store.
- The session record `last-generated-session-v2` in the same store (`last-result.mjs`): capped by `MAX_SESSION_BYTES = 32 MiB` (faces, scrub frames, video), video kept only with storage headroom.
- `localStorage` `facemorph-slider-v1` (slider preference); model caches belong to the manager.
- Clear removes the originals records, the session record and (if media.session-words lands) the tab-scoped words; it leaves the slider preference and model caches (the manager's own clear, if exposed, is separate and never deletes completed exports). The Help line states what Clear removes and what it leaves.
- Ceiling: measure record sizes first (event log of sizes over the standard journeys); set the ceiling from that measurement; until then report "measured, no threshold". Eviction is oldest-first by last use, never evicts a record referenced by the current session or a file being prepared.

Named tests: `storage-size.matches-estimate`, `storage-clear.removes-app-records`, `storage-clear.keeps-model-cache-and-prefs`, `faces-store.ceiling-at-cap`, `faces-store.ceiling-over-cap-evicts-oldest`, `faces-store.never-evicts-current-session`.

## Decision-log entry required: agent-chosen rule, not PLAN text (polish r2)
The rule below was chosen by the round-1 bead-polish agent on 24 October 2026; PLAN.md does not state it. It is therefore not silently decided: the first implementing change writes the entry `docs/decisions/2026-10-24-storage-clear-scope.md` with status `proposal, operator may veto`, decided-by `planner agent (bead polish r1, 24 Oct 2026); no PLAN.md text`, the rule as written here, the evidence it rests on, the alternatives listed below, and what changes if it is vetoed. The bead implements the rule as written unless a veto or change entry exists (this is not an approval gate), and its receipt cites the entry. Identity's decision log (fm-orh, area A) should list it beside P1-P4.
- Rule: Clear removes the originals records (`checkface-originals-v1`), the session record (`last-generated-session-v2`) and, if `media.session-words` lands, the tab-scoped words. It keeps the slider preference in `localStorage` and the model caches (cleared only by the manager's own clear, if exposed), and never deletes completed exports.
- Evidence: defect 22 asks for stored size and a Clear action; the plan separates model cache quota/eviction (manager) from app records; deleting model caches would force a re-download behind a consent prompt.
- Alternatives: (a) one Clear that also removes model caches, with the re-download size stated; (b) Clear keeps the session record so the last result survives.
- If vetoed: change only the removed-store list and the Help sentence; the ceiling and eviction rules stand unless also vetoed (P4).

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Size shown matches actual storage usage within the browser estimate API's precision; Clear empties app records and the size updates.
- [ ] Store ceiling enforced in unit tests at and over the cap.
- [ ] Operated UI acceptance: act with real pointer/touch input at the control's visible position and assert via `elementFromPoint` that the element there is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role clicks only to set up state; repeating controls exercised at 0/1, 2, 3, many and the cap; text inputs with an empty, a very long and a pasted value; a phone-width (390 px) and a desktop-width (1,280 px) screenshot per case.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] If vetoed: decision recorded in `docs/decisions/`, feature absent, item closed as vetoed.
- [ ] Clear removes exactly the listed app records (originals, session record, tab-scoped words) and leaves model caches and preferences; eviction never removes a record used by the current session or a file being prepared.
- [ ] The agent-chosen rule is written as a decision-log entry with status `proposal, operator may veto` and decided-by naming the polish agent and the absence of PLAN.md text; the receipt cites the entry; the decision validator passes on it.

Position in the shared-file sequence: after morph.neighbour-rule (edge added polish r2), because the session record path (`last-result.mjs` rememberSession/readSession and generateNameOrSeed) is called from `product-bridge.mjs`. Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Leaves that must not edit these three files: ws:crop.repro (failing tests and the failure analysis only), crop.policy, media.envelope-helpers, media.recovery-schema, morph.descriptor-geometry, compute.consumer-example, compute.names-equality, and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept leaf. They keep the module export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) and move logic behind them into the package. If such a leaf finds it must edit one of the three files, it records the file in the check-migration map conflict list and adds a needs edge to the latest leaf in the sequence that edits it; it never edits concurrently. Each sequenced leaf lists every file it edits in the check-migration map conflict list at claim time.

title: Write numeric count and byte ceilings into the contracts
description:
## Background

The contracts must freeze numeric source/crop-count and byte ceilings for retained sources, crop
buffers and transient decode separately, before batch admission, plus aggregate acquisition buffer and
live-residency limits. No unbounded default.

## Why

Confirmed-crop, face controls batch admission and acquisition consent cite these values; they are the two-phase numeric acceptance.

## Scope

- Per-route transient decode bounds from the measurement; retained source and crop-buffer ceilings;
  batch count ceiling; aggregate transfer/read-ahead/hash/write-buffer limits; aggregate live-residency
  limits; frame/slot budget constants.
- Over-budget admission before any extra keypoint allocation, with an actionable reduce-selection/
  remove-retry-input message (no truncation or hidden eviction).
- Record the measurement beside the values; revise only by contract revision.
- Boundary test vectors (at and one over each ceiling) for downstream workstreams.

## Typed outputs (citable)

Draft first under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`, then moved by the milestone type-test bead to the module below. Exported names are stable: downstream beads cite them; a rename needs a contract revision and an update of the `contracts.md` export index.

- `apps/web/src/contracts/ceilings.ts`: `CEILINGS` (per-route transient decode, retained source, crop buffer, batch count, frame/slot budget) with unit and route scope; manager-side values filled into `AcquisitionBudget`/`LiveResidencyLimit` constants in `packages/browser-model-manager/src/contracts/budgets.ts`; engine memory bounds into the `MemoryBoundName` table.
- `apps/web/src/contracts/ceilings.vectors.json`: at-boundary and one-over vectors per ceiling, consumed by `crop.byte-ceilings`, `face.batch-proposal` and `consent.*` tests.

## Out of scope

Implementing the admission checks (confirmed-crop and face controls).

## Considerations

Values are implementation contracts to qualify, not browser RSS control claims.

description:
## Goal
Locate every candidate preview-chrome and retirement string that must change before production, with its exact replacement or removal, so the candidate edit set and the monorepo app work from one checked list; and add a build scan that fails when a production build links to a retired API host or to the candidate branch, so copy regressions fail a check instead of relying on review.

## Scope
- **Copy inventory** (machine-readable, read by the candidate edit set and the monorepo app): per string file and line in candidate source at the frozen revision and at the current branch head, current text, replacement text or removal, owning edit bead. Strings: the "Experimental preview" strip and its Classic and retirement links; the tester invite; the "Use classic FaceMorph" error link; the desktop README link; the "Preview version" footer label; FAQ entries about `next.facemorph.me`, the self-hostable API (documents a retired host), Upload image, the model sizes and the support address; obsolete API FAQ links; classic fallback links; native desktop-download/update recommendations; GUID/link-preservation promises; fixed-date assurances (legacy production still announces October 25), including the tester/retirement notice wording.
- Draft retirement copy: old GUIDs, results and links are not preserved; no new share URLs exist; the operator controls timing; no fixed date unless the operator sets one. Operation limitations, CPU/WebGPU/mobile guidance and names/result capability match the chosen artifact's actual behaviour. Classic self-host Compose is described in Help only, not as a primary recovery link. Plain words.

Making the edits (candidate edit set; provider simplification owns Help/native copy in the monorepo); fixing scan hits.

title: Render the Prepare encoder entry beside Choose image in the Encode image modal
description:
## Background
Acquisition consent owns the Prepare encoder action, its grant and Cancel semantics; face controls renders the entry
beside Choose image (tie-break table). The audit unified the name ("Prepare photo models" -> "Prepare encoder").

## Why
Lets a person start approved photo setup before choosing a source, overlapping transfer with choosing.

## Scope
- One compact **Prepare encoder** control beside Choose image in the Encode image modal, shown only when eligible
  required assets are missing; Choose image stays directly usable.
- Setup progress and Cancel setup in the modal's existing status/footer, then the owning tile after OK.
- No page-wide download action, offer toast or permanent panel.

## Out of scope
Grant/ownership logic (`consent.prepare-encoder`).

## Considerations
Hidden entirely when assets are verified cached or photo encoding is unavailable.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** It renders the Prepare encoder entry in the ported source step; the action itself is fm-vho5's. If implementation finds it must edit one of them after all, it first runs `br dep add fm-8q8h fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph), adds the file to the conflict list in fm-bhw and records the change in its receipt (the plan's rule: an edge is added when an edit is discovered).

- [ ] Operated-UI rule: each acceptance step acts with real pointer input (touch tap at phone widths) at the control's visible position, asserts `document.elementFromPoint` at that point returns the control (or a descendant) and that the point lies inside the region a person would look in (named per control below); by-name/by-role clicks are used only to set up state, never as the acceptance step.

title: Import hosting directories; staging, runtime mirror and entry Worker

## Goal
Bring the application side of classic's deploy path into `hosting/` from committed Git objects with an allowlist and provenance, and make frontend staging, the local runtime restage/mirror and entry-Worker/analytics staging reproducible from a clean clone against the `deploy-next/` contract. ## Scope
- Export the application-side files the boundary decision assigns to `hosting/` (versus `packages/cloudflare-model-host`) from `hosting/next-static/`, `hosting/next/`, `hosting/next-cloudflare/`, `hosting/gallery/` at the frozen revision (classic candidate `6107f80` or later; 48 tracked files, about 4.3 MB at `b2d945a8`), from Git objects, never a working tree.

- Exclude: `hosting/next-cloudflare/.wrangler/cache/cf.json` and `.wrangler/state/v3/kv/miniflare-KVNamespaceObject/*.sqlite*` (tracked state files), any staged `public/` directories, credentials, private provenance (`review-artifacts/` references stay references), ignored inputs, and package-side files (imported by the hosting beads).

title: Morph as a parent intent with one current result: scheduling, invalidation, late-completion rejection
description:
## Goal
Morph must compose with photo encodes and face generation without duplicate inference, deadlock or a permanently disabled button. This bead integrates `renderMorph` with the operation controller's scheduler as a parent intent with exactly one current result, after the Morph acceptance checks (`morph.guards`, fm-fy2.9) have landed. The built-app matrix and paired comparison follow in `morph.guards.acceptance`.

## Scope
**Parent-intent scheduling**
- Integrate `renderMorph` with the operation controller's scheduler: Morph is a parent intent, not an extra heavyweight lease while waiting; dependencies are admitted once and join an existing operation for the same slot/revision (join the compute-ready milestone, not default-file completion); compute admission is released before awaiting dependencies or consent; the frame-production lease goes through the same scheduler; parent Cancel stops only work owned solely by that parent; failed/cancelled inputs settle the parent with a specific recovery action.
- Exactly one current morph result. Changing the ordered faces or any setting creates a new revision: the old result's Share/Save readiness is withdrawn, its prepared file is no longer current, obsolete production is aborted, and late frame/video/file completions are discarded and cannot install. Settings stay disabled during an active morph as in the candidate. Repeated clicks after acceptance cannot queue a second intent. A completed face stays usable when another fails.

- The Morph acceptance checks from `morph.guards` (frame budget, MP4 probe, identical neighbours) run before the parent intent is admitted; a refusal settles the intent with no Morph-owned acquisition or inference.

## Out of scope
The frame budget, MP4 probe and identical-neighbour rule themselves (`morph.guards`, fm-fy2.9); the built-app five-mode matrix, retained lanes and paired comparison (`morph.guards.acceptance`). Scheduler implementation (operation controller, `opctl.scheduler`); Morph button/progress/Cancel presentation (face controls). New performance campaigns.

## Notes
- Split on 2026-10-24 for swarm size into three beads, edited in this order: `morph.guards` (this ID, fm-fy2.9: frame budget, MP4 probe, identical-neighbour rule), `morph.guards.intent` (parent-intent scheduling and one current result) and `morph.guards.acceptance` (built-app matrix, retained lanes and the paired comparison against the pinned control). The first two edit the shared files in turn; the third edits none.
- Shared-file order (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October; revised in the 24 October final pass): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in one sequence enforced by needs edges, never concurrently: `provider.native` -> `provider.webgl` -> `provider.route-admission` -> `migration.project-json` (one-line ProjectJson import swap) -> typed facade (`migration.facade`) -> `compute.synthesis` -> `compute.photo-descriptor` -> `compute.app-rebind` -> `crop.fix` -> `crop.queue` -> `media.reader-wiring` -> `media.export` -> `media.schema` -> `morph.render` -> `morph.guards` -> `media.session` -> face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Rows that must not edit these files: `crop.repro`, `compute.blend`, `compute.package-surface`, `media.envelope`, `provider.admission` (evidence), `crop.ported-app` and `compute.ported-app` (acceptance on the ported app; a fix they need follows the out-of-turn rule below) and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept row; code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) until the bridge's own turn. A row that finds it must edit one of these files outside its turn adds a needs edge to the latest row in the sequence that edits it. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs. Within the morph pipeline this bead edits after `morph.guards` and before `media.session`.
- Inputs: the real-bridge trace `apps/web/test/harness/opctl-expected-trace.json` and whole-action progress from `opctl.progress` (fm-vbj7); the parent-intent scheduler from `opctl.scheduler`.
- No fakes: the scheduling core is a pure state machine fed timestamped events as plain values; the same cases run again through the real bridge with real timers.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #morph-pipeline, #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts, #clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation, known candidate defect 6.

- [ ] Scheduler tests (the scheduling core as a pure state machine fed timestamped events as plain values, plus real-bridge runs with real timers): photo -> queued Morph; Morph auto-generation -> explicit face request; capability loss while queued; Cancel at each dependency boundary; competing provider loads; idle retained encoder while generator loading is requested; delayed/failed face-file preparation not blocking ready inputs nor duplicating inference; bounded endpoint reuse; no starvation/deadlock, no duplicate inference. One real-bridge run extends `apps/web/test/harness/opctl-expected-trace.json` (from `opctl.progress`) with the renderMorph frame-production lease events and passes against it.
- [ ] `morph-intent.single-current-result`, `.input-change-invalidates`, `.setting-change-invalidates`, `.late-completion-rejected`, `.repeated-click-no-duplicate`, `.face-failure-keeps-others`.

title: Verify preflight without model network, estimates and timing-check outcomes
description:
## Background
Device check budgets: about two seconds of sampling, five-second UI deadline, 16 MiB scratch buffers, 100 KiB checker code; skip, timeout and GPU loss yield 'no reliable estimate'. Estimates never become admission proof or a phone gate.

## Why
Guidance must not block names or eligible actions, and must not fetch models.

## Scope
- Preflight-without-model-network evidence.
- Denied/skipped/timed-out checks; unknown calibration; context-specific photo/synthesis estimates; cold/warm overhead; material-cost change consent.
- Timing skip cannot bypass admission; viewport width/touch hints cannot suppress an eligible route.
- Check prediction error against available paired measurements; record uncalibrated cells honestly; uncalibrated time fields stay honest; slow-work WebGPU-computer copy contextual.
- The cold-device estimate text (defect 20, unreachable in the candidate) appears when its condition holds.
- Rows graded: R13; defect 20 (estimate text part).

## Out of scope
Calibration campaigns; physical-phone benchmarks.

## Considerations
- Prediction-error and estimate-budget thresholds are set at their contract milestone; until then 'measured, no threshold'.
- Calibration measurements feed the support-and-evidence table.
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.

- [ ] Skip/timeout/GPU-loss runs show 'no reliable estimate' and consent remains usable.

title: Run the independent registry-package review and retain the report
description:
## Background
See the parent (`fm-fy2.21`) for the full journey, which this item executes unchanged.

## Why
Packages are not declared independently accepted until this passes.

## Scope
- Reviewer starts from the input packet only; installs exact registry versions in a clean external project; follows public quickstart literally through convert (public tagged converter), host, manager-loaded inference and morph, PNG/lossless-WebP export/reopen with exact recovery and lossless pixels, direct caller-loaded use, non-face example (no detector/e4e download), progress/abort/error/disposal, cold/warm costs, no network at construction/status reads; inspects installed tarballs.
- Report retained in `docs/receipts/` with versions/integrity, lockfile, identities, commands, outputs, every undocumented or confusing step, verdict per capability.
- Fix loop: failures -> fix -> publish a new version -> independent recheck of the new registry bytes.

## Out of scope
Author smoke tests (package publication and documentation).

## Considerations
- Does not block web promotion or API retirement.
- Numerical evidence uses the frozen tolerances (RGB <= 1/255, sampled raw float <= 0.002; e4e <= 0.0001; descriptor-specific tolerances for other models).

## Reviewer checklist, copied from the parent so this item stands alone (polish r1)
The reviewer records pass, fail or unverified (with reason) for each line; nothing is marked passed from an author's statement, an internal example, a typecheck or a tarball scan.
1. Clean external project installs the exact registry versions; record versions, integrity hashes and the lockfile.
2. Trusted checkpoint acquisition per public docs (source, digest, terms).
3. Conversion with the public tagged converter container: build, convert, verify with the upstream reference check.
4. Static hosting under the reviewer's control per public docs (no FaceMorph hostname, catalogue, alias or secret).
5. Manager-loaded inference and a morph.
6. Direct caller-loaded engine use without the manager.
7. PNG and lossless-WebP export and reopen: exact recovery values, lossless decoded pixels.
8. Non-face example and its descriptor/support boundary; no face detector or e4e download.
9. Emitted JS, types, `exports` and worker assets; public build integration (bundler, worker and WASM paths, COOP/COEP for threaded routes, single-thread behaviour).
10. Model identity and numerical evidence against the frozen or descriptor-specific tolerances.
11. Progress, abort, errors and disposal; cold and warm costs; no network at construction or status reads (from the network log).
12. README/API docs, copyable commands, licences/notices, model terms, ownership/resource semantics, troubleshooting.
13. Installed tarball inspection for missing files, repository-only paths, secrets or bundled weights (the reviewer may run `package-tarball-content-scan` as one input, never as the verdict).
14. Advertised targets only; unsupported Node/browser/model cells recorded as limitations.
Friction log: every undocumented step or confusing instruction, with the doc location.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.

Restore the legacy fullscreen, gapless, headerless names grid with names overlaid on faces and an accepted Back exit, and stop sending requests per keystroke. title: Publish the three packages to npm
description:
## Goal
Publish the reusable engine (`stylegan-js`), `browser-model-manager` and `cloudflare-model-host` to the public npm registry with provenance, from exactly the tarballs that passed their checks, and prove they install and compile from a clean environment. Package scope settled by the operator on 17 October; the converter ships as a pinned container, not npm. Independent published-package acceptance follows and is not inferred from this.

## Scope
- No operator decision: package publication goes ahead once its checks pass (operator, 24 October: only the live cutover pushes need the operator; package publication needs only its npm credentials and the packed-tarball checks). It does not wait on `gate:cutover`. Needs npm scope and credentials (`gate:npm-creds`), an execution prerequisite, not a decision.
- Reviewer named first: `pkgaccept.review` (fm-fy2.21) runs after publication, so this bead checks its logistics part before publishing: the independent reviewer role (a non-author person or agent session, and how independence is ensured) and the input packet (published names, versions and public documents only), with the review budget, environments and report template, are committed by `pkgdocs.release` (fm-oagi), which this bead already needs; no separate presence check.
- Working folder names are not reserved names; the real npm names/scope come from the package name check at publication. No pretrained weights ship.
- Before state per package: `npm view <name> versions dist-tags --json`, or 404 for a new name.
- Re-run pack/install, metadata and licence checks on the exact tarballs; run `scripts/packages/check-tarball-contents.mjs` (test ID `package-tarball-content-scan`, owned by the package-preparation work) on the exact tarballs about to be published: rejects weights, repository-only paths, secret patterns and private hostnames; requires the listed files; JSON report kept in the CI run.
- Publish with provenance (`npm publish --provenance` from CI with OIDC, or the recorded equivalent); record names, versions, tarball integrity (sha512) and source commit.
- Post-publication check (no web host change, so the web `app` check is `not applicable: no host change`): `npm view` shows the new versions and dist-tags; in a clean temp dir with an empty npm cache `npm install <name>@<version>` of all three succeeds; installed integrity equals the packed tarball; each entry point imports under Node; a TypeScript consumer compiles against the emitted declarations; the provenance attestation resolves to the recorded source commit.

## Out of scope
Docs/quickstarts; independent published-package acceptance; converter container publication.

## Notes
- Never publish a tarball whose content scan or integrity differs from the one checked; a failed publish of one package is reported per package, not hidden behind the others.
- Unfinished package work never forces the hosted API to stay on.
- 24 October rules: evidence is the publish workflow run; no receipt file or `docs/decisions/` path.
- Plan: #delivery-and-publication, #package-boundaries, #independent-published-package-acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The publish job runs without any operator-decision check (none is needed, 24 October); it refuses only when `gate:npm-creds` credentials, the reviewer logistics or the tarball checks below are missing, each with a named reason in the run log.
- [ ] Before and after registry state per package (versions, dist-tags) in the run output.
- [ ] Content scan clean on the exact tarballs; each scanned tarball's sha512 equals the published integrity.
- [ ] Clean-directory, empty-cache post-publication check passes for all three: install, Node import, TypeScript consumer compile, provenance resolves to the source commit; output (package@version, integrity, registry host and bytes, outcome) retained as a CI artifact.

title: Freeze the model descriptor and external developer journey contract
description:
## Background

Generic APIs currently assume FFHQ's fixed 1024 px and 18-by-512 latent. The external developer
journey: choose a checkpoint from a compatibility table; run the pinned conversion container; host on
standard HTTPS static hosting; install packages in a clean project and authorise acquisition through
the manager or load directly; export PNG/lossless WebP and reopen exact metadata; multi-input morph.
The proposed non-face fixture is NVlabs AFHQ cat 512 px, not yet claimed supported.

## Why

Dimensional assumptions cannot remain implicit in generic APIs; compute, media, conversion and package docs build on this.

## Scope

- Descriptor fields: latent/output shapes, W/W+ layer count, layout/normalisation, noise, truncation,
  optional class conditioning, resource requirements, provider qualification, identity/digest.
- Dynamic-shape recovery schema versioning preserving earlier candidate readers; equal-shaped latents
  from different checkpoint identities cannot be combined; unknown models viewable as media only.
- Compatibility table shape (serialization variants, architecture, conditional, resolution/channels,
  Z/W dims, precision/operators, qualified providers, unsupported cells, conversion route, terms).
- The five-step journey as a contract walkthrough; non-face generation never loads a face detector or FFHQ e4e.

## Typed outputs (citable)

Draft first under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`, then moved by the milestone type-test bead to the module below. Exported names are stable: downstream beads cite them; a rename needs a contract revision and an update of the `contracts.md` export index.

- `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/descriptor.ts`: `ModelDescriptor` (latent/output shapes, W/W+ layer count, layout/normalisation, noise, truncation, optional class conditioning, resource requirements, provider qualification, identity/digest), `LatentSchema`, `CompatibilityRow`, `DescriptorQualification` (`qualified` | `unqualified: <blocker>`).
- Example descriptors as test fixtures: FFHQ 1024 (18×512) and a hypothetical 512 px model; no hidden 1024/18×512 constants in generic signatures.
- Consumers: `compute.descriptor`, `conversion.*`, `media.recovery-schema`, `pkgdocs.*`, `verify.packages-nonface`.

## Out of scope

Conversion and qualification of the fixture (conversion, compute, media workstreams).

## Considerations

Until the joint proof passes, non-face support is labelled unqualified with the named blocker.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts.md` descriptor section and draft type; the FFHQ 1024 descriptor and a hypothetical 512 px descriptor both express all fields with no hidden constants.
- [ ] The journey walkthrough traces all five steps through contract types only.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Every name listed under "Typed outputs (citable)" exists in the draft type file and has a row in the `contracts.md` export index naming its consumers.
- [ ] Recovery schema versioning for dynamic shapes is frozen here: candidate-produced fixtures (schema 1 and 2, PNG and WebP) parse through `parseRecoveryMetadata` unchanged; a fixture from a 512 px descriptor with a different layer count round-trips; a morph request mixing equal-shaped latents from two different `ModelIdentity` values is rejected with a typed error (type test plus validator vector).
notes: Anchor: PLAN.md#external-developer-journey-and-non-face-models.

title: Rendering port: explain/FAQ, debug area, error box, toasts and tester tools
description:
## Background
`Product.fs` at the pinned commit: `faq`/`explainSection` (~1125-1181, page body below the fold), `debugArea` (~1182-1192), error box (`.next-error`, `.next-error-retry`, `.next-error-reference`, `.next-error-classic`), toasts (`.next-consent-toast`, `.next-consent-message`, model toast `.next-model-progress`, failure toast, `.next-invite`/`.next-invite-note` for `?testing`), `.next-project-open` (hidden since 21 September), `?testing` bulk Generate faces, Help/footer issue/contact links.

## Why
Retained candidate behaviour (tie-break table): `?testing` bulk Generate and Help/footer issue links stay; diagnostics consent/one-shot report must survive.

## Scope
Components with the same contract and text as the control.

## Out of scope
Native-link removal and computer/browser Help (provider guidance), `#debug-reporting` disclosure and toast repairs (ws:diag), retirement/FAQ copy (ws:domain).

## Considerations
Keep the `.next-*` DOM/class contract and carry `product-ux.scss`. MUI v4->v9 pixel differences are reviewed and recorded, not gated; anything that hides, overlaps or mislabels a control is a defect. Defects frozen as repair rows are not reproduced: where carrying candidate CSS would reproduce one (defect 1: MUI button style out-ranks the Remove close-button rule so it renders below the image, invisible, over the mode menu), carry the stylesheet's intended placement and leave the operated repair acceptance to the owner (face controls). Test-only actions never appear in normal product UI.

## Source map (classic, read-only, classic `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (or the frozen import revision recorded in `inventory.md`; re-check line numbers there with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`))
`Product.fs`: `faq` 1125-1127 and `explainSection` 1128-1181 (page body below the fold, present on load); `debugArea` 1182-1192; in `view`: invite section `.next-invite` (~1226-1235, `?testing` only, "Turn on debug reporting" / "Not now", `.next-invite-note`), error box 1289-1308 (`.next-error.box`, `.next-error-reference`, `.next-actions`, `.next-error-retry`, `.next-error-classic`), hidden project open 1309-1318 (`.next-project-open`, `projectFilesVisible=false`), model toast ~1376-1407 (`.next-consent-toast.next-model-toast`, `.next-consent-message`, `.next-model-progress`, auto-hide 5,000 ms when done), failure toast ~1429-1443 (`.next-consent-toast.next-failure-toast`, shown only when FailureToast && not Debug && Error && no model toast && no Gate), trial-phase consent snackbar ~1444-1453. Tester bulk Generate is the `?testing` path (`testingInvited`, `testing-link.test.mjs`).
Repair rows not to reproduce: stacked toasts covering Create Morph (defect 16) and the failure toast's "Send report" label turning standing reporting on (defect 12) are owned by diagnostics control; carry the candidate rendering for parity rows only where the freeze classes them parity, otherwise leave them owner-graded.

## Goldens replayed
Flow rows (DOM level): Report error with/without standing consent, Use tester bulk Generate faces or support/contact links, Turn standing debug reports On/Off (candidate debug area), First app visit (trial-phase prompt).

## Goldens and grading (polish r1)
- **Golden store.** Goldens are the recorder output chosen by `migration.golden-spike` (reducer transitions or journey-step DOM/state snapshots), committed under `apps/web/test/goldens/control/<flow-row-id>/` with a `goldens.json` index naming the control `deploy-next/` SHA-256, the recorder command and, per step, the freeze class of its row. Replays run `scripts/fetch-control.mjs` first and refuse to run if the index digest differs from `control-artifact.json`.
- **Parity rows** (freeze class *present and unchanged*): the port's transitions/DOM must equal the golden exactly (state fields, emitted effect descriptions, text, flow order, round-trip bytes). No tolerance, no "close enough".
- **Repair rows** (candidate defects 1-23) and **declared-change rows**: never parity. The recorder tags their steps `repair:<n>` or `declared:<section>` and the replay lists them as owner-graded instead of asserting them. No test in this repository may encode a candidate defect as expected output. Where the defect lives entirely in what this leaf writes (a string, a CSS rule order, a label), write the specification's version; where the repair needs the owner's design or copy, carry the nearest candidate behaviour without asserting it and leave the repair, and its grading against the plan specification, to the named owner.
- **Absent rows** are specification-graded by their owners after parity; this leaf adds no behaviour for them.
- A row the recorder cannot exercise is listed `untested` with the reason, never passed.

## Tester tools and issue links: safety checks (polish r2)
Candidate preservation comparison, 12 October:
- `?testing` bulk Generate faces and the Help/footer issue and contact links are retained.
- Test-only actions never appear in normal product UI.
- Prefilled issue context carries only safe facts: source version, device/browser class, actual route and report reference. Never photos, latents, typed words or seeds, file names or raw error strings.
- There is no automatic issue submission: opening the link is plain navigation.

A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Without `?testing` a DOM scan finds no bulk-Generate or invite control; with it, the bulk action works (operated). The issue URL built by the bridge's `issueUrl` is unit-tested to contain only version, device/browser class, actual route and report reference (a typed word, a seed, a file name and a thrown error message are each absent); clicking the issue link issues no request other than the navigation (event log).

title: Retire Triton inference and both API hostnames
description:
## Goal
Stop paying for and operating hosted inference: retire Triton, encoder/legacy API hosting and both `api.facemorph.me` and `checkface.facemorph.me` completely — no replacement, static artifact API, GUID resolver, redirect or proxy at those hostnames — while model chunks, the names catalogue, preview/latent assets and consented diagnostics keep serving. Old Mongo GUIDs, uploaded-photo links and historic morph URLs are deliberately unsupported; self-host users run classic Compose. Because this is irreversible, it keeps a full receipt.

## Scope
- Authority: before any change, confirm the operator's cutover decision (`gate:cutover`, PLAN.md dated decisions) names **API retirement**; otherwise make no change and record `blocked: no authorizing decision`.
- Preconditions from the action list: preview/latent snapshot verified; the `multi-morph-test.vercel.app` user told; the operator's chosen order relative to promotion recorded; names.facemorph.me redirected, or the recorded order accepts that the standalone names grid stops until promotion.
- Before state: DNS records, Pages/Workers bindings, tunnels, processes and API-only credentials per the retirement inventory, and HTTP responses of both hostnames (status, headers, body digest).
- Remove processes, routes, tunnels, API-only credentials and DNS/Pages bindings per the retirement inventory; keep shared resources (model chunks, catalogue, preview/latent Workers, collector, `models.facemorph.me` and its bucket/credentials, the `/stats/v1` statistics Worker and its scrape token, `metrics.facemorph.me` Grafana, and the triton Prometheus with its stored series of the old API counters `image_generating_total`, `image_encoding_total`, `request_processing_seconds`, `generator_network_seconds`, `ffmpeg_processing_seconds` — the "before" side of the changeover statistics, kept 5 years). Retiring Triton inference stops the inference and API processes only: the triton machine stays as a development worker and Prometheus host. Retire the Vercel publisher if not already done.
- After state: `post-delivery-check --mode retired` for both hostnames; `post-delivery-check --mode app` on every live app host (facemorph.me if promoted, next.facemorph.me) incl. the `models.facemorph.me` chunk comparison, catalogue and a test diagnostics report; each shared resource on the keep list probed.
- Changeover statistics: post the cutover annotation with `scripts/delivery/annotate-cutover.mjs` (tag `facemorph-cutover`, action `api-retirement`).
- **Receipt** (`docs/receipts/delivery-api-retirement.md`): what was removed, with the runbook's exact commands; before/after state per retirement-inventory item; what stopped and what did not; source commit; the operator decision cited; snapshot manifest digest; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; evidence link.

## Out of scope
Production data disposal (a separate explicit operation); deleting repository history; re-archiving `checkface`; promotion.

## Notes
- Order relative to promotion is the operator's call. After this, the legacy production UI depends on a dead API and is not a rollback; rollback is a retained on-device artifact.
- Unfinished package work never keeps the hosted GPU/API on.
- Receipt kept per PLAN.md "Acceptance receipts" (an irreversible action reads it).
- Plan: #retire-hosted-inference-and-the-old-api-completely, #delivery-and-publication, #domain-handover-and-retirement-preparation, #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance.

title: Verify Morph parent-intent scheduling, disposal and no starvation
description:
## Background
Shared-resource contract: Morph is a parent intent, not an extra heavyweight lease while waiting for prerequisite face jobs; dependencies are admitted once and join an existing operation for the same slot/revision; compute admission is released before awaiting dependencies or consent; the frame-production lease is requested through the same scheduler; parent Cancel stops work owned solely by that parent and leaves independently requested face results; failed/cancelled inputs settle the parent with a specific recovery action. Join the dependency's compute-ready milestone rather than default-file completion. The plan states the morph pipeline verifies competing intents, disposal and no starvation/deadlock.

## Why
Morph must compose with photo encodes and face generation without duplicate inference, deadlock or a permanently disabled button.

## Scope
- Integrate `renderMorph` with the operation controller's scheduler interface.
- Tests: photo -> queued Morph; Morph auto-generation -> explicit face request; capability loss while queued; Cancel at each dependency boundary; competing provider-load requests; idle retained encoder while generator loading is requested; delayed/failed face-file preparation not blocking ready inputs and not duplicating inference; bounded endpoint reuse.
- Changing an input or setting supersedes the intent, aborts obsolete production and cannot install stale files; settings stay disabled during active morph as in the candidate.

## Out of scope
Scheduler implementation (operation controller). Progress/Cancel presentation (face controls).

## Considerations
- Uses the operation controller's fake-clock harness plus one real-bridge run.

## One current result and revision invalidation (polish r1)
- Exactly one current morph result exists. Changing the ordered faces or any morph setting creates a new morph revision: the old result's Share/Save readiness is withdrawn, its prepared file is no longer offered as current, and any late frame, video or file completion from the old revision is discarded (`morph.stale-rejected` event) and cannot install.
- A completed face stays usable when another face fails; the morph settles with the failed slot's specific recovery action.
- Once Morph is accepted, repeated clicks cannot queue a second intent (`morph.intent-accepted` count stays 1 until it settles or is superseded).
- Named tests: `morph-intent.single-current-result`, `morph-intent.input-change-invalidates`, `morph-intent.setting-change-invalidates`, `morph-intent.late-completion-rejected`, `morph-intent.repeated-click-no-duplicate`, `morph-intent.face-failure-keeps-others`.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Fake-clock tests for every listed case pass with no starvation/deadlock and no duplicate inference (operation event log).
- [ ] One real-bridge run asserts the expected operation trace.

title: Pin Oxlint and Oxfmt with root configs and scripts
description:
## Background

Plan: Oxlint for authored JS/TS/JSX/TSX, Oxfmt for supported source/config/docs. Snapshot versions
(16 October): oxlint 1.88.0, oxfmt 0.73.0 (pre-1.0). Planned scripts: `lint` = `oxlint
--deny-warnings`; `lint:fix` = `oxlint --fix`; `format` = `oxfmt`; `format:check` = `oxfmt --check`.

## Why

One small, consistent toolchain for the TS monorepo; read-only CI gates.

## Scope

- Pin `oxlint` and `oxfmt` as root devDependencies in the lockfile (exact versions selected and tested
  here, never `npx ...@latest`).
- One root `.oxlintrc.json` and `.oxfmtrc.json` (JSON so tool config is independent of TS loaders),
  explicit file overrides and ignore patterns, editor instructions in the dev guide.
- Oxlint native TypeScript and verified React/hooks rules with environment overrides for browser UI,
  workers and Node tooling; correctness rules on.
- Oxfmt: 100-column width, two-space indentation, import/package-field reordering off.
- Include authored app/package files, maintained scripts, configs, current docs; exclude dependencies,
  generated outputs, build/distribution assets, vendored code, weights, fixtures, tracker state/export
  (`.beads/`), and immutable historical scripts/reports named by the inventory (including the frozen
  `autoresearch/candidates/`, history and reviews trees). Exclusions name frozen artifacts rather than
  hiding all future autoresearch code or maintained adapters.

## Out of scope

Running the formatter over the tree (next item). Python/F#/Rust/shader formatting.

## Considerations

Linter coverage does not establish dependency isolation, numerical correctness or type checking; TS remains a separate gate. Any type-aware lint mode needs its own verified setup.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Scripts exist and use the pinned configs locally, in CI and per the editor instructions.
- [ ] A listing shows the discovered roots and ignored paths match the inventory's frozen list.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] A config unit test asserts the four root `package.json` scripts exactly (`lint` = `oxlint --deny-warnings`, `lint:fix` = `oxlint --fix`, `format` = `oxfmt`, `format:check` = `oxfmt --check`), that `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are exact devDependency versions (no `^`/`~`), that `.oxfmtrc.json` sets print width 100, two-space indentation and import/package-field sorting off, and that `.oxlintrc.json` enables correctness plus TypeScript, React and react-hooks rules with browser, worker and Node overrides.
- [ ] A seeded 101-column line fails `format:check`, a seeded warning-level lint finding fails `lint`, running `format` twice leaves the tree unchanged (idempotence), and frozen/generated/vendored paths are byte-identical before and after `format` (digest list recorded).
