title: Consent modal and Prepare encoder
description:
26 October operator clarification: optional early preparation belongs beside the top Auto/CPU/WebGPU selector, above the first +. No per-card Prepare encoder or blank Encode source modal. Skipping early preparation still automatically opens explanatory consent on Generate/Morph/fresh-photo preparation when prerequisites are missing, after recovery inspection and before model acquisition. One modal explains separate synthesis/encoder purposes, missing bytes and ranges/unknowns; only approved scopes download. Changing provider alone authorizes nothing. Page-level preparation is independently owned and survives cancelling an unrelated card chooser. This supersedes conflicting placement and source-modal lifecycle prose; existing behavioral acceptance remains.

26 October operator correction: use the actual face card for file chooser/drop/paste, with no empty Encode source modal. Keep crop confirmation/adjustment for fresh photos. Generate/Cancel/Cancelling/Retry belongs inline beside the textbox; all validation, cancellation, stale-result, consent, recovery and batch guarantees remain. Placement/source-entry assertions below supersede conflicting historical wording; no behavioral acceptance is waived.

## Goal
One compact, action-triggered consent modal (**Generate and encode** / **Generate**) with honest per-purpose rows, one figure per purpose everywhere, and a Prepare encoder action that lets approved photo setup overlap the native file chooser. It replaces the candidate's "Download the face model?" dialog, proactive offer toast and arrival prompts, whose figures disagree, and it brings the codec fallback inside consent.

## Scope
- **Defects fixed.** Defect 10: toast says 149 MB, 1.1 GB and 1.2 GB while progress says 158 MB and 1,040 MB. Defect 19 (codec part): the 32 MB video-fallback codec is outside every consent. Remove the proactive offer toast; no arrival download.
- **Triggers.** Only Generate, Morph or photo preparation (including Prepare encoder), after route/resource admission. Never on arrival, for static names, recovered-file display/Save or valid cache hits. Opening Encode image or the page alone authorizes nothing.
- **Choices and rows.** Two labelled choices: **Generate and encode** (recommended only when the photo route passes admission) and **Generate**. Rows: "Generate: {missing bytes}; download {range/unknown}; generate {range/unknown}" and "Encode: {additional bytes}; download {range/unknown}; encode {range/unknown} per face" (plus a batch range when several faces are selected). "Download time depends on your connection" when there is no evidence; cached scopes say "Already downloaded, subject to verification"; a short first-use setup caveat with optional details; codec fallback bytes included in the row of the purpose that needs them. Only the requested action's rows; no technical breakdown in the main decision at narrow widths. Unknown estimates are a supported state (no wait on calibration).
- **One figure per purpose**, in one unit, identical in modal, progress and any status line.
- **Cannot-keep line.** When `navigator.storage.estimate()` quota minus usage is below the package's remaining bytes, that purpose's row adds one line with the same byte count as the row, e.g. "This device can't keep the 1,040 MB download, so it downloads again on each visit." Decided from reported quota and usage, never from a user agent or "iPhone" label. Unknown quota (API absent or throwing) shows no line and no guess. Provenance: every iOS storage check (143) reported a 1,000 MB quota with zero use while the CPU package is 1,040 MB; the one cold iPhone attempt stopped at 678 MB (`docs/findings/diagnostics-learnings-2026-10-18.md`; provider phone-CPU check supplies the measured figures). The line ships driven by the predicate even if every tested cell can keep the package.
- **Dismissal.** Download and continue authorizes the selected bundle. Cancel, Escape, backdrop and Back start nothing, restore focus to the initiating control and preserve completed work.
- **Generate chosen from a fresh-photo request.** Say "Encoding needs the photo encoder" and pause that continuation; the chosen source stays in tab memory within its byte ceiling so a later Generate and encode approval resumes without choosing the file again; the tile returns to useful face generation.
- **Acquisition failure after approval** (download, integrity, cache write or quota): the owning progress area says what failed in plain words, truthful downloaded/remaining bytes in the same unit, a bounded explicit **Retry** that resumes from kept verified chunks within the unchanged scope, completed work preserved. Quota failure is worded as storage, not as an execution-capability limit. Quota/cache-retention failure after a completed result: the prepared file's Save still works, the action area says the downloaded model could not be kept, and no transient execution is offered unless its bounded path is qualified.
- Slow-work nudge copy from the device workstream appears in the same area when a range suggests a substantial wait.
- **Prepare encoder.** Shown beside the top Auto/CPU/WebGPU selector above the first +, only when eligible required assets are missing (rendering is in face.selector-names); it opens the same bundle consent. After a fresh source is inspected, the consent is used automatically where prerequisites are missing.
- **Setup ownership.** **Cancel setup** stops that setup owner's remaining acquisition/warming while keeping local source/crop work; a later OK uses verified complete assets; missing assets need explicit resume/reapproval through the same flow, never a silent revival. Cancelling a card chooser/crop abandons only that action owner and continuation, preserving independently approved page-level preparation; cancelling a later add-file chooser leaves the batch/setup intact; independent owners survive. If a result is ready before optional preparation finishes, its actions work while the compact status keeps cancellation.

## Out of scope
Range computation (device workstream); scheduling (consent.grant); measuring quota or keepability (provider phone-CPU check); rendering of the Prepare encoder entry (face.selector-names).

## Notes
- React rendering in the ported UI sources plus a small quota predicate in app code; setup-owner lifecycle in the consent and operation modules. Edits none of the shared bridge/runtime/worker files; if that changes, add the morph-pipeline ordering edge first.
- Prepare encoder tie-break: consent owns the action and its ownership, face controls renders the entry beside the top provider selector (PLAN.md#workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership).
- Anchors: PLAN.md#lightweight-device-check-and-pre-download-guidance, #consented-downloads-useful-overlap-and-cached-model-warming, #provider-simplification, #clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation. Audit rows 10 and 19.
acceptance_criteria:
Operated rule throughout: real pointer input (touch tap at phone width) at the visible position, `elementFromPoint` returns the control, the point lies in the named region; by-name clicks only for setup. Each case at 390 px and 1,280 px, light and dark, one screenshot per case.
- [ ] **Generate and encode** / **Generate** (modal body, above the rows), **Download and continue** (footer right) and **Cancel** (footer left) operated; Escape, backdrop and Back each equal Cancel: zero model-host requests (intercepted), focus back on the initiating Generate/Morph/Encode image control.
- [ ] The modal opens from operated Generate, Create Morph, Encode image photo preparation and Prepare encoder, each with only the rows its purpose needs.
- [ ] Batch rows with 1, 2, 3, 30, 64 and 150 photo faces selected: per-face and batch range (or labelled unknown); layout stays inside the modal at 320 px.
- [ ] Byte figures: string comparison of the same number and unit across modal, progress and status, including codec fallback bytes when the codec is needed.
- [ ] Cannot-keep unit tests over predicate and string: quota 1,000 MB / usage 0 with a 1,040 MB package shows the line with "1,040 MB" (same string as the row) and "each visit"; quota 5,000 MB, API throwing, API absent, and an iPhone UA with a large quota each show no line.
- [ ] Cold page load, static-name selection and opening a recovery-bearing still: no modal and zero model-host requests.
- [ ] Generate-only approval from a photo request: zero encoder requests; pause line shown; source held so a later Generate and encode resumes without re-choosing; operated Generate on another face works.
- [ ] Acquisition failure (the real local model server returns 500 mid-transfer or serves corrupted bytes; a real browser storage quota runs out on cache write, giving a real `QuotaExceededError`): plain message in the owning progress area, downloaded/remaining bytes in the row unit; operated **Retry** resumes without re-downloading verified chunks (intercepted bytes); completed faces unchanged; quota worded as storage.
- [ ] `QuotaExceededError` on cache write after a successful generate: Save still works, storage wording, no unqualified transient execution offered.
- [ ] 320 px copy check: only the requested action's rows, no technical breakdown. Unknown estimates render labelled unknown and the modal stays usable.
- [ ] Prepare encoder owner-lifecycle unit tests: card chooser/crop cancel abandons only its action owner and preserves page-level preparation; add-file cancel keeps; Cancel setup then OK with missing assets -> reapproval prompt; independent owner survives.
- [ ] Request-interception run: Prepare encoder -> approve -> encoder requests start before any file is chosen; Cancel setup -> no new encoder request after the declared bound.
- [ ] Acquisition, cancellation and negative-path checks of PLAN.md#integrated-verification for consent pass on the built app.
- [ ] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test`) and pass.
- [ ] phone CPU figures at close come from fm-fy2.19 (with fm-fy2.19). If fm-fy2.19 has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-fy2.19 (`br update fm-fy2.19 --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-fy2.19
- [ ] Optional preparation is reachable beside the top selector at 390/1280 px; selecting a provider alone starts zero model requests. Skip preparation, operate Generate/Morph/fresh-photo entry, and verify explanatory consent before missing assets are fetched, with separate Generate/Encode rows and only approved scopes requested. Recovery-bearing still/cache hit needs no consent. No blank source modal or per-card preparation control.

title: Run the non-face joint proof from checkpoint to export and reopen
description:
## Background
Proposed fixture: NVlabs AFHQ cat 512 px, subject to converter compatibility and acquisition terms; not currently claimed supported. Generic code must drop FFHQ's fixed 1024 px / 18x512 assumptions; descriptors govern shapes. Non-face generation must not load the face detector or FFHQ e4e.

## Why
Only this joint proof qualifies the documented non-face capability; component completion or publication alone does not.

## Scope
Independently of the FaceMorph app, in the clean consumer built by `verify.packages-clean-consumers` (same
tarballs, same integrity hashes). Input is the hand-off bundle from `conversion.nonface` (fm-i3k6): checkpoint
source, digest and terms; container and base-image digests and the exact commands; reference errors against the
declared tolerance; descriptor and schema-valid manifests. Re-check every digest in the bundle before use; a
mismatch aborts the run. If `conversion.nonface` recorded the fixture as blocked, this leaf records non-face support
as unqualified with that blocker and runs nothing else.
- Trusted checkpoint acquisition (source/digest, terms recorded).
- Pinned container conversion and independent reference checks with a declared small tolerance for this model.
- Developer-controlled static hosting (no FaceMorph hostname, catalogue, alias or secret).
- Manager-loaded and directly caller-loaded inference; seed mapping, synthesis, multi-input morph.
- PNG/lossless-WebP export and reopen with exact model/latent metadata; equal-shaped latents from different checkpoints not silently combined.
- Request log: no detector/e4e download.

## Out of scope
Dataset training; generic non-face photo encoder.

## Considerations
- If the fixture is blocked (converter or terms), label non-face support unqualified and name the blocker; this does not delay API retirement.
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Joint-proof report with checkpoint digest, container digest, tolerance, hosting URL class, both load paths, morph, export/reopen results.
- [ ] Request log shows zero face detector or e4e requests.
- [ ] The receipt links the `conversion.nonface` hand-off bundle and shows each of its digests re-verified.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome) through the shared emitter from `build.event-log-core` (fm-bd03) and passes `scripts/check-event-log.ts`; the log is kept as a CI artifact, privacy-filtered like diagnostics; screenshots kept on failure.
- [ ] Each case is listed in this leaf's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix row IDs or defect numbers it grades.
- [ ] Ran against the named release-candidate artifact digest (the same digest the join report checks); a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded failed or untested, never passed.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Delete the old-wording diagnostics reports with a receipt, then repeat until none older than the boundary remain
description:
## Background
Operator, 18 October: "I do want to delete the telemetry collected under the 30 days verbiage once we have mined it for
insights. Keep the insights." The candidate's corrected consent line went live at **2026-10-17 20:28:59 UTC** (commit
`40c63a9`, deploy job finish) - the **boundary**. The mined set is the 801 objects under `runs/` in R2 bucket
`facemorph-diagnostics` uploaded 22 September to 17 October 08:02 UTC, key-list digest
`c3833f1f056ae0700e82d997a592e9009114d014a7b1ce8ae21c45cd8c07e0fb`. A dry run on 18 October confirmed all 801 exist,
none newer than the mined set, all before the boundary. **The earliest reports passed 30 days on 22 October, so the old
promise is overdue as of this polish (24 October).** KV fallback copies expire after 30 days by their own setting. Raw
working copies from the WebGL read (17 October) and the mining (18 October) sit in session scratch directories.

## Why
Keeps the old promise and leaves only the findings (PLAN.md#debug-reporting-control-and-consent, retention decision
items 2-5).

## Scope
One-off script `scripts/diagnostics/delete-old-wording-reports.mjs` (standalone Node 22, no workspace dependencies;
not a bucket rule), run unattended once its preconditions pass. Steps, in order, each logged to the structured event
log (no keys or contents):
1. **Preconditions (all automated; any failure stops the run before any delete and is reported):**
   a. The note `docs/findings/diagnostics-learnings-2026-10-18.md` is committed and reachable from the default
      branch on the remote (`git fetch` then `git merge-base --is-ancestor 7875aaf origin/main`, or the default branch
      the identity map names), so the only kept copy of the insights is durable before the raw data goes. **Precondition outside the graph (an operator action, not an approval):** as of
      24 October local `main` is 4 commits ahead of `origin/main` and `7875aaf` is not pushed, so this check fails
      until someone with push rights pushes `facemorph.me` `main`. Pushing is not a decision or sign-off about the
      deletion: the operator already ordered the deletion (18 October) and nothing in this bead asks anyone to
      confirm it. The script checks the push itself; when it is absent the run exits with status
      `precondition-a-unmet` before any listing or delete, writes nothing to the bucket, and leaves the bead open.
      The next run after the push (any agent claiming the bead, re-running the same idempotent script) proceeds
      through steps 1-6 with no further input.
   b. `scripts/diagnostics/scan-learnings-note.mjs` passes on the note at HEAD.
   c. `docs/receipts/diagnostics/learnings-ingest.md` exists, is committed and passes `scripts/receipts/check-receipt.mjs`.
   d. A **read-only** token (R2 Object Read, scoped to `facemorph-diagnostics`) lists the bucket: the set
      D = objects uploaded before the boundary; its count and the SHA-256 of its sorted keys are computed in memory.
      If D's digest equals `c3833f1f…e0fb` (count 801), proceed. If D contains objects not in the mined set (uploaded
      after 08:02 and before the boundary), stop the delete and run the **mine-then-delete repeat**: aggregate those
      objects into a new dated section of the findings note (aggregates only, scan passes), commit, record the new
      key-list digest, then restart from step 1 with the union as the mined set.
2. **Pre-delete receipt section** written to `docs/receipts/diagnostics/old-report-deletion-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`:
   count of D, its key-list digest, the boundary moment, the mined-set upper bound (08:02 UTC 17 October), the count
   and key-list digest of objects uploaded after the boundary (set A, kept untouched).
3. **Delete** exactly the keys in D with a separate short-lived token (R2 Object Read & Write, scoped to the one
   bucket), created by the script through the logged-in `cf` CLI and revoked immediately after the deletes; token IDs
   (never values) and creation/revocation times recorded. Deletes run in batches with retry on transient errors; the
   key list lives only in memory.
4. **Post-checks with the read-only token:** re-list; count of D's keys present = 0; count of objects uploaded before
   the boundary = 0; set A's count and digest unchanged (nothing after the boundary was touched); the bucket lifecycle
   configuration (`GET /accounts/{account}/r2/buckets/facemorph-diagnostics/lifecycle`) contains only the default
   multipart-abort rule and no expiration rule; bucket lock absent. KV fallback namespace: list (read-only) the count of
   remaining fallback entries and the latest `expiration`, recorded (they expire on their own 30-day TTL; no action).
5. **Working copies:** delete every raw working copy of the reports. The script searches `/tmp`, `$TMPDIR`,
   `~/.cache`, `~/Work` and any path listed in `scripts/diagnostics/working-copy-paths.txt` for files or directories
   that contain any run ID or key from D (matched in memory), plus the known scratch directories of the 17 and 18
   October sessions (found from the session record); deletes them; re-scans to confirm zero matches. The receipt
   records the number of files and bytes removed and the scanned roots, with run IDs redacted from any path.
6. **Receipt completion:** outcome, post-check results, deviations, untested cells (for example, a workstation not
   reachable from the run host), evidence link (the CI/job log artifact); passes `check-receipt.mjs`; committed.
- Never touch objects uploaded after the boundary. Add no expiration rule; make no deletion promise for later reports.
- Repeat the mine-then-delete pass until a listing finds nothing uploaded before the boundary.

## Out of scope
Collector code changes (`diag.collector-rebinding`); the new app's retention copy (`diag.disclosure-control`).

## Considerations
Runs on its own once the note is on the remote default branch and the ingest receipt verifies; no human approval step (operator,
18 October: "it runs on its own once the note is committed and does not wait for a human"; PLAN.md's earlier round note
"runs on the operator's go" is superseded by that ruling). Needs only bucket access and the `cf` CLI, no monorepo
prerequisite. P0 because it is overdue. The script's own unit tests use a fake R2 client (list/delete/lifecycle) and a
temp directory tree for working copies.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** It adds one standalone script under `scripts/diagnostics/` and a receipt; it edits no app source. It must stay unordered with respect to the shared-file chain (PLAN.md 17 October: the names data-shape spike, generator and publication, and the diagnostics learnings ingestion, edit none of these files): never add an edge from this bead to ws:migration.facade, ws:compute, ws:crop or ws:morph. If implementation finds it must edit one of them after all, it first runs `br dep add fm-9n5b fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph), adds the file to the conflict list in fm-bhw and records the change in its receipt (the plan's rule: an edge is added when an edit is discovered).
acceptance_criteria:

title: Typed loaded handles with reference-counted asset leases and disposal
description:
## Background
Contracts milestone 1 freezes loaded handles (ownership, digests, shapes, mapping/synthesis/encoder). Loaded handles identify actual providers, admission and validation state.

## Why
The engine gets a capability that cannot acquire more files; deletion/eviction cannot pull assets from under a running operation.

## Scope
- Loaded-handle type per contract; reference-counted leases on required verified local assets; manager-controlled deletion/eviction excludes leased assets.
- Browser eviction, corruption, cross-tab deletion or device/worker loss invalidates the capability with a typed error; affected operations settle and release without network repair.
- Disposal releases leases and sessions; reacquisition/re-admission happen outside engine execution through app policy.

## Out of scope
Provider adapter (next leaf).

## Considerations
Leases constrain manager behaviour, not the browser's ability to reclaim storage.

title: Implement export identity, filenames, collisions and prepared-file cache
description:
## Background
Operator ruling on filenames: short informative defaults from the result's name, entered text, seed or source-file basename, e.g. `emma-k4p7s2.webp`, `seed-42-j8m3r6.png`, `holiday-face2-v9d2h5.webp`, `emma-noah-linear-c6q8t3.mp4`, `emma-noah-figure8-b7w4n2.mp4` (suffixes illustrative). Contracts milestone 2 freezes stable export identity and collision-safe suggested names with platform-specific no-clobber behaviour.

## Why
Different exports must never be mistaken for one another, and repeated Save/Share of the same prepared file must reuse its name and bytes.

## Scope
- Stable export identity over crops, ordered inputs, morph modes/settings, models and encoding options; short suffix derived from it; collision detection/extension within the app's known export set (labels alone, timestamps alone and slot numbers are insufficient).
- Label rules: preserve a recognizable short label; for longer paths first/last label plus a face count; include morph mode; distinguish selected crops; strip source extension, path components, control/bidi characters, filesystem-reserved characters and names; normalize whitespace; truncate the descriptive part before the suffix to at most 64 characters before the real extension; `face`/`morph` only when no informative label exists.
- After reload latents do not recover words/basenames: reuse a safe opened filename where applicable, otherwise generic label plus stable suffix; never add labels to metadata.
- Extension and MIME match the actual WebP/PNG/MP4 bytes (PNG fallback updates both).
- Prepared-file cache: one current prepared file per selected revision/format plus a bounded cache for additional formats; a format change invalidates only that file's readiness and never re-runs inference; identity preserved through restoration.
- Optional File System Access writes use no-clobber naming or explicit overwrite confirmation.
- API for face controls to propose/edit the name while keeping the identity suffix.

## Out of scope
Rendering and editing the filename, Share/Save buttons and format control (face controls).

## Considerations
- Browsers cannot inspect existing Downloads; do not claim absolute filesystem uniqueness from a short suffix.
- Informative filenames are visible to recipients but do not authorize adding text/source names to metadata or diagnostics.

## Concrete rules and tests (polish r1)
- **Identity.** `exportIdentity({kind, orderedInputs: [{inputIdentity, confirmedCropIdentity?}], morph?: {mode, settings}, modelIdentity, format, encodingOptions})` -> SHA-256; the short suffix is derived from it using the encoding and length frozen in contracts milestone 2 (the operator examples, e.g. `emma-k4p7s2.webp`, show 6 lowercase letters/digits without vowels). A collision within the app's known export set (same suggested name, different identity) is resolved by the contracts' collision rule (for example extending the suffix) until unique; the test forces collisions by stubbing the hash.
- **Prepared-file cache.** Key = (result revision, format, encoding options). One current prepared file per selected revision and format, plus a bounded cache of other formats (bound declared in the contracts milestone 2 record; tested at cap and cap + 1 with oldest-first eviction). A completion for a superseded revision is discarded (`prepared.stale-rejected` event). A format change prepares only that format with no inference (spy). "Preparing file..." is the state between pixels shown and file ready; encode failure keeps the visible result and offers file-preparation retry. System-share cancellation is not an error and triggers no download.
- **Encoding policy** comes from the `export-policy` module (media.split): WebP quality 0.8 default, PNG as explicit lossless choice and as WebP fallback; MP4 settings unchanged. The format is part of identity, so WebP and PNG of the same result get distinct suffixes but share the label.
- **Labels after reload.** By default latents do not recover words or basenames, so a restored result uses a safe opened filename where applicable, otherwise `face`/`morph` plus the stable suffix. If the defect 9 proposal (media.session-words) lands and a tab-scoped label was restored, that label may be used; labels never go into metadata or diagnostics either way.
- Named tests: `export-name.label-rules` (control/bidi characters, reserved names such as `CON`/`NUL`, path components, extension stripping, whitespace, 64-character truncation before the suffix, empty, very long, pasted multi-line), `export-name.examples` (reproduces each operator example shape), `export-identity.matrix` (distinct same-basename sources, multiple crops, text/seed/name inputs, reversed endpoints, linear vs figure-eight vs settings changes, invalid labels, forced collisions), `export-identity.same-bytes-same-name`, `prepared-cache.revision-format`, `prepared-cache.cap`, `prepared-cache.stale-rejected`, `prepared-cache.format-change-no-inference`, `export-mime.matches-bytes` (WebP, PNG fallback, MP4), `fs-access.no-clobber` (optional picker writes use a new name or explicit overwrite confirmation).

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests for every label rule including bidi/control/reserved-name stripping, 64-character truncation, very long and pasted labels, empty labels.
- [ ] Identity matrix tests: distinct source files sharing a basename, multiple crops, text/seed/name inputs, reversed morph endpoints, linear/figure-eight/settings changes, truncated or invalid labels and forced suffix collisions each yield distinct names; identical prepared bytes keep their name.
- [ ] MIME/extension match tested for WebP, PNG fallback and MP4.
- [ ] Format change does not trigger inference (spy assertion); prepared-file cache bounded (unit test at cap).
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Named tests under 'Concrete rules and tests (polish r1)' pass; the suffix is derived from the export identity, and forced collisions are resolved by extension, asserted in the test log.
- [ ] Prepared-file cache: superseded-revision completions are rejected (event logged), a format change prepares only that format with zero inference, and the cache bound is tested at cap and cap + 1 (bound cited from the contracts milestone 2 record; until then 'measured, no threshold').
notes: Position in the shared-file sequence: after media.recovery-reader, before media.mp4-metadata. Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Leaves that must not edit these three files: ws:crop.repro (failing tests and the failure analysis only), crop.policy, media.envelope-helpers, media.recovery-schema, morph.descriptor-geometry, compute.consumer-example, compute.names-equality, and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept leaf. They keep the module export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) and move logic behind them into the package. If such a leaf finds it must edit one of the three files, it records the file in the check-migration map conflict list and adds a needs edge to the latest leaf in the sequence that edits it; it never edits concurrently. Each sequenced leaf lists every file it edits in the check-migration map conflict list at claim time.

description:
## Goal
Re-home the diagnostics collector Worker with its tests so diagnostics survive the move and collector bindings stay independent of Triton/API retirement, and give the names-catalogue staging and publication workflow a home in this repository that does not depend on the hosted API being alive.

## Scope
- Collector: `hosting/next-cloudflare/` (`worker.mjs`, `validation.mjs`, `delete-run.mjs`, `worker.test.mjs`, `wrangler.toml`, `README.md`) from candidate `6107f80` or later. Never import `.wrangler/`.
- Route/host bindings become per-environment configuration; `next.facemorph.me` (today `reporting.mjs` posts to `https://next.facemorph.me/diagnostics/events`) is not hard-coded outside the environment file.
- Carry `hosting/next-cloudflare/worker.test.mjs` unchanged (covers `validation.mjs`, the privacy allowlist, and `delete-run.mjs`) and list it in test discovery (classic ran it in the artifact job's `node --test` list).
- `src/Next/reporting.test.mjs` imports `hosting/next-cloudflare/validation.mjs`: keep that path resolvable after the move, or update both sides in one revision, so the client/collector allowlist cannot drift.
- No expiration rule on the bucket (retention decision 17/18 October): no `expiresAt` on R2 objects, no KV TTL.
- Supply a local collector fixture command that diagnostics and integrated verification post to for their consented/declined sample checks.
- Catalogue pipeline: `hosting/gallery/` (`materialize.py`, `wrangler.jsonc`, `names-wrangler.jsonc`, provenance notes); entry points live in `hosting/gallery/` and the workflow in `.github/workflows/`.
- Remove the hosted-API dependency: `materialize.py` (`--output`, `--origin` HTTPS static origin, `--limit`) fetches `https://api.facemorph.me/api/face/?value=...&dim=1024` (line ~56) for a name whose image is not on disk; inputs come from the verified local selection and the static-names generator instead.
- `wrangler.jsonc` and `names-wrangler.jsonc` deploy static-only Workers (no worker code, no upload endpoint). `hosting/next-static/catalogue.json` is the names index staged by `stage.py --catalogue`.

- Shared client/collector action list (defect 13), retention wording, production collector rebinding (`diag.rebinding`, delivery).

- The catalogue generator and its data shape (`names.generator`, `names.spike`); publication order (`names.publish`).

## Notes

title: Collect control/control noise and lock margins
description:
## Background

First collect compatible control/control noise where missing, then freeze margins, sample/confirmation rules and stopping decisions before observing candidate benefit.

## Why

Margins must come from variability, not from favourable samples.

## Scope

- Control/control runs per supported workload cell on available workers under the lease; complete context and raw noise reports; margins frozen in the specs.

## Out of scope

Candidate comparisons.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Noise reports with raw data and frozen margins committed; ledger rows appended as baseline evidence.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script involved emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform and provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, retains the log as a CI artifact, and any network claim is asserted from that log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Outputs and event logs are copied to the durable output location named in the launch recipe (outside transient CI artifacts) and the round record cites that path; private or local-only raw files are labelled as such; a CI artifact is only a convenience copy.
- [ ] Noise reports split within-run, separate-browser-start and rebuild variability; each frozen margin cites the level and the control/control pairs it came from.

title: Catalogue result generator
description:
## Goal
Produce canonical recovery-bearing WebP results for every catalogue name from the same text resolver typed input uses, so picking a name is inference-free and identical to typing it. Latents are not the gap; canonical recovery-bearing pixels are: every current full-size name image is a lossy JPEG fetched from the retiring API by `materialize.py`, and that tooling stops working at API retirement. The generator never calls the hosted API.

## Scope
- Run the exact lowercase names through a qualified runtime on a capable worker under the shared device lease. The pinned candidate runtime in a headless browser is an acceptable producer because extraction must preserve its raw output within the same tolerances; published identity must not depend on which runtime produced it.
- Write the default recovery-bearing WebP through the media envelope helpers (candidate envelope code until extraction). Sizing to confirm: ~117 KB per 1024 px WebP, ~0.6 GB for 5,055 (PNG at 4.38 MB per face would be ~22 GB and is not a catalogue format).
- One canonical text-generation resolver shared with typed input; check each result's raw synthesis against the independent reference within the frozen tolerances (max RGB diff 1, max sampled raw-float error 0.002) and the latent exactly; compressed images use export-quality rules, never byte parity.
- Reuse already valid matching assets; generate only missing/incompatible rows; resumable manifest so an interruption regenerates no valid row. Never attach a guessed latent to a historic JPEG.
- Record model/generation identity in the publication manifest. Data-shape bars come from names.spike.

## Out of scope
Publication (names.publish); typed-name re-check on the extracted engine (names.static-result).

## Notes
- Offline tool under the names pipeline; edits no shared bridge/runtime/worker file and stays unordered with respect to the shared-file chain. Uses the candidate's envelope helpers so names are not held behind the refactor.

title: Scan and classify identity references and integrations
description:
## Goal
Produce, by re-runnable read-only scripts, the classified list of every `check-face`/GitHub reference and every GitHub/hosting integration, plus the current identity of each repository and live host, so that the organization rename has a prepared edit list and a pre/post check, and the application inventory and domain handover start from verified facts. This is the first step of the organization rename (PLAN.md "Source and repository identity"). A repository, a branch and a live hostname are different identities; legacy production is still current production.

## Scope
- **Identity reader** `scripts/identity/read-identity.mjs` (read-only): for each identity reads repository ID, owner/name URL, default branch, archive state, relevant branches, live hostname, the currently served artifact/build identity read from the live bytes (build id, asset hashes via bundle fetch + sha256) and its source commit only if a deploy record attests it. Every value carries the verification timestamp and the exact command (`gh api repos/...`, `git ls-remote`, `curl -sI`, bundle fetch + sha256). One JSON line per value: identity, field, value, command, ISO timestamp, exit code. A second run diffs against the checked-in values and reports drift instead of overwriting.
- Identities to cover: legacy production web (`https://facemorph.me`, Vercel from classic `master` via `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`); legacy hosted API (`api.facemorph.me`, `checkface.facemorph.me`); legacy names site (`https://names.facemorph.me`, `facemorph-names`, repo 348379171); retained application `facemorph.me-classic` (295956585); the on-device candidate (branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, `src/Next/`, `https://next.facemorph.me`); the new monorepo `facemorph.me` (1413979666, `main`); the classic self-host distribution (`self-host/`, frontend pin `0abb215f27b16e17e3919cf78b616b6ae4998a5d`); archived `checkface` (185985766); `encoder4editing` (368806700); `models.facemorph.me` (second runtime origin: Worker over R2 bucket `facemorph-runtime-mirror`, source classic `hosting/next-mirror/`); the model-chunk, names-catalogue, preview/latent and diagnostics-collector hosts.
- Legacy production: attest what can be attested (Vercel deployment id, `master` head at check time); its exact deployed source revision is marked unknown unless a deployment record proves it. Never inferred from classic's default branch or the candidate checkout.
- next.facemorph.me identity is re-read from live bytes, not copied from the 11 October receipt (planning ref `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, recorded delivery `001ba853b277775a060030a3ab23a3900af28f16` build `next-04403766fff8630a`; since then `40c63a9` went live 2026-10-17 20:28:59 UTC, `bacd6e5` and `6107f80` landed 21 October; classic HEAD `6107f80` on 24 October).
- Re-check `users/facemorph-me` (404 on 11 and 15 October; not a reservation).
- **Integrations**: enumerate per repository (five repos) and per hosting target (next.facemorph.me, facemorph.me, names.facemorph.me, api/checkface hosts, `models.facemorph.me` with its service binding to the site Worker and its deploy-and-warm step in classic `next-site.yml`, model/catalogue/diagnostics Workers and R2): Cloudflare GitHub app/project connections, webhooks, Actions permissions/variables and secret *names*, OIDC subject restrictions, package/container owner paths, names hosting connection, the Vercel project (`vercel --prod` on every `master` push). Per integration: binding type (repo ID, owner/name, branch), publisher → target with trigger and credential names, status verified (command or console path, date) or needs-inspection (what is missing).
- **Org-link scan** `scripts/identity/scan-org-links.mjs`: search tracked code/config and maintained docs in all five repos plus the monorepo for `check-face`, github.com/raw/codeload/release URLs, `gh -R`/API paths and workflow `uses`. Classify each hit: active link to update (target URL); repository-name correction (wrong repo from the earlier rename); immutable provenance (add current-resolution mapping); frozen evidence (leave); archived (leave); native updater (retirement disposition, not migration); candidate source (edited by the candidate edit set). Known hits (classic unless noted): five `.git/config` origins; README/AGENTS/plan links; `hosting/next-static/promote.py` `REMOTE` (currently the wrong `check-face/facemorph.me`) and workflow-source validation; `self-host/Dockerfile` and `self-host/README.md`; `src/Config.fs` and `self-host/frontend-overlay/source/src/Config.fs`; `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` `ISSUE_REPO`; `src/Next/Product.fs` desktop documentation link; `desktop/scripts/prepare-release.mjs` updater endpoint and `desktop/tests/packaging.test.mjs`; `.github/workflows/research-built-ui-media-v1.yml` retained-run lookup; `self-host/frontend-overlay/source.json`, `self-host/REPOSITORY-PROVENANCE.md`; `src/explain.md`, API FAQ copy, repository homepage fields. Output: one JSON line per hit (repo, file, line, hit, class, disposition) plus per-class counts; an unclassified hit fails the run. The classification rules are checked in as the scripts' data and re-used by the rename acceptance.

## Out of scope
Any remote mutation; fixing or reconnecting integrations; making the link edits (rename and candidate edit set); the deep application inventory; DNS/credential inventory for retirement (inventory and domain handover); a committed prose identity map, receipts or a decision log.

## Notes
- Read-only. Plain names from the PLAN.md surface table, never "old app/current app/Next". Keep recorded receipts distinct from fresh observations. Secret and variable values are never written, only names.
- Candidate `ISSUE_REPO` keeps pointing at the candidate's actual repository until new-app handover; classic builds link to classic, the new app to the monorepo. One publisher per target is a later handover invariant: record current publishers precisely.
- GitHub does not redirect reusable action `uses` or Pages URLs on rename, and the old org name can be reclaimed.
- Dropped per 24 October "Bead size and ceremony": the separate committed identity map, the five receipts and the `docs/decisions/` log (operator decisions live once in the PLAN.md dated table; open questions Q1–Q4 and planner proposals P1–P4 live in PLAN.md "Remaining choices" and in their owning beads' acceptance). PLAN.md "Source and repository identity" (no separate committed map) supersedes the older surface-map text.
- Plan: #source-and-repository-identity, #source-names-live-surfaces-and-what-each-supplies, #organization-rename-first-known-reference-changes, #behavior-authorities-for-development.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `read-identity.mjs` tests make the real read-only `gh api`, `git ls-remote` and `curl -sI` calls (no recorded responses); a second run against the checked-in values reports zero drift or lists the drift.
- [x] Every identity value carries repo ID or hostname, branch(es), live artifact reference, verification timestamp and the command that produced it; the values validate against the live `gh api` reads they cite.
- [x] Legacy production's deployed revision is attested by a named record or explicitly marked unknown; next.facemorph.me's artifact identity is read from live bytes and its source commit attested or marked unknown.
- [x] `models.facemorph.me` and the model-chunk, catalogue, preview/latent and diagnostics hosts are covered (owner, source path, serving Worker/bucket).
- [x] Every integration is marked verified or needs-inspection; each publisher-to-target binding (Vercel/`master` → facemorph.me; classic `next-site.yml` deploy → next.facemorph.me and its `models.facemorph.me` deploy-and-warm step; names host; Workers) lists its trigger and credential names; a secret scan finds no secret values in checked-in data.
- [x] `scan-org-links.mjs` unit tests with a fixture tree cover each class and an unclassified hit failing the run; a run over the five repos plus the monorepo yields zero unclassified hits and prints per-class counts.
- [x] Classify the generic GitHub host E2E assertions without exempting repository links and pass the real organization-link scan and its test.

Real six-tree scan: 2295 hits, zero unclassified. node --test scripts/identity/scan-org-links.test.mjs: 5/5 pass (/tmp/fm-identity-tests15.log).

title: Carry over the site lane and the real-UI CPU e2e lane

## Goal

Move classic's ordinary candidate-push lane (`next-site.yml`: artifact, compiled-ui, qualify) and the exact-artifact real-UI CPU qualification (`next-e2e.yml`) into this repository on `apps/web` and package paths, without mocks or rebuilt copies, so every later lane tests the exact bytes the artifact job uploads. It uses the shared artifact lookup, path filters and request-interception helper delivered by `build.ci-shared`, and wires the retired-host scan into the artifact job.

## Scope

**Workflow `next-site.yml`**
- Keep classic's workflow name and job IDs (`artifact`, `qualify`, `compiled-ui`; `deploy` added later by the deploy workstream) so required-status names map one-to-one.
- Triggers: push to default and `candidate/*` branches, pull_request, workflow_dispatch. Path filters from `scripts/ci/path-filters.json`. Concurrency `next-site-${{ github.ref }}`, cancel-in-progress for test builds only; publication jobs keep their own non-cancelling group.

**`artifact` job** (classic `ubuntu-22.04`), over `deploy-next/` (control artifact first, Vite build later), every classic step present or replaced:
- static gates first: `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`; `npm ci`; `scripts/check-tests-listed.mjs`;
- the classic "shipping runtime, media, privacy and input regressions" `node --test` list (37 named files, each at its destination path);
- `check-progress-copy.mjs` unchanged against the retained bridge and `stage-labels.mjs`;
- `check-bridge-imports.mjs` and `verify-fable.mjs ProjectJson.fs.js` reported `not-applicable until the port` (Fable output is not in Git; classic's separate step scanned zero files), never passed; replaced later by strict TS at the typed facade and `project-json.test.ts`;
- `src/Next/geometry/verify.mjs`; `npm run build:next`; historic preview byte compare (`cmp .../preview/hello-1024.webp deploy-next/preview/hello-1024.webp`);
- `check-no-third-party.mjs deploy-next` and exact pinned/self-hosted runtime dependency checks;
- the retired-host scan from `domain.copy` (`api.facemorph.me`, `checkface.facemorph.me`, `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, with its allowed shared hosts) over `deploy-next/`: while `deploy-next/` is the pinned control it runs report-only and lists the expected candidate hits (the control is classic's artifact); from the first monorepo Vite build in `deploy-next/` it is blocking, so a production build that links a retired host or the candidate branch fails CI (PLAN.md "Acceptance receipts", domain handover acceptance). One JSON line per hit plus a total in the job summary;
- `next-site-SHA256SUMS` + `next-site-source.txt` (source repo ID, run, commit) uploaded as `next-site-<sha>`, 14-day retention.
- Pass: every step exits 0; zero third-party runtime references; the SHA256SUMS digest equals the identity-hashing artifact digest.

**`compiled-ui` job** (`ubuntu-24.04`, `needs: artifact`): fetch `next-site-<sha>` via `fetch-artifact` and `sha256sum -c next-site-SHA256SUMS`; `python3 -m compileall` over retained Python scripts; WebGPU bundle contract gate (`webgpu_contract_test.py` at its destination path); actual artifact in Chromium via `browser-harness==0.1.8` with request interception; evidence artifact `next-artifact-ui-evidence`. **`qualify` caller and `next-e2e.yml`**

The shared artifact lookup, path filters and interception helper (`build.ci-shared`); the `deploy` job (deploy workstream); changing asserted journeys beyond path/adaptor updates; canonical-artifact fan-out (later points this lookup at canonical bytes); operated-input harness and journey assertions (integrated verification); publishing anything.

title: Spike: observe Elmish messages in the control bundle, or fall back to DOM/state snapshots
description:
## Background
Reducer-level goldens assume the minified control bundle exposes its Elmish message stream (`Msg` cases such as `Edit`, `Mode`, `RunFace`, `Progressed`, `Completed`, `CropAccept`, `DownloadsChanged`, `ChooseName` in `Product.fs` lines ~263-279 at the pinned commit). Without .NET, goldens can only come from driving the control artifact in a headless browser (with `project-v1.fixture.json`).

## Why
Decides the oracle granularity for the controller port: reducer transitions (fine) or journey-step DOM/state snapshots (coarser but observable).

## Scope
- Try, for one flow (e.g. type a word -> Generate -> Completed on CPU), to observe messages and model states through the control bundle: a development hook, the bridge's events (`subscribe` progress, `facemorph-report-status`), or DOM state transitions.
- If it works, write the recorder for reducer transitions (message, prior state digest, next state) used by the controller leaves.
- If not, write the Playwright recorder for DOM and state snapshots at journey-step level, which the reducers are then tested against.
- Record which was used, why, and the recorder's limits as a dated entry in `docs/decisions/`.

## Out of scope
Recording every flow (done per controller leaf and in the freeze). Rebuilding the control with hooks (forbidden: no F# build).

## Considerations
The spike is expected to be small (the plan says a few hours) but has no time box. Both outcomes are acceptable; what is not acceptable is an unrecorded choice. Recorder output must exclude photos, latents and typed inputs from anything retained outside the test run.

## Recorder output contract (polish r1)
Whichever oracle is chosen, the recorder writes `apps/web/test/goldens/control/<flow-row-id>/<step>.json` and an index `goldens.json` with: control `deploy-next/` SHA-256, recorder command and version, browser and viewport, runtime/model identities used, and per step the input action (operated pointer/touch coordinates or keyboard), the observed message (if reducer-level) or DOM/state snapshot (class list, text, ARIA state, focused element), the freeze class placeholder (filled by `migration.flow-matrix-drive`), and a privacy flag confirming no photo bytes, latents or typed inputs are retained beyond the test run (typed inputs in fixtures are synthetic words/seeds only). Every controller and rendering leaf consumes this format.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Decision entry in `docs/decisions/` names the oracle (reducer transitions or DOM/state snapshots), the recorder command and its blind spots.
- [ ] Recorder produces a golden file for the sample flow from the verified control artifact (digest re-checked first).
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, and the log is retained as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics). Network claims are asserted from the log, never from screenshots.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/migration/golden-spike.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes: Plan anchor: PLAN.md#application-migration (Golden capture, with a stated fallback).

title: Grade every frozen flow-matrix row and candidate-defect repair row
description:
## Background
The flow-matrix freeze (`ws:migration.freeze`) classifies each journey row of the plan's "UI flow matrix and open
journey contracts" table: **parity-graded** (exact against the pinned control artifact), **specification-graded**
(a planned or settled change, graded against the plan's contract) or **repair** (a candidate defect, graded against
the plan's specification and never frozen as parity). Migration's parity milestone covers the unchanged port; this
bead grades the final integrated app. It is the collation leaf: other verify leaves run the cases and this bead
assigns every row and every candidate defect a grade with evidence.

## Why
The join may only claim journeys whose row passed on the named artifact. Without one table that lists every row and
defect, uncovered journeys hide between leaves.

## Scope
- Build the graded matrix from the leaves' case manifests (step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` mapped to row IDs
  and defect numbers, see the harness). Each row: row ID, class (as frozen), grade, evidence links (event log,
  screenshots, receipt), artifact digest, platform/provider cells exercised, cells untested.
- Grades use exactly the join's closed outcome set (`ws:verify.join` rule 3), with the same spelling: `passed`,
  `failed`, `untested`, `unsupported`, `inconclusive`, `deferred` (out of release scope by operator decision),
  `not-applicable-by-decision` (a planner proposal the operator vetoed; link the decision entry), and
  `measured, no threshold`. Only `passed` is claimable. A row with any required cell untested is not `passed`.
- Rows whose evidence ran on another digest are `untested` for this artifact.
- Every intentional difference from the baseline is traced to the plan (drift ledger or behaviour-authority table).
- Open questions from the 18 October audit (old text links, autoplay, plain blend, cropper extras) keep candidate
  behaviour until answered; grade against whatever `docs/decisions/` says at grading time.

### Row coverage (row IDs follow the plan table order; class in brackets is the expected freeze class, the freeze decides)

After the default WebP/PNG/MP4 paths work, explore extra image and video exports for a specific goal (a smaller shareable file, a lossless still for later editing, a format a recipient asked for) in a compact **More export options** disclosure inside the result's existing action area, shown only when qualified options exist. Kept so the proposal is not lost, without making every codec a release blocker.

## Scope
- JPEG is today only a scrub/display derivative; downloadable JPEG, GIF, animated WebP, WebM or other codecs are proposed capabilities, not current ones.
- For each proposed format/preset record actual MIME/container/codec, quality/resolution/frame order, destination, browser encoder/decoder/share support, metadata carrier and reader round-trip, memory/asset/time costs and evidence per retained matrix cell.
- Expose only qualified options per browser; explain an unavailable requested format in the existing action/help area; keep the prepared default usable.
- Reuse pixels/frames without new inference; each format has its own readiness, Cancel/Retry, filename/extension (export identity rules) and user-gesture share; extra codec assets go through the existing cost/consent boundary.
- Every offered file keeps recovery metadata; a "small/social" preset cannot silently remove editable data.
- A format is labelled supported only when export plus validated metadata-reader round-trip (and still-image UI reopening) works.

## Out of scope
A mandatory export wizard, a page-wide toolbar, long disabled-format lists, a quality slider. New output codecs as a prerequisite for release or retirement.

## Notes
- Deferred: start only when explicitly picked up.
- Needs `face.export` (edge added in the 24 October final pass): the disclosure lives in that row's result action area.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #file-sharing-and-export-direction, ownership tie-break row "goal-based formats", #remaining-choices-completion-and-cutover-authority.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] For each shipped option: export plus metadata-reader round-trip and still-image reopen evidence, per-cell outcomes in the release summary, and consent for any extra asset; unqualified options are not shown.
- [ ] Format switch to an extra option reuses existing pixels/frames (inference spy 0) and keeps the default prepared file usable.
- [ ] Operated check of the More export options disclosure and each option: real pointer/touch at the visible position with `elementFromPoint` confirming the control; by-name/role clicks only for setup; options at 0 (disclosure hidden), 1, 2, 3 and all; filename input empty, very long and pasted; 390 px and 1,280 px screenshots per case.

title: Reduce classic to the distribution, add the pointer, re-run acceptance
description:
## Goal
Reach the operator's end state for `facemorph.me-classic`: a very clean repository serving the self-host Docker distribution plus its Git history. Remove everything else from the default branch, add a forward pointer to this repository, and prove by the README-executed clean-clone acceptance that the cleanup did not break the distribution. Terminal for the wind-down workstream; runs as stage commits, each gated by its CI precondition check (`winddown.publishers`), without approval steps.

## Scope
- **Allowed end-state tree**: `self-host/`, its README, whatever the fresh-clone quickstart proves it needs, and the rot-check/GPU workflows. Nothing else: no candidate source, experiments or research tooling, hosting or staging scripts, desktop/native packages, publisher workflows. The default branch is the D4 distribution branch, so most of this holds by construction.
- **Clean-tree stage** preconditions: research tree verified byte-identical in the monorepo (digest list); experiment-ledger prefix hash recorded; protected input paths (`inventory/protected-paths.json`) moved or kept; hosting sources still deployed from classic (e.g. `hosting/next-mirror/`, `hosting/next-cloudflare/`) have a monorepo home that deploys them. Then remove remaining non-distribution paths on the default branch in one commit; uncommitted paths and paths other sessions are editing are skipped and reported, never overwritten. Reversal: revert the commit.
- **Forward-pointer stage**: one short README section with the monorepo URL under the final org (new development, autoresearch and the on-device app live there); the quickstart block stays byte-identical so the harness still extracts it; the README stays the frozen self-host doc.
- **Final acceptance stage**: run the README harness verbatim on the GPU worker on the cleaned tree; restore any path it proves necessary (revert specific removals; restoring a path is not a feature change) and re-run until it passes. Final checks: tree lists only distribution, README and rot-check workflows; research tree byte-identical in the monorepo; ref snapshot shows no deleted branch or tag and no rewritten history.
- Each stage is a commit gated by its CI precondition; a failed precondition means no change and a reported `not run`.

## Out of scope
History rewrite; deleting branches, tags or the repository; feature changes to the distribution; deleting personal production records.

## Notes
- Newer PLAN.md "Acceptance receipts" (each stage a commit gated by its CI precondition) wins over the older per-stage receipt wording in "Classic wind-down": no receipt files; each stage commit and its CI run are the evidence (no stage runner or per-stage reports; sweep, 24 October).
- Plan: #classic-wind-down, #end-state-of-the-repositories, #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clean-tree stage: CI preconditions green on the stage commit; tree listing after the commit matches the allowed set (plus restored needs); ref snapshot identical before/after except the default branch advancing; skipped uncommitted paths reported.
- [ ] Forward pointer present; quickstart block byte-identical to before (diff check in CI).
- [ ] Verbatim harness run on the cleaned tree passes on the GPU worker (needed paths restored).
- [ ] Final checks pass: only distribution, README and rot-check workflows on the default branch; research tree byte-identical in the monorepo (digest compare); Git history unchanged; no branch or tag deleted.

title: Convert official FFHQ in the container with independent numerical parity
description:
## Background
The product's FFHQ generator (mapping + synthesis, direct-WebGPU coefficients from `manifest.webgl` that must be preserved) and the 108-shard FP32 e4e encoder were produced by the classic export scripts. Hosted artifacts have known digests in the runtime manifests.

Raw-synthesis tolerances, frozen and stated concretely (never widened, never a precision change, never replaced by a visual spot-check): the product synthesis canaries require **maximum RGB difference 1 on the 0-255 scale** and **maximum sampled raw-float error 0.002** (candidate `src/Next/browser/canary-qualification.mjs`: `maxRgb <= 1 && maxFloat <= .002`, alpha channel excluded); the applicable research/reference suites keep their own frozen coverage and tolerances; the separate **e4e latent tolerance is maximum absolute error 0.0001** (`photo-runtime/README.md`, `encoder-stream/qualification/report.json`). The comparison is the network's raw output before compression against the independent qualified reference for the same model, latent, noise, preprocessing and workload, including across CPU/WebGPU routes. Other models need their own independent reference and declared small tolerance; they never inherit FFHQ values. Encoded image bytes are never a correctness gate.

## Why
Official FFHQ is the first supported conversion; the container must reproduce provider artifacts the manager/engine accept.

## Scope
- Convert official NVlabs FFHQ (acquired per documented terms) and the e4e encoder in the container; produce chunks, descriptor, manifests and a parity report.
- Compare outputs with the currently hosted artifacts: identical digests where deterministic, otherwise numerical parity against the independent PyTorch reference within the frozen tolerances (synthesis canaries RGB <= 1/255, sampled raw float <= 0.002; research suites' own; e4e W+ <= 0.0001).
- Load check: converted artifacts run in the candidate runtime harness (component load); the manager/engine journey joins integrated verification.

## Out of scope
Hosting/publishing (model hosting). Changing the production artifacts (only if a later decision adopts the converted set).

## Considerations
- Preserve descriptor/content identities; WebGL execution removal does not delete shared coefficient assets.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Parity report passes the stated tolerances; nondeterministic fields listed.
- [ ] Component load in the runtime harness passes on CPU.
- [ ] Runs on a worker under the device lease; Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Correct the failure-toast consent labels and keep one non-covering prompt at a time
description:
## Background
Defect 12 (source `Product.fs:738`): the failure toast's "Send report" calls `setDebug(true, "toast")`, turning
standing reporting on for good, while the error box's "Send this report" sends once. Defect 16 (operated): the first
visit stacks two bottom toasts; at 1,280x800 the first covers Create morph (element at its centre is the toast) and on a
phone it fills a third of the screen.

## Why
One-shot must stay one-shot; prompts must not cover actions.

## Scope
- Keep one contextual report toast while standing reporting is Off. **Send this report** sends only the owning failed
  attempt's bounded safe records, never enables standing reporting or overrides a stored refusal.
- Any ongoing-consent action is labelled **Turn on debug reporting** and explains future sending.
- No opt-in request while On; reporting never blocks Retry; inline owning-error access without duplicate prompts or focus
  stealing; withdrawal via the disclosure at any time.
- At most one prompt visible at a time and no prompt covers an action (hit-test at action centres).

## Out of scope
Disclosure itself.

## Considerations
Scoped reporting must exclude unrelated staged slot records.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits a shared file, so it follows the morph pipeline.** A one-shot **Send this report** must carry the owning failed attempt's reference so unrelated staged slot records are excluded. The bridge's `sendReportOnce()` takes no attempt argument and run scoping sits in its `photoStage`/`closePhotoRun`, so this bead changes `product-bridge.mjs` (that export's signature and run scoping) as well as `reporting.mjs` and the toast UI. Edge `fm-b7mt -> fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph) added in polish r2; it sits in the "diagnostics edits" position after the morph pipeline, beside `diag.typed-failure-causes` (fm-imm9) and `diag.collector-rebinding` (fm-ea3n).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Operated-UI rule: each acceptance step acts with real pointer input (touch tap at phone widths) at the control's visible position, asserts `document.elementFromPoint` at that point returns the control (or a descendant) and that the point lies inside the region a person would look in (named per control below); by-name/by-role clicks are used only to set up state, never as the acceptance step.
- [ ] Every case is checked at a phone width (390 px) and a desktop width (1,280 px) with one screenshot per case kept as evidence.
- [ ] Operated Send this report: one upload with only the owning attempt's records; stored preference unchanged (still Off/refusal).
- [ ] Operated Turn on debug reporting: standing On; later withdrawal via the footer link works.
- [ ] While On: no toast offers opt-in.
- [ ] First visit at 1,280x800 and 390x844: at most one prompt; `elementFromPoint` at Create Morph and each face action centre returns the action, not a prompt.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic run in CI (`npm test` workspace target) and pass.
- [ ] Each end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Every network claim is asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Regions: the toast sits at the bottom edge and overlaps no action (checked at Create Morph and every face action centre at 1, 2, 3 and 8 faces); the error box's **Send this report** sits inline in the owning tile status or Morph status.

title: Legacy crop-dialog reference data and cropper spike
description:
## Goal
Pin down, element by element, what the locked crop references and the classic `EncodeImageDialog.fs` show, and choose the cropper basis (`react-advanced-cropper` 0.20.1 or our own component) by a spike judged against `crop 2.png`. The source step, confirmation modal, crop editor and alignment-failure layout are all built and checked against this bead's geometry JSON and colour table (read by the face.encode and face.crop-editor tests), so it lands first. The operator asked (16 October) for a crop flow very similar to the old hosted UI. There is no separate design-review document: the many-face presentation, Remove placement, result area and Morph slot are designed and accepted in their own implementing beads against the plan's bars.

## Scope
- **Locked images** in `../reference-locks/2026-10-11-original-plan-and-images/images/` (verify against that bundle's `SHA256SUMS` first; hashes also in PLAN.md#supplied-ui-references: `crop image.png` `dc2b0708…a280`, `crop 2.png` `753f4ad6…6c1`, `failed to align.png` `074096a9…255b`, `recovered image.png` `d67fdf00…0b62`). Content:
  - `crop image.png` (~395 x 520) "Encode an image": dark grey modal over a dimmed page; white title top left; FaceMorph line-drawn logo top right; square proposed-crop preview centred under the title (face aligned in it); **ADJUST CROP** text button (uppercase, no fill) centred below; **CANCEL** bottom left (light grey fill, dark text); **OK** bottom right (indigo fill, white text). No other copy.
  - `crop 2.png` (~623 x 885) "Crop your image": same chrome; source photo letterboxed in a wide frame (black band); square stencil, thin light outline, **eight white square handles** (corners and edge midpoints); outside not darkened; inside a **translucent light oval face guide** with **two dark round eye markers** on a horizontal line in its upper half. Below, centred: a **crop-rotate icon** and degree readout **"0°"**; a **full-width slider** (indigo track, round thumb centred at 0°). Copy, left aligned: bold **"Cropping is generally not necessary, as faces are usually auto detected."**, then "Try to leave a bit above the top of the head and below the chin." and "Lining up the eyes is most important." Footer: **CANCEL** left (light grey), **USE CROP** right (indigo).
  - `failed to align.png` (~615 x 784) "Upload an image": same chrome; full uploaded image as preview (not a square crop); **red/pink filled CROP** button centred under it; red line **"Unable to auto align face."**; white guidance "When the face isn't aligned you may get strange results. Try a different image or manually crop it. Make sure the entire face is in frame and looking towards to camera." (sic); footer CANCEL left, OK right (indigo).
  - `recovered image.png`: historical two-face page with the controls the plan removes (duplicate filename caption "daniel image.jpeg", **CROP PHOTO** after encoding, **Hold to compare**).
  - Historical `src/EncodeImageDialog.fs` (classic history): `react-advanced-cropper` fixed-aspect stencil, a **90° rotate button** plus fine-rotation slider, a **file chooser** and an **"Or paste image here"** field inside the dialog; server detection and encoding before confirmation.
- **Element list** as a typed constant in `apps/web/src/photo/legacy-dialog-reference.ts` (no separate inventory document; face.encode and face.crop-editor tests iterate it): one entry per visual element, copy string, control, interaction (choose file, paste, drag stencil, resize from each of eight handles, rotate 90°, fine-rotate, readout update, Cancel, OK/Use Crop, CROP from failure) and state (source empty, proposal, editor, failure), each marked **reproduce** or **deliberate difference** with reason and owning bead.
- **Deliberate differences**, each with its plan anchor: confirm (proposal -> ADJUST CROP -> OK) **before** encoding; on-device detection replaces server detection, guidance copy stays; failure title becomes **"Encode an image"** and red **CROP** becomes **ADJUST CROP** (same red fill, centred); the "towards to camera" typo is corrected to "towards the camera" by default (choice stated); one short explanation that encoding recreates the face and may change details (confirmation modal); Prepare encoder beside Choose image only when eligible required assets are missing.
- **Geometry** `docs/design/legacy-encode-dialog-geometry.json` (boxes as fractions of modal width, comparable at 390 and 1,280 px) plus the measuring script: modal width/padding, title baseline, logo box, preview square size/offset, ADJUST CROP box, CANCEL/OK/USE CROP/CROP boxes, handle size, stencil outline width, oval guide box relative to stencil, eye-marker diameter/spacing, rotate icon and readout boxes, slider track/thumb, copy block.
- **Colour table** sampled from the PNGs (modal background, title text, CANCEL fill/text, OK/USE CROP fill, CROP fill, failure red, slider track/thumb, handle fill, oval opacity) with contrast ratios; light-theme equivalents with every text pair >= 4.5:1. Opaque light-theme variants for confirmation, editor and failure states.
- **Open operator question** (wheel/pinch zoom, crop square past the photo edge, pre-upload "look straight forward" tip): not built until answered; default is candidate behaviour. The spike states whether each basis could add these later.
- **Cropper spike.** Two throwaway prototypes in a scratch workspace package (not shipped): `react-advanced-cropper` 0.20.1 (React >= 16.8) and hand-written. Each reproduces the `crop 2.png` square stencil with 8 handles, oval guide with 2 eye markers, crop-rotate button (90° per press) and full-width fine-rotation slider with live degree readout. Compare touch (drag, resize from each handle, rotate at phone width), rotation and coordinates (output rectangle/rotation in source-pixel coordinates after EXIF orientation, round-tripping exactly into the contracts milestone 1 confirmed-crop preprocessing policy), keyboard operability, bundle size, licence, maintenance (release cadence, open issues, React support). The chosen basis, with measurements and deviations from the geometry, is stated in the reference module's header comment and the merge commit, which face.crop-editor reads; the prototypes are deleted after the choice. The candidate's fixed-square pan/zoom DOM (drag, zoom 1-8, 90° rotate, no guide) is not a substitute for the locked design.

## Out of scope
Building the production crop components; behaviour implementation; names-picker visuals.

- Do not edit the locked bundle or commit its personal-photo pixels: commit measurements, crops of non-face chrome only if needed, and hashes.
- No time box and no approval step (operator, 17 October): the comparison decides. The design-review deliverable of the old item is dropped by the consolidated row; its state list (tile states, source step, batch selection with ordered badges, mixed candidates, many-face presentation at 1/2/3/4/8/30/64/150 faces (no fixed count; virtualised past about 100), Remove, Undo, Start over, result area, Morph slot) is covered by face.tiles, face.encode, face.batch, face.mixed-batch, face.many, face.export and face.morph-output.

- Anchors: PLAN.md#crop-fidelity-and-export-flow-clarification, #locked-original-requirements-and-images, #supplied-ui-references, #face-controls-and-modals.
