title: Define the e2e event-log schema, TS and Python writers, host classes, privacy filter, validator and network primitives
description:
## Background

End-to-end evidence convention (PLAN.md, 17 October): every end-to-end script emits a structured
event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform and provider, network requests by host
class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots are kept on failure; the log is retained as a
CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics; claims such as "no model network before approval"
and "no speculative network" are asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.

Split out of `build.docs-decisions-receipts` (fm-ucl) in polish round 2 so the log format can be
reviewed on its own. This leaf is the language-neutral core with no browser dependency; browser
capture is `build.event-log-capture`.

## Why

One schema, one validator and one set of network primitives keep logs comparable across CI lanes,
research drivers and integrated verification, and make every network claim a query over a log.

## Ordering

Needs only `ws:identity`, like fm-ucl. Dependency-free: erasable-syntax-only TypeScript run by Node 24
type stripping, and Python 3 standard library only. Joins `typecheck`/`npm test` when
`build.workspaces-ts` lands.

## Scope

- `docs/schemas/e2e-event-log.v1.schema.json`. JSON Lines, one event per line. First line a `run`
  header: `schema: e2e-event-log/v1`, run ID, script name + version, source commit, artifact digest,
  platform, provider requested, worker/runner, start time, host-class map version.
- Each event: `step_id`, `ts` (ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds), `artifact_digest`, `platform`,
  `provider` (actual where known), `kind` (`step-start` | `step-end` | `request` | `console` |
  `assert` | `screenshot` | `note`), `outcome` (`pass` | `fail` | `skip` | `error` on step-end and
  assert), request fields (`host_class`, `method`, `url_redacted`, `status`, `bytes_in`, `bytes_out`,
  `from_cache`, `initiator` page/worker/service-worker), console fields (`level`, `message_class`,
  redacted-text hash). Final `summary` line: per-host-class request counts and bytes, console error
  count, step outcomes, overall outcome.
- `step_id` format: `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` (for example
  `verify.flows-functional/R08/pick-name`), characters `[a-z0-9._:/-]`, unique within a run. This is
  the field `verify.harness` case manifests map to flow-matrix rows and defect numbers. Short
  dotted IDs used by carried-over lanes are written as `<lane key>/<job>/<step>`.
- Host classes: `app` (artifact origin), `model-host` (model/runtime origins including
  `models.facemorph.me`), `names-host`, `collector` (diagnostics endpoint), `third-party` (anything
  else), `local` (data:/blob:). Default map in versioned `scripts/evidence/host-classes.json` keyed by
  origin. The writer accepts an injected map (`createEventLog({hostClasses})`) for preview/staging
  origins and for the app's own map supplied by `verify.harness`; the header records the map digest.
- Privacy filter (same classes as diagnostics filtering), applied in the writer before anything is
  written: never photos or pixels, latents, typed words/names, file names, raw error strings or query
  strings; URLs keep origin + path template only; console text is reduced to a class plus a hash.
- Writers: `scripts/evidence/event-log.ts` `createEventLog({script, artifactDigest, platform,
  provider, out, hostClasses})` returning `step(id, fn)`, `request(...)`, `console(...)`,
  `assert(...)`, `screenshot(...)`, `close()`; `scripts/evidence/event_log.py` with the same API.
- Network primitives used by every network claim, same names in TS and Python:
  `requestsIn(log, {hostClass, fromStep, toStep})`, `assertNoRequests(log, hostClass, window)`,
  `assertOrder(log, before, after)`, `bytesBy(log, hostClass)`.
- `scripts/check-event-log.ts <file>`: validates any log regardless of producer: schema, monotonic
  timestamps, unique step IDs matching the format, every line carries the header's artifact digest,
  summary consistent with lines, no filtered value class present. Prints one JSON verdict line.

## Out of scope

Browser hooks and the CI upload convention (`build.event-log-capture`). Receipts (fm-ucl). Journey
assertions and operated input (`verify.harness`).

## Considerations

- No `ajv`: the validator is hand-written; the schema file is kept equal to it by a test.
- A log that cannot prove a network claim (missing window, missing requests from a worker) fails the
  claim; it never passes by absence of data.

title: Create the check-migration map with the shared-file conflict list
description:
## Background

The map lives beside the inventory (`docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/inventory.md`) at `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/check-migration-map.md`. Known seams: `check-next-artifact.sh` assumes the
provider lives in `.next-advanced`, includes WebGL and exposes a separate Browse names button;
`check-progress-copy.mjs` asserts frame-only morph copy and old bridge source patterns; photo/crop
tests read `Product.fs`; bridge-import checks inspect generated `.fs.js`; Fable project qualification
invokes `ProjectJson.fs.js`. Without .NET, golden project JSON and state transitions come from driving
the control artifact headlessly with `project-v1.fixture.json`. Deliberate release changes to map
without deleting coverage: `browser/runtime.test.mjs` GPU-to-CPU retry, `browser/route-priors.test.mjs`
CPU ordering, mobile-runtime/resource checks.

## Why

Ensures no protected behaviour loses coverage through an unexplained test removal and serialises shared-file edits.

## Scope

- One row per check: protected behaviour, source/layout assumptions, destination invocation, the declared
  plan change that replaces any obsolete expectation, and the owning workstream/revision for that change.
- Stale-harness entries: `check-next-artifact.sh` repair lands with provider simplification (WebGL,
  `.next-advanced`) and face controls (Browse Names moved into the face menu); `check-progress-copy.mjs`
  repair lands with the whole-action progress change; `next-matrix.mjs` repair is its own item now.
- Inherited independent-encode image-hash or decoded-lossy equality assertions mapped to the synthesis/
  export rules; keep prepared-file reuse, corruption checks and raw numerical comparisons.
- Source-language assertions → equivalent TS/schema/operation/built-product checks; numerical,
  acquisition, cleanup, resource and export-integrity coverage survives.
- Native packaging/parity checks marked historical or retired, never substituted for browser checks.
- Shared-file conflict list: `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs`, `browser/ort-worker.mjs`
  and ported UI sources, with the mandatory order: provider simplification → typed facade → compute
  extraction → confirmed-crop fix → morph pipeline → static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics
  reporting rebinding. Each workstream adds files it edits.
- A check that verifies the map: every test/check file in the tree appears in the map (CI fails otherwise).

## Stale-harness rows and the beads that carry each repair

The map records each repair; the repair itself lands in the owning bead's revision, and that bead's
acceptance must cite the map row. Rows to create now:

| Check | Stale assumption | Repair lands in | Expected destination behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scripts/check-next-artifact.sh` | provider lives in `.next-advanced` and offers WebGL | `provider.webgl-removal` (fm-ybbi), shared-file order step 1 | no WebGL route; provider selector location as built; coefficient asset `manifest.webgl` still present for direct WebGPU |
| `scripts/check-next-artifact.sh` | separate Browse names button on the field | `face.browse-names-entry` (fm-uq8p) | Browse Names reachable from each face's burger menu, no field adornment |
| `scripts/check-progress-copy.mjs` (reads `product-bridge.mjs` and `stage-labels.mjs`, JS only, not F#) | none until whole-action progress lands | not repaired by the controller port: keeps running unchanged against the retained bridge and labels; its paths move with the TS sources only when `migration.ren-*` replaces those files, with identical expectations | same copy expectations, re-pointed paths recorded in this row |
| `scripts/check-progress-copy.mjs` | frame-only morph copy, per-stage resets | `opctl.progress` (fm-vbj7) with `face.morph-controls-output` (fm-j4i8) rendering | one monotonic whole-action bar with secondary frame counter |
| `scripts/next-matrix.mjs` | bulk Generate / post-result Crop controls; saved-result `photoE4e` fixture | `build.next-matrix-repair` (fm-so0) | declared controls; independent metadata-free photo with encoder events |
| `src/Next/crop-queue.test.mjs` (3 tests read `Product.fs`) | F# source text | `migration.ctl-photo` (fm-p2le), retired in `migration.ctl-golden-replay` (fm-7wsd) | `crop.test.ts` cases: crop queue ordering and exits |
| `src/Next/photo-selection.test.mjs` case "the multiple-faces sentence is shared" (reads `Product.fs`) | F# source text | `migration.ctl-photo` (fm-p2le) | `photo.test.ts` import check of the single shared constant; the file's other cases read JS and keep running |
| `scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs` (walks generated `.fs.js`) | Fable output, which is not in Git (classic `.gitignore` excludes `*.fs.js`) | until the port: recorded `not-applicable until the port`, never passed; replaced by strict TypeScript import resolution at `migration.facade-types` (fm-pth3), which swaps `./ProjectJson.fs.js` and empties the unresolved-import list | `tsc --noEmit` over the facade plus `unresolved-imports.mjs` reporting zero entries. Note: classic's separate CI step runs before `build:next` and scans zero files (vacuous); the real classic check ran inside `build-next.cjs` between Fable and webpack |
| `src/Next/verify-fable.mjs ProjectJson.fs.js` | Fable output | `migration.ctl-projectjson` (fm-dtmm): its acceptance ports every `verify-fable.mjs` assertion | `project-json.test.ts` round-trip goldens from driving the control with `project-v1.fixture.json`; recorded `not-applicable until the port` before that |
| `scripts/next-matrix.mjs` project skip (~lines 164-169, reads `Product.fs`) | F# source text | `build.next-matrix-repair` (fm-so0) with the TS flag from `migration.ctl-projectjson` | matrix step reads the TS flag; until then the project stage reports `incomplete-not-shipped` |
| other `next-site.yml` candidate tests (`scheduler`, `estimate`, `last-result`, `photo-selection` other cases, `fresh-review`, `route-choice`, `testing-link`, `logging`, `route-report`, `reporting`, `stage-labels`) | none (read JS) | no repair; stay listed in `check-tests-listed.mjs` | unchanged |
| `browser/runtime.test.mjs` GPU→CPU retry, `browser/route-priors.test.mjs` CPU ordering | WebGL in the route set | `provider.webgl-removal` | same coverage without WebGL |
| `desktop/scripts/verify-web-artifact.py` invoked by browser/e2e workflows | lives under native `desktop/` | `provider.native-retirement` (fm-be10) | re-homed web-artifact verifier, same checks |

## Disabled-test and hash-assertion guards (polish r2)

- `scripts/check-no-disabled-tests.mjs`: fails on `.skip`, `.only`, `test.todo`, `xit`, `describe.skip`,
  `@pytest.mark.skip`/`skipif` without a reason string, `unittest.skip`, a workflow step with
  `if: false`, or a test step with `continue-on-error: true`, unless the map has a row for that
  location giving reason, owner bead and removal condition. This enforces "no blanket disabled suite".
- Inherited independent-encode image-hash or decoded-lossy equality assertions: each gets a map row
  naming its replacement (raw numerical tolerance from `contracts.numerics-export-rules`,
  prepared-file reuse, or corruption check). `scripts/check-image-hash-asserts.mjs` greps maintained
  tests for SHA-256/hash comparisons over encoded image or video outputs and fails on any not listed.

## Classic workflow disposition

The map also lists every classic workflow and its destination (see `build.required-status-inventory` for
the status bindings): `next-site.yml`, `next-e2e.yml`, `next-matrix.yml`, `mobile-browser.yml`,
`next-gpu-lane.yml` (this workstream); research workflows (`research.workflows-path-filters`);
`name-catalogue.yml` (`names.publish-pipeline`); `self-host-build.yml` (stays in classic);
`deploy.yml` (historical); `desktop-*.yml` (retired, shared browser checks re-homed).

## Out of scope

Performing the provider/UI-owned repairs (they land in those revisions).

## Considerations

No blanket disabled suite. Immutable historical scripts stay in classic history; maintained destination checks are versioned separately.

A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] The stale-harness table names, for `check-next-artifact.sh` (fm-ybbi, fm-uq8p), `check-progress-copy.mjs` (fm-7wsd, fm-vbj7/fm-j4i8), `next-matrix.mjs` (fm-so0), the F#-source checks and `verify-web-artifact.py` (fm-be10), the owning bead and expected destination behaviour.
- [ ] Unit tests for the map-completeness check: an unlisted test file fails it, a listed-but-deleted file fails it, a row missing a column fails it; tests run in the workspace test command.
- [ ] Every classic workflow file at the import revision has a disposition row.
- [ ] The F#-reading rows are one per check, matching the retired-check table in `migration.ctl-golden-replay` (fm-7wsd): `crop-queue.test.mjs` and the `photo-selection.test.mjs` shared-sentence case (fm-p2le), `check-bridge-imports.mjs` (fm-pth3; recorded not-applicable until the port, with the note that classic's separate CI step is vacuous), `verify-fable.mjs` (fm-dtmm acceptance), the `next-matrix.mjs` project skip (fm-so0); `check-progress-copy.mjs` is recorded as JS-reading and unchanged until `opctl.progress`. A unit test asserts each of these check paths has exactly one map row carrying an owner bead id and a destination invocation, and fails if one is missing.

title: Record one nightly ORT run in the bleeding-edge lane
description:
## Background

Nightly builds run only in the qualified bleeding-edge lane, never shipped.

## Why

One recorded data point on the upcoming release, with exact version and hash.

## Scope

- One run of numerics and the paired desktop screen with the nightly; exact version and integrity hash; artifact copied to durable storage.

## Out of scope

Shipping or adopting the nightly.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.

title: Keep MP4 project metadata, internal reader and codec fallback correct
description:
## Background
Morph MP4 files embed the ordered controls and morph settings needed to reconstruct the project (candidate MP4 project metadata and readers named in the behaviour-authority table). External MP4 project-open UI is deferred; MP4 format help says "Video; reopening this file as a project is not available in this release." The accepted 512 x 512 path remains available and the actual resolution is shown with the result.

## Why
Every offered file must embed recoverable data; MP4 export/internal metadata round-trip and retained session playback remain required.

## Scope
- MP4 project metadata writer/reader as computational helpers with schema/version validation (dynamic-shape aware).
- Codec fallback: WebCodecs probes 1024 then 512, FFmpeg 512 fallback; actual resolution reported with the file.
- Internal reader validation of produced files; corruption behaviour documented.
- Unit and browser tests: round-trip ordered controls/settings, fallback resolution reported, truncated file rejected.

## Out of scope
MP4-availability probe at Morph accept and renderMorph orchestration (morph pipeline). App-visible MP4 import (deferred).

## Considerations
- The FFmpeg fallback codec download (about 32 MB) joins the acquisition consent (owned by acquisition consent); this item only keeps the fallback correct.

## Settings and disclosure (polish r1)
MP4 encoder settings come from the `export-policy` module (media.split) and must stay identical to the candidate (codec `avc1.42002A`, WebCodecs 1024 then 512, FFmpeg 512, bitrate formula, framerate = fps). The produced file result carries `{width, height, route: 'webcodecs'|'ffmpeg', reason}` so the app can disclose the actual resolution beside the result and, when known earlier, before Morph (morph.mp4-probe).

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.

- [ ] Produced file results report `{width, height, route, reason}`; a forced 512 WebCodecs run and a forced FFmpeg run each report 512 and keep valid project metadata.
notes: Position in the shared-file sequence: after media.export-identity, before morph.render-api. Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Leaves that must not edit these three files: ws:crop.repro (failing tests and the failure analysis only), crop.policy, media.envelope-helpers, media.recovery-schema, morph.descriptor-geometry, compute.consumer-example, compute.names-equality, and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept leaf. title: Verify diagnostics consent behaviour and outside-request privacy on the release artifact
description:
## Background
Candidate defects: 11 (requests per keystroke to a `workers.dev` host, analytics beacon, 3.4 MB name list on first keystroke; privacy text incomplete), 12 ("Send report" silently turns standing reporting on), 13 (client sends an action the collector rejects; one bad event drops the batch), 16 (stacked toasts cover Create morph). Diagnostics consent control owns the `#debug-reporting` disclosure.

## Why
Diagnostics behaviour is part of the declared UI changes that integrated verification must include; privacy claims need request-log evidence.

## Scope
- One-shot report stays one-shot and its label says so; standing opt-in is explicit; Off-state report toast remains; no redundant opt-in toast while On.
- `Debug reports: Off/On` disclosure after Help/FAQ at `#debug-reporting`; FAQ/footer Privacy & reports links expand it and focus the checkbox.
- Turning On/Off, reload restores saved choice; withdrawal aborts/discards unsent reports; persistence failure disclosed as tab-only.
- Typing sends nothing per keystroke; every outside request is named in the privacy text, as is what a saved file contains.
- Client and collector action lists agree (shared-list test passes against the deployed collector config).
- Only one prompt shows at a time and none covers an action.
- Rows graded: R31 (no per-keystroke requests), R45, R48; defects 11, 12, 13, 16.

## Out of scope
Collector retention decision and old-report deletion (diagnostics learnings). Analytics policy changes.

title: Build the ordinary post-delivery check script
description:
## Background
Every delivery action ends with ordinary checks (PLAN.md "Acceptance receipts" > Delivery and publication): the app loads, a diagnostics report is accepted, models load, the names catalogue is served, and, for API retirement, retired hosts do not answer. No phone or shutdown-parity certification. Since `6107f80` (21 October) the runtime has a second origin, `models.facemorph.me`, that the page uses for chunk retries on `*.facemorph.me` hosts; it is part of serving, so the check covers it.

## Why
One reusable script keeps each action's receipt consistent, and lets every action (early promotion, candidate-edit merge, candidate-source handover, production promotion, API retirement, classic publication) cite the same evidence shape.

## Scope
- Playwright script `scripts/delivery/post-delivery-check.mjs`, parameterised by hostname, expected artifact identity and mode:
  - `app` (default): page loads (HTTP 200, no console error), the served artifact identity (build id / identity file digest) equals the expected digest, the runtime manifest is fetched and one model chunk verifies against its pin from the site origin **and** the same chunk from `models.facemorph.me` (direct fetch, digest compared), the names catalogue is fetched and parses, and a test diagnostics report (marked test, filterable) is accepted by the collector.
  - `retired`: DNS and HTTP probes for given hosts (`api.facemorph.me`, `checkface.facemorph.me`) assert they no longer serve: NXDOMAIN, connection refused, or a 4xx/5xx response with no API body. A 2xx **or any 3xx redirect** is a failure, because the plan allows no replacement, GUID resolver, result-link redirect or proxy at a retired hostname. Probes use `/`, `/api/face/?seed=0&dim=512` and one historic GUID-style path per host, with redirects not followed; each probe's status, `Location` header (if any) and body digest are recorded per host.
  - `page`: page loads and a given text is present (for legacy pages with no collector or model manifest, e.g. the legacy notice edit); parts not applicable are reported as such, never as passed.
  - `redirect`: for the standalone names host. Asserts `names.facemorph.me` answers 301 or 308 with a `Location` on the expected app origin (redirects not followed for the assertion), then runs `app` mode on the target. Used by production promotion and planned by `domain.names-host`.
  - `unchanged`: reads the current artifact identity of each given host and compares with a supplied before-identity (used by classic publication and the rename to show no publisher fired).
- Every run writes the structured event log and a summary JSON the receipts embed.
- Unit tests for the parameter/assertion layer: wrong digest fails; missing chunk fails; mirror digest mismatch fails; a retired host that still answers 200 fails; a retired host that answers 301/302/307/308 fails; `redirect` mode fails on a 200, on a 302 and on a `Location` outside the expected origin; a not-applicable part is reported `not_applicable`, not `pass`; test-report marker present.

## Out of scope
Integrated verification journeys; package registry checks (package publication has its own post-publication check).

## Considerations
The test report must be filterable from real diagnostics (marker field documented for the collector). Read-only apart from the test report.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, retains the log as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics), and every network claim is asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] `app` mode runs green against next.facemorph.me today (read-only except the test report), including the `models.facemorph.me` chunk comparison; `retired` mode run against a host known to be absent passes and against a live host fails (proves the probe); `page` and `unchanged` modes each exercised once.
- [ ] Unit tests listed above pass.
- [ ] Receipt `docs/receipts/delivery-post-delivery-check.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime/model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Its structured event log is written with the emitter from `build.docs-decisions-receipts` (fm-ucl: `scripts/evidence/event-log.ts`, or `scripts/evidence/event_log.py` for Python harnesses) using the host classes in `scripts/evidence/host-classes.json`, and the log passes `node scripts/check-event-log.ts <log>`; the receipt passes `node scripts/check-receipts.ts` (polish r2).
- [ ] `redirect` mode exercised once against a fixture server (308 to the expected origin passes; 302 and a foreign `Location` fail), and `retired` mode's redirect rejection is covered by a unit test (polish r2).
notes: Plan anchors (PLAN.md): #delivery-and-publication, #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026, #programme-boundaries-and-finish-line; receipts rule: #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance.

title: ONNX Runtime Web currency evaluation
description:
## Summary

Evaluate whether the latest ONNX Runtime Web gives the app anything (operator request, 16 October). It
runs through the re-homed autoresearch pipeline and gates no release: the release can ship the pinned,
verified runtimes under the currency policy's recorded hold-back. "No benefit" and "hold" are valid
outcomes. The runtime files are a release-consistent mirror, so the npm package and mirrored runtime
move together. `webonnx/wonnx` is excluded (archived; last release v0.5.1, September 2023).

Facts (verified 16 October; not measured for this app): npm latest 1.30.0; 1.31.0 GitHub release of
9 October not yet npm `latest`; nightly `1.31.0-dev.20260918-bc8e7ed75`. Candidate runs CPU 1.24.3 and
WebGPU 1.22.0 (a JSEP build). ORT Web announced in 1.29.0 it will deprecate and remove JSEP and WebGL:
default bundle flips to the native WebGPU EP with a temporary `onnxruntime-web/jsep` escape hatch for
one release, then JSEP is deleted. Moving the WebGPU route forward is a migration to the native EP.
Possible gains (hypotheses): graph capture (1.24.1), convolution optimisations, subgroup-matrix
MatMul/Gemm incl. WASM, subgroup-size control (1.30.0). Expect modest or no gain.
## Outcome

Adopt (bump the immutable release-consistent runtime mirror with manifest and canaries), hold (reason,
re-check trigger, JSEP removal timeline) or adopt in part (for example CPU only). Tolerances and
retained cells do not change. Feeds compute extraction's provider adapters (soft) and integrated
verification (the decision is recorded).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/` with the evidence receipts.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Compare preserved performance paths against the pinned control on existing cells
description:
## Background
Retained achieved evidence (not limits): eris RTX2080 SUPER WebGPU pipeline 129.8->69.7 ms/frame and RGBA8 42.6->37.1; OPFS model load 1430->640 ms; Ubuntu Chrome CPU repeat Save 100.72->66.49 ms; iPhone16Pro Simulator first face 25287 ms. Source invariants: canary-set keyed admission receipts (one canary before the first cold face, rest deferred), `ort-worker.mjs` `warmMapping()` overlap, CPU 1-4 threads, single-threaded streamed e4e, cache-only worker and digest reuse, Firefox storage permission timing, pinned self-hosted runtimes, no-third-party gate.

## Why
The plan requires keeping all integrated performance optimizations through the refactor; integrated verification records no-regression comparisons on cells that already exist (no new campaign).

## Scope
- Inputs: the evidence register and the one no-regression comparison protocol in `build.preservation-map-extension`
  (fm-rqc): control identified by hash, same cell and workload, margins declared from control variability, no
  verdict from a single hosted-CI timing. Every one of its 12 evidence rows gets a row here, even when the verdict is
  `untested`.
- Use the pinned candidate artifact (or explicitly qualified rebuild) as control and the same available cell/workload for the release artifact.
- Record provider/model/runtime, resolution/FPS/frame count, cold/retained/resident/restored state, visible-tab state, finish boundary.
- Protect first/nth face, confirmed-photo work, complete video, first/repeated Save, restore, responsiveness, acquired/output bytes, memory reservations, cancellation.
- Verify each source invariant above still holds (code check plus a run that shows it).
- Bounded paired comparisons on suitable workers under the device lease.

## Out of scope
New benchmark campaigns; control/control report; release-wide no-regression claim without comparisons; physical-iPhone timing.

## Considerations
- Correctness/resource regressions fail. A latency/bytes regression is investigated with compatible repeated evidence and a margin declared from control variability; a single noisy hosted-CI timing is not a verdict.
- Never offset phone CPU slowdowns with desktop GPU gains; 512 px video is not a free speedup over 1024 px.
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Comparison table per retained cell: control vs release, same workload and boundary, verdict in {no regression, regression investigated, inconclusive, untested}.
- [ ] Each source invariant has a recorded check.
- [ ] The comparison script has unit tests: a release value inside the declared margin is `no regression`; outside it with fewer than the protocol's repeats is `inconclusive`; a run on another digest or another cell is `untested`; a correctness or resource failure is `regression` regardless of timing; a cell from fm-rqc's register with no run is listed `untested`.
- [ ] Ran against the named release-candidate artifact digest (the same digest the join report checks); a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded failed or untested, never passed.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes: Anchors: #retained-performance-evidence-and-no-regression-checks, #workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership (no-regression tie-break).

title: Build the pinned conversion container and opt-in Compose service
description:
## Background
Container contract: Dockerfile, pinned Python/PyTorch/export dependencies, `.dockerignore`, opt-in Compose conversion service; converter code/tools and notices but no pretrained weights; caller-acquired checkpoint inputs mounted read-only, outputs writable, optional tool/download caches as separate volumes; host-compatible file ownership; credentials and large/generated artifacts out of the build context/image. CPU-capable reference conversion/verification where the exporter permits; optional documented NVIDIA configuration with host driver/container toolkit and a pinned CUDA/PyTorch stack, without silent fallback or arbitrary GPU claims. The classic API's inference container is separate and unchanged.

## Why
Avoid host-specific virtualenv setup and record the actual toolchain used to create provider artifacts; release builds use the same qualified image.

## Scope
- `packages/model-conv/Dockerfile` with base images pinned by digest; locked Python deps; `.dockerignore` bounding context; Compose service behind an opt-in profile.
- Documented clean-clone `build`, `convert`, `verify` commands (copyable, real); CPU path; optional NVIDIA profile.
- Report records image digest, tool/source versions, input checkpoint checksum/provenance, conversion flags and output manifest/digests.
- Empty-cache and repeat conversion, interrupted/error cleanup (no partial outputs left labelled complete), host ownership of outputs.
- Validated OS/architecture/provider matrix with absent hardware evidence shown explicitly.

## Out of scope
Registry image publication (none planned). Conversion in app startup.

## Considerations
- Byte-reproducibility is claimed only if proven; otherwise record nondeterministic fields and require numerical/identity parity.
- Containerization grants no model rights; acquisition terms and acknowledgements remain explicit.

## Independent reference check in `verify` (polish r1)
`verify` must compare the converted artifacts against a reference that does not come from the converter's own export path: the pinned upstream PyTorch implementation (NVlabs stylegan2-ada-pytorch at the recorded revision, e4e for the encoder) loads the original checkpoint inside the container and produces raw outputs for a recorded seed/latent set with constant noise; the converted artifacts run under ONNX Runtime CPU on the same inputs. The report records max absolute raw-float error, max RGB difference (0-255) and, for the encoder, max absolute W+ error, against the tolerance declared for that model before the run. FFHQ uses the frozen values; other models use their own declared tolerance.

Named tests: `model-conv.verify-uses-upstream-reference` (the reference path imports the upstream module and reads the original checkpoint, not the converted files), `model-conv.verify-fails-on-perturbed-artifact` (a deliberately perturbed chunk fails verify), `model-conv.failure-cleanup` (a killed conversion leaves no output labelled complete), `model-conv.output-ownership` (outputs owned by the invoking UID/GID).

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clean clone on a CPU worker: build, convert, verify succeed from the documented commands verbatim.
- [ ] Empty-cache, repeat and forced-failure runs behave as specified; outputs owned by the invoking user.
- [ ] Image content scan: no weights, credentials or generated artifacts.
- [ ] NVIDIA profile run on a GPU worker under the device lease, or recorded as untested.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] `verify` computes its reference with the pinned upstream PyTorch code from the original checkpoint, and a perturbed artifact fails verify (both as named tests).

title: Application deploy and collector re-homing
description:
## Background
Classic owns the application's deploy path: `hosting/next-static/` (frontend staging, runtime restaging and mirroring, `promote.py`, `attach-domain.py`, entry Worker, analytics), `hosting/next/` (runtime preparation), `hosting/next-cloudflare/` (diagnostics collector Worker with tests), `hosting/gallery/` (names-catalogue pipeline) and the `deploy` job of `next-site.yml` (CI deploys `next.facemorph.me` on qualified candidate pushes). About 4.3 MB across 48 tracked files; the collector directory also tracks `.wrangler/` cache/state files that must stay out of the allowlist.

## Why
Without this the monorepo cannot publish `next.facemorph.me` and classic cannot be wound down.

## Scope
Import from committed objects with allowlist/provenance; staging; fail-closed promotion; collector; catalogue pipeline without the hosted API; CI deploy workflow with single-publisher rule.

## Out of scope
Reusable chunk/manifest hosting (ws:hosting); production promotion actions (ws:delivery); diagnostics consent UI and retention wording (ws:diag); names generator (ws:names).

## Considerations
Any publish is an explicit operator action (`--publish`); exactly one repository's workflow may publish a given target at a time. Operator rulings: no time boxes, no human approval gates, no fallbacks or backports to the old stack, no .NET/F#/Webpack in this repository. Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.

## Re-homing coverage map (polish r1)
| Classic piece (candidate `6107f80`) | Home here | Leaf |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hosting/next-static/stage.py`, `restage-runtime.py`, `mirror-runtime.py`, entry `worker.mjs`/`wrangler.jsonc`, `analytics.mjs` | `hosting/next-static/` (application functions per the boundary decision) | `deploy.import`, `deploy.staging` |
| `hosting/next-static/promote.py`, `attach-domain.py` | `hosting/next-static/` | `deploy.promotion` (attach-domain is imported; using it is a delivery action) |
| `hosting/next-cloudflare/` collector Worker + tests | `hosting/next-cloudflare/` | `deploy.collector` |
| `hosting/gallery/` + `catalogue.json` staging | `hosting/gallery/` | `deploy.catalogue-pipeline` |
| `hosting/next-mirror/` second runtime origin | `packages/cloudflare-model-host` | `hosting.serving`; deploy/warm called by `deploy.ci-workflow` |
| `next-site.yml` `deploy` job (verify artifact, restore/rebuild runtime, stage, deploy, live-byte checks, mirror deploy + warm) | `.github/workflows/` here | `deploy.ci-workflow` |
"Runtime mirror" means two things in classic: `mirror-runtime.py` rebuilding `.runtime-public` from the pinned manifest during staging, and the `models.facemorph.me` second origin. The first is `deploy.staging`; the second is `hosting.serving`, deployed and warmed by `deploy.ci-workflow`.

## Runtime mirror deploy-and-warm: owned here (polish r2)
This workstream owns the step that, in classic, runs after every site deploy: "Deploy the runtime mirror" (`npx -y wrangler@4.149.0 deploy --config hosting/next-mirror/wrangler.jsonc`) followed by "Warm the runtime mirror with every immutable runtime file". Classic warm step (`next-site.yml` deploy job, `6107f80` lines ~215-220): select every staged path matching `^runtime/(assets|chunks|manifests|photo|encoder-stream)/`, request each from the mirror with `curl -I --retry 3 --retry-all-errors` (8 in parallel), fail the job on any non-200 and print `<n> runtime files held by models.facemorph.me`.
The commands themselves are the model-host package's (`hosting.serving` fm-qp4i). The step that calls them, its order (after the site deploy and its live-byte checks), its guard and its receipt belong to `deploy.ci-workflow` (fm-7vo1).

title: Confirmed-crop and recovery-class built-UI acceptance on the ported app
description:
## Goal
Accept the confirmed-crop repair and the still-recovery wiring where people meet them: in the Vite-built ported app. `crop.fix`, `crop.queue` and `media.reader-wiring` edit the shared bridge before the TS/React milestone and prove themselves in the real-bridge facade harness, because `build:next` never bundles the imported source before the rendering port (`import.checks`); this row runs their built-UI and operated checks on the first artifact that has both the port and those changes. It holds the locked requirement's visible proof: a confirmed crop that the detector cannot re-find goes straight to one real e4e attempt with no crop loop. Created in the 24 October final pass so the compute, crop and media chain can run in parallel with the port instead of after it.

## Scope
**Single-crop built-UI acceptance (moved from `crop.queue`)**
- On the ported (parity) crop flow in the Vite-built app, before face controls' crop editor redesign: forced detection/alignment failure after confirmation (the flipped `crop.repro` built-UI test); no-face, multi-face, oriented (all eight EXIF orientations sampled), non-square and malformed fixtures; Cancel before and after OK; stale revision (edit during encode).
- Over-limit inputs through the real file entry: 64 MiB + 1 byte, a header declaring more than 120 × 1024² pixels, a 20,001 px edge each show the actionable message with zero e4e and zero keypoints; files exactly at each limit proceed. A 30 MB file shows the detector as not run; manual crop confirms and reaches one e4e attempt.
- Guide overlay visible and hidden on the same rectangle give the same `tensorDigest`.
- Manual-crop path numerical qualification (e4e W+ <= 0.0001) independent of speed.
- Operated clicks on crop OK/Cancel and Adjust Crop where they exist in the ported flow. Synthetic or licensed fixtures only; personal photos stay outside Git.

**Recovery-class built-UI acceptance (moved from `media.reader-wiring`)**
- Through the face file entry and drop targets of the ported app: `matching` installs with zero model/detector requests; `missing` offers Encode image and starts nothing until pressed; `damaged` (truncated, bit-flipped) keeps identity and offers Use as photo only when decodable; `incompatible-schema` viewable and saveable with the version named; model mismatch shows the image, Save returns the opened bytes, the engine receives no latent and Morph excludes the face with a reason.
- Multi-file drops of 1, 2, 3 and many (8, 30) mixed files.

**Logging**
- Every case logs the counters it asserts (`crop-confirmed`, detect/align/warp after confirmation, `e4e.attempt-start`, `crop.open`, classification kind, requests by host class) on structured lines; traces and screenshots kept on failure.

## Out of scope
- Multi-selection built-UI acceptance at 1/2/3/8 slots (`face.batch`); crop editor redesign (`face.crop-editor`); the fixes themselves (`crop.fix`, `crop.queue`, `media.reader-wiring`).

## Notes
- Edits no shared bridge/runtime/worker file except to fix a defect it finds; such a fix follows the out-of-turn rule in the shared-file note (a needs edge to the latest merged row that edits the file).
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#confirmed-crop-encoding (built-UI acceptance on the existing crop flow); #media-and-recovery (still-image UI re-import); #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance (UI acceptance is operated).

title: Confirmed-crop encode queue module: ordered slots, one live encoder, per-slot cancel/retry, tab-only pixels
description:
## Goal
Build the queue that encodes an ordered list of frozen crops one e4e at a time, with per-slot cancel, retry and tab-only reference-counted pixel ownership, as a module over the package's `encode` and the confirmed-crop policy. fm-fy2.8 then wires it into the bridge and proves the direct-e4e ruling through the real bridge.

## Scope
- `enqueueConfirmedCrops(batchRevision, crops) -> SlotId[]` (click order preserved, one slot per crop, shared prefix reported in each slot's progress); `maxLiveEncoders = 1`; `cancelSlot`, `retrySlot -> AttemptId` (only for cancelled/failed with retained pixels; reuses the frozen record and derived pixels; else `no-retained-pixels`), `removeSlot`/`replaceSlot`/`disposeBatch`; late results discarded by revision.
- Reference-counted, tab-only pixel ownership; never persisted to OPFS, IndexedDB, sessionStorage or localStorage; after reload unfinished slots report "lost; use Encode image".
- Slot events `slot.queued|started|progress|succeeded|failed{kind}|cancelled|released` with slot ID, attempt ID and batch revision; test-build hook `pixelRefs(slotId)`. Use the operation controller's scheduler interface if available. `face.batch` renders on top and must not reimplement it. Candidate reference: `crop-queue.test.mjs`.

## Rules
- This bead edits NONE of the shared files (`apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs`). Code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today until the bridge's own turn in the shared-file sequence; the bridge rewiring is the original bead's job.
- Tests run against real models, real browsers and real files where stated; no mocks, fixtures or captures stand in for live proof. The original bead's real-bridge/built-app checks still have to pass before the feature counts as done.
- Split from the original bead in the parallelism pass (operator, 24 October 2026: more parallel work from the start).
- Original bead: fm-fy2.8 (Bounded serial encode queue for confirmed crops, proven through the real bridge); anchors as listed there.

- [x] Queue tests with the real CPU e4e through the package: order preserved through async completion; cancel of one queued slot leaves siblings running in order; retry gets a new attempt ID with the same frozen crop; remove releases pixels (`pixelRefs`); no duplicate keypoints.
- [x] `crop-queue.retry-reuses-derived-pixels` (derivation and detector spies 0), `crop-queue.no-pixels-no-retry`, `crop-queue.reload-drops-unfinished`, `crop-queue.no-persistence` (storage spy).

title: Rendering port: morph slot, More options, video slot and frame slider
description:
## Background

## Why
Morph playback/scrub and settings are parity rows; retained-frame/slider behaviour must not regress.

## Scope
Components with the same contract; slider reads frames via `window.__nextFrames`/`sliderFrames`; video playback loop/inline.

## Considerations
Keep the `.next-*` DOM/class contract and carry `product-ux.scss`. MUI v4->v9 pixel differences are reviewed and recorded, not gated; anything that hides, overlaps or mislabels a control is a defect. Defects frozen as repair rows are not reproduced: where carrying candidate CSS would reproduce one (defect 1: MUI button style out-ranks the Remove close-button rule so it renders below the image, invisible, over the mode menu), carry the stylesheet's intended placement and leave the operated repair acceptance to the owner (face controls). By this point WebGL has been removed by provider simplification, so the Advanced selector shows Auto/CPU/WebGPU; the flow-matrix freeze classes the WebGL entry as a declared change.

## Source map (classic, read-only, classic `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (or the frozen import revision recorded in `inventory.md`; re-check line numbers there with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`))

## Goldens replayed
Flow rows (DOM level): Change morph settings/start/cancel/retry, Play video/switch to slider, Save face WebP/PNG or morph MP4, Share/cancel share, Return with completed retained work (video and slider). Disabled-Create-Morph-looks-enabled (defect 20) is a repair row graded by face controls; whole-action progress is a declared change (operation controller/face controls).

## Goldens and grading (polish r1)
- **Golden store.** Goldens are the recorder output chosen by `migration.golden-spike` (reducer transitions or journey-step DOM/state snapshots), committed under `apps/web/test/goldens/control/<flow-row-id>/` with a `goldens.json` index naming the control `deploy-next/` SHA-256, the recorder command and, per step, the freeze class of its row. Replays run `scripts/fetch-control.mjs` first and refuse to run if the index digest differs from `control-artifact.json`.
- **Parity rows** (freeze class *present and unchanged*): the port's transitions/DOM must equal the golden exactly (state fields, emitted effect descriptions, text, flow order, round-trip bytes). No tolerance, no "close enough".

The recorder tags their steps `repair:<n>` or `declared:<section>` and the replay lists them as owner-graded instead of asserting them. No test in this repository may encode a candidate defect as expected output. title: Add package export, worker-entry and clean pack/install consumer checks
description:
## Background

Language contract: `stylegan-js` ships ESM JS plus generated `.d.ts`, explicit exports and explicit
emitted worker entry points with tested bundler loading; consumers must not need the app's Vite
aliases or filesystem layout. `browser-model-manager` import must not access globals or start I/O.
Clean pack/install tests include public types, emitted worker assets, export resolution and a consumer
outside the monorepo.

## Why

These are the type and worker gates the extraction workstreams are accepted against.

## Scope

- Per package: pack, install into a temporary consumer outside the workspace, type-check against
  public declarations, resolve every `exports` entry, load emitted worker assets through at least one
  bundler, assert no repository-only path aliases in runtime imports.
- Import-side-effect check: importing each package in a sandbox touches no globals and performs no I/O.
- Boundary checks: packages do not import app code or React (except app), and the engine has no
  network/cache imports (simple dependency-graph assertion).
- Wire into CI for every package edit.

## Out of scope

Real package content (extraction workstreams). Publication docs (pkgdocs).

## Considerations

- Shared-file serialisation: `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and
  `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited only in the mandated order (provider simplification, typed facade,
  compute extraction, confirmed-crop fix, morph pipeline, names picker/diagnostics); build items change
  tooling and CI, and add any shared file they touch to the check-migration map's conflict list.
- No worktrees, resets or cleans; preserve other sessions' uncommitted work.
- Hosted-minute economy: use capable workers where practical, but never weaken a required check or
  substitute Linux WebKit for Safari/iOS; never cancel a live publication halfway.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] CI job runs the consumer checks for all four placeholders and fails on a seeded alias import and a seeded side-effecting import.

A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Unit tests for the boundary/dependency-graph assertion (package importing app code, engine importing a network/cache module, non-app package importing React) and for the side-effect sandbox run in the workspace test command.

title: Bounded e4e photo-encode orchestration and descriptor-driven mapping and synthesis
description:
## Split (parallelism pass, 24 October 2026)
The package/core work of this bead moved to fm-qjcs (stylegan-js core: bounded e4e encode and descriptor-driven mapping and synthesis), which edits no shared file and starts as soon as its own inputs exist. This bead keeps: rewiring the bridge/runtime photo-encode and mapping/synthesis calls to the package's `encode` and descriptor-driven paths, and the app-side checks. The scope text below is kept for context; where it describes work now owned by fm-qjcs, that bead owns and accepts it and this bead consumes the result.

## Goal
Give `stylegan-js` a typed photo `encode` over a caller-supplied encoder capability that runs the bounded streamed e4e on preverified local shards, and make mapping and synthesis read every dimension from the model descriptor instead of FFHQ's fixed 1024 px and 18 × 512. The engine must never hold file, cache or downloader access, must not need the whole encoder in memory, and must serve non-face StyleGAN2 checkpoints at other resolutions or reject unsupported ones with an actionable error.

## Scope
**Photo-encode orchestration**
- Candidate: 108 sequential FP32 ORT sessions (`photo-runtime/encoder-stream/execute.mjs`, manifest `encoder-stream/assets/manifest.json`), bounded unshared single-threaded WASM, constrained sequential worker teardown, encoder-to-generator residency transition. Today the stream may fetch verified shards over HTTP mid-run; moving acquisition ahead of engine operations is a deliberate boundary change.
- `encode(pixels per the frozen preprocessing policy) -> W+` with cancel/dispose, attempt identity and per-stage timing hooks, on the manager's encoder capability (lazy verified-local shard reads; no `acquireBytes` callback, URL or OPFS handle visible to the engine). Do not expose the existing network-repair-capable cache handle as an offline capability.
- Preserve bounded sequential session create/run/release, unshared single-threaded WASM, constrained worker teardown on phones, and encoder-to-generator transition accounting (finished inference does not imply reclaimed memory).
- Preserve qualified WASM photo helpers (mapping/codec helpers) without reinstating the per-device lab encoder check in ordinary startup.
- Timing facts kept: e4e verified read/session-create/run/total timings and actual WASM and max-live-session facts. e4e tolerance max absolute W+ error 0.0001 (latest recorded 2.83718e-5). No silent fp16 e4e or tolerance widening.
- Acquisition and verification of the encoder's shards finish before its admission; unrelated authorized acquisition may continue under its own budgets.

**Descriptor-driven mapping and synthesis**
- Contracts milestone 2 freezes the descriptor: latent/output shapes, layout/normalization, noise, truncation, optional class conditioning, resource requirements. Today `geometry/latent-path.mjs` accepts only `[512]`/`[18,512]` and runtime/media code fixes tensor sizes.
- Mapping and synthesis read Z/W size, W+ layer count, output resolution/channels, layout/normalization, noise, truncation and optional conditioning from the descriptor carried by the loaded capability.
- Descriptive typed rejection of unsupported descriptors/operator combinations, naming the unsupported field.
- Component check with a qualified caller-loaded reference at a different output resolution and latent layer count: the non-face fixture from conversion.qualify when available, otherwise a test descriptor with an independent reference from the pinned reference implementation, at its own declared small tolerance (FFHQ values not inherited).
- Non-face capabilities never load a face detector or FFHQ e4e.

## Out of scope
Detector proposal and the confirmed-crop preprocessing policy (crop.fix). Consent/acquisition ordering (acquisition consent). Batch scheduling (operation controller, crop.queue). Descriptor-driven morph geometry (morph.render). Dynamic-shape recovery schema (media.schema). Converter qualification (conversion.qualify). The full external-developer journey (integrated verification).

## Notes
- The descriptor component checks unblock media/app integration; they do not establish complete non-face package support, which closes only in `verify.packages`.
- Shared-file order (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October; revised in the 24 October final pass): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in one sequence enforced by needs edges, never concurrently: `provider.native` -> `provider.webgl` -> `provider.route-admission` -> `migration.project-json` (one-line ProjectJson import swap) -> typed facade (`migration.facade`) -> `compute.synthesis` -> `compute.photo-descriptor` -> `compute.app-rebind` -> `crop.fix` -> `crop.queue` -> `media.reader-wiring` -> `media.export` -> `media.schema` -> `morph.render` -> `morph.guards` -> `media.session` -> face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Rows that must not edit these files: `crop.repro`, `compute.blend`, `compute.package-surface`, `media.envelope`, `provider.admission` (evidence), `crop.ported-app` and `compute.ported-app` (acceptance on the ported app; a fix they need follows the out-of-turn rule below) and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept row; code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) until the bridge's own turn. A row that finds it must edit one of these files outside its turn adds a needs edge to the latest row in the sequence that edits it. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #compute-extraction, #external-developer-journey-and-non-face-models.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] fm-qjcs is closed; its modules are what this bead wires in (no second copy of the moved code left in the app).
- [x] Real-bridge harness photo encode through the package meets W+ error <= 0.0001 and issues zero requests during encode.
- [x] Source scan of the rewired app (`runtime.mjs`, `ort-worker.mjs`, bridge) finds no hardcoded 1024 or 18x512 outside the FFHQ descriptor allowlist.
close_reason: All 3 acceptance items met (4665b88): package encode wired into the worker (no app copy of the schedule), real-bridge photo encode W+ 3.22e-6 with zero requests on a warm encode, geometry source scan clean; P30 warm face 17 s.

title: Apply FAQ and retirement copy to the candidate
description:
## Background
Edits to the candidate source are ordinary work on the working candidate and need no separate approval (operator, 18 October). They are made on a non-deploying classic branch (e.g. `delivery/candidate-edits`) branched from `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, and merged only after the ordinary qualification via `delivery.candidate-edits-merge`, because the candidate branch publishes to next.facemorph.me on every qualified push. Run commands in `facemorph.me-classic` per its development guide. The copy inventory locates each preview-chrome and FAQ string with its replacement.

## Why
A promoted artifact must not promise GUID/link preservation, a fixed date or link a retired host.

## Scope

If the candidate build serves it (check `deploy-next/` for its rendered text), it gets the same retirement copy. If only the historical app uses it, the copy inventory records it as historical-only with that evidence and it is left unchanged (polish r2).

## Out of scope
Names-limitation text and native links (own leaves).

## Considerations
Preview chrome removal may be production-only; if next.facemorph.me keeps a preview label, gate by host config rather than forking source (record choice).

title: Autoresearch re-homing
description:
## Summary

Move the maintained research system out of classic into this repository's `autoresearch/` so new rounds
optimise the new application and packages. A workstream of its own, independent of release. Source facts
at classic `b2d945a` (15 October): tracked `autoresearch/` is 137 files, about 9.7 MB (88 files / 8.8 MB
historical `candidates/`); `results.tsv` is the 11-column header plus 69 rows; `state/` is ignored; two
research workflows (`research-built-ui-media-v1.yml`, `research-rgba-screen-v1.yml`) and
`hosting/next-static/promote.py` reference the tree; four documents carry uncommitted edits
(`README.md`, `loop-v3-proposal.md`, `reviews/README.md`, `reviews/2026-10-10/next-directions.md`).

Two stages: **`ws:research.s1`** (guides, protocol, templates, runner, lease, ledger continuation,
provenance map, and the byte-identical tree import) needs only the application inventory; **`ws:research.s2`**
(drivers and recipes that consume an app artifact, workflow path filters) needs stage 1, candidate import
and workspace build milestone 1.
## Interim rule until stage 1 closes

Until `ws:research.s1` closes, the only executable research checkout is classic: any research command that
must run (for example reproducing an existing measurement or a lease smoke) uses the plan's targeted launch
recipe there and appends to classic's history under its append-only rules. No new optimisation round starts
in classic; new rounds target the new application and packages from this repository after stage 1. After
the handover point classic receives only the forward pointer, and `scripts/check-research-ledger.mjs`
(`research.ledger-handover`) reports any row appended there.

## Acceptance (workstream)

From a clean clone one documented command runs a bounded smoke through the lease runner on a worker and
journals it; the ledger prefix is byte-identical to the frozen classic prefix; every other tracked file of
the classic tree at the snapshot is present byte-identical (digest list) or listed with the reason; the
69-row accounting resolves through the provenance map; no guide tells an agent to start research in
classic; a concurrent classic run is held off by the shared lease. Claims no performance result and does
not require the evaluator.

- [ ] `ws:research.s1` and `ws:research.s2` closed.

A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Port ProjectJson to typed TS schema code with round-trip goldens
description:
## Background
`src/Next/ProjectJson.fs` (266 lines at the pinned commit) defines the project schema used for embedded MP4 project metadata and session recovery. The candidate bridge imports its Fable output directly (`import {decode,encode} from './ProjectJson.fs.js'` in `product-bridge.mjs`), and Fable project qualification invokes `ProjectJson.fs.js`. The fixture is `src/Next/project-v1.fixture.json`. The new repo has no F# build.

## Why
Project JSON round trips are exact parity (structural). The bridge needs a non-Fable `decode`/`encode` before the typed facade can claim the bridge is fully TypeScript-reachable.

## Scope
- Strict-TS `ProjectJson` module with identical `decode`/`encode` semantics: field names, version handling, rejection of unknown/invalid versions, numeric formatting.
- Validate untrusted payloads (it reads files users drop).
- Goldens: decode/encode `project-v1.fixture.json` and projects recorded from the control artifact (project JSON embedded in control-exported MP4s and session records) byte-for-byte where the format is textual.
- Replace the bridge-import check and Fable qualification that read `ProjectJson.fs.js` with equivalent TS/schema checks (check-migration map entry).

## Out of scope
Dynamic-shape recovery schema versioning (media and recovery). The bridge import line swap itself is made inside the facade milestone (`migration.facade-types`), because the facade is the milestone that edits the shared bridge file.

## Considerations
This leaf belongs to the controller milestone but lands before the facade's bridge edit so the facade can swap the import. A round-trip failure is a blocker fixed in TS, never by importing F#. Shared-file serialization (decided 16/17 October): `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in the order provider simplification -> typed facade -> compute extraction -> confirmed-crop fix -> morph pipeline -> static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics reporting rebinding. Add any file this item edits to the check-migration map's conflict list.

## Source map and checks to replace (classic, read-only, classic `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (or the frozen import revision recorded in `inventory.md`; re-check line numbers there with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`))
- `src/Next/ProjectJson.fs` (266 lines, namespace `CheckFace.Next`), compiled by `src/App.fsproj`; its Fable output `ProjectJson.fs.js` is imported by `product-bridge.mjs` (`import {decode,encode} from './ProjectJson.fs.js'`).
- Fixture `src/Next/project-v1.fixture.json`.
- Classic checks that depend on Fable output and must be replaced with TS/schema checks in the check-migration map: the `next-site.yml` artifact-job step `node src/Next/verify-fable.mjs src/Next/ProjectJson.fs.js`; `scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs` (walks `.fs.js` files to compare bridge exports with F# imports); `scripts/next-matrix.mjs` lines ~164-169 (skips project export/open because `projectFilesVisible=false` and defers the round trip to `verify-fable.mjs`).

## Goldens and grading
Round-trip goldens are parity (exact): the fixture, plus project JSON taken from control-exported MP4s and session records recorded by the golden recorder. Byte-for-byte equality where the format is textual; structural equality plus numeric identity otherwise. There are no repair rows inside ProjectJson; if the freeze shows one, it is graded by its owner (media and recovery) against the specification, not copied.

## `verify-fable.mjs` assertions this leaf takes over (polish r2)
Classic `src/Next/verify-fable.mjs` (`6107f80`) ran `decode`/`encode` from the Fable output and counted its checks. `project-json.test.ts` carries every one of them as a named case against the TS module:
- Round trip (`decode` ok, `encode` ok, `JSON.parse(encode(decode(x)))` deep-equals `x`) for each morph kind: `linear`, `pairwise-ellipse`, `pairwise-figure8`, `full-smooth-ellipse`, `full-smooth-figure8`.
- Round trip with `bundle.version` = `quote" slash\ newline\n emoji 🙂` and `truncationPsi` = `0.12345678901234567` (exact float).
- These 12 inputs are rejected: `{`, `null`, `[]`, a duplicate `schemaVersion` key, `schemaVersion: 2`, an unknown top-level field `future: true`, morph kind `unrecognized`, `closed: "true"` (a string), a width of `1e999`, `"schemaVersion":01`, valid JSON followed by `null`, and 18-deep nested arrays.
- Round trip for latent `space` `z`, `w` and `w-plus` on every control. Rejected: `space` missing, `q`, `d` or `unknown`. Rejected: mixed spaces across controls (`z` and `w-plus`).
The receipt records the classic check count beside the TS case count, and the TS count is not lower. Typed errors replace Fable's `tag === 1` result.

## Bridge-import check successor (polish r2)
The classic `scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs` exists because webpack bundled a missing bridge export as `undefined`, and in R2-15 that shipped a dead photo path (`selectPhoto is not a function`). Its successor here, `apps/web/scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs`, checks that every name the typed facade imports from a hand-written module (including `export *` barrels) is exported there. Its unit test is a fixture facade that imports a missing name, and the script must fail on it. `migration.facade-types` (fm-pth3) wires the script into CI when it swaps the import. Strict `tsc` module resolution over the facade then makes the same failure a compile error.

## Hidden project files (polish r2)
Project export and open stay hidden (`projectFilesVisible = false` at `Product.fs` 978, off since 21 September; there is no project toolbar). This leaf supplies the schema for embedded MP4 recovery and session records only.
design: Files: `apps/web/src/project/project-json.ts` (decode/encode + typed errors), `project-json.schema.ts` (validator for untrusted input), `apps/web/scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs` replacement that compares bridge exports against the TS facade's imports instead of `.fs.js`. Tests `project-json.test.ts` (fixture round trip; every recorded control project; unknown version rejected; missing field rejected; wrong types rejected; numeric formatting identical for 0, negative zero, 1e-7, 4,294,967,295), `project-json.fuzz.test.ts` (fast-check: random valid projects round-trip; random bytes never throw untyped). Replay/e2e runs emit the structured event log (step ID = `<flow-row-id>/<step>`, ISO timestamp, control and port artifact digests, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); the log is a CI artifact.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Round trip of the fixture and every recorded control project is exact; invalid/unknown-version inputs are rejected with typed errors.
- [ ] Property/fuzz test: random valid projects survive encode->decode; malformed JSON never throws untyped.
- [ ] Check-migration map updated: Fable `ProjectJson.fs.js` checks replaced by TS schema checks, coverage preserved.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic are listed in the destination test discovery (no unlisted test files) and pass in CI.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/migration/ctl-projectjson.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Every assertion of classic `verify-fable.mjs` has a named counterpart in `project-json.test.ts` (5 morph kinds, escaped-string/psi round trip, the 12 malformed inputs, 3 accepted and 4 rejected spaces, mixed spaces); receipt records classic check count vs TS case count (TS >= classic); map row `verify-fable.mjs ProjectJson.fs.js` cites this bead.
- [ ] Bridge-export check successor (`apps/web/scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs`) fails on a fixture facade importing a non-exported name and passes on the real facade; reason strings in `next-matrix.mjs` (~164-169) and `next-e2e-browser.py` (`projectSaveReopen`) name `project-json.test.ts` instead of `verify-fable.mjs`.

title: Add the hold-back register and its check
description:
## Background

A hold-back needs a recorded reason and a re-check trigger (the next updater run that passes the gates, or the upstream release named in the reason). The ORT Web runtime hold-back is recorded before the first lockfile.

## Why

Makes every pin below latest stable explicit and re-checkable.

## Scope

- A machine-readable register next to the pins (package, pinned version, latest seen, reason, re-check
  trigger, date) and the updater's ignore rules generated from or checked against it.
- A CI check comparing pinned versions with registry latest stable (from the updater's data or a cached
  lookup, no build-time `latest` fetch into the build) and failing when a non-latest pin lacks a register entry.

## Out of scope

Deciding hold-backs for specific packages beyond ORT (each is recorded when it occurs).

## Considerations

- Shared-file serialisation: `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and
  `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited only in the mandated order (provider simplification, typed facade,
  compute extraction, confirmed-crop fix, morph pipeline, names picker/diagnostics); build items change
  tooling and CI, and add any shared file they touch to the check-migration map's conflict list.
- No worktrees, resets or cleans; preserve other sessions' uncommitted work.
- Hosted-minute economy: use capable workers where practical, but never weaken a required check or
  substitute Linux WebKit for Safari/iOS; never cancel a live publication halfway.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Removing the ORT register entry makes the check fail; restoring it passes.
- [ ] Unit tests cover this item's own logic and run in the workspace test command.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] A lockfile check fails if any dependency outside the bleeding-edge lane resolves to a prerelease (`-dev`, `-canary`, `-alpha`, `-beta`, `-rc`, `-next`); a nightly is adopted only once it reaches a stable release (fixture test).

title: Paired desktop performance comparison of ORT runtimes
description:
## Background

Existing initial paired design: discarded warmup and same-cell ABBA ×3; control/control noise first, then frozen margins.

## Why

Decide adoption on measured cold/warm cost, bytes and memory, not release notes.

## Scope

- Paired ABBA runs on the RTX 2080 SUPER (eris) under the shared lease for WebGPU, and CPU paired runs,
  only for sets that passed numerics.
- Metrics: cold start, warm per-frame time, runtime download bytes (they enter consent/acquisition
  costs), peak memory. Fixed 32-frame/16 FPS/1024 px workload where supported.
- Results recorded as experimental evidence with the control artifact by hash; ledger rows appended
  (scoped outcomes).

## Out of scope

Kernel changes.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Report with raw distributions, paired effects, noise margins and ledger row IDs.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script involved emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform and provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, retains the log as a CI artifact, and any network claim is asserted from that log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] For each numerics-passing set and provider (WebGPU on the RTX 2080 SUPER worker, and CPU paired runs), the report gives cold start, warm ms/frame, runtime download bytes and peak memory, each with raw distributions and a paired effect against the control set; sets that failed numerics are listed as excluded, never timed.

title: Publish the catalogue immutable-first with an atomic pointer switch
description:
## Goal
Publish the generated catalogue so users never see a pointer to results that fail checks: immutable content-addressed assets first, then an atomic switch of one small pointer after validation. Delivery decides what the names host may claim after this; the picker consumes the published shape.

## Scope

- Keep the existing `catalogue.json` served unchanged beside the new shape until cutover retires it.

title: Rebind analytics/reporting hosts for production and remove the collector's unenforced expiry
description:
## Background
`analytics.mjs` scopes to `next.facemorph.me`; `reporting.mjs` posts to `https://next.facemorph.me/diagnostics/events`.
The collector writes `customMetadata.expiresAt` (Cloudflare lifecycle rules cannot match custom metadata) and a KV
fallback with a 30-day expiration. Deploy re-homing supplies the collector source.

## Why
Production needs deliberate host bindings, and no code may claim a deletion it does not perform.

## Scope
- Deliberate host/route configuration for production (and the candidate host while it serves), independent of
  Triton/API retirement.
- Re-homed collector: stop writing `expiresAt`; drop the KV fallback's 30-day expiry; no bucket expiration rule.
- Consented sample reaches the collector; declined/blocked sample never prevents generation; failures non-blocking.

## Out of scope
Delivery's production collector action.

## Considerations
Bridge-consuming reporting rebinding: ordered after the morph pipeline.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits a shared file, so it follows the morph pipeline.** Reporting/analytics host rebinding is the plan's named "bridge-consuming edit of diagnostics control's reporting rebinding" (`product-bridge.mjs` host and issue-link references, `reporting.mjs`, `analytics.mjs`). Direct edge to ws:morph (fm-fy2.9) is present.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Against the configured collector: consented sample accepted (stored object found); declined and network-blocked samples do not affect generation (job completes).
- [ ] Stored objects have no `expiresAt`; KV writes carry no 30-day TTL (inspected).
- [ ] Config test: production build posts to the production route; no `next.facemorph.me` literal outside the configured host map.
- [ ] Each end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Every network claim is asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
