title: Run the retained desktop, mobile and GPU lanes against the release artifact
description:
## Background
Retained lanes: next-site (artifact, qualify, compiled-ui; its deploy job is not a verification lane), next-e2e real-ui-cpu, next-matrix (Ubuntu Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, macOS WebKit/Firefox), mobile-browser android (API35 Pixel6 emulator, eight components), ios (Simulator, eight components), ios-product-artifact/simulator, next-gpu-lane webgpu-benchmark (self-hosted GTX1050, Chrome for Testing 141.0.7390.54, non-gating). The last manual desktop matrix run (37555426933) failed on 7 October; recent GPU evidence failed adapter admission. `scripts/next-matrix.mjs` targets stale controls and uploads a recovery-bearing file for `photoE4e`.

Lanes as carried over by workspace build (the job names this bead triggers):
| Workflow / jobs | Carried over by | Platform | Gating |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `next-site.yml` `artifact` | `build.ci-site-lane` (fm-aa8) | ubuntu-24.04 | yes |
| `next-site.yml` `compiled-ui` | `build.ci-site-compiled-ui` (fm-ekk4) | ubuntu-24.04 | yes |
| `next-site.yml` `qualify` calling `next-e2e.yml` `real-ui-cpu` | `build.ci-e2e-cpu-lane` (fm-fy8) | ubuntu-24.04 Chrome, browser-harness 0.1.8 | yes |
| `next-matrix.yml` `engines`, `summary` (five cells) | `build.ci-desktop-matrix-lane` (fm-snu) | Ubuntu Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, macOS WebKit/Firefox | yes |
| `mobile-browser.yml` `android` (eight component IDs) | `build.ci-mobile-android-lane` (fm-xi3) | API 35 x86_64 pixel_6, SwiftShader | yes |
| `mobile-browser.yml` `ios` (eight component IDs) | `build.ci-mobile-ios-lane` (fm-hlv) | macOS 15, iPhone 16 Pro Simulator | yes |
| `mobile-browser.yml` `ios-product-artifact`, `ios-product-simulator` | `build.ci-ios-product-lane` (fm-34iy) | macOS 15, iPhone 16 Pro Simulator | yes |

The `next-site.yml` `deploy` job belongs to `deploy.ci-workflow` and is not run here (it deploys, it does not verify).
Cross-run artifact lookup and digest verification come from `build.ci-artifact-lookup` (fm-z70g); this bead
checks that every lane consumed the release artifact by digest through it, and records any rebuild as a deviation.

## Why
Native retirement does not retire desktop-browser, mobile or GPU checks; their outcomes are evidence cells in the support table.

## Scope
- Trigger each retained lane (as carried over by workspace build) on the release artifact digest; prefer canonical-artifact reuse; record any unavoidable rebuild.
- Confirm the repaired matrix uses an independent metadata-free photo with actual encoder events.
- Record each cell pass/fail/untested; software adapters rejected; adapter failures named.
- Collect results with one script, `scripts/verify/collect-lane-results.ts`: it reads each run's jobs and artifacts
  (`gh run view --json jobs,headSha` plus the uploaded `e2e-log-*` artifacts), checks the artifact digest in every

  lane x platform x provider with the outcome from the join's closed set, the run ID and the log digest. The support
  table and the no-regression comparison read this JSON.

## Out of scope
Adding Windows or physical-phone qualification. Making the GPU lane a promotion gate.

## Considerations
- Definition of a lane is not a passing result; do not advertise all cells as passing.
- Use development workers and the device lease to save GitHub minutes.
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.

- [ ] Unit tests for `collect-lane-results.ts` with fixture run JSON: a skipped or cancelled job becomes `untested`; a run whose logs carry another digest becomes `untested`; a software adapter on the GPU lane becomes `failed` with the adapter name; a log that fails `check-event-log.ts` makes its cell `untested`; a missing lane is listed, never omitted.

title: Split media computation from Save/Share; export policy, identity, filenames and prepared-file cache
description:
## Split (parallelism pass, 24 October 2026)
The package/core work of this bead moved to fm-l6mq (Computational media core: export policy, export identity and filenames, prepared-file cache), which edits no shared file and starts as soon as its own inputs exist. This bead keeps: rewiring the app's Save/Share gestures, object URLs, retention split of `last-result.mjs` (with the TS/React port) and the bridge onto the computational modules, with the existing media tests. The scope text below is kept for context; where it describes work now owned by fm-l6mq, that bead owns and accepts it and this bead consumes the result.

## Goal
Separate computational media (encoding, codec fallback, prepared-file reuse) from the app's user-gesture Save/Share, URLs and retention, state the product's lossy export policy once in code, and give every export a stable identity with a short informative, collision-safe filename and a prepared-file cache keyed by revision and format. Different exports must never be mistaken for one another, and repeated Save/Share of the same prepared file must reuse its name and bytes with no extra encode or inference.

## Scope
**Split**
- Candidate `src/Next/media.mjs` (~180 lines) mixes computation with Save/Share policy; `video-worker.mjs` runs WebCodecs 1024->512 and the FFmpeg 512 fallback with eight-frame raw segments, bounded codec queues and stream-copy concatenation; `last-result.mjs` (~80 lines) holds on-origin retention. The 4,096-frame path limit lives in `video-worker.mjs` and `last-result.mjs`.
- Move still encoding helpers, computational MP4 writer pieces and codec fallback selection into `stylegan-js` or a clearly computational app module; Save/Share gestures, object URLs and retention stay in the app.
- Split `last-result.mjs` retention policy from media computation jointly with the TS/React port (which owns the retention side).
- Preserve once-only background WebP with PNG fallback/read compatibility, bounded ordered face/video/scrub restore, integrity and quota handling, prepared-file/repeat reuse. Model-cache eviction never deletes completed exports or recovery records.

**`export-policy` module (computational, no DOM; the only source of encoder settings)**
- Still default lossy WebP quality 0.8 (candidate `image-encoder-worker.mjs` `convertToBlob({type: 'image/webp', quality})`) with the envelope for the actual payload.
- PNG: explicit lossless choice and the fallback when WebP encoding is unavailable (MIME and extension updated together).
- MP4 unchanged from candidate `probeVideoEncoder`: codec `avc1.42002A`, WebCodecs probes 1024 then 512, bitrate `round(size * size * fps * 0.25 / 1000) * 1000`, framerate = fps, one 64 × 64 correctness encode per bundle, FFmpeg fallback at 512.
- JPEG quality 0.85 stays a scrub/display derivative only, never a download. No quality slider.

**Export identity and filenames**
- Operator examples: `emma-k4p7s2.webp`, `seed-42-j8m3r6.png`, `holiday-face2-v9d2h5.webp`, `emma-noah-linear-c6q8t3.mp4`, `emma-noah-figure8-b7w4n2.mp4` (suffixes illustrative).
- `exportIdentity({kind, orderedInputs: [{inputIdentity, confirmedCropIdentity?}], morph?: {mode, settings}, modelIdentity, format, encodingOptions})` -> SHA-256; the short suffix uses the encoding and length frozen in contracts milestone 2 (examples show 6 lowercase letters/digits without vowels). Labels alone, timestamps alone and slot numbers are insufficient. A collision in the app's known export set (same name, different identity) is resolved by the contracts' rule (for example extending the suffix) until unique. Format is part of identity: WebP and PNG of one result share the label, differ in suffix.
- Label rules: short recognizable label from the result's name, entered text, seed or source basename; for longer paths first/last label plus face count; include morph mode; distinguish selected crops; strip source extension, path components, control/bidi characters, filesystem-reserved characters and names (`CON`, `NUL`); normalize whitespace; truncate the descriptive part to at most 64 characters before the suffix and real extension; `face`/`morph` only when no informative label exists.
- After reload latents do not recover words/basenames: reuse a safe opened filename where applicable, else `face`/`morph` plus the stable suffix; if `media.session` restored a tab-scoped label it may be used. Labels never go into metadata or diagnostics.
- Extension and MIME match the actual WebP/PNG/MP4 bytes.
- API for face controls to propose/edit the name while keeping the identity suffix.
- Optional File System Access writes use no-clobber naming or explicit overwrite confirmation. Browsers cannot inspect Downloads; do not claim absolute uniqueness from a short suffix.

**Prepared-file cache**
- Key (result revision, format, encoding options): one current prepared file per selected revision and format plus a bounded cache of other formats (bound from contracts milestone 2; oldest-first eviction). Completions for a superseded revision are discarded. A format change prepares only that format and never re-runs inference. Identity survives restoration.
- "Preparing file…" is the state between pixels shown and file ready; an encode failure keeps the visible result and offers file-preparation Retry. System-share cancellation is not an error and triggers no download.

## Out of scope
Save/Share buttons, format control and filename editing UI (face controls). Morph writer orchestration (morph.render).

## Notes
- Existing `media.test.mjs`, `video-worker.test.mjs`, `last-result.test.mjs` keep passing, adapted only where the control they assert moves.
- Shared-file order (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October; revised in the 24 October final pass): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in one sequence enforced by needs edges, never concurrently: `provider.native` -> `provider.webgl` -> `provider.route-admission` -> `migration.project-json` (one-line ProjectJson import swap) -> typed facade (`migration.facade`) -> `compute.synthesis` -> `compute.photo-descriptor` -> `compute.app-rebind` -> `crop.fix` -> `crop.queue` -> `media.reader-wiring` -> `media.export` -> `media.schema` -> `morph.render` -> `morph.guards` -> `media.session` -> face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Rows that must not edit these files: `crop.repro`, `compute.blend`, `compute.package-surface`, `media.envelope`, `provider.admission` (evidence), `crop.ported-app` and `compute.ported-app` (acceptance on the ported app; a fix they need follows the out-of-turn rule below) and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept row; code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) until the bridge's own turn. A row that finds it must edit one of these files outside its turn adds a needs edge to the latest row in the sequence that edits it. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #file-sharing-and-export-direction, #media-and-recovery.

title: Add versioned adapters for the built-UI driver and next-e2e flows
description:
## Background

Starting points: the maintained built-UI paired driver and `scripts/next-e2e.md` flows; extend supported release workloads.

## Why

Each driver's correctness and timing scope must be explicit in the evaluator.

## Scope

- Versioned adapter per driver mapping its outputs to the evaluator's verdict inputs with declared timing boundaries and correctness checks.

## Out of scope

Overlap/warming adapters.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.

- [ ] Each adapter has fixture-based tests and one leased run against the control artifact.

A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Survey candidate adapter signatures and open contracts.md
description:
## Background

The candidate's browser adapters live in classic at the pinned import revision: `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs`,
`src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` and `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, with `Assets/model-cache.mjs`,
`Assets/shard-store.mjs`, `photo/crop.mjs`, `media.mjs`, `video-worker.mjs`, `last-result.mjs`,
`browser/identity.mjs`, `image-envelope.mjs` and `estimate.mjs`. `product-bridge.mjs` statically
imports `desktop/runtime.mjs`. The application inventory (`docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/inventory.md`) records moving paths, consumers
and worker URLs. The current bounded encoder runs 108 sequential ORT sessions over FP32 shards.

## Why

Every later contract item needs the actual signatures, ownership and message shapes, not guesses.
Freezing types from the real adapters keeps the port and extraction faithful to the candidate.

## Scope

- Read the adapters above at the pinned revision (in classic until imported) and record each
  exported function, worker message type, callback, promise and resource it owns.
- Classify `desktop/runtime.mjs` as a retirement seam (provider simplification removes native
  dispatch), not a new native contract.
- Create `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts.md` with its section skeleton (engine, manager, host manifest, app batch/progress,
  scheduler/residency, preflight, export identity, model descriptor, UI walkthrough, ceilings) and a
  per-adapter appendix linking each candidate function to its future contract owner.
- Create `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/` for draft TypeScript type sources, one file per area.
- List every place where the candidate passes signals/callbacks/promises across a worker boundary,
  and every network-repair-capable handle (`model-cache.mjs` `acquire()`, `bytes()`, `open()`).

## Export index (skeleton created here)

`contracts.md` gets an "Export index" table with columns: exported name, module path, owning contract bead, milestone, downstream consumer beads. Proposed module roots: engine `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/` (`capability.ts`, `timing.ts`, `operations.ts`, `worker-messages.ts`, `recovery-metadata.ts`, `crop-policy.ts`, `numerics.ts`, `descriptor.ts`); manager `packages/browser-model-manager/src/contracts/` (`lifecycle.ts`, `leases.ts`, `errors.ts`, `grant.ts`, `budgets.ts`, `manifest.ts`); app `apps/web/src/contracts/` (`inputs.ts`, `tiles.ts`, `batch.ts`, `progress.ts`, `pixels.ts`, `consent-state.ts`, `scheduler.ts`, `preflight.ts`, `export-identity.ts`, `ceilings.ts`, `ui-states.ts`). Sibling contract beads fill their rows; the milestone type-test beads verify every row resolves to a real export.

## Out of scope

Writing the contracts themselves (sibling items). Any code change to the adapters.

## Considerations

- Read-only. Source paths refer to classic until imported with provenance.
- `estimate.mjs` cold synthesis constants are historical single-device priors and its `encodeMs`
  is video export, not a photo-encoder estimate; record that so preflight types do not inherit it.

title: Input journeys (words, seeds, names, photo, remove to one, retained tools) on the release artifact
description:
## Goal
Architecture completion requires that the final app keeps existing features and that the planned additions work; a cleaner repository alone does not complete the plan. The candidate's `next-e2e.yml` real-ui-cpu job covers CPU name/seed, e4e, crop, original reuse, recovered still without inference, GPU refusal/fallback scope, playable/saved MP4 and face/video/slider restore; the final app adds the locked crop design, static names, paste, Share/Save/format/filename, many-face layout, Morph preparing unfinished inputs and the weighted blend view. This bead operates the input journeys on the release artifact: words, seeds, names, photo, removing down to one face and the retained tools. Its cases are part of sub-result 1 (app flows), collated by `verify.flows`.

## Scope
Operate on the release artifact with real models:
- **Words (R04, defects 5, 8):** typing clears the old displayed result; one Generate action inside the tile; Enter invokes the same Generate/Retry and respects IME composition; empty and whitespace-only input give a field error and no Generate; 512 UTF-8 bytes accepted, 513 refused; text reaches the generator exactly as typed (no autocapitalise, correction, spell-check, trim or normalisation; `autocapitalize=off` checked under a phone user agent); a typed word with no instant picture shows "Press Generate to make this face" and photo entry stays in the mode menu and by drop.
- **Seeds (R05):** 0 and 4,294,967,295 generate; -1, 1.5, 4,294,967,296 and empty give a field error; pasted digits are validated as typed and never silently become another seed.
- **Names (R08, R10, R11):** Browse names from a face's menu binds to that face's stable ID and returns there (counts 1, 2, 3, many); selecting a name fills the text field and shows the prepared static result with no generator acquisition and no inference start (request log); editing the filled name clears the selection and enables normal Generate; typing a known name and pressing Generate yields the same identity as the picker result (latent/model identity, not pixels). The engine-level equality proof is in `names.static-result` (fm-fy2.18); if its engine or catalogue identity differs from the release identity record, the engine part of R11 is `untested` until re-run.
- **Photo (R18, R20, R21, R22):** paste an image into the main field and drop one on a tile and on the background (first empty or appended slot; unsupported input reported in context); confirm one detected crop: the exact confirmed pixels reach one e4e attempt, no repeated detection or crop loop, orientation correct; Adjust/rotate crop: Cancel restores the proposal, Use Crop returns to confirmation; no detectable face offers the manual crop path and the confirmed pixels reach e4e.
- **Remove down to one face (R46, defect 7):** Generate, Encode and Save remain; Add face stays enabled at every count (no fixed face count); Morph explains it needs a second compatible face. Remove, Undo and Start over at 0/1, 2, 3 and many (30, 64, 150).
- **Retained tools (R47):** `?testing` bulk Generate works; Help/footer issue links carry safe source, device, actual route and report reference and point at the correct repository.
- Every case is operated through the `verify.harness` (fm-48bj) helpers, every network or consent claim is asserted from intercepted requests (the request-interception helper from `build.ci-site`, fm-aa8), and every case is listed in this bead's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix rows or defect numbers it grades.

## Out of scope
Morph, session walk and result journeys (`verify.functional.results`); the weighted blend view and the numerical synthesis/export comparison (`verify.functional.synthesis`). External MP4 project-open UI (deferred). Old GUID/share links. Server-pixel or legacy API comparison. Byte identity of image files across builds. Full-tensor coverage claims. The expensive encoder lab check on every visitor.

## Notes
- Inspect rendered crop/result bounds (all four corners) and decoded full-size output, not only intrinsic sizes (earlier feedback: intrinsic dimensions passed while the displayed face was clipped).
- Never widen tolerances, change precision or replace numerics with a visual spot-check. Other models need their own references (the non-face proof in `verify.packages`).
- Integrated verification checks the final integrated app (after the planned UI and package changes) against the Next baseline (`facemorph.me-classic` branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) plus the plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped. Not historic-API parity and not a shutdown-qualification campaign. Performance and reliability against the control, including control/control noise and the physical iPhone, are judged by the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27), not here. Correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found here are fixed in the owning bead and this bead re-runs. Wording says planned, experimental, implemented or deployed. No weights, secrets, photos or typed inputs in Git.
- Split on 2026-10-24 for swarm size by journey family into three beads, all part of sub-result 1 (app flows) collated by `verify.flows` (fm-35zs): `verify.functional` (this ID, fm-ejwq: words, seeds, names, photo, remove down to one, retained tools), `verify.functional.results` (morph, session walk, results: play/scrub, Save/Share, reopen) and `verify.functional.synthesis` (weighted blend view and the numerical synthesis/export comparison). The harness, interception, manifest and release-artifact rules apply to each bead's own cases.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #integrated-verification, #end-to-end-experience-and-design-fidelity-check, #synthesis-correctness-and-export-quality, #file-sharing-and-export-direction, #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each journey above has a scripted operated case with pass/fail outcome, mapped to rows R04, R05, R08, R09 (online part), R10, R11, R18, R20 (photo-entry part), R21, R22, R26 (single-face part), R46, R47 and defects 5, 7, 8.
- [ ] Name selection shows zero model-host requests and no inference start; picker identity equals typed-name identity, and the `names.static-result` engine-equality result names the same engine and catalogue identity as the release identity record (else R11 engine part `untested`).
- [ ] Word and seed boundary cases (empty, whitespace, 512/513 bytes, pasted, IME; seeds 0, 4,294,967,295, -1, 1.5, 4,294,967,296) each have a recorded outcome.
- [ ] Confirmed crop shows exactly one e4e attempt per confirmation and no repeated detection.
- [ ] Every UI step is operated through the `verify.harness` (fm-48bj) helpers: real pointer/touch at the control's visible position with an `elementFromPoint` assertion that the hit element is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role locators only for setup; phone-width and desktop-width screenshot per case.
- [ ] Every network or consent claim is asserted from intercepted requests by host class and bytes (the request-interception helper from `build.ci-site`, fm-aa8), never from a screenshot; traces and screenshots are kept on failure as privacy-filtered CI artifacts.
- [ ] Every case is listed in this bead's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix rows or defect numbers it grades; a case without a mapping fails manifest validation.
- [ ] All cases ran in the release-verification workflow against the named release artifact digest; a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded `failed` or `untested`, never `passed`.
notes: Split 2026-10-24 by journey family: morph, session-walk and result journeys moved to fm-y2jb (verify.functional.results); blend-view journey and numerical synthesis/export comparison moved to fm-ve73 (verify.functional.synthesis). The harness, interception, manifest and release-artifact criteria are restated per bead for its own cases.

title: Carry over the next-site compiled-ui job against the uploaded artifact bytes
description:
## Background

Classic `next-site.yml` job `compiled-ui` runs on `ubuntu-24.04` after `artifact`: it checks the
uploaded bytes, parses the Python scripts, runs the WebGPU bundle contract gate and drives the actual
artifact in Chromium. Split out of `build.ci-site-lane` (fm-aa8) in polish round 2; fm-aa8 keeps the
workflow file and the `artifact` job.

## Why

The compiled-UI check is the first browser run against the exact uploaded bytes on every candidate
push; it must survive the move without a mock or a rebuilt copy.

## Scope

- Job `compiled-ui` in `.github/workflows/next-site.yml` (`ubuntu-24.04`, `needs: artifact`), job ID
  kept so the required-status name maps one-to-one.
- Steps carried over: fetch `next-site-<sha>` through `.github/actions/fetch-artifact`
  (`build.ci-artifact-lookup`) and `sha256sum -c next-site-SHA256SUMS`; `python3 -m compileall` over
  the retained Python scripts; WebGPU bundle contract gate (`webgpu_contract_test.py`, at its
  destination path from the check-migration map); the actual artifact in Chromium via
  `browser-harness==0.1.8`; evidence artifact `next-artifact-ui-evidence`.
- The Chromium run attaches `scripts/evidence/cdp_capture.py` (`build.event-log-capture`), step IDs
  `build.ci-site-compiled-ui/<job>/<step>`, and uploads through `.github/actions/event-log-upload`.
- Pass thresholds: every step exits 0; zero `third-party` requests in the event log; the artifact
  digest on every log line and in the receipt equals `next-site-SHA256SUMS`.
- Each step has a row in the check-migration map with its destination invocation.

## Out of scope

The `artifact` job and workflow triggers (fm-aa8). The `qualify` job (`build.ci-e2e-cpu-lane`).
The `deploy` job (`deploy.ci-workflow`).

## Considerations

- A workflow definition is not a passing result: record the actual run outcome.
- This repository's lanes never publish `next.facemorph.me` before the source handover.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A recorded `next-site.yml` run shows `compiled-ui` passing on `ubuntu-24.04` against the bytes `artifact` uploaded (same `next-site-SHA256SUMS`), with `next-artifact-ui-evidence` and `e2e-log-next-site-compiled-ui-<run_id>` retained.
- [ ] The event log validates with `check-event-log`, carries the `next-site-SHA256SUMS` digest on every line, and `assertNoRequests(log, 'third-party', whole run)` passes.
- [ ] A seeded run with one byte changed after upload fails at `sha256sum -c` (recorded run), and a seeded broken `webgpu_contract_test.py` expectation fails the gate.
- [ ] Every classic `compiled-ui` step appears in the check-migration map with its destination invocation; none is silently dropped.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Fix the candidate Remove control so a person can remove a face
description:
## Background
Edits to the candidate source are ordinary work on the working candidate and need no separate approval (operator, 18 October). They are made on a non-deploying classic branch (e.g. `delivery/candidate-edits`) branched from `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, and merged only after the ordinary qualification via `delivery.candidate-edits-merge`, because the candidate branch publishes to next.facemorph.me on every qualified push. Run commands in `facemorph.me-classic` per its development guide. Defect 1: each face's Remove control is meant as a close button top right of its image; the component library's button style wins the specificity tie, so the control sits in normal flow below the image, clipped and invisible, dark grey, over the mode-menu button. A real click at its position opens 'Change mode' and removes nothing; candidate checks pass because they click by accessible name. Evidence at 1,280 px with two faces: control 32×32 at (201, 611), image 376×376 at (206, 229). Injecting one rule that nests the style under the image put it inside the image top right; a real click (desktop) and a real tap (390 px) each removed exactly one face (tried live; nothing deployed).

## Why
People cannot remove faces on next.facemorph.me today.

## Scope
- One CSS rule in `src/Next/product-ux.scss` nesting the Remove style under the image container.
- A candidate operated test that clicks/taps at the visible position.

## Out of scope
Many-face layout, bulk remove, Undo/Start over, 44 px target size (face controls in the monorepo).

## Considerations
The control stays 32 px (under the 44 px comfortable size); record that as a known limitation for the face-controls workstream rather than widening this edit.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Operated UI acceptance: real pointer and real touch at the control's visible position, with an `elementFromPoint` assertion that the hit element is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role clicks only for setup; repeating controls exercised at 1, 2, 3, many and the cap; text inputs with empty, very long and pasted values; a phone-width (390 px) and a desktop-width (1,280 px) screenshot per case.
- [ ] Real click on desktop and real tap at 390 px each remove exactly one face; `elementFromPoint` at the control centre is the Remove button inside the image box; cases 2, 3 and many faces; the last face's rule unchanged.
- [ ] The end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, retains the log as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics), and every network claim is asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt `docs/receipts/delivery-edit-remove-control.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime/model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Prove eris Firefox cells on real journeys and correct the lab status record
description:
## Goal
The lab's eris-firefox-cpu and eris-firefox-webgpu adapters (fm-qa3q) are committed but the monorepo guide still claims the lab has no eris Firefox adapter. Prove both cells on real journeys and make the recorded status match reality.

## Scope
- Run operated, cold-face and warm-face on eris-firefox-cpu and eris-firefox-webgpu.
- Record launcher, version, WebGPU adapter admission and route verdicts per cell.
- Correct the stale no-Firefox-adapter claim in AGENTS.md to the proven state.

title: Move cache, shard store and manifest into the manager; local-only reads
description:
## Goal
Make `packages/browser-model-manager` the owner of model-cache, shard-store, SHA-256 and manifest logic, first as an isomorphic move with no behaviour change, then with verified-local-only reads and typed invalidation on both OPFS and Cache Storage. Warming and offline execution need zero model-network requests including repair; the candidate's cache handles can repair over the network, and a network-repair-capable handle must never be exposed as an offline capability. "Loaded" means verified and ready for offline operations.

## Scope
- Move `src/Next/Assets/model-cache.mjs`, `Assets/shard-store.mjs`, `Assets/sha256.mjs` and manifest parsing into the package as strict TS with declaration output (the package is an empty, building, packable placeholder after workspace build milestone 1).
- Keep storage keys, digests, URL-independent pinned reuse, per-read SHA, exact-length buffers and migration without duplicate storage.
- Classic facts to preserve (frozen import revision, read-only): `MODEL_CACHE_NAME = 'checkface-model-blobs-v1'` (never app-versioned or age-purged), `validateAsset`, `CHUNK_RETRY_DELAYS_MS = [1000, 4000, 10000, 20000]`, `RUNTIME_MIRROR = 'https://models.facemorph.me'` and `runtimeMirror()` (present from candidate commit `6107f80`; absent at `b2d945a8`), `PROGRESS_INTERVAL_BYTES = 1 MiB`, `createRecordAccess`, `createModelCache` (`readShards`/`openVerified` with `allowRepair`), `createBrowserModelCache` (`openShardStore({readOnly})`), `storageStatus`.
- Leave a re-export shim at the old `src/Next/Assets/` paths so `product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are not edited here (their consumers move under compute extraction in the shared-file order).
- Carry `Assets/model-cache.test.mjs` with unchanged expectations.
- Then add verified-local-only access (for example `allowRepair:false`) on both backends, with typed cache-miss, corruption and eviction errors.
- Disk presence or an unchecked peek never bypasses digest validation.
- Constructing the manager and reading status or capabilities trigger no acquisition.
- Bounded lazy local reads remain (streamed e4e may read verified shards lazily); never load all encoder shards into RAM.

## Out of scope
- New semantics during the move step.
- Acquisition (`manager.acquisition`). Acquisition budgeting (`src/Next/browser/acquisition-budget.mjs` + test) moves with `manager.acquisition`, not here.

## Notes
- Shared-file serialization (decided 16/17 October): `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in the order provider simplification -> typed facade -> compute extraction -> confirmed-crop fix -> morph pipeline -> static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics reporting rebinding. This bead does not edit them (shim).

title: Per-operation and per-resource admission with early refusal reasons
description:
## Background
The candidate emits `route-admitted`/`route-rejected` progress, probes the GPU adapter before GPU acquisition (`navigator.gpu` alone once caused about 180 MiB of wasted Simulator downloads), and the pinned overlay has `encoderStream.phoneAdmitted:true` with a 268,435,456-byte e4e WASM limit (scope `friends-and-family-candidate`, `ios-simulator` evidence, not physical/release qualified).

## Why
Admit Generate, photo encoding and Morph by actual capabilities, never by phone/desktop labels, viewport width or touch; a missing WebGPU adapter alone never makes the app unsupported.

## Scope
- Admission per operation/provider from capabilities, memory and qualified runtime/model evidence; generator admission does not establish encoder/codec support.
- Probe adapters before GPU-only acquisition; absence/failure selects the qualified CPU route.
- A known-ineligible operation stops before its detector/model network or crop work, with a short reason for the owning action (`.next-tile-status` or `.next-morph-reason`); other supported operations stay usable; static names and completed files remain model-free.
- Bounded CPU fallback on actual GPU admission/execution failure as a declared transition; material slowdown or extra assets go through the existing revised decision; no native fallback; no racing alternative downloads; healthy slow GPU not demoted.
- Capture requested/actual providers, model and authorization scope per intent (events consumed by ws:opctl).
- Preserve quick product admission separately from full lab numerical checks (no 20 s+ encoder guard on startup).

## Out of scope
Consent modal (ws:consent); device timing check (ws:device); scheduler (ws:opctl).

## Considerations
Shared-file serialization (decided 16/17 October): `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in the order provider simplification -> typed facade -> compute extraction -> confirmed-crop fix -> morph pipeline -> static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics reporting rebinding. Add any file this item edits to the check-migration map's conflict list.

## Requested versus actual route reporting (polish r1)
Each admitted or refused operation emits one typed event carrying: operation (face/photo-encode/morph), requested route (`auto`|`cpu`|`webgpu`), actual provider, fallback taken (none or `gpu-failure-to-cpu` with the stage), refusal reason code, model/runtime identity and authorization scope. The candidate already reports `requestedProvider` and `provider` (`reporting.mjs` ~273; `route-report.test.mjs` "Route facts reach the collector and survive its allowlist"); keep those fields and allowlist entries, and add any new field to the reporting allowlist and privacy text list for `ws:diag` in the same revision. The UI shows the actual route only in the owning action or beside the selector (rendering is face controls'); this leaf supplies the data and the short reason strings' keys (the copy itself is `provider.guidance-copy`).

## Boundary with face controls (`face.provider-selector`, fm-5kpx) (polish r1)
- **Provider simplification owns:** WebGL execution removal and saved-preference migration; the choice semantics behind the selector (Auto = fixed failure-only WebGPU -> CPU preference filtered by real admission; explicit CPU and explicit WebGPU stay meaningful; measured timings inform guidance, never automatic ranking; a healthy slow GPU route is never demoted); requested-versus-actual route capture and reporting (per intent, in operation events and in `reporting.mjs`/`analytics.mjs` fields such as `requestedProvider` and `provider`); bounded CPU fallback as a declared transition; per-operation admission and refusal reasons; Help and guidance copy, including the `#computer-requirements` / supported-browsers Help sections the selector's optional links open; native retirement.
- **Face controls owns (`face.provider-selector`):** rendering the compact Auto/CPU/WebGPU selector above the first insertion +, removing the More options -> Advanced entry, showing the candidate's recommendation and actual-route explanation beside it from the data this workstream exposes, and the selector's operated UI acceptance.
- No provider leaf moves, restyles or re-places the selector, and `face.provider-selector` changes no route semantics. Until the move lands, the ported Advanced selector (`migration.ren-morph-video`) shows Auto/CPU/WebGPU with these semantics.

## Refusal reasons are accessible data (polish r2)
Each refusal emits a reason key plus its plain sentence (copy owned by `provider.guidance-copy`) and a Help anchor. Face controls renders this as readable text tied to the disabled control (visible status text or `aria-describedby`), never a hover-only tooltip. This leaf's event and type contract makes that possible: the reason is a string in the state, not only a CSS state. Raw runtime exception text never enters the reason field. A test feeds a thrown `Error('WebGPU device lost: ...')` and asserts the emitted reason is a known key.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests with mocked capabilities: null adapter, insufficient limits, failed canary, device loss, encoder-unavailable-but-generator-admitted; each yields the right per-operation result and no acquisition for refused routes.
- [ ] Network-log test: refused route issues zero detector/model requests.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, and the log is retained as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics). Network claims are asserted from the log, never from screenshots.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic are listed in the destination test discovery (no unlisted test files) and pass in CI.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/provider/admission.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Event-shape tests: requested route, actual provider, fallback and refusal reason present for each of the five mocked capability cases; reporting allowlist test accepts the fields and still parses historical `webgl` values.
- [ ] E2E (Playwright, CPU lane, mocked null adapter): Auto -> CPU face completes; the event log shows requested `auto`, actual `cpu`, zero GPU asset requests by host class.
- [ ] Refusal events/state carry `reasonKey`, plain text and Help anchor for every refusal case; a thrown raw runtime error maps to a known key (test); the type makes a reason mandatory whenever an action is disabled for a capability reason.
notes:
Plan anchors: PLAN.md#provider-simplification; #web-release-and-desktop-package-retirement--12-october-2026; #clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation; #autoresearch-coverage-and-preservation-map (Phone/iPhone preservation contract).

title: Reproduce the crop-confirm loop as a failing built-UI test
description:
## Goal
The plan requires reproducing the confirmed-crop failure in the actual built UI before fixing it. Today a manually confirmed crop is pushed back through face detection, and a crop the detector cannot re-find loops back to the crop prompt instead of encoding. This row lands right after candidate import, before compute extraction, as tracked expected-to-fail tests that `crop.fix` flips.

## Scope
- Mechanism to trace and document: the photo path calls `alignPhoto` with `requireSingleFace=true` (`src/Next/photo/align-photo.mjs`), rejecting any result with `faceCount !== 1`, a `facePolicy` other than `exactly-one-face-v1`, or (with `tryAlign`) no alignment, with `MULTIPLE_FACES_MESSAGE` ("Choose a clear photo containing exactly one face."). In `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` (around line 405) a job failure matching `No face was found|More than one face was found` sets `cropFace` for the target, reopening crop. `chooseDetectedFace`/`cropPhotoReported` build the crop with `cropPhoto` (`photo/crop.mjs`). Worker provenance (`preprocessingSha256` vs `manifest.alignmentSha256`) is checked in the bridge. Also trace `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `photo-runtime/align-photo.mjs`.
- Note the 25 MB limit in `align-photo.mjs` versus the 64 MiB compressed limit in `photo/crop.mjs` (crop.fix uses this).
- Failure analysis with file/line references at the imported revision, as a header comment in the failing test, so `crop.fix` can read it.
- Failing built-UI e2e against the pinned control artifact (`deploy-next/`) with a forced detection/alignment failure after crop confirmation (a fixture where redetection fails on the confirmed crop, plus a detector-failure hook present only in test builds), asserting the intended behaviour: one real e4e attempt, no crop reopen.
- Failing bridge-level unit tests for the same cases.
- Tests marked expected-to-fail (tracked, linked to this bead) so CI stays green until the fix flips them.
- Fixtures: no-face, multi-face, oriented, non-square, malformed, redetection-fails-on-confirmed-crop; synthetic or licensed images only, never personal photos.

## Out of scope
The fix, the preprocessing policy and batch flows (crop.fix, crop.queue).

## Notes
- Uses the contracts' preprocessing section only as reference; needs nothing from compute extraction. Compute extraction carries these tests across when it moves code.
- Must not edit `product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` or `browser/ort-worker.mjs`: failing tests and the analysis only.
- Until `migration.rendering` the e2e runs against the control-labelled `deploy-next/`; afterwards against the Vite-built ported UI, which carries the candidate loop (parity) and keeps failing for the same documented reason until `crop.fix` lands; the bridge-level tests flip in `crop.fix` and the built-UI test flips in `crop.ported-app`.

title: Route eligible confirmed crops straight to e4e without redetection
description:
## Background
See `ws:crop.repro` for the failure mechanism (exactly-one-face check after confirmation; bridge reopens crop on detection errors). After compute extraction the photo orchestration lives in `stylegan-js`, and the bridge/runtime/worker files are next in the shared-file order.

## Why
Locked requirement (alignment-failure reference): an eligible confirmed crop must proceed to e4e without another successful detection or a repeated crop loop.

## Scope
- Before confirmation: run detector-driven alignment/warping to propose a crop and display that proposal; multi-face selection precedes confirmation.
- After OK: apply only the frozen policy to approved pixels and call e4e directly; no redetect/rewarp; optional validation may log but cannot change pixels or block.
- Remove the post-confirmation exactly-one-face requirement and the error-text-driven crop reopen; detector/alignment failure after confirmation never reopens crop; only an explicit Adjust Crop starts another adjustment.
- Not-run detector (assets refused/absent) is not labelled a detection failure; refusing detector assets keeps manual crop usable and starts no downloads.
- Preserve cancellation and input revisions; Cancel before confirmation abandons preparation without e4e or extra keypoints.
- Flip the repro tests to passing.

## Out of scope
Crop modal/editor visuals (face controls). Multi-selection UI (face controls). Consent modal (acquisition consent).

## Considerations
- e4e can produce odd reconstructions for unaligned crops; that warning does not forbid the direct route. Malformed/unsupported pixels still fail clearly.
- Shared-file serialization (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in the order provider simplification -> typed facade -> compute extraction -> confirmed-crop fix -> morph pipeline -> static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics reporting rebinding. Add every file this item edits to the check-migration map's conflict list. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.

## Properties this item must make testable (polish r1)
- **No re-detect or re-warp after OK.** After the `crop-confirmed` event the bridge, runtime and worker make zero calls to the detector, `alignPhoto`, alignment or warp code. Test with spies on those entry points and with event-log counts (`detect`, `align`, `warp` events after `crop-confirmed` = 0). Optional validation, if kept, emits only `crop.validate` and cannot change `tensorDigest` or block.
- **Exactly one e4e attempt or an actionable error.** An eligible confirmed crop produces exactly one `e4e.attempt-start` (with its attempt ID) ending in `e4e.result` or exactly one terminal error from a closed set (`unsupported-pixels`, `over-limit`, `encoder-unavailable`, `encoder-invalidated`, `cancelled`), each with plain recovery text. Zero attempts without an error, or a second attempt without an explicit Retry, fails the test.

title: Typed loaded handles with leases; port one provider adapter
description:
## Goal
Give the engine a loaded-handle capability that cannot acquire more files, backed by reference-counted leases so manager deletion or eviction cannot pull assets from under a running operation, and port one candidate provider adapter onto it. This completes the manager loaded-handles milestone that compute extraction waits for (compute moves only engine-side orchestration and consumes the manager's adapter, so the two workstreams never claim the same code) and that acquisition consent builds on.

## Scope
- Loaded-handle type per the contracts milestone 1 contract (ownership, digests, shapes, mapping/synthesis/encoder); loaded handles identify actual providers, admission and validation state.
- Reference-counted leases on required verified local assets; manager-controlled deletion/eviction excludes leased assets.
- Browser eviction, corruption, cross-tab deletion or device/worker loss invalidates the capability with a typed error; affected operations settle and release without network repair.
- Disposal releases leases and sessions; reacquisition/re-admission happen outside engine execution through app policy.
- Port one provider adapter from the candidate: the one compute extraction needs first (for example the generator ORT session adapter); state the choice in the PR. The adapter owns shard reads and bounded session lifecycle. Candidate encoder: 108 sequential ORT sessions, streamed, single-threaded, bounded; generator: CPU/WebGPU ORT and direct WebGPU sessions.
- Preserve acquisition/create/run attribution timings (verified read, session create, run, total; WASM/max-live-session facts).
- Typed stage/timing hooks await actual inference/readback completion (including GPU `mapAsync`), never submission time.

## Out of scope
- Remaining adapters (follow under compute extraction or later manager work).
- Quota, eviction policy and extra backends (`manager.quota`; they do not gate compute).

## Notes
- Leases constrain manager behaviour, not the browser's ability to reclaim storage.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#model-manager-extraction (First milestone); #browser-model-manager; #consented-downloads-useful-overlap-and-cached-model-warming (browser-model-manager leases); #package-and-operation-contracts (timing hooks).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Test: a leased asset survives manager eviction.
- [x] Test: cross-tab deletion invalidates the handle with a typed error; affected operation settles and releases with zero network requests.
- [x] Test: dispose releases all leases and sessions (leak check).
- [x] The ported adapter passes the disposal, lease and invalidation tests.
- [x] The adapter runs a real synthesis and produces canary-identical output to the candidate path on CPU (required); GPU under lease or reported untested in the PR.
- [x] Test: timing hooks fire on inference/readback completion, not submission.
- [x] All unit tests are listed in the destination test discovery and pass in CI.

title: Record the acceptance receipt for the diagnostics learnings ingestion
description:
## Background
Implemented 18 October: a read-only pass over the whole `runs/` prefix of R2 bucket `facemorph-diagnostics`
(801 objects, 5.2 MB, uploaded 22 September to 17 October 08:02 UTC; 12,057 events, 309 runs, 22 devices) produced the
committed note `docs/findings/diagnostics-learnings-2026-10-18.md` in this repository (commit `7875aaf`, "Record what
the consented debug reports show (aggregates only)"), with aggregates only and key-list digest
`c3833f1f056ae0700e82d997a592e9009114d014a7b1ce8ae21c45cd8c07e0fb` (SHA-256 of the sorted keys, one per line, trailing
newline as recorded in the note). Findings already folded into the plan: typed failure causes (`diag.typed-failure-causes`)
and iPhone cache capacity (`provider.phone-cpu-check`, `consent.modal`). The read script itself was not committed; the
note states the read used "a read-only listing and per-object get; nothing was written to the bucket".

This leaf is the **automated precondition** of `diag.old-report-deletion`, which is overdue (the earliest reports
passed 30 days on 22 October). It has no prerequisite and is ready now.

## Why
PLAN.md#acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance (diagnostics learnings): the note is aggregates only, a scripted
scan finds no device, session or run identifiers, and the read used a read-only credential and wrote nothing. The
deletion may run only after that is verified and receipted.

## Scope
1. **Identifier scan script** `scripts/diagnostics/scan-learnings-note.mjs` (standalone Node 22, no workspace
   dependencies), committed with fixtures. It fails (non-zero exit, offending line numbers printed, matched text
   redacted) on: UUIDs; hex runs of 16+ characters other than the allowlisted key-list digest; base64/base64url runs
   of 20+ characters; R2 keys (`runs/` followed by an ID); IPv4/IPv6 addresses; email addresses; user-agent strings
   with build numbers; any string that matches one of the bucket's run IDs (the script optionally takes
   `--keys-from-bucket` to list current run IDs with a read-only token, held in memory only, never written).
   Run it on the note at commit `7875aaf` and at HEAD. If it finds an identifier: redact the note in a new commit,
   re-run, and record the redaction in the receipt.
2. **Read-only and no-write evidence**, recorded truthfully:
   - The credential used on 18 October is established from the session record (Cass search of the 18 October
     mining session for the command lines, e.g. `cf r2 objects list/get --bucket-name facemorph-diagnostics`) and its
     scope from the token/OAuth grant metadata (`cf user tokens list` or the Cloudflare API token-verify call; scope
     names only, never values). If it was not a read-only-scoped credential, the receipt says so under deviations.
   - No-write evidence independent of the credential: a fresh listing with a **read-only** token (R2 "Object Read"
     scoped to bucket `facemorph-diagnostics`, created for this check with `cf user tokens create` and revoked after,
     token ID recorded) shows that the sorted keys of all objects uploaded at or before 2026-10-17 08:02:59 UTC hash
     to `c3833f1f…e0fb`, that their count is 801, and that every one of those objects' `uploaded` time is unchanged
     from the mined window (none on or after 18 October, so none was rewritten by the read). This listing is kept in
     memory only.
3. **Receipt** `docs/receipts/diagnostics/learnings-ingest.md` with the schema fields plus: note path and commit,
   scan script commit and result at `7875aaf` and HEAD, credential scope finding (or deviation), the read-only
   re-listing result (count 801, digest match yes/no, latest uploaded time), the token ID used and its revocation
   time. No keys, run IDs or report contents.
4. A small receipt-lint script `scripts/receipts/check-receipt.mjs` (shared with the deletion) that fails when a
   receipt lacks any schema field; the deletion script calls it on this receipt as a precondition.

## Out of scope
Re-mining; requirement changes beyond those already folded in; the deletion itself.

## Considerations
Status: the ingestion is implemented (18 October); this leaf records verification. No human approval step: scan,
re-listing and receipt run unattended; a failed check stops here and is reported, it does not wait for a person.
Tokens are created and revoked by the script through the logged-in `cf` CLI (as for the CI deploy token), never
stored in Git or logs.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** It adds standalone scripts under `scripts/diagnostics/` and `scripts/receipts/` and a receipt; it edits no app source. It must stay unordered with respect to the shared-file chain (PLAN.md 17 October: the names data-shape spike, generator and publication, and the diagnostics learnings ingestion, edit none of these files): never add an edge from this bead to ws:migration.facade, ws:compute, ws:crop or ws:morph. If implementation finds it must edit one of them after all, it first runs `br dep add fm-fk5m fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph), adds the file to the conflict list in fm-bhw and records the change in its receipt (the plan's rule: an edge is added when an edit is discovered).

- [ ] `scripts/diagnostics/scan-learnings-note.mjs` committed with unit tests over fixtures (each identifier class detected; the allowlisted key-list digest not flagged; matched text redacted in output); the scan passes on the note at `7875aaf` and at HEAD (or a redaction commit exists and the scan passes on it).

title: Verified-local-only reads with typed invalidation across OPFS and Cache Storage

Acquisition (later leaf).

title: Acquisition primitives
description:
## Goal
The manager supplies acquisition primitives (grant enforcement, priority classes, aggregate buffer budget, shared fetch ownership, bounded retries with alternate-origin fallback); consent and priorities are app policy. Acquisition authorization is a bounded grant over manifest identity, route, purpose, required asset digests and remaining-byte scope, owned by the app.

## Scope
- Acquire only under a supplied grant; revalidation never inflates the approved budget; out-of-scope assets need a revised grant.
- No download before authorization; an output-cache hit avoids download.
- Priority classes: foreground-required outranks optional preparation.
- Aggregate transfer/read-ahead/hash/write-buffer budget across workers (the two-chunk per-worker read-ahead is not an aggregate bound); digest deduplication.
- Shared fetch ownership: the fetch stops when the last authorized owner leaves; ownership transfer; verified chunks kept for retry.
- Bounded retry of transient chunk failures. Retry delays stay `CHUNK_RETRY_DELAYS_MS = [1000, 4000, 10000, 20000]` ms unless contracts milestone 2 freezes different numbers.
- Alternate origin is package configuration: `alternateOrigins: string[]`, default empty. Retries alternate between primary and alternate in classic's order, stay inside the grant's byte scope, and an alternate-origin byte counts against the same budget.
- Classic `RUNTIME_MIRROR` / `runtimeMirror()` becomes application configuration: the app passes `https://models.facemorph.me` only when the page host is `facemorph.me` or `*.facemorph.me` (classic's scoping), so a local harness or another host never contacts it. The second origin was added after an edge returned HTTP 500 on 20 October and is present in the frozen import revision (`6107f80` or later).
- Move `src/Next/browser/acquisition-budget.mjs` (+ `acquisition-budget.test.mjs`) into the package.

## Out of scope
- Consent UI and Cancel semantics (consent workstream); warming policy.

## Notes
- Aggregate limits are frozen in contracts milestone 2; until then the budget is "measured, no threshold".
- Classic sources (read-only): `src/Next/browser/acquisition-budget.mjs`, `model-cache.mjs` retry schedule and `RUNTIME_MIRROR`/`runtimeMirror()` (from candidate commit `6107f80`).
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#model-manager-extraction; #browser-model-manager; #consented-downloads-useful-overlap-and-cached-model-warming; #gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design (acquisition grant); #cloudflare-model-host (second origin).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Real-network test (request log on a real local server): no request without a grant.
- [x] Test: over-scope asset refused without a revised grant; revalidation does not inflate the budget.
- [x] Test: two owners share one fetch; last-owner cancel stops the fetch within the bound; ownership transfer keeps verified chunks.
- [x] Test: transient 500 retried on the `[1000, 4000, 10000, 20000]` ms schedule (real timers, against a real local server that fails and then recovers), then the alternate origin in classic order within grant scope.
- [x] Test: corrupt chunk rejected and refetched only under the grant.
- [x] Test: with no alternate origin configured, zero requests leave the primary origin.
- [x] App-config test: `models.facemorph.me` is used only for `facemorph.me`/`*.facemorph.me` page hosts; a localhost run makes zero requests to it.
- [x] Test: foreground-required work outranks optional preparation; aggregate budget holds across workers; identical digests are fetched once.
- [x] Test: output-cache hit issues zero downloads.
- [x] Carried `acquisition-budget.test.mjs` passes; all unit tests listed in test discovery and pass locally with the CI command; CI verifies after push.
- [x] Field requirement (diagnostics learnings, 18 October: 3 of 6 cold full-package downloads did not finish): a cold full-package acquisition on the device lab's phone and eris cells completes, and a real mid-download network interruption resumes without re-fetching verified chunks.
- [x] budgets cite frozen ceilings (with fm-fy2.2). If fm-fy2.2 has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-fy2.2 (`br update fm-fy2.2 --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-fy2.2
- [x] Field requirement (fm-vf9l device lab, 24 October): a chunk attempt that receives no byte for the stall bound (classic CHUNK_STALL_MS, 30 s) is abandoned and retried like a dropped connection (real local server that goes silent mid-body, no reset); the per-asset deadline counts silence, not size, so a big asset on a slow but steady link completes

title: repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor (epic)
description:
## Goal
Finish the sustainable FaceMorph replacement. Carry the working on-device Next candidate (`facemorph.me-classic`
branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, live at
https://next.facemorph.me) into this strict-TypeScript monorepo; keep its features and every integrated performance
optimization; apply the plan's declared changes; and, on the operator's decision, retire hosted Triton inference and
the hosted API (`api.facemorph.me`, `checkface.facemorph.me`). Deliver a clearer repository, independently usable
packages (`stylegan-js`, `browser-model-manager`, `cloudflare-model-host`, the `model-conv` container), a reproducible
frozen classic Docker distribution, repaired photo encoding (the confirmed crop goes straight to e4e) and simpler
face controls. This epic is the implementer's entry point to the consolidated graph (roughly 130 beads after the 24 October
2026 consolidation; `br count` gives the live number). It is navigation, not work.

## Scope
**What done means**
- **Architecture complete:** the monorepo app, the packages and the classic distribution work for their documented
  capabilities. Proof is the CI-generated release summary from `verify.join` (fm-fy2.11) on one named release
  artifact digest, plus the classic clean-clone acceptance on the wound-down tree (`winddown.tree`, fm-b1x).
  Repository setup alone proves nothing.
- **The app:** the candidate's features and journeys, plus the locked crop design, ordered multi-face selection, the
  inference-free static names picker, paste, Share/Save/format/filename, consented downloads with synthesis-first
  overlap, device estimates, anchored debug-report consent, a many-face layout with a Remove control a person can hit
  (no fixed face count; only real resource budgets limit it, with a plain message), and the weighted face blend as an advanced view (24 October). Web only (native desktop packages
  retired); browser CPU/WebGPU selector, bounded CPU fallback and phone/iPhone paths kept; WebGL execution removed.
  Phones are first-class.
- **Strictly not worse than the candidate** (operator, 24 October): before the next.facemorph.me handover and the
  facemorph.me promotion, the paired lab gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27, run on the lanes and control/control noise
  from `verify.not-worse-lanes`, fm-0q4h) shows the release no slower, heavier or less reliable than the pinned
  candidate artifact on every platform class, physical iPhone included; an untested or inconclusive cell blocks its
  class. After the handover, anonymous real-visitor statistics (`diag.usage-stats`, fm-5yqq;
  `verify.field-not-worse`, fm-js8i) confirm it per platform class, with rollback to the candidate available until
  they do.
- **Changeover statistics:** the stats Worker (`services/stats/`), the Prometheus scrape job and the "FaceMorph before
  and after" Grafana dashboard (`ops/grafana/`) already exist in this repository; the app carries the candidate's
  anonymous sink with a Usage statistics switch.
- **Classic** ends as the self-host Docker distribution plus its Git history; development and autoresearch live here.
  Its success criterion: clone, `docker compose up`, everything builds, and a complete local CheckFace runs with the
  NVIDIA GPU passed through on current GPU generations (compute capability 7.0-12.x, driver 570 or newer; an
  unsupported GPU gets one plain message naming it), proven by the README-executed clean-clone acceptance
  (`classic.acceptance`, fm-fy2.16), re-run on the wound-down tree.
- **Delivery** (candidate-source handover, production promotion, API retirement, package publication, classic
  publication) is a set of separate actions. The production pushes (promotion, API retirement, and the optional
  early promotion of the retained candidate) each run only after the operator authorizes them through `gate.cutover`;
  package and classic publication need no decision. No action's completion is inferred from another. Promotion may happen earlier from the working
  candidate. October 25 is aspirational; no date or score triggers it.
- **Package acceptance** happens only after publication, by an independent reviewer using the registry
  (`pkgaccept.review`, fm-fy2.21).
- Research (stage 1/2, the optional evaluator) completes on its own and is not a release prerequisite.

**How to pick work**
1. Read the repository `AGENTS.md` and `README.md` (PLAN.md is frozen background, not the authority), run `git status`, search earlier feedback with Cass
   (`cass search ... --robot`). Preserve other sessions' edits. No worktrees, reset or clean; separate clones only
   for read-only runs.
2. Implementation began 24 October 2026. Non-gate work is claimable; this navigation epic stays deferred. One agent operates directly outside NTM until the operator changes mode. Skip Agent Mail in solo mode and use AGENT_MAIL_GUARD_MODE=warn on commits AND pushes.
3. Pick work with `br ready --exclude-label gate` (full ready set, highest priority first; `--limit 10` for a short
   list, `--format json` for scripts, `-l ws-<name>` to stay in one workstream) or `bv --robot-next` (single best pick)
   and `bv --robot-plan` (parallel tracks and what each unblocks). `bv` robot modes ignore assignees and can list a
   gate: skip any bead labelled `gate`. Never run bare `bv` (interactive screen).
4. Workstreams are labels, not beads: `ws-identity`, `ws-rename`, `ws-inventory`, `ws-import`, `ws-contracts`,
   `ws-build`, `ws-currency`, `ws-ortweb`, `ws-research`, `ws-manager`, `ws-hosting`, `ws-conversion`, `ws-classic`,
   `ws-deploy`, `ws-provider`, `ws-migration`, `ws-opctl`, `ws-compute`, `ws-media`, `ws-crop`, `ws-morph`,
   `ws-consent`, `ws-device`, `ws-face`, `ws-names`, `ws-diag`, `ws-domain`, `ws-delivery`, `ws-pkgdocs`,
   `ws-pkgaccept`, `ws-verify`, `ws-winddown`. There are no parent, workstream or milestone beads. A "milestone"
   (contracts m1/m2, build m1, migration freeze/facade/controller/rendering/parity, research s1/s2 ...) is the bead
   that completes it. Each bead's `external_ref` is `plan:<key>`.
5. With every bead opened, the day-one ready set is the beads with no needs: `identity.map` (fm-a4b),
   `names.spike` (fm-zg31) and `diag.learnings` (fm-xgww, the old-report deletion follows its ingest inside the same
   bead). `identity.map` then opens rename, the import and surfaces inventories and domain actions; import, build
   scaffold and contracts milestone 1 follow, and conversion starts after contracts milestone 1. Check this against
   `bv --robot-plan` rather than trusting the list.
6. Claim with `br update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <you>`; read the whole bead with `br show <id>`. Beads are
   self-contained and are the execution authority: where a bead and PLAN.md differ, the bead wins, and PLAN.md anchors in
   Notes are provenance only. A scope change is made in the affected beads (`br update`), never only in PLAN.md; an
   operator decision is also recorded once in the plan's dated decisions table.
7. Respect ordering edges. `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited
   in one order only: provider simplification (`provider.*`), typed facade (`migration.facade`), compute extraction
   (`compute.*`), confirmed-crop fix (`crop.fix`), morph pipeline (`morph.*`), `media.session`, then static-names picker bridge edits
   (`names.static-result`) and diagnostics bridge edits (`diag.disclosure`, `diag.rebinding`). Face-controls work touching those files follows
   the morph pipeline. Never edit them from two beads at once; a bead that discovers it must edit one adds the
   ordering edge (`br dep add`) before editing. The tail of the chain (`face.batch`, `names.static-result`,
   `diag.disclosure`, `diag.rebinding`, `consent.warming`) all follows `media.session` but is not ordered internally;
   those beads serialize their edits to these files with an exclusive Agent Mail file reservation held for the whole edit.
8. Local-first loop (operator, 25 October, hand-driven revision): build and test the affected behavior before pushing, with proportional real browser/GPU/phone checks. Versioned hooks check exact staged/pushed format/lint only; no whole-lane local Actions interpreter. Tick only executed acceptance and close completed ordinary work on local evidence, then flush Beads, commit own paths/hunks and push main. Never wait for CI to close or start useful work. main.yml finishes the current run and retains only the newest pending push, selecting cumulative changes since last green. Inspect CI once at startup; diagnose real failures and explicitly update/reopen responsible beads with logs and a repair acceptance item. Automatic CI reopening is not implemented. Hosted Android/iOS/macOS/Windows lanes are currently release-only; physical phone checks are local, never CI. No indefinite watching, mandatory automated bisection or forced pane restart. Full release qualification below is unchanged.
9. Release manager: the hat worn by whichever agent takes the release bead (`delivery.handover`, fm-s3o) when the rest
   of the release's beads are done; there is no standing release-manager agent. That agent runs the full local
   validation (every plan flow, the strictly-not-worse gate, the four lab cells, the hosted lanes), then deploys; a real
   failure stops the release and passes the affected beads back, and an unavailable device is recorded as untested.
   It prepares, and never makes, the operator's cutover decision.

**Validation approach (after the 24 October ceremony cut)**
1. Tests for the bead's own logic, named in its acceptance, run by the workspace test command. **No fakes** (operator,
   24 October): no mocks, stubs, test doubles, fake clocks or timers, mocked browser APIs, or recorded responses replayed
   as proof. Pure decision logic takes time, capabilities and digests as plain values and is tested by calling it;
   anything with I/O runs against the real thing: the real app, engine and worker, real browsers and devices (WebGPU
   disabled at launch for a null adapter, real storage quotas), real temporary Git repositories with a bare remote, a real
   S3-compatible object store run locally (storage scripts speak the S3 API, so R2 is one endpoint, not a dependency of the
   tests), real Prometheus and Grafana containers, and real local HTTP servers with a fault switch (500, truncation,
   corrupt bytes). Planted input files are inputs, not fakes. A case nothing real can produce is reported untested.
2. Static gates in CI: strict TypeScript, read-only Oxc lint/format, contracts as TS modules with type-level tests
   and a limits file, validator fuzzing, identity hashing, and the retired-tests check (`tests/retired.txt`: a removed
   test must be listed with its replacement).
3. Operated end-to-end check for any user-visible behaviour, inside the bead: real pointer/touch at the control's
   visible position plus `elementFromPoint`; repeating controls at 0 or 1, 2, 3, many and, where a real resource limit exists, at that limit and its degraded state (no fixed face or slot count, operator 24 October); text
   inputs empty, very long and pasted; phone-width and desktop-width screenshot per case. Network/consent tests
   intercept requests and assert by host class and bytes, never from a screenshot; traces and screenshots kept on
   failure.
4. Evidence for an ordinary bead is its source commit and executed local checks; CI adds backstop evidence after push. No per-bead receipt files, decision-log
   entries, maps or ledgers.
5. Integrated verification: one release-verification workflow runs the four sub-results (app flows, platform and
   resource, packages and non-face, release artifact and evidence) and the strictly-not-worse gate against one artifact
   digest and writes the release summary (`verify.join`).
6. The operator's cutover decision, then each authorized delivery action with its post-delivery smoke check (app
   loads, a diagnostics report is accepted, models load).
7. After publication: independent published-package review.

Pass rule everywhere: a check passes only if it ran on the named artifact and platform and met its stated threshold.
Raw synthesis tolerances never widen (max RGB difference 1 on 0-255, sampled raw float 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001);
exported file bytes may differ. A threshold not yet set (byte ceilings until contracts milestone 2, parity rows until
the flow-matrix freeze, names data-shape bars until the spike, device-estimate and warming thresholds until their
beads) is reported "measured, no threshold", never "passed". Untested and unsupported are recorded as such.

**The single operator gate**
After execution starts, the only operator decision is `gate.cutover` (fm-4gw7): production promotion to
`facemorph.me`, retiring the old API, and the optional early
promotion of the retained candidate. Package publication goes ahead without a decision (operator, 24 October). Each
live push runs only when a dated row in PLAN.md "Operator decisions (dated)" names it as authorized.
`gate.npm-creds` (fm-0uhh) is an operator-supplied prerequisite for package publication (scope and token), not a
decision. Both are assigned to
`operator`: agents never claim, perform or close them (`br ready --unassigned` also hides them). Everything else is
automated: no time boxes, no per-step approvals, no checkpoints, fallbacks or backports to the old stack. No agent
message is operator consent.

**Where evidence lives**
- Commits and executed local checks, supplemented by CI runs (ordinary beads). Traces, screenshots and test logs are CI artifacts, privacy-filtered
  like diagnostics.
- Two file receipts, because an irreversible action reads them: API retirement (`delivery.api-retirement`, fm-9dz:
  what was removed, with the runbook's commands) and old-report deletion (`diag.learnings`, fm-xgww: count and key-list
  digest).
- The CI-generated release summary (`verify.join`, fm-fy2.11), including the strictly-not-worse gate's verdicts, which
  the cutover decision reads; after the handover, the real-visitor check's scheduled run output.
- Operator decisions: once, in the dated table in PLAN.md (no separate decision log). The requirements drift ledger
  stays in PLAN.md.

## Out of scope
Implementation work itself (the beads). Any blocking edge into or out of this epic. Workstream or milestone join beads.

## Notes
- Graph conventions: edges come only from the plan's Needs column and the mandatory ordering edges; soft preferences
  and Feeds cells are not edges. Never use `parent-child` links (they block in `br` and deadlocked the first graph);
  this epic has no edges of any kind (PLAN.md "Bead size and ceremony"); find work by label and `br ready`. Check the loaded graph with `br dep cycles` and
  `bv --robot-insights`; never assert acyclicity by reading.
- Optional beads (label `optional`, priority 3-4, one deferred bead each): `research.evaluator` (fm-fy2.3),
  `media.extra-formats` (fm-avy4), `consent.warming` (fm-832d). Nothing required waits on them. Planner proposals
  awaiting a veto sit inside their owning bead's acceptance as removable clauses.
- Bead size: one reviewer, one sitting, roughly under 1,500 changed lines excluding pure moves and generated files.
- Background (frozen reference since 24 October, not the authority): PLAN.md sections "Goal and source of direction", "Programme boundaries and finish line",
  "Implementation approach and sequencing", "Decomposition order, size and tracker coverage" (Bead size and ceremony,
  24 October), "Remaining choices, completion and cutover authority". ID `fm-fy2` kept per the 18 October decision
  (rewrite the tracker, keep IDs); the 22 earlier `fm-fy2*` IDs are kept on the beads that absorbed their workstreams.
- Superseded by the 24 October cut: `docs/receipts/` per bead, `docs/decisions/`, the
  structured event-log field convention, the check-migration map, workstream parent beads and "closes when children
  close" rules.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every non-optional bead is closed; each optional bead is closed or dropped with its reason in the close reason.
- [ ] The `verify.join` release summary exists for one named source commit and artifact digest, is `complete`, and lists every unsupported, untested or unclaimed capability and every "measured, no threshold" cell.
- [ ] Classic distribution clean-clone acceptance passes on the wound-down tree (`winddown.tree`), with the GPU passed through on a current GPU generation.
- [ ] The release summary for each promoted monorepo artifact shows the strictly-not-worse gate passed on required local P30 Pro/eris and available hosted classes; unavailable hosted runners/simulators and optional physical-iPhone evidence are explicitly untested/unclaimed with reasons, never passing; the real-visitor check ran its 14- and 28-day comparisons after the handover with no open regression.
- [ ] Each delivery action that happened ran its post-delivery smoke check and cites the PLAN.md decision row that authorized it; the API-retirement receipt exists if the API was retired; no action's completion is inferred from another.
- [ ] The independent published-package review exists for the published versions (or `pkgaccept.review` stays open with named gaps).

- [ ] Candidate handover is live and its required journeys pass against the deployed artifact in all six local CPU/WebGPU cells: eris Chrome, eris Firefox and actual Huawei Chrome, plus normal applicable CI; missing local cells remain incomplete and hosted availability exemptions remain explicit.
