title: Inventory import inputs: allowlist, toolchain, assets, licences, defects
description:
## Goal
Turn source inspection into a reproducible destination build: freeze the committed candidate import revision, export a machine-readable file allowlist from Git objects, and state the toolchain, commands, check inputs, runtime/photo asset acquisition, licences/notices and the candidate's known-defect and declared-change rows that the import, the first checks and the flow-matrix parity spec read. Every later commit and every unresolvable reference becomes a reviewed, owned line instead of a surprise during the first destination check. Makes no remote changes.

## Scope
- **Frozen import revision**: the then-current committed head of classic `candidate/next-delivery-20260916` (on 24 October `6107f80`), never a dirty tree. Reviewed delta from the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, commit by commit (re-read at freeze; any further commit gets a row), with a disposition per changed path (imported / F# specification only / workflow, listed for its re-homing owner / hosting, listed for its owner / excluded). Known rows: `dce7f27` (16 Oct; `src/index.html`, `src/public/og-next.png`: imported); `40c63a9` (18 Oct; retention wording, 4 strings in `src/Next/Product.fs`, live 2026-10-17 20:28:59 UTC: F# specification, not imported); `bacd6e5` (21 Oct; chunk retries in `src/Next/Assets/model-cache.mjs` + test: imported); `6107f80` (21 Oct; second runtime origin `models.facemorph.me`: `hosting/next-mirror/{worker.mjs,worker.test.mjs,wrangler.jsonc}`, Worker over R2 `facemorph-runtime-mirror` with service binding to the site copying only immutable `runtime/{assets,chunks,manifests,photo,encoder-stream}/`; `model-cache.mjs` alternates retries; `reporting.mjs` classifies download failures as `network`; `next-site.yml` test/deploy/warm step: `src/Next/**` imported, workflow step not imported and listed for the deploy workstream).
- `hosting/next-mirror/` gets a row with digests; not part of the `apps/web` closure unless a closure test imports it (then at temporary root path `hosting/next-mirror/`); owner hosting (serving), deploy-and-warm step owner deploy; both take it from this same frozen revision.
- **Allowlist** `import/allowlist.json`: source repo ID 295956585 and commit, source → destination path (under `apps/web`, keeping the `src/Next` structure; temporary root paths for `desktop/runtime.mjs`, required `scripts/` and imported `hosting/` files such as `hosting/next-cloudflare/validation.mjs` imported by `src/Next/reporting.test.mjs`), consumer of each temporary path, sha256. Closure contents per PLAN.md "Candidate source import and bootstrap". Excluded: F# sources (`Product.fs`, `ProjectJson.fs`, `Contracts.fs`, `Runtime.fs`, `ModelAssets.fs`, `Config`, `FancyButton`, `Logos`, `ThemedApp`, `header`), `global.json`, `.config` Fable pins, Webpack config, generated Fable output, `node_modules`, weights/caches, delivery directories, credentials, `.wrangler/` state, any legacy Server/API file.
- **Unresolved imports**: every specifier in imported modules not resolvable in the allowlisted tree, with owner and swap point. Expected exactly one: `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs → ./ProjectJson.fs.js` (Fable output, gitignored `*.fs.js`, in no Git object). Kept byte-identical (no shim, stand-in, Fable output or bridge edit); owner the ProjectJson TS port with round-trip goldens and swap at the typed facade, both in `migration.facade` (fm-pia9). Any other entry blocks the freeze until imported, excluded with reason, or owned. Pre-port checks never load the bridge as an ES module (`fresh-review.test.mjs`, `estimate.test.mjs` evaluate it as text in `node:vm`; `check-progress-copy.mjs` reads text; `build:next` populates `deploy-next/` from the control artifact).
- `scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs` and `src/Next/verify-fable.mjs` consume Fable output: imported as files, marked `not applicable until the port`, never reported passed. Classic CI's separate `check-bridge-imports` step runs before `build:next` and scans zero files (vacuous); the effective run is inside `scripts/build-next.cjs`, so the destination replacement is not modelled on the vacuous step. `verify-fable.mjs`'s assertions seed the ProjectJson acceptance in `migration.facade` (fm-pia9); the bridge-import guarantee passes to strict TS at the typed facade.
- Working-tree overlays listed by owner/digest; uncommitted classic files (currently `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.gitignore`, four `autoresearch/` docs, `desktop/README.md`, `docs/`) excluded with digests. Destination collision list protects `PLAN.md`, entry guides, `.beads/`.
- **Build inputs** (machine-readable beside the allowlist): pinned toolchain and install/build commands with working directories (classic today: Node 22, .NET 5, pinned Fable; `npm run build:next` plus exact-artifact/UI/device harnesses); applicable baseline checks (unit, runtime, bridge-import, exact-artifact) with artifact inputs; the `next-site.yml` job `artifact` check list at the frozen revision, each marked runs on the closure / needs Fable output / needs files left in classic (owner); `hosting/next-mirror/worker.test.mjs` and where it runs after import; control artifact identity and fetch location; runtime/photo asset locations, digests and acquisition/mirror commands, separating mirror/reuse inputs from full-rebuild inputs (ignored `experiment/`, installed ORT/FFmpeg, external `review-artifacts`); model-term/download authorization; the two worker graphs (bundler-emitted app workers vs manifest-pinned hosted runtime workers/modules with transitive WASM/codec/photo siblings) with URLs.
- **Licences and notices**: per imported or published input (app code, packages, converter, model/data: NVIDIA StyleGAN2-ADA, e4e, dlib landmarks, ONNX Runtime, FFmpeg, ...) licence, required notice text, restrictions, provenance; unresolved redistribution rights named; feeds the shipped notices file set.
- **Defect and declared-change tags** live in the parity spec (`migration.freeze`, fm-hn9e: `defect:<n>` with owner), the one machine-readable defect list; no separate `import/defects.json` (24 October ceremony cut). Content, keyed to PLAN.md "Known candidate defects" numbers 1–23, not restating them): evidence class (operated 18 Oct at 390/1,024/1,280/1,920 px for 1–3; source-read for 4–23 per `docs/findings/candidate-audit-2026-10-18.md`), what the port must do, owner workstream and lead bead, early candidate-edit flag (1, 5 and the one-string parts of 20), status `required` / `planner proposal — operator may veto` (3's Undo/Start over, 9, 15's no-network job, 22) / `decided` (23: no preview badge); declared changes (crop-loop repair, static names, provider/WebGL removal, control/progress changes, native retirement); the four open audit questions (old text/seed links, autoplay, plain 50/50 blend, cropper extras) as `open — candidate behaviour kept until answered`. Repair rows are graded against the specification, never frozen as parity. Not reproduced: legacy Universal Analytics tag. Decided: names picker drops search/header/Close/Show more for a floating Back on touch.

## Out of scope
Copying files (import closure); porting ProjectJson; running the build in the monorepo; fixing defects or answering open questions; fixing the candidate notices link (provider guidance copy); surfaces/hosting/native inventory (inventory surfaces).

## Notes
- PLAN.md "Application inventory" (newer) wins over the absorbed beads: no separate `inventory.md` document; the allowlist is `import/allowlist.json`; the defect list is PLAN.md's, so the JSON only carries ids, owners and status for the parity spec. No receipts, no decision-log links.
- D1: no .NET in the monorepo. The frozen revision and the control artifact's source commit should match; if not, list the delta.
- Legacy production's deployed revision stays an explicit uncertainty in the surfaces inventory; it does not block a pinned candidate build. Weights never enter Git.
- Plan: #application-inventory, #candidate-source-import-and-bootstrap, #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026.

title: Release summary: one workflow, one artifact digest, graded flow matrix and tested-platform cells
description:
## Goal
Release-qualification claims for the new monorepo must rest on one consistent, complete set of evidence for one
artifact; a claim about a different build, an untested cell or an unset threshold is not evidence. This bead builds
the one release-verification workflow that runs the four sub-results (`verify.flows`, `verify.platform`,
`verify.packages`, `verify.artifact`) and the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27) against one
artifact digest, grades every flow-matrix row and candidate defect,
grades every platform/browser/provider cell, and writes the CI-generated release summary. The operator's cutover
decision reads that summary; candidate-source handover, production promotion from this repository and package
publication rely on it.

## Scope
- **Workflow:** one release-verification workflow (reusing the build's lane runners and device lease) runs the four
  sub-results and the not-worse gate on one artifact digest from `release-identity.json` and then `scripts/verify-join.ts` (strict TS, run with
  Node type stripping). Output: the release summary (Markdown plus JSON) as a workflow
  artifact, containing the artifact digest, each sub-result's pass/fail/untested cells, the not-worse gate's per-platform-class verdicts and table, the graded flow
  matrix, the
  tested browser/OS list that Help copies, and every unsupported or unclaimed capability.
- **Summary rules (applied exactly):**
  1. Inputs present and complete: the four sub-result outputs and the not-worse gate output exist and validate
     against their schema.
  2. One commit, one digest: source commit and artifact digest byte-identical across the five outputs and equal to
     `release-identity.json`. A mismatch fails; the stale sub-result reruns on the named artifact. A case or capture
     with another digest makes its cells `untested` (never borrows a pass from another build).
  3. Closed outcome set: `passed`, `failed`, `untested`, `unsupported`, `inconclusive`, `deferred`,
     `not-applicable-by-decision`, `measured, no threshold`. Only `passed` is claimed. `measured, no threshold` cells
     are listed in their own section with the bead that will set the threshold and never counted or worded as passed.
  4. Full row coverage: rows R01-R49, the added planned-feature row X01 (weighted face blend view, graded from
     `verify.functional`) and defects 1-23 all graded; a missing row or defect fails.
  5. Every non-`passed` cell listed with capability, platform/browser, provider, reason and the sub-result that
     recorded it. The not-worse gate's verdict per platform class is reported; a class whose gate result is `failed`,
     `untested` or `inconclusive` (the physical iPhone included) blocks promotion for that class.
  6. Blocking failures: a `failed` cell in correctness, privacy, cancellation or resource behaviour, and any not-worse
     platform class that is not `passed`, blocks; it is fixed
     in the owning bead, a new artifact is built and every sub-result reruns on that digest. Other failures (for example
     the GPU lane rejecting its adapter) are listed as limitations and limit claims.
  7. Baseline accounting: every intentional difference from the baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, commit
     `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`) cites the PLAN.md drift ledger or behaviour-authority table;
     unlisted Next features remain usable; preservation of warm reuse, bounded pipelines, session/video/scrub
     recovery and export reuse is stated with its evidence.
  8. Unsupported and unclaimed capabilities listed, including non-face support if its proof was blocked and
     verified-cache warming if it did not ship.
  The summary states its outcome as `complete` (rules 1-8 hold) or `incomplete` with the failing rule; never "release
  passed".
- **Flow-matrix grading:** a collation script builds the graded matrix from the verify beads' case manifests and
  captures. Each row: row ID, class as frozen by `migration.freeze` (parity-graded exact against the pinned control
  artifact; specification-graded against the plan's contract; repair for candidate defects, never frozen as parity),
  grade, evidence links, artifact digest, platform/provider cells exercised, cells untested. A row with any required
  cell untested is not `passed`; evidence from another digest is `untested`; an unmapped row or defect is `untested`
  and is fixed by adding the case to the owning verify bead. Open 18 October audit questions (old text links,
  autoplay, plain blend on the morph slider, cropper extras, shuffle weights) keep candidate behaviour until answered;
  grade against the PLAN.md decisions at grading time. Parity thresholds exist only after the flow-matrix freeze;
  before that, "measured, no threshold".
- Evidence keys: FN/RS/SE = `verify.functional`; CR/MB/DG/RJ = `verify.flows`; PC/PV/PS = `verify.consent-device`;
  PD/PR/PG = `verify.platform`. Expected class in brackets (the freeze decides):
  R01 first visit [spec] RJ,PC; R02 return with retained work [spec] CR; R03 phone/CPU or unavailable op [spec] PD;
  R04 new words, Enter/IME, invalid [spec] FN; R05 numeric seed incl. 0 [spec] FN; R06 cancel/fail, retry unchanged
  [spec] CR; R07 edit/mode/remove queued or running tile [spec + repair 17] CR; R08 names from a face menu [parity] FN;
  R09 name on cold/slow/offline [spec] PD,FN; R10 edit a picked name [spec] FN; R11 known name by typing [spec] FN;
  R12 names modal Back/Escape/focus/history [spec + repair 14] RJ; R13 device check run/skip/timeout [spec] PV;
  R14 CPU/WebGPU selection [parity] PS,PD; R15 approve/refuse acquisition [spec] PC; R16 download/cache/quota failure
  [spec] PD,PC; R17 replace face with photo, cancel picker/crop [spec + repair 17] CR; R18 paste/drop [spec] FN;
  R19 several files, several faces [spec] MB; R20 confirm one crop [parity] FN,SE; R21 adjust/rotate crop [spec] FN;
  R22 no face / refused detector [spec] FN,PC; R23 several detected faces [spec] MB; R24 photo with encoder/generator
  absent [spec] PC; R25 cancel/retry one encode [spec] CR; R26 add/remove controls [spec + repair 1] PG,FN; R27 many
  faces then remove most [repair 2, 3] PG; R28 Undo/Start over (proposal) [spec] PG; R29 keyboard alone [repair 4] RJ;
  R30 identical neighbours [repair 6] FN; R31 word with no instant picture [repair 8, 11] FN,DG; R32 capitalising phone
  keyboard [repair 5] FN; R33 reload after morph (proposal) [repair 9] CR; R34 offline with cached models [repair 15]
  PD; R35 morph unfinished inputs [spec] FN,PS; R36 morph settings/start/cancel/retry [spec] CR,PS; R37 play/slider
  [spec] RS; R38 save WebP/PNG/MP4 [spec] RS,SE; R39 share/cancel/unsupported [spec] RS; R40 repeat/rename/format/
  after reload [spec] RS; R41 reopen still [spec] RS,SE; R42 reopen external MP4 [deferred] RS; R43 missing/damaged/
  incompatible media [spec] CR; R44 background/reload/close mid-work [spec] CR; R45 report with/without consent [spec +
  repair 12] DG; R46 remove down to one [parity + repair 7] FN; R47 tester bulk Generate, support links [parity] FN;
  R48 debug reports On/Off, persistence failure [spec] DG; R49 desktop-package recommendation retired [spec, absence]
  PD; X01 weighted face blend view (planned 24 October, PLAN.md#weighted-face-blend-advanced-mode) [spec] FN.
- Defects (1-22 repair rows, 23 decision confirmation): 1 Remove unhittable PG (+ harness fixture); 2 more than two
  faces do not fit PG; 3 no way to remove/reset many PG; 4 Tab skips controls RJ; 5 field capitalises FN; 6 identical
  neighbours generic error FN; 7 Add face disabled at one FN,PG; 8 wrong typed-word tile text FN; 9 words lost on
  reload (proposal) CR; 10 sizes disagree PC; 11 per-keystroke requests, beacon, 3.4 MB list, privacy text DG; 12 Send
  report turns standing on DG; 13 collector rejects action, batch dropped DG; 14 names contrast 1.18:1, empty failed
  dialog RJ; 15 offline cached fails, manifest re-fetched PD; 16 stacked toasts cover Create morph DG; 17 stale
  completions CR; 18 cap on one of three paths MB,PG; 19 32 MB fallback outside consent PC; 20 typos, placeholder,
  cold-device text, disabled-looking button, transparent crop panel RJ,PV; 21 licence page RJ; 22 stored data/Clear
  (proposal) RJ; 23 preview faces no badge, label kept RJ.
- **Platform cells (inside the release summary, no separate support table):** the summary's cell section is generated
  from the four sub-result outputs, `collect-lane-results.ts` output and the device calibration result
  (`device.calibration`, if present), over the cell list declared in the browser matrix (`build.vite-shell`). One row
  per capability x platform/browser/provider cell with the closed-set outcome, artifact digest and run link;
  generated, never typed. Includes the small intended-feature matrix and which version was exercised, calibration
  cells (honest when uncalibrated), the ONNX Runtime Web evaluation decision if recorded, and physical-iPhone
  cells filled only from the not-worse gate's physical-lane runs (Simulator results never fill a physical cell). A small preflight success never promotes a cell to full-model
  tested. Help's tested browser/OS list is generated from the summary JSON.

## Out of scope
Deciding cutover (`gate.cutover`). Publishing packages (delivery). Re-running control-artifact goldens
(`migration.parity`). Running cases owned by another verify bead. Marketing claims; inferred cells.

## Notes
- Integrated verification checks the final integrated app (after the planned UI and package changes) against the Next baseline (`facemorph.me-classic` branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) plus the plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped. Not historic-API parity and not a shutdown-qualification campaign. Performance and reliability against the control, including control/control noise and the physical iPhone, are judged by the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27), not here. Correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found here are fixed in the owning bead and this bead re-runs. Wording says planned, experimental, implemented or deployed. No weights, secrets, photos or typed inputs in Git.
- 24 October cut: the join report and four sub-result receipts in `docs/receipts/` become one
  CI-generated release summary over machine-readable sub-result outputs; "receipts exist and pass
  check-receipts.ts" becomes "outputs exist and validate". The workstream parent and milestone nodes are gone.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #integrated-verification (structure for decomposition and pass criteria),
  #ui-flow-matrix-and-open-journey-contracts,
  #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026,
  #behavior-authorities-for-development, #workspace-build-and-artifact-identity, #questions-raised-by-the-18-october-audit.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests for `scripts/verify-join.ts` with fixture outputs: a commit mismatch fails; a digest mismatch fails; a digest differing from `release-identity.json` fails; an output failing its schema fails; a case with another digest turns its cells `untested`; a `measured, no threshold` cell is never counted as passed; an outcome outside the closed set fails; a missing flow-matrix row or defect fails; an open blocking-category failure fails; a missing or wrong-digest not-worse output fails; a failed required/available not-worse platform class or missing any of the six required local CPU/WebGPU cells (eris Chrome, eris Firefox, Huawei Chrome) makes the outcome `incomplete`; an explicitly unavailable hosted runner/simulator is untested with a reason and no claim, not an indefinite release blocker.
- [ ] Unit tests for the matrix collation script: a row is `untested` when no case maps to it, when evidence carries another digest, or when a required cell is missing; it never turns `measured, no threshold`, `deferred` or `not-applicable-by-decision` into `passed`; it rejects grades outside the closed set.
- [ ] Unit tests for the platform-cell generation: a cell with no sub-result evidence is `untested`; an outcome outside the closed set is rejected; evidence from another digest is `untested`; a physical-iPhone row without a physical-lane run is `untested` and permits no physical-iPhone claim; it is optional, and iOS Simulator evidence remains separately labelled; a matrix cell with no row in the summary fails.
- [ ] A test fails when Help's tested browser/OS list and the release summary's passed cells disagree.
- [ ] The release-verification workflow runs all four sub-results and the not-worse gate on one digest and produces the release summary (Markdown plus JSON) with sections: claimed (passed) cells; the not-worse per-class verdicts and table; untested/unsupported/inconclusive/deferred cells with reasons; `measured, no threshold` cells with their threshold bead; unsupported or unclaimed capabilities; baseline differences with plan citations; graded matrix of all 49 rows, X01 and 23 defects with class, grade, evidence links and digest; the platform cells and the tested browser/OS list Help copies.
- [ ] Parity rows are exact against the control artifact; repair rows show the defect fixed by an operated case; specification rows cite their contract; every intentional baseline difference cites its drift-ledger or behaviour-authority entry.
- [ ] On the release candidate the summary outcome is `complete`; nothing is reported passed that did not run on the named artifact/platform.
notes:
Operator, 25 October 2026 (fm-ajcf): reuse existing classic-style iOS Simulator inside the GitHub macOS runner and Android emulator CI alongside ordinary tests. Hosted runner/simulator unavailability is best effort: bounded attempt, explicit untested reason, no passing or physical-iPhone claim and no permanent release block. Actual available-lane failures require repair. Physical phone never runs in CI. Candidate handover needs no further approval and is incomplete until actual P30 Pro and eris CPU/WebGPU checks plus post-delivery-check pass against the deployed artifact. This supersedes older all-platform-availability and physical-iPhone release prerequisites; other product/performance requirements remain.
Operator, 25 October 2026: handover completion requires normal applicable CI plus six local cells on the deployed artifact: CPU and WebGPU in eris Chrome, eris Firefox and actual Huawei Chrome. Missing local evidence, silent browser substitution or CPU fallback cannot pass that grid. fm-qa3q implements the missing six-cell lab support and blocks fm-s3o. Current lab has only four Chromium/Huawei cells. For iteration use fastest sufficient scripts/CLI/API and reuse helpers; escalate to browser protocols and real operated input only as required, then clean task-owned state. This clarifies local journey coverage, not a new full timing campaign per edit.

Handover (2), the release outcome: bind facemorph.me to the chosen on-device artifact from this repository, retire the old publisher, point names.facemorph.me at the main app with its names modal, and confirm the site serves its app, models, catalogue and diagnostics. Production starts fresh. This is one of the distinct delivery actions (candidate-source handover, production promotion, API retirement, package publication, independent package acceptance, classic publication); none is inferred complete from another, and remaining work is reported plainly.

## Scope
- Authority: before any change, confirm the operator's cutover decision (`gate:cutover`, PLAN.md dated decisions; it reads the CI-generated release summary from integrated verification) names **production promotion of the monorepo artifact** and its digest; otherwise make no change and report `blocked: no authorizing decision`. The cutover decision is the single operator gate and sits only on the live pushes: early promotion, candidate-source handover, production promotion and API retirement (operator, 24 October) — not on package publication, the candidate edit set, the legacy notice edit, classic publication or independent package acceptance.
- Before state: DNS/bindings and publisher of facemorph.me and names.facemorph.me, current artifact identity.
- Execute the action list: bind facemorph.me to the monorepo publisher; disable the Vercel publisher (or the early-promotion binding); redirect names.facemorph.me (301/308) to the main app with its fullscreen names modal (no names-only route).
- Decide and state what the names host claims, after static names. If static names are incomplete, show the limitation; redirects or phone inference cannot substitute.
- Rollback target: a retained working on-device artifact with matching assets and collector config; its runtime paths confirmed held by `models.facemorph.me`. The rollback artifact, its runtime paths and its collector config stay available until the real-visitor comparison (`verify.field-not-worse`, fm-js8i) reports clean on every platform class (PLAN.md "Strictly not worse", after release).
- Second runtime origin for the promoted artifact: `models.facemorph.me` fills from `https://next.facemorph.me/`, and pages on facemorph.me retry chunks through it. Before switching, confirm by HEAD list that it holds every runtime path of the promoted artifact; if next.facemorph.me is not serving that artifact (for example the handover has not happened, or next has moved on), warm the copy explicitly from the artifact's staging location first.
- Changeover statistics: after the switch, post the cutover annotation with `scripts/delivery/annotate-cutover.mjs` (from `domain.actions`; tags `facemorph-cutover`, action `production-promotion`, artifact digest) so the "FaceMorph before and after" dashboard marks the moment.
- Production starts fresh: no GUID resolver, share URLs, historic-data migration or cross-origin OPFS/session transfer. Any promoted artifact preserves qualified browser CPU/WebGPU/mobile behaviour and carries no native recommendations.
- The workflow summary records before/after state, artifact digest, commands and checks.

## Out of scope
API retirement; package publication; phone or full shutdown-parity certification.

## Notes
- October 25 is aspirational; neither a date nor a test score triggers the decision.
- 24 October rules: per-action evidence is the delivery workflow run with its post-delivery check; no per-action or workstream receipt files and no `docs/decisions/` paths.
- Plan: #delivery-and-publication, #programme-boundaries-and-finish-line, #remaining-choices-completion-and-cutover-authority, #domain-handover-and-retirement-preparation.

title: Quota, eviction and cross-tab, with the browser acceptance matrix
description:
## Goal
Finish the reusable model manager: bounded, truthful quota and eviction behaviour kept separate from app retention policy, cross-tab coordination, the Cache Storage fallback, and a real-browser acceptance matrix proving the package in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit and the mobile component lanes rather than only in Node. The package owns manifest/chunk acquisition, checksum validation and recovery, OPFS/device caching, reuse/eviction/quota and loaded provider handles, which the engine consumes without reaching back for files.

## Scope
- Quota estimation and reporting; typed quota errors distinct from execution capability. iOS storage checks reported a 1,000 MB quota (CPU package 1,040 MB).
- Manager eviction policy that excludes leased assets and never touches app records: model-cache eviction must never delete completed user exports or application recovery records.
- Cross-tab coordination and invalidation.
- Cache Storage fallback where OPFS is unavailable; Safari worker sync handles on OPFS.
- Firefox persistent-storage permission is requested only after explained download approval (app-level, `storage-request.test.mjs`); the matrix has an explicit cell for its timing.
- Real-browser matrix: load/cache/read/reload/quota/checksum/error/cancel, missing/corrupt shards after admission, leased deletion, cross-tab, both backends, Safari worker sync handles, no download before authorization, output-cache hit, disposal. Lanes: Playwright Chromium, Firefox, WebKit; macOS WebKit/Firefox; Android emulator components; iOS Simulator components.
- After missing/corrupt shards, leased-cache deletion, cross-tab effects, cancellation and disposal, every affected operation settles, releases resources and reports typed invalidation without hidden network repair. Speculative reads cannot fetch replacement data.
- Cold-photo boundary change: the candidate's streamed e4e may materialize verified shards over HTTP during execution; the manager moves network acquisition ahead of engine operations deliberately. Qualify its component cost here: peak stored bytes and peak live encoder shards for a cold photo acquisition through the manager; the product-level cold-photo time-to-encoded-face, port vs control, is a paired cell in `compute.app-rebind` (real-bridge harness, where the app first runs e4e on manager handles) and in `compute.ported-app` (product lanes). Show bounded lazy local reads, never all encoder shards (108 sequential streamed sessions) resident in RAM.
- Cold, model-cached and output-cached are three separate cells per lane. An output-cache hit issues zero model requests.
- Package docs: qualified independent-library CPU/reference consumers of the manager are documented and qualified separately; the app keeps its qualified CPU/WebGPU routes and no native distribution is implied. The alternate runtime origin is package configuration, set by the app (`manager.acquisition`).

## Out of scope
- App retention ceilings (media and recovery) and storage Help/Clear (defect 22, media and recovery).
- Non-face consumer proof (integrated verification).
- App policy: bundle consent, priorities, eager-warming (consent); engine orchestration (compute).

## Notes
- Leases do not stop browser reclamation.
- Physical-phone OPFS speed and quota remain unqualified; report them as untested cells.
- Preserve keys/hashes, candidate cache identities and on-origin result/session formats. No weights or secrets in Git.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#model-manager-extraction; #browser-model-manager; #consented-downloads-useful-overlap-and-cached-model-warming (Acceptance).

- [x] Real-browser matrix runs in CI with each cell reported passed/failed/untested by name per lane (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, macOS WebKit/Firefox, Android emulator components, iOS Simulator components), including explicit Safari worker sync-handle and Firefox storage-permission-timing cells.

- [x] Cold / model-cached / output-cached cells reported separately per lane; an output-cache hit shows zero model requests.

title: Digest-consistent serving, release-consistent sets, staging qualification
description:
## Goal
Serve model and runtime bytes from `packages/cloudflare-model-host` with the required headers, immutable digest-addressed paths and the second runtime origin; keep asset sets release-consistent so an in-flight app keeps one immutable manifest identity while a new app is published; and qualify the package end to end on an explicitly identified test origin, proving it serves bytes the manager and engine accept. On 20 October one Cloudflare edge returned HTTP 500 from static-asset storage for single encoder chunks for about ten minutes at a time; the candidate now retries and alternates with `models.facemorph.me`, so the second origin is part of serving, not an optional extra.

## Scope
- Required MIME, CORS, embedding (COEP/CORP) and cache headers; immutable digest-addressed paths; no accidental Worker invocation on primary model requests.
- Mirror Worker source: `hosting/next-mirror/{worker.mjs,worker.test.mjs,wrangler.jsonc}` from the frozen import revision recorded by `inventory.import` (committed head of `candidate/next-delivery-20260916` at freeze, `6107f80` or later; classic `b2d945a8` predates the directory). Export from Git objects (never a working tree) into `packages/cloudflare-model-host/`; digests equal the `hosting/next-mirror/` row of the import path map; the package provenance file lists source repo, commit, per-file SHA-256 and destination paths.
- Reusable shape: in classic the Worker fills itself from `https://next.facemorph.me/` (hard-coded, service binding) over R2 bucket `facemorph-runtime-mirror` and copies only immutable `runtime/{assets,chunks,manifests,photo,encoder-stream}/` paths. In the package the upstream origin, bucket name and copied path prefixes are configuration; external developers can run it with no FaceMorph hostname. FaceMorph's values live in the app's deploy configuration (`hosting/`).
- Two package commands for `deploy.promotion`'s CI workflow, both taking the target as an explicit argument and publishing only with `--publish`: deploy the mirror Worker (today `npx wrangler deploy --config hosting/next-mirror/wrangler.jsonc`) and `warm`, which takes the staged manifest and target origin and implements classic warm semantics: every immutable path, `--retry 3` on transient errors, 8-way parallelism, failure on any non-200, held count reported.
- Release consistency: stage immutable referenced assets before the app that uses them; keep referenced assets for the supported active-session/rollback window (window and storage cost named in domain handover's delivery inventory); garbage-collect only by a documented retention policy. `models.facemorph.me` keeps referenced immutable assets for the same window, and a rollback artifact's paths are confirmed held there (HEAD list) before rollback is claimed.
- Cases: old open tab keeps one manifest identity mid-operation after a new app/manifest is published, requesting only old-manifest digests; a missing old asset yields a clear reload/recovery action within a bounded number of requests (no unbounded retry, no silent switch to new digests). Interrupted acquisition resumes with verified chunks kept. A catalogue with assets from an incompatible manifest is refused with a typed error, nothing half-applied. After an ordinary rollback the previous app runs against its own manifest.
- Retention and model-cache eviction never delete completed user exports or application recovery records.
- Staging qualification: stage the qualified runtime/model set to a named test origin with explicit `--publish`; verify every chunk reconstructs, client manager/engine agree on schema and hashes, exact tested headers and runtime bytes are served, and mirror fallback works when the primary returns 500. Name the origin in the CI run.

## Out of scope
- Client retry logic (`manager.acquisition`); service worker/offline install.
- Frontend/catalogue/diagnostics staging and app-domain promotion (`deploy.staging`, which stages the application site; this bead stages model/runtime chunks through the package); production promotion and live-byte checks (delivery).
- Package README and hosting guides (`pkgdocs.others` writes and finalizes them).

## Notes
- Exactly one repository's workflow may publish a target at a time (classic keeps publishing until handover).
- Tie-break: release-consistent sets, old-tab compatibility and retention window belong here (retention, publication order) with workspace build owning identity.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#model-hosting-extraction; #cloudflare-model-host; #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts; #workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership.

- [x] All classic `worker.test.mjs` cases pass in the package, plus new tests: a non-immutable path is refused; a configured upstream is the only origin fetched.
- [x] Mirror Worker files match the frozen-revision digests from `inventory.import`; provenance file committed.
- [x] Source scan: no literal `next.facemorph.me` / `models.facemorph.me` in package source.
- [x] Header check on a staged sample passes (MIME, CORS, COEP/CORP, cache); request interception shows primary model requests do not invoke a Worker.
- [x] `warm` test against a local test mirror: one missing path -> non-zero exit naming it; complete -> exit 0 with held count equal to the manifest's immutable path count; deploy and warm make no writes without `--publish`.
- [x] Retention policy documented in the package.
- [ ] E2E against the staging/test origin, requests intercepted and asserted by host class and bytes: old tab requests only old digests; missing old asset -> reload/recovery action within a bounded request count; interrupted acquisition resume bytes equal remaining bytes; mixed/incompatible catalogue -> typed refusal, nothing half-applied; rollback runs the previous app on its own manifest; rollback paths HEAD-200 on the test mirror.
- [x] Storage spy: retention/eviction deletes nothing outside model-cache keys (exports and recovery records untouched).
- [x] Staging run on the named test origin: every chunk reconstructs, manager loads from it and agrees with the engine on schema and hashes, exact headers/bytes served, mirror fallback succeeds when the primary is forced to 500.
- [x] Traces and screenshots kept on failure; unit tests listed in test discovery and pass locally with the CI command; CI verifies after push.
- [x] end-to-end staging qualification at close needs fm-ffn7 (with fm-ffn7). If fm-ffn7 has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-ffn7 (`br update fm-ffn7 --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-ffn7
- [x] Repair main run 40152661930 scaffold dry-run failures on Triton (real workerd compatibility); execute affected tests on a supported runner.
- [x] Repair main 40170681507 manager-cache release-consistency browser module-fetch failure; retain exact old-tab, missing-asset and interrupted-resume assertions.
- [x] Diagnose main40175982257 staging-origin fetch timeout and verify real manager primary/mirror acquisition still passes; preserve real failure behavior.

title: Convert FFHQ and one real non-face checkpoint with independent parity
description:
## Goal
Prove the conversion container on real checkpoints: official FFHQ (the product's generator and the 108-shard FP32 e4e encoder) and one real non-face checkpoint, each verified against an independent upstream PyTorch reference within a declared numerical tolerance. FFHQ shows the container reproduces provider artifacts the manager and engine accept; the non-face checkpoint, ideally at another resolution, exposes hardcoded assumptions and becomes the fixture for compute, morph and media descriptor checks and the integrated non-face joint proof. Until this passes, non-face support stays labelled unqualified.

## Scope
**FFHQ**
- Convert official NVlabs FFHQ (acquired under its documented terms) and the e4e encoder in the container; produce chunks, descriptor, manifests and a parity report.
- Compare with the currently hosted artifacts (known digests in the runtime manifests): identical digests where deterministic, otherwise numerical parity against the independent PyTorch reference within the frozen tolerances.
- Preserve descriptor/content identities and the direct-WebGPU coefficients from `manifest.webgl`; WebGL execution removal does not delete shared coefficient assets.
- Load check: converted artifacts load and run in the candidate runtime harness (component load). The manager/engine journey is integrated verification's.

**Frozen tolerances (never widened, never a precision change, never replaced by a visual spot-check)**
- Product synthesis canaries: max RGB difference 1 on 0–255 and max sampled raw-float error 0.002 (candidate `src/Next/browser/canary-qualification.mjs`: `maxRgb <= 1 && maxFloat <= .002`, alpha excluded).
- Research/reference suites keep their own frozen coverage and tolerances.
- e4e latent: max absolute W+ error 0.0001 (`photo-runtime/README.md`, `encoder-stream/qualification/report.json`).
- Comparison is raw network output before compression against the independent qualified reference for the same model, latent, noise, preprocessing and workload. Encoded image bytes are never a correctness gate. Other models never inherit FFHQ values.

**Non-face checkpoint**
- Proposed fixture: NVlabs AFHQ cat 512 px, subject to converter compatibility and acquisition terms (not currently claimed supported). If it fails on compatibility or terms, name the blocker, choose a compatible non-face checkpoint and state which and why in the compatibility table.
- Trusted checkpoint acquisition: source URL, publisher, SHA-256 of the downloaded pickle, licence/usage and redistribution terms, trusted-pickle warning, written in the compatibility table and converter docs. The checkpoint is never committed.
- Real copyable `build`, `acquire`, `convert`, `verify` commands in the container; image and base-image digests, tool versions and conversion flags in the verify report.
- Independent reference: outputs from the pinned upstream PyTorch implementation on the original checkpoint (not the converted artifacts) for a recorded seed set; this model's own small tolerance, declared and justified from its reference before the run; measured errors reported.
- Output set ready for developer-controlled static hosting: chunks, descriptor (resolution, channels, Z/W size, W+ layer count, noise, truncation, conditioning) and manifests valid against the contracts schema, with digests.
- Update the compatibility table; until the joint proof passes, non-face support is labelled unqualified with the blocker named.
- Generation and morph for non-face models never load a face detector or FFHQ e4e.

## Out of scope
Hosting/publishing (model hosting). Changing the production artifacts (only if a later decision adopts the converted set). Manager-loaded inference, hosting and export of the non-face model (integrated verification's joint proof, `verify.packages`).

## Notes
- The non-face joint proof runs in `verify.packages` from local packs before npm publication, then again from the final docs in `pkgdocs.release` and by the independent reviewer (`pkgaccept.review`); this row supplies its inputs (checkpoint source/digest/terms, container digests, exact commands, upstream-reference errors versus the declared tolerance, descriptor and schema-valid manifests with digests).
- Builds and verifies on its own; workspace-build CI lanes are a soft input. The component load uses the imported candidate runtime harness, hence the `import.checks` edge (24 October final pass).
- Anchors: PLAN.md #conversion-tooling, #model-conversion-container, #external-developer-journey-and-non-face-models, #synthesis-correctness-and-export-quality.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] FFHQ parity report passes the frozen tolerances (synthesis canaries RGB <= 1/255 and sampled raw float <= 0.002; research suites at their own; e4e W+ <= 0.0001), or digests are identical; nondeterministic fields listed.
- [x] Converted FFHQ artifacts pass the component load in the runtime harness on CPU; runs on a worker under the device lease.
- [x] Non-face artifacts verify against the independent upstream reference within the declared, justified tolerance; the descriptor declares the non-1024 resolution and its latent shape (or the substitute checkpoint's actual values).
- [x] The commands in the converter docs are exactly the commands CI ran (scripted verbatim run).
- [x] Hand-off set present: checkpoint source, SHA-256 and terms; container and base-image digests; exact commands; upstream-reference errors versus tolerance; descriptor and schema-valid manifests with digests.
- [x] Compatibility table updated from these runs; non-face label reads unqualified until `verify.packages` passes.
- [x] Acquisition docs imply neither bundled weights nor blanket support for third-party checkpoints; unsupported CPU/GPU/architecture cells explicit, with no silent fallback.

title: GPU acceptance, README-is-the-test harness, rot check
description:
## Goal
Prove the frozen classic distribution's CUDA claim on a real NVIDIA worker from empty volumes, with a harness that extracts the README's marked quickstart block and runs it verbatim (the README is the test), and keep it honest over time with an on-change and monthly clean-clone rot check, so rot, including a dead weight link, shows up as a failed run. The README claims only matrix cells that actually ran.

## Scope
- **Harness**: extraction + runner script that takes the README's marked quickstart block and runs it verbatim (never a hand-copied equivalent) into an empty directory with no existing images, volumes or build cache. Pre-switch mode substitutes the branch explicitly (the only change, logged) and labels the run a development run.
- Harness assertions: build from empty cache, download/verify, healthy, URL logged; `/healthz` reports `"provider":"cuda"` and the GPU name; `/api/face/?seed=0&dim=512` returns an image; the frontend renders a face (`smoke_*` scripts as the starting point); photo, morph and media endpoints; old seed/text semantics; `down`/`up` reuses volumes with no re-download and is healthy within a documented time; kill-during-setup recovery; corrupt-asset rejection by hash; missing-terms fast fail; host without NVIDIA runtime (or container toolkit absent) fails clearly with no CPU fallback; CPU override run.
- **GPU acceptance** on the planned CUDA cell: RTX 2080 SUPER (Turing) on the workstation (Docker 29.7.2, Compose 5.5.1, driver 610.57.04) under the shared device lease; nothing has run on it yet. Measure first-run duration and disk use. Attempt the TrueNAS GTX 1050 (Pascal, compute capability 6.1; cu128 wheels in `torch 2.9.1` are not expected to support it, confirm): on real hardware the default CUDA start must end in the startup capability check's plain message (card, capability, supported range), and the explicit CPU override must then serve a face. GitHub-hosted runners have no GPU and cover build and CPU path. Record commit, image digests, driver, GPU, Docker/Compose versions per assertion and list untested matrix cells.
- **README content**: validated-matrix table (OS, Docker, driver, GPU, commit, date) claiming only cells that ran; measured first-run time and disk use; "frozen, no feature updates"; upstream weight hosts (dlib.net, NVIDIA CDN, one Google Drive link; D6); "Not guaranteed" list (GPUs older than Volta or newer than the wheels' kernels/PTX, future Docker/driver behaviour, third-party weight hosts); what the default build reaches on the user's machine (D5: Docker Hub, Debian apt, PyPI, download.pytorch.org, GitHub for pinned NVlabs `d72cc7d`) and that dlib compiles from source; minimum Compose v2 version supporting `include`.
- **Rot check** workflow on the distribution branch: `push` path filter, monthly `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch`; GPU job on the self-hosted worker (lease), CPU/build job on hosted runners. On failure open an issue owned by the classic distribution workstream.
- Classic stays frozen: a rot failure never triggers a general dependency bump. It opens an issue that an agent works as ordinary work with no approval step (operator, 24 October): restore the pinned input where it is still obtainable; if a pinned input is gone for good (a deleted base-image digest, a yanked wheel), the only allowed change is the minimal re-pin of that input behind the same README-executed acceptance, stated in the README matrix. A dead upstream weight link is reported as such and not worked around (D6). The documented allowed unfreeze (a new GPU generation outside the arch list) is the other exception.

## Out of scope
Pixel parity with historic production; the recorded post-switch acceptance run and the default-branch switch (classic delivery); dependency bumps.

## Notes
- Scheduled workflows run only from the default branch's files; verify the rot check after the switch (classic delivery).
- `self-host/validation/2026-10-10/gpu.json` stays as historical evidence (one GPU/driver, synthetic inputs, source-only delivery).
- 24 October rules: no receipts and no vendored `event_log.py`/`e2e-event-log.v1` convention; weight-download claims are asserted from captured requests by host class and bytes; evidence is the CI run.
- Plan: #classic-distribution, #classic-distribution-acceptance, #frozen-classic-distribution (validation: the README is the test).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Extraction unit tests: the marked block is found and run verbatim; a README without the markers fails; `<canonical-url>`/branch substitution is the only change in pre-switch mode and is logged.
- [ ] A development run of the harness passes on the RTX 2080 SUPER worker from empty images, volumes and build cache, every assertion above recorded with commit, image digests, driver, GPU and Docker/Compose versions; first-run duration and disk use measured and stated in the README.
- [ ] Restart run shows zero weight bytes downloaded (asserted from captured download requests by host class and bytes); kill-during-setup, corrupt asset, missing terms, no-NVIDIA and CPU-override cases each pass their assertion.
- [ ] Pascal cell on the GTX 1050: the default CUDA start prints the plain unsupported-GPU message (card, 6.1, supported range) with no raw `no kernel image` CUDA error in the logs, and the CPU override then returns a face from `/api/face/?seed=0&dim=512`; untested cells listed in the README matrix.
- [ ] A forced rot failure produces an issue whose text names the failed assertion and the pinned input involved; no workflow in the rot check bumps a dependency.
- [ ] Rot check: one dispatched run passes both jobs; a forced failure (bad hash) opens an issue.
- [ ] Modern-GPU support (PLAN.md, 24 Oct): README support table (compute capability 7.0–12.x, driver 570+, Pascal CPU-only, tested rows dated).
- [ ] Startup capability check against torch.cuda.get_arch_list(): an unsupported GPU gets one plain message (card, capability, supported range), never a raw CUDA 'no kernel image' error; the check is a pure function of the arch list and the device capability, tested with real values from the pinned torch build and from the RTX 2080 SUPER and GTX 1050; no patched torch.
- [ ] Each rot-check run records GPU, capability, arch list and driver.
- [ ] Before the release tag, the README-executed acceptance also passes once on the newest available GPU generation (Blackwell, rented if none is at hand).
- [ ] One allowed unfreeze is documented: bump the torch/CUDA pin behind the same acceptance when a new GPU generation is not in the arch list; the support table states the moved lower bound.
- [ ] close-check (conditional, from the parallelism pass): use the fm-zxj lease if landed, else the existing device lock; tick once it holds or does not apply, saying which in the close reason
notes:
The TrueNAS GTX 1050 (Pascal) cell needs operator access (`build.truenas-runners`, fm-ip6g) and the Blackwell cell needs a machine the operator supplies or approves renting; each is reported untested with its blocker until then, never passed.
Compute (operator, 24 October): the Pascal acceptance cell runs on triton's GTX 1080 (compute capability 6.1), so it no longer waits on TrueNAS access; the TrueNAS GTX 1050 becomes an optional extra cell.

title: Keyboard-only pass and responsive sweep for face controls
description:
## Goal
Close out face controls on the actual built app: every face journey works with the keyboard alone, and the face controls pass the responsive width sweep with live resize, zoom and short viewports, with every overlap, clip, overflow or lost focus fixed. Earlier feedback showed intrinsic-dimension and component checks passing while the displayed face was clipped, so this is a width sweep on the running app, not endpoint screenshots. This is the separately accepted responsive-sweep item in the face split, and it is where audit rows 1-8, 18 and 20 are confirmed closed together.

## Scope
- **Keyboard defect 4**: Tab skips Change mode, Browse names and the empty-tile photo button (`tabIndex=-1` at `Product.fs:820,826,859,898`); classic's were reachable.
- **Keyboard-only journeys** (Playwright keyboard input only, no pointer): generate words/seed; Encode image (source step with Choose image, "Or paste image here" with Ctrl/Cmd+V, Prepare encoder when shown, CANCEL; confirm; adjust; failure path; batch selection order; per-slot Cancel/Retry); Remove/Undo/Start over; Share/Save/format/filename; Morph/Cancel; the blend view (button, slots, weights, Reset, Make it 1, Add to morph, Back to morph); provider selector; Browse Names. Fix every unreachable or out-of-order control; visible focus; focus returned after each dialog; topmost modal owns Escape/Back; removed buttons leave no hidden shortcut or stale focus target.
- **Sweep widths**: 320, 360, 390, 480, 600, 768, 900, 1,024, 1,280, 1,920, 2,560 px, and widths immediately either side of each actual layout breakpoint read from the built CSS.
- Continuous resize through transitions and portrait/landscape or height changes while the crop modal, download modal, keyboard focus, queue/progress and results are active; short viewports (568 px high); long names/errors; browser zoom 200% / text enlargement; touch virtual-keyboard occlusion where available.
- Grid reflow with 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 30, 64 and 150 faces at each width (virtualised strip or grid past about 100 faces); the blend view at 1, 2, 3, 8, 16, 40 and 100 slots (scrolling slot panel with the result in view, compact rows).
- Fix every overlap, clip, page-wide overflow or lost focus found (fixes land here).
- Workstream-wide checks: responsive rendered controls, keyboard/accessibility behaviour, denied consent, changed input/late result, file and clipboard entry and Save/Share usability pass in the built app; no post-encode Crop button, hold-to-compare gesture/button or duplicate filename line remains; confirmation/editor/failure layouts match the locked images; text >= 4.5:1 in light and dark themes; every UI flow-matrix row assigned to face controls has a passing operated test in its owning bead.

## Out of scope
Names picker internals; diagnostics disclosure; integrated verification's whole-app sweep, which re-runs this on the final artifact.

## Notes
- Layout checks use available browsers/devices; not a physical-phone release gate. The run output records exact viewport/zoom/artifact digest and unsupported environments.
- UI restraint (12 October): keep the candidate visual language; every added control must help choose an action, understand a cost, recover or access the product.
- Focus order and CSS fixes in the ported UI only; no shared bridge/runtime/worker file.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#face-controls-and-modals, #integrated-verification (responsiveness acceptance), #ui-flow-matrix-and-open-journey-contracts (keyboard row), #decomposition-order-size-and-tracker-coverage.

description:

Generate/Cancel/Cancelling/Retry belongs inline beside the textbox; all validation, cancellation, stale-result, consent, recovery and batch guarantees remain. ## Goal
Build the Encode an image modal from source to confirmed crop, faithful to the locked `crop image.png`: direct source selection/paste/drop in the owning face card, then a crop confirmation state where the proposed crop is accepted with OK before any encoding starts. "Crop only before encoding" and the confirmed-crop flow are original requirements; always confirming first is a real change from the candidate, which opens the encoder consent straight away for one clear face with no crop step, and whose crop panel is transparent in light mode (defect 20).

Card chooser/drop/paste remain direct and recovery-first; crop/action-owned status stays in the card/crop footer and then owning tile. Cancelling a card action preserves independently approved page-level preparation.
- **After a source**: recovery metadata first; a valid matching recovered still installs without models and closes the modal; a fresh photo moves to confirmation in the same modal; several candidates move to the batch proposal (face.batch). Cancelling the native chooser keeps the card and prior result unchanged, without opening a modal.
- **Source cancel.** Cancelling the native chooser leaves the face unchanged and returns focus to its initiating control; crop Cancel/Escape/Back/backdrop abandons only that action continuation/setup owner. No source-only modal exists; separately approved top-level preparation survives.
- **Confirmation.** Detect/propose on the source first (any detector-driven warp completes before display). If detector/alignment assets are absent the consent gate runs first; declining keeps local manual crop (ADJUST CROP) and starts no downloads. Layout per locked image: square preview centred under the title, **ADJUST CROP** centred below, CANCEL footer left, OK footer right (indigo). One short explanation that encoding recreates the face and may change details, between the preview and the footer (the only added copy; no resemblance approval). The preview stays square and fully visible (four corners inside the viewport at 320 px and in a 568 px-high viewport). Guides are never burned into pixels.
- ADJUST CROP opens the editor state (face.crop-editor) in the same modal; Use Crop returns with the updated proposal.

Restoring a previous face on Cancel is desirable where simple, not mandatory.
- Keyboard: card controls follow visual order; optional top-level preparation follows the provider selector in visual order, never inserted into the card chooser tab sequence.

Editor and alignment failure (face.crop-editor); batch selection (face.batch); encoding itself (crop.queue); Prepare encoder grant logic (consent.modal); main-field paste (face.tiles).

title: Static-result selection; typed-name equality on the engine; acceptance
description:
## Goal
Make name selection inference-free and identical to typing the same name: replace the candidate's `ChooseName -> RunFace` (which synthesizes on selection) and remove `generateNameOrSeed`'s silent fallback from catalogue W+ to text mapping, so a picked name installs a validated published result. Re-run the typed-name equality check on the extracted engine, and run the static names acceptance journeys end to end. "Instant" means no model download, inference or Generate step, not zero network latency.

## Scope
- **Selection.** Fills the name into the ordinary text field, shows the preview immediately, fetches only that result's bounded assets plus at most one integrity lookup, validates image/latent/recovery; then the text revision becomes a completed Save/Morph input and the default file is prepared. Progress completes after validation and default file preparation.
- Loading/Retry in the target tile's image-area action slot; stale target responses rejected; never substitute synthesis on catalogue failure; cold/offline/corrupt/stale states explicit; offline works only for cached, complete, validated assets.
- Morph with selected names acquires the generator only via consent; the name's validated image serves preview, slider and video at that endpoint (no re-synthesis).
- Editing selected text invalidates the ready result and enables ordinary Generate/Retry; store result identity and provenance, not a persistent names mode.
- One canonical resolver: transient catalogue availability cannot change the face associated with a typed string; the typed path never reads the catalogue.
- An unchanged-migration build keeps the candidate's synthesizing selection, labelled as such; the final contract never falls back to synthesis.
- **Typed-name equality on the extracted engine.** For a declared sample (the full set where the lease budget allows) of published names: map the exact lowercase text through the extracted engine's canonical resolver and compare the latent exactly and raw synthesis within the frozen tolerances (max RGB <= 1/255, sampled raw float <= 0.002) with the published result's recovered latent/model identity; include cold/offline catalogue and cache-miss cases. Compressed catalogue images use export-quality rules, never raw thresholds on lossy pixels. On mismatch fix the engine or regenerate the asset from the canonical resolver; never widen tolerances. Runs under the shared device lease.
- **Acceptance journeys.** Gapless overlay-name grid, no search/header/X, explicit target, keyboard/touch dismissal; cold/offline/corrupt/stale states; selection/Save/reopen with generator acquisition and inference disabled; Morph then acquires the generator only with consent; catalogue/model consistency; bounded visible-preview fetching; modal Back/focus; selection-to-text editing; exact catalogue-versus-typed identity. Walk: select two names, morph, cancel/retry, play/scrub, save and reload; reopen a saved still.

## Out of scope
Grid UI (names.picker); generating or publishing the catalogue; integrated verification's join; any claim of zero network latency or fully offline uncached browsing.

## Notes
- **Shared files.** Selection replaces `ChooseName -> RunFace`, removes the synthesizing fallback in `generateNameOrSeed` and changes `loadNames`, all in `product-bridge.mjs`: the plan's named bridge-consuming edit of the static names picker, ordered after confirmed-crop and the morph pipeline. The equality check is a script and edits none of the shared files; it must not hold up compute extraction, and it feeds integrated verification's flow row R11 (exact-name typing equals picker identity).
- Context: `facemorph-seed-gallery` (8,966 lossy images, 364,039,372 bytes) and `facemorph-name-catalogue` (pinned 36,864-byte W+ latents for all 5,055 names, run 38029582696) are the current static Workers.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#static-names-and-picker, #names-selection-implementation-gap-and-complete-target, #implementation-approach-and-sequencing (mandatory ordering edges), #end-to-end-experience-and-design-fidelity-check.
acceptance_criteria:
Operated rule: real pointer/touch at the visible position with `elementFromPoint` in the named region; by-name only for setup; 390 px and 1,280 px, screenshot per case.
- [ ] Generator never acquired (fresh browser profile, no download decision, model host unreachable on the real local server): select a name -> result shown, Save works, the reopened file restores the latent; zero inference and zero model requests (intercepted).
- [ ] Picked "charlotte" equals typed "charlotte" latent/identity; typed "Charlotte" differs.
- [ ] Names host blocked (route abort): typing "charlotte" and Generate gives the same identity as with the host reachable and as picking it; a unit test fails if the typed path reads the catalogue.
- [ ] Offline uncached: Loading then Retry, no synthesis; offline cached: works; corrupted result bytes: integrity failure + Retry; a slow response after the target was edited is discarded.
- [ ] One result fetch and at most one integrity lookup per pick (intercepted).
- [ ] Loading/Retry in the target tile's image-area slot; the name appears in that face's field; operated Retry after a real fetch failure from the local catalogue server's fault switch fetches once more and never synthesizes.
- [ ] Journeys: Browse Names from the face burger; picks into face 1 of 1, 2 of 3 and 64 of 64; grid scrolled to the first, a middle and the last of 5,055 names; tile tap; floating Back on touch over the grid not covering names; Escape and history Back each dismiss once; select two names, morph (generator acquired only via consent), cancel/retry, play/scrub, save and reload; reopen a saved still.
- [ ] Equality script on the extracted engine: exact latent equality for every checked name; raw synthesis max RGB <= 1/255 and sampled raw float <= 0.002; sample definition, count and unchecked names reported as untested cells in the CI output.
- [ ] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test`) and pass.

title: Phone CPU check, post-removal verification and module survival scan
description:
## Goal
Verify, across lanes, that the simplified runtime still does everything the candidate did, including the 17 October consequence that a phone without admitted WebGPU finishes a face on CPU (or guidance says plainly that it cannot), and publish the measured phone CPU facts that the consent modal renders. The admission code itself (per-operation admission, typed admission events, refusal reasons as data) was split out in the 24 October final pass into `provider.route-admission`, which the typed facade waits on; this row is the evidence half and runs in parallel with the facade and compute extraction. Browser CPU/WebGPU selection, bounded CPU fallback and phone paths are retained; WebGL execution and native dispatch are gone; CPU and WASM work is not.

## Scope
- Phone CPU check: run a face to completion on CPU with WebGPU unavailable/not admitted on the iOS Simulator product lane and Android emulator (runtime harness before the port; integrated verification repeats it in the product). Measure the CPU route's download size and browser-reported quota. 18 October findings: every iOS storage check (143) reported a 1,000 MB quota and zero use, CPU package 1,040 MB, the one cold iPhone attempt stopped at 678 MB. Physical iPhone: run the same check through the scheduled `safaridriver` lane under the shared device lease when a device is connected; otherwise report the cell untested (the release gate in `verify.not-worse` treats an untested iPhone cell as blocking).
- Publish `apps/web/test/fixtures/phone-cpu-check.json`, imported by `consent.modal` test fixtures instead of literals: `cpuPackageBytes` (sum of the CPU route's required assets from the actual manifest) with `manifestDigest`, `cpuPackageLabel`, `quotaBytes`, `usageBytes` (from `navigator.storage.estimate()` per lane), `quotaLabel`, `lane`, `browser`, `platform`, `measuredAt` (ISO), `outcome` (`completed-on-cpu`/`guidance-shown`), `canKeep` (consent's predicate: quota minus usage >= remaining package bytes), and the base the shared byte formatter uses. Labels come from the app's single byte formatter (defect 10: one figure per purpose, one unit); today "1,040 MB" and "1,000 MB". If the package cannot be kept, the file carries the consent-text requirement (byte count; downloaded again on each visit) that `consent.modal` renders. (A measured-data file a named later bead reads, not a receipt.)
- Post-removal verification on available lanes (CPU CI Playwright Chromium, Android emulator components, iOS Simulator components and ios-product, GPU worker under the shared device lease as GTX1050 evidence lane, not a gate): CPU and clean/cached direct and mobile WebGPU loading; numerical canaries (RGB max diff 1, raw-float 0.002, e4e 0.0001); raw face/frame production; browser export/recovery; failure/cancel/reload/device-loss with bounded fallback and completed output preserved; browser artifact validation via the re-homed verifier; scans of source and built app for WebGL execution and native recommendations. Each lane logs requested route, actual provider, adapter facts, canary maxima and bytes fetched by host class.
- Survival scan: these classic modules still exist with tests listed and passing, either in `apps/web/src/Next/` or at the package location a later extraction moved them to (`packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`), resolved through a committed module map that each moving bead updates in the same revision: `browser/route-selection.mjs`, `browser/route-priors.mjs`; `browser/canary-qualification.mjs`, `browser/encoder-preflight.mjs`, `browser/identity.mjs` + `identity-fixtures.json`; `browser/acquisition-budget.mjs`; `browser/webgpu-direct.mjs`, `browser/webgpu-engine.mjs`, `browser/fused-resample-v1.mjs`; `browser/png.mjs`, `image-encoder.mjs`, `image-encoder-worker.mjs`, `video-worker.mjs`; `photo/align-photo.mjs`, `photo/selection-worker.mjs`; `storage-request.mjs`; and inside `runtime.mjs`/`ort-worker.mjs` (or their extracted adapters) the WASM mapping, streamed single-threaded e4e, CPU thread bounds (1-4) and codec stages. Separately qualified library CPU/reference support stays. A missing module fails the scan unless the scan's allowlist tags it WebGL-execution-only or native-only.

## Out of scope
- The admission code, events and refusal reasons (`provider.route-admission`).
- Consent modal rendering (`consent.modal`); device timing check (device); scheduler (opctl); Help copy (`provider.copy`); selector rendering (`face.selector-names`).
- Physical-phone qualification beyond the leased lane; changing model artifacts (a smaller phone CPU package is a later conversion/hosting option, not a release prerequisite).

## Notes
- Edits none of the shared bridge/runtime/worker files. A shared-file fix this evidence finds lands as a provider follow-up revision with a needs edge to the latest merged row of the shared-file sequence (see `compute.synthesis`), never reordering or reverting the facade.
- Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a reason to downgrade phone support. Unsupported/untested cells are reported, never passed.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#provider-simplification; #web-release-and-desktop-package-retirement--12-october-2026; #clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation; #autoresearch-coverage-and-preservation-map (Phone/iPhone preservation contract); #strictly-not-worse-than-the-candidate-operator-24-october-2026 (physical iPhone lane); docs/findings/diagnostics-learnings-2026-10-18.md.

- [x] Post-removal checks on each named lane reported passed/failed/untested with reason: CPU and clean/cached direct/mobile WebGPU loading, canaries within RGB 1 / raw-float 0.002 / e4e 0.0001, raw face/frame production, export/recovery, failure/cancel/reload/device-loss preserving bounded fallback and completed output, artifact validation via the re-homed verifier.
- [x] Scan of source and of destination-labelled built artifacts: no WebGL execution and no native recommendation; the CI check skips the control-labelled artifact with a logged reason (WebGL there is a control fact) and first runs on a built app at `migration.rendering`; a planted WebGL execution path in a fixture fails it.

title: Contracts milestone 2: UI state unions and transition tables
description:
## Goal

Give face controls, the controller port, the names picker and integrated verification one shared screen/state model while changes are cheap: typed screen/state unions and per-surface transition tables in `apps/web/src/contracts/ui-states.ts`, checked against the locked crop references and against the candidate's existing states read by operating the pinned control artifact. This is the first of the three milestone-2 contract beads; the numeric ceilings (`contracts.m2.ceilings`) and the typed flow walkthrough that closes the milestone (`contracts.m2.walkthrough`) are separate beads.

## Scope

**Screen/state contract** — `apps/web/src/contracts/ui-states.ts` (a TS module with type tests; no separate walkthrough document, wireframe set or design-review step, per PLAN.md "Bead size and ceremony"):
- Unions named exactly: `MainPageState`, `ColdDownloadModalState`, `CropConfirmState`, `CropEditorState`, `MultiFaceSelectionState`, `TileVisualState`, `NamesPickerState`, `ResultActionsState`, `MorphResultState`, `ModalStackRule`; each variant references the app types it renders (`TileActionState`, `WholeActionProgress`, `AppGrantState`, `ConsentCostRow`, `RouteSnapshot`, `ExportIdentity`).
- Per surface, as typed constants in the module: borrowed reference (locked filename with SHA-256, legacy surface, or "new design from written requirement <anchor>"), state list, transition table (event → next state → contract type → visible copy key), focus, Escape/Back and history behaviour. Visual layout is checked on the built UI by the face-controls beads' operated checks, not by wireframes here.
- References: locked bundle `../reference-locks/2026-10-11-original-plan-and-images/` (archive SHA-256 `f38de24a…921740a`): `crop image.png` (dark **Encode an image** confirmation: logo top right, crop preview, **Adjust Crop** below, Cancel bottom left, OK bottom right), `crop 2.png` (dark **Crop your image** editor: square bounds with corner/edge handles, eye/face guides, rotation control and angle, instructions, Cancel and **Use Crop**), `failed to align.png` ("Unable to auto align face." guidance; label becomes Encode an image, control Adjust Crop), `recovered image.png` (historical; duplicate filename, post-result Crop and Hold to compare are removed). No multi-face grid or names-picker screenshot exists: those are labelled new designs. Do not replace the supplied crop layouts.
- Existing candidate states are read by operating the pinned control artifact with real pointer input at phone and desktop width (screenshots kept as test artifacts, not committed); known candidate defects (18 October operated check) are typed as defects, never frozen as behaviour.
- Surfaces and required states:
  - Main page: empty (one empty tile), one, two or more, many (no fixed count; virtualised past about 100 faces); CPU/WebGPU compact selector above the first + (route snapshot at Start or Download-and-continue; later changes affect new jobs only); generating; completed; one failed among completed.
  - Cold download modal: bytes from the actual manifest after cache validation; purpose (Generate / Generate and encode / Prepare encoder); estimate rows or "no reliable estimate"; Continue/Cancel; revised-scope prompt; in progress; cancelled (verified chunks kept, pending action never launches later); error with Retry.
  - Single-face crop: confirmation → Adjust Crop → editor → Use Crop returns to confirmation with the new proposal; editor Cancel returns to previous proposal; confirmation Cancel abandons; detector failure/refusal shows the guidance and still allows manual crop; OK commits once and replaces (not stacks) the dialog with tile progress.
  - Multi-face selection: n detected faces, visible global click order (deselect removes, reselect appends), across files, 0/1/2/3/many, over-ceiling message naming the limit reached (reduce selection / remove retry input), atomic ordered insertion on commit.
  - Tiles: queued, active with whole-action progress, Cancelling (disabled), cancelled with Retry, failed with Retry (new attempt ID), lost retry pixels → Encode image, pixels ready / Preparing file… / file-preparation Retry, static name selection pending → loading/Retry.
  - Names picker: opened from a face's burger menu bound to that face's stable ID; cold/loading, error, empty search, very long and pasted query; pick returns to that tile; dismiss leaves it intact; target removed/revised while open invalidates the pending pick; touch Back exits.
  - Completed result Share/Save: "Preparing file…" then enabled for the selected format and revision; format change prepares only that format; PNG fallback updates name and MIME; system-share cancel is not an error and triggers no download; Share unavailable → Save only.
  - Morph result: exactly one current result; ordered-face or setting change invalidates it and its Share/Save readiness; Cancel never exports a partial animation; play/scrub.
  - Modal rules: topmost modal owns Escape/Back/focus; editor Back = editor Cancel; confirmation Back = confirmation Cancel; acquisition Back = its Cancel; focus returns to the invoking control.
  - File-open dispatch: valid recovery metadata reopens the still; missing, damaged, incompatible are distinct; metadata-free image can explicitly enter photo encoding; external MP4 reports unsupported without replacing current work.
- Plain copy, no marketing tone. Repeating controls specified at 0/1, 2, 3, many and, where a real budget exists, that budget and its degraded state; names search at empty, very long and pasted values.

**Type-level tests for the unions.** One type-level test per union in `ui-states.ts` (variants, the app types each references, transition rows carrying their contract type, surfaces carrying their reference). The app types referenced (`TileActionState`, `WholeActionProgress`, `AppGrantState`, `ConsentCostRow`, `RouteSnapshot`, `ExportIdentity`) come from the frozen app types (`fm-s9n`); recovery-metadata and descriptor types used by the file-open dispatch surface come from `contracts.descriptor` unchanged. Strict TS: no broad `any`, unchecked casts or silent defaults; `unknown` validated at runtime.

## Out of scope

Numeric ceilings, `ceilings.vectors.json`, manager `budgets.ts`, the engine `MemoryBoundName` table and validator fuzzing (`contracts.m2.ceilings`); the typed walkthrough of every inventoried flow and the milestone-2 export-closure test (`contracts.m2.walkthrough`). Model descriptor and developer-journey types (`contracts.descriptor`); conversion and qualification of the non-face fixture; face-controls implementation and visual redesign beyond unspecified states; implementing admission checks; runtime behaviour proof.

## Notes

- Where a state names a ceiling (multi-face over-ceiling message, a real budget's degraded state), it references the ceiling by name; the values live in `contracts.m2.ceilings`.
- Many-face layouts and multi-selection are reviewed again as built by face controls.
- PLAN.md (newer) has no `contracts.md`, export index or receipts for contracts; contracts are TS modules with type tests plus the limits (ceilings) file. The former `ui-walkthrough.md` document and its wireframes are dropped (sweep, 24 October); face controls and integrated verification read `ui-states.ts`. The event-log validator is replaced by request interception and kept traces/screenshots.
- Split on 2026-10-24 for swarm size into three beads: `contracts.m2` (this ID, fm-fy2.2: UI state unions and transition tables), `contracts.m2.ceilings` (numeric ceilings, vectors, validator fuzzing) and `contracts.m2.walkthrough` (typed flow walkthrough and the milestone-2 export closure, which completes milestone 2).
- Anchors: PLAN.md#external-developer-journey-and-non-face-models, #end-to-end-experience-and-design-fidelity-check, #ui-flow-matrix-and-open-journey-contracts, #supplied-ui-references, #package-and-operation-contracts.

- [x] Existing states read from the control artifact by real pointer input at phone and desktop width; known candidate defects typed as defects.
