title: Repair links, remotes and integrations after the rename
description:
## Goal
After the organization rename, make every active clone, help, source and Actions link and every name-bound integration resolve to the right repository under `facemorph-me`, keep immutable provenance distinguishable from current URLs, update the candidate's own organization links through its ordinary qualified flow, and prove the rename acceptance from PLAN.md. Integrations that bind by name otherwise break silently or bind to a reclaimed old name; classic publication waits on this for its final README URL, and `promote.py` depends on it.

## Scope
- **Repository links.** Merge the prepared edit branches after their ordinary checks: monorepo docs (AGENTS.md, plan pointer docs, README), sibling repos (`facemorph-names`, `encoder4editing` readmes and homepage fields), non-candidate classic paths (`self-host/Dockerfile` clone URL; provenance mapping in `self-host/REPOSITORY-PROVENANCE.md` and `self-host/frontend-overlay/source.json`). Repository homepage fields updated.
- Immutable provenance gets a current-resolution mapping; historical bytes, frozen reports and model digests are never rewritten. Archived `checkface` content stays as-is.
- Classic `self-host` edits go to the frozen distribution branch (D4) or are superseded by vendoring; never merged into `master`. `self-host/frontend-overlay/source/src/Config.fs` source/repository links classified active point at the renamed classic repository; its `apiAddr` stays unchanged (historical and classic only).
- Monorepo issue form `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.yml` with fields matching what the candidate's Report-error link pre-fills (read the `ISSUE_REPO` URL builder in classic `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` at the frozen revision: title, body sections, labels). The candidate's own link is not changed by this.
- **Integrations.** Re-check every integration from the identity scan: Cloudflare GitHub app/project connections, webhooks, Actions permissions/variables, OIDC subject restrictions (they embed owner/repo names), package/container owner paths, names hosting connection, Vercel project, the retained-run artifact lookup in `research-built-ui-media-v1.yml`. Fix name-bound ones (OIDC subjects, webhooks, `uses` paths). Resolve the research workflow's retained run by repository ID; frozen evidence gets a lookup mapping. Confirm each publisher still targets the right source and branch; no publisher is added or moved; no shared secret recreated; reconnect only where verification shows it is needed. Remaining needs-inspection items keep their reason.
- **Candidate-source links** (ordinary work on the working candidate, operator 18 October), on a non-deploying classic branch (e.g. `delivery/candidate-edits`) from `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, run in `facemorph.me-classic` per its development guide: `src/Config.fs` source links; `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` `ISSUE_REPO` (stays at the candidate's actual repo, new org prefix); `hosting/next-static/promote.py` `REMOTE` (now the wrong `check-face/facemorph.me`; must be `facemorph-me/facemorph.me-classic` while promoting retained candidate artifacts) and its workflow-source validation (verified against the renamed repo ID in a non-publishing dry run); `src/explain.md`. Candidate links are not pointed at the monorepo before new-app handover.
- This candidate edit merges **on its own**, not in the candidate edit-set batch, because it waits for the rename: candidate's ordinary qualification, merge to `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, then `post-delivery-check --mode app` on next.facemorph.me and the retired-host scan on the deployed artifact. If it lands after an early promotion, the promoted artifact changes only with a later promotion.
- **Acceptance run.** Run the rename check script, the org-link scan and the link checker over all repos and the built candidate.

## Out of scope
The rename itself; moving publishers (delivery); the classic README publication (classic delivery); native updater endpoint migration (retirement disposition only); any deploy other than the ordinary candidate merge above.

## Notes
- Any changed build gets its normal checks before publishing; a rename is not a deploy, so a changed built artifact is reported separately.
- PLAN.md gets the `check-face` → `facemorph-me` link-prefix update as an ordinary edit (no approval step, operator 24 October); any other PLAN.md wording change is left to the planner.
- Organization branding is not a prerequisite for domain handover, early promotion or API retirement.
- Old tracker edges gating the rename behind release qualification and classic are stale and not kept.
- Plan: #organization-rename-execution, #organization-rename-first-known-reference-changes, #delivery-and-publication.

title: Independently accept published npm packages and public documentation
description:
## Goal
The operator explicitly requested this deferred acceptance gate on 12 October 2026; it is the one operator-authorized acceptance bead, and its requirements below are preserved intact. Perform an unbiased acceptance review of the **actual published npm distributions and their public documentation**, to check whether someone outside the project can really use what we shipped. No packages are published or accepted by creating or rewriting this record. Publication can occur before this review; packages are not declared independently accepted until it passes. This final package-usability gate does not block an earlier operator-controlled web promotion or retirement of `api.facemorph.me` / `checkface.facemorph.me`.

## Scope
**Reviewer and inputs**
- The reviewer must not be an author of those implementations and starts with no implementation conversation, no private checkout (the public tagged repository is allowed for the converter, which is not an npm package), no workspace aliases, private lab assets or unpublished setup instructions. They get actual package names/versions, public docs/model-acquisition references and declared supported capabilities only.
- Reviewer logistics (16 October), settled before the first package publication (written and committed by `pkgdocs.release`, fm-oagi, which `delivery.packages` needs): name the reviewer role (a person, or an agent session that did not author the packages) and how independence is ensured; fix the input packet (published names, versions, public documents only); set a bounded review budget in time and resources, because the journey includes conversion, hosting, inference and a round trip; list the worker/browser environments available; commit a report template (registry versions/integrity, lockfile, identities, copied commands, outputs, friction log, verdict per capability). The budget bounds only the review session, not implementation; any journey skipped for budget or environment reasons is recorded as unverified, never passed, and the bead stays open until a later run covers it. An author-run smoke test is never substituted for the review.

**What publishes (settled 17 October)**
- Three TypeScript packages on npm: the engine (`stylegan-js`, no model or resources bundled), the browser model manager and the Cloudflare model host (the journey needs all three from the registry). The converter ships as the pinned container with its opt-in Compose service at a tagged public release, not an npm package. Real names and scope chosen at publication by registry availability check (working names first, operator-controlled scope as fallback). npm credentials are an execution prerequisite, not a decision gate.
- Prerequisites: immutable registry versions with public docs/examples; supported provider/browser/model boundaries and converter/hosting instructions published; legally obtainable qualified model assets under the documented acquisition path. A local `npm pack` is preflight, not completion. Review any engine/manager/hosting distribution advertised as released and follow the converter's actual public distribution/docs. No dependency on unrelated native/API/research completion.

**Acceptance journey and checklist (pass, fail or unverified with reason per line; nothing passes from an author's statement, internal example, typecheck or tarball scan)**
1. A clean external project installs the exact **registry** versions; record versions, integrity hashes and the lockfile.
2. Trusted checkpoint acquisition per public docs (source, digest, terms).
3. Conversion with the public tagged converter container: build, convert, verify with the upstream reference check.
4. Static hosting under the reviewer's control per public docs (no FaceMorph hostname, catalogue, alias or secret).
5. Manager-loaded inference and a morph.
6. Direct caller-loaded engine use without the manager.
7. PNG and lossless-WebP export and reopen: exact recovery values, lossless decoded pixels.
8. The documented non-face example and its descriptor/support boundary; no face detector or e4e download for non-face generation.
9. Emitted JS, types, `exports` and worker assets; public build integration (bundler, worker and WASM paths, COOP/COEP for threaded routes, single-thread behaviour).
10. Real model identity and numerical evidence against the frozen or descriptor-specific tolerances.
11. Progress, abort, errors and disposal; cold and warm costs; no network at package construction or status reads (from intercepted requests).
12. README/API docs, copyable commands, licences/notices, model terms, ownership/resource semantics, errors, troubleshooting and examples, as part of usability.
13. Installed tarball inspection for missing files, repository-only paths, secrets or bundled weights (`package-tarball-content-scan` may be one input, never the verdict).
14. Actual advertised targets only; unsupported Node/browser/model cells are clear limitations, not inferred support.
- Friction log: every undocumented step or confusing instruction, with its doc location. Record browser/provider/model/runtime identity, copied commands and outputs.

**Synthesis and compression acceptance**
- Compare raw network output before compression against independent qualified references for the same model/input/noise/settings with frozen small tolerances: FFHQ product canaries max RGB error 1 (0–255) and max sampled raw-float absolute error 0.002; full reference suites keep their own coverage; other models need independently qualified descriptor-specific references/tolerances; e4e max absolute latent error 0.0001 where applicable. No widened tolerances or visual-only synthesis acceptance. Encoded files need no byte equality; compression/container differences are acceptable; lossy exports use practical visual quality and dimensions/orientation/format checks; lossless helpers preserve supplied pixels; recovery values stay exact and integrity metadata describes each actual payload. Compression never excuses synthesis drift.

**Verdict, fixes and delivery outcome**
- The verdict names usable capabilities and concrete failures/gaps. If instructions need unpublished help or an advertised journey fails, the bead stays open/deferred; fix, publish a **new** version, then independently recheck the actual registry bytes. Never overwrite a published version or point the reviewer at local source.
- Completion requires a retained independent acceptance report linked to those published versions, including docs. The report states the outcome per package; the versions and tarball integrity the review accepted are compared by script with those the publication workflow recorded, and a mismatch is recorded as the review having accepted something else. Package acceptance is never inferred from publication.

## Out of scope
Author smoke tests (`pkgdocs.release`). Publishing (`delivery.packages`).

## Notes
- Newer PLAN.md (24 October) keeps this report as a retained file because it is this operator-requested bead's deliverable; the generic per-bead receipt schema is dropped. The reviewer packet and report template replace the former `docs/decisions/` logistics entry.
- Ordering: the logistics part (reviewer role, packet, budget, template) is committed by `pkgdocs.release` (fm-oagi, moved there in the 24 October final pass because nothing that runs after publication can gate it); this bead runs the review after publication (it depends on fm-96v).
- Anchors: PLAN.md #independent-published-package-acceptance, #external-developer-journey-and-non-face-models, #synthesis-correctness-and-export-quality, #delivery-and-publication. Existing record fm-fy2.21 (operator-authorized 12 October), extended with the 16–17 October additions.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Reviewer role, input packet, review budget, environments and report template committed before the first package publication.
- [ ] An independent non-author reviewer installs the exact registry versions into a clean external project and follows only public docs through the declared generation/morph/export/recovery/direct-caller/non-face journeys; records versions, integrity, lockfile, identities, commands, outputs, friction and support limits; advertised journeys and docs are usable.
- [ ] The report has a verdict (pass, fail or unverified with reason) for each of the 14 checklist lines, plus the friction log; numerical lines use the frozen or descriptor-specific tolerances.
- [ ] Any fix publishes a new version and the affected lines are rechecked independently against the new registry bytes; no published version is overwritten.
- [ ] Skipped journeys recorded as unverified, never passed; no author-run smoke substituted.
- [ ] Retained independent acceptance report linked to the published versions and docswith the outcome per package, and a script comparison shows the accepted versions/integrity equal the published ones.

title: Research evaluator and workload specs (deferred until a campaign is requested)
description:
## Goal

When a targeted research campaign is requested, provide the machinery that turns driver runs into honestly scoped verdicts: a versioned workload spec schema and campaign specs, an evaluator core that wraps existing drivers instead of interpreting generic success, driver adapters, a control/control noise baseline that locks margins before any candidate benefit is observed, and overlap/warming adapters that model consent and ownership explicitly. Invalid, missing or expected-failure cases must never become speed wins or release certificates. Not on the release path: migration and cutover do not wait for it; only optional verified-cache warming waits on its adapters. Opened only when a campaign is requested.

## Scope

**Workload spec schema** (JSON schema + validator, shared with the evaluator)
- Fields frozen before candidates: workload, timing boundary, source/artifact/runtime/model/fixture/evaluator digests, provider, device/browser, cache state, network, visibility (visible tab vs hidden/background) per cohort, warmup/order, expected outcomes, required cells, statistical method, confidence level, sample and confirmation rules, invalid-pair/invalid-run handling, practical margins from control/control evidence, protected metrics (first/nth face, confirmed photo, complete video, first/repeated Save, restore, no lockups, bytes, memory reservations, cancellation), screen vs confirmation identity, regression decision rules.
- Fixed 32-frame / 16 FPS / 1024 px workload where supported. Initial comparisons: discarded warmup and ABBA ×3, raw distributions, paired effects; cold profiles empty; baseline warmup in separate profiles (no optional-warmup false cache state). Cohorts: empty cache, cached files/new browser, live resident session, cached output, restored result — cold, warm and output-cache cases distinguishable. Finish boundaries: decoded/drawn face, useful scrub frame, playable video, prepared file, Save/share handoff (`img.src` is not a rendered finish; share-sheet handoff is not delivery). Metadata-free photos must execute the actual encoder.

**Named gates**: specs for package extraction, UI port and provider refactor comparisons using current harnesses and the pinned control artifact or a qualified rebuild, each naming control digest, cells, method and decision rule, mapped to retained cells and CI/worker roles (no whole-matrix rerun per small idea). Correctness failure rejects; missing supported evidence is inconclusive; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a performance keep.

**Campaign specs** (one each, fresh run labels; system-imposed waits plus the full useful journey; automated dwell labelled synthetic; timeline-based overlap accounting; each names the overlap/warming adapter version it requires):
1. Consented acquisition during input selection — empty/partial cache, Generate vs approved Generate and encode, fixed selection/crop dwell, seed request while encoder assets transfer. Protected: consent → first useful face; photo selection → reconstruction/file-ready totals; stage overlap on a timeline; actual bytes; no foreground lockup; Cancel and route failure. Synthesis-first ordering exists; current prefetch pauses for foreground work, so broader overlap is new.
2. Verified-cache runtime warming — cached files/new browser vs resident session, eager selected-generator preparation vs demand load, immediate next-face request, missing/corrupt shard and memory-constrained cases. Protected: reload → first/nth new face; CPU/GPU mapping/load/readback; peak live reservations; foreground wait; zero speculative network (asserted by request interception); recovery without inference. Cache-only prefetch creates no session today; eager hydration is a hypothesis.
3. Photo preparation and e4e lifecycle — padded/nonpadded metadata-free photos, first/next encode, constrained phone teardown vs qualified desktop reuse. Protected: source → confirmed → reconstructed photo; per-shard verified-local read/create/run/copy/teardown; memory/bytes; cancellation. Reuse warm-hydration/padded-photo/streamed-e4e findings; no revival of rejected precision changes (no silent fp16 e4e or tolerance widening).
- Instrumentation: explicit bundle grant, ownership/request/attempt IDs, approved transfer timeline; natural-user/OS-picker observations are separate evidence.

**Evaluator core**: keeps `run.py` for budgets, cleanup and leases; consumes specs; verifies frozen digests before running. Verdict classes: execution, validity, correctness, non-regression, paired-benefit, architecture; every verdict reports effect uncertainty. Expected-failure tests can pass cleanup/correctness without becoming timings. Appends scoped outcomes to the ledger only for evaluated outcomes. No release-qualification field; a `keep` creates no integration-commit or deployment record. Frozen historical scripts/reports keep their bytes; new campaign code is versioned.

**Driver adapters**: versioned adapters for the maintained built-UI paired driver and `scripts/next-e2e.md` flows, mapping outputs to verdict inputs with declared timing boundaries and correctness checks; historical analysis pins old source/artifacts and is never repurposed as the current baseline.

**Noise baseline**: control/control runs per supported workload cell on available workers under the lease; complete context and raw noise reports split into within-run, separate-browser-start and rebuild variability; margins, sample/confirmation rules and stopping decisions frozen in the specs, each margin citing its level and control/control pairs; ledger rows appended as baseline evidence.

**Overlap/warming adapters**: model the explicit bundle grant, ownership/request/attempt IDs, approved transfer timeline, stage timelines and independent confirmation, built against the contract grant types; zero-speculative-network assertions via request interception; exercised against the app once acquisition consent exists. The existing auto-consent/file-injection driver cannot establish native chooser latency.

**Outputs**: copied to a durable output location (outside transient CI artifacts) and cited by the round record; private/local-only raw files labelled.

## Out of scope

Running the campaigns or the named gates (optional research after features exist); candidate comparisons beyond the noise baseline.

## Notes

- Deferred: one optional bead per PLAN.md 24 Oct ("the research evaluator ... is one deferred bead"); stays deferred until a campaign is requested.
- Research discipline: lease before every heavy step; fresh run labels; append-only ledger/log; numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances first; results are experimental evidence at their scope; new opportunities are proposals.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#research-workload-design, #research-evaluator, #targeted-autoresearch-launch-and-preserved-history, #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Spec schema and validator committed; the example spec validates; table-driven tests reject a spec missing any required field (outcomes, cells, statistical method, confidence, sample/confirmation rules, protected metrics, invalid-run handling, cohort, cache/network/visibility state, decision rule), a spec whose screen and confirmation sets share an identity, and a cold cohort sharing an optional warmup.
- [ ] Named-gate specs (package extraction, UI port, provider refactor) validate, each naming control digest, cells, method and decision rule.
- [ ] The three campaign specs pass the spec validator; each names its adapter version, marks dwell synthetic and declares timeline overlap fields.
- [ ] Evaluator unit tests: invalid run, missing cell, expected failure and correctness failure each give the right scoped verdict, never benefit; frozen-digest mismatch on control, candidate or fixture gives `invalid`; paired-benefit requires confirmation disjoint from screening, a complete screened list and an interval clearing the frozen margin — reused holdout, missing screened record or min-only claim give no benefit; screening-only correctness without the applicable full31 suite is `inconclusive`, never `keep`.
- [ ] Each driver adapter has fixture tests and one leased run against the control artifact; given a frozen historical path (e.g. `candidates/direct-rgba-media-v1/built-ui-analysis.md` or a `reviews/2026-10-10/` report) as control it refuses with a named error.
- [ ] Noise reports with raw data split by variability level and frozen margins citing their pairs; baseline ledger rows appended; outputs in the durable location.
- [ ] Overlap/warming adapter tests with synthetic timelines; a dry run against the control artifact records the timeline fields.
- [ ] Every spec validates and one dry run (no measurement claim) passes through `run.py` on a worker, journaled.

title: Scaffold workspaces, strict TS and Oxc gates
description:
## Goal

Turn the imported candidate into an npm-workspace monorepo with the four packages present as empty, building, packable placeholders, strict TypeScript, Oxlint/Oxfmt at their latest versions, a formatting-only baseline revision and read-only CI format/lint/type gates. Extraction acceptance (a package edit changes identity and triggers its checks) cannot be met before the workstreams it gates unless the workspaces exist first, and read-only gates protect every later revision.

## Scope

**Workspaces and TypeScript**
- Layout: `apps/web/` (imported JS closure keeping the `src/Next` structure, with temporary root paths for `desktop/runtime.mjs` and required `scripts/`), `packages/stylegan-js/`, `packages/browser-model-manager/`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host/`, `packages/model-conv/`, `autoresearch/`, `hosting/`, `scripts/`, root `package.json`/`package-lock.json`, `tsconfig.base.json`. npm workspaces only; no other package manager or orchestration framework.
- Each package is an empty placeholder that builds, emits declarations and packs (`npm pack`), with explicit `exports`.
- `tsconfig.base.json`: `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `isolatedModules`, type-only imports; scoped DOM, WebWorker and Node configs so shared contracts get no accidental globals; no package override of the strict flags.
- Scripts: `typecheck` (explicit, separate from bundling), declaration builds in workspace dependency order, aggregate `test`, `build:next` kept working.
- First lockfile at the latest release of every dependency: each declared as a caret range at its latest version (`npm install <pkg>@latest`), never an exact pin or a held-back version (operator, 24 October 2026). The lockfile records what resolved and CI installs with `npm ci`. No Wrangler: Cloudflare operations use the installed `cf` CLI (operator, 24 October 2026). Node: current LTS in CI; `engines` a range compatible with Oxc (`^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`). Never fetch `latest` at build time.
- Tools using the TypeScript compiler API (declaration emit, type-aware lint if enabled, Vite and test plugins) run under the latest TypeScript; a tool that fails is fixed or replaced, never held on an older TypeScript.
- Temporary JS interop through narrow adapters, each with tests; no mechanical `.mjs` → `.ts` renames.
- React 19/MUI upgrades land with the port, not here; this pins what the imported closure needs plus tooling.

**Oxc tooling**
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` as root devDependencies at their latest versions (caret ranges), run from the lockfile install, never `npx ...@latest`.
- Root `.oxlintrc.json` and `.oxfmtrc.json` (JSON, independent of TS loaders) with explicit overrides and ignore patterns; editor instructions in the dev guide.
- Scripts exactly: `lint` = `oxlint --deny-warnings`, `lint:fix` = `oxlint --fix`, `format` = `oxfmt`, `format:check` = `oxfmt --check`.
- Oxlint: correctness rules, native TypeScript, verified React and react-hooks rules, with browser UI, worker and Node tooling overrides. Oxfmt: print width 100, two-space indentation, import/package-field sorting off.
- Include authored app/package files, maintained scripts, configs, current docs. title: Parity run: every parity row exact; fix defects
description:
## Goal
Accept the application migration: on the TS/React milestone commit, every parity-tagged row of the frozen flow matrix behaves exactly as in the control artifact before the declared face-controls/static-names changes, with port defects fixed in TypeScript. End result of the initiative's port: the monorepo app offers the same features and journeys as `next.facemorph.me` plus the plan's declared changes, in strict TypeScript/React/Vite, without losing any integrated performance optimization (warm reuse, bounded worker/frame pipelines, cache recovery, background encoding, compressed session/video/scrub restoration). Integrated verification's app-flows result uses these parity rows.

## Scope
- Run the full parity harness (`migration.parity-harness`) on the TS/React milestone commit (merge of `migration.rendering`); fix port defects in TypeScript; rerun to green.
- Parity rows pass only when exact (structure/DOM contract, text, flow, project-JSON and recovery round trips); performance and retained cells per the shared no-regression protocol, including the four baseline-note items.
- `changed`, `new` and defect rows are excluded from this run and graded against the plan by their owners after parity; the run's output names each with its owner. Untestable rows are skipped with reason.
- A fix that reintroduces a candidate defect to make a row match is rejected: that row was misclassified, so retag it in the parity spec in the same PR with the reason.
- Source/asset identity and supported on-origin/file compatibility stay explicit; no old-server pixel/URL parity or phone pass is required.
- Context: the candidate UI is Fable/Elmish F# (`src/Next/Product.fs` about 1,470 dense lines; about 2,000 with `ProjectJson.fs`, `Contracts.fs`, `Runtime.fs`, `Assets/ModelAssets.fs` and shared `Config`, `FancyButton`, `Logos`, `ThemedApp`, `header`) calling `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` (about 620 lines) through about 60 functions. F# is never imported or built; the port reads it in classic at the frozen revision as specification and the control artifact is the behavioural oracle.

## Out of scope
- Declared UX changes (face controls, static names, provider selector move) land after parity in their own checked revisions. Compute extraction needs only the facade.

## Notes
- No time box, no fallback (operator, 17 October): a real blocker is fixed in TypeScript against the same control; never a .NET build, F# import or classic change. The two-week/25% checkpoint and container fallback are withdrawn.
- Versions: the port builds on the first destination lockfile (latest-stable React, MUI, Vite, TypeScript); MUI v4->v9 pixel differences reviewed, not gated; later dependency bumps are grouped revisions apart from behaviour changes; facade/port/build changes stay apart from engine changes.
- The old "threshold set at freeze, measured no threshold until then" is resolved by the parity spec: the threshold is every parity test passing exactly.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-migration; #ui-flow-matrix-and-open-journey-contracts; #existing-next-implementation-and-feature-disposition; #workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership.

title: Rebind the app to stylegan-js; harness proof and paired harness comparison against the candidate bridge
description:
## Goal
Finish compute extraction: the product actually runs on `stylegan-js` with its qualified CPU/WebGPU/mobile and WASM-helper behaviour, cancellation and performance mechanisms intact, and the duplicated engine code and every engine-originated download are gone from the app. The package surface, caller-loaded example and shared tarball content scan moved to `compute.package-surface` in the 24 October final pass. A cleaner package that loses Next behaviour, or a rebound app that is slower or less reliable than the candidate, fails the plan.

## Scope
**App rebinding**
- Replace the app's engine paths (`product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs`, `browser/ort-worker.mjs` behind the typed facade) with `stylegan-js` imports; delete duplicated engine code and every engine-originated download/cache path.
- The app keeps interaction, consent, input revisions, display URLs, retention and reporting transport.
- The app imports `stylegan-js` only through the package's `exports` entry points, never deep paths or workspace aliases. This row does not wait for `compute.package-surface`: if that row has not landed, this row adds the entries it needs to the exports map and `compute.package-surface` completes it (the two rows never edit the same shared bridge file).
- Before the TS/React milestone (`build:next` never bundles the imported source before the rendering port, `import.checks`), prove the rebinding where it can run: the real-bridge facade harness with real runtime bytes (first/nth face, confirmed photo, complete video, first/repeat Save, restore, cancellation, memory reservations), next-site.yml artifact/unit/import/geometry/integrity checks and `check-no-third-party.mjs`, exact CPU qualification through the harness, mobile-browser.yml android/ios eight components, and next-gpu-lane.yml (non-gating GTX1050 WebGPU evidence; software adapters rejected).
- Paired harness comparison under the strictly-not-worse rule (PLAN.md #strictly-not-worse-than-the-candidate-operator-24-october-2026): control = the imported candidate bridge and runtime at the facade commit in the same harness, same device/browser/provider/cache state, ABBA order, at least 5 pairs per cell. A timing, byte or memory measure fails when the 95% interval of the new/control ratio lies entirely above 1 plus the control/control noise margin of that cell; any run that produced a face, photo or video on the control and fails on the new build fails the row. Cells include desktop CPU in CI, WebGPU on a leased GPU worker and the mobile component lanes, and cold photo (empty profile) time-to-encoded-face with peak stored bytes: the app first runs e4e on manager handles here, which moves shard acquisition ahead of the engine (the boundary change `manager.quota` qualifies at component level). The CI output prints a per-cell table (cell, measure, pairs, ratio interval, margin, verdict).
- The product lanes on the Vite-built artifact (Chromium compiled UI, next-e2e real-ui-cpu, ios-product, next-matrix) and the product-level paired comparison against the pinned candidate artifact run in `compute.ported-app` once the TS/React milestone lands.
- Update a stale harness assertion only in the change that replaces the control it asserts; a removed test is listed in `tests/retired.txt` with its replacement.

## Out of scope
Product lanes and the product-level paired comparison on the ported app (`compute.ported-app`). Package surface, caller-loaded example, capability table and the tarball content scan (`compute.package-surface`). Morph frame production (morph.render). Crop fix (crop.fix). New performance campaigns. Public README/API docs and quickstart (pkgdocs.engine). npm publication (delivery). The typed-name equality re-run on the engine, now in `names.static-result`.

## Notes
- A single hosted-CI timing is never a verdict; the paired rule above is. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a reason to drop phone paths; the cell is reported untested.
- Ownership: the manager owns adapter shard reads and session lifecycle; compute moves only engine-side orchestration. Descriptor-driven morph geometry is morph's; dynamic-shape recovery schema is media's.
- Does not wait for the port (PLAN.md #compute-extraction). The built-app half of this row's acceptance is `compute.ported-app`, the "final integration joins both" point, created in the 24 October final pass so the extraction, crop and media chain runs in parallel with the TS/React port.
- Shared-file order (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October; revised in the 24 October final pass): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in one sequence enforced by needs edges, never concurrently: `provider.native` -> `provider.webgl` -> `provider.route-admission` -> `migration.project-json` (one-line ProjectJson import swap) -> typed facade (`migration.facade`) -> `compute.synthesis` -> `compute.photo-descriptor` -> `compute.app-rebind` -> `crop.fix` -> `crop.queue` -> `media.reader-wiring` -> `media.export` -> `media.schema` -> `morph.render` -> `morph.guards` -> `media.session` -> face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Rows that must not edit these files: `crop.repro`, `compute.blend`, `compute.package-surface`, `media.envelope`, `provider.admission` (evidence), `crop.ported-app` and `compute.ported-app` (acceptance on the ported app; a fix they need follows the out-of-turn rule below) and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept row; code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) until the bridge's own turn. A row that finds it must edit one of these files outside its turn adds a needs edge to the latest row in the sequence that edits it. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #compute-extraction, #stylegan-js, #workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership.

title: Dynamic-shape recovery schema, MP4 project metadata, blend recipe and media round-trip acceptance
description:
## Split (parallelism pass, 24 October 2026)
The package/core work of this bead moved to fm-fzzd (Recovery schema core: dynamic-shape schema, MP4 project metadata, blend recipe, format docs), which edits no shared file and starts as soon as its own inputs exist. This bead keeps: the real-bridge facade-harness round trips, earlier candidate stills through the bridge's file entry, and linking the format docs from app Help. The scope text below is kept for context; where it describes work now owned by fm-fzzd, that bead owns and accepts it and this bead consumes the result.

## Goal
Recovery-bearing exports are the product's only durable result. This row versions the recovery schema so non-face exports at other shapes reopen exactly and cannot be mixed with other checkpoints, keeps MP4 project metadata, its internal reader and the codec fallback correct, adds the weighted-blend recipe to saved files, and proves through the real bridge (and on the ported app in `compute.ported-app`) that every offered format exports and recovers before it is called supported, with the format limits documented. Every offered Save/Share format embeds and recovers latent/model data (and full project data for morphs); no metadata-free exports; no extra encode or inference pass for sharing.

## Scope
**Dynamic-shape schema**
- New schema version recording latent space/shape from the descriptor, checkpoint/model identity and generator identity; writers emit it; readers accept it plus schema-1 PNG and schema-2 PNG/WebP.
- Descriptive typed rejection of schema/version mismatches; unknown models stay viewable as media without editable inference. Cross-checkpoint equal-shape combination rejected. Contract changes go through a contract revision.
- Adds `inspect-still.matching-dynamic-shape` to the media.envelope reader suite.

**MP4 project metadata**
- Writer/reader as computational helpers with schema/version validation (dynamic-shape aware), embedding the ordered controls and morph settings needed to reconstruct the project.
- Codec fallback from `export-policy` (unchanged: `avc1.42002A`, WebCodecs 1024 then 512, FFmpeg 512, bitrate formula, framerate = fps). The produced file result carries `{width, height, route: 'webcodecs'|'ffmpeg', reason}` so the app discloses the actual resolution beside the result and, when known earlier, before Morph (morph.guards).
- Internal reader validation of produced files; corruption behaviour documented. External MP4 project-open UI stays deferred; MP4 format help says "Video; reopening this file as a project is not available in this release." The 512 × 512 path stays available.
- The FFmpeg fallback download (~32 MB) joins acquisition consent; this row only keeps the fallback correct.

**Blend recipe (per PLAN.md "Weighted face blend (advanced mode)")**
- A saved blend result carries ordinary recovery metadata holding the blended W+ latent plus a recipe: per slot, its kind (word, seed, name or photo), latent digest and weight. Typed words, seeds and file names are not embedded.
- Reopening a saved blend restores it as an ordinary face anywhere; the reader returns the recipe so the blend view can restore the weights of any slot whose latent digest matches.
- Export identity of a blend includes the recipe (slot latent digests and weights), so different blends never share a suggested name; the label comes from the existing filename rule (for example `blend-3-faces-k4p7s2.webp`). No blend-specific size or format: the full model frame (1024 × 1024 for the face model), WebP 0.8 default or PNG.

**Round-trip acceptance and docs**
- Real-bridge facade-harness round trips: generate a face, Save (WebP default), Save again (reuse, same name), Save PNG, re-import each through the bridge's file entry (installs without inference); morph, Save MP4, validate with the internal reader; promise/object-URL cleanup after each. The built-app matrix on the ported app is `compute.ported-app` and the recovery classes through the built UI are `crop.ported-app` (moved there in the 24 October final pass).
- Export quality rules: no byte identity between builds; lossy pixels need no exact parity (check dimensions, upright orientation, valid decode/playback to the last frame with the expected frame count, practical visual quality under the retained quality policy `../facemorph.me-classic/autoresearch/reviews/2026-10-10/quality-policy.md` or its re-homed copy); lossless helpers preserve pixels; model/latent/provenance values exact; a re-encoded file's integrity hash matches its own payload.

Converter manifests (conversion). Morph geometry and the MP4 probe at Morph accept (morph rows). App-visible MP4 import (deferred). The blend view and restoring slot weights in it (`face.blend-view`). Extra export formats (media.extra-formats). Share-sheet UX acceptance (face controls).

title: Bounded serial encode queue for confirmed crops, proven through the real bridge
description:
## Split (parallelism pass, 24 October 2026)
The package/core work of this bead moved to fm-d760 (Confirmed-crop encode queue module: ordered slots, one live encoder, per-slot cancel/retry, tab-only pixels), which edits no shared file and starts as soon as its own inputs exist. This bead keeps: wiring the queue into the bridge and the real-bridge facade-harness acceptance. The scope text below is kept for context; where it describes work now owned by fm-d760, that bead owns and accepts it and this bead consumes the result.

## Goal
Confirmed-crop encoding owns real encoding and fallback for every independently confirmed crop. This row adds the bridge-level queue that encodes an ordered list of frozen crops one e4e at a time, with per-slot cancel, retry and tab-only pixel ownership, which face controls' multi-selection builds on; and it proves the direct-e4e ruling end to end through the real bridge in the facade harness. Single-crop built-UI acceptance on the ported app is `crop.ported-app`; multi-selection built-UI acceptance is face controls'.

## Scope
**Queue (API owned here; `face.batch` renders tiles and controls on top and must not reimplement the queue, attempt identities or reference counting)**
- `enqueueConfirmedCrops(batchRevision, crops: ConfirmedCrop[]) -> SlotId[]`: click order preserved, one slot per crop, the shared acquisition/preparation prefix reported inside each slot's progress; independent progress and results per slot.
- Bounded concurrency: one live e4e encoder (`maxLiveEncoders = 1`, the plan's "initially one e4e encode at a time"; no simultaneous full encoder loads). Raising it needs measured evidence and a plan change.
- `cancelSlot(slotId)`: only that slot settles `cancelled`; queued siblings continue in frozen order; no implicit batch-wide Cancel after OK.
- `retrySlot(slotId) -> AttemptId`: only for a `cancelled`/`failed` slot whose pixels are retained; reuses the frozen `ConfirmedCrop` record and retained derived pixels (no second derivation, no detector call) and appends a new attempt ID to the pending queue; otherwise refused with `no-retained-pixels`. Neither Retry nor Remove reopens crop or allocates keypoints.
- `removeSlot(slotId)` / `replaceSlot(slotId, crop)` / `disposeBatch(batchRevision)` release references; late results for a removed or replaced slot are discarded by revision.
- Reference-counted, tab-only ownership of source/derived crop pixels for pending/running/retryable slots; success releases retry inputs; never persisted to OPFS, IndexedDB, sessionStorage or localStorage. After a reload unfinished slots report "lost; use Encode image" and never offer Retry.
- No partial failure restarts the batch or creates duplicate keypoints.
- Slot events `slot.queued`, `slot.started`, `slot.progress`, `slot.succeeded`, `slot.failed{kind}`, `slot.cancelled`, `slot.released` (slot ID, attempt ID, batch revision) for tests and the operation controller; test-build-only hook `pixelRefs(slotId) -> number`.
- Use the operation controller's scheduler interface if available. Contracts freeze batch, revision, cancellation and retry types. Candidate reference: `crop-queue.test.mjs`.

**Harness acceptance**
- In the real-bridge facade harness: forced detection/alignment failure after confirmation and a no-face confirmed crop each run exactly one real e4e attempt through the queue; Cancel before and after OK; stale revision (edit during encode). The single-crop built-UI and operated acceptance on the ported app is `crop.ported-app` (moved there in the 24 October final pass).

## Out of scope
Selection UI, badges, keypoint insertion, tile Cancel/Retry/Remove controls and their operated acceptance at 1/2/3/8 slots (`face.batch`). Global scheduler permits (operation controller). Crop modal redesign fidelity (face controls).

## Notes
- Shared-file order (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October; revised in the 24 October final pass): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in one sequence enforced by needs edges, never concurrently: `provider.native` -> `provider.webgl` -> `provider.route-admission` -> `migration.project-json` (one-line ProjectJson import swap) -> typed facade (`migration.facade`) -> `compute.synthesis` -> `compute.photo-descriptor` -> `compute.app-rebind` -> `crop.fix` -> `crop.queue` -> `media.reader-wiring` -> `media.export` -> `media.schema` -> `morph.render` -> `morph.guards` -> `media.session` -> face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Rows that must not edit these files: `crop.repro`, `compute.blend`, `compute.package-surface`, `media.envelope`, `provider.admission` (evidence), `crop.ported-app` and `compute.ported-app` (acceptance on the ported app; a fix they need follows the out-of-turn rule below) and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept row; code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) until the bridge's own turn. A row that finds it must edit one of these files outside its turn adds a needs edge to the latest row in the sequence that edits it. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #confirmed-crop-encoding, #confirmed-crop-and-ordered-multi-selection-flow (encoding parts).

title: Morph acceptance checks: frame budget, MP4 probe, identical-neighbour rule
description:
## Goal
Known morph limits must be found before expensive work. This bead adds the checks run when Morph is accepted, before any acquisition or inference: the frame budget, MP4 availability, and the identical-neighbour rule (candidate defect 6), each with a plain message in Morph status. Parent-intent scheduling (`morph.guards.intent`) and the built-app matrix with the paired comparison (`morph.guards.acceptance`) are separate beads that follow this one.

## Scope
**Frame budget**
- Pure function (selected count, geometry/settings, actual output shape) -> ok | over-budget reason. The limit is a budget, not a fixed count: frame memory, storage and time per route from the contracts ceilings (`apps/web/src/contracts/ceilings.ts`, written from measurements; this row makes no new measurement). Until that file carries a measured frame budget for a route, the classic 4,096-frame path value (`video-worker.mjs`, `last-result.mjs`) is that route's budget. There is no face count limit; the analytics `frames` range ([0, 4096] in `analytics.mjs` NUMBERS) widens to the budget so longer morphs are recorded, not clamped.
- Called at Morph acceptance before any acquisition or inference; message in `.next-morph-reason`/`.next-status` naming the limit reached and the estimate, with the useful recovery (reduce length in the existing More options). Never truncate selected faces; batch pixel limits and frame limits have separate messages; no new settings screen. Independently requested photo encoding need not wait for a future morph to fit. (Defect 18: a 65-face morph fails with a generic project error. The port has no face cap, so a many-face morph either fits the budget or gets this plain over-budget reason before frame inference.)

**MP4 probe**
- Fixed order: WebCodecs `avc1.42002A` at 1024, then 512, then the FFmpeg 512 fallback only if its asset is cached or inside the approved acquisition scope (acquisition consent asks for it). Settings from `export-policy`. Returns available resolution or unavailable reason.
- Runs before the first synthesis of the morph; with no route, zero synthesis, an explanation in Morph status, ready faces stay saveable, and an interactive preview is never described as an exported video.
- When 512 is chosen (WebCodecs or FFmpeg), Morph status says the video will be 512 × 512 before frames start, and the result shows the actual resolution beside the format/result actions.
- A later codec failure keeps frames and offers export-only Retry that never re-runs inference. Unavailable-codec checks run in a real browser without the codec (open-source Chromium has no H.264); they add no physical-device qualification.

**Identical neighbours (defect 6)**
- Today the same word twice, or A, B, A, fails with "This project is invalid or uses an unsupported format." Every product morph is a closed loop (`product-bridge.mjs` builds all five shapes with `closed: true`; `latent-path-v1` checks `controls[i]` with `controls[(i + 1) % n]`, rejecting chord norm below 1e-12).
- Rule: refuse a morph when any two cyclically adjacent faces are the same (face i and i+1, and last and first); non-adjacent repeats are allowed. A,A refused; A,B,B refused; A,B,A refused (closing pair); A,B,A,C and A,B,C allowed.
- "Same" = equal latent digest and model identity, or latent difference norm below 1e-12. Display labels are never compared (two words resolving to one latent are the same face; the same word under different models is not).
- Pre-check at Morph acceptance before any acquisition or inference, with a plain message naming the faces, e.g. "Faces 3 and 1 are the same, and the loop goes from face 3 back to face 1. Change one of them or add a different face between them." Re-checked when inputs change; a valid change clears it.

## Out of scope
Parent-intent scheduling, one current result and invalidation of stale results (`morph.guards.intent`); the built-app five-mode matrix, retained lanes and paired comparison (`morph.guards.acceptance`). Face-entry admission checks, Morph button/progress/Cancel presentation and face input UI (face controls). Scheduler implementation (operation controller). FFmpeg asset consent (acquisition consent). Format controls (face controls). New performance campaigns. Setting the frame-budget values (`contracts.m2.ceilings`, fm-2o8q).

## Notes
- Split on 2026-10-24 for swarm size into three beads, edited in this order: `morph.guards` (this ID, fm-fy2.9: frame budget, MP4 probe, identical-neighbour rule), `morph.guards.intent` (parent-intent scheduling and one current result) and `morph.guards.acceptance` (built-app matrix, retained lanes and the paired comparison against the pinned control). The first two edit the shared files in turn; the third edits none.
- The closed-loop A,B,A rule was chosen during bead conversion and is listed in PLAN.md "Planner proposals awaiting a veto". Removable clause: if vetoed, the A,B,A test flips and the message text changes; the geometry check is untouched. Rejected alternatives: dropping the closing pair for linear (needs a forbidden `GEOMETRY_VERSION` bump), or silently skipping the duplicate. No `docs/decisions/` entry (24 October rule).
- Shared-file order (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October; revised in the 24 October final pass): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in one sequence enforced by needs edges, never concurrently: `provider.native` -> `provider.webgl` -> `provider.route-admission` -> `migration.project-json` (one-line ProjectJson import swap) -> typed facade (`migration.facade`) -> `compute.synthesis` -> `compute.photo-descriptor` -> `compute.app-rebind` -> `crop.fix` -> `crop.queue` -> `media.reader-wiring` -> `media.export` -> `media.schema` -> `morph.render` -> `morph.guards` -> `media.session` -> face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Rows that must not edit these files: `crop.repro`, `compute.blend`, `compute.package-surface`, `media.envelope`, `provider.admission` (evidence), `crop.ported-app` and `compute.ported-app` (acceptance on the ported app; a fix they need follows the out-of-turn rule below) and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept row; code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) until the bridge's own turn. A row that finds it must edit one of these files outside its turn adds a needs edge to the latest row in the sequence that edits it. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.
- The frame budget is read from `apps/web/src/contracts/ceilings.ts` (`contracts.m2.ceilings`, fm-2o8q) when it carries a measured value for the route; until then the classic 4,096-frame value applies, so this bead does not wait for it.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #morph-pipeline, #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts, #clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation, known candidate defect 6.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Budget unit tests at, under and one over the contract frame budget (the 4,096-frame value until measured) across shape modes and counts 2, 3, many, 64 and 150; no face count refusal; the message names the limit reached and the estimate and offers reduce length; e2e over-budget Morph shows the reason with zero model requests (intercepted) and zero inference.
- [ ] `mp4-probe.1024`, `.512-webcodecs`, `.ffmpeg-cached`, `.ffmpeg-needs-consent`, `.none`, `.probe-before-synthesis`, `.disclosure-512`; e2e with WebCodecs disabled and no fallback explains before any synthesis; forced codec failure after frames keeps them and export-only Retry produces the MP4 with zero inference.
- [ ] `neighbour-rule.aa`, `.abb`, `.aba-closing-pair`, `.abac-allowed`, `.abc-allowed`, `.same-latent-different-words`, `.same-word-different-model`, `.near-identical-below-1e-12`, `.message-names-faces`, `.no-work-before-refusal` (zero model requests, zero inference); built-UI A,B,A and same-word-twice refusals appear in Morph status, and changing face 3 clears it and Morph proceeds.

title: Carry over the real-UI CPU end-to-end lane
description:
## Background

Classic `next-e2e.yml` real-ui-cpu: Ubuntu 24.04 Google Chrome, actual CPU name/seed and e4e, crop,
original reuse, recovered still without inference, GPU refusal/fallback scope, playable/saved MP4,
face/video/slider restore. Exact-artifact promotion qualification with real-model events and final
file/readiness/resource checks. Browser/E2E workflows invoke `desktop/scripts/verify-web-artifact.py`
until provider simplification re-homes it.

## Why

Exact-artifact promotion qualification must survive the move without mock substitutes.

## Scope

- Destination job against the canonical artifact, real runtime/model bytes acquired by the documented digest-checked mirror procedure (no weights in Git).

- Artifact lookup, provenance (source repository ID, workflow, run, commit), digest verification,
  the shared path-filter list `scripts/ci/path-filters.json` (every new code root: `apps/web/**`,
  `packages/**`, `scripts/**`, relevant `hosting/**`, not only `src/Next`), concurrency and cache
  keys come from `build.ci-artifact-lookup` (`.github/actions/fetch-artifact`); inherited
  `context.repo` or a corrected org prefix is never used. This lane adapts its own paths, worker
  discovery and source assertions for `apps/web` and all four packages.
- Event log through `build.event-log-capture` (`cdp_capture.py` / `attachPlaywright`), validated by
  `check-event-log` and uploaded with `.github/actions/event-log-upload`.
- Retain the lane's protected behaviour, trigger coverage, required-check role and retained evidence;
  cancel superseded test builds; cache pinned dependencies and immutable runtime assets by identity.
- Every mapped check is listed in the check-migration map with its destination invocation.

## Destination workflow, platforms and pass thresholds

- Caller job `qualify` in `.github/workflows/next-site.yml` (moved here from `build.ci-site-lane` in
  polish round 2, so the caller and the called workflow change together): `needs: artifact`, calls
  `next-e2e.yml` via `workflow_call` with explicit `artifact_run`, `artifact_name` and the pinned
  `runtime_sha` (classic value `d9e37e50…650a5c` until the runtime pin changes through currency/ORT).
  Push and dispatch only, as classic (PR merge artifacts are not qualified). Job ID kept for the
  required-status mapping.

- File `.github/workflows/next-e2e.yml` ("Exact new-site qualification"), job ID `real-ui-cpu` on
  `ubuntu-24.04` Google Chrome headless, triggered by `workflow_call` from `next-site.yml` `qualify` and by
  `workflow_dispatch` with explicit `artifact_run` / `artifact_name` / `runtime_sha` inputs.
- Steps carried over: restore the pinned runtime mirror and rebuild the runtime tree from the pinned
  manifest (`hosting/next-static/mirror-runtime.py`); validate artifact-run provenance (source repo ID,
  run, commit); verify exact artifact bytes; serve under production-like TLS/host mapping
  (`scripts/next-e2e-server.py`); drive `scripts/next-e2e-browser.py` with `browser-harness==0.1.8` under
  the 1500 s step watchdog; upload `next-e2e-<run_id>`.

title: Move mapping, synthesis and numerical gates into stylegan-js
description:
## Background
Mapping and synthesis currently run inside `browser/ort-worker.mjs`/`runtime.mjs` and the direct engine; synthesis admission uses content/provider/canary-set keyed receipts (`canary-qualification.mjs`): a genuinely cold visitor runs one canary before the first face, remaining canaries run one at a time behind foreground work and resume safely; compatible warm receipts skip canaries; CI `fullQualify` runs all. Typed stage/timing hooks await actual inference/readback completion (including GPU `mapAsync`).

Raw-synthesis tolerances, frozen and stated concretely (never widened, never a precision change, never replaced by a visual spot-check): the product synthesis canaries require **maximum RGB difference 1 on the 0-255 scale** and **maximum sampled raw-float error 0.002** (candidate `src/Next/browser/canary-qualification.mjs`: `maxRgb <= 1 && maxFloat <= .002`, alpha channel excluded); the applicable research/reference suites keep their own frozen coverage and tolerances; the separate **e4e latent tolerance is maximum absolute error 0.0001** (`photo-runtime/README.md`, `encoder-stream/qualification/report.json`). The comparison is the network's raw output before compression against the independent qualified reference for the same model, latent, noise, preprocessing and workload, including across CPU/WebGPU routes. Other models need their own independent reference and declared small tolerance; they never inherit FFHQ values. Encoded image bytes are never a correctness gate.

## Why
Inference and numerical qualification are the core of the reusable engine; extraction must preserve raw output within the frozen tolerances so published identity (e.g. static names) does not depend on which runtime produced it.

## Scope
- Strict-TS `map(seed|text latent)` and `synthesize(latent)` operations with abort/dispose, request/input-revision/attempt IDs and actual provider identity in results.
- Move the canary set, admission receipts and numerical gate code into the package; keep ordinary-versus-lab/CI scheduling (one canary cold, rest behind foreground; `fullQualify` in CI).
- Preserve integrated performance mechanisms: bounded GPU submit/readback overlap, RGBA8 direct output, `warmMapping()` overlap, bounded CPU threads, warm reuse and output-cache hits needing no inference.
- Typed stage/timing hooks (reporting-transport-free events) that await real completion, never submission time or whole-bridge duration.
- Unit tests for operation validation, abort at each stage, stale-result rejection; numerical tests against the independent reference.

## Out of scope
Descriptor generalization (next item). e4e (photo orchestration item). Morph frame production (morph pipeline). App rebinding (app-rebind item).

## Considerations
- Do not widen tolerances, change precision or substitute a visual check to make a faster implementation pass.
- No new performance claim: architecture parity without faster timings is not a performance keep.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Product canaries pass with max RGB difference <= 1 (0-255) and max sampled raw-float error <= 0.002 on CPU and WebGPU routes against the independent reference; research/reference suites pass at their own frozen tolerances.
- [ ] Cold ordinary admission runs exactly one canary before the first face (event-log assertion); warm compatible receipts skip; `fullQualify` runs all in CI.
- [ ] Timing hooks report verified inference completion (GPU `mapAsync` awaited) in a unit test with a fake device.
- [ ] Abort/dispose/stale-revision unit tests pass; no promise/signal crosses the worker boundary.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes: Position in the shared-file sequence: after compute.provider-adapters, before compute.photo-orchestration. Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Leaves that must not edit these three files: ws:crop.repro (failing tests and the failure analysis only), crop.policy, media.envelope-helpers, media.recovery-schema, morph.descriptor-geometry, compute.consumer-example, compute.names-equality, and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept leaf. They keep the module export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) and move logic behind them into the package. If such a leaf finds it must edit one of the three files, it records the file in the check-migration map conflict list and adds a needs edge to the latest leaf in the sequence that edits it; it never edits concurrently. title: Encode independently confirmed crops in a bounded serial queue
description:
## Background
Multi-selection: each selected photo face has a frozen confirmed crop with request/attempt identity and input revision; only selected photo encodes run, initially one e4e encode at a time (no simultaneous full encoder loads). Contracts freeze batch, revision, cancellation and retry types; face controls owns the modal, ordered selection, atomic keypoint insertion and interaction evidence. The candidate has a crop queue (`crop-queue.test.mjs`) for single crops.

## Why
Confirmed-crop encoding owns real encoding and fallback for every independently confirmed crop; face controls' multi-selection acceptance builds on this.

## Scope
- Bridge-level encode path accepting an ordered list of frozen crops with click-order identities; bounded serial e4e; independent progress and results per slot.
- Per-slot Cancel cancels only that slot, queued siblings continue in frozen order; no implicit batch-wide Cancel after OK.
- Retry resumes one existing cancelled/failed slot with its frozen crop and a new attempt ID appended to the pending queue; neither Retry nor Remove reopens crop or allocates keypoints.
- Reference-counted tab-only ownership of source/derived crop pixels for pending/running/retryable slots; success releases retry inputs; Remove/replace/dispose release remaining references; never persisted to OPFS/session storage.
- No partial failure restarts the batch or creates duplicate keypoints.
- Unit/integration tests with fake encoder and one real-e4e run.

## Out of scope
Selection UI, badges, keypoint insertion and the built-UI multi-selection acceptance (face controls). Global scheduler permits (operation controller) - use its interface if available.

## Considerations
- Shared-file serialization (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in the order provider simplification -> typed facade -> compute extraction -> confirmed-crop fix -> morph pipeline -> static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics reporting rebinding. Add every file this item edits to the check-migration map's conflict list. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.

## Boundaries and extra cases (polish r1)
- Overlap with face controls' `face.batch-slot-cancel-retry` (fm-2rwl): this item owns the bridge-level queue, attempt identities and pixel reference counting; that bead owns the tiles, per-slot Cancel/Retry controls and their operated acceptance, and calls this queue.
- Each slot holds its frozen `ConfirmedCrop` record (crop.policy); Retry reuses the record and the retained derived pixels (no second derivation, no detector call).
- A frozen rectangle without pixels cannot satisfy Retry: after a reload (pixels are tab memory only, never OPFS/session storage) unfinished slots report "lost; use Encode image" and never offer Retry.
- Tests add: `crop-queue.retry-reuses-derived-pixels`, `crop-queue.no-pixels-no-retry`, `crop-queue.reload-drops-unfinished`, `crop-queue.no-persistence` (storage spy: no image bytes written to OPFS, IndexedDB, sessionStorage or localStorage).

## Queue API and the face-controls boundary (polish r2)
The boundary with `face.batch-slot-cancel-retry` (fm-2rwl, area E) is drawn by one API. This item implements it; fm-2rwl renders tiles and controls on top of it and must not reimplement the queue, attempt identities or pixel reference counting (fm-2rwl already waits for this item through ws:crop).
- `enqueueConfirmedCrops(batchRevision, crops: ConfirmedCrop[]) -> SlotId[]` (click order preserved; one slot per crop; the common acquisition/preparation prefix is reported inside each slot's progress).
- `cancelSlot(slotId)`: only that slot settles `cancelled`; queued siblings continue in frozen order.
- `retrySlot(slotId) -> AttemptId`: allowed only for a `cancelled`/`failed` slot whose pixels are still retained; appends a new attempt to the pending queue; refused with `no-retained-pixels` otherwise.
- `removeSlot(slotId)` / `replaceSlot(slotId, crop)` / `disposeBatch(batchRevision)`: release references; late results for a removed or replaced slot are discarded by revision.
- Events (structured, for the event log): `slot.queued`, `slot.started`, `slot.progress`, `slot.succeeded`, `slot.failed{kind}`, `slot.cancelled`, `slot.released` with slot ID, attempt ID, batch revision and timestamp.
- Test hook (test builds only): `pixelRefs(slotId) -> number` for reference-count assertions.
Ownership of checks: queue order, cancellation, retry identity, reference counts and storage spies are unit/integration tests here (fake encoder, plus one real-e4e run). Operated tile Cancel/Retry/Remove at 390 px and 1,280 px, with 1/2/3/8 slots, are fm-2rwl's. The bounded concurrency is one live e4e encoder (`maxLiveEncoders = 1`), the plan's "initially one e4e encode at a time"; raising it needs a measured decision entry in `docs/decisions/`.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.

- [ ] Tests: A1, B2, A2 order preserved through async completion, cancel of one queued slot, retry of a failed slot (new attempt ID, same frozen crop), remove releases pixels (ref-count assertions), no duplicate keypoints.
- [ ] Real e4e for two confirmed crops runs serially (max one live encoder) with W+ error <= 0.0001.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. title: Compare the direct WGSL engine with the native WebGPU EP on synthesis
description:
## Background

The candidate integrates direct WGSL kernels for desktop synthesis with RGBA8 conversion; mobile uses ORT WebGPU mapping. Custom kernels carry maintenance and mobile-safety risk.

## Why

If the native EP matches the direct engine, retiring custom kernels would cut risk; otherwise record the gap.

## Scope

- Paired comparison of direct engine vs native WebGPU EP on the synthesis network (eris, leased), same workload and numerics checks.

## Out of scope

Any kernel change or retirement (exploratory; no change follows from this result alone).

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Report with paired effect and numerics for both routes; recorded as exploratory.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Import the candidate JS closure and pin the control artifact
description:
## Goal
Bring the on-device candidate's runnable JS closure into `apps/web` as one checked revision regenerable from Git objects, pin the built control artifact (the port's oracle under D1) by SHA-256 in durable storage, and provide verified acquisition of the candidate's runtime overlay and photo siblings, so the first destination checks, the facade and the port have real code, real runtime bytes and an oracle that cannot disappear or drift. Node only; no .NET, Fable or Webpack. No remote publisher or domain change.

## Scope
- **Control artifact.** Choose the reverified live candidate artifact at import time (record why); never assume the recorded `001ba853…`/`next-04403766fff8630a` is still live (it changed on 17 October with `40c63a9`, probably again after `bacd6e5`/`6107f80`). Fetch its bytes from the live host or staging record, compute artifact and per-file digests, and compare with the live bytes at pin time. A rebuilt artifact or current checkout is never presented as the live control.
- Upload the exact control `deploy-next/` bytes, plus the runtime-manifest and catalogue identities it was exercised with, as a **release asset** of this repository (classic CI artifacts have limited retention). Record SHA-256 and source identity (classic repo ID 295956585, workflow/run, commit, build id, runtime manifest digest, artifact name) in `control-artifact.json`. Artifact lookup names repo ID, workflow/run, commit and artifact explicitly; inherited `context.repo` or a corrected org prefix cannot locate a classic artifact.
- `scripts/fetch-control.mjs` downloads to scratch, re-verifies, logs source identity, expected/actual SHA-256 and bytes, exits non-zero on mismatch; every golden/parity/freeze script calls it first and fails closed. The control stays labelled as the control with classic's identity, never as this repository's build. Compare its source commit with the frozen import revision: equal, or the commits between listed with their closure effect (a control built before `6107f80` has no second-origin alternation in `model-cache.mjs`).
- **Closure.** Export allowlisted files from Git objects of the frozen commit (`git -C ../facemorph.me-classic archive <commit> <paths>` or `git show <commit>:<path>`; never the working tree, which holds other sessions' edits) under `apps/web` keeping `src/Next` structure; temporary root paths for `desktop/runtime.mjs`, required `scripts/` and any `hosting/` file a closure test imports, each with its consumer. Later-delta files (`dce7f27`, `bacd6e5`, `6107f80` `model-cache.mjs` and `reporting.mjs`) at their frozen-revision bytes; `hosting/next-mirror/` only if the allowlist says a closure test imports it, otherwise left for hosting/deploy to take from the same revision. Provenance (repo ID, frozen commit, reviewed delta from `b2d945a`, path map, notices) stays in the repo without copying `.git`, resetting or creating a worktree.
- Merge only required dependency settings into destination `package.json`/lock. Review collisions first; protect `PLAN.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.beads/`.
- Generated Fable output stays out: `ProjectJson.fs.js` is not created, copied from a build or shimmed. `product-bridge.mjs` is imported byte-identical including its line-9 `./ProjectJson.fs.js` import, unresolved until `migration.facade` (fm-pia9) swaps in its ProjectJson TS module; until then nothing loads the bridge as an ES module or bundles it.
- Check scripts under `scripts/import/`: `verify-closure.mjs` (every imported sha256 equals the allowlist; none missing; none extra); `scan-exclusions.mjs` (no `*.fs`/`*.fsproj`, no `*.fs.js`/`*.fs.js.map`, no `global.json`/`.config/dotnet-tools.json`, no Webpack config, no legacy Server/API file, no weights by extension and size threshold, no `.wrangler/`, no credentials by secret-pattern scan); `unresolved-imports.mjs` (shared with the inventory; output equals the allowed list). Each prints one JSON line per finding and a summary (`files`, `mismatches`, `excluded_hits`, `unresolved`).
- **Runtime reuse.** `scripts/runtime/acquire.mjs` (or a wrapper around the classic procedure from the build inputs) acquires the runtime overlay (`hosting/next-static/runtime-overlay/` + `manifest.json`, refreshed by `mirror-runtime.py`/`restage-runtime.py`) and pinned photo siblings (detector, landmark, codec WASM) with notices, sha256-checked against the manifest, into an ignored cache dir (`.gitignore`). Model-term/download authorization is explicit (flag or env such as `ACCEPT_MODEL_TERMS=yes`, never defaulted). Reuse never depends on ignored `experiment/`, installed ORT/FFmpeg or external `review-artifacts`.
- Two worker lists: app-emitted workers vs manifest-pinned runtime workers/modules (transitive imports, WASM/codec/photo siblings, URLs). `scripts/runtime/check-pins.mjs` fails when emitted or staged runtime bytes change without matching pin updates; one JSON line per file (path, expected, actual, graph emitted|pinned).
- `models.facemorph.me` is a serving surface (hosting/deploy), not an acquisition source; a clean destination never depends on it.

## Out of scope
Building the candidate or the control (never rebuilt); native packages or release automation; moving temporary paths; porting ProjectJson or swapping the import; converter/model-host extraction; copying a private lab; deploying or changing `models.facemorph.me`; populating `deploy-next/` (import checks).

## Notes
- If the candidate branch moved after the freeze, import the frozen revision anyway; newer commits are a later, separately reviewed delta.
- Temporary source paths leave only after their mapped consumers migrate. No weights in Git or in the control asset.
- 24 October rules: provenance lives in `import/allowlist.json` and `control-artifact.json`, not `inventory.md`; no receipts and no shared event-log emitter — the acquisition network assertion is made by request interception by host class and bytes.
- Plan: #candidate-source-import-and-bootstrap, #application-migration (control custody).
