title: Update candidate-source organization links after the rename
description:
## Background
Edits to the candidate source are ordinary work on the working candidate and need no separate approval (operator, 18 October). They are made on a non-deploying classic branch (e.g. `delivery/candidate-edits`) branched from `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, and merged only after the ordinary qualification (this edit by its own merge, see Scope; the rest of the set via `delivery.candidate-edits-merge`), because the candidate branch publishes to next.facemorph.me on every qualified push. Run commands in `facemorph.me-classic` per its development guide. Candidate-source hits from the classified inventory: `src/Config.fs` source links, `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` `ISSUE_REPO` (stays at the candidate's actual repo, new org prefix), `hosting/next-static/promote.py` `REMOTE` (currently the wrong repo `check-face/facemorph.me`; must be `facemorph-me/facemorph.me-classic` while promoting retained candidate artifacts) and workflow-source validation, `src/explain.md`.

## Why
Bug-report, source and promotion lookups must resolve to the right repository.

## Scope
- Apply the classified edits for candidate-source paths.
- Verify `promote.py` workflow-source validation against the renamed repo ID in a non-publishing dry run.
- **Merged on its own** (polish r2): this edit waits for `rename.execute`, which needs org-owner credentials and an accepted login, so it is not part of the `delivery.candidate-edits-merge` batch. It goes through the same flow: non-deploying classic branch, the candidate's ordinary qualification, merge to `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, then `post-delivery-check --mode app` on next.facemorph.me and the retired-host scan on the deployed artifact. Organization branding is not a prerequisite for domain handover, early promotion or API retirement (PLAN.md "Organization rename execution"); if it lands after an early promotion, the promoted artifact is updated only by a later promotion and the receipt says so.

Monorepo links; native updater endpoints (retirement disposition only).

Do not point candidate links at the monorepo before new-app handover.

title: Rebound engine on the ported app: retained product lanes, paired candidate comparison, media round trips
description:
## Goal
Prove on the Vite-built ported app that the product runs on `stylegan-js` and the extracted media helpers and is strictly no worse than the candidate: the retained product lanes and the paired control comparison for the rebound engine (moved from `compute.app-rebind`), and the built-app media round-trip matrix (moved from `media.schema`). `compute.app-rebind` and `media.schema` land before the TS/React milestone with harness and component evidence, because `build:next` never bundles the imported source before the rendering port; this row is where "final integration joins both" (PLAN.md #compute-extraction). Created in the 24 October final pass so the extraction chain runs in parallel with the port.

## Scope
**Retained product lanes and paired comparison**
- On the Vite-built artifact with the rebound engine: next-site.yml (artifact build/unit/import/geometry/integrity, `check-no-third-party.mjs`, exact CPU product qualification, Chromium compiled UI), next-e2e.yml real-ui-cpu, mobile-browser.yml android/ios eight components and ios-product, next-gpu-lane.yml (non-gating GTX1050 WebGPU evidence; software adapters rejected), next-matrix.yml (manual cells, harness under repair).
- Paired comparison: run the shared not-worse workload and runner (`verify.not-worse-lanes`, fm-0q4h) with the Vite-built ported artifact as the build under test and the pinned candidate as control, on the lanes that exist when this row runs (at least desktop CPU in CI, iOS Simulator, Android emulator and WebGPU on a leased GPU worker; physical iPhone when connected, otherwise untested), and apply the gate's pass rule (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27) unchanged. Add the cold photo (empty profile) time-to-encoded-face and peak stored bytes measures to that workload if it lacks them; do not write a second workload, runner or rule here. The recorded first-Save size/time trade is the only exception.

**Built-app media round trips (moved from `media.schema`)**
- Generate a face, Save (WebP default), Save again (reuse, same name), Save PNG, re-import each through the face file entry (installs without inference); morph, Save MP4, validate with the internal reader; promise/object-URL cleanup after each.
- Matrix on Chromium CPU in CI (retained engines where available; untested cells listed): WebP default 1024 × 1024 with exact recovery, PNG pixel-exact to the prepared pixels, MP4 unchanged settings with reported resolution; repeat Save reuses name and bytes (zero encode events); a format switch prepares only that format (zero inference); Share cancel triggers no download.
- Earlier candidate files reopen through the face file entry: schema-1 PNG and schema-2 PNG/WebP with exact latent and model identity.
- File size, first-Save preparation latency and repeat-Save latency reported per format and platform.

**Logging**
- The CI output prints a per-cell table (cell, measure, pairs, ratio interval, margin, verdict) and, per media case, format, bytes, identity suffix and encode/inference counters; traces and screenshots kept on failure.

## Out of scope
- Morph built-app matrix (`morph.guards.acceptance`); building the workload, runner or pass rule (`verify.not-worse-lanes`, `verify.not-worse`); crop and recovery-class built-UI checks (`crop.ported-app`); the release-wide gate across all journeys (`verify.not-worse`).

- Edits no shared bridge/runtime/worker file except to fix a defect it finds; such a fix follows the out-of-turn rule in the shared-file note.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#compute-extraction; #media-and-recovery; #strictly-not-worse-than-the-candidate-operator-24-october-2026; #platform-ci-retention-and-performance-preservation.

title: Blend view output: saved blend and recipe, reopen, Add to morph, batch slot fill, blend job report
description:
## Goal
Make a weighted blend from the blend view something a person keeps and builds on, as the retired API's `num_multi` users (the Synthetic Data Ltd tester building a library of fictitious ID-photo-style faces) did: save it with a recipe, reopen it anywhere, insert it into the morph row, fill many slots at once from photos or saved faces, and report each blend job. Follows `face.blend-view` (fm-2kse), which builds the view, slots, weights and blend run.

## Scope
- **Saved blend file.** The result exports like any other face through the established export controls. The suggested filename may carry labels under the filename rule, e.g. `blend-3-faces-k4p7s2.webp`. Saved files carry the blended W+ latent and the recipe (each slot's kind word/seed/name/photo, latent digest and weight; no typed words, seeds or file names), written by media through the recipe format from `media.schema` (fm-fy2.7).
- **Reopen.** Reopening a saved blend restores it as an ordinary face anywhere with zero inference; in the blend view it also restores the weights of any slot whose latent digest matches. Reopening saved WebP/PNG faces restores the latent at once with no photo encoding.
- **Add to morph** inserts the blended result at the end of the morph row as a recovered still labelled "Blend of N faces", through the same admission check as every other entry path: real budgets only, never a face count; a refusal names the limit reached in one plain message.
- **Filling many slots at once** uses the existing ordered multi-selection and mixed-batch flows: choosing or dropping several photos or saved faces opens the one batch proposal; each detected face gets a proposed crop that can be accepted as is; saved faces are staged without re-encoding; one OK fills that many slots in click order. A batch over the retained photo-input byte budget (contracts ceilings) gets the existing reduce-selection message naming that limit, never silent truncation. Reopening saved WebP/PNG faces restores the latent at once with no photo encoding.
- **Job report.** A completed blend reports one job with action `blend` (route and outcome) to the analytics sink and the usage-statistics sink.

## Out of scope
The view, deep link, slot list, weight controls, running a blend and layout (`face.blend-view`, fm-2kse). The recipe format itself (media.schema); the `blend` entry in the shared diagnostics action list (diagnostics); the cross-file batch and mixed-batch flows themselves (`face.batch` fm-3peb, `face.mixed-batch` fm-q5b9), which this bead reuses. Old GUIDs or links; result-sharing URLs; a hosted endpoint; new models, encoders, downloads, workers or hosting.

## Notes
- Split on 2026-10-24 for swarm size: `face.blend-view` (this ID, fm-2kse: view, deep link, slots, weights, running a blend, layout and capacity) and `face.blend-view.output` (saved blend file and recipe, reopen, Add to morph, filling many slots from one batch, the `blend` job report). The original estimate for the whole view was two to three days.
- Batch fill reuses the existing ordered multi-selection and mixed-batch flows; per the 24 October parallelism pass they are not start dependencies of the blend view, so the batch-fill check runs at close on their merged result (fm-3peb, fm-q5b9). Add to morph inserts a recovered still through the reader wiring already implied via fm-fy2.7.
- Ship before API retirement where practical (a preference, not a gate); the retirement notice (domain handover) points the tester to the view and link. Old GUIDs do not carry over.
- UI in the ported sources only; no shared bridge/runtime/worker file. Arithmetic context: `sum(weight_k * W+_k)` over W+ `[1,18,512]`, unnormalised; equals `num_multi` for photo slots (`LatentByMultiLerp`); word/seed slots deliberately differ from the API's Z-space handling. About 0.4 s warm on WebGPU in the tester's diagnostics (one device, not a promise).
- Anchor: PLAN.md#weighted-face-blend-advanced-mode.
acceptance_criteria:
Operated rule: real pointer/touch at the visible position with `elementFromPoint` returning the control in its region; by-name only for setup; screenshot per case.
- [ ] Unit tests in CI: a batch at and one over the photo-input byte ceiling: accepted, then refused with the reduce-selection message naming the limit and nothing added; recipe weight restore by matching latent digest; saved recipe carries each slot's kind, latent digest and weight and no typed words, seeds or file names.
- [ ] Operated run at 1,280 px, and the same run at 390 px where admitted: with three slots filled, fill five more from one multi-photo batch proposal in click order (each detected face's proposed crop accepted as is; saved faces staged without re-encoding).
- [ ] Save a PNG of the blend (full 1024 x 1024 frame, established export controls), reopen it as a face on the main page with zero inference, and use Back to return to the view with the session intact.
- [ ] **Add to morph** with a long morph row (64 and 150 faces) inserts "Blend of N faces" at the end of the row through the shared admission check; with a real budget forced one over (stored-session size) it shows that budget's plain message and adds nothing.

title: Run the responsive width sweep with live resize, zoom and keyboard occlusion

title: Implement budgeted verified-cache warming with zero network and foreground preemption (only if the round ships it)
description:
## Background
Existing `model-cache.mjs` `acquire()` handles can fetch missing/corrupt assets through `bytes()`/`open()`;
`readOnly` and `has()`/`peek()` do not enforce a local-only boundary. The manager supplies verified-local-only access
(for example `allowRepair:false` across OPFS and Cache Storage) with typed invalidation.

## Why
Hide repeat-visit setup when measured beneficial.

## Scope
- On a visible idle app for an eligible anticipated route, after boot/recovery, warm only the selected route's verified
  cached synthesis assets/session/mapping through low-priority scheduler admission and explicit residency reservations;
  reuse admission receipts; one product canary plus deferred checks when needed; never the full encoder lab gate.
- Zero model-network requests including repair; required runtime/helper assets must be locally ready; skip on cache
  miss/corruption/eviction.
- Foreground work outranks: stop new warm submissions, settle the in-flight unit, release or transfer compatible
  resources; count idle warm memory until release; never evict foreground resources.
- Constrained iPhone/unknown-memory paths defer or release generator warmth before e4e and rehydrate after teardown.
- Static names and completed-result display/Save never initialize inference.

## Out of scope
If the round says drop: close this leaf as dropped with a pointer to the decision.

## Considerations
Do not promise instant preemption of submitted GPU work.

title: Carry over the iOS Simulator and Android emulator lanes
description:
## Goal

Phones are first-class targets. Move classic `mobile-browser.yml` into this repository with its Android emulator and iOS Simulator component jobs and its iOS Simulator product jobs (the only retained lane that runs real inference on an iOS browser engine), keeping job IDs, triggers and pass contracts, on `apps/web` and package paths. Simulator results are never physical-iPhone evidence, but losing the lane would leave no iOS product check.

## Scope

**Shared for all jobs**: artifact lookup, provenance, digest verification, path filters, concurrency and cache keys come from the shared `fetch-artifact` action and `scripts/ci/path-filters.json` delivered by `build.ci-shared` (this lane does not wait for the site lane: until canonical-artifact fan-out, the artifact under test is the `build:next` output built in-lane, labelled "rebuilt, digest X") (never inherited `context.repo` or a corrected org prefix); network claims use the request-interception helper; traces/screenshots kept on failure; superseded test builds cancelled; pinned dependencies and immutable runtime assets cached by identity. Each lane adapts its own paths, worker discovery and source assertions for `apps/web` and the four packages. Job IDs kept so required-status names map one-to-one.

**Android `android`** — `.github/workflows/mobile-browser.yml` ("Mobile browser components"), `ubuntu-24.04` with KVM, `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2`, API 35, `google_apis`, `x86_64`, profile `pixel_6`, `-gpu swiftshader_indirect -no-snapshot`; `python3 tests/mobile/run.py --platform android`; artifact `mobile-android-components`.
- Triggers: workflow_dispatch; push to default and `candidate/*`; pull_request; path filters `tests/mobile/**`, `apps/web/**`, `packages/stylegan-js/**`, `packages/browser-model-manager/**`, `scripts/next-ios-sim.py`, `.github/workflows/mobile-browser.yml`. Concurrency `mobile-components-${{ github.ref }}`, cancel-in-progress.
- Pass = classic `assess()` in `tests/mobile/run.py`: run ID matches, `completed: true`, no error, `secureContext: true`, `inferenceExecuted: false`, `e4eExecuted: false`, `evidenceLevel: browser-component`, and exactly these eight components all `passed: true`: `worker-module-hash`, `integrity-rejection`, `cancel-partial-retry`, `concurrent-download-dedup`, `corrupt-cache-repair`, `png-1024-roundtrip`, `portrait-exif-crop`, `reload-retained-offline`. Missing or extra component fails. No synthesis/e4e in this lane.

**iOS `ios` component job** — `macos-15`, Safari in iOS Simulator, `python3 tests/mobile/run.py --platform ios`, artifact `mobile-ios-components`; same `assess()` contract and same eight components, `inferenceExecuted: false` (the README's older seven-check text is superseded). Triggers and path filters as Android. Runs against the artifact under test (canonical bytes once fan-out lands).

**iOS product jobs**
- `ios-product-artifact` (`ubuntu-22.04`): until canonical-artifact fan-out lands, builds the artifact under test and uploads `next-ios-artifact-<run_id>`, stating "rebuilt, digest X" beside the canonical digest; after fan-out it fetches and verifies canonical `next-site-<sha>` via `fetch-artifact` (that switch is fan-out's acceptance). Never present a rebuilt digest as canonical.

title: Freeze the flow matrix as the Playwright parity spec; choose the golden-capture method
description:
## Goal
Gate the controller port: drive the verified control artifact through every journey row and classify it, so only rows that are present and unchanged gate the port and the port neither copies candidate defects nor drifts without trace; and decide the oracle granularity for the controller port by spiking whether the minified control bundle exposes its Elmish message stream (reducer transitions) or whether goldens must be journey-step DOM/state snapshots. The freeze output is the Playwright parity spec itself; its run against the control is the grading.

## Scope
- Journey table (about 50 rows): first visit, return with retained work, phone/CPU route, words, seeds incl. zero and 0..4,294,967,295, Retry unchanged input, edit/remove queued tile, names open/pick/edit/close, device timing, CPU/WebGPU selection, consent approve/refuse, quota failure, photo replace/paste/drop/multi-file, crop confirm/adjust/no-face, add/remove, many faces, Undo/Start over, keyboard-only, identical neighbours, reload after morph, offline with cache, morph unfinished inputs, morph settings/cancel/retry, play/slider, Save/Share/rename/format, reopen still, report error, debug On/Off, remove down to one face, `?testing` bulk Generate, desktop-package link.
- Exercise variants where possible: cold-model / model-cached / output-cached, narrow/intermediate/wide, keyboard/touch, unsupported/unknown capability, offline and changed-input.
- Write the Playwright parity spec (for example `apps/web/test/parity/flow-matrix.spec.ts`): one test per journey row with a stable `rowId` (also the golden directory name), tagged `parity` (present and unchanged), `changed` (present and changed by a declared UX change, citing the live plan section: UI requirements table, flow matrix, known candidate defects) or `new` (absent, specification-graded), with owner (workstream key) for non-parity rows, variants exercised, control digest, and screenshots at phone 390 px and desktop 1,280 px for parity rows. A row that cannot be exercised against the control is a skipped test with its reason, never a pass.
- Candidate defects 1-23 (18 October operated check and audit: Remove unclickable, >2 faces do not fit, no reset, Tab skips mode menu/names/file picker, autocapitalize, identical neighbours error, Add disabled at one face, wrong empty-tile hint, words lost on reload, inconsistent sizes, per-keystroke requests, report label, collector action list, names contrast, offline failure, stacked toasts, stale completions, 64-cap (replaced by budget-based admission in the port), consent gaps, typos, unlinked licence page, storage, preview badge) are each a repair row with its named owner, never parity.
- Known declared-change rows (not parity): WebGL entry in the Advanced selector (provider), selector position above the first + (`face.selector-names`), names search/header/Show more (static names), Morph auto-generation of unfinished inputs (operation controller), bounded consent grant and copy (acquisition consent), native desktop links (provider).
- Steps that act on controls use real pointer/touch input at the visible position (defect 1 shows by-name clicks hide unusable controls).
- Golden spike: for one flow (type a word -> Generate -> Completed on CPU), try to observe messages and model states through the control bundle (`Msg` cases such as `Edit`, `Mode`, `RunFace`, `Progressed`, `Completed`, `CropAccept`, `DownloadsChanged`, `ChooseName`, `Product.fs` ~263-279) via a development hook, the bridge's events (`subscribe` progress, `facemorph-report-status`), or DOM state transitions, with `project-v1.fixture.json`. If it works, write the reducer-transition recorder (message, prior state digest, next state); if not, write the Playwright DOM/state snapshot recorder at journey-step level. Both outcomes are acceptable; the choice is stated in the recorder index.
- Recorder output contract: `apps/web/test/goldens/control/<rowId>/<step>.json` plus index `goldens.json` with oracle used and its blind spots, control `deploy-next/` SHA-256, recorder command and version, browser and viewport, runtime/model identities, and per step the input action (pointer/touch coordinates or keyboard), observed message or DOM/state snapshot (class list, text, ARIA state, focused element), the row's tag from the parity spec, and a privacy flag confirming no photo bytes, latents or typed inputs are retained beyond the test run (fixture inputs are synthetic words/seeds only). Every controller and rendering bead consumes this format.
- Publish the parity-row list (the spec's `parity` tag) and the recorder command for downstream beads; `migration.parity` derives its row-level acceptance from the spec.

## Out of scope
- Fixing defects (owners: face controls, morph pipeline, media and recovery, acquisition consent, static names, diagnostics control, operation controller, provider Help).
- Recording every flow (done per controller bead). Rebuilding the control with hooks (forbidden: no F# build). Any reducer or component implementation.

## Notes
- Newer PLAN.md text wins over the old "committed table (md + JSON) and receipt": the freeze output is the Playwright parity spec, tags `parity`/`changed`/`new`; defects are `changed` tests annotated `defect:<n>` with their owner. Old docs paths `flow-matrix-freeze.{md,json}` are not produced.
- The spike is expected to be small but has no time box.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-migration (Freeze the flow matrix first; Golden capture, with a stated fallback); #ui-flow-matrix-and-open-journey-contracts; #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Parity spec has one test per journey row with `rowId`, tag, owner for non-parity rows; every parity test has Playwright steps and phone/desktop screenshots, and its run against the verified control (digest re-checked first) passes.
- [x] Defects 1-23 each appear as a non-parity row with owner; a check fails if any defect row is tagged `parity`.
- [x] Unexercisable rows are skipped tests with a reason; none counts as passed.
- [x] Parity steps act with real pointer/touch at the control's visible position and assert `elementFromPoint`; by-name/by-role clicks only for setup.
- [x] Recorder produces a golden for the sample flow from the verified control artifact; `goldens.json` names the oracle, its blind spots, the control digest and the recorder command.
- [x] Privacy test: recorder output retained outside the run contains no photo bytes, latents or typed inputs.
- [x] Traces and screenshots kept on failure.

title: Research lease: per-machine device lease state and command
description:
## Goal
One device lease per physical machine, shared by local agents, research runs, heavy self-hosted CI and both repositories, so two heavy runs never share a GPU or the phone at once. Split from research stage 1 (fm-zxj) in the parallelism pass (operator, 24 October 2026): most consumers (device-lab optimisation, not-worse lanes, checker calibration, decode measurement, parity harness, converter parity, catalogue generator, CI lease wrapper, field-lead profiling) need only the lease, not the guides or ledger handover, so this starts immediately with no prerequisites.

## Scope
- One absolute state directory per physical machine (eris, TrueNAS, triton) via machine-level config or an environment variable, documented; classic invocations on those machines use the same directory (machine config or documented `--state-dir`; any classic code change is a separately reviewable classic commit excluding other sessions' changes). The old relative `autoresearch/state` gave two leases per GPU.
- Lease runner at `autoresearch/run.py` in this repository, seeded from classic's `run.py` at the pinned revision (the research-tree import, fm-86u, records this path as already re-homed rather than overwriting it): budgets (default 600 s, max 3600 s), busy exit 75 or bounded `--wait`, owned process-group cleanup, `state/runs.jsonl` journal; refuses a nested second lease from the same process tree and a lease device differing from the host doing the work.
- Entry command: `python3 autoresearch/run.py --lane <lane> --device <machine> --state-dir "<absolute per-machine lease dir>" --timeout <s <= 3600> -- <driver command>`.
- The device lab's own lock (`tools/device-lab` `lab_lock`) takes or honours the same lease for the phone and eris cells, so lab runs and research runs never overlap.

## Out of scope
Guides, protocol, ledger handover and the clean-clone smoke (fm-zxj); the CI wrapper (fm-wzy); drivers (stage 2).

- [x] Runner tests: busy device without `--wait` exits 75; bounded `--wait` acquires or exits non-zero; nested lease refused; lease device differing from the working host refused; owned process group cleaned up on timeout.
- [x] Cross-repo concurrency test: a leased run from this repository and one from classic on the same machine — the second (either direction) exits busy or waits within the bound.
- [x] A device-lab run and a leased research run on eris never overlap (one waits or exits busy).
- [x] Per-machine state directory documented and configured on eris and triton (TrueNAS when its runner bead lands).

title: Contracts milestone 1: manager lifecycle, leases, grant, budgets, manifests; milestone checks
description:
## Goal

Complete contracts milestone 1 by freezing, as exported TypeScript in `packages/browser-model-manager`, the manager lifecycle with verified-local reads and asset leases, the acquisition grant and budget structure, and manifest compatibility with its producer-facing JSON schema — built on the engine-side types from `contracts.engine` — and run the milestone-wide checks across both packages (one type test over every citable name, validator fuzzing, and an external consumer compiling against the packed declarations). Compute extraction, the typed facade, the model manager, hosting, conversion and the operation controller build against this milestone; the operation controller and acquisition consent need the grant types, hosting and conversion need the manifest schema.

## Scope

**Manager lifecycle and leases** — `packages/browser-model-manager/src/contracts/lifecycle.ts`, `leases.ts`, `errors.ts`:
- `ModelManager`: construct (no globals, no I/O), `status()`/`capabilities()` acquisition-free, `authorize(grant)`, `acquire`, `verify`, `load` → handle wrapping `LoadedModelCapability`, lease, invalidate, `dispose`; `ManagerStatus`; `VerifiedLocalReader` (`allowRepair: false` across OPFS and Cache Storage; `readOnly`/`has()`/`peek()` alone are not a boundary).
- `AssetLease` (reference-counted; manager eviction/deletion cannot remove leased assets), `LeaseInvalidationCause` (`browser-eviction` | `corruption` | `cross-tab-deletion` | `device-loss` | `worker-loss`), `SettlementRule`; affected operations settle and release without network repair. Active operations cannot fetch replacement shards; reacquisition and re-admission happen outside engine execution under the app's consent policy.
- `ManagerError` union: `cache-miss` | `corrupt` | `evicted` | `invalidated` | `quota` | `manifest-rejected` | `unknown-status` | `network`.
- Retained mechanisms: per-read platform SHA, exact-length buffers, unit corruption repair, URL-independent pinned reuse, Safari worker sync-handle support, Cache Storage fallback. Candidate cache identities and on-origin result/session formats stay compatible; model caches split from app retention; model-cache eviction never deletes exports or recovery records. An in-flight app uses one immutable manifest identity.

**Acquisition grant and budgets** — `grant.ts`, `budgets.ts`:
- `AcquisitionGrant` (manifest identity, route, `GrantPurpose` = `generate` | `generate-and-encode` | `prepare-encoder`, asset digests, advertised remaining-byte scope, owners), `GrantOwnerId`, `GrantDecision` (`approved` | `declined` | `cancelled` | `revision-required`), `AcquisitionPriority` (`foreground-required` | `synthesis-prerequisite` | `detector-prerequisite` | `optional` | `speculative-warming`), `WarmingOwnership`, `AcquisitionBudget` (aggregate transfer, read-ahead, hash, write-buffer bytes) and `LiveResidencyLimit` as named fields.
- Approval covers deferred stages and retry within unchanged scope only; extra/replacement scope needs a revised decision; cache revalidation cannot inflate the budget silently. Cancel releases that owner; a shared fetch stops when its last authorised consumer leaves; verified chunks are kept; no revival of cancelled transfers. Digest deduplication; acquisition holds no compute permit while waiting. Unknown cache/manifest status (candidate's unknown inventory bypassing `gateScope`) yields bounded inspection or a retryable error, never permission to fetch. The old two-chunk phone read-ahead is per-worker and does not bound overlapping workers. Manager supplies primitives; policy lives in the app.

**Manifest compatibility** — `packages/browser-model-manager/src/contracts/manifest.ts` and `schema/model-manifest.v1.schema.json`:
- `ModelManifestV1`, `MANIFEST_SCHEMA_MAJOR`, `parseModelManifest(unknown)` → `Result<ModelManifestV1, ManifestError>` (unknown/newer major rejected), `RuntimeManifest` (kernel provenance: candidate ID and source hash; `encoderStream.phoneAdmitted`; e4e WASM limit 268,435,456 bytes), `AssetIdentity` (generator, optional photo encoder, preprocessing identities separate).
- The manager owns the producer-facing JSON schema; `cloudflare-model-host` and `model-conv` validate their emitted manifests against it as a dev-dependency (no runtime dependency from manager to host/converter). Weights stay out of tarballs; private source provenance stays out of published manifests. Preserve descriptor/content identities through renames (WebGL coefficient assets also feed direct WebGPU).
- Runtime validators for every `unknown` boundary (manifest, metadata, worker payload): narrow, tested, no broad `any`, unchecked casts or silent defaults.

**Placement and tests.** All types live directly in the packages scaffolded by the build workstream, as public exports; no runtime implementation beyond validators; contract type environments scoped so they gain no accidental DOM/Node globals.

**Milestone-wide checks.** One type test imports every citable name of both packages (engine names from `contracts.engine` plus the names above) from the package entry points; validator fuzzing covers the manifest here and re-runs the engine's metadata and worker-payload validators in the same CI job; the external consumer compiles against both packed packages.

## Out of scope

Engine-side contracts (`contracts.engine`); engine/manager implementation; numeric byte ceilings and app batch/progress/scheduler/preflight types (milestone 2 rows); the consent modal and UI; any change to candidate adapters.

## Notes

## Notes

- PLAN.md (newer) says contracts are TS modules in the owning packages with type tests and a limits constants file and "there is no separate `contracts.md`". The absorbed beads' `contracts.md`, draft `docs/plans/.../contracts/` files and export-index table are dropped; the citable export names above are kept and checked by a type test instead.
- Stable exported names: downstream workstreams cite them; a rename is a contract revision.
- Any alternative encoder ownership needs equivalent independent-consumer, memory and acquisition-boundary evidence. Worker placement and GPU residency are measured implementation choices, not contract.
- Shared files: the facade and compute extraction later edit `product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs`, `browser/ort-worker.mjs`; this bead only defines types.
- Leases constrain manager behaviour, not the browser's ability to reclaim storage.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#package-and-operation-contracts, #stylegan-js, #browser-model-manager, #cloudflare-model-host, #model-conv, #synthesis-correctness-and-export-quality, #confirmed-crop-and-ordered-multi-selection-flow, #consented-downloads-useful-overlap-and-cached-model-warming.
- The adapter survey lives in `contracts.engine`; the manager-side owners it names (`model-cache.mjs` `acquire()`, `bytes()`, `open()`, `shard-store.mjs`) are the inputs here.

- [x] All listed exports exist in `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/` and `packages/browser-model-manager/src/contracts/`; a type test imports every citable name from its package entry point and fails on a missing or renamed export; it runs in CI.
- [x] Type-level tests per discriminated union (exhaustiveness; invalid states unrepresentable); a deliberately invalid state in a fixture fails compilation; `npm run typecheck` passes.
- [x] Type test: no repair-capable handle is reachable from `status()`, `capabilities()` or `VerifiedLocalReader`; each `LeaseInvalidationCause` maps to a `ManagerError` and a `SettlementRule`.
- [x] Grant walkthrough as typed test cases: approve both then Cancel crop; Generate-only then photo request; shared fetch with two owners where one cancels; unknown inventory → no fetch.
- [x] The candidate's current runtime manifest validates against `model-manifest.v1.schema.json` (recorded fixture) and `parseModelManifest`; a newer-major fixture is rejected with a typed error.
- [x] Validator fuzzing (manifest, metadata, worker payload) runs in CI with a fixed seed and a recorded case count; every rejection yields a typed error.

The import is a runnable JS closure: `src/Next` `.mjs` modules (bridge, browser, photo, geometry, assets), tests and fixtures (incl. `project-v1.fixture.json`), `product-ux.scss`, `src/index.html`, styles/public assets, package/lock entries for the JS modules, catalogue input, surviving build/check scripts (hashing, verification), `desktop/runtime.mjs` (statically imported by `product-bridge.mjs`, hashed by `scripts/build-next.cjs`), `desktop/scripts/verify-web-artifact.py` (invoked by browser/E2E workflows), and hosting files the closure's tests import (e.g. `hosting/next-cloudflare/validation.mjs` is imported by `src/Next/reporting.test.mjs`). ### The one Fable-output import (`ProjectJson.fs.js`)
`src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` line 9 is `import {decode,encode} from './ProjectJson.fs.js';`. That file is Fable's compiled output of `ProjectJson.fs`; classic's `.gitignore` excludes `*.fs.js`, so it is **not in any Git object** and `git archive` of the frozen commit cannot contain it. The import rules also exclude generated Fable output. It is the only such import in the closure at `b2d945a` and at `6107f80` (`git grep "fs.js" -- src/Next`). How the closure still satisfies its checks before the port:
- The specifier is kept byte-identical (no shim, no hand-written stand-in, no Fable output, no edit to the bridge). It is listed as the single **known unresolved import**, with owner `migration.ctl-projectjson` (fm-dtmm, ports ProjectJson to typed TS with round-trip goldens) and swap point `migration.facade-types` (fm-pth3, needs fm-dtmm), which replaces the specifier with the TS module.
- Nothing in the import-time checks loads the bridge as an ES module: the tests that exercise the bridge (`src/Next/fresh-review.test.mjs`, `src/Next/estimate.test.mjs`) read `product-bridge.mjs` as text, strip `import` lines with `plain()` and evaluate it in a `node:vm` context with injected stubs, and `scripts/check-progress-copy.mjs` reads it as text. Evidence that they need no Fable output: classic's own `next-site.yml` (at `6107f80`) runs the `node --test` list and `check-progress-copy.mjs` before `npm run build:next`, the step that first runs `dotnet fable`; the exact-artifact harness runs the webpack-bundled control artifact, where ProjectJson is already compiled in; `build:next` populates `deploy-next/` from the control artifact, not from the imported source. No bundler build of the imported bridge is attempted before the rendering port.
- Two classic checks consume Fable output and therefore cannot run in the destination: `scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs` (scans `*.fs.js` for imports from hand-written modules; with no Fable output it would find zero files and pass vacuously) and `src/Next/verify-fable.mjs` (run in classic CI as `node src/Next/verify-fable.mjs src/Next/ProjectJson.fs.js`). Both are imported as files but recorded `not applicable until the port` — never reported as passed. (Side finding: classic's separate `check-bridge-imports` CI step also runs before `build:next`, so in classic CI it scans zero files and passes vacuously; the effective run is the one `scripts/build-next.cjs` makes between `dotnet fable ./src` and webpack. Record this in the check-migration map so the destination's replacement is not modelled on the vacuous step.) `verify-fable.mjs`'s assertions are the starting acceptance for fm-dtmm; the bridge-import guarantee is taken over by strict TS type checking at the typed facade (recorded in `build.check-migration-map`, fm-bhw).

## Why
The import must be a reproducible export from Git objects, not a developer's prepared tree; and every later commit and every unresolvable reference must be a reviewed, owned line rather than a surprise during the first destination check.

## Scope
- **Freeze the committed import revision**: the then-current committed head of `candidate/next-delivery-20260916` (on 24 October that is `6107f80`), never a dirty tree. Record the reviewed delta from `b2d945a` commit by commit (table above, re-read at freeze; any further commit gets a row) with a disposition per changed path: imported, F# specification only, workflow (listed for its re-homing owner), hosting (listed for its owner), excluded.
- **`hosting/next-mirror/`** (present at the frozen revision, absent at `b2d945a`): a row in the frozen revision's path map with digests. Disposition: not part of the `apps/web` closure unless a closure test imports it (then it is imported at the temporary root path `hosting/next-mirror/` like other hosting files and its test is listed); in either case its owner is `ws:hosting` (the second runtime origin is part of serving, PLAN.md "cloudflare-model-host") with the deploy-and-warm step owned by `ws:deploy`, and both take it from this same frozen revision so provenance is one commit.
- Allowlist with source repo ID (295956585)/commit, source → destination path (under `apps/web`, keeping the `src/Next` structure; temporary root paths for `desktop/runtime.mjs`, required `scripts/` and imported `hosting/` files), consumer of each temporary path, file digest (sha256).
- **Unresolved-import list**: every import specifier in imported modules that does not resolve inside the imported tree, each with owner bead and swap point. Expected content: exactly `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs → ./ProjectJson.fs.js` (owner fm-dtmm, swap fm-pth3). Any other entry blocks the freeze until it is imported, excluded with reason, or owned.
- Any working-tree overlay is listed separately by owner/digest; uncommitted files are excluded with digests (classic currently has uncommitted edits in `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.gitignore`, four `autoresearch/` docs, `desktop/README.md`, `docs/`; none is imported).
- Destination collision list (protect `PLAN.md`, entry guides, `.beads/`).

## Out of scope
Copying files (`import.closure`); porting ProjectJson (fm-dtmm).

## Considerations
Never include other sessions' edits or label dirty source as the pinned snapshot. D1: no .NET in the monorepo. The frozen revision and the control artifact's source commit (`import.control-artifact`) should match; if the live control was built from a different commit, list the delta between them.

title: Remove native desktop links and recommendations from the candidate
description:
## Background
Edits to the candidate source are ordinary work on the working candidate and need no separate approval (operator, 18 October). title: Qualify one real non-face checkpoint through the container
description:
## Background
Qualify one real non-face checkpoint end to end, preferably at another resolution to expose hardcoded assumptions. NVlabs' AFHQ cat 512 px model is the proposed fixture, subject to converter compatibility and acquisition terms; it is not currently claimed supported. If it is unsupported, resolve with a compatible non-face checkpoint and document the actual boundary.

## Why
Non-face support stays unqualified until a real checkpoint converts and verifies; this is also the fixture for compute/morph/media descriptor checks and integrated verification's joint proof.

## Scope
- Check AFHQ cat 512 converter compatibility and terms; record the decision (or the substitute checkpoint and why) in `docs/decisions/`.
- Run real copyable acquire/convert/verify commands in the container; produce all chunks, descriptor, manifests and a reference/parity report against an independent reference with an appropriately small declared tolerance for this model.
- Update the compatibility table; until passing, label non-face support unqualified and name the blocker.

## Out of scope
Manager-loaded inference, hosting and export of the non-face model (integrated verification's joint proof).

## Considerations
- FFHQ tolerances are not inherited; declare and justify this model's tolerance from its own reference.
- Generation/morph for non-face models must not load a face detector or FFHQ e4e.

## What this item hands to the non-face joint proof (polish r1)
The joint proof itself is integrated verification's `verify.packages-nonface` (fm-9lt0), run from local packs before npm publication, then re-run from the final docs by `pkgdocs.consumer-smoke` and by the independent reviewer (`fm-fy2.21`). This item must leave these concrete inputs:
1. **Trusted checkpoint acquisition:** source URL, publisher, SHA-256 of the downloaded pickle, licence/usage and redistribution terms, and the trusted-pickle warning, in `docs/decisions/` and in the compatibility table. The checkpoint is never committed.
2. **Pinned container conversion:** the exact `build`, `acquire`, `convert` and `verify` commands, the image digest and base-image digests, tool versions and conversion flags, copied into the receipt.
3. **Independent reference checks:** reference outputs from the pinned upstream PyTorch implementation on the original checkpoint (not from the converted artifacts) for a recorded seed set, the declared tolerance with its justification, and the measured errors.
4. The output set ready for developer-controlled static hosting: chunks, descriptor (resolution, channels, Z/W size, W+ layer count, noise, truncation, conditioning) and manifests valid against the contracts schema, with digests.
If AFHQ cat 512 fails on compatibility or terms, record the blocker, choose a compatible non-face checkpoint, and say which one and why; non-face support stays labelled unqualified until the joint proof passes.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Converted non-face artifacts verify against the independent reference within the declared tolerance; descriptor declares the non-1024 resolution and its latent shape.
- [ ] Commands in docs are the exact commands run (copied into the receipt).
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Hand-off bundle recorded: checkpoint source, digest and terms; container and base-image digests; exact commands; upstream-reference errors versus the declared tolerance; descriptor and schema-valid manifests with digests.

title: Freeze the bounded acquisition grant, priority and buffer budget types
description:
## Background

Candidate `DownloadConsent` is a broad route/photo set, and unknown inventory currently bypasses
`gateScope`. The plan requires a bounded grant over manifest identity, route, purpose, required asset
digests and advertised remaining-byte scope, with an explicit owner. The old two-chunk phone
read-ahead is a per-worker bound and does not bound overlapping workers.

## Why

Consent, overlap and warming need a grant the manager can enforce and the app can own.

## Scope

- Grant type: manifest identity, route, purpose (Generate / Generate and encode / Prepare encoder),
  asset digests, byte scope, owner(s); approval covers deferred stages and retry within unchanged
  scope only; additional/replacement scope needs a revised decision; cache revalidation cannot inflate
  the budget silently.
- Owner semantics: Cancel releases that owner; a shared fetch stops when its final authorised consumer
  leaves; verified chunks are kept; no revival of cancelled transfers.
- Acquisition priority (foreground-required outranks optional; synthesis prerequisites first; small
  detector/alignment prerequisite promptly) and aggregate transfer/read-ahead/hash/write-buffer
  budget with digest deduplication; acquisition holds no compute permit while waiting.
- Speculative warming ownership and aggregate live-residency limit structure (values in m2).
- Unknown cache/manifest status: bounded inspection or retryable error, never permission to fetch.

## Typed outputs (citable)

Draft first under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`, then moved by the milestone type-test bead to the module below. Exported names are stable: downstream beads cite them; a rename needs a contract revision and an update of the `contracts.md` export index.

- `packages/browser-model-manager/src/contracts/grant.ts`: `AcquisitionGrant` (manifest identity, route, `GrantPurpose` = `generate` | `generate-and-encode` | `prepare-encoder`, asset digests, advertised remaining-byte scope, owners), `GrantOwnerId`, `GrantDecision` (`approved` | `declined` | `cancelled` | `revision-required`), `AcquisitionPriority` (`foreground-required` | `synthesis-prerequisite` | `detector-prerequisite` | `optional` | `speculative-warming`), `WarmingOwnership`.
- `packages/browser-model-manager/src/contracts/budgets.ts`: `AcquisitionBudget` (aggregate transfer, read-ahead, hash and write-buffer bytes) and `LiveResidencyLimit` as named fields; values set by `contracts.byte-ceilings-freeze`.
- Consumers: `consent.grant-model`, `consent.*`, `manager.acquisition`, `opctl.*`, `evaluator.overlap-warming-adapters`.

## Out of scope

The consent modal and UI (acquisition consent workstream). Numeric limits (m2 ceilings item).

## Considerations

The manager supplies primitives only; policy lives in the app (ownership tie-break).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts.md` grant section with draft types for grant, owner, priority class and budget structure.
- [ ] Walkthroughs: approve both then Cancel crop; Generate-only then photo request; shared fetch with two owners where one cancels; unknown inventory → no fetch.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Every name listed under "Typed outputs (citable)" exists in the draft type file and has a row in the `contracts.md` export index naming its consumers.
notes: Anchors: PLAN.md#gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design (Operation/resource ownership); #consented-downloads-useful-overlap-and-cached-model-warming.

title: Implement the alignment-failure and detector-refusal path with optional manual crop
description:
## Background
Locked `failed to align.png` (reference bundle, SHA-256 `074096a9…255b`): old **"Upload an image"** modal with the
logo top right; the **full uploaded image** as preview (not a square crop); a **red/pink filled CROP button** centred
under it; a red line **"Unable to auto align face."**; white guidance "When the face isn't aligned you may get strange
results. Try a different image or manually crop it. Make sure the entire face is in frame and looking towards to
camera."; **CANCEL** bottom left, **OK** bottom right (indigo). The candidate refuses unaligned photos (audit); classic
accepted them with a warning. The plan's ruling (PLAN.md#supplied-ui-references and
#confirmed-crop-and-ordered-multi-selection-flow): retain the failure message and guidance, update the title to
**"Encode an image"** and the control to **ADJUST CROP**; manual crop is optional; explicit continuation with eligible
pixels may use direct e4e; never an automatic crop loop. Measured boxes/colours from `face.legacy-dialog-inventory`.

## Why
The confirmed-crop loop repair is an original requirement (PLAN.md#next-release-ui-and-photo-requirements, Repair
confirmed-crop loop).

## Scope
- Layout per the locked image with the two renames: title **"Encode an image"**, logo top right, full-image preview
  (whole image visible at its aspect ratio), the red filled button centred under the preview labelled **ADJUST
  CROP**, the red line **"Unable to auto align face."**, the guidance copy (verbatim except the typo decision recorded
  in the inventory: default "looking towards the camera"), CANCEL bottom left, OK bottom right.
- Three distinct states:
  1. **No face detected** (detector ran): the locked failure layout above.
  2. **Detector assets refused/unavailable**: same layout but the red line says detection did not run (for example
     "Face detection did not run."), never "Unable to auto align face."; an unrun detector is never a failure.
  3. **Malformed/unsupported pixels**: actionable terminal error in the modal (what to do: choose another image),
     no ADJUST CROP, no OK; no encoder request.
- ADJUST CROP opens the editor (`face.crop-editor-modal`); USE CROP returns to the confirmation state with the manual
  crop; OK there encodes it.
- OK directly from the failure state continues with the eligible whole-image pixels (the default square proposal the
  inventory records) and reaches exactly one e4e attempt or an actionable error; detection failure after OK cannot
  reopen the crop prompt; repeated OK presses produce one attempt.
- Detector refusal abandons that acquisition only; OK/manual continuation is a new explicit request for its remaining
  prerequisites, never a revival of the refused detector.

## Out of scope
Encoding/fallback internals (`ws:crop`); consent grant (`ws:consent`).

## Considerations
Do not force manual repair; do not automatically encode unconfirmed pixels. The guidance already warns that results
may look odd ("you may get strange results").
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** It renders the typed detector failure kinds that `crop.fix` (ws:crop) exposes, in the ported crop modal; detector/alignment calls go through the facade unchanged. If implementation finds it must edit one of them after all, it first runs `br dep add fm-i8s5 fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph), adds the file to the conflict list in fm-bhw and records the change in its receipt (the plan's rule: an edge is added when an edit is discovered).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Operated-UI rule: each acceptance step acts with real pointer input (touch tap at phone widths) at the control's visible position, asserts `document.elementFromPoint` at that point returns the control (or a descendant) and that the point lies inside the region a person would look in (named per control below); by-name/by-role clicks are used only to set up state, never as the acceptance step.
- [ ] Every case is checked at a phone width (390 px) and a desktop width (1,280 px) with one screenshot per case kept as evidence, in light and dark themes.
- [ ] Fixture with no face (a landscape illustration like the locked image): rendered-geometry comparison against the inventory's failure-layout boxes (title top-left, logo top-right, full-image preview with all four image corners visible, red ADJUST CROP button centred under the preview, red failure line, guidance block, CANCEL footer-left, OK footer-right) within tolerance; exact strings "Encode an image", "ADJUST CROP", "Unable to auto align face." and the guidance text asserted; the failure line's colour matches the inventory red and meets 4.5:1 against the modal background.
- [ ] Operated OK (region: footer right) -> one e4e attempt in the log; no second crop prompt appears; three rapid OK taps -> one request ID.
- [ ] Operated ADJUST CROP (region: centred under the preview) -> editor opens; USE CROP -> confirmation with the manual crop; OK -> one e4e attempt with those pixels (pixel check).
- [ ] Detector consent declined: red line says detection did not run (string asserted; "Unable to auto align face." absent); ADJUST CROP remains; zero detector requests in the network log.
- [ ] Corrupt file and an unsupported type: actionable terminal error, no ADJUST CROP or OK rendered, zero encoder requests.
- [ ] Operated CANCEL (region: footer left), Escape and Back: no encode, no keypoints, focus restored.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic run in CI (`npm test` workspace target) and pass (state selection: no-face / detector-not-run / malformed; one-attempt guard).
- [ ] Each end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Every network claim is asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] No raw runtime exception text appears as visitor copy; one message owner per failed action.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Remove, Undo, Start over and the many-face layout; budget-based admission
description:
## Goal
The face row is designed for many faces, not for two; there is no fixed face count (operator, 24 October: only real constraints). Remove must be a real control a person can hit at any count, "I added thirty and want to remove twenty" must be bearable on a phone and a desktop, and every entry path must go through one admission check against real budgets, with one plain message naming the limit reached. Fixes defects 1, 2, 3, 7, 17 (remove part) and 18 found by the 18 October operated check; this is the separately accepted split item "many-face layout and removal".

## Scope
- **Defects.** 1: the Remove control loses a stylesheet tie to the component library, sits in normal flow below the image (clipped, invisible) in dark grey over the mode-menu button; a real click opens "Change mode" while by-name checks pass (at 1,280 px: control 32x32 at (201, 611), image box 376x376 at (206, 229)). 2: layouts exist for two and three faces only; at 1,280 px the third tile reaches x = 1,488; from the third face the row is a sideways strip with no cue; fourteen faces make a ~6,000 px strip, or ~7,000 px of stacked ~480 px tiles on a phone. 3: no undo/reset; thirty to ten is twenty taps. 7: with one face, Add face is disabled beside a note to add a second face. 17: removing a generating face does not stop its job. 18: the 64 cap is enforced in one of three places ("+" silently does nothing, multi-file drop uncapped, a 65-face morph fails with the generic project error).
- **Remove.** A visible close button on each face image (top right), at rest on touch and desktop, not overlapped by any control, keyboard reachable, hit area >= 44 x 44 px at touch widths (drawn circle may be smaller). Its style must not depend on the component library's rule ordering; acceptance tests the rendered result. Remove aborts that slot's owned work through the operation service and releases its resources; siblings unaffected; late results rejected by the revision check. Focus moves to a sensible neighbour. The last face is non-removable with a readable reason. With one face left, Generate, Encode image and Save still work and Create Morph is disabled with a reason saying a second face is needed.
- **Undo.** After Remove a short notice (near the face row, covering no face action or Create Morph, announced in a live region) offers **Undo**, restoring the face at the same index with its content; it disappears after its timeout or the next action without moving focus. During the Undo window the face is hidden in controller state (with `invalidateMorph` for the current morph and excluded from Create Morph) and the facade's `invalidateFace` call is deferred until the notice expires or the next action replaces it, so Undo re-shows the retained result with no bridge call and no inference.
- **Start over** in More options returns the project to two empty faces in one action, with the same Undo.
- **Layout.** Past the width where two or three full tiles fit, a contained strip with a visible scroll cue (edge fade or arrows, and a scrollbar) and snapping, or a compact grid; on a phone, tiles beyond the fourth shrink to a compact row (small image, field, Remove). This bead picks the presentation against the locked references and these bars (the plan fixes bars, not pixels). Thirty faces should take a few phone screens, not about fourteen. Past about a hundred faces the strip or grid renders only the tiles near the view (virtualised), so the page stays responsive; scrolling, Tab order, Remove and Undo still reach every face.
- No page-level sideways scroll and no hidden scrolling surface at any count at any sweep width. Every face's image, field, slot action and Remove (except the last face) visible or reachable by normal scrolling of the page or the strip/grid, with a visible cue whenever a face is off screen. Remove stays inside its face image (or compact-row thumbnail) with the 44 x 44 hit area at every count and width. Insertion + controls between faces stay hittable (not covered by tiles, arrows or fades).
- **Add face** stays enabled at every count.
- **One admission check** before any bridge call, used by every entry path: insertion +, Add face, multi-file drop, batch OK, paste into a new face, background drop (and the blend view's Add to morph). It checks real budgets only: retained photo-input bytes and stored-session size from the contracts ceilings (`apps/web/src/contracts/ceilings.ts`), never a face count. A refusal names the actual limit reached in one plain message with the existing reduce-selection option; never silent truncation or a silent no-op. Morph's frame budget is checked at Morph (`morph.guards`, fm-fy2.9), with the estimate and reduce length, before frame inference.
- **Count limits removed in the port.** `MaxControls = 64` in classic `ProjectJson.fs` (carried as-is for parity into `apps/web/src/project/project-json.ts` by `migration.facade`, fm-pia9) is replaced here by a byte-size sanity bound on untrusted project files from the contracts ceilings, not a face count. The analytics `faces` range ([0, 64] in `analytics.mjs` NUMBERS) widens so larger counts are recorded, not clamped.
- Sweep widths: 320, 360, 390, 480, 600, 768, 900, 1,024, 1,280, 1,920, 2,560 px plus 1 px either side of each layout breakpoint read from the built CSS; touch widths (at or below the phone/tablet breakpoint) run with `hasTouch`/`isMobile`.

## Out of scope
The full responsive sweep with live resize/zoom (face.sweep); Morph's frame budget check (`morph.guards`); the session-restore count check in `last-result.mjs` (`media.session`, fm-5hww).

## Notes
- **Operator may veto**: Undo and Start over are planner proposals. If vetoed before close, drop them; the Remove, focus and last-face cases still pass.
- The candidate one-rule Remove repair is ordinary candidate work in delivery's early edit set; this bead implements the full set in the port. Layout CSS, the controller-side admission check and the `project-json.ts` bound swap only; no shared bridge/runtime/worker file edited.
- The compact tile defined here is reused by the blend view.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#face-controls-and-modals (many faces and removal), #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026, #integrated-verification.

title: Lay out 1 to 64 faces and pass the operated many-face removal matrix (no sideways scroll, one cap, Add face enabled)
description:
## Background
Operated check, 18 October (PLAN.md#known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026):
- Defect 2: the candidate has layouts for two and three faces only. At 1,280 px the third tile is cut off (its box
  reaches x = 1,488 in a 1,280 px window); from the third face the row is a sideways strip with no visible scroll cue;
  fourteen faces make a strip about 6,000 px long; on a phone tiles stack at about 480 px each (fourteen faces about
  7,000 px tall).
- Defect 3: thirty faces down to ten is twenty taps through that strip; no undo or reset.
- Defect 7: with one face left Add face is disabled beside a note telling the person to add a second face.
- Defect 18 (source): the 64-face cap is enforced in one of three places ("+" silently does nothing, multi-file drop
  is uncapped, a 65-face morph fails with the generic project error).
The Remove control itself, Undo and Start over are built by `face.remove-undo-startover`; this leaf owns the layout at
every count and the plan's operated many-faces acceptance (PLAN.md#face-controls-and-modals, "Many faces and removal"),
which is the separately accepted split item "many-face layout and removal".

## Why
The face row is designed for the cap (64), not for two. "I added thirty faces and want to remove twenty" must be
bearable on a phone and a desktop.

## Scope
- Presentation chosen in `face.design-review`: past the width where two or three full tiles fit, a contained strip
  with a visible scroll cue (edge fade or arrows, and a scrollbar) and snapping, or a compact grid; on a phone, tiles
  beyond the fourth shrink to a compact row (small image, field, Remove).
- No page-level sideways scroll and no hidden scrolling surface at any count up to 64 at any sweep width.
- Every face's image, field, Generate (or its current slot action) and Remove (except the last face) visible or
  reachable by normal scrolling of the page or the contained strip/grid, with a visible cue whenever any face is off
  screen.
- Remove stays inside its face image (the compact-row thumbnail for compact rows), not overlapped, with a 44 x 44 px
  hit area at touch widths, at every count and width.
- Add face stays enabled from 1 face up to the cap.
- One cap check with one plain message (for example "You can have up to 64 faces.") for every entry path: the
  insertion +, Add face, multi-file drop, batch OK, paste into a new face and background drop.
- Insertion + controls between faces remain hittable at every count (not covered by tiles, cue arrows or fades).

## Out of scope
The full responsive sweep with live resize/zoom (`face.responsive-sweep`); Morph's own count checks (`ws:morph`).

## Considerations
Thirty faces should take a few phone screens, not about fourteen; the measured height is recorded. Sweep widths
(PLAN.md#integrated-verification): 320, 360, 390, 480, 600, 768, 900, 1,024, 1,280, 1,920 and 2,560 px, plus 1 px
either side of each actual layout breakpoint read from the built CSS. Touch widths are those at or below the
phone/tablet breakpoint and are run with touch emulation (`hasTouch`, `isMobile`).
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** It is layout CSS and controller-side cap enforcement in the ported UI; the cap check runs before any bridge call. If implementation finds it must edit one of them after all, it first runs `br dep add fm-ifkk fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph), adds the file to the conflict list in fm-bhw and records the change in its receipt (the plan's rule: an edge is added when an edit is discovered).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Operated-UI rule: each acceptance step acts with real pointer input (touch tap at phone widths) at the control's visible position, asserts `document.elementFromPoint` at that point returns the control (or a descendant) and that the point lies inside the region a person would look in (named per control below); by-name/by-role clicks are used only to set up state, never as the acceptance step.
- [ ] Matrix: face counts 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 30 and 64 x widths 320, 360, 390, 480, 600, 768, 900, 1,024, 1,280, 1,920, 2,560 px and 1 px either side of each built-CSS breakpoint (faces set up by the controller fixture, not by clicking). One screenshot per cell; the receipt lists every cell with pass/fail and the untested ones.
- [ ] Per cell: `document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth` (no page sideways scroll); no element other than the declared strip/grid container has `scrollWidth > clientWidth` with overflow hidden (no hidden scrolling surface); a scroll cue (fade/arrow and scrollbar) is visible whenever any face's box is outside the viewport or the container's visible box.
- [ ] Per cell, for every face (scrolling the page or the strip/grid with real wheel/swipe input to reach it): image, field and slot action are inside the viewport after scrolling and `elementFromPoint` at each centre is that control.
- [ ] Per cell with 2 or more faces, for every face: Remove's box lies inside its face image box (compact-row thumbnail for compact rows); `elementFromPoint` at Remove's centre is Remove; at touch widths the hit area is at least 44 x 44 px (measured from the hit target, and `elementFromPoint` at the four corners of that 44 x 44 box returns Remove); no other interactive control's box overlaps it.
- [ ] Per cell with 1 face: no Remove rendered or enabled; Add face enabled; operated Add face (region: the face row's add control) adds a second face.
- [ ] Per cell with 2 or more faces: a real click (desktop) or tap (touch widths) at the centre of a middle face's Remove removes exactly that face (face IDs before/after), with no page reload (navigation count unchanged), and focus lands on a neighbour (the next face's Remove or field, else the previous); operated **Undo** in the notice (region: the notice near the face row, not covering any face action) restores the face at the same index with the same content identity.
- [ ] At 30 and at 64 faces, at 390 px and 1,280 px: every face's Remove is visible-and-hittable after scrolling; removing twenty faces one tap each removes exactly one face per tap; operated **Start over** in More options (region: More options menu) returns the project to two empty faces in one action, and Undo restores all 30 (or 64) faces in order with their content.
- [ ] At 64 faces: the insertion +, Add face, a multi-file drop, a paste into a new face, a background drop and a batch OK that would exceed the cap each show the same plain cap message (string equality across paths) and add nothing; no silent no-op (event log shows the refusal).
- [ ] Phone width (390 px), 30 faces: page height measured and recorded (target: a few screens; record the number of 844 px screens).
- [ ] Insertion + controls: at 3, 8 and 64 faces, `elementFromPoint` at each visible + centre returns that +.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic run in CI (`npm test` workspace target) and pass (single cap check called from every entry path; layout mode selection by width/count).
- [ ] Each end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Every network claim is asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes:
Audit rows 2, 7, 18. Plan anchors: PLAN.md#face-controls-and-modals (many faces and removal), #integrated-verification (responsiveness acceptance).
Polish r1 (E): now owns the plan's full operated many-faces matrix (1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 30, 64 x sweep widths) incl. Remove containment, 44 x 44 hit area, Undo and Start over; title updated.
Polish r2 (E): design field states the shared-file order decision for this bead.

title: Typed failure causes, collector rebinding, built-UI checks
description:
## Goal
Make every failed event say what failed and where, with one action/event list shared by client and collector; bind analytics and reporting deliberately to production hosts; remove the collector's unenforced expiry so no code claims a deletion it does not perform; and pass the debug-reporting built-UI checks against the actual configured collector. Today all 81 failed events in the mined reports carry `operation_failed` (kind `unknown` 47, `decode` 25, `unsupported` 9; 21 with no stage), and defect 13 (`validation.mjs:13`, `reporting.mjs:275`, `worker.mjs:24-27`): the collector accepts actions `faces`, `morph`, `project`, the client sends `photo`, and one bad event rejects the whole batch.

## Scope
- **Closed cause list**: photo decode, route refused, canary failed, storage or quota, download or integrity, synthesis, alignment, encoding, export, page hidden or closed; plus the stage. `unknown` only for a caught exception that matched nothing, counted as a defect. Never record photos, latents, typed inputs or raw error strings.
- **One shared action/event list module** imported by client and collector, with a CI test that fails if they differ; it includes the `blend` operation for the weighted face blend. A bad event is rejected alone, not the batch.
- **Event registry**: every event added by consent, batch, scheduler, warming, the device check or the blend view is listed with its allowlist and privacy-policy entry before that bead is accepted.
- **Host rebinding**: deliberate host/route configuration for production (and the candidate host while it serves), independent of Triton/API retirement. Today `analytics.mjs` scopes to `next.facemorph.me` and `reporting.mjs` posts to `https://next.facemorph.me/diagnostics/events`; the usage-statistics sink keeps its own production host list (`diag.usage-stats`, fm-5yqq), which this bead folds into the map; no `next.facemorph.me` literal remains outside the configured host map.
- **Re-homed collector** (`hosting/next-cloudflare/worker.mjs`, source supplied by deploy re-homing): stop writing `customMetadata.expiresAt` (lifecycle rules cannot match custom metadata); drop the KV fallback's 30-day expiry; no bucket expiration rule (bucket `facemorph-diagnostics`, created 21 September 2026, has none).
- A consented sample reaches the collector; declined or blocked samples never prevent generation; failures are non-blocking.
- **Built-UI checks** of PLAN.md#debug-reporting-control-and-consent on the built artifact against the configured collector: saved On/Off/refusal; storage failure; keyboard/label/link focus; withdrawal during an active job; aborted/discarded sends; no new debug traffic after Off without a separately approved one-shot; scoped reporting with unrelated staged slot records; Off-only toast visibility; explicit ongoing opt-in and later withdrawal; the failure-toast consent fix; the configured collector's retention and production host bindings.

## Out of scope
Delivery's production collector go-live; usage-analytics policy changes. No iPhone pass, analytics success rate or diagnostics-derived score controls cutover.

## Notes
- **Shared file.** Typed causes change error paths reached through `product-bridge.mjs` (plus `reporting.mjs` and collector validation), and host rebinding is the plan's named bridge-consuming edit (`product-bridge.mjs` host and issue-link references, `reporting.mjs`, `analytics.mjs`), so this bead follows the morph pipeline in the diagnostics-edits position. The built-UI checks add tests only.
- The `blend` action-list entry comes from PLAN.md#weighted-face-blend-advanced-mode (Owners: diagnostics consent control adds it).
- Anchors: PLAN.md#diagnostics-consent-control, #debug-reporting-control-and-consent (retention item 4), #diagnostics-that-must-survive-the-move, #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance (typed failure causes). Audit row 13.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Forced failure at each stage (corrupt photo, refused route, failed canary, storage full, broken download, synthesis error, alignment failure, encoding failure, export failure, page hidden) produces the matching cause and stage in the report.
- [ ] Scan of the test reports finds no `unknown` without a counted defect.
- [ ] Client/collector list equality test in CI (including `blend`); a batch with one invalid event delivers the valid ones.
- [ ] Registry test: every event emitted by the app has an allowlist and privacy-policy entry.
- [ ] Config test: the production build posts to the production route from the host map; no `next.facemorph.me` literal outside it.
- [ ] Against the configured collector: a consented report is stored (found by the reference shown in the disclosure); the object carries no `expiresAt`; KV writes carry no 30-day TTL; declined and network-blocked samples do not affect generation (job completes).
- [ ] Operated built-UI checks (real pointer/touch with `elementFromPoint` at the named regions; 390 and 1,280 px, light and dark): saved On / Off / No thanks restore with no false render; localStorage throwing shows the tab-only message and reload shows Off; Tab, label click, Space and footer/FAQ links work; withdrawal during an active job aborts and discards while the job completes; after Off zero collector requests except one approved one-shot holding only the owning attempt's records; Off-only single toast, none offering opt-in while On, and at 1,280x800 and 390x844 `elementFromPoint` at Create Morph and every face action returns the action; **Turn on debug reporting** then footer withdrawal works; **Send this report** leaves the stored preference unchanged.
- [ ] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test`) and pass.
- [ ] Field leads (diagnostics learnings, 18 October): once typed causes ship, the first reports at the former `unsupported` stages (`face`, `original-cache-hit`) and at interruptions are classified by cause, and each new cause gets a bead.
- [ ] event registry complete at close (fm-fy2.9 events listed) (with fm-fy2.9). If fm-fy2.9 has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-fy2.9 (`br update fm-fy2.9 --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-fy2.9
