title: Scheduler, cancellation, and Morph and Blend parent intents
description:
## Goal
One application scheduler authority over photo encodes, face synthesis and morph production that bounds aggregate GPU/WASM/model memory (per-slot queues cannot: the 120 x 1024^2 source limit alone can be 480 MiB for one RGBA buffer), settles every cancellation before resources are reused, and treats Morph as a dependency-aware parent intent that never holds a heavyweight lease while waiting for its own prerequisite faces and never duplicates inference. Settled 12 October: Create Morph automatically generates unfinished valid text/seed inputs before frames, as one accepted intent with shared consent/progress/Cancel.

## Scope
- Admit one heavyweight operation at a time per shared provider context; keep bounded internal frame pipelining and qualified warm reuse.
- Admission covers manager/provider runtime initialization, model/session loading and real-model numerical admission (canaries), not only the final inference call.
- Separate compute permit from residency reservations (loaded sessions, shard buffers, WASM heaps, GPU allocations); verified disk-cache leases distinct from live-memory reservations; idle warm resources count until actual release/worker termination; reserve before allocating; account for the encoder-to-generator transition with the candidate's retention policy (encoder residency only under a qualified desktop memory policy; alignment/encoder workers terminated before the next heavy phase on constrained devices, since releasing an ONNX session does not shrink its WASM heap).
- Downloads, image preparation and file encoding use their own budgets; no speculative warmup evicts foreground live resources; waiting jobs never hold resources the active job needs.
- Busy/unavailable capabilities reported through the same contract; request order preserved (no starvation of an eligible morph by a stream of faces). Release compute admission after compute settles; awaiting file preparation holds no idle heavyweight permit.
- Numeric residency/byte ceilings wired from contracts milestone 2's decode measurement; tests use symbolic budgets until those exist.
- Cancellation: per-slot Cancel (actual abort/worker stop where supported; candidate aborts with `active?.abort(); writer?.dispose(); runtime?.cancel()`), Cancelling state until settlement, then Retry if input remains. Shared fetch/acquisition stops when its final authorized consumer leaves; other explicit owners continue. Cancelling a morph never destroys a separately requested face job. Cancel is distinct from Hide (candidate prefetch toast offers Hide). Removal invalidates and releases that slot without affecting unrelated completed faces. Network/worker submissions stop within the declared bound. Do not promise instant preemption of submitted GPU work; settle the in-flight unit. Revision invalidation alone is not permission to keep running abandoned work.
- Morph parent: snapshots ordered compatible input revisions and settings; unfinished words/seeds become dependency face jobs; pending selected-name/confirmed-photo results are dependencies; invalid/unconfirmed inputs block acceptance with a reason. Join an existing operation for the same slot/revision rather than enqueueing duplicates; dependencies admitted once. Release/yield compute admission before awaiting dependencies or download consent; request the frame-production lease through the same scheduler when ready. Join a dependency's compute-ready milestone (verified latent + usable endpoint), not its default-file completion; delayed/failed face-file preparation never duplicates inference or blocks ready inputs. Parent Cancel stops work owned solely by the parent, detaches from independently requested faces and leaves their results; failed/cancelled dependencies settle the parent with a specific recovery action (no permanently disabled Morph or dangling promise). Encoder and generator capabilities stay explicit; synthesis eligibility does not imply encoder admission. A newer face edit abandons the old morph.
- Frame budget (estimate owned by morph against the contracts frame budget) does not hold other work: independently requested photo encoding or face generation never waits for a future Morph's budget; a Morph that does not fit settles with its reduce-length reason before any Morph-owned acquisition or inference; selected faces are never dropped to make it fit.
- Blend parent (PLAN.md "Weighted face blend (advanced mode)", Owners: the operation controller owns the blend parent intent and supersession): a typed `request blend` (ordered slot input revisions + weights) added to the operation-service interface. Like Morph it is a parent intent: it waits for each slot's latent (mapping for an unfinished word or seed, the confirmed encode for a photo, the catalogue latent for a name), not for slot images or files, holds no permit while waiting, then runs `blend(latents, weights)` (compute.blend) and one synthesis. Slots at weight 0 are skipped; all-zero weights are refused with a typed reason before any work. A newer weight change supersedes a pending blend (latest wins by input revision; the superseded result is never installed). Leaving the view cancels a pending blend synthesis while slot photo encodes keep running.

## Out of scope
- Additional concurrency (only with measured aggregate memory and cancellation evidence).
- Consent-dialog Cancel semantics beyond releasing the intent's ownership (consent).
- Frame-budget estimate, frame production, MP4 availability probe, identical-neighbour refusal (morph).

## Notes
- No fakes (operator, 24 October): the scheduling core is a pure state machine fed timestamped events as plain values, and the same cases run again through the real worker with real timers. Each test logs a permit/reservation trace, printed on failure.

title: Freeze scheduler, compute permit, residency reservation and Morph parent-intent contract
description:
## Background

One application scheduler governs competing photo encodes, face synthesis and morph production;
per-slot queues cannot bound aggregate GPU/WASM/model memory. Initially one heavyweight operation at a
time per shared provider context, retaining bounded internal frame pipelining and qualified warm reuse.
The 120 × 1024² source limit is 480 MiB for one RGBA buffer alone. Existing 4,096-frame path limit.
Constrained iPhone/unknown-memory paths terminate alignment/encoder workers before the next heavy phase
(releasing an ONNX session does not shrink its WASM heap).

## Why

The application operation controller implements this; morph pipeline and acquisition consent rely on it.

## Scope

- Separate compute permit, loaded-asset (disk) leases and live runtime-residency reservations (sessions,
  shard buffers, WASM heaps, GPU allocations). Admission includes runtime init, model/session loading
  and canary execution, not only final inference. Idle warm memory counts until actual release.
- Reserve before allocating; encoder-to-generator transition; constrained teardown vs qualified desktop
  warm reuse; waiting jobs do not hold resources the active job needs; no speculative warmup evicts
  foreground live resources.
- Morph as parent intent: yields its permit while awaiting dependencies or consent; joins existing
  operations for the same slot/revision; frame-production lease through the same scheduler; parent
  Cancel detaches from independently requested face jobs; failed/cancelled inputs settle the parent
  with a specific recovery action; join compute-ready rather than file-complete.
- Frame/slot budget estimation before Morph-owned work; 4,096-frame limit; no truncation of selected faces.
- Route snapshot at Start/Download approval: requested CPU/WebGPU route, bounded fallback scope,
  runtime/model identity; actual provider recorded; selector changes affect new jobs only.
- Busy/unavailable capabilities reported through the same contract by browser adapters.

## Typed outputs (citable)

Draft first under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`, then moved by the milestone type-test bead to the module below. Exported names are stable: downstream beads cite them; a rename needs a contract revision and an update of the `contracts.md` export index.

- `apps/web/src/contracts/scheduler.ts`: `ComputePermit`, `ResidencyReservation` (sessions, shard buffers, WASM heaps, GPU allocations; reserved before allocation), `AssetLeaseRef` (wraps the manager `AssetLease`), `MorphParentIntent` (yields permit while waiting; joins same slot/revision), `IntentSettlement` (with specific recovery action), `RouteSnapshot` (requested route, bounded fallback scope, runtime/model identity; actual provider recorded later), `FrameBudget`, `CapabilityStatus` (busy/unavailable from adapters), `ConstrainedTeardownPolicy`.
- Consumers: `opctl.interface`, `opctl.*`, `morph.*`, `consent.overlap-scheduling`, `compute.app-rebind`.

## Out of scope

Implementation and fake-clock tests (operation controller workstream).

## Considerations

Additional concurrency only with measured aggregate memory and cancellation evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts.md` scheduler section with draft types for permit, reservation, lease, intent and settlement.
- [ ] Walkthroughs: photo → queued Morph; Morph auto-generation → explicit face request; capability loss while queued; Cancel at each dependency boundary; idle retained encoder while generator load is requested.

title: renderMorph in stylegan-js with descriptor-driven geometry
description:
## Split (parallelism pass, 24 October 2026)
The package/core work of this bead moved to fm-suaa (renderMorph core in stylegan-js with descriptor-driven geometry), which edits no shared file and starts as soon as its own inputs exist. This bead keeps: rewiring the bridge's morph path to `renderMorph` (app keeps URL creation, retention and slider preference), deleting the moved app code, and the real-bridge check. The scope text below is kept for context; where it describes work now owned by fm-suaa, that bead owns and accepts it and this bead consumes the result.

## Goal
Move morph orchestration (geometry, infill, frame store and writer) behind one `renderMorph` in `stylegan-js` with bounded memory, and make morph geometry read latent shape from the model descriptor so non-face checkpoints with other layer counts or latent sizes morph through the same algorithm or fail with an actionable error. The engine owns geometry, bounded frame production and computational media helpers; the app keeps indices-to-UI mapping, URLs, retention and the slider preference. No partial animation is ever exported as complete.

## Scope
**renderMorph**
- Candidate sources: `src/Next/morph-frames.mjs` (~280 lines), `infill.mjs`, the bridge, `media.mjs`, `video-worker.mjs` (WebCodecs 1024->512, FFmpeg 512, eight-frame raw segments, 4,096-frame path limit shared with `last-result.mjs`).
- `renderMorph({endpoints, settings, descriptor, signal, onFrame, onProgress}) -> video result` composing geometry, infill, frame store and writer; contracts define endpoints, settings, display callbacks and the result.
- Canonical indices and presentation order exposed; the app keeps URL creation, retention and slider preference.
- Preserve bounded GPU submit/readback overlap, windows, ordered delivery and fallback resumption (morph-frame-pipeline-v1), sparse preview anchors that cannot deadlock ordered video drain, direct RGBA display/video input, eight-frame raw segments, bounded codec queues and stream-copy concatenation.
- Paths with distinct callback/drain semantics, each tested: cached frames, raw sparse anchors, blob stream, bounded sequential browser paths, retained-then-encode.
- Typed settle status: `complete` (every frame of the accepted path encoded, container finalized with project metadata), `cancelled`, `failed`, `export-failed` (frames produced, writer failed). Only `complete` yields a shareable video result. Cancel at any frame k returns no video file, the app offers no Save/Share video for that revision, and retention stores no video for it. `export-failed` keeps frames for export-only Retry (morph.guards) and is never shown as finished.

**Descriptor-driven geometry**
- `geometry/latent-path.mjs` (`latent-path-v1`) today accepts only Z/W `[512]` (rotating halves J(a,b)=(-b,a)) and W+ `[18,512]` (same rotation per layer, no layer mixing). Shape modes: linear, pairwise-ellipse, pairwise-figure8, full-smooth-ellipse, full-smooth-figure8; 2–64 controls; at most 100,000 total frames; fps 1–120.
- Lift the `latent-path-v1` 2–64 control-count check (operator, 24 October: no fixed face count; PLAN.md defect 18): any count from 2 is accepted, bounded by the contracts frame budget that `morph.guards` checks at acceptance. Outputs for every input the old check accepted are unchanged, so `GEOMETRY_VERSION` stays; the 100,000-total-frame and fps 1–120 checks stay as untrusted-input sanity bounds.
- Read latent space/shape from the descriptor (any even width, any declared layer count) with the same per-layer rotation rules; reject unsupported shapes with a typed actionable error.
- Keep `GEOMETRY_VERSION` semantics: never replace an imported version; unknown algorithms rejected; outputs for existing shapes must not change, so no version bump for them. All five modes survive unchanged for FFHQ; existing `geometry/verify.mjs` checks keep passing.
- Check with a qualified caller-loaded reference at a different output resolution/layer count (the conversion.qualify non-face fixture or the compute.photo-descriptor test reference).

## Out of scope
Scheduler/parent intent (operation controller; integration in morph.guards). Morph button, progress and Cancel UI (face controls). Frame budget and MP4 probe (morph.guards). Mapping/synthesis generalization (compute). Recovery schema (media.schema).

## Notes
- Geometry changes edit none of the shared files; the bridge rewiring for `renderMorph` does.
- Shared-file order (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October; revised in the 24 October final pass): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in one sequence enforced by needs edges, never concurrently: `provider.native` -> `provider.webgl` -> `provider.route-admission` -> `migration.project-json` (one-line ProjectJson import swap) -> typed facade (`migration.facade`) -> `compute.synthesis` -> `compute.photo-descriptor` -> `compute.app-rebind` -> `crop.fix` -> `crop.queue` -> `media.reader-wiring` -> `media.export` -> `media.schema` -> `morph.render` -> `morph.guards` -> `media.session` -> face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Rows that must not edit these files: `crop.repro`, `compute.blend`, `compute.package-surface`, `media.envelope`, `provider.admission` (evidence), `crop.ported-app` and `compute.ported-app` (acceptance on the ported app; a fix they need follows the out-of-turn rule below) and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept row; code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) until the bridge's own turn. A row that finds it must edit one of these files outside its turn adds a needs edge to the latest row in the sequence that edits it. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #morph-pipeline, #external-developer-journey-and-non-face-models.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] fm-suaa is closed; its modules are what this bead wires in (no second copy of the moved code left in the app).
- [ ] Real-bridge harness morph (32 frames, 16 FPS) through `renderMorph` yields a `complete` MP4 whose decoded frame count equals `totalFrames`; cancel mid-production offers no video.
- [ ] Existing app morph tests pass, adapted only where the code they assert moved; no second copy of morph-frames/infill left in the app.

title: Inventory the legacy Encode image dialog behaviour against the locked images
description:
## Background
The locked images are in the reference bundle `../reference-locks/2026-10-11-original-plan-and-images/images/`
(SHA-256 in that bundle's `SHA256SUMS` and in PLAN.md#supplied-ui-references: `crop image.png` `dc2b0708…a280`,
`crop 2.png` `753f4ad6…6c1`, `failed to align.png` `074096a9…255b`, `recovered image.png` `d67fdf00…0b62`). They were
viewed 16 October and again at bead polish (24 October). What they show, element by element:

**`crop image.png` (about 395 x 520 px screenshot) - title "Encode an image".** Dark grey modal over a dimmed page;
white title top left; the FaceMorph line-drawn face logo top right; a square proposed-crop preview centred under the
title (the face already aligned and centred in it); the text button **ADJUST CROP** (uppercase, no fill) centred below
the preview; **CANCEL** bottom left as a light grey filled button with dark text; **OK** bottom right as a blue
(indigo) filled button with white text. No other copy.

**`crop 2.png` (about 623 x 885 px) - title "Crop your image".** Same modal chrome (title top left, logo top right).
The source photo shown letterboxed in a wide frame (a black band where the photo does not fill it); over it a square
crop stencil drawn as a thin light outline with **eight white square handles** (four corners, four edge midpoints);
the area outside the stencil is not darkened in the screenshot; inside the stencil a **translucent light oval face
guide** sized to the face, with **two dark round eye markers** on a horizontal line in its upper half. Below the
photo, centred: a **crop-rotate icon** followed by the degree readout **"0°"**. Below that a **full-width slider**
(indigo track, round thumb at the centre for 0°). Then the copy, left aligned: bold **"Cropping is generally not
necessary, as faces are usually auto detected."**, then on new lines "Try to leave a bit above the top of the head
and below the chin." and "Lining up the eyes is most important." Footer: **CANCEL** bottom left (light grey filled),
**USE CROP** bottom right (indigo filled).

**`failed to align.png` (about 615 x 784 px) - title "Upload an image".** Same chrome. The full uploaded image as a
preview (not a square crop; in the screenshot a landscape illustration with no face). A **red/pink filled CROP
button** centred under the preview. Then a red line **"Unable to auto align face."** followed by white guidance
"When the face isn't aligned you may get strange results. Try a different image or manually crop it. Make sure the
entire face is in frame and looking towards to camera." (sic: "towards to"). Footer: **CANCEL** bottom left, **OK**
bottom right (indigo).

**`recovered image.png`** shows the historical two-face page with the controls the plan removes: the duplicate
filename caption ("daniel image.jpeg" under the field), **CROP PHOTO** after encoding, and **Hold to compare**.

**Historical `src/EncodeImageDialog.fs`** (classic checkout `facemorph.me-classic`, history) uses a
`react-advanced-cropper` stencil with a fixed aspect ratio, a **90° rotate button** plus the fine-rotation slider, a
**file chooser** and an **"Or paste image here"** field inside the dialog; it detected faces on the server and
encoded before confirmation.

## Why
PLAN.md#crop-fidelity-and-export-flow-clarification (operator, 16 October: make the crop flow very similar to the
old hosted UI) assigns this inventory to face controls before any crop-modal behaviour work. The cropper spike
(`ws:face.cropper`), the source step, the confirmation modal, the editor modal and the alignment-failure layout are
all judged against it.

## Scope
- Write `docs/design/legacy-encode-dialog-inventory.md`: one row per visual element, copy string, control,
  interaction (choose file, paste into "Or paste image here", drag stencil, resize from each of the eight handles,
  rotate 90°, fine-rotate with the slider, degree readout update, Cancel, OK/Use Crop, CROP from the failure state)
  and state (source empty, proposal, editor, failure), from the three crop PNGs and `EncodeImageDialog.fs`. Each row
  is marked **reproduce** or **deliberate difference** with the reason and the owning bead.
- The settled deliberate differences to record, each with its plan anchor:
  - Flow: proposal -> ADJUST CROP -> OK confirms **before** encoding; the old dialog encoded first.
  - On-device detection replaces server detection; the guidance copy stays.
  - Failure dialog title "Upload an image" becomes **"Encode an image"** and its red **CROP** button becomes
    **ADJUST CROP** (same red filled style and centred position), per PLAN.md#supplied-ui-references.
  - The guidance copy's typo "looking towards to camera" (decide: reproduce verbatim or correct to "towards the
    camera"; record the choice; the default is to correct the typo only).
  - Add the one short explanation that encoding recreates the face and may change details (confirmation modal).
  - Prepare encoder appears beside Choose image only when eligible required assets are missing (consent tie-break).
- Geometry table measured from the locked images: modal width and padding, title baseline, logo box, preview
  square size and offset, ADJUST CROP box, button boxes (CANCEL, OK, USE CROP, CROP), handle size, stencil
  outline width, oval guide box relative to the stencil, eye-marker diameter and spacing, rotation icon and readout
  boxes, slider track and thumb, copy block. Store as `docs/design/legacy-encode-dialog-geometry.json` (boxes as
  fractions of modal width so they can be compared at 390 px and 1,280 px) plus the measuring script.
- Colour table sampled from the PNGs (modal background, title text, CANCEL fill/text, OK/USE CROP fill, CROP fill,
  failure-line red, slider track/thumb, handle fill, oval fill opacity), recorded with contrast ratios; light-theme
  equivalents chosen so text stays at 4.5:1 or better.
- Record the open operator question (wheel/pinch zoom, crop square past the photo edge, pre-upload "look straight
  forward" tip): not included until the operator answers; default is candidate behaviour.

## Out of scope
Building any component; the cropper library choice (`ws:face.cropper`).

## Considerations
The faithful port needs only the control artifact pinned by candidate import (`ws:import`). Do not edit the locked
bundle or commit its personal-photo pixels (the plan keeps personal photos out of Git): commit measurements,
crops of non-face chrome only if needed, and the hashes.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** It writes an inventory document, a geometry JSON and a measuring script. If implementation finds it must edit one of them after all, it first runs `br dep add fm-iosz fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph), adds the file to the conflict list in fm-bhw and records the change in its receipt (the plan's rule: an edge is added when an edit is discovered).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/design/legacy-encode-dialog-inventory.md` committed: a row for every element listed in Background (three titles; logo; preview square; ADJUST CROP; CANCEL; OK; stencil; eight handles; oval guide; two eye markers; rotate icon; degree readout; slider; the two-part bold/plain guidance copy; USE CROP; full-image failure preview; red CROP button; red "Unable to auto align face." line; failure guidance copy; file chooser; "Or paste image here"; 90° rotate button) and every interaction in `EncodeImageDialog.fs`, each marked reproduce / deliberate difference with reason and owning bead.
- [ ] A scripted check fails if any of those element names is missing from the inventory (list-coverage test committed).
- [ ] `docs/design/legacy-encode-dialog-geometry.json` and the measuring script committed; re-running the script on the locked PNGs (verified against `SHA256SUMS` first) reproduces the JSON byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Colour table committed with sampled values and contrast ratios; every text pair in the light-theme equivalents is >= 4.5:1.
- [ ] Deliberate differences listed exactly as in Scope (flow order, on-device detection, failure title and ADJUST CROP rename, typo decision, recreation explanation, Prepare encoder condition), each with its plan anchor.
- [ ] Open cropper-extras question recorded with the candidate-behaviour default.
- [ ] No personal-photo pixels committed (scan of the commit for image files larger than chrome crops; hashes only).
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] The inventory's open cropper-extras question cites the Q4 `docs/decisions/` entry written by fm-orh by path, rather than restating a separate question.
notes:
Plan anchors: PLAN.md#crop-fidelity-and-export-flow-clarification, #locked-original-requirements-and-images, #supplied-ui-references.
Polish r1 (E): element-by-element description of the three locked crop PNGs (viewed 24 October), geometry/colour tables and coverage test added; failure-dialog rename recorded as a deliberate difference.
Polish r2 (E): design field states the shared-file order decision for this bead.

title: Controller port: photo and crop reducers; full controller golden replay
description:
## Goal
Complete the controller port: port the candidate's photo and crop reducers (photo picking, recovered stills, crop queue, crop editing, detected-face picker, multi-file drop) to pure TS on the effect runner from `migration.controller`, then replay every parity row's goldens at controller level and retire the last checks that read `Product.fs` or generated `.fs.js`. Photo flows carry the recovery-first dispatch and crop-geometry fixes that must survive exactly before confirmed-crop and face-controls changes land. Split from `migration.controller` (fm-v80g) in the 24 October final pass.

## Scope
- Source: classic `b2d945a8` or the frozen import revision (re-check lines with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`).
- Photo/crop (`reducers/photo.ts`, `crop.ts`): helpers `nextCrop` 378-381 (advances `CropQueue`, calls `focusCropArea`) and `dequeue` 383-387 (multi-photo queue -> `selectPhoto` one file at a time); `PickPhoto` 444-448; `Cropped` 449 (dropped when `revision<>photoRevision id`) and 450-464; `PhotoFailed` 465-467; `PhotoError` 468-472; `Photo` variants 473-493 (project file -> Import; recovered still; crop offer -> `Crop`/`CropQueue`) and 537-547 (null file clears PreparingFaces via `schedule`; plain file -> encode); `RequestCrop` 494-498; `CropViewport` 499, `CropPan` 503, `CropZoom` 507, `CropRotate` 511, `CropCancel` 515-521, `CropAccept` 522-536 (`cropPhotoReported`); `Photos` 548-572 (N files: first empty face or append, one face per file in drop order, uncapped: defect 18); `DismissDetected` 652-656, `ChooseDetected` 657-665 (`chooseDetectedFace`); `Failed` with `multipleFacesMessage` 679-682 (re-offers the picker). View drop handler 1196-1199 dispatches `Photos(None, photoFiles e)`. Queued crops no longer revoke each other. Crop math stays in `photo/crop-view.mjs` (`createCrop`, `pan`, `zoomTo`, `rotate`, `rect`, `frame`, `resizeViewport`) called as pure functions.
- Retained JS: bridge `selectPhotoReported`, `previewPhotoReported`, `cropPhotoReported`, `photoRevision`, `chooseDetectedFace`, `cancelPhotoRun`, `warmPhotoTools`, `rememberSourcePhoto`, `sourcePhotoUrl`; `photo-selection.mjs` (`photoFiles`, `openPhotoPicker`, `dragPhoto`, `focusCropArea`); `photo/align-photo.mjs` `MULTIPLE_FACES_MESSAGE`; crop math in `photo/crop-view.mjs` called as pure functions.
- Effects: photo reducers return descriptions (`rememberSourcePhoto`, `invalidatePhotoSelections`, `focusCropArea`, preview/select/crop calls) executed by the runner from `migration.controller`; effect order as there.
- Golden replay: `apps/web/test/controller/replay.test.ts` iterates `goldens.json`, runs each parity step through composed reducers + runner with the control's recorded events fed to the pure reducers as input data (no service double), diffs next state and emitted effects; prints a per-row result (`passed`/`failed`/`owner-graded`/`untested`) in the CI log. Replays run `scripts/fetch-control.mjs` first and refuse on digest mismatch with `control-artifact.json`. Parity rows exact; repair/declared rows owner-graded, never asserted; no test encodes a candidate defect; unexercisable rows `untested`. Failures are fixed, not skipped; no blanket disabled suite.
- Rows replayed: Replace a face with a photo / cancel picker or crop, drop on tile or background (paste is absent in the control), Drop several files, Confirm one detected crop, Adjust/rotate crop and cancel/accept, No detected face, Select several detected faces (candidate single-choice picker), Reopen recovery-bearing still. Declared changes (confirmed-crop policy, batch proposal, paste, crop editor) and repair row 18 are owner-graded.
- Full controller-level replay: after this row's reducers land, run the replay over every row in `goldens.json` (rows from `migration.ctl-model`, `migration.controller` and this row).
- Retire source-reading checks, each replaced by a named TS test: `src/Next/crop-queue.test.mjs` (three tests: a crop for another face queues; every crop exit advances the queue; the queue is declared and starts empty) -> `crop.test.ts`; `photo-selection.test.mjs` "the multiple-faces sentence is shared, not duplicated" -> `photo.test.ts` import check. Then scan every active check and workflow for `Product.fs`, `.fs.js` or `verify-fable` references (historical notes allowlisted).

## Out of scope
- Confirmed-crop repair (crop); batch proposal and crop modal redesign, paste entry (face controls); React components and rendering-level checks; scheduler/intent implementations (operation controller).

## Notes
- Pure typed reducers (no I/O); scheduling/cancellation only through `opctl.interface`.
- Crop math stays in `photo/crop-view.mjs`; never reimplemented in TS.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-migration (Controller port versus the operation layer; split at the controller/rendering seam); #confirmed-crop-and-ordered-multi-selection-flow (candidate behaviour carried for parity).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `photo.test.ts` / `crop.test.ts` replay goldens and named cases: `Cropped` with a stale revision is ignored; two queued crops for different faces both survive in queue order; every crop exit (Cancel, Accept, failure) calls `nextCrop`; a three-file drop onto a two-face project fills empties then appends in drop order; `multipleFacesMessage` failure reopens the picker (constant imported, never a literal); a recovered still restores without an encode effect; crop geometry asserted by calling `crop-view.mjs` with golden inputs.
- [x] Import-boundary test covers `reducers/photo.ts` and `reducers/crop.ts` (only `controller/**` and `operations/service.ts` types).
- [x] Full golden replay: every parity row passes, zero parity rows skipped; repair/declared rows reported owner-graded with owner; untested rows with reason; scan confirms no `repair`/`defect` step is asserted.
- [x] Retired checks listed in `tests/retired.txt` with their replacement tests; scan finds no `Product.fs`, `.fs.js` or `verify-fable` reference in any active check or workflow (historical notes allowlisted).
- [x] `photo-selection.test.mjs` other cases pass unchanged; unit tests listed in test discovery and pass locally with the CI command; CI verifies after push.
- [x] Classic's Product.fs source assertions re-pointed at the ported TS reducer: crop-queue.test.mjs (crop offers queue; same-face offer replaces; no revoke of the previous crop) and photo-selection.test.mjs 'the multiple-faces sentence is shared, not duplicated' (the reducer compares against MULTIPLE_FACES_MESSAGE, not a literal); both restored to next-site.yml's 'Shipping runtime...' run and its two not-applicable summary lines removed (with fm-aa8)
- [x] Photo effects map real promise rejection to PhotoFailed(id, message); pure rejection-contract tests and the real-bridge photo controller harness verify the mapping (transferred from fm-v80g effect-runner item).
close_reason: Complete typed photo/crop controller, real photo/rejection/Save-reopen checks, all available recorded controller parity rows passing, retained source-reading checks replaced and restored in CI.

description:
## Background

The plan requires a small reviewable screen/state walkthrough before migration translation or face
controls behaviour work: main page, cold download modal, single/multi-face crop, queued/cancelled/
failed tiles, names picker and completed-result Share/Save. Face controls and modals implements it;
integrated verification checks the real result. References: the locked bundle
`../reference-locks/2026-10-11-original-plan-and-images/` (archive SHA-256 `f38de24a…921740a`):
`crop image.png` (dark **Encode an image** confirmation: logo top right, crop preview, **Adjust Crop**
below, Cancel bottom left, OK bottom right), `crop 2.png` (dark **Crop your image** editor: square
bounds with corner/edge handles, eye/face guides, rotation control and angle, instructions, Cancel and
**Use Crop**), `failed to align.png` (old **Upload an image** modal with "Unable to auto align face."
guidance; label becomes Encode an image, control Adjust Crop), `recovered image.png` (historical two-face
page showing duplicate filename, post-result Crop and Hold to compare, which are removed). Legacy
production and names references and the candidate's retained controls cover the rest. The archive has
no multi-face grid or names-picker screenshot; those come from written requirements and are labelled as
new designs, never as supplied mocks. Personal-photo pixels stay out of Git.

## Why

It checks the locked design while changes are cheap, fills only unspecified states, and gives face
controls, the controller port, names picker and integrated verification one state model to cite.

## Deliverables (typed, citable)

1. `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/ui-walkthrough.md`, one section per surface below,
   each with: the borrowed reference (locked filename or legacy surface, or "new design from written
   requirement <anchor>"); a state list; a transition table (event → next state → contract type that
   carries it → visible copy); low-fidelity wireframes at phone width (390 px) and desktop width
   (1280 px) for every state (SVG or PNG committed beside the doc, no personal photos); focus, Escape/
   Back and history behaviour.
2. `apps/web/src/contracts/ui-states.ts`: one exported discriminated union per surface, named exactly:
   `MainPageState`, `ColdDownloadModalState`, `CropConfirmState`, `CropEditorState`,
   `MultiFaceSelectionState`, `TileVisualState`, `NamesPickerState`, `ResultActionsState`,
   `MorphResultState`, plus `ModalStackRule`. Each variant references the m2 contract types it renders
   (`TileActionState`, `WholeActionProgress`, `AppGrantState`, `ConsentCostRow`, `RouteSnapshot`,
   `ExportIdentity`). Type tests live with `contracts.m2-type-tests`.
3. Current-state screenshots of the existing candidate surfaces, captured by operating the pinned
   control artifact (real pointer input, phone and desktop width) with the shared event-log emitter, so
   retained behaviour is documented from the running app, not from source reading. Known candidate
   defects (18 October operated check) are marked as defects, not frozen as behaviour.

## Surfaces and the states each must cover

- **Main page**: empty (one empty tile), one face, two or more faces, many faces up to the cap, CPU/WebGPU
  compact selector above the first + (route snapshot taken at Start or Download and continue; later
  changes affect new jobs only), generating, completed, one failed among completed.
- **Cold download modal**: bytes known from the actual manifest after cache validation, purpose
  (Generate / Generate and encode / Prepare encoder), pre-download estimate rows or "no reliable
  estimate", Continue/Cancel, revised-scope prompt for additional assets, download in progress, cancelled
  (verified chunks kept; pending action never launches later), error with Retry.
- **Single-face crop**: confirmation (`crop image.png` layout) → Adjust Crop → editor (`crop 2.png`) →
  Use Crop returns to confirmation with the new proposal; editor Cancel returns to the previous proposal;
  confirmation Cancel abandons; detector failure/refusal shows the "Unable to auto align face." guidance
  and still allows manual crop; OK commits once and replaces (not stacks) the dialog with tile progress.
- **Multi-face selection**: n detected faces, visible global click order (deselect removes, reselect
  appends), across files, 0/1/2/3/many/cap selections, over-ceiling message (reduce selection / remove
  retry input), atomic ordered insertion on commit.
- **Tiles**: queued, active with whole-action progress, Cancelling (disabled), cancelled with Retry,
  failed with Retry (new attempt ID), lost retry pixels → Encode image entry, pixels ready / Preparing
  file… / file-preparation Retry, static name selection pending → loading/Retry.
- **Names picker**: opened from a face's burger menu bound to that face's stable ID, cold/loading, error,
  empty search, very long and pasted query, pick returns to that tile, dismiss leaves it intact, target
  removed/revised while open invalidates the pending pick, touch Back exits.
- **Completed result Share/Save**: "Preparing file…" then Share/Save enabled for the selected format and
  revision; format change prepares only that format; PNG fallback updates name and MIME; system-share
  cancel is not an error and triggers no download; Share unavailable → Save only.
- **Morph result**: exactly one current result; ordered-face or setting change invalidates it and its
  Share/Save readiness; Cancel never exports a partial animation; play/scrub.
- **Modal rules**: topmost modal owns Escape/Back/focus; editor Back = editor Cancel; confirmation
  Back = confirmation Cancel; acquisition Back = its Cancel; focus returns to the invoking control.
- **File-open dispatch**: valid recovery metadata reopens the still; missing vs damaged vs incompatible
  metadata are distinct states; metadata-free image can explicitly enter photo encoding; external MP4
  reports unsupported without replacing current work.

## Out of scope

Implementation (face controls). Visual redesign beyond filling unspecified states. Proving inference.

## Considerations

Do not replace the supplied crop layouts. A walkthrough does not establish working inference. Plain
copy; no marketing tone. Many-face layouts and multi-selection are reviewed again as built by
`face.design-review`.

title: Morph controls, whole-action progress, complete output layout
description:
## Goal
Present Morph honestly: a Create Morph button that is visibly disabled from the accepted intent onward, one whole-action monotonic progress bar with Cancel at its right, refusals before frame inference, and complete face and morph outputs that are never clipped. The morph pipeline owns production, the frame-budget check, the MP4-availability probe and the identical-neighbours rule; the operation controller owns Morph as a parent intent; face controls owns button, progress and Cancel presentation and the complete-output display (tie-break table). Fixes defect 6 presentation (identical neighbours show "This project is invalid or uses an unsupported format.") and defect 20 (disabled Create morph looks enabled).

## Scope
- `.next-morph-slot`/`.next-status` beside Create Morph: disabled from accepted intent onward (visibly distinct, readable reason); one whole-action monotonic bar, Cancel at its right, frame count secondary; useful recovery named here (Retry, or reduce length in existing More options); morph refusals (identical neighbours, invalid/unconfirmed inputs, known-unavailable MP4 preparation) shown before frame inference with the pipeline's plain message.
- Morph on unfinished valid text/seed inputs: one accepted intent generates the faces then frames, at most one consent decision when assets are missing, no separate Generate press.
- Retry after Cancel or failure restarts the morph reusing completed faces. Completed faces survive Morph failure/cancellation; cancellation never labels a partial animation complete.
- Complete face output in `.next-face-image`: whole model frame at its aspect ratio, no ancestor clipping or overlay.
- Complete morph output in `.next-video-slot`: one current full-frame result; playable video when scrub frames are absent (fall back from slider mode without regeneration); actual resolution and a disclosed qualified 512 px fallback without cropping/shortening, disclosed beside the result actions and before Morph when known; settings disabled during an active morph.
- Short/narrow screens keep aspect ratio and reachable actions with normal scrolling. Intrinsic canvas size and `object-fit: contain` are not evidence; check rendered content bounds.
- Update `scripts/check-progress-copy.mjs` expectations to the new copy (one monotonic whole-action bar, secondary frame counter, no per-stage reset copy); the old frame-only/per-stage-reset expectation is listed in `tests/retired.txt`.
- **Open operator questions** (autoplay; a plain 50/50 blend): keep candidate behaviour until answered: the result waits for a click and is not autoplayed; no plain-blend shortcut beyond the existing shapes; `Classic linear` stays selectable in More options.
- No raw runtime exception text as visitor copy; one message owner per failed action.

## Out of scope
Morph production and probes (morph pipeline); progress computation (operation controller).

## Notes
- Renders operation-controller progress and morph refusals in the ported UI; edits no shared bridge/runtime/worker file, but consumes morph pipeline output (direct edge).
- Anchors: PLAN.md#clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation, #gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design (whole-action progress), #end-to-end-experience-and-design-fidelity-check. Audit rows 6 (presentation) and 20 (disabled look).
acceptance_criteria:
Operated rule: real pointer/touch at the visible position with `elementFromPoint`; by-name only for setup; 390 px and 1,280 px, screenshot per case.
- [x] Operated Create Morph; repeated clicks after acceptance queue no duplicate intent; Cancel at the bar's right stops the morph and completed faces remain.
- [x] Create Morph at 1 face (disabled, reason says a second face is needed), 2, 3 and 8 faces.
- [ ] Progress values sampled from the DOM are monotonic per attempt and never reset between stages; `check-progress-copy.mjs` passes in CI against the built app in the same revision.
- [x] Disabled Create Morph visibly distinct (contrast/opacity measured) with its reason announced.
- [x] Two typed faces with no result: operated Create Morph generates both then frames, at most one consent decision, no Generate press.
- [x] Operated Retry in `.next-status` after Cancel and after failure reuses completed faces (zero face inference for them).
- [x] Rendered content bounds: four corners of face and video frames visible at 320, 390, 1,024, 1,920 px and a 568 px-high viewport.
- [x] Scrub frames absent: player usable, slider falls back, zero inference requests.
- [x] Real codec probe in a browser without the codec (open-source Chromium): 512 px fallback disclosed beside the actions and before Morph.
- [x] Identical neighbours (hello, hello) refused before work with the pipeline's plain message in the Morph status.
- [x] Autoplay and plain-blend: result not autoplayed; `Classic linear` selectable; no extra blend shortcut (until the operator answers).
- [x] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test`) and pass.
- [x] device-lab failure fixed and a later lab run passed (ticked by lab.py on that pass)
notes: Local operated, codec, phone and affected unit/type checks complete; acceptance items 3 and 12 remain unchecked only for actual new-revision CI progress-copy/built-app and npm-test passes. No CI execution or deployment claimed from local evidence.

title: Add the recurring clean-clone rot check
description:
## Background
Run on every change to the distribution and monthly. A failure opens an issue owned by the classic distribution workstream and updates the README's validated date. GitHub-hosted runners cover build and CPU path; the GPU lane uses a self-hosted worker under the lease.

## Why
Rot, including a dead weight link, must show up as a failed run.

## Scope
- Workflow on the distribution branch: `push` path filter, monthly `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch`.
- GPU job on the self-hosted worker (lease), CPU/build job on hosted runners.
- On failure: open an issue; on success: update the validated date/matrix row via a commit or a recorded artifact.

## Out of scope
Bumping dependencies on failure (frozen; fixes are explicit operator decisions).

## Considerations
Scheduled workflows run only from the default branch; verify after the switch.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] One dispatched run passes both jobs; a forced failure (bad hash) opens an issue; both jobs write the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, commit and image digests, host OS/Docker/Compose/driver/GPU, provider cuda|cpu, network requests by host class and bytes for weight downloads, container exit codes, outcome per assertion), retained as a CI artifact or committed evidence file, with every network/download claim asserted from the log.
- [ ] Receipt `docs/receipts/classic-rot-check.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime/model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] The run uses the harness's vendored `event_log.py` (see `classic.readme-harness`, fm-ujd) and its log passes `node scripts/check-event-log.ts <log>` (polish r2).
notes: Plan anchors (PLAN.md): #classic-distribution, #frozen-classic-distribution, #classic-distribution-acceptance; receipts rule: #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance.

New named workstream (no old record). Candidate `route-priors.mjs` and `estimate.mjs` hold historical single-device

desktop CPU 1.28 s; iOS reports a 1,000 MB quota with zero use in all 143 checks.

title: Inventory required statuses and bind equivalent checks in this repository
description:
## Background

Required statuses and branch-protection bindings are inventoried, not inferred from a workflow filename.

## Why

Required-check roles must carry over, or a lane can silently stop gating.

## Scope

- Read classic's branch protection/rulesets and required status names (read-only).
- Map each to destination job names; configure equivalent required checks on this repository's
  default branch (a change to this repository's settings only).
- Record mapping in the check-migration map.

## Lanes and statuses to account for

- Classic workflows at the import revision and their disposition (every one appears in the map):
  `next-site.yml` (artifact → `build.ci-site-lane` fm-aa8; qualify caller → `build.ci-e2e-cpu-lane` fm-fy8; compiled-ui → `build.ci-site-compiled-ui` fm-ekk4; deploy → `deploy.ci-workflow`),
  `next-e2e.yml` (real-ui-cpu → this repo), `next-matrix.yml` (engines, summary; manual, never required),
  `mobile-browser.yml` (android → fm-xi3; ios → fm-hlv; ios-product-artifact and ios-product-simulator → `build.ci-ios-product-lane` fm-34iy),
  `next-gpu-lane.yml` (webgpu-benchmark; self-hosted, deliberately not required),
  `research-built-ui-media-v1.yml` and `research-rgba-screen-v1.yml` (→ `research.workflows-path-filters`,
  experimental, never required), `name-catalogue.yml` (→ static names publication, `names.publish-pipeline`),
  `self-host-build.yml` (stays in classic as the distribution's rot check), `deploy.yml` (legacy .NET/Vercel
  CI; historical, not carried), `desktop-product.yml`, `desktop-native-inference.yml`,
  `desktop-candidates.yml` (native packaging, retired with `provider.native-retirement`; any shared
  browser/artifact/media check they supplied is re-homed, never substituted for a browser check).
- Required statuses are read from classic's branch protection/rulesets (`gh api` read-only), not inferred
  from this list; the expected mapping keeps status names `<workflow name> / <job id>` identical where the
  job IDs are kept.
- Non-required by design: the manual matrix, the GPU lane, research workflows and the bleeding-edge lane.

## Out of scope

Changing classic's settings (classic wind-down).

## Considerations

- Shared-file serialisation: `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and
  `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited only in the mandated order (provider simplification, typed facade,
  compute extraction, confirmed-crop fix, morph pipeline, names picker/diagnostics); build items change
  tooling and CI, and add any shared file they touch to the check-migration map's conflict list.
- No worktrees, resets or cleans; preserve other sessions' uncommitted work.
- Hosted-minute economy: use capable workers where practical, but never weaken a required check or
  substitute Linux WebKit for Safari/iOS; never cancel a live publication halfway.

A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Write the integrated verification join report
description:
## Background
Integrated verification is four sub-results and a join: `ws:verify.flows` (app flows), `ws:verify.platform`
(platform and resource), `ws:verify.packages` (packages and non-face) and `ws:verify.artifact` (release artifact and
evidence). Each sub-result ends in a receipt. The join is what candidate-source handover, production promotion from
this repository and package publication rely on, and the evidence the operator reads for `gate:cutover`.

## Why
Release-qualification claims for the new monorepo must rest on one consistent, complete set of evidence for one
artifact. A claim about a different build, an untested cell or an unset threshold is not evidence.

## Scope
Write `scripts/verify-join.ts` (strict TypeScript, run with Node type stripping like the `scripts/evidence/` modules) and run it to produce the join report (`docs/receipts/verify-join-<digest>.md` plus
JSON). The script applies this rule exactly:
1. **Inputs present and complete.** The four sub-result receipts exist and pass `scripts/check-receipts.ts`; so do
   the leaf receipts each one links.
2. **One commit, one digest.** The source commit and the artifact digest are byte-identical across the four
   sub-result receipts and equal the release identity record written by `verify.artifact-identity`. Any mismatch
   fails the join; the stale sub-result is rerun on the named artifact. A leaf receipt or event log with another
   digest makes that leaf's cells `untested` (it never borrows a pass from another build).
3. **Closed outcome set.** Every cell is one of `passed`, `failed`, `untested`, `unsupported`, `inconclusive`,
   `deferred`, `not-applicable-by-decision`, `measured, no threshold`. Only `passed` cells are claimed. A
   `measured, no threshold` cell is listed in its own section with the milestone that will set its threshold and is
   never counted or worded as passed.
4. **Full row coverage.** The graded flow matrix from `verify.flows-matrix` grades all rows R01-R49 and candidate
   defects 1-23; a missing row or defect fails the join.
5. **Untested cells listed.** Every non-`passed` cell is listed with capability, platform/browser, provider, the
   reason, and the receipt that recorded it. Physical iPhone appears as an evidence gap.
6. **Blocking failures.** A `failed` cell in correctness, privacy, cancellation or resource behaviour blocks closure:
   it is fixed in the owning workstream, a new artifact is built, and every sub-result reruns on that digest.
   Other failures (for example a retained GPU lane rejecting its adapter) are listed as limitations and limit claims.
7. **Baseline accounting.** Every intentional difference from the candidate baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`,
   reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`) cites the drift ledger or behaviour-authority table;
   unlisted Next features remain usable; preservation of warm reuse, bounded pipelines, session/video/scrub recovery
   and export reuse is stated with its evidence.
8. **Unsupported and unclaimed capabilities listed**, including non-face support if its joint proof was blocked and
   verified-cache warming if it did not ship.

## Out of scope
Deciding cutover (operator gate). Publishing packages (delivery).

## Considerations
- The report states its own outcome as `complete` (rules 1-8 hold) or `incomplete` with the failing rule; it never says "release passed".
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests for `scripts/verify-join.ts` with fixture receipts: a commit mismatch fails; a digest mismatch fails; a digest that differs from the identity record fails; a receipt missing a schema field fails; a leaf with another digest turns its cells `untested`; a `measured, no threshold` cell is never counted as passed; an outcome outside the closed set fails; a missing flow-matrix row or defect fails; an open blocking-category failure fails.
- [ ] Join report committed in `docs/receipts/` (Markdown plus JSON) linking the four sub-result receipts and the identity record, outcome `complete`.
- [ ] Sections present: claimed (passed) cells; untested/unsupported/inconclusive/deferred cells with reasons; `measured, no threshold` cells with their threshold milestone; unsupported or unclaimed capabilities; baseline differences with their plan citations.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes: Anchor: #integrated-verification (structure for decomposition and pass criteria).

title: Journey registry and budgets: fixed high-value e2e set, per-cell wall-clock budgets, CI guard against sprawl
description:
## Goal

Keep the end-to-end suite fast and high-value forever: one fixed registry of named journeys, each protecting a named plan flow, each with a wall-clock budget per cell, enforced mechanically. This is the guard against the suite-sprawl failure mode: CI wall-clock is the swarm's iteration latency (merge queue runs one at a time), and every journey added without a budget makes every future push slower.

## Why

Operator direction, 25 October 2026 (AGENTS.md "Journey suite"): agents iterate locally on the one journey their bead touches; CI runs the whole registry every push; the phone is verified locally. That only works if the registry stays small and budgeted.

## Scope

- A committed registry (JSON next to browser-matrix.json, or the journey table in tools/device-lab/lab.py) listing every journey: name, the plan flow it protects, per-cell budget in seconds. Seed set: cold-face, warm-face, morph. Named additions as their product beads land: photo-face (upload, crop, e4e, add face; fm-ejwq), export assertions (images + MP4; fm-y2jb, fm-qh1s), blend/advanced multi-face journey (fm-ve73).
- lab.py summary (and the hosted-lanes summary) fails when a journey exceeds its budget or a run names a journey outside the registry.
- Budgets are measured once (lab.py run --repeat 3 on eris-webgpu, eris-cpu, phone-webgpu, phone-cpu), then frozen; changing a budget or adding a journey is a reviewed diff to the registry file and needs a bead naming the flow.
- main.yml e2e/device-lab summaries print per-journey duration vs budget.

## Out of scope

Writing the photo-face and blend journeys themselves (owned by fm-ejwq/fm-ve73 as their flows land); performance qualification (strictly-not-worse, fm-mc27) which pairs runs rather than asserting budgets.

## Acceptance

title: Real-visitor before/after check per platform class after the handover
description:
## Goal
After real visitors start getting the monorepo build, compare their timings and failure rates with the candidate's last weeks, per platform class (iPhone, Android, desktop) and route, from the changeover statistics, and treat a regression like a failed gate: investigate, fix, and keep rollback to the control artifact available until the comparison is clean (PLAN.md "Strictly not worse than the candidate", "After release, from real visitors"). This is the field half of the gate whose lab half is `verify.not-worse` (fm-mc27).

## Scope
- **Windows.** Before: the candidate's last 28 days (`build="candidate"`). After: the monorepo build's first 14 and 28 days (`build="monorepo"`) from the next.facemorph.me handover (`delivery.handover`, fm-s3o), which serves the same audience the candidate did. Once facemorph.me is promoted, its traffic (`host="production"`) is a row of its own: a different audience, so it informs but does not replace the next.facemorph.me comparison. The `build` and `host` labels come from `diag.usage-stats` (fm-5yqq). Each cutover step is a Grafana annotation tagged `changeover`.
- **Measures per platform class and route:** median and 90th-percentile job duration per action (face, photo, morph, blend) from the `fm_web_job_duration_seconds` buckets; time to first result, cold and warm (`fm_web_time_to_first_result_seconds`); failure and cancel share from `fm_web_jobs_total` by outcome; first-visit model megabytes per first visit.
- **Noise and verdict.** The margin per class and measure is the largest week-over-week change of that measure across the before window's four weeks; a quantile that moves within one histogram bucket reads as unchanged. A regression is flagged when the after value is worse than the before value by more than the margin. A class, route or action with too few completed jobs to estimate that week-to-week noise is `untested`, never `passed`; the script prints the minimum it used and why.
- **Check script** `ops/stats/field-not-worse.ts` queries the triton Prometheus HTTP API with a read-only credential from a CI secret, prints one table (class x route x measure: before, after, margin, verdict) and exits non-zero on a regression.
- **Scheduled workflow** `field-not-worse.yml` runs it weekly on a development worker from the handover until 28 days after the later of the handover and the facemorph.me promotion, and on a flag opens or updates one GitHub issue naming the class, route and measure. Rollback to the candidate artifact through delivery's promote path stays available until a run is clean.
- **Dashboard.** A "Real-visitor not-worse" row in "FaceMorph before and after": both builds by class and route with the changeover annotations, provisioned from `ops/grafana/` like the rest.

## Out of scope
Lab measurements (`verify.not-worse`); the blog post; old-API counter panels (already in the dashboard).

## Notes
- Approximate by design: beacons are batched, opt-outs remove some visitors and automation is filtered. A flag is a reason to reproduce the regression with the lab gate's paired runs on the affected class, then fix it in the owning bead.
- The candidate has sent statistics since candidate commit `551b607` (24 October), so the before window fills before the handover; candidate beacons carry no build field and count as `build="candidate"`.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#strictly-not-worse-than-the-candidate-operator-24-october-2026, #changeover-statistics-in-grafana.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Check-script tests against a real Prometheus (pinned container) loaded with generated series (`promtool tsdb create-blocks-from openmetrics`): clean; regressed on one platform class only (the flag names that class, route and measure); a change inside the before window's week-to-week margin passes; a change within one histogram bucket reads unchanged; too few jobs gives `untested`; a higher failure share flags even when timings improve.
- [ ] Run against the live Prometheus after the handover prints the table with both builds' series present.
- [ ] Dashboard row provisioned from `ops/grafana/` shows both builds per class and route with the changeover annotations.
- [ ] The scheduled workflow ran the 14-day and 28-day checks after the handover; a dry run on that real Prometheus with a planted regression opens the issue.
- [ ] Any flagged regression has a linked fix and the rollback path is confirmed available until a later run is clean.
- [ ] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test`) and pass.

title: Stage-2 acceptance: leased runs of re-homed drivers against the pinned control
description:
## Background

Stage-2 completion check before the evaluator and ORT evaluation build on it.

## Why

Proves drivers, recipes and workflows work together from this repository.

## Scope

- A bounded leased run of each maintained driver on its worker against the control artifact, journaled; recorded as a dated `log.md` entry and journal events, never as a `results.tsv` row (smoke runs are not evaluated outcomes; the ledger appends evaluated outcomes only).

## Out of scope

Performance claims.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Journal entries and outputs recorded with artifact digests.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script involved emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform and provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, retains the log as a CI artifact, and any network claim is asserted from that log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Outputs and event logs are copied to the durable output location named in the launch recipe (outside transient CI artifacts) and the round record cites that path; private or local-only raw files are labelled as such; a CI artifact is only a convenience copy.

title: Cut main CI to ~5 min per run: correctness-only main, heavy lanes in the pre-deploy gate
description:
## Goal
Cut main CI wall time from ~50–70 min to ~15 min without dropping checks, so beads close on CI within minutes of a push. Operator request, 26 Oct 2026.

## Measured (runs 40300178097, 40295992353, 40290030872)
- `contracts-m1 / browsers` (runs-on: ubuntu-24.04): **3151 s in `setup-playwright`** (hosted cache miss → `playwright install --with-deps chromium firefox webkit`) for **19 s of tests**. It alone sets the 69-min wall time.
- `web-shell / e2e`: 1771 s in a single serial `npm run test:e2e`.
- `web-shell / facade`: 1088 s in one step ("Typed facade through the real CPU bridge").
- `web-shell / runtime-e2e`: 486 s. Next tier: model-conv acceptance 8 min, scaffold gates 8 min.
- 49 jobs, ~142 runner-minutes per run; 14 self-hosted runners. Runner count isn't the limit: the longest jobs are.

## Scope
1. Move `contracts-m1 / browsers` to `[self-hosted, linux-x64]`, where browsers are cached, or fix its hosted cache. Confirm WebKit runs on every linux-x64 runner (eris, triton, tempcpu); if not, pin it to the runners that can.
2. Shard `web-shell / e2e` and `facade` across runners (matrix shards or the test runner's own sharding), and/or raise in-job test concurrency on the big runners. Target ≤ 8 min each. Keep every test; no skips.
3. Look for repeated work across jobs: the same package builds, `npm ci` and runtime acquisition in many jobs. Build once in one job and pass the output as an artifact, or share it through the runner's cache.
4. Report before/after wall time and runner-minutes from real main runs.

## Constraints
Keep one main pipeline at a time, newest-only, never cancelled mid-run (merge-queue rule). Prefer bigger runners and in-job parallelism over more runners. No weakened assertions or skipped tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] contracts-m1/browsers no longer spends minutes installing browsers; its wall time is under 3 min on main.
- [ ] web-shell e2e and facade each finish in ≤ 8 min on main with every test still running.
- [x] Before/after table (wall time, runner-minutes, slowest 5 jobs) from real main runs is in the close reason.
notes:
2026-10-26 orchestrator: eris hit load average 30-40 on 12 cores during main runs (bursty; 85% idle between runs), and CI timeouts (firefox manager-cache, web-shell e2e/facade) correlate. Five temporary runners (tempcpu-1..5, linux-x64, 26 cores) sit idle because most jobs pin [self-hosted, eris]. As part of this bead, move every job that doesn't need eris hardware (GPU, device lab, phone) from 'eris' to 'linux-x64' so it can land on tempcpu or triton, and cap eris to what only eris can do.
27 Oct operator target: about 5 minutes per main run, replacing the 15-minute target. Plan (from run 40410247006 timings): (1) main runs correctness only; crop-acceptance (42 min), runtime-e2e (14 min), real-ui-cpu, mobile/iOS, full e2e and the GPU benchmark move to the on-demand pre-deploy all-lanes gate (fm-fy2.11); (2) build packages and app once, upload them, and have downstream jobs download instead of running npm ci and rebuilding; (3) split scaffold/gates (11.5 min serial) into parallel format, lint, typecheck and sharded npm test jobs across the 14 runners; (4) pass the changes job's output into test shards so bead/docs-only pushes take about 1 min; (5) put Playwright browsers, model weights and the npm cache on the self-hosted runners; (6) main must be green: fix the failing import-checks, package-gates, facade(4) and e2e jobs once, and move anything still flaky out of main. Keep fm-98po queueing unchanged.

title: Frontend staging, runtime restage/mirror and entry Worker from a clean clone
description:
## Background
Classic restaging can depend on ignored `experiment/`, installed ORT/FFmpeg packages and external `review-artifacts` absent from a fresh clone. The entry Worker and analytics live in `hosting/next-static/`.

## Why
Staging must be reproducible from a clean clone against the `deploy-next/` contract.

## Scope
Staging of `deploy-next/` (control-labelled first, Vite build later) with runtime overlay/mirror reuse via explicit digest-checked acquisition commands; entry Worker and analytics staging; receipt fields equal to classic's. (Deploying and warming the `models.facemorph.me` second origin is `deploy.ci-workflow`'s step through the model-host package; this leaf only rebuilds the local runtime set.)

## Out of scope
Publishing.

## Considerations
Do not copy a prepared private lab; explicit model-term/download authorization for clean destinations.

## Classic commands to reproduce (candidate `6107f80` `next-site.yml` deploy job)
1. Verify the downloaded artifact: `cd web && sha256sum --quiet -c next-site-SHA256SUMS`.
2. Rebuild the runtime from the pinned manifest: `python3 hosting/next-static/mirror-runtime.py --output .runtime-public` (CI caches it keyed on `runtime-overlay/manifest.json` + `mirror-runtime.py`).
3. Stage: `python3 hosting/next-static/stage.py --runtime .runtime-public --frontend web/deploy-next --catalogue hosting/next-static/catalogue.json --output public` (the names index must be the one built into the qualified artifact, `promote.py`'s rule).
The clean-clone run executes the re-homed equivalents with explicit, digest-checked acquisition (no ignored `experiment/`, no preinstalled ORT/FFmpeg, no `review-artifacts`), and diffs the staged file list and digests against a classic run on the same artifact.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clean-clone staging run reproduces classic receipt fields for the same artifact.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, and the log is retained as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics). Network claims are asserted from the log, never from screenshots.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/deploy/staging.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Clean-clone staging script logs each step (step ID, timestamp, input/output digests, bytes fetched by host class) and fails if any input is read from outside the clone or the declared acquisition cache.
notes: Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-deploy-and-collector-re-homing; #candidate-source-import-and-bootstrap.
