title: Sub-result 4 (release artifact and evidence): identity, retained lanes, invariants, register hand-off
description:
## Goal
Sub-result 4 of integrated verification: release artifact and evidence. Every other result must point at one artifact;
claims about an unnamed build are not evidence. Native retirement does not retire desktop-browser, mobile or GPU
checks, and the plan requires keeping every integrated performance optimization through the refactor. This bead binds
the release artifact identity, runs the retained CI lanes against that digest, checks the source invariants behind
the preserved performance paths, hands the retained evidence register to the strictly-not-worse gate
(`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27), which owns the paired comparison against the pinned control, and emits the sub-result 4
output.

## Scope
- **Identity record:** source repository ID (`1413979666`), commit, artifact digest, runtime versions and digests,
  model manifest identities and catalogue identity in a machine-readable `release-identity.json` (with a JSON schema
  committed beside its generator), produced by the release-verification workflow and read by the harness artifact
  fixture and `scripts/verify-join.ts`. This digest is the one all four sub-results and the release summary must name.
  Workspace build's identity hashing covers app and packages; a package edit changes identity.
- Verify the artifact references only staged immutable assets; the no-third-party gate (`check-no-third-party.mjs`)
  passes; production headers present. Release-consistent set: an open tab during a new publication keeps its manifest
  identity or gets a clear reload action (from hosting/build CI results or run here).
- **Retained lanes** triggered on the release artifact digest (prefer canonical-artifact reuse; any unavoidable rebuild
  is a deviation), as carried over by workspace build:
  `next-site.yml` `artifact` and `compiled-ui` (`build.ci-site`, fm-aa8; ubuntu-24.04; gating);
  `next-site.yml` `qualify` calling `next-e2e.yml` `real-ui-cpu` (`build.ci-site`; ubuntu-24.04 Chrome,
  browser-harness 0.1.8; gating); `next-matrix.yml` `engines`, `summary`, five cells (`build.m1`, fm-7ge; Ubuntu
  Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, macOS WebKit/Firefox; gating); `mobile-browser.yml` `android`, eight component IDs
  (`build.ci-mobile`, fm-hlv; API 35 x86_64 pixel_6, SwiftShader; gating); `mobile-browser.yml` `ios`, eight component
  IDs, and `ios-product-artifact`, `ios-product-simulator` (`build.ci-mobile`; macOS 15, iPhone 16 Pro Simulator;
  gating); `next-gpu-lane.yml` `webgpu-benchmark` (`build.workers-lease`, fm-wzy; `[self-hosted, truenas, gpu-vulkan]`
  GTX 1050, Chrome for Testing 141.0.7390.54; non-gating). The `next-site.yml` `deploy` job deploys and is not run
  here. Cross-run artifact lookup and digest verification come from `build.ci-site`'s artifact lookup; check that every
  lane consumed the release artifact by digest.
- Confirm the repaired matrix uses an independent metadata-free photo with actual encoder events (history: manual
  desktop matrix run 37555426933 failed on 7 October; recent GPU evidence failed adapter admission;
  `scripts/next-matrix.mjs` targeted stale controls and uploaded a recovery-bearing file for `photoE4e`). Software
  adapters rejected; adapter failures named; unavailable H.264/project controls labelled incomplete/not shipped.
- `scripts/verify/collect-lane-results.ts` reads each run's jobs and artifacts (`gh run view --json jobs,headSha` plus
  uploaded test artifacts), checks the artifact digest in every retained run, and writes one JSON cell per lane x
  platform x provider with an outcome from the closed set, the run ID and the capture digest. The release summary's platform cells
  and the no-regression comparison read this JSON.
- **Register hand-off (no second comparison here):** the evidence register (12 rows) and the comparison protocol from
  `build.identity-map` (fm-pud) go to `verify.not-worse`, which compares against the pinned candidate artifact on every
  platform class with one pass rule. For each register row record what the gate needs to map it to a cell and measure:
  provider/model/runtime, resolution/FPS/frame count, cold/retained/resident/restored state, visible-tab state and
  finish boundary, and which of first/nth face, confirmed-photo work, complete video, first/repeated Save, restore,
  no lockups, acquired/output bytes, memory reservations or cancellation it protects.
  Retained achieved evidence (context, not limits): eris RTX 2080 SUPER WebGPU pipeline 129.8 -> 69.7 ms/frame and RGBA8 42.6
  -> 37.1; OPFS model load 1,430 -> 640 ms; Ubuntu Chrome CPU repeat Save 100.72 -> 66.49 ms; iPhone 16 Pro Simulator
  first face 25,287 ms. Source invariants each checked (code check plus a run showing it): canary-set keyed admission
  (one canary before the first cold face, rest deferred), `ort-worker.mjs` `warmMapping()` overlap, CPU 1-4 threads,
  single-threaded streamed e4e, cache-only worker and digest reuse, Firefox storage permission timing, pinned
  self-hosted runtimes, no-third-party gate.
- **Sub-result 4 output:** machine-readable result naming the same commit and digest, the lane cells, the register
  hand-off and the invariant checks.

## Out of scope
Deployment (delivery). Adding Windows qualification; making the GPU lane a promotion gate. New benchmark campaigns. The
paired performance and reliability comparison, control/control noise and physical-device runs (`verify.not-worse` and
`verify.not-worse-lanes`).

## Notes
- Correctness/resource failures in the lanes fail this sub-result. Latency, byte and memory verdicts come from
  `verify.not-worse`. A lane definition is not a passing result; never advertise all cells as passing.
- Use development workers and the device lease to save GitHub minutes.
- 24 October cut: the identity record moves from `docs/receipts/release-identity-<digest>.json` to a workflow-produced
  artifact; per-leaf receipts dropped. Platform cells are generated into the release summary by `verify.join`; there is no separate support table.
- Integrated verification checks the final integrated app (after the planned UI and package changes) against the Next baseline (`facemorph.me-classic` branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) plus the plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped. Not historic-API parity and not a shutdown-qualification campaign. Performance and reliability against the control, including control/control noise and the physical iPhone, are judged by the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27), not here. Correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found here are fixed in the owning bead and this bead re-runs. Wording says planned, experimental, implemented or deployed. No weights, secrets, photos or typed inputs in Git.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #workspace-build-and-artifact-identity, #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts,
  #platform-ci-retention-and-performance-preservation, #retained-performance-evidence-and-no-regression-checks,
  #development-workers-and-github-minute-use, #integrated-verification (structure item 4).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `release-identity.json` validates against its schema; unit tests show the digest recomputed from the artifact files equals the recorded digest, and a changed file, a missing runtime digest or a missing model/catalogue identity fails validation.
- [ ] No-third-party gate output attached; production headers present; open-tab check recorded (keeps manifest identity or shows the reload action).
- [ ] Per-lane run IDs and outcomes recorded against the artifact digest, one row per job in the lane list above; any rebuild listed as a deviation.
- [ ] Unit tests for `collect-lane-results.ts` with fixture run JSON: a skipped or cancelled job becomes `untested`; a run carrying another digest becomes `untested`; a software adapter on the GPU lane becomes `failed` with the adapter name; an invalid capture makes its cell `untested`; a missing lane is listed, never omitted.
- [ ] Each source invariant has a recorded check (code check plus a run showing it).
- [ ] The sub-result 4 output names the same commit and digest as the identity record; nothing is reported passed that did not run on that artifact/platform.

title: Acquisition consent, overlap and warming
description:
## Background
New named workstream (no old record). The candidate opens "Download the face model?" with bytes, Cancel and Download
and continue, alongside a proactive model-offer toast (live preview `001ba85`, 12 October). Its `DownloadConsent` is a
broad route/photo set and unknown inventory bypasses `gateScope`; the 32 MB video-fallback download is outside every
consent (defect 19); sizes disagree across toast, dialog and progress (defect 10: 149 MB, 1.1 GB, 1.2 GB vs 158 MB and
1,040 MB). The reusable model manager exposes capabilities only (verified-local-only handles, leases, typed
invalidation); policy lives here.

## Why
Explicit acquisition consent constrains when network work starts, but must not serialize authorized downloads with
photo selection (performance objective). Owns the consent modal, Prepare encoder, grant ownership, overlap and optional
warming (tie-break table).

## Scope
Children: bounded grant state machine; the Generate and encode / Generate consent modal; synthesis-first overlap
scheduling under aggregate buffers; Prepare encoder action and setup ownership; request-log verification; optional
milestone `ws:consent.warming` (targeted round, then implementation only if it shows a foreground-safe benefit).

## Out of scope
Manager primitives (`ws:manager`); device estimates (`ws:device`, soft: unknown estimates allowed); face-modal
rendering of the Prepare encoder entry (`face.prepare-encoder-entry`).

## Considerations
Consent and overlap do not wait on warming. Device check feeds consent copy softly (no Needs edge). Each new
diagnostics event is listed with allowlist and privacy entry before acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Children closed with receipts; warming milestone closed as shipped or dropped with its decision record.
- [ ] Grant state-machine unit tests; a request-log run asserts zero model-host requests before approval or after Cancel, synthesis-first order, and zero requests from warming unless it shipped (PLAN.md#acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance).
- [ ] Acquisition, cancellation and negative-path checks of PLAN.md#integrated-verification pass on the built app.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] When the reported storage quota cannot hold a selected package (the iPhone case: 1,000 MB quota, 1,040 MB CPU package), the consent modal says with the byte count that it is downloaded again on each visit (requirement from provider.phone-cpu-check).
notes:
Plan anchors: PLAN.md#acquisition-consent-overlap-and-warming, #consented-downloads-useful-overlap-and-cached-model-warming, #lightweight-device-check-and-pre-download-guidance (download modal), #gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design (operation/resource ownership, cold photo sequence).

title: Make the privacy text name every outside request and what a saved file contains
description:
## Background
Defect 11 (operated): the FAQ says nothing leaves the device, but preview requests go to a `workers.dev` host, a
Cloudflare analytics beacon loads on every visit, and the name list is fetched on the first keystroke; saved files carry
the exact latent and nothing says so. Static names fixes the requests; this leaf owns the text.

## Why
Privacy copy must be complete and true.

## Scope
- Name every outside request (host class, purpose, trigger) from the static names request inventory and the analytics
  configuration, and state that saved PNG/WebP/MP4 files embed the exact latent and model/provenance metadata (never
  photos, typed words or filenames).
- Keep the debug disclosure distinct from the analytics disclosure.

## Out of scope
Help page structure (`ws:provider`).

## Considerations
Re-check when any workstream adds an outside request.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** It is privacy copy in the ported Help/FAQ sources. If implementation finds it must edit one of them after all, it first runs `br dep add fm-kjjv fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph), adds the file to the conflict list in fm-bhw and records the change in its receipt (the plan's rule: an edge is added when an edit is discovered).

title: Computational media core: export policy, export identity and filenames, prepared-file cache
description:
## Goal
Move computational media (still encoding helpers, computational MP4 writer pieces, codec fallback selection) into `stylegan-js` or a computational app module with no DOM, state the lossy export policy once in code, and give every export a stable identity, a collision-safe short filename and a prepared-file cache. fm-eeki then rewires the app's Save/Share, URLs and retention onto it.

## Scope
- `export-policy` (no DOM, only source of encoder settings): WebP 0.8 default; PNG explicit lossless and fallback (MIME and extension together); MP4 unchanged from candidate `probeVideoEncoder` (`avc1.42002A`, WebCodecs 1024 then 512, bitrate `round(size*size*fps*0.25/1000)*1000`, framerate = fps, one 64 × 64 correctness encode, FFmpeg fallback at 512); JPEG 0.85 only for scrub/display; no quality slider.
- `exportIdentity({kind, orderedInputs, morph?, modelIdentity, format, encodingOptions})` -> SHA-256; short suffix per the contracts encoding (examples: `emma-k4p7s2.webp`, `seed-42-j8m3r6.png`, `emma-noah-figure8-b7w4n2.mp4`); collision rule extends the suffix; label rules (strip extension/path/control/bidi/reserved names like `CON`/`NUL`, normalize whitespace, truncate to 64 characters, `face`/`morph` fallback); extension and MIME match bytes; API for proposing/editing the name while keeping the suffix; no-clobber File System Access naming.
- Prepared-file cache keyed (revision, format, encoding options) with a bounded cache of other formats (bound from contracts milestone 2, fm-2o8q, at close; until then "measured, no threshold"); superseded completions discarded; format change never re-runs inference.
- Preserve once-only WebP with PNG fallback/read compatibility.

## Rules
- This bead edits NONE of the shared files (`apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs`). Code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today until the bridge's own turn in the shared-file sequence; the bridge rewiring is the original bead's job.
- Tests run against real models, real browsers and real files where stated; no mocks, fixtures or captures stand in for live proof. The original bead's real-bridge/built-app checks still have to pass before the feature counts as done.
- Split from the original bead in the parallelism pass (operator, 24 October 2026: more parallel work from the start).
- Original bead: fm-eeki (Split media computation from Save/Share; export policy, identity, filenames and prepared-file cache); anchors as listed there.

- Decoded MP4 contains the whole accepted path at the admitted, disclosed resolution with valid project metadata; rendered content bounds and all four corners checked.
- Retained CI lanes on the artifact. Paired morph timing (time to playable video, time per frame on the 32-frame/16 FPS/1024 px workload where supported) comes from the shared not-worse workload and runner (`verify.not-worse-lanes`, fm-0q4h) run against this artifact with the gate's pass rule (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27); no second workload, runner or rule here (a single CI timing is never a verdict).

## Out of scope
Implementing the Morph acceptance checks (`morph.guards`) or the parent intent (`morph.guards.intent`); a defect found here is fixed in the owning bead (or, if it needs a shared-file edit, under the shared-file ordering rule) and this bead re-runs. - Split on 2026-10-24 for swarm size into three beads, edited in this order: `morph.guards` (this ID, fm-fy2.9: frame budget, MP4 probe, identical-neighbour rule), `morph.guards.intent` (parent-intent scheduling and one current result) and `morph.guards.acceptance` (built-app matrix, retained lanes and the paired comparison against the pinned control). title: Per-operation route admission, typed admission events and refusal reasons
description:
## Split (parallelism pass, 24 October 2026)
The package/core work of this bead moved to fm-4umi (Route admission policy: pure per-operation admission, typed events and refusal reasons), which edits no shared file and starts as soon as its own inputs exist. This bead keeps: wiring the admission module into runtime/bridge (probe ordering, early stop before detector/model/crop work, reason shown at `.next-tile-status`/`.next-morph-reason`), the structured admission log line, and the network, runtime-harness and field-case checks. The scope text below is kept for context; where it describes work now owned by fm-4umi, that bead owns and accepts it and this bead consumes the result.

## Goal
Admit Generate, photo encoding and Morph by actual capabilities, never by phone/desktop labels, viewport width or touch, so a missing WebGPU adapter alone never makes the app unsupported and a known-ineligible operation stops early with a short, accessible reason. This is the code half of provider simplification's per-operation admission (split from `provider.admission`, fm-fy2.19, in the 24 October final pass): it edits the shared bridge/runtime files, so the typed facade (`migration.facade`, through `migration.project-json`) waits on it, while the lane evidence (phone CPU check, post-removal verification, module survival scan) stays in fm-fy2.19 and runs in parallel with the facade and compute work. Browser CPU/WebGPU selection, bounded CPU fallback and phone paths are retained; WebGL execution and native dispatch are already gone (`provider.webgl`, `provider.native`); CPU and WASM work is not.

## Scope
- Candidate facts: emits `route-admitted`/`route-rejected` progress; probes the GPU adapter before GPU acquisition (`navigator.gpu` alone once caused about 180 MiB of wasted Simulator downloads); pinned overlay has `encoderStream.phoneAdmitted:true` with a 268,435,456-byte e4e WASM limit (scope `friends-and-family-candidate`, `ios-simulator` evidence, not physical/release qualified).
- Admission per operation/provider from capabilities, memory and qualified runtime/model evidence; generator admission does not establish encoder/codec support.
- Probe adapters before GPU-only acquisition; absence/failure selects the qualified CPU route.
- A known-ineligible operation stops before its detector/model network or crop work, with a short reason for the owning action (`.next-tile-status` or `.next-morph-reason`); other supported operations stay usable; static names and completed files remain model-free.
- Bounded CPU fallback on actual GPU admission/execution failure as a declared transition; material slowdown or extra assets go through the existing revised decision; no native fallback; no racing alternative downloads; healthy slow GPU not demoted.
- Keep quick product admission separate from full lab numerical checks (no 20 s+ encoder guard on startup).
- One typed event per admitted or refused operation: operation (face/photo-encode/morph), requested route (`auto`|`cpu`|`webgpu`), actual provider, fallback (none or `gpu-failure-to-cpu` with the stage), refusal reason code, model/runtime identity and authorization scope (consumed by the operation controller). Keep `requestedProvider`/`provider` (`reporting.mjs` ~273; `route-report.test.mjs` "Route facts reach the collector and survive its allowlist"); add any new field to the reporting allowlist and privacy text list in the same revision.
- Refusal reasons are data: a `reasonKey`, its plain sentence (copy from `provider.copy`; until it lands a placeholder sentence per key that `provider.copy` replaces) and a Help anchor in state, not only a CSS state; the type makes a reason mandatory whenever an action is disabled for a capability reason; raw runtime exception text never enters the reason field. Face controls renders it as readable text tied to the disabled control (visible text or `aria-describedby`), never hover-only.
- Detailed logging: each admission decision logs operation, requested route, probed adapter facts (or `null adapter`), decision, reason key and fallback stage on one structured line, so a failed lane run shows why a route was chosen.

## Out of scope
- Phone CPU check, `phone-cpu-check.json`, post-removal lane verification and the module survival scan (fm-fy2.19 `provider.admission`).
- Consent modal rendering (`consent.modal`); device timing check (device); scheduler (opctl); Help copy (`provider.copy`); selector rendering (`face.selector-names`).

## Notes
- Shared-file order: third provider edit (`provider.native` -> `provider.webgl` -> this row), then `migration.project-json` and the typed facade. Edits `product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs`, `browser/ort-worker.mjs` and `reporting.mjs`.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#provider-simplification; #web-release-and-desktop-package-retirement--12-october-2026; #clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation (Consequence for acceptance; Added 18 October; row 'Attempted blocked face or Morph action'); #workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership (application migration's ordering edge on provider simplification).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] fm-4umi is closed; its modules are what this bead wires in (no second copy of the moved code left in the app).
- [x] Network test (requests intercepted, asserted by host class and bytes): a refused route issues zero detector/model requests.
- [x] Runtime-harness E2E (Playwright CPU lane, real null adapter: Chromium launched with WebGPU disabled): Auto -> CPU face completes; requested `auto`, actual `cpu`, zero GPU asset requests; the structured admission log line is present in the run output.
- [x] Field case (diagnostics learnings, 18 October: one WebGL-only Windows device failed 11 of 11 runs at route admission with 0 MB loaded): a desktop browser whose only GPU path fails its canary is admitted to CPU and completes a face, on a real Chromium launched with WebGPU disabled.
- [x] Unit tests listed in test discovery and pass locally with the CI command; CI verifies after push.
close_reason: Committed per-operation runtime admission qualified locally with real null-adapter CPU generation, refusal with zero model requests/workers and structured decision logs; unit and real GPU evidence attached.

title: Record the ORT adopt, hold or partial decision and apply it
description:
## Background

Outcomes: adopt, hold (reason, re-check trigger, JSEP removal timeline) or adopt in part.

## Why

Closes the currency policy's hold-back for this dependency with evidence.

## Scope

- Write the decision entry with all receipts linked.
- If adopt/partial: bump the immutable release-consistent runtime mirror together with the npm package,
  manifest and canaries in one revision through the normal gates (soft input to compute extraction's
  provider adapters).
- If hold: update the hold-back register entry (reason, re-check trigger, JSEP timeline).

## Out of scope

Changing tolerances or retained cells.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Decision entry in `docs/decisions/`; register or runtime manifest updated consistently; gates pass.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] The decision entry states outcome (adopt, hold or partial) per route and links the numerics, desktop-perf, phones, direct-vs-native and nightly receipts; on hold or partial it gives the reason, the re-check trigger (next passing updater run or a named upstream release) and the JSEP removal release/timeline; `currency.holdback-register`'s check passes on the updated register entry.

title: Write the operator handover and retirement action list
description:
## Background
Two hosting handovers: (1) next.facemorph.me switches its build source from classic `candidate/next-delivery-20260916` to the monorepo; (2) facemorph.me switches from legacy production (Vercel from classic `master`) to the chosen on-device artifact. During handover only one repository's workflow may publish to a target; disable/rebind the old publisher. After API retirement the historical production UI is not a working rollback; rollback uses a retained working on-device artifact with its immutable runtime/model/catalogue assets and diagnostics configuration inside the declared retention window.

## Why
Delivery executes this list on the operator's cutover decision; nothing may be improvised then.

## Scope
- Actions: early retained-candidate promotion; candidate-source handover; production promotion; API retirement; names-host redirect; Vercel publisher retirement; classic publication's default-branch switch pre-checks reference.
- Per action: preconditions (verifiable), exact commands/console steps, rollback target and steps, owner, proving check (ordinary post-delivery check: app loads, diagnostics report accepted, models load).
- One-publisher enforcement step per target.
- Step to tell the `multi-morph-test.vercel.app` user (Synthetic Data Ltd tester) before API retirement that it stops and the weighted blend replaces it.
- No production-data migration, GUID archive or restore rehearsal.
- Per action, the exact post-delivery check invocation (`delivery.post-delivery-check` mode and parameters: hostname, expected artifact digest, retired hosts to probe) and the receipt path under `docs/receipts/delivery-*.md`, so every action ends with its own receipt and checks.
- Second runtime origin: `models.facemorph.me` copies immutable runtime paths from `https://next.facemorph.me/` (hard-coded in classic `hosting/next-mirror/worker.mjs`) and the page uses it for retries on any `*.facemorph.me` host, including production. For each action state what keeps it complete: after the candidate-source handover next.facemorph.me serves the monorepo build, so an early-promoted candidate on facemorph.me (or a rollback artifact) relies on the paths the copy already holds; the step is to warm every runtime path of each live and rollback artifact before the handover, or to re-point the copy's origin, and to verify by HEAD requests from the log.

## Out of scope
Executing any action; deleting personal production records.

## Considerations
October 25 is aspirational; the operator chooses timing and order. Retention window comes from model hosting extraction.

- [ ] Action list committed (`docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/handover.md`) with all fields per action.

title: Fix lint findings and wire read-only format, lint and type gates into CI
description:
## Background

CI runs `format:check`, `lint` and explicit TS checks before build/qualification, without writing fixes.

## Why

Read-only gates that fail on violations protect every later revision.

## Scope

- Rule fixes in their own revision(s); bounded, justified suppressions (each with a reason comment),
  no blanket disabled legacy ruleset.
- CI job ordering: `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck` before build and qualification jobs.
- Fixture tests: a deliberate formatting violation and a deliberate lint violation each fail their check.

## Out of scope

Behaviour refactors.

## Considerations

- Shared-file serialisation: `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and
  `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited only in the mandated order (provider simplification, typed facade,
  compute extraction, confirmed-crop fix, morph pipeline, names picker/diagnostics); build items change
  tooling and CI, and add any shared file they touch to the check-migration map's conflict list.
- No worktrees, resets or cleans; preserve other sessions' uncommitted work.
- Hosted-minute economy: use capable workers where practical, but never weaken a required check or
  substitute Linux WebKit for Safari/iOS; never cancel a live publication halfway.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] CI fails on a seeded formatting violation and on a seeded lint violation (recorded runs), and passes on the clean tree.
- [ ] Suppression count and reasons listed in the receipt.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] CI also fails on a seeded type error (recorded run); after the format, lint and typecheck steps, `git diff --exit-code` passes, proving the gates write nothing; the gates run before build and qualification steps in every lane that builds.

title: Re-run the many-face layout and removal matrix (1-64 faces x sweep widths) on the release artifact
description:
## Background
Defects 2-3: the candidate fits two or three faces; from the third face the row becomes a sideways strip with no scroll cue; phones stack about 480 px per tile. Face controls specify a many-face layout (compact grid, compact rows beyond the fourth on phones), working Remove, Undo and Start over.

## Why
Every face's image, field, Generate and Remove must stay visible and reachable at any count up to the cap.

## Scope
This leaf re-runs, on the release artifact, the same operated matrix that `face.many-face-layout` (fm-ifkk) passes
at workstream level, with the same cell IDs, so the two receipts can be diffed cell by cell.
- **Matrix:** face counts `GRID_COUNTS` = 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 30, 64 x widths `SWEEP_WIDTHS` = 320, 360, 390, 480, 600,
  768, 900, 1,024, 1,280, 1,920 and 2,560 px, plus 1 px either side of each layout breakpoint read from the built CSS
  (both lists from `verify.harness`). Widths at or below the phone/tablet breakpoint use touch emulation
  (`hasTouch`, `isMobile`) and touch taps. Faces are set up by the controller fixture, not by clicking.
- **Each cell checks:** no page-level sideways scroll and no hidden scrolling surface; a visible scroll cue whenever
  any face is off screen; every face's image, field, Generate (or current slot action) and Remove (except on the
  last face) visible or reachable by normal scrolling; Remove sits inside its face image (or the compact-row
  thumbnail), not overlapped, with a 44 x 44 px hit area at touch widths, checked with `elementFromPoint` at its
  four corners and centre; the insertion + controls between faces are hittable (not under tiles, cue arrows or
  fades); Add face is enabled from 1 face up to the cap.
- **Removal per cell:** a real tap or click at Remove's visible position removes exactly that face (defect 1),
  without a reload; focus moves to a neighbour; Undo restores the face in place.
- **Start over** from 30 and from 64 faces returns to two empty faces; Undo reverses it.
- **Phone height:** page height at 30 faces on 390 px is recorded (the target is a few phone screens, not the
  candidate's about 7,000 px for fourteen).
- **Cap:** at 64 faces the same plain message appears on all six entry paths (insertion +, Add face, multi-file
  drop, batch OK, paste into a new face, background drop). `verify.flows-mixed-batch` grades defect 18 from its own
  batch cases; this leaf records the layout-side cases.
- Rows graded: R26, R27, R28; defects 1, 2, 3 (and layout evidence for 7 and 18).

## Out of scope
Direct face reordering.

## Considerations
- Defect 1 regression: real click at Remove's visible position removes exactly one face.
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Width x count matrix: 7 counts x (11 widths + 2 per breakpoint) cells, one screenshot per cell, every cell listed in the receipt as passed, failed or untested with its reason; the cell count is asserted by the script.

title: Write the research provenance map and resolve the 69-row accounting
description:
## Background

Ledger census: 14 keep, 41 inconclusive, 5 proposed, 3 discard, 2 blocked, 2 baseline, 2 candidate
(recorded verdicts, not adopted features). All 22 unique historical v2 source/portfolio references are
absent at their recorded paths; catalogue/hashes survive. Links in PLAN.md into classic `autoresearch/`
describe the snapshot.

## Why

Every ledger row and preserved family must resolve to a file here or to classic history at the snapshot commit.

## Scope

- Map source path → destination path for every file; for each of the 69 rows, the evidence paths it cites
  and where they now resolve (here, classic history at snapshot, or 'evidence unavailable').
- Cross-reference the families in the preservation map.

## Out of scope

Re-qualifying any row.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.

A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Strictly-not-worse gate: paired performance and reliability against the pinned candidate
description:
## Goal
Hold the live cutover pushes (next.facemorph.me handover, facemorph.me promotion) until the monorepo release is shown strictly no worse than the current next.facemorph.me candidate in performance and reliability on every platform class, iPhone included (PLAN.md "Strictly not worse than the candidate", operator 24 October 2026). The candidate "works and we do get faces"; that is the floor. Declared UI changes may change a journey's shape but must not make the same work slower, less reliable or heavier.

## Scope
- **Run.** The paired workload and lanes from `verify.not-worse-lanes` (fm-0q4h). Control: the pinned candidate artifact (by hash, from candidate import). Under test: the release artifact named in `release-identity.json` (`verify.artifact`, fm-k752), served through the integrated-verification harness's artifact fixture (`verify.harness`, fm-48bj) with its digest checked. Same workload, device, browser, provider and cache state for both; ABBA order; at least 5 pairs per cell, more where the cell's control/control spread is wide. Cells: iOS Simulator; physical iPhone (`safaridriver`); Android emulator, plus a physical Android phone when one is leased; desktop WebGPU on eris and on the Mac; desktop CPU in CI.
- **Pass rule (applied exactly).**
  - Reliability: every run that produced a face, a photo face or a video on the control produces it on the new build; no new crash, tab reload, out-of-memory kill or fallback in any pair.
  - Timing, byte and memory measures: per cell and measure, the paired log ratio new/control per pair and its 95% interval (bootstrap over pairs, seed recorded); the measure fails when the whole interval lies above log(1 + noise margin), the margin coming from that cell's control/control runs.
  - Inconclusive (interval too wide to decide, or fewer pairs than required) and untested cells block their platform class and never count as passing. Gains on one cell never offset a loss on another; 512 px video is never compared with 1024 px as a speedup.
- **Deliberate trades.** The only exception is a trade recorded in PLAN.md that names its measure; the gate reads them from a typed list in code, each citing its PLAN.md anchor, and reports them as `trade`, not `passed`.
- **Retained evidence register.** Each of the 12 register rows from `build.identity-map` (fm-pud), handed over with its cell and boundary by `verify.artifact`, maps to a cell and measure here (for example eris WebGPU warm morph ms/frame, Ubuntu CPU repeat Save, iPhone 16 Pro Simulator first face); a row with no matching run is `untested`. Historical values are context, never absolute limits.
- **Fix loop.** A regression is fixed in the owning bead, a new artifact is built and the gate re-runs on that digest.
- **Output.** Machine-readable result naming the commit and artifact digest: a verdict per platform class (`passed`, `failed`, `untested`, `inconclusive`) and the cell x measure table (pairs, ratio, interval, margin, verdict, trade citation). `verify.join` (fm-fy2.11) puts it in the release summary, which the cutover decision reads.

## Out of scope
Building the workload, lanes and noise runs (`verify.not-worse-lanes`); the real-visitor check after cutover (`verify.field-not-worse`, fm-js8i); new optimization work (opportunities go to the operator/planner with evidence or a hypothesis); historic-API parity.

## Notes
- Replaces the earlier "no control/control report, no physical-iPhone pass" wording. A connected device is setup, not an approval; an unavailable cell is untested and blocks that platform class.
- The no-regression comparison that `verify.artifact` used to own lives here, so there is one comparison rule.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#strictly-not-worse-than-the-candidate-operator-24-october-2026, #retained-performance-evidence-and-no-regression-checks, #integrated-verification.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Comparison unit tests on fixture runs: clearly faster gives `passed`; slower beyond the margin gives `failed`; slower inside the margin gives `passed`; too few pairs or a wide interval gives `inconclusive`; a missing cell gives `untested` and permits no performance claim for its class; missing required local P30 Pro/eris evidence blocks handover, while an explicitly unavailable hosted runner/simulator does not permanently block; a new crash, reload, out-of-memory kill or fallback in any pair gives `failed` whatever the timings; a PLAN.md trade gives `trade` with its citation; a gain on one cell leaves another cell's verdict unchanged; the same seed reproduces the same intervals.
- [ ] Gate run on the release artifact (digest checked against `release-identity.json`) on every listed cell with at least 5 ABBA pairs, using the lanes' control/control noise margins.
- [ ] The output names the same commit and digest as the identity record; the release summary shows the per-class verdicts and the table; an untested or inconclusive cell permits no claim for that class; physical-iPhone evidence is optional and is never inferred from the iOS Simulator. Required local P30 Pro/eris checks must pass; real failures on available hosted lanes require repair.
- [ ] Logs name every cell, measure, pair count and verdict; failing runs keep traces and screenshots as privacy-filtered CI artifacts.
- [ ] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test`) and pass.
notes: Operator, 25 October 2026 (fm-ajcf): reuse existing classic-style iOS Simulator inside the GitHub macOS runner and Android emulator CI alongside ordinary tests. Hosted runner/simulator unavailability is best effort: bounded attempt, explicit untested reason, no passing or physical-iPhone claim and no permanent release block. Actual available-lane failures require repair. Physical phone never runs in CI. Candidate handover needs no further approval and is incomplete until actual P30 Pro and eris CPU/WebGPU checks plus post-delivery-check pass against the deployed artifact. This supersedes older all-platform-availability and physical-iPhone release prerequisites; other product/performance requirements remain.

title: Controller port: reporting consent, toasts and slider reducers
description:
## Background

Calls to scheduling/cancellation/progress go through the operation-service interface (`opctl.interface`), backed by the retained bridge until `ws:opctl` lands. Do not copy candidate defects frozen as repair rows; keep the candidate behaviour for parity rows exactly. Never record photos, latents, typed inputs or raw error strings.

## Source map (classic, read-only, classic `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (or the frozen import revision recorded in `inventory.md`; re-check line numbers there with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`))

title: Weighted face blend operation in stylegan-js
description:
## Goal
Add a pure `blend(latents, weights)` to `stylegan-js` that reproduces the retired API's `num_multi` arithmetic for photo slots: `sum(weight_k * W+_k)` over each slot's W+ latent, each weight clamped to [-2, 2] and **not** normalised, ready for one synthesis. This is the engine half of the weighted face blend (advanced mode), which replaces the API's only feature the app lacks for the Synthetic Data Ltd tester, in the visitor's browser with no server, GPU host, new model, encoder or download. It is pure arithmetic, descriptor-driven so non-face models get it too, and can land before the rest of compute extraction.

## Scope
- Pure strict-TS `blend(latents, weights)`: inputs are W+ latents shaped by the model descriptor (`[1,18,512]` for FFHQ; layer count and width from the descriptor for other models) and one weight per slot.
- Clamp each weight to [-2, 2]; unnormalised weighted sum (weights 1, 1 give the sum, not the mean); negative weights allowed; report the weight sum (the view shows it).
- Any number of slots from 1; no fixed slot limit (operator, 24 October: only real constraints; the API's 16 was a server choice, not a hardware limit). Cost is one weighted sum, linear in N, plus one synthesis. Refuse 0 slots, a non-W+ latent and latents of mismatched shape, each with a typed error. Memory for retained photo inputs is the caller's admission check against the contracts byte budgets, not a slot count here.
- Cache key built from the clamped weights and the latent digests; any weight or digest change changes the key.
- Arithmetic matches classic `LatentByMultiLerp` (`checkface/src/server/checkface.py`), which sums the weighted dlatents. For word and seed slots the API held Z vectors and summed in Z space (or applied weights inside the mapping network when a photo was present); that is not a linear blend and is deliberately **not** matched (verified in source 24 October). The app holds every face (photo, name, word, seed) as W+, so a blend is one weighted sum plus one `synthesize(latent)`.
- The engine accepts the API's full [-2, 2] range for library callers; the view's 0–1 slider limit is the view's concern.

## Out of scope
The blend view, **Blend faces** button, `#blend` deep link, slots, weight controls, Reset/Make it 1 and Add to morph (`face.blend-view`). The blend parent intent, waiting for slot latents, skipping weight-0 slots, refusing all-zero weights, latest-wins supersession and cancellation (operation controller, `opctl.scheduler` fm-in6a). The recipe in saved files (`media.schema`). The `blend` entry in the diagnostics action list (diagnostics consent control). Old GUIDs or links, a hosted endpoint, blending inside the morph video, automatic or batch generation of many blends, model training. A **Shuffle weights** button is a planner proposal the operator may accept or veto; not planned here.

## Notes
- Newer PLAN.md (section "Weighted face blend (advanced mode)", revised 24 October) wins over the 21 October bead text on three points: (1) a non-W+ latent is refused rather than broadcast from W to W+ (callers map first); (2) synthesis of the result is covered by the existing raw-synthesis canaries, so there is no separate parity image or blend-specific synthesis test here, despite the row sketch's "one parity image"; (3) this row is pure arithmetic in the package and edits none of the shared bridge/runtime/worker files, so it no longer waits for the morph pipeline; the app-side synthesis entry and controller wiring belong to the face and controller rows.
- Cost reference: about 0.4 s warm on WebGPU for blend + synthesis in the tester's own diagnostics (one device, not a promise). Effort: about a day with tests.
- Anchor: PLAN.md #weighted-face-blend-advanced-mode.

title: Refuse identical neighbours before morph work (defect 6)
description:
## Background
Candidate defect 6 (operated, 18 October audit): the same word in both faces, or A, B, A, fails with "This project is invalid or uses an unsupported format." The geometry rejects adjacent chord norm below 1e-12. Required: refuse identical neighbours before any work, with a plain message naming what to change; A, B, A is allowed or refused by one stated rule (the closed loop makes the last face a neighbour of the first).

## Why
A generic project error for a common input is a broken journey.

## Scope
- Record the A, B, A rule below in `docs/decisions/` (the rule is stated here so the implementer does not choose it).
- Pre-check at Morph acceptance comparing adjacent input identities (and the closing pair for closed paths) before any acquisition/inference; plain message in Morph status naming the faces to change.
- Unit tests and an operated UI check.

## Out of scope
Face input UI (face controls).

## Considerations
- Identity comparison uses latent/model identity, not display labels.

## The one stated rule (polish r1)
Every product morph path is a closed loop: candidate `product-bridge.mjs` builds the project with `closed: true` for all five shapes, including linear, and `latent-path-v1` checks each consecutive pair plus the closing pair (`controls[i]` with `controls[(i + 1) % n]`, chord norm below 1e-12 rejected).

**Rule: refuse a morph when any two cyclically adjacent faces are the same, meaning face i and face i+1, and the last face and the first. Faces that repeat without being adjacent are allowed (they are separate visits).**
- A, A: refused (faces 1 and 2).
- A, B, B: refused (faces 2 and 3).
- A, B, A: refused, because the loop returns from face 3 to face 1 and they are the same.
- A, B, A, C: allowed (no adjacent pair is equal, including C back to A).
- A, B, C: allowed.

"Same" means the same latent and model identity (latent digest and model identity equal), or latents whose difference has norm below 1e-12, the geometry's own test. Display labels are never compared (two different words that resolve to the same latent are the same face; the same word under different models is not).

Message, in Morph status before any acquisition or inference, naming the faces: for example "Faces 3 and 1 are the same, and the loop goes from face 3 back to face 1. Change one of them or add a different face between them." The check runs again when inputs change; a valid change clears the message.

Named tests: `neighbour-rule.aa`, `.abb`, `.aba-closing-pair`, `.abac-allowed`, `.abc-allowed`, `.same-latent-different-words`, `.same-word-different-model`, `.near-identical-below-1e-12`, `.message-names-faces`, `.no-work-before-refusal` (event log: zero model requests, zero inference events).

## Decision-log entry required: agent-chosen rule, not PLAN text (polish r2)
The rule below was chosen by the round-1 bead-polish agent on 24 October 2026; PLAN.md does not state it. It is therefore not silently decided: the first implementing change writes the entry `docs/decisions/2026-10-24-identical-neighbours-closed-loop.md` with status `proposal, operator may veto`, decided-by `planner agent (bead polish r1, 24 Oct 2026); no PLAN.md text`, the rule as written here, the evidence it rests on, the alternatives listed below, and what changes if it is vetoed. The bead implements the rule as written unless a veto or change entry exists (this is not an approval gate), and its receipt cites the entry. Identity's decision log (fm-orh, area A) should list it beside P1-P4.
- Rule: every product morph path is a closed loop, so Morph is refused when any two faces next to each other around the loop are the same, including last -> first. A,A, A,B,B and A,B,A are refused; A,B,A,C and A,B,C are allowed. "Same" = equal latent and model identity, or chord difference below 1e-12; display labels are never compared.
- Evidence: candidate `product-bridge.mjs` builds every morph with `closed: true`, and `latent-path-v1` already rejects a consecutive or closing pair whose chord norm is below 1e-12, so A,B,A fails inside geometry today with a less useful message. Defect 6 asks for an early, plain refusal.
- Alternatives: (a) refuse only literally adjacent pairs and drop the closing pair for linear shapes (needs a geometry change and a `GEOMETRY_VERSION` bump, which the plan forbids for existing shapes); (b) silently skip the duplicate face.
- If vetoed: the A,B,A test flips and the message text changes; the geometry check is untouched.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Same word twice and A, B, A (per the stated rule) show the plain message with zero inference (event log); valid A, B, C proceeds.
- [ ] Operated UI acceptance: act with real pointer/touch input at the control's visible position and assert via `elementFromPoint` that the element there is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role clicks only to set up state; repeating controls exercised at 0/1, 2, 3, many and the cap; text inputs with an empty, a very long and a pasted value; a phone-width (390 px) and a desktop-width (1,280 px) screenshot per case.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots are kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Network claims are asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] The stated rule is recorded in `docs/decisions/` and the named tests pass: A,A; A,B,B; and A,B,A (closing pair) are refused with a message naming the two faces; A,B,A,C and A,B,C proceed.
- [ ] Built-UI check for A,B,A and same word twice: the refusal appears in Morph status with zero model requests and zero inference events in the event log; changing face 3 clears it and Morph proceeds.
- [ ] The agent-chosen rule is written as a decision-log entry with status `proposal, operator may veto` and decided-by naming the polish agent and the absence of PLAN.md text; the receipt cites the entry; the decision validator passes on it.
notes: Position in the shared-file sequence: after morph.scheduling, before media.session-words, media.storage-clear and the face/names/diagnostics edits. Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Leaves that must not edit these three files: ws:crop.repro (failing tests and the failure analysis only), crop.policy, media.envelope-helpers, media.recovery-schema, morph.descriptor-geometry, compute.consumer-example, compute.names-equality, and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept leaf. They keep the module export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) and move logic behind them into the package. If such a leaf finds it must edit one of the three files, it records the file in the check-migration map conflict list and adds a needs edge to the latest leaf in the sequence that edits it; it never edits concurrently. Each sequenced leaf lists every file it edits in the check-migration map conflict list at claim time.

title: Replace ChooseName -> RunFace with validated static-result selection
description:
## Background
`ChooseName -> RunFace` synthesizes on selection; `generateNameOrSeed` silently falls back to text mapping. This is the
picker's bridge-consuming edit, ordered after confirmed-crop and the morph pipeline (shared `product-bridge.mjs`).

## Why
Selection must be inference-free and identical to typing the same name.

## Scope
- Selection fills the name into the ordinary text field, shows the preview immediately, fetches only that result's
  bounded assets plus at most one integrity lookup, validates image/latent/recovery, then the text revision becomes a
  completed Save/Morph input; the default file is prepared.
- Loading/Retry in the target tile's action slot; stale target responses rejected; never substitute synthesis on
  catalogue failure; cold/offline/corrupt/stale states explicit; offline works only for cached complete validated
  assets.
- Morph with selected names acquires the generator only via consent; the name's validated image serves preview, slider
  and video at that endpoint (no re-synthesis).
- Editing selected text invalidates the ready result and enables ordinary Generate/Retry; store result identity and
  provenance, not a persistent names mode.
- Transient catalogue availability cannot change the face associated with a typed string.

## Out of scope
Grid UI.

## Considerations
Progress for name selection completes after validation and default file preparation.

button (no fill) centred below the preview; **CANCEL** bottom left (light grey filled, dark text); **OK** bottom right
(indigo filled, white text). Measured boxes and colours come from `face.legacy-dialog-inventory`
(`docs/design/legacy-encode-dialog-geometry.json`). The candidate shows the encoder consent dialog straight away for
one clear face with no crop step (audit section 3); its crop panel is transparent in light mode (defect 20).
Confirmed-crop encoding (`ws:crop`) makes an eligible confirmed crop reach exactly one e4e attempt.

## Why
"Crop only before encoding" and the confirmed-crop flow (PLAN.md#confirmed-crop-and-ordered-multi-selection-flow)
are original requirements; the always-confirm-first flow is a real change from the candidate.

## Scope
- Detect/propose on the source before confirmation; display the proposal (any detector-driven warp completes first).
  If detector/alignment assets are absent, the same consent gate runs first (consent owns it); declining keeps local
  manual crop (ADJUST CROP) and starts no downloads.
- Modal per the locked image and the inventory geometry: title "Encode an image", logo top right, square preview,
  ADJUST CROP centred below, CANCEL bottom left, OK bottom right; same button styles; opaque background in light and
  dark themes (repairs defect 20's transparent crop panel); text 4.5:1 or better in both.
- One short explanation that encoding recreates the face and may change details, placed between the preview and the
  footer (the only copy added to the locked layout; recorded as a deliberate difference). No resemblance approval.
- ADJUST CROP opens the editor state (`face.crop-editor-modal`) in the same modal; Use Crop returns here with the
  updated proposal.
- OK freezes crop rectangle, rotation, orientation and input revision, closes the modal, returns to the main page and
  the tile action slot shows Cancel; encoding queues without waiting for downloads to finish. Repeated OK presses
  produce one attempt.
- Cancel (and Escape/Back/backdrop) before OK abandons preparation: no e4e, no extra keypoints; focus returns to the
  initiating control. Only the topmost modal owns Escape/Back/focus; the page beneath is inert.
- If a new consent must follow OK, replace the dialog rather than stacking focus traps.
- Single-candidate default; the multi-candidate grid is the batch leaf; the source step is `face.encode-source-step`.

## Out of scope
The editor; alignment failure; batch selection; encoding itself; the source step.

## Considerations
Guides are never burned into pixels. Restoring a previous face on Cancel is desirable where simple, not mandatory.
The preview square scales with the modal at narrow widths but stays square and fully visible (four corners inside
the viewport at 320 px and at a 568 px-high viewport).
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** It is the ported crop confirmation modal; previews come from the facade's existing photo preview/crop calls. If implementation finds it must edit one of them after all, it first runs `br dep add fm-nxdb fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph), adds the file to the conflict list in fm-bhw and records the change in its receipt (the plan's rule: an edge is added when an edit is discovered).

title: Shared CI pieces: explicit-provenance artifact lookup, path filters, request-interception helper
description:
## Goal

Deliver, before any lane is carried over, the shared CI pieces every lane and every network-asserting end-to-end test uses: one tested artifact lookup with explicit provenance (never inherited `context.repo` or a corrected org prefix), one path-filter list with the concurrency and cache conventions for all lanes, and the request-interception helper (TypeScript for Playwright, Python over CDP for `browser-harness`) that asserts network behaviour by host class and bytes. Split out of the site-lane bead in the 24 October final pass so the site, mobile and GPU lanes can be carried over in parallel and each bead stays reviewable in one sitting.

## Scope

**Shared artifact lookup** — `.github/actions/fetch-artifact/action.yml` wrapping `scripts/ci/fetch-artifact.ts`:
- Required inputs, none inherited: `source_repo_id` (numeric repo ID, not owner/name), `workflow`, `run_id`, `commit` (full SHA), `artifact_name`. Query the run via REST (job token or read-only token for classic); refuse when the run's `repository.id`, `head_sha` or workflow file differ; download; verify sums file and `next-site-source.txt`. Outputs `artifact_dir`, `artifact_digest` (identity-hashing digest), `provenance_json`. One JSON verdict line per call. Never uses `context.repo` or a corrected org prefix.
- Fail closed with named errors (API error, missing sums, digest mismatch); never silently rebuilds. An expired classic artifact (14-day retention) reports `blocked: artifact expired`.
- `scripts/ci/path-filters.json`: one list for all lanes (`apps/web/**`, `packages/**`, `scripts/**`, `hosting/**`, `photo-runtime/**` if imported, `tests/mobile/**`, `package*.json`, `tsconfig*.json`, `.oxlintrc.json`, `.oxfmtrc.json`, the lane's workflow and actions) with per-lane narrowing.
- Concurrency `<lane>-${{ github.ref }}`, cancel-in-progress for test builds only, never on publish/deploy jobs. Caches: dependencies keyed by lockfile hash; immutable runtime/model assets by manifest digest, never branch or date.

**Request-interception helper**
- TS for Playwright (`attachPlaywright(pageOrContext)`, duck-typed, imports no Playwright package) and Python for `browser-harness==0.1.8` over CDP (`Network.*`, `Runtime.consoleAPICalled`, `Log.entryAdded`, `Target.setAutoAttach` for workers), used by `next-matrix.mjs`, `next-e2e-browser.py`, `next-gpu-benchmark.py`, `next-ios-sim.py`, `tests/mobile/run.py`.
- Records page, dedicated-worker and service-worker requests with initiator, status (incl. failures), bytes, `from_cache` where observable, and console errors; URLs kept as origin + path template.
- Host classes: `app`, `model-host` (incl. `models.facemorph.me`), `names-host`, `collector`, `third-party`, `local` (data:/blob:); versioned default map with an injectable map for preview/staging origins.
- Same-named primitives in TS and Python: `requestsIn(rec, {hostClass, fromStep, toStep})`, `assertNoRequests(rec, hostClass, window)`, `assertOrder(rec, before, after)`, `bytesBy(rec, hostClass)`. Missing data for a window fails a claim, never passes by absence; unobservable fields are declared and dependent claims report `untested`.
- Traces and screenshots kept on failure as CI artifacts (14-day retention unless the lane states more).

## Out of scope

Carrying over any lane (site lane `build.ci-site`, mobile lanes `build.ci-mobile`, GPU lane `build.workers-lease`); the identity hasher itself (`build.identity-map`, whose digest the lookup reports); canonical-artifact fan-out (later points this lookup at canonical bytes); journey assertions (integrated verification); publishing anything.

## Notes

- Consumers: the site, mobile and GPU lanes, research stage 2 drivers (`next-matrix.mjs`, `next-e2e-browser.py`, `next-gpu-benchmark.py`, `next-ios-sim.py`, `tests/mobile/run.py`), the integrated-verification harness and every consent, names, device-check and diagnostics end-to-end test (PLAN.md "Acceptance receipts" → network assertions: intercept requests and assert by host class and bytes, never from a screenshot).
- Logging: one JSON verdict line per lookup call (inputs, run found, repository id, head SHA, workflow, digest expected/actual, verdict or named error) and one per assertion primitive (primitive, host class, step window, request count, bytes, verdict); traces and screenshots kept on failure.
- PLAN.md (24 Oct) drops the general event-log schema, validator and privacy filter and the receipts; this helper is the network-assertion mechanism.
- Build beads change tooling and CI only; no shared app file is edited.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#platform-ci-retention-and-performance-preservation, #workspace-build-and-artifact-identity, #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance.

- [x] `fetch-artifact` unit tests (against the real GitHub API and real workflow artifacts; the flipped-byte case mutates a real downloaded copy): wrong `repository.id`, wrong `head_sha`, wrong workflow, missing sums and one flipped byte each fail with a distinct named error; a correct fixture yields the expected digest; no input defaults to `context.repo`.
- [x] A workflow run here fetches a classic `next-site-<sha>` by explicit inputs and verifies it; using owner/name in place of the numeric ID is refused.
- [x] Path-filter coverage test fails on a fixture tree with an uncovered top-level code root.

title: Licences and notices, version binding, and the packed-tarball clean-consumer smoke with content scan
description:
## Goal
Prepare the three npm packages (engine `stylegan-js`, browser model manager, Cloudflare model host) and the converter's tagged container release for publication: licences, notices and model terms checked against what is actually published; each version bound to its source commit and build provenance; and an author-run clean-consumer smoke from the packed tarballs that follows the final docs verbatim through the whole non-face journey, with the shared content scan. It catches missing files, repository-only paths and doc steps that only work inside the monorepo. **It publishes nothing; publishing is the delivery action (`delivery.packages`).** A local `npm pack` is preflight, not independent acceptance.

## Scope
**Licences and notices**
- Per package: `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES` covering bundled code (ONNX Runtime Web, WGSL kernels, WebCodecs/FFmpeg integration, and in the converter NVlabs, e4e, dlib/Pillow photo tooling), `package.json` licence field; per model in docs: usage/redistribution terms.
- Notice-check script comparing bundled third-party files in each tarball and the converter build context against the notices list.
- The converter image is not pushed to a registry; any later push needs a licence check first.

**Version binding**
- Versioning policy (semver, changelog per package); `repository`/`homepage` fields with the post-rename organization URLs (coordinate with the organization rename if it has not landed).
- Source commit and build identity recorded in a provenance file inside each package (from workspace-build identity hashing).
- CI publish workflow prepared and exercised here only as `npm publish --dry-run`, which needs no registry credentials; the real publish (`delivery.packages`) supplies the scope credentials (`gate.npm-creds`) and npm provenance attestation where the registry supports it. Published versions are immutable; fixes publish a new version.

**Reviewer logistics for `pkgaccept.review` (moved here in the 24 October final pass so it is committed before publication)**
- Commit, before `delivery.packages` can run, the independent-review packet that fm-fy2.21 specifies: the reviewer role (a person, or an agent session that did not author the packages) and how independence is ensured; the fixed input packet (published names, versions and public documents only); the review budget in time and resources (bounding only the review session); the worker/browser environments available; and the report template (registry versions/integrity, lockfile, identities, copied commands, outputs, friction log, verdict per capability for the 14 checklist lines). `pkgaccept.review` reads it when the review starts.

**Clean-consumer smoke (fresh directory outside the monorepo, no workspace links, three packed tarballs at their bound versions, final docs verbatim)**
1. Trusted checkpoint acquisition: acquire the documented non-face checkpoint per the converter docs; SHA-256 matches the published value; the trusted-pickle warning precedes the command.
2. Pinned container conversion: clone the converter at the release-candidate tag, build (image digest recorded), convert, run `verify`; the upstream PyTorch reference check passes the declared tolerance.
3. Developer-controlled static hosting: publish outputs with the host package's commands to a local HTTPS static server under the test's control (no FaceMorph hostname, catalogue, alias or secret); check MIME, CORS and cache/digest headers.
4. Manager-loaded inference: authorize acquisition, load the capability, pass it to `stylegan-js`, map a seed and synthesize; raw output within the model's declared tolerance.
5. Caller-loaded inference without importing the manager; same checks.
6. Morph of at least 3 inputs with the same model; descriptor-driven geometry.
7. PNG and lossless-WebP export and reopen: latent and model identity exact, decoded pixels equal supplied pixels; an equal-shaped latent from another checkpoint is refused for combination.
8. Network assertions from intercepted requests: zero at package construction and status reads; zero face detector or e4e requests anywhere in the non-face run.
- Every missing or confusing doc step found is fixed in the docs before closing.
- `package-tarball-content-scan` (created by `compute.package-surface`) runs on the three tarballs (profiles `stylegan-js`, `browser-model-manager`, `cloudflare-model-host`) and the converter build context (`model-conv-context`): no weights, repository-only paths, secrets or private provenance; emitted JS, types, exports and worker assets present. This row adds no rules; a missing rule goes into `compute.package-surface`'s profiles and self-test.

## Out of scope
Running the publish and holding npm credentials (delivery, `gate.npm-creds`). Independent review of registry versions (`pkgaccept.review`). Classic distribution notices.

## Notes
- Author-run smoke never substitutes for the independent review.
- Integrated verification's `verify.packages` proves the non-face joint journey from local packs; this is the publication-preparation run against the final docs and bound versions.
- Edits no shared bridge/runtime/worker file.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #independent-published-package-acceptance (what publishes), #delivery-and-publication, #external-developer-journey-and-non-face-models.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Notice-check script passes on every packed tarball and the converter build context.
- [ ] Reviewer packet for `pkgaccept.review` committed (role and independence, input packet, budget, environments, report template with the 14 checklist lines).
- [ ] `npm publish --dry-run` from CI (no credentials) succeeds for each package with the bound version and provenance fields; each tarball contains the provenance record matching the commit and artifact digest.
- [ ] The eight smoke steps each pass as a separate step in the run's output, from the docs verbatim, with the three tarballs installed in a clean external project.
- [ ] Intercepted requests: none at construction/status reads; no detector/e4e requests for the non-face run.
- [ ] `package-tarball-content-scan` passes on all three tarballs and the converter build context; its self-test fails each planted violation (weight file, repository-only path, fake secret, missing required file); JSON reports kept as CI artifacts.
- [x] From fm-3osh: packages/cloudflare-model-host ships a LICENSE once the licence is decided (none exists in the repository yet). After that, its package-tarball-content-scan reports outcome clean, and cloudflare-model-host.yml stops allowing the required-file LICENSE finding.
notes:
2026-10-26 operator: this artefact is the finish line for packages today; real npm publish (fm-96v) deferred to the operator. Make sure the tarballs and dry-run output are retained as CI artifacts.
2026-10-26 operator decision: licence is MIT for the monorepo and all three npm packages (stylegan-js, browser-model-manager, cloudflare-model-host). Model weights don't ship; their NVIDIA/upstream terms stay documented per model.

title: Intent snapshots, revisions and stale-completion rejection (defect 17)
description:
## Background
Operator ruling (12 October): requested CPU/WebGPU route, permitted failure-fallback scope and runtime/model identity are captured at Start/download approval and stay with queued work; later selector changes apply to new jobs. Candidate audit defect 17 (source): removing a generating face does not stop its job; a saved-MP4 drop can leave Morph queued for good and replaces every face without asking; replacing a photo destroys the face before the new photo is checked; cancelling a queued re-generate can leave a broken image.

## Why
Late results must never replace newer input, and approved scope must not silently change.

## Scope
- Snapshot per intent: requested route, bounded fallback scope, runtime/model identity, input revisions, request ID; new attempt ID per Retry; actual execution provider recorded.
- Typing/changing a source creates a new revision, invalidates old prepared file/morph immediately; replacement commit points per the plan (keep previous target through cancelled selection/rejected recovery where straightforward; never save the old face under a new name; never install a late result into a newer target).
- Each defect-17 case becomes a stale-completion test: remove while generating stops and releases the job; MP4 drop never leaves Morph queued forever and does not replace faces without the defined commit point; photo replacement checks the new photo before destroying the face; cancelling a queued re-generate leaves the previous verified image or an empty retryable target.

## Out of scope
UI rendering of these states (ws:face).

## Considerations
Local staging/revision checks are enough; no undo/history or transactional whole-project import.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests: selector change after queueing does not alter the queued intent; late completion for an old revision is discarded; each defect-17 case has a passing test.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic are listed in the destination test discovery (no unlisted test files) and pass in CI.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/opctl/intents.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Named tests in `apps/web/src/operations/intents.test.ts`: `selector change after queueing keeps the queued snapshot`, `late completion for an old revision is discarded`, `remove while generating stops and releases the job`, `MP4 drop never leaves Morph queued forever`, `MP4 drop does not replace faces before its commit point`, `photo replacement checks the new photo before destroying the face`, `cancelling a queued re-generate leaves the previous verified image or an empty retryable target`, `Retry creates a new attempt ID`.

## Why

## Scope
