title: Write specs and launch recipes for the three initial targeted campaigns
description:
## Background

Campaigns: (1) consented acquisition during input selection: empty/partial cache, Generate vs approved
Generate and encode, fixed selection/crop dwell, seed request while encoder assets transfer; (2) verified
-cache runtime warming: cached files/new browser vs resident session, eager selected-generator
preparation vs demand load, immediate next-face request, missing/corrupt shard and memory-constrained
cases; (3) photo preparation and e4e lifecycle: padded/nonpadded metadata-free photos, first/next encode,
constrained phone teardown vs qualified desktop reuse.

## Why

Makes the targeted rounds runnable once features exist, with honest instrumentation.

## Scope

- One spec per campaign with protected boundaries and source limits from the plan; synthetic dwell
  labelled synthetic; timeline-based overlap accounting.
- Launch recipe per campaign (checkout/worker, readiness checks, exact command, device identity, absolute
  lease dir, fixtures, browser profile, output locations) using fresh run labels.
- Instrumentation requirements: explicit bundle grant, ownership/request/attempt IDs, approved transfer
  timeline; natural-user/OS-picker observations as separate evidence.

## Protected boundaries per campaign (carried into each spec)

| Campaign | Protected boundaries and source limits |
| --- | --- |
| Consented acquisition during input selection | consent → first useful face; photo selection → reconstruction/file-ready totals; stage overlap on a timeline; actual bytes; foreground responsiveness; Cancel and route failure. Synthesis-first ordering exists; current prefetch pauses for foreground work, so broader overlap is new. |
| Verified-cache runtime warming | reload → first/nth new face; CPU/GPU mapping/load/readback; peak live reservations; foreground wait; zero speculative network (asserted from the event log); recovery without inference. Cache-only prefetch creates no session today; eager hydration is a hypothesis. |
| Photo preparation and e4e lifecycle | source → confirmed → reconstructed photo; per-shard verified-local read/create/run/copy/teardown; memory/bytes; cancellation. Reuse warm-hydration/padded-photo/streamed-e4e findings; no revival of rejected precision changes. |

Each launch recipe uses `autoresearch/templates/launch-recipe.md` (from `research.guides-protocol`) and
records each system-imposed wait plus the full useful journey; automated dwell is labelled synthetic; the
existing built-UI driver's auto-consent cannot establish chooser latency, so specs name the versioned
adapter from `evaluator.overlap-warming-adapters` they require.

## Out of scope

Running the campaigns (optional research after features exist).

## Considerations

Do not revive rejected precision changes (no silent fp16 e4e or tolerance widening).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The three specs pass the workload spec validator and their launch recipes pass the launch-recipe validator (no reviewer step): every placeholder is an explicit named field the validator lists, each spec names its required adapter version, marks dwell as synthetic, and declares timeline-based overlap fields; a copy of each recipe with one placeholder left unfilled fails the validator.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Snapshot published name previews and latents before the API stops
description:
## Goal
Copy every published name preview and latent from the two public Workers into durable storage, with a verified manifest and a restore path that never touches the hosted API, so the names catalogue can still be rebuilt after API retirement. `hosting/gallery/materialize.py` (run by `.github/workflows/name-catalogue.yml`) today fetches a 1024px JPEG preview from `api.facemorph.me` for every name missing from the Actions cache (2,144 in run 38029582696); a cold-cache run after retirement fails. Static names' first publication needs this snapshot, and API retirement may not start without it.

## Scope
- Snapshot script downloads every published preview and latent from both Workers into durable storage (R2 bucket or equivalent, never Git), resumable and idempotent: a re-run downloads nothing already verified; a corrupted object is re-fetched.
- Manifest checked in: name, source URL, size, sha256 per object; total count and total bytes; counts equal the published set.
- Restore path: a script (the one the catalogue pipeline will use) reads the snapshot instead of the API; restore test rebuilds a sample from the snapshot and compares hashes.

## Out of scope
The canonical-result generator (static names; it must never call the API); re-homing the catalogue workflow (deploy re-homing); retiring the API.

## Notes
- Do this early: the API may be retired any time after the operator's cutover call.
- Preview/latent Workers stay as shared resources until the snapshot and static names replace their API dependency.
- 24 October rules: no receipt; the API-retirement receipt cites this snapshot's manifest digest.
- Plan: #domain-handover-and-retirement-preparation, #retire-hosted-inference-and-the-old-api-completely, #known-active-references-to-the-retiring-hosts--source-scan-15-october-2026.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Snapshot stored durably; manifest with sha256 per object checked in; count and bytes equal the published set from both Workers.
- [x] Unit tests: a re-run downloads nothing already verified; a corrupted object is detected by digest and re-fetched; a missing object is reported.
- [x] Restore test rebuilds a sample from the snapshot with matching hashes, and request interception asserts zero requests to `api.facemorph.me` or `checkface.facemorph.me` (by host class and bytes).

title: Seed docs/decisions with the closed operator decisions
description:
## Background
PLAN.md "Acceptance receipts and gate-style acceptance" > *Operator decisions*: each operator decision is a dated entry in a decision log in the repository, with the outcome and who decided. The log lives in `docs/decisions/` and receipts in `docs/receipts/`. **Division of work with workspace build (fixed, not "whichever lands first"):**
- **This bead (source and repository identity) runs first.** It creates the two directories `docs/decisions/` and `docs/receipts/`, writes the first dated decision entries listed below (one file each), the open-item entries below, and its own receipts (`docs/receipts/identity-*.md`). It writes no README, template, schema or validator.
- **`build.docs-decisions-receipts` (fm-ucl, group B, needs `ws:identity`) runs after it** and adds the READMEs for both directories, the decision-entry and receipt templates, the receipt front-matter schema, `scripts/check-receipts.mjs` (CI), and the e2e event-log schema/emitter. It keeps every entry this bead wrote; if its template differs it may reformat the front matter but must not change any entry's date, outcome, decider or status, and its validator must pass on these entries.

Because the validator does not exist yet, this bead's entries and receipts must already carry every field by hand (see Design for the entry format).

## Why
Later beads cite a decision by its entry path instead of re-reading the plan's review record, and open questions stay visible as open instead of being decided silently by whichever implementer reaches them first.

## Scope
### 1. Decided entries (required set, from PLAN.md *Operator decisions*)
17 October 2026 (operator rulings round):
1. **No port checkpoint or fallback.** "We do it instantly. We have the ability. No hacks, back porting, or patches for legacy." The two-week/25% checkpoint and the .NET 5 container fallback are withdrawn; the port runs to completion. Decided by: operator.
2. **Diagnostics retention.** Ingest the learnings from existing reports first (read-only, aggregates only); keep reports; no expiration rule; the 30-day line is removed from the new app's copy and the re-homed collector; no deletion promise for later reports. Decided by: operator. (Amended 18 October, entry 9.)
3. **Dependency update lane is automated.** A dependency updater opens grouped update changes, existing gates decide; no review calendar and no named owner; the bleeding-edge lane never ships; the frozen classic distribution is excluded. Decided by: operator (the calendar was a planner's mechanism).
4. **Package scope.** Three TypeScript packages publish (engine `stylegan-js`, `browser-model-manager`, `cloudflare-model-host`); the converter ships as a pinned container (Dockerfile + Compose in the tagged public repository, no registry image); real npm names chosen at publication. Decided by: operator, from the original plan; flagged inference: manager and host publish because the acceptance journey needs them from the registry.
5. **WebGL removal.** Consented diagnostics read the same day (791 reports, 300 runs, 22 devices); WebGL was slowest everywhere a comparison existed; WebGL execution is removed, shared coefficient assets kept. Decided by: operator.

18 October 2026 (operator answers and follow-up):
6. **Candidate-source edits are ordinary work.** "We are working on the next candidate, so we change it as we work on it." The 17 October no-legacy-patches ruling concerns the old stack and fallbacks, not the working candidate. Decided by: operator.
7. **The tracker is rewritten from the plan.** Planner's reading: keep the 22 existing IDs (`fm-fy2*`) and replace their content. Decided by: operator (rewrite); keeping IDs is the planner's call — record both.
8. **Classic ends as the self-host Docker distribution plus Git history**, with an automated wind-down (preconditions, receipts, reversal paths); the experiment record moves to the monorepo. Decided by: operator.
9. **Old-wording diagnostics reports are deleted once mined; insights kept.** Replaces the "keep them" default for those reports only; no expiration rule; the boundary is the go-live of candidate commit `40c63a9` (2026-10-17 20:28:59 UTC). Decided by: operator.
10. **No human approval after conversion.** "I don't want to block on human after this plan goes to beads and is built." The only operator call left is the explicit cutover decision (promotion, retiring the old API, publishing packages; `gate:cutover`, fm-4gw7, records its own entry when made) plus execution prerequisites such as npm credentials. Decided by: operator.

### 2. Decided entries (earlier, also entered so later beads can cite them)
16 October 2026: D1 (no .NET/Fable/Webpack build in the monorepo; direct TS/React/Vite port with the built control artifact as oracle; operator), D2 (a picked name contributes its latent and validated image; no endpoint re-synthesis; the fifty-name measurement dropped as a gate; operator), D3 (superseded: it concerned `catalogue.json` size, now internal static-names work; planner reclassification after operator reply), D4 (frozen distribution on its own branch in classic, tagged, default-branch switch on its pre-checks, never merged into `master`; operator), D5 (no published backend image; operator, citing the original plan), D6 (upstream author weight hosts accepted, no mirrors; operator), D7 (latest MUI, "upgrade and make it work"; operator); cropper library optional, decided by spike (operator). 17 October: shared-file serialization by mandatory ordering edges (planner's call).

### 3. Open entries (status `open`; nothing here is decided by an agent)
Questions raised by the 18 October audit (PLAN.md "Questions raised by the 18 October audit"). Until the operator answers, the plan keeps the candidate's behaviour; each owning bead builds the candidate behaviour and cites this entry in its receipt:
- **Q1 Old text and seed links** (`?from_value=hello&to_value=world`, no server needed): honour, notice, or open empty as the candidate does? Owner: `ws:face` (fm-fy2.17; leaf to be named by group E); graded by `verify.flows-matrix` (fm-amjw).
- **Q2 Autoplay** of the result video (classic: muted loop; candidate: waits for a click). Owners: `face.morph-controls-output` (fm-j4i8), `migration.ren-morph-video` (fm-d8gv).
- **Q3 A plain 50/50 blend of two faces** as an easy path (candidate needs shape "Classic linear"). Owners: `face.morph-controls-output` (fm-j4i8), `migration.ren-morph-video` (fm-d8gv).
- **Q4 Cropper extras** (wheel/pinch zoom, crop square past the photo edge, pre-upload "look straight forward" tip). Owners: `face.crop-editor-modal` (fm-z0et), `face.legacy-dialog-inventory` (fm-iosz), `ws:face.cropper` (fm-fcm9).

Planner proposals the operator may veto (status `proposal, operator may veto`). The owning bead implements the proposal as the plan writes it unless a veto entry exists; a veto is recorded as a new dated entry and the owner drops that scope. This is not an approval gate:

title: Pass the face-controls responsive sweep (separately accepted)
description:
## Background
Earlier feedback: intrinsic dimensions and component checks passed while the displayed face was clipped. The
responsiveness acceptance (PLAN.md#integrated-verification) requires a width sweep, not endpoint screenshots.

Integrated verification's whole-app sweep (`ws:verify.platform`) re-runs this on the final artifact.

Layout checks with available browsers/devices; not a physical-phone release gate. Record exact viewport/zoom/
artifact and unsupported environments.

title: Define the versioned workload spec schema
description:
## Background

Freeze before candidates: workload, timing boundary, source/artifact/runtime/model/fixture/evaluator
digests, provider, device/browser, cache state, network, warmup/order and regression decision rules.
Fixed 32-frame/16 FPS/1024 px workload where supported. Controlled initial comparisons: discarded
warmup and ABBA ×3, raw distributions, paired effects; cold profiles empty; baseline warmup in separate
profiles. Cohorts: empty cache, cached files/new browser, live resident session, cached output, restored
result. Finish boundaries: decoded/drawn face, useful scrub frame, playable video, prepared file,
Save/share handoff (`img.src` is not a rendered finish; share-sheet handoff is not delivery).

## Why

One schema shared with the evaluator avoids a cycle and makes specs machine-checkable.

## Scope

- JSON schema plus validator for specs with all fields above, statistical method, confidence, sample and
  confirmation rules, invalid-pair handling, practical margins from control/control evidence, protected
  metrics (first/nth face, confirmed photo, complete video, first/repeated Save, restore, responsiveness,
  bytes, memory reservations, cancellation), screen vs confirmation identity.
- Metadata-free photos must execute the actual encoder.

## Out of scope

Evaluator implementation.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Schema and validator committed; an example spec validates; a spec missing a decision rule fails.
- [ ] Unit tests cover this item's own logic and run in the workspace test command.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] The schema requires cache, network and visibility state fields (visible tab vs hidden/background) per cohort, and cold, warm and output-cache cases are distinguishable values; the validator rejects a spec missing any of them.
- [ ] Table-driven validator tests reject a spec missing any required field (outcomes, cells, statistical method, confidence, sample and confirmation rules, protected metrics, invalid-run handling, cohort), a spec whose screen and confirmation sets share an identity, and a cold cohort whose profile shares an optional warmup (false cache state); the valid example passes.

title: Controller port: photo, crop queue and detected-face reducers
description:
## Background
`Product.fs` cases at the pinned commit: `PickPhoto`, `Photo` variants (project file, recovered still, crop offer, null/non-null file; ~444-547), `Photos` (multi-file drop, one face per file in drop order; ~548-572), `Cropped` with photo revision check, `PhotoFailed`, `PhotoError`, `RequestCrop`, `CropViewport`/`CropPan`/`CropZoom`/`CropRotate`/`CropAccept`/`CropCancel` with `CropQueue` (queued crops no longer revoke each other), `ChooseDetected`/`DismissDetected` (~652-665), `Failed` with the multiple-faces message. Crop geometry helpers come from `photo/crop-view.mjs` (`createCrop`, `pan`, `zoomTo`, `rotate`, `rect`, `frame`, `resizeViewport`).

## Why
Photo flows carry the recovery-first dispatch and crop geometry fixes that must survive the port exactly before the confirmed-crop and face-controls changes land.

## Scope
Pure reducers with transition tests; crop math stays in the existing JS module called as pure functions; revision checks (`photoRevision`) preserved so late crops are dropped.

## Out of scope
Confirmed-crop repair (ws:crop), batch proposal and crop modal redesign (ws:face), paste entry.

## Considerations
Pure typed reducers (no I/O); effects are returned as descriptions and executed by `migration.ctl-effects`. Calls to scheduling/cancellation/progress go through the operation-service interface (`opctl.interface`), backed by the retained bridge until `ws:opctl` lands. Do not copy candidate defects frozen as repair rows; keep the candidate behaviour for parity rows exactly.

## Source map (classic, read-only, classic `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (or the frozen import revision recorded in `inventory.md`; re-check line numbers there with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`))
`Product.fs` `updateCore`: helpers `nextCrop` 378-381 (advances `CropQueue`, calls `focusCropArea`) and `dequeue` 383-387 (multi-photo queue -> `selectPhoto` one file at a time); `PickPhoto` 444-448; `Cropped` 449 (dropped when `revision<>photoRevision id`) and 450-464; `PhotoFailed` 465-467; `PhotoError` 468-472; `Photo` variants 473-493 (project file -> Import path; recovered still; crop offer -> `Crop`/`CropQueue`) and 537-547 (null file clears PreparingFaces via `schedule`; plain file -> encode); `RequestCrop` 494-498; `CropViewport` 499, `CropPan` 503, `CropZoom` 507, `CropRotate` 511, `CropCancel` 515-521, `CropAccept` 522-536 (`cropPhoto` via bridge `cropPhotoReported`); `Photos` 548-572 (drop of N files: first empty face or append, one face per file in drop order, uncapped — defect 18); `DismissDetected` 652-656 and `ChooseDetected` 657-665 (`chooseDetectedFace`); `Failed` with `multipleFacesMessage` 679-682 (re-offers the picker). View-side drop handler: `view` 1196-1199 dispatches `Photos(None, photoFiles e)`.
Retained JS: `photo/crop-view.mjs` (`createCrop`, `pan`, `zoomTo`, `rotate`, `rect`, `frame`, `resizeViewport`) called as pure functions; `photo-selection.mjs` (`photoFiles`, `openPhotoPicker`, `dragPhoto`, `focusCropArea`); `photo/align-photo.mjs` `MULTIPLE_FACES_MESSAGE`; bridge `selectPhotoReported`, `previewPhotoReported`, `cropPhotoReported`, `photoRevision`, `chooseDetectedFace`, `cancelPhotoRun`, `warmPhotoTools`, `rememberSourcePhoto`, `sourcePhotoUrl`.
Candidate checks to replace here (they read `Product.fs` as text): `src/Next/crop-queue.test.mjs` (three tests: a crop for another face queues; every crop exit advances the queue; the queue is declared and starts empty) and the `photo-selection.test.mjs` test "the multiple-faces sentence is shared, not duplicated". Replace each with an equivalent TS reducer test and record the pair in the check-migration map.

## Goldens replayed
Flow rows: Replace a face with a photo / cancel picker or crop, Paste an image or drop one on tile or background (drop only; paste is absent in the control), Drop several files (candidate one-face-per-file behaviour), Confirm one detected crop, Adjust/rotate crop and cancel/accept, No detected face, Select several detected faces (candidate single-choice picker), Reopen recovery-bearing still. Rows the freeze classes repair (defects 17, 18) or declared change (confirmed-crop policy, batch proposal, paste, crop editor) are owner-graded, not asserted.

## Goldens and grading (polish r1)
- **Golden store.** Goldens are the recorder output chosen by `migration.golden-spike` (reducer transitions or journey-step DOM/state snapshots), committed under `apps/web/test/goldens/control/<flow-row-id>/` with a `goldens.json` index naming the control `deploy-next/` SHA-256, the recorder command and, per step, the freeze class of its row. Replays run `scripts/fetch-control.mjs` first and refuse to run if the index digest differs from `control-artifact.json`.
- **Parity rows** (freeze class *present and unchanged*): the port's transitions/DOM must equal the golden exactly (state fields, emitted effect descriptions, text, flow order, round-trip bytes). No tolerance, no "close enough".
- **Repair rows** (candidate defects 1-23) and **declared-change rows**: never parity. The recorder tags their steps `repair:<n>` or `declared:<section>` and the replay lists them as owner-graded instead of asserting them. No test in this repository may encode a candidate defect as expected output. Where the defect lives entirely in what this leaf writes (a string, a CSS rule order, a label), write the specification's version; where the repair needs the owner's design or copy, carry the nearest candidate behaviour without asserting it and leave the repair, and its grading against the plan specification, to the named owner.
- **Absent rows** are specification-graded by their owners after parity; this leaf adds no behaviour for them.
- A row the recorder cannot exercise is listed `untested` with the reason, never passed.
design: Files: `apps/web/src/controller/reducers/photo.ts`, `crop.ts`. Tests `photo.test.ts`, `crop.test.ts` replaying goldens plus named cases: `Cropped` with a stale revision is ignored; two queued crops for different faces both survive and appear in queue order; every crop exit (Cancel, Accept, failure) calls `nextCrop`; a three-file drop onto a two-face project fills empties then appends in drop order; `multipleFacesMessage` failure while a face is active reopens the picker (the constant is imported, never a literal); a recovered still restores without an encode effect. Crop geometry is asserted by calling `crop-view.mjs` with the golden's inputs, not by re-deriving math in TS. Replay/e2e runs emit the structured event log (step ID = `<flow-row-id>/<step>`, ISO timestamp, control and port artifact digests, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); the log is a CI artifact.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Transition tests per case against goldens, including late `Cropped` with a stale revision being ignored and two queued crops both surviving.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic are listed in the destination test discovery (no unlisted test files) and pass in CI.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/migration/ctl-photo.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Check-migration map row 'photo/crop tests reading `Product.fs`' updated in this revision: each of the three `crop-queue.test.mjs` tests and the `photo-selection.test.mjs` multiple-faces-sentence case is paired with its named TS test (`crop.test.ts` / `photo.test.ts`) protecting the same behaviour; the classic files are not listed as active tests in the destination.

title: Set one absolute lease state directory per machine shared by both repositories
description:

title: Inventory surfaces, hosting, staging and native paths; set the hosting boundary
description:
## Goal
Give every release surface an owner and a retained or rebuildable input before migration starts, name every hosting binding, credential and publisher so domain handover can remove API-only resources and keep shared ones, protect the paths that model staging and the self-host distribution still read so wind-down never drops them, list native paths for retirement, capture dated visual references before the old hosts disappear, and decide which hosting files become `packages/cloudflare-model-host` and which stay in the application's `hosting/`. Read-only; makes no remote changes.

## Scope
- **Surfaces** (read at the frozen import revision, not only `b2d945a`; a surface added later gets its own row with the commit that added it): candidate app (`src/Next/`), hosted runtime overlay (`hosting/next-static/runtime-overlay/manifest.json`), second runtime origin `models.facemorph.me` (classic `hosting/next-mirror/` since `6107f80`; pages on `*.facemorph.me` alternate chunk retries with it; owner hosting, deploy/warm owner deploy), model/catalogue/diagnostics hosts, legacy production, names site, self-host Compose, research tree, desktop/native leftovers. Per surface: owner workstream, moving paths, consumers (code, workflows, scripts, Workers), build/worker URLs, persistent identities (OPFS/Cache Storage keys, IndexedDB stores, recovery envelopes schema-1 PNG and schema-2 PNG/WebP, MP4 project metadata, runtime manifest digests, catalogue identities), source revision and live receipt. Map remaining browser/research consumers of classic's Fable/Webpack build wrappers. Legacy production's deployed revision stays an explicit uncertainty in its own row.
- **Dated visual references**: read-only screenshots of legacy production `https://facemorph.me` (two face inputs, per-input Browse Names, the embedded picker with its dark "Select an Image" header and X, the retirement notice), `https://names.facemorph.me` (gapless labelled grid) and the current `https://next.facemorph.me` main page, each at 390 px and 1,280 px. PNGs stored outside Git (R2 or a release asset, same store as the control artifact) with a committed manifest `visual-references.json` (URL, viewport, ISO timestamp, served artifact identity read at capture: build id or HTML digest, PNG sha256). The only durable copy face controls and the names picker can compare against.
- **Hosting**: per hostname (Vercel legacy production from `master`; Cloudflare Pages/Workers/R2 for next.facemorph.me; runtime overlay staging; `models.facemorph.me`: Worker over R2 `facemorph-runtime-mirror`, service binding `SITE` to the next.facemorph.me Worker, origin hard-coded `https://next.facemorph.me/`, deployed and warmed by a `next-site.yml` step; model chunks; names catalogue and previews/latents on two public Workers; diagnostics collector `hosting/next-cloudflare/`; Triton/encoder/API processes, tunnels/proxies and DNS for `api.facemorph.me` and `checkface.facemorph.me`; `metrics.facemorph.me` Grafana and the Prometheus on triton holding the old API counters (5-year retention) plus the `/stats/v1` statistics Worker and its `facemorph_web` scrape job) record DNS records, Pages/Workers/route bindings, origin process/host, publisher, owner account. Per credential: name, scope, consumer, API-only or shared (never values). Per publisher: workflow/job → Worker/Pages project/R2 path (incl. mirror deploy-and-warm), trigger, credential names. Classify every resource API-only / shared (model/names/diagnostics/runtime origins, statistics Worker, Grafana, triton Prometheus and the triton machine as a development worker) / app. `models.facemorph.me`, its bucket, binding and deploy credentials are shared (kept at API retirement); it copies from next.facemorph.me, so what next serves after the candidate-source handover decides what the copy can fill on first request (content-addressed paths; a path no longer served is available only if already held).
- **Protected paths** `inventory/protected-paths.json` (path, reader, owner workstream, move-or-keep): every path read by staging (`hosting/next/`, `hosting/next-static/` incl. `runtime-overlay/`, `mirror-runtime.py`, `restage-runtime.py`), the second-origin deploy (`hosting/next-mirror/` and its deploy-and-warm step), conversion inputs, the self-host build (`self-host/**`, frontend pin `0abb215`), with the reading script; `experiment/` is not deleted nor production weights moved without this list. External model sources (author hosts, mirrors): URL, size, digest, terms; provenance/history-transfer needs per path.
- **Native retirement list**: `desktop/` (packaging, `prepare-release.mjs` updater endpoint, `packaging.test.mjs`), three `desktop-*.yml` workflows, consumers; shared browser dependencies to retain/re-home (`desktop/runtime.mjs`: imported by `product-bridge.mjs`, hashed by `scripts/build-next.cjs`; `desktop/scripts/verify-web-artifact.py`: browser/E2E workflows); installed-client/update-feed references and where they point; classic GitHub Releases carrying native installers or updater manifests (tag, asset names and sizes, whether `prepare-release.mjs` or an installed client's feed reads them) via a read-only `gh release list/view` script. Disposition per item: retire / re-home shared check / keep as history; release assets preserved, release text marked historical by the wind-down publisher stage; clients never redirected into the fresh repository.
- **Hosting boundary**: per file/function, destination `packages/cloudflare-model-host` (chunking, manifest generation, digest-consistent publication, header contract, mirror serving) or `hosting/` (frontend staging, promotion, collector, catalogue pipeline, domain attach, analytics) or historical, with reason, as an assignment table in the package README skeleton that deploy re-homing reads. title: Write the candidate known-defect and declared-change ledger
description:
## Background
Two sources: the operated check of the live candidate on 18 October (headless Chromium, real pointer and touch, 390/1,024/1,280/1,920 px; defects 1-3) and the candidate audit of 18 October (`docs/findings/candidate-audit-2026-10-18.md`; defects 4-23, "source" means read in code, not run). They are candidate defects: repair rows graded against the specification at the flow-matrix freeze, never frozen as parity, and the port must not copy them. Declared changes (also repair rows, not parity): crop-loop repair, static names, provider/WebGL removal, control/progress changes, native retirement.

Defect list with the owner workstream (lead bead as of polish round 1; confirm by plan key):
1. Remove control unclickable (library button style wins; control 32x32 at (201,611) under a 376x376 image at (206,229); real click opens Change mode). Owner: face controls (`face.remove-undo-startover` fm-id4c); early edit `delivery.edit-remove-control` (fm-ent).
2. More than two faces do not fit (third tile cut off at 1,280 px; sideways strip with no cue; ~7,000 px page on phone at 14 faces). Owner: `face.many-face-layout` (fm-ifkk).
3. No bulk remove or reset; last face never removable. Owner: fm-id4c (Undo/Start over is a planner proposal, see below).
4. Tab skips Change mode, Browse names, Choose photo. Owner: `face.keyboard-pass` (fm-agfy).
5. No `autocapitalize=off` on the text field; "hello" becomes "Hello", a different face. Owner: face controls; early edit `delivery.edit-capitalisation` (fm-pea).
6. Identical neighbours (and A, B, A) fail with the generic project error. Owner: `morph.neighbour-rule` (fm-nc0p).
7. Add face disabled at one face. Owner: face controls (`ws:face`).
8. Typed word with no instant picture shows "Drop a photo, or tap to choose". Owner: `face.tile-states` (fm-25um).
9. Words lost on reload ("Restored face"). Owner: `media.session-words` (fm-5hww) — planner proposal, operator may veto.
10. Download sizes disagree (149 MB / 1.1 GB / 1.2 GB vs 158 MB / 1,040 MB). Owner: acquisition consent (`ws:consent`).
11. Privacy text incomplete (per-keystroke seed previews from a `workers.dev` host, analytics beacon, 3.4 MB name list on first keystroke; saved files carry the exact latent). Owners: `names.no-keystroke-requests` (fm-96if), `diag.privacy-text` (fm-kjjv).
12. "Send report" turns standing reporting on; "Send this report" sends once (source). Owner: `diag.toast-consent-fix` (fm-b7mt).
13. Photo-selection reports use an action the collector rejects; one bad event drops the batch (source). Owner: `diag.typed-failure-causes` (fm-imm9).
14. Names dialog text contrast 1.18:1; failed name list leaves an empty dialog. Owner: `names.picker-ui` (fm-yhj9).
15. Offline new face fails ("The local generation engine stopped."); every job re-fetches the manifest. Owner: `opctl.offline` (fm-szxh) — stating what works offline is required; the no-network cached job is a planner proposal.
16. First visit stacks two toasts; one covers Create morph. Owner: fm-b7mt.
17. Stale completions: removing a generating face does not stop its job; saved-MP4 drop can leave Morph queued and replaces faces without asking; photo replacement destroys the face first; cancelling a queued re-generate can break the image (source). Owner: application operation controller (`opctl.cancellation` fm-6bch).
18. 64-face cap enforced in one of three places (source). Owner: face controls (`ws:face`).
19. 32 MB video-fallback download outside consent; gate lets work start when sizes are unknown (source). Owner: `ws:consent`.
20. Copy: "about 1 seconds", "smaller than25 MB" + two more missing spaces, seed placeholder "Just type anything", cold-device estimate text unreachable, disabled Create morph looks enabled, transparent crop panel in light mode (source). Owner: face controls; the one-string parts join the early edit `delivery.edit-typos` (fm-olp).
21. Licence/notices page linked from nowhere and misstates the codec host (source). Owner: `provider.guidance-copy` (fm-gbdt).
22. Nothing shows or clears stored data; faces store unbounded (source). Owner: `media.storage-clear` (fm-8keo) — planner proposal, operator may veto.
23. Preview faces look like generated faces (source). Already decided: no badge; owner none; listed so it is a choice.

## Why
The flow-matrix freeze grades these as repair rows against the specification, never as parity; owners need one table to cite.

## Scope
- One row per defect/declared change: id, evidence class (operated/source), the port must…, owner workstream and lead bead id, whether it joins the early candidate edit set (1, 5 and the one-string parts of 20), and decision status: `required`, `planner proposal — operator may veto` (3's Undo/Start over, 9, 15's no-network job, 22), or `decided` (23).
- Rows for the four open audit questions (old text/seed links, autoplay, plain 50/50 blend, cropper extras) marked `open — candidate behaviour kept until answered`, each linking its `docs/decisions/` open entry (written by `identity.decision-log`, fm-orh) and its owner.
- Link the findings note `docs/findings/candidate-audit-2026-10-18.md` and the decision-log entries.
- Machine-readable copy (`inventory/defect-ledger.json`) so `migration.flow-matrix-drive` and `verify.flows-matrix` can load rows by id.

## Out of scope
Fixing defects; answering open questions.

## Considerations
Not reproduced: a legacy Universal Analytics tag (record as not reproduced). Decided and unchanged: the names picker drops search/header/Close/Show more for a floating Back on touch (record the loss of search as a choice).

A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Turn off capitalisation and correction on the candidate text field
description:
## Background
Edits to the candidate source are ordinary work on the working candidate and need no separate approval (operator, 18 October). They are made on a non-deploying classic branch (e.g. `delivery/candidate-edits`) branched from `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, and merged only after the ordinary qualification via `delivery.candidate-edits-merge`, because the candidate branch publishes to next.facemorph.me on every qualified push. Run commands in `facemorph.me-classic` per its development guide. Defect 5: the text field lacks `autocapitalize=off` (classic sets it). A phone keyboard turns 'hello' into 'Hello', a different face because text is hashed exactly; picked names fill in lowercase.

## Why
Phone users get a different face than they intended.

## Scope
- Set `autocapitalize="off"`, `autocorrect="off"`, `spellcheck="false"` (and `autocomplete="off"` if consistent with classic) on the main text field in the candidate source.
- Never trim or normalise text.

## Out of scope
Monorepo text field (face controls).

## Considerations
If the attribute lives in F# (`Product.fs`) the edit is there; the change is one attribute set.

- [ ] Operated UI acceptance: real pointer and real touch at the control's visible position, with an `elementFromPoint` assertion that the hit element is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role clicks only for setup; repeating controls exercised at 1, 2, 3, many and the cap; text inputs with empty, very long and pasted values; a phone-width (390 px) and a desktop-width (1,280 px) screenshot per case.
- [ ] DOM attributes asserted; empty, very long and pasted values are kept byte-exact (hash of typed text equals hash of the field value); phone-emulated input of 'hello' yields the same face identity as a desktop 'hello'.

title: Freeze preflight evidence, estimate and consent-cost types and budgets
description:
## Background

A model-free preflight reads capabilities and actual WebGPU adapter/features/limits, WASM/SIMD/
threading and coarse CPU/memory hints, and may run a short worker WASM sample and small WebGPU compute
sample. Design budgets: about two seconds of sampling, five-second UI deadline, at most 16 MiB scratch
buffers, at most 100 KiB compressed checker code. Route state before real-model checks is "eligible;
model check pending". Generator and encoder admission are separate.

## Why

Device check and estimates, consent copy and the support table need shared evidence/estimate types.

## Scope

- Evidence types: capability facts, unknown vs failed, sample results with completion (not submission)
  times, warmup/compilation distinguished; outcomes skip/timeout/GPU loss → "no reliable estimate".
- Estimate types: ranges per stage (photo preprocessing, e4e per confirmed crop, synthesis per output,
  model load/check, video export) with calibration scope (checkpoint/resolution, provider/runtime,
  thread mode, workload) and source class (recent actual-device, calibrated local check, comparable device).
- Separate generator/encoder admission; consent screen rows (missing bytes, download range, use range
  or unknown), cold/warm costs, material-cost change requiring revised consent.
- Budgets above as named constants for fake-timer tests.

## Typed outputs (citable)

Draft first under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`, then moved by the milestone type-test bead to the module below. Exported names are stable: downstream beads cite them; a rename needs a contract revision and an update of the `contracts.md` export index.

- `apps/web/src/contracts/preflight.ts`: `PreflightEvidence`, `CapabilityFact` (`known` | `unknown` | `failed`), `SampleResult` (completion time, warmup/compile separated), `PreflightOutcome` (`ok` | `skip` | `timeout` | `gpu-lost`; the last three map to "no reliable estimate"), `RouteEligibility` ("eligible; model check pending"), `StageEstimate` (range per stage with `CalibrationScope` and `EstimateSourceClass`), `AdmissionSplit` (generator, encoder), `ConsentCostRow` (missing bytes, download range, use range or unknown; cold/warm), `MaterialCostChange`.
- `PREFLIGHT_BUDGETS`: `samplingMs: 2000`, `uiDeadlineMs: 5000`, `scratchBytes: 16 MiB`, `checkerCodeBytesCompressed: 100 KiB`.
- Consumers: `device.checker`, `device.calibration`, `device.estimate-copy`, `consent.*`, `build.support-table-schema` (evidence classes).

## Out of scope

Checker implementation and calibration (device check workstream).

## Considerations

Device scores stay local under diagnostics consent. A synthetic check never establishes full-model success.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts.md` preflight section and draft types; each budget is a named constant with its unit.
- [ ] Walkthrough: unknown memory, no adapter, timeout, and eligible GPU all produce typed states without any model-asset reference.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Every name listed under "Typed outputs (citable)" exists in the draft type file and has a row in the `contracts.md` export index naming its consumers.
notes: Anchor: PLAN.md#lightweight-device-check-and-pre-download-guidance.

title: Typed facade over the bridge and its real-bridge harness
description:
## Goal
Build the strict-TS typed facade over the retained candidate bridge, the seam both the TS/React port and compute extraction build on, prove it at runtime through the real bridge with real runtime bytes, on top of the bridge that `migration.project-json` made loadable (its ProjectJson TS port and one-line import swap were split out in the 24 October final pass). A facade proven only by `tsc` says nothing about runtime behaviour; the harness catches signature/semantic drift before the port and compute extraction rely on it. Unblocks compute extraction, the operation controller and the controller port; second position in the mandatory shared-file order.

## Scope
- Facade: strict TS discriminated-union types and a facade module covering every bridge export the UI uses (execute/subscribe/cancel, save/share/export/import project, downloads subscribe/consent, photo preview/crop/select/choose-detected, names load/public preview, restore last result, queue/cancel face, invalidate face/morph, report/debug consent, slider frames, measured timings, source version/issue URL). Typed against contracts milestone 1 (operation signatures, loaded-handle types). Retained-candidate adapters; no extracted packages.
- Runtime validation of untrusted payloads crossing the boundary; no `any` at the boundary except validated `unknown` inputs.
- Source map (classic `b2d945a8` or the frozen import revision; re-check line numbers with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`): `Product.fs` lines 29-213 import about 60 functions: `product-bridge.mjs` (`loadNames`, `publicPreview`, `drawFace`, `execute`, `subscribe`, `cancel`, `saveMedia`, `shareMedia`, `exportProject`, `importProject`, `measuredFaceMs`, `measuredFrameMs`, `measuredVideoMs`, `jobProgress`, `sliderFrames`, `rememberView`, `plannedFrames`, `stagedReportCount`, `reportReference`, `cancelPhotoRun`, `setDebug`, `sendReportOnce`, `consentAnswered`, `subscribeDownloads`, `downloadModels`, `consentToDownload`, `sourceVersion`, `issueUrl`, `restoreLastResult`, `rememberSourcePhoto`, `sourcePhotoUrl`, `queueFace`, `cancelQueuedFace`, `chooseDetectedFace`, `invalidateArrivalRestore`, `photoRevision`, `invalidateFace`, `invalidateMorph`, `checkCachedFace`, `displayMilestone`, `previewPhotoReported`, `cropPhotoReported`, `selectPhotoReported`, `warmPhotoTools`), `last-result.mjs` (`sliderPreference`, `sliderPosition`, `rememberSlider`), `scheduler.mjs` (`nextScheduled`), `estimate.mjs` (`createEstimator`, `describeMs`, `describeMeasuredMs`, `isSlowJob`), `photo/crop-view.mjs` (`createCrop`, `pan`, `zoomTo`, `rotate`, `rect`, `frame`, `resizeViewport`), `photo-selection.mjs` (`photoFiles`, `openPhotoPicker`, `dragPhoto`, `invalidatePhotoSelections`, `focusCropArea`, `openNamesFocus`, `closeNamesFocus`, `namesKey`), `photo/align-photo.mjs` (`MULTIPLE_FACES_MESSAGE`). Record shapes: `Input`, `Face`, `PublicPreview`, `NameFace`, `Progress`, `Output`, `Request` (lines 15-27), `Downloads` (84). A list of these imports generated once in the PR is the coverage checklist.
- Replace the classic Fable-dependent check `scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs` (walked `.fs.js` files; exists because webpack bundled a missing bridge export as `undefined`, which in R2-15 shipped a dead photo path, `selectPhoto is not a function`). Successor `apps/web/scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs` checks every name the facade imports from a hand-written module (including `export *` barrels) is exported there; wired into CI here; strict `tsc` resolution makes the same failure a compile error.
- Bridge text-evaluating tests (`src/Next/fresh-review.test.mjs`, `src/Next/estimate.test.mjs`, which strip `import` lines with `plain()` and run under `node:vm`) and `scripts/check-progress-copy.mjs` keep passing unchanged.
- Headless harness: Playwright `apps/web/test/harness/facade.spec.ts` loads the facade against the real bridge and runtime bytes (candidate `src/Next/browser/runtime-test.html` and `serve-local.py` with production-style headers are the starting point; runtime bytes from the digest-checked immutable runtime mirror/overlay). Steps: cpu-name, cpu-seed, cancel-mid-run, photo-preview-crop-encode (CPU where admitted), save-face, export-short-morph, restore-last, downloads-subscription, report-staging. Assert typed events/outputs and resource settlement after cancel. Required CI check for facade/bridge changes.

## Out of scope
- Changing bridge behaviour (the one-line ProjectJson swap is `migration.project-json`); moving compute/model I/O; React components; UI parity.
- ProjectJson port and its round-trip goldens (`migration.project-json`).
- Dynamic-shape recovery schema versioning (media and recovery).
- GPU lanes (run where a GPU worker is available under the shared device lease, otherwise reported untested).

## Notes
- Shared-file order (16/17 October): `product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs`, `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited provider simplification -> typed facade -> compute extraction -> confirmed-crop fix -> morph pipeline -> static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics reporting rebinding. This bead follows the provider code-editing beads (`provider.native`, `provider.webgl`, `provider.route-admission`) and `migration.project-json` (the one-line swap), and precedes compute extraction. It does not wait for the phone CPU check or post-removal verification (`provider.admission`, evidence); a shared-file fix they find lands as a provider follow-up on top, never reordering or reverting the facade.
- Keep facade changes apart from engine changes in each revision. This row edits no shared bridge/runtime/worker file.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-migration; #package-and-operation-contracts; #workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership; #workspace-build-and-artifact-identity (Fable project qualification seam).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` strict passes; no `any` at the facade boundary except validated `unknown` inputs.
- [x] Type-level tests for each union; validator tests reject malformed payloads.
- [x] Coverage checklist: every import in `Product.fs` lines 29-213 maps to one typed facade export (shown in the PR); `check-bridge-imports.mjs` and strict `tsc` enforce it afterwards.
- [x] `apps/web/scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs` fails on a fixture facade importing a non-exported name and passes on the real facade; a deliberately missing bridge export fails both it and `tsc --noEmit`.
- [x] `fresh-review.test.mjs`, `estimate.test.mjs` and `check-progress-copy.mjs` pass unchanged; the retired `scripts/check-bridge-imports.mjs` (`.fs.js` walker) is listed in `tests/retired.txt` with its successor.
- [x] Facade harness passes on CPU in CI against the imported runtime bytes (digests checked); each step reports its settled-resource check; the cancel case shows no late result and released workers.
- [x] Traces and screenshots kept on failure; unit tests listed in test discovery and pass locally with the CI command; CI verifies after push.
- [x] required statuses green (with fm-7ge). If fm-7ge has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-7ge (`br update fm-7ge --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-7ge
- [x] Repair main40189678136 controller-photo transition timeout after Encode source/confirmation migration; execute real CPU queued-crop, cancellation, encode and recovery Save/reopen journey without weakening assertions.

- 24 October final pass: the ProjectJson port, its `MaxControls = 64` note and the one-line bridge swap moved to `migration.project-json`.

Harness incorrectly awaited the retired preconfirmation Gate after PickPhoto; now waits actual Crop/CropQueue, exercises CropAdjust/cancel/Use before confirmation and retains every queued/cancel/CPU encode/recovery assertion. Added explicit no gate/job/input replacement before confirmation, cancelled source unchanged, editor blocks confirmation and exact proposal restored on cancellation. Real targeted CI command FACEMORPH_REQUIRE_RUNTIME=1 node --test --test-name-pattern=^controller-photo: --test-timeout=1200000 test/e2e/facade.e2e.ts passed1/1 in91s, all301 runtime pins verified; /tmp/pearli-pia9-fixed-real.log. title: Freeze host and converter manifest compatibility and metadata validation
description:
## Background

`cloudflare-model-host` generates manifests and serves digest-consistent chunks; `model-conv`
produces manifest/digest/shape metadata; the manager consumes them. Untrusted manifest, metadata and
worker values arrive as `unknown` and must be validated at runtime. The candidate's runtime manifest
(`hosting/next-static/runtime-overlay/manifest.json`) carries kernel provenance and phone-admission
facts such as `encoderStream.phoneAdmitted:true` and a 268,435,456-byte e4e WASM limit.

## Why

Conversion, hosting and the manager must agree on one schema with explicit version rejection.

## Scope

- Manifest schema and version field; rejection of unknown/newer major versions with a typed error.
- Metadata schema/version rejection for recovery envelopes; never follow model URLs from a file.
- Keep weights out of package tarballs and private source provenance out of published manifests.
- Generators, optional photo encoder and preprocessing identities kept separate.
- Runtime validators for every `unknown` boundary (manifest, metadata, worker payload).

## Typed outputs (citable)

Draft first under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`, then moved by the milestone type-test bead to the module below. Exported names are stable: downstream beads cite them; a rename needs a contract revision and an update of the `contracts.md` export index.

- `packages/browser-model-manager/src/contracts/manifest.ts`: `ModelManifestV1`, `MANIFEST_SCHEMA_MAJOR`, `parseModelManifest(unknown)` → `Result<ModelManifestV1, ManifestError>` (unknown/newer major rejected), `RuntimeManifest` (kernel provenance: candidate ID and source hash; `encoderStream.phoneAdmitted`; e4e WASM limit 268,435,456 bytes), `AssetIdentity` (generator, optional photo encoder and preprocessing identities kept separate).
- `packages/browser-model-manager/schema/model-manifest.v1.schema.json`: the producer-facing schema. The manager (reader, runs in browsers) owns it; `cloudflare-model-host` and `model-conv` emit manifests that their own tests validate against it (dev-dependency only; no runtime dependency from manager to host or converter).
- Consumers: `hosting.chunk-manifest`, `conversion.package`, `manager.split`, `deploy.promotion` (kernel provenance check).

## Out of scope

Model descriptor details for non-face models (m2 descriptor item), beyond fields needed now.

## Considerations

Preserve descriptor/content identities during any rename (WebGL coefficient assets also feed direct WebGPU).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts.md` manifest section and draft schema/type with version rules.
- [ ] The candidate's current manifest validates against the schema (recorded fixture), and a deliberately newer-version fixture is rejected in the walkthrough.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Every name listed under "Typed outputs (citable)" exists in the draft type file and has a row in the `contracts.md` export index naming its consumers.

title: Rendering port: Vite app shell, theme, header/footer and worker bundling
description:
## Background
The candidate view root (`view`, `Product.fs` ~1193) wraps `App.ThemedApp` with header/topline/tagline, preview strip (`.next-preview-strip*`), faces area, morph and video slots, explain/FAQ, debug area and the classic-style footer (`.next-footer*`, version line, logo). Shared F# pieces `Config`, `FancyButton`, `Logos`, `ThemedApp`, `header` are read in classic as specification. `src/index.html`, styles and public assets are imported by ws:import.

## Why
Vite is the only bundler from the first app build; the shell is the frame every per-screen component mounts into.

## Scope
- `apps/web` Vite + React entry, MUI theme equivalent to `ThemedApp`, header/topline/tagline, preview strip, footer with source version (`sourceVersion`) and issue links (`issueUrl`).
- Bundler-emitted app workers (`image-encoder-worker.mjs`, `video-worker.mjs`, bridge workers) bundled and tracked separately from manifest-pinned hosted runtime workers/modules.
- `product-ux.scss` carried and compiled.

## Out of scope
Production headers and `deploy-next/` replacement (`migration.ren-build-deploy` with ws:build.m2).

## Considerations
Keep the `.next-*` DOM/class contract and carry `product-ux.scss`. MUI v4->v9 pixel differences are reviewed and recorded, not gated; anything that hides, overlaps or mislabels a control is a defect. Defects frozen as repair rows are not reproduced: where carrying candidate CSS would reproduce one (defect 1: MUI button style out-ranks the Remove close-button rule so it renders below the image, invisible, over the mode menu), carry the stylesheet's intended placement and leave the operated repair acceptance to the owner (face controls).

## Source map (classic, read-only, classic `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (or the frozen import revision recorded in `inventory.md`; re-check line numbers there with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`))
`Product.fs` `view` 1193-1468: root `main.facemorph-page.next-product` with `data-next-busy` and background drag/drop handlers (1194-1199); preview strip `aside.next-preview-strip` with lead text and links Classic facemorph.me / Its server is retiring / Report an issue (`issueUrl state.Route`) (~1200-1208); `App.header` (~1223) and tagline `p.next-tagline` (~1224); `next-faces-area` with `data-next-faces` (~1236); footer `next-footer`/`next-footer-inner`/`next-footer-text`/`next-footer-version`/`next-footer-logo` (1454-1468). Shared F#: `src/App.fs` `header` (line 277) and `ThemedApp` (line 375), `src/Config.fs`, `src/FancyButton.fs`, `src/Logos.fs`. Styles: `src/Next/product-ux.scss`. Program wiring: `src/Index.fs` (`withReactSynchronous "elmish-app"` mount id).
The preview-strip copy and links are retirement/preview chrome: their final wording is a declared change owned by domain handover (`domain.copy-inventory`); port them as in the control for parity and do not invent replacements.

## Goldens and grading (polish r1)
- **Golden store.** Goldens are the recorder output chosen by `migration.golden-spike` (reducer transitions or journey-step DOM/state snapshots), committed under `apps/web/test/goldens/control/<flow-row-id>/` with a `goldens.json` index naming the control `deploy-next/` SHA-256, the recorder command and, per step, the freeze class of its row. Replays run `scripts/fetch-control.mjs` first and refuse to run if the index digest differs from `control-artifact.json`.
- **Parity rows** (freeze class *present and unchanged*): the port's transitions/DOM must equal the golden exactly (state fields, emitted effect descriptions, text, flow order, round-trip bytes). No tolerance, no "close enough".
- **Repair rows** (candidate defects 1-23) and **declared-change rows**: never parity. The recorder tags their steps `repair:<n>` or `declared:<section>` and the replay lists them as owner-graded instead of asserting them. No test in this repository may encode a candidate defect as expected output. Where the defect lives entirely in what this leaf writes (a string, a CSS rule order, a label), write the specification's version; where the repair needs the owner's design or copy, carry the nearest candidate behaviour without asserting it and leave the repair, and its grading against the plan specification, to the named owner.
- **Absent rows** are specification-graded by their owners after parity; this leaf adds no behaviour for them.
- A row the recorder cannot exercise is listed `untested` with the reason, never passed.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Vite dev and production builds succeed; emitted worker graph listed and checked for completeness.
- [ ] Shell DOM classes match the control at the parity rows for header/footer.
- [ ] UI acceptance is operated: real pointer/touch input at each control's visible position plus an `elementFromPoint` check that the element there is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role clicks only for setup; repeating controls exercised at 0 or 1, 2, 3, many and the cap; text inputs with empty, very long and pasted values; phone-width and desktop-width screenshot per case.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic are listed in the destination test discovery (no unlisted test files) and pass in CI.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/migration/ren-vite-shell.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Typed facade: strict-TS declarations and adapters over the retained bridge
description:
## Background
`Product.fs` lines ~29-213 import about 60 functions from `product-bridge.mjs`, `last-result.mjs`, `scheduler.mjs`, `estimate.mjs`, `photo/crop-view.mjs`, `photo-selection.mjs`, `photo/align-photo.mjs` with untyped records (`Input`, `Face`, `Output`, `Request`, `Progress`, `Downloads`, `NameFace`, `PublicPreview`). Contracts milestone 1 freezes operation signatures and loaded-handle types.

## Why
The facade is the typed seam both the TS/React port and compute extraction build on. Compute extraction needs only this milestone.

## Scope
- Strict TS discriminated-union types and a facade module covering every bridge export the UI uses (execute/subscribe/cancel, save/share/export/import project, downloads subscribe/consent, photo preview/crop/select/choose-detected, names load/public preview, restore last result, queue/cancel face, invalidate face/morph, report/debug consent, slider frames, measured timings, source version/issue URL).
- Runtime validation of untrusted payloads crossing the boundary.
- Retained-candidate adapters (no extracted packages yet); typed against contracts milestone 1.
- Swap the bridge's `ProjectJson.fs.js` import to the TS module from `migration.ctl-projectjson`.

## Out of scope
Changing bridge behaviour; moving compute/model I/O; React components.

## Considerations
Shared-file serialization (decided 16/17 October): `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in the order provider simplification -> typed facade -> compute extraction -> confirmed-crop fix -> morph pipeline -> static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics reporting rebinding. Add any file this item edits to the check-migration map's conflict list. This item is the "typed facade" position in that order. It follows provider simplification's code-editing leaves: `provider.native-retirement` (fm-be10), `provider.webgl-removal` (fm-ybbi) and `provider.admission` (fm-ezub). Each of those verifies its own edit (canaries, verifier, admission tests). It precedes compute extraction. It does not wait for `provider.acceptance` (fm-dr4c) or `provider.phone-cpu-check` (fm-8dt2), because those are evidence across lanes, not shared-file edits. If they turn up a fix in a shared file, it lands as a provider follow-up revision on top of whatever has merged; it never reorders or reverts the facade (polish r2). Keep facade changes apart from engine changes in each revision.

## Source map (classic, read-only, classic `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (or the frozen import revision recorded in `inventory.md`; re-check line numbers there with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`))
`Product.fs` lines 29-213 declare the imports the facade must type. By module: `product-bridge.mjs` (`loadNames`, `publicPreview`, `drawFace`, `execute`, `subscribe`, `cancel`, `saveMedia`, `shareMedia`, `exportProject`, `importProject`, `measuredFaceMs`, `measuredFrameMs`, `measuredVideoMs`, `jobProgress`, `sliderFrames`, `rememberView`, `plannedFrames`, `stagedReportCount`, `reportReference`, `cancelPhotoRun`, `setDebug`, `sendReportOnce`, `consentAnswered`, `subscribeDownloads`, `downloadModels`, `consentToDownload`, `sourceVersion`, `issueUrl`, `restoreLastResult`, `rememberSourcePhoto`, `sourcePhotoUrl`, `queueFace`, `cancelQueuedFace`, `chooseDetectedFace`, `invalidateArrivalRestore`, `photoRevision`, `invalidateFace`, `invalidateMorph`, `checkCachedFace`, `displayMilestone`, `previewPhotoReported`, `cropPhotoReported`, `selectPhotoReported`, `warmPhotoTools`), `last-result.mjs` (`sliderPreference`, `sliderPosition`, `rememberSlider`), `scheduler.mjs` (`nextScheduled`), `estimate.mjs` (`createEstimator`, `describeMs`, `describeMeasuredMs`, `isSlowJob`), `photo/crop-view.mjs` (`createCrop`, `pan`, `zoomTo`, `rotate`, `rect`, `frame`, `resizeViewport`), `photo-selection.mjs` (`photoFiles`, `openPhotoPicker`, `dragPhoto`, `invalidatePhotoSelections`, `focusCropArea`, `openNamesFocus`, `closeNamesFocus`, `namesKey`), `photo/align-photo.mjs` (`MULTIPLE_FACES_MESSAGE`). Record shapes to type: `Input`, `Face`, `PublicPreview`, `NameFace`, `Progress`, `Output`, `Request` (lines 15-27) and `Downloads` (84). A generated list of these imports is the facade's coverage checklist.

## The ProjectJson import swap and the unresolved-import list (polish r2)
- This leaf edits exactly one line of the retained bridge for ProjectJson. `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` line 9, `import {decode,encode} from './ProjectJson.fs.js';`, becomes an import of the TS module from `migration.ctl-projectjson` (`apps/web/src/project/project-json.ts`, with an explicit `.ts` extension so Node 24 type stripping and the test runner resolve it). The bridge keeps the names `decode` and `encode`, and nothing else in the bridge changes in that revision.
- That import was the single entry in the unresolved-import list, recorded by `inventory.import-allowlist` (fm-hyw) and run by `import.checks` (fm-1sg) as `unresolved-imports.mjs` (owner fm-dtmm, swap point here). After the swap, the expected list is empty and the script's allowed-entries config is emptied in the same revision, so any unresolved specifier fails CI from then on.
- The tests that evaluate the bridge as text (`src/Next/fresh-review.test.mjs`, `src/Next/estimate.test.mjs`, which strip `import` lines with `plain()` and run under `node:vm`) and `scripts/check-progress-copy.mjs` keep passing unchanged.
- `check-bridge-imports.mjs` was recorded `not applicable until the port`. That map row closes here: the successor script from fm-dtmm is wired into CI, and strict `tsc` resolution over the facade fails on any facade import the bridge does not export.

description:
## Background

title: Extend identity hashing and add the retired-tests CI check
description:
## Goal

Make every app and package edit change build/snapshot identity and select its required checks, and make it impossible to lose protected coverage silently: removing or renaming a listed test fails CI unless `tests/retired.txt` names its replacement or the plan change that made it obsolete, disabled tests and inherited encoded-image hash assertions are caught, and the stale `next-matrix` harness is repaired against the declared controls. This replaces the earlier check-migration map document with CI checks.

## Scope

**Identity hashing**
- Start from candidate tooling: `scripts/build-next.cjs` (hashes sources incl. `desktop/runtime.mjs`), `scripts/check-tests-listed.mjs`, bridge/progress/artifact checks, test server/stage/restage paths.
- Include `apps/web` and every package (sources, lockfile entries, configs) in build/snapshot identity; record the exact required test invocation in identity.
- Worker completeness: bundler-emitted app workers and manifest-pinned hosted runtime workers/modules (transitive imports, WASM/codec/photo siblings, URLs) are enumerated and hashed separately; changed emitted runtime bytes require updated matching pins.
- Artifact identity carries source repository ID, commit, workflow/run and build identity. `deploy-next/` initially holds the pinned control artifact, labelled control with classic's identity; the ported Vite build later records its own commit/build identity plus import provenance. Never present the classic commit as this repository's deploy source.

**Retired-tests check**
- Extend `scripts/check-tests-listed.mjs` to cover new test roots (`apps/web`, packages) so discovery cannot silently drop a file, and to fail when a listed test is removed or renamed unless `tests/retired.txt` names it with its replacement test or the declared plan change.
- `scripts/check-no-disabled-tests.mjs`: fails on `.skip`, `.only`, `test.todo`, `xit`, `describe.skip`, `@pytest.mark.skip`/`skipif` without a reason string, `unittest.skip`, a workflow step with `if: false`, or a test step with `continue-on-error: true`, unless the location carries a reason, owner and removal condition. No blanket disabled suite.
- `scripts/check-image-hash-asserts.mjs`: greps maintained tests for SHA-256/hash comparisons over encoded image or video outputs and fails unless the assertion names its replacement under the synthesis/export rules (raw numerical tolerance, prepared-file reuse or corruption check). Source-language assertions become equivalent TS/schema/operation/built-product checks; numerical, acquisition, cleanup, resource and export-integrity coverage survives; native packaging/parity checks are historical or retired, never substituted for browser checks.

**`next-matrix` repair** (`scripts/next-matrix.mjs`)
- Migrate selectors from the old bulk Generate / post-result Crop controls to the declared product/tester controls of the control artifact.
- `photoE4e` uses an independent metadata-free photo fixture with actual encoder-event checks (a saved recovery-bearing result can bypass e4e and proves nothing).
- Preserve stage coverage: same stage IDs as classic; H.264 and project stages report `incomplete-not-shipped` while those controls are absent, never fabricated passes. The project skip (~lines 164–169, reads `Product.fs`) later reads the TS flag from the project-JSON port.

## Out of scope

Performing provider/UI-owned harness repairs (they land in the owning beads); running the full deployed-origin matrix (build milestone 1); release-consistent asset retention (model hosting); a new benchmark campaign; recovering missing historical raw reports.

## Notes

- Where stale repairs land (each owning bead updates or retires the check in the same revision and uses `tests/retired.txt` when a test goes): `check-next-artifact.sh` `.next-advanced`/WebGL → provider simplification (keep `manifest.webgl` coefficient assets for direct WebGPU); its separate Browse names button → face controls (Browse Names in each face's burger menu); `check-progress-copy.mjs` (JS only: reads `product-bridge.mjs` and `stage-labels.mjs`) runs unchanged until whole-action progress lands (operation controller progress with face-controls morph output); paths re-point with identical expectations when the TS port replaces those files; `crop-queue.test.mjs` (3 tests read `Product.fs`) and the `photo-selection.test.mjs` "multiple-faces sentence is shared" case → controller photo port, retired at golden replay; `check-bridge-imports.mjs` walks generated `.fs.js` that is not in Git — not applicable until the port, replaced by `tsc --noEmit` over the facade plus `unresolved-imports.mjs` reporting zero (classic's separate CI step is vacuous; the real check ran inside `build-next.cjs`); `verify-fable.mjs ProjectJson.fs.js` → project-JSON port (goldens from driving the control with `project-v1.fixture.json`); `browser/runtime.test.mjs` GPU→CPU retry and `route-priors.test.mjs` CPU ordering keep coverage without WebGL; `desktop/scripts/verify-web-artifact.py` re-homed with native retirement. Other `next-site.yml` tests (`scheduler`, `estimate`, `last-result`, `photo-selection` other cases, `fresh-review`, `route-choice`, `testing-link`, `logging`, `route-report`, `reporting`, `stage-labels`) need no repair.
- Classic workflow destinations: `next-site.yml`, `next-e2e.yml`, `next-matrix.yml`, `mobile-browser.yml`, `next-gpu-lane.yml` (build lanes); research workflows (research stage 2); `name-catalogue.yml` (static names); `self-host-build.yml` stays in classic; `deploy.yml` historical; `desktop-*.yml` retired with shared browser checks re-homed.
- Shared-file order: provider simplification → typed facade → compute extraction → confirmed-crop fix → morph pipeline → static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics rebinding (`product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs`, `browser/ort-worker.mjs`, ported UI sources). Build beads change tooling and CI only.
- The retained performance evidence register and no-regression protocol are PLAN.md#retained-performance-evidence-and-no-regression-checks; comparison beads cite that section directly. Research-family accounting (v2 portfolio, negative lessons, backlog) lives with the research provenance map in research stage 1. PLAN.md (newer) replaces the check-migration map with `tests/retired.txt`.
- No worktrees/resets/cleans. Anchors: PLAN.md#workspace-build-and-artifact-identity, #autoresearch-coverage-and-preservation-map, #platform-ci-retention-and-performance-preservation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Editing a file in each package and in `apps/web` changes identity and selects that root's required checks (scripted test per root).
- [x] Altering one byte of an emitted app worker or a hosted runtime sibling without updating its pin fails the identity check; adding an unlisted transitive worker import fails it (fixture tests).
- [x] Identity output for the control artifact (labelled control, classic identity) and for a destination build both include repo ID, commit, workflow/run and build identity.
- [x] Unit tests for `check-tests-listed`: removing or renaming a listed test fails; the same change with a `tests/retired.txt` entry (replacement or plan change) passes; an entry missing a field fails; a new unlisted test file under `apps/web` or a package fails.
- [x] `check-no-disabled-tests.mjs` runs in CI; fixtures `.skip`, `.only`, `@pytest.mark.skip`, `if: false` step and `continue-on-error: true` test step each fail without reason/owner/removal condition and pass with it.
- [x] `check-image-hash-asserts.mjs` runs in CI; a fixture comparing SHA-256 of an encoded WebP output fails until it names its replacement.

title: Parity harness, including performance paths
description:
## Goal
A repeatable, logged comparison of port versus control that later revisions can rerun: the frozen flow matrix through Playwright, the DOM contract, responsive screenshots, project-JSON and recovery round trips, plus the preserved performance paths and retained CI cells (unchanged because the compute path is the same JS). Carry the actual candidate code forward: equal visual output is insufficient if warm reuse, bounded resources, restoration or export reuse are lost.

## Scope
- Runner that re-verifies the control digest, serves control and port with the same runtime bytes, and runs each parity test of the `migration.freeze` spec on both; CI job definition.
- DOM contract diff (`.next-*` classes, ARIA states, text), flow order, screenshots at phone/intermediate/desktop widths (reviewed, not gated; anything that hides, overlaps or mislabels a control fails), project-JSON and recovery round trips (control-written records read by the port and vice versa within the origin).
- Grading: parity tests exact. `changed`/`new`/defect rows are never compared to the control; the harness emits them `owner-graded` with the owner key for integrated verification to grade against the plan. A comparison that would pass only because the port reproduces a candidate defect is a harness bug.
- Every acting step is operated (pointer/touch at the visible position plus `elementFromPoint`); by-name clicks are setup only.
- Performance and retained cells, run with the pinned control and the TS/React milestone build on the same workload/cell. Retained lanes: `next-site.yml` (artifact/qualify/compiled-ui), `next-e2e.yml` real-ui-cpu (actual CPU name/seed and e4e, crop, original reuse, recovered still without inference, GPU refusal/fallback scope, playable/saved MP4, face/video/slider restore), `next-matrix.yml` (Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, macOS WebKit/Firefox), `mobile-browser.yml` (Android emulator 8 components, iOS Simulator components, ios-product), `next-gpu-lane.yml` (GTX1050 evidence, not a gate). Invariants: keyed synthesis admission (one cold canary, deferred rest), `warmMapping()` overlap, bounded 1-4 CPU threads, single-threaded streamed e4e, cache-only worker, warm output hits need no inference, Firefox storage-permission timing, no-third-party gate.
- Comparison method: the shared no-regression protocol in the preservation map (`build.identity-map`, "No-regression comparison protocol"), also used by `verify.not-worse` (fm-mc27), `compute.ported-app` (fm-gwa0) and `ortweb.bump`. Control = pinned candidate artifact by hash (`import.closure` control custody) on the same cell and workload. Record provider/model/runtime, resolution/FPS/frame count, cold/retained/resident/restored state, visible-tab state and the same finish boundary. Protected metrics: first/nth face, confirmed-photo work, complete video, first/repeated Save, restore, no lockups, acquired/output bytes, memory reservations, cancellation. Correctness and resource regressions fail. Timing, byte and memory measures use the strictly-not-worse pass rule (operator, 24 October; PLAN.md #strictly-not-worse-than-the-candidate-operator-24-october-2026): paired ABBA runs, at least 5 pairs per cell, and a measure fails when the 95% interval of the new/control ratio lies entirely above 1 plus the control/control noise margin of that cell (the research evaluator noise baseline if it exists; not waited for; otherwise own control/control pairs). A single hosted-CI timing is never a verdict; an inconclusive cell is reported untested, never passed. The only exception is a deliberate trade recorded in the plan (the first-Save size/time trade below). Encoded-byte differences are size/cost, not image identity; no compensating phone CPU with desktop GPU gains, or 512 px video with 1024 px. If this text and the protocol differ, the protocol wins and the difference is reported.
- Raw synthesis keeps frozen tolerances (RGB max diff 1, raw-float 0.002, e4e 0.0001); encoded bytes may differ.
- Evidence-register rows protected: eris RTX 2080 SUPER, Chromium 152 WebGPU, warm 26-frame morph ABBA×4 (pipeline 129.8->69.7 ms/frame; RGBA8 42.6->37.1 ms/frame; warm face 103.5->75.6 ms), re-run under the shared device lease or reported untested; Ubuntu 24.04 Chrome CPU ABBA×3 repeat original 113.00->88.76 ms and repeat Save 100.72->66.49 ms must not regress (first-Save 108.63->202.17 ms while 4.38 MB->117 KB is an accepted tradeoff); iPhone 16 Pro Simulator iOS 18.5 product job (first full-1024 face 25,287 ms; warm synthesis 4,741.2 ms) through `build.ci-mobile`. Evidence-gap rows (physical iPhones, current Firefox/WebKit full performance, GTX 1050 inference) are untested, never passed.
- Baseline-note items (11 October delivery note at classic `b2d945a8`), each a port-vs-control cell: mobile controls and crop geometry fixes; background WebP retention with PNG fallback; bounded compressed multi-face/video/scrub session recovery without repeated inference; corrected asynchronous retention checks.

## Out of scope
- Running the full matrix for acceptance (`migration.parity`); new benchmark campaigns; physical-iPhone qualification.

## Notes
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-migration (Parity is judged against the control artifact); #platform-ci-retention-and-performance-preservation; #retained-performance-evidence-and-no-regression-checks; #synthesis-correctness-and-export-quality.
