title: Recovered stills beside crop candidates in one batch
description:
## Goal
Multi-file entry must not re-encode saved faces or reject them because a sibling needs unavailable compute. A valid recovered still is staged as a ready candidate beside fresh-photo crop candidates in the same batch view and click sequence, and installed without inference. This is also how a folder of saved faces refills slots quickly (used by the blend view).

## Scope
- Inspect every file's recovery metadata (media's reader: schema-1 PNG, schema-2 PNG/WebP still envelopes) before any target commit; a valid recovered still is one ready candidate in the same selection view and global click sequence as photo candidates.
- Recovered candidates bypass detection, crop adjustment and e4e; batch OK installs them alongside confirmed-photo slots after budget/revision checks, in click order.
- Damaged recovery never silently becomes a photo: omit, or explicit Use as photo. Unknown-model/incompatible recovered stills stay selectable/viewable/saveable with compute disabled.
- Photo operation unavailable: recovered candidates stay selectable; photos are identified unavailable without detector/crop/model work; the recovered subset can be confirmed in click order.
- Budgets: staged recovered assets under the completed-result budget; photos under their byte ceilings.
- Cancel releases staged resources without partial import.
- A single recovered still dropped alone keeps its direct recovery path (no batch view).
- Extends the batch proposal; no other import screen and no change to the locked editor.

## Out of scope
External MP4 opening (deferred by operator, 12 October).

## Notes
- If staging touches `product-bridge.mjs` it is already ordered after the morph pipeline through face.batch; otherwise it edits no shared file.
- Tie-break: the mixed recovered-still and photo batch UI belongs to face controls (PLAN.md#workstream-prerequisites-and-requirement-ownership). Anchor: PLAN.md#gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design (mixed batch).
acceptance_criteria:
Operated rule: real pointer/touch at the visible position with `elementFromPoint`; by-name only for setup; 390 px and 1,280 px, screenshot per case.
- [ ] Recovered R -> photo A2 -> photo B1, omitting a corrupt fourth file: Cancel before OK leaves the project unchanged; then confirm: exact order R, A2, B1 with zero inference/model requests for R (intercepted requests and operation trace).
- [ ] Damaged recovery file offers Use as photo only explicitly; an incompatible-model still is selectable with compute disabled.
- [ ] Photo encoding genuinely refused (WebGPU disabled at launch and the encoder assets absent from the local artifact server): recovered subset confirms; photos show the unavailable reason; zero detector/model requests.
- [ ] Single recovered still dropped alone takes the direct recovery path (no batch view).
- [ ] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test`) and pass.

title: Rebind candidate hosts and routes for production
description:
## Background
Edits to the candidate source are ordinary work on the working candidate and need no separate approval (operator, 18 October). They are made on a non-deploying classic branch (e.g. `delivery/candidate-edits`) branched from `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, and merged only after the ordinary qualification via `delivery.candidate-edits-merge`, because the candidate branch publishes to next.facemorph.me on every qualified push. Run commands in `facemorph.me-classic` per its development guide. For promotion to facemorph.me the candidate's diagnostics collector host, model asset and runtime hosts, names catalogue origin and analytics must resolve for the production origin. Production starts fresh with no cross-origin storage transfer.

## Why
The promoted app must load models, names and send consented diagnostics from facemorph.me.

## Scope
- Configure per-host endpoints (host config, not forked source) for production.
- Record the retained static origins the chosen artifact uses.
- Collector routes accept the production origin.
- Second runtime origin: `runtimeMirror()` in `src/Next/Assets/model-cache.mjs` already maps any `*.facemorph.me` page (incl. facemorph.me) to `https://models.facemorph.me`; confirm its CORS/CORP headers serve the production origin and record that its fill origin stays `https://next.facemorph.me/` (see `domain.action-list` for the warming step).

## Out of scope
Applying the diagnostics retention decision (ws:diag.learnings); changing DNS (action execution).

## Considerations
A production collector needs the retention decision applied with no expiry written.

title: Provide the still-image recovery reader for re-import and mixed batches
description:
## Background
The candidate dispatches dropped/chosen files recovery-first: a valid matching recovered still installs image/latent without model acquisition or encoding (`src/Next/photo-selection.mjs`, bridge recovery paths). Face controls' mixed-batch UI stages recovered stills beside crop candidates and needs a reader that classifies each file before any target commit.

## Why
Recovered/static results must satisfy requests without inference startup, and damaged recovery must never silently become a photo.

## Scope
- `inspectStill(file) -> {kind: 'matching'|'missing'|'damaged'|'incompatible-schema'|'incompatible-model'|'unknown-model', image, latent?, modelIdentity?, reason}` with validated integrity, used by single-file entry, paste and multi-file batches. (Polish r1: `not-recovery` renamed `missing` and `incompatible-schema` added so the plan's three cases, missing, damaged and incompatible metadata, are distinct values.)
- Valid unknown-model or model-incompatible stills remain viewable/saveable with compute disabled; damaged recovery offers explicit Use as photo only when decodable (UI by face controls).
- Never follow model URLs or arbitrary metadata URLs from a file.
- Equal-shaped latents from different checkpoint identities are not combinable (exposed as incompatibility).
- Unit tests per classification and per earlier schema.

## Out of scope
Batch UI, click order and keypoint insertion (face controls). MP4 project import (deferred).

## Considerations
- The reader runs before any target replacement; late imports are rejected by the app's revision checks.

## Classification rules (polish r1)
The plan requires missing, damaged and incompatible metadata to be told apart:
- `missing`: a decodable image with no recovery chunk. It may enter photo encoding only through an explicit action (Encode image / Use as photo); never automatically.
- `damaged`: a recovery chunk is present but fails parsing, integrity hash or bounds. Never silently re-encoded (its identity must not change); Use as photo is offered only when the pixels decode, and only as an explicit action.
- `incompatible-schema`: a well-formed envelope whose schema/version this build does not support. Viewable and saveable; no latent use; reason names the version.
- `incompatible-model`: valid envelope whose model/checkpoint identity is known but differs from the loaded model (including equal-shaped latents from another checkpoint). Viewable and saveable with compute disabled.
- `unknown-model`: valid envelope with an identity this build does not know. Same handling as `incompatible-model`.
- `matching`: installs image and latent without model acquisition, detector or encoder.

**Model mismatch: view/save without latent use.** For `incompatible-*` and `unknown-model`, the image is shown, Save/Share hands over the original file bytes unchanged (byte-equal to the input; no re-encode, so its envelope is kept), the latent is never passed to the engine, and the face is excluded from morph inputs with a plain reason. No URL found in metadata is fetched.

Named tests: `inspect-still.missing`, `.damaged-truncated`, `.damaged-bitflip`, `.damaged-oversized`, `.incompatible-schema`, `.incompatible-model`, `.unknown-model`, `.matching-schema1-png`, `.matching-schema2-png`, `.matching-schema2-webp`, `.matching-dynamic-shape`, `.mismatch-save-bytes-unchanged`, `.mismatch-latent-not-used` (engine spy receives nothing), `.no-metadata-url-fetch`.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests cover each classification, each earlier schema and corrupt inputs; no network request is made by inspection (network log in a browser test).
- [ ] A recovered still re-imported through the built UI installs without any model or detector request (e2e, event log assertion).
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots are kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Network claims are asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Each of the six kinds (`missing`, `damaged`, `incompatible-schema`, `incompatible-model`, `unknown-model`, `matching`) has fixture tests; `damaged` and `incompatible-*` never reach photo encoding without an explicit action (encoder and detector spies stay at 0) and keep their identity.
- [ ] Model mismatch: built-UI e2e shows the image, Save returns bytes equal to the opened file, the engine receives no latent from it, Morph excludes it with a reason, and the network log shows zero requests caused by the file.
notes:
Polish r1: the `inspect-still.matching-dynamic-shape` test is owned by media.recovery-schema (fm-qi01) and is added to this reader's suite when that schema lands; the reader item does not wait for it.
Position in the shared-file sequence: after media.split, before media.export-identity. Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Leaves that must not edit these three files: ws:crop.repro (failing tests and the failure analysis only), crop.policy, media.envelope-helpers, media.recovery-schema, morph.descriptor-geometry, compute.consumer-example, compute.names-equality, and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept leaf. They keep the module export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) and move logic behind them into the package. If such a leaf finds it must edit one of the three files, it records the file in the check-migration map conflict list and adds a needs edge to the latest leaf in the sequence that edits it; it never edits concurrently. Each sequenced leaf lists every file it edits in the check-migration map conflict list at claim time.

title: ONNX Runtime Web bump through the currency lane
description:
## Goal

Decide, from measurement rather than release notes, whether the latest ONNX Runtime Web gives the app anything (operator request, 16 October), and move every route to it as one grouped dependency change (bump the immutable release-consistent runtime mirror with the npm package, manifest and canaries). No hold-backs (operator, 24 October 2026): "hold" is not an outcome, and a route that fails a gate on the latest release is a bug fixed here. It runs through the re-homed research pipeline and gates no release; "no measured benefit" is a valid finding, not a reason to stay behind. Tolerances and retained cells never change.

## Scope

**Facts** (verified 16 October; not measured for this app): npm latest 1.30.0; 1.31.0 GitHub release of 9 October not yet npm `latest`; nightly `1.31.0-dev.20260918-bc8e7ed75`. Candidate runs CPU 1.24.3 and WebGPU 1.22.0 (JSEP). ORT Web announced in 1.29.0 that JSEP and WebGL are deprecated and removed: the default bundle flips to the native WebGPU EP with a temporary `onnxruntime-web/jsep` escape hatch for one release, then JSEP is deleted — moving WebGPU forward is a migration to the native EP. Hypothesised gains: graph capture (1.24.1), convolution optimisations, subgroup-matrix MatMul/Gemm incl. WASM, subgroup-size control (1.30.0); expect modest or none. `webonnx/wonnx` excluded (archived; last release v0.5.1, September 2023).

**Staging**: non-shipping, digest-pinned, release-consistent runtime sets for control (pinned candidate runtime by hash: CPU 1.24.3, WebGPU 1.22.0 JSEP, the candidate's runtime overlay), latest npm stable (1.30.0 or newer at execution), 1.31.x if npm `latest` by then, and native WebGPU EP bundles (`./webgpu`, `./jspi`); each set's manifest, file digests and staging location recorded; drivers address sets by digest. Staging/mirroring uses the re-homed deploy tooling; production is changed only by the final bump.

**Numerics first** (per set × provider, CPU WASM and WebGPU; eris RTX 2080 SUPER under the lease, CPU on a capable worker): product canaries and the applicable reference suite; raw max RGB diff, max sampled raw-float error, e4e latent error against unchanged tolerances (RGB ≤ 1, raw-float ≤ 0.002, e4e 0.0001). A runtime that fails numerics is fixed before it ships, regardless of speed.

**Paired desktop comparison** (numerics-passing sets only): discarded warmup, same-cell ABBA ×3, control/control noise first, then frozen margins. WebGPU on eris and CPU paired runs. Metrics: cold start, warm ms/frame, runtime download bytes (they enter consent/acquisition costs), peak memory; fixed 32-frame / 16 FPS / 1024 px workload where supported. Comparison protocol per PLAN.md#retained-performance-evidence-and-no-regression-checks.

**Phones**: each staged set's mobile route checks in the iOS Simulator (WebKit) and Android emulator lanes, per bundle (`./webgpu`, `./jspi`) × lane; never assume the native-EP bundle runs where JSEP does; e4e WASM heap peak over all 108 FP32 shards vs 268,435,456 bytes where the lane executes models — exceeding it is a defect fixed before that route moves.

**Direct vs native EP** (exploratory): paired comparison of the direct WGSL engine (desktop synthesis with RGBA8 conversion) vs the native WebGPU EP on synthesis, eris, leased, same workload and numerics; no kernel change or retirement follows from this alone.

**Nightly data point**: comes from the bleeding-edge lane (`currency.bleeding-edge`, fm-8iv), whose scheduled run already carries the ORT Web nightly with numerics and a paired desktop screen; this bead cites that run's ledger rows in its outcome when one exists and does not wait for it (the bleeding-edge lane is a P3, non-shipping lane and is not a prerequisite).

**Apply**: bump the runtime mirror together with `onnxruntime-web`, manifest and canaries to the latest stable on every route in one revision through the normal gates (and update the `runtime_sha` pin used by the e2e lane); WebGPU moves to the native EP before JSEP is deleted upstream. Measured effect stated per route.

**Optional, removable**: exploratory WebNN EP probe — where a browser exposes WebNN on an available worker, run the numerics canaries and one timing screen, or record "not available on workers"; no product route is added.

## Out of scope

Changing tolerances or retained cells; kernel changes; physical-phone qualification (evidence gap remains); shipping or adopting a nightly.

## Notes

- Research discipline for every run: acquire the shared lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>`, absolute state dir) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and load first; fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite logs or measured source. `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends (corrections reference prior IDs); `log.md` appends at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps; `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored journal. Architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`. Results are experimental evidence at their scope; Simulator/desktop never stand in for physical phones. New opportunities are proposals with their next refuting test.
- Feeds compute extraction's provider adapters (soft) and integrated verification's release summary.
- PLAN.md (24 Oct): the evidence is the ledger rows, the CI runs and the merged bump; no `docs/decisions/` entry or receipts.
- Anchor: PLAN.md#onnx-runtime-web-currency-evaluation, #dependency-currency-and-the-frozen-self-host-guarantee--16-october-2026.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each staged set's manifest and digests are recorded; the control set digest equals the pinned candidate runtime.
- [ ] Numerics per set × provider give raw max RGB diff, sampled raw-float error and e4e latent error with pass/fail at unchanged tolerances; failing sets are not timed until fixed.
- [ ] Desktop comparison gives, per numerics-passing set and provider, cold start, warm ms/frame, runtime download bytes and peak memory with raw distributions, control/control noise margin and paired effect against control; ledger row IDs appended.
- [ ] Phone rows per bundle × lane (iOS on WebKit in the Simulator) with load/canary result, named failures and e4e heap peak pass/fail against 268,435,456 bytes.
- [ ] Direct-vs-native-EP paired effect and numerics recorded as exploratory ledger rows.
- [ ] The outcome cites the bleeding-edge lane's latest ORT nightly ledger rows when they exist, or states that no nightly run exists yet.
- [ ] A merged bump on every route whose canaries pass within the frozen tolerances per runtime and whose lockfile/runtime-mirror consistency check passes.
- [ ] (Optional, removable) WebNN probe result or "not available on workers" recorded.
- [ ] from fm-bxwv (operator, 24 October: no hold-backs, latest releases): ship onnxruntime-web at latest (1.30.0 or newer) in the runtime mirror on both routes. CPU WASM, and WebGPU on the native EP build that ort.webgpu.min.mjs loads from 1.23 (JSEP is deprecated upstream). 'Hold' is not an outcome. Numerics already pass on eris at the unchanged gates (tools/ort-qualify, 5adabb0): CPU identical to 1.24.3, native-EP WebGPU max sampled float 2.8e-5.
- [ ] A phone-cpu journey passes on the bumped ONNX Runtime Web (lab.py run --cell phone-cpu --journey warm-face); the photo/e4e encoder path on the phone is recorded untested (no photo journey yet), not assumed

title: Share/Save, format choice, editable filename, Preparing file
description:
## Goal
Below every face and morph result: Share as the primary action, Save, a compact format choice and an informative, editable filename, using prepared files so Share runs inside the user gesture and repeated Save/Share reuse the same bytes. The candidate (operated 18 October) offers Share image / Save image and Share morph / Save video, WebP 0.8 with PNG fallback, no format choice, and names every file `facemorph.mp4` or `facemorph.webp`.

## Scope
- In `.next-face-actions` (face) and `.next-actions` (morph), directly below the face image / video, wrapping inside the tile: Share (primary where `navigator.canShare({files})`), Save (primary when file sharing is unavailable), compact format choice (face: WebP default at quality 0.8, PNG lossless; morph: MP4), proposed filename shown and optionally editable inline (no dialog), actual resolution for video.
- Prepare the selected file before enabling Share so the click calls `navigator.share({files})` in the user gesture; "Preparing file…" keeps pixels visible with Save/Share disabled until prepared; file-preparation Retry on failure, never inference.
- Share cancel (AbortError) keeps the result ready and triggers no download; an actual share failure saves the same file.
- Format change prepares only that format (no inference); an actual PNG fallback shows PNG MIME/extension.
- Format help: WebP/PNG "Includes editable face data"; MP4 "Video; reopening this file as a project is not available in this release." plus codec/resolution fallback disclosure.
- Repeated Save/Share reuses the prepared bytes and name; edits keep the identity suffix; filenames are sanitized (path separators, bidi characters) and truncated per media's 64-character rule. Save after reload reuses the restored export identity; the filename is the opened filename or the generic safe label when the original text is unavailable.
- **More export options** disclosure only when qualified extra options exist (none initially).
- Do not auto-open the share sheet; no export wizard, page toolbar or quality slider. Filenames are visible to recipients but never added to metadata or diagnostics.

## Out of scope
Export bytes, metadata, identity, filename rules and the prepared-file cache (media workstream); extra formats (deferred optional media bead).

## Notes
- Calls the export API the media export-identity bead exposes; any bridge change it needs belongs to media. Edits no shared bridge/runtime/worker file.
- The blend view's result reuses these controls unchanged.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#file-sharing-and-export-direction, #crop-fidelity-and-export-flow-clarification, #clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation, #gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design (open/share/export affordances).

- [x] Real `navigator.share` on the device lab's physical Android phone (the share sheet dismissed through adb for AbortError): called within the click gesture with one file whose name/MIME/extension match the bytes; AbortError -> no download, result ready; failure -> same file downloaded. Share unsupported -> Save primary.
- [x] WebP -> PNG -> WebP: zero inference requests; repeated Save reuses the same bytes (digest equal) and name.
- [x] Filename edit: empty, very long (64-character rule), pasted value with path separators/bidi characters -> sanitized; identity suffix kept.
- [x] Delayed preparation shows "Preparing file…" with Save/Share disabled; injected failure -> file-preparation Retry, pixels visible.
- [x] Restored result after reload: Save reuses its identity, filename is the opened name or the safe label, suffix kept, zero inference.

title: Version the dynamic-shape recovery schema
description:
## Background
Current envelopes assume FFHQ shapes (18 x 512 W+, 1024 px). The external developer journey requires exporting PNG/lossless-WebP for other checkpoints and reopening exact model/latent metadata, while preserving the earlier candidate readers.

## Why
Recovery must carry the descriptor-driven latent shape and model identity so non-face exports reopen exactly and cannot be mixed with other checkpoints.

## Scope
- A new schema version recording latent space/shape from the descriptor, checkpoint/model identity and generator identity; writers emit it, readers accept it plus schema-1/schema-2.
- Reject schema/version mismatches descriptively; unknown models stay viewable as media without editable inference.
- Unit tests with FFHQ and the different-resolution reference descriptor; cross-checkpoint equal-shape combination rejected.

## Out of scope
Converter output manifests (conversion). Morph geometry (morph pipeline).

## Considerations
- Contracts freeze metadata schema/version rejection; changes go through a contract revision.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Round-trip exact for FFHQ and a non-FFHQ descriptor (latent values and model identity byte-exact in the decoded metadata).
- [ ] Earlier schema fixtures still read; unsupported versions rejected with a typed error.
- [ ] Mixed-identity morph inputs refused in a unit test.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes: This leaf (media.recovery-schema) is outside the shared-file sequence and must not edit the three shared files. Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. They keep the module export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) and move logic behind them into the package. title: Scaffold npm workspaces, the four package placeholders and strict TypeScript
description:
## Background

Candidate import places the JS closure under `apps/web` (keeping the `src/Next` structure), with
temporary root paths for `desktop/runtime.mjs` and required `scripts/`. Target layout: `apps/web/`,
`packages/stylegan-js/`, `packages/browser-model-manager/`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host/`,
`packages/model-conv/`, `autoresearch/`, `hosting/`, `scripts/`, root `package.json`/`package-lock.json`,
`tsconfig.base.json`. Use npm workspaces; no other package manager or orchestration framework.
Currency snapshot (16 October; superseded by the first lockfile): TypeScript 7.0.2, Node LTS 24.22.0
(CI moves to 24), Vite 8.3.4, Playwright 1.64.1, Wrangler 4.151.0.

## Why

Extraction acceptance cannot be met before the workstreams it gates unless the package workspaces exist first as building, packable placeholders.

## Scope

- Root npm workspaces for `apps/web` and the four packages; each package is an empty placeholder that
  builds, emits declarations and packs (`npm pack`), with explicit `exports`.
- `tsconfig.base.json`: `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`,
  `isolatedModules`, type-only imports; scoped DOM, WebWorker and Node configs so shared contracts do
  not pick up accidental globals.
- Scripts: `typecheck` (explicit, separate from any bundling), declaration builds with workspace
  dependency ordering, `test` aggregate, `build:next` kept working.
- First lockfile at latest stable versions per the currency policy; Node pinned (`engines`, `.nvmrc` or
  equivalent) compatible with Oxc (`^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`) and CI Node 24.
- Record the ONNX Runtime Web runtime hold-back (reason: measured runtimes under evaluation, JSEP
  removal pending; re-check trigger, one of the two the currency policy allows: the next updater run that passes the gates, or the upstream ONNX Runtime Web release that removes JSEP from its default bundle; the ORT Web decision (fm-lvd) then replaces this entry) before the first lockfile lands.
- Temporary JS interop through narrow adapters with tests and a named retirement owner; do not
  mechanically rename `.mjs`.

## Evidence modules and typecheck coverage

- Include `scripts/evidence/**` (the receipt/event-log modules from `build.docs-decisions-receipts`, which
  land earlier as erasable-syntax TypeScript run directly by Node) in the strict `typecheck` scope, and
  their `node --test` suites in the aggregate `npm test`.
- Unit tests for this item's own logic (workspace ordering script, any interop adapter) are listed in
  `check-tests-listed` and run in `npm test`.

## Out of scope

Vite app build (build.m2 / migration). Contract types (contracts items).

## Considerations

Do not fetch `latest` at build time. React 19/MUI upgrades land with the port, not here; this item pins what the imported closure needs plus tooling.

A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

- [ ] Each tool that uses the TypeScript compiler API (declaration emit, type-aware lint if enabled, Vite and test plugins) runs under the pinned TypeScript 7.x in CI; a tool that fails gets a hold-back entry with reason and re-check trigger instead of a silent older TypeScript.

title: stylegan-js core: bounded e4e encode and descriptor-driven mapping and synthesis
description:
## Goal
In `packages/stylegan-js`, add typed photo `encode` over a caller-supplied encoder capability running the bounded streamed e4e on preverified local shards, and make mapping and synthesis read every dimension from the model descriptor instead of FFHQ's fixed 1024 px and 18 × 512. fm-dmlz then rewires the app.

## Scope
- Candidate: 108 sequential FP32 ORT sessions (`photo-runtime/encoder-stream/execute.mjs`, manifest `encoder-stream/assets/manifest.json`), bounded unshared single-threaded WASM, constrained sequential worker teardown, encoder-to-generator residency transition.
- `encode(pixels per the frozen preprocessing policy) -> W+` with cancel/dispose, attempt identity and per-stage timing hooks, on the manager's encoder capability (lazy verified-local shard reads; no `acquireBytes`, URL or OPFS handle visible). Preserve max one live session, constrained teardown on phones, transition accounting, qualified WASM photo helpers. e4e tolerance max absolute W+ error 0.0001; no silent fp16 or widening.
- Descriptor (from the engine contracts, fm-z5wy; any later revision in contracts milestone 2 is checked at close): Z/W size, W+ layer count, output resolution/channels, layout/normalization, noise, truncation, optional conditioning; descriptive typed rejection naming the unsupported field; component check with a qualified reference at a different resolution and layer count (conversion.qualify fixture when available, else a test descriptor with an independent reference from the pinned reference implementation, at its own declared tolerance). Non-face capabilities never load a detector or FFHQ e4e.

## Rules
- This bead edits NONE of the shared files (`apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs`). Code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today until the bridge's own turn in the shared-file sequence; the bridge rewiring is the original bead's job.
- Tests run against real models, real browsers and real files where stated; no mocks, fixtures or captures stand in for live proof. The original bead's real-bridge/built-app checks still have to pass before the feature counts as done.
- Split from the original bead in the parallelism pass (operator, 24 October 2026: more parallel work from the start).
- Original bead: fm-dmlz (Bounded e4e photo-encode orchestration and descriptor-driven mapping and synthesis); anchors as listed there.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Real e4e through the package on CPU (and the phone-constrained profile in the iOS Simulator lane where it already runs) meets max absolute W+ error <= 0.0001 against `encoder-stream/qualification/*`.
- [x] Intercepted requests: zero during `encode`; a missing or corrupt shard after admission gives a typed invalidation and a settled operation, with no fetch.
- [x] Max live sessions = 1 and teardown behaviour unchanged versus the control (unit and runtime assertions).
- [x] Unit tests: cancel between sessions settles within the declared bound and releases the worker; invalidation mid-encode; disposal releases sessions.
- [x] FFHQ outputs unchanged within the frozen tolerances after generalization.
- [x] A different-resolution, different-layer-count reference passes mapping and synthesis within its own declared tolerance; descriptor and reference provenance committed with the test.
- [x] Each unsupported descriptor field yields a descriptive typed rejection; a scripted source scan of the package finds no hardcoded 1024 or 18x512 outside an allowlist for FFHQ descriptor data.
- [x] Non-face run's intercepted requests contain no detector or e4e asset request.
notes:
BronzeFalcon 26 Oct, commit 6ce99c0 (local main; push waits on QuietCrane's unpushed 48d737f under that agent's reservations). FFHQ after the descriptor generalization: node --test test/engine/cpu.test.ts and the other package Node tests, 113/115 pass. All seven product canaries on the CPU adapter are maxRgb 1, maxFloat <= 5.3e-6, equal to the candidate CPU table. The 2 failures were routes.test's kernel-identity tests, which then took FFHQ's side from the descriptor (still exact string equality); they now pass. Real-browser harness test/engine/browsers.test.ts on built dist: Playwright Chromium, Firefox and WebKit CPU, plus Chrome 156 NVIDIA WebGPU ORT engine and direct engine. All pass with 7/7 canaries at RGB 1 / float 0.002 and zero engine requests. ORT also ran full31 31/31, max RGB 1, float 3.7e-5. The direct cell failed once right after the ORT cell's deliberate GPU-process crash, then passed on its own (canaries, mapAsync, device loss typed). The direct engine's OUT/RGBA8 WGSL at FFHQ's plane equals the previous text (compared).
BronzeFalcon 26 Oct, 6ce99c0: AFHQ cat 512 (AFHQ_CAT_512_DESCRIPTOR: 16 x 512 W+, 15 noise planes, 512 px) through loadCpuGenerator with descriptor. Mapping uses the package's NumPy RandomState z (equal bit for bit to the reference z) plus psi 0.7 / cutoff 8 truncation. Synthesis is the model-conv conversion (manifest 2aa475d7...). Compared with an independent reference: NVlabs/stylegan2-ada-pytorch@d72cc7d on the original checkpoint f62fd750..., generated in the model-conv container by test/vectors/afhq-cat-512/make-reference.py. Held to its own declared tolerance (raw 1e-3, RGB 1). Node, test/engine/descriptor-engine.test.ts: seed 0 W+ 3.46e-6, raw 4.75e-5, RGB 1; seed 1 W+ 1.91e-6, raw 3.73e-5, RGB 1. The same seed 0 in Playwright Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (test/engine/nonface-browser.test.ts) gives identical errors. Committed: test/vectors/afhq-cat-512/reference.json, with the digests of every reference array, the checkpoint, the container, versions and the converted manifest digest; the test verifies the arrays against it. Weights and arrays stay out of Git (packages/model-conv/out, gitignored).
BronzeFalcon 26 Oct, 6ce99c0: engine/model.ts engineGeometry() rejects with a typed DescriptorUnsupported {code invalid|unsupported|inconsistent, field, message 'field: reason'}, and engineError maps it to 'unsupported'. Fields covered: $.conditioning (class), $.output.shape[1] (channels), $.output.range, $.truncation.cutoff, and $.identity.modelSha256 for the ort-webgpu/direct-webgpu engines, whose kernels are FFHQ-only. Contract-invalid fields are named the same way: $.output layout, $.noise mode, $.architecture, $.latent.layers, $.photoEncoder on non-face. checkManifest flags $.identity.* and $.noise.planes[i] as inconsistent. All three loaders reject before any read or adapter probe (asserted 0 reads, 0 probes). Scan test/engine/source-scan.test.ts walks every src/** file (comments and byte arithmetic skipped) for 1024/1024u, 1048576, 33554432/3145728, 18x512, layers:18 and 9216. Allowlist: the FFHQ descriptor data, plus four documented non-geometry constants (CROP_OUTPUT, VideoResolution and its validator, video fullSize, BLEND_RECIPE_MAX_SLOTS). The scan is self-tested against known positives and negatives, with no stale entries. Green with QuietCrane's descriptor-based encode.ts.
BronzeFalcon 26 Oct, 6ce99c0: test/engine/nonface-browser.test.ts, Playwright Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, all 3 passing. The manager acquires the AFHQ assets and the pinned CPU runtime under a grant ('acquire'). The engine loads, maps and synthesizes AFHQ with zero requests of every class ('engine'). Then the reference is compared ('compare'). Across all 80-83 recorded requests in every step, no URL names an encoder, landmark/detector or /photo/ path, or any digest of manifest.encoder, encoderStream (108 shards, runtime, canaries), landmarks, photo or photoCanaries. The generator's reads contain no photo-pipeline digest. Only shared bytes are excluded: the stream's ORT API module is identical to the CPU runtime's. Node: the descriptor-engine test asserts that the reads are only AFHQ manifest assets.

title: Controller port: model, inputs, settings, names, reporting, slider
description:
## Goal
Port the F# controller's typed model, message union, `init`, derived view-state helpers and the everyday reducers (inputs, settings, names, reporting consent, toasts, slider) to pure TS, tested against goldens recorded from the control. Every other controller bead builds on the model; these transitions are the bulk of exact parity rows; diagnostics behaviour must survive (privacy allowlists, one-shot Send this report, report reference, non-blocking failures) and slider choice survives hide/show.

## Scope
- Source (classic `b2d945a8` or the frozen import revision; re-check lines with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`): records `Input`/`Face`/`PublicPreview`/`NameFace`/`Progress`/`Output`/`Request` 15-27; `Downloads` 84; `State` 215-261 (Inputs, Faces, Previews, VideoUrl, Kind/Width/Pinch/Frames/Fps/Provider, Busy/JobId/Stage/Status/Fraction, Preparing, Browse/Names/NameQuery/NameLimit, Crop/CropQueue, Route/Rejected, Invite, UseSlider/SliderFrames/SliderFrame, Warn/Overflow/PhotoQueue, PendingFaces/PendingJobs/PendingMorph/PendingImport, RunInputs/RunSettings, PreparingFaces, Comparing, PhotoChoice, CachedFaces, ActiveFace, Remaining, ConsentPrompt, Downloads, ModelToastHidden, DownloadConsent, Gate, LastRun, FailureToast) and `CropChoice` 262; `Msg` union 263-279 (64 cases); URL predicates `namesRequested` 282, `testingInvited` 287, `labsOrigin` 289; `trialPhase` 295; `previewCmd` 297-300; module-level `estimator` 139 and `admittedRoute` 138.
- Files: `apps/web/src/controller/state.ts` (State, CropChoice, records), `msg.ts` (one variant per F# case, same payload shape), `init.ts`, `derived.ts`, `reducers/inputs.ts`, `reducers/names.ts`, `reducers/reporting.ts`, `reducers/slider.ts`; scaffold `apps/web/test/controller/scaffold.ts` (loads a golden step, builds State from its prior-state record, applies the reducer, diffs).
- `init` 303-311 with the same defaults: `face-1` text `hello`, `face-2` text = today `yyyy-MM-dd`, preview `/preview/hello-1024.webp`, `Kind="full-smooth-figure8"`, `Width=0.2`, `Pinch=true`, `Frames=16`, `Fps=16`, `Provider="auto"`, `NameLimit=48`, `NextId=3`, `ConsentPrompt = trialPhase && not testingInvited && not labsOrigin && not consentAnswered()`; init effects `restoreLastResult`, `subscribe`, `subscribeDownloads`, `BrowseNames "face-1"` when `namesRequested()`.
- Derived helpers: `remainingText` 316, `perFrameText` 329, `predictedMorphMs` 335, `isSlowDevice` 344 (20,000 ms or CPU route), `scopeReady` 349, `gateScope` 352-366, `megabytes` 368, `estimate` 758-767. Retained JS called unchanged: `estimate.mjs` (`createEstimator`, `describeMs`, `describeMeasuredMs`, `isSlowJob`), bridge `measuredFaceMs`, `measuredFrameMs`, `jobProgress`, `plannedFrames`.
- Input/settings/names reducers (`updateCore` 371-744): `Edit` 431-436 and `Mode` 437-443 (via `change` 372-374: `invalidateFace`, clears `CachedFaces`, the face, `VideoUrl`, `Status`); `AddAt` 573-578 (guard `Inputs.Length<64`, id from `NextId`); `Remove` 579 (guard `Inputs.Length>1`; effects `invalidateFace`, `rememberSourcePhoto id null`, `invalidatePhotoSelections`; drops the face from Faces/PreparingFaces/CachedFaces/Inputs/PendingJobs/PendingFaces, clears `VideoUrl`); `Kind`/`PinchToggle`/`Frames` 580-582 (`invalidateMorph`, clear `VideoUrl` and `SliderFrames`); `Provider` 583 (only when not Busy); `OverflowToggle` 584; `Compare` 585; `CachedFaceChecked`; `BrowseNames` 717 (`openNamesFocus`, reset query/limit 48, `loadNames` once), `NamesLoaded` 718, `PreviewLoaded` 719-724, `SearchNames` 725, `ChooseName` 726-732, `CloseNames` 733 (`closeNamesFocus`), `MoreNames` 734 (+48). Names modal state as the candidate has it (search/Show more still present; their removal is static names' declared change). `previewCmd` issues `publicPreview` (per-keystroke request is defect 11, repair owned by static names: port the call for parity rows, never assert it as required).
- The `update` wrapper (746-750) calls `rememberView` when Inputs/Kind/Frames/Pinch change: emitted by `migration.controller`; reducers here must leave fields so the rule fires identically.
- Reporting/slider reducers: `Debug` 699-701 (`setDebug enabled "checkbox"`), `Consent` 702 (`setDebug enabled basis`), `DismissConsentPrompt` 703, `SendReportOnce` 705-707, `DismissInvite` 708, `DismissWarn` 709, `UseSliderToggle` 710-713 (`sliderFrames`, `rememberSlider`), `SliderLoaded` 714-715, `SliderFrameSet` 716 (`rememberSlider state.UseSlider (max 1 frame)`), `DismissError` 735-737, `ReportFailure` 738 (`setDebug true "toast"`, defect 12 repair owned by diagnostics), `DismissFailureToast` 739. View visibility rules reading this state: `failureToastVisible` (~1436: FailureToast && not Debug && Error && not model toast && no Gate) and the trial-phase snackbar (~1444: ConsentPrompt && not model toast && no Gate && not failure toast). Reporting calls stay in `reporting.mjs`/`analytics.mjs` (unchanged) via effects.
- Pure typed reducers (no I/O); effects are returned as descriptions and executed by `migration.controller`. Scheduling/cancellation/progress go through the operation-service interface (`opctl.interface`), backed by the retained bridge until the operation controller lands. Elmish `Program.withReactSynchronous` processes one message at a time; the store keeps that.
- Goldens: recorder output from `migration.freeze` under `apps/web/test/goldens/control/<rowId>/` with `goldens.json`; replays run `scripts/fetch-control.mjs` first and refuse if the index digest differs from `control-artifact.json`. Parity rows must equal the golden exactly (state fields, effect descriptions, text, flow order); no tolerance. Repair and declared-change rows are listed as owner-graded, never asserted; no test may encode a candidate defect as expected output. Where a defect lives entirely in what this bead writes (string, CSS order, label), write the specification's version; otherwise carry the nearest candidate behaviour unasserted. Absent rows add no behaviour. An unexercisable row is `untested`, never passed.
- Rows replayed: First app visit (init/preview), Enter new words, Enter a numeric seed (0, 4,294,967,295, empty, negative, fractional, out of range), Edit/change mode/remove a queued or running tile, Open names from a face menu, Open/close fullscreen names Back/Escape, Find a known name (search is declared change), Add/remove controls, Remove down to one face, Select CPU/WebGPU (`Provider` message only), Report error with/without standing consent, standing debug On/Off, Play video/switch to slider, Return with completed retained work (slider choice). Repair rows 1, 5, 7, 8, 11, 12, 16, 18 and the `#debug-reporting` declared change are owner-graded.
- Defect 20 strings ("about 1 seconds" from `estimate.mjs` `describeMs` ~59; "smaller than25 MB" in `photo/align-photo.mjs` line 9 and `photo/image-header.mjs` line 3) live in retained JS imported unchanged; repair rows owned by face controls, never asserted as parity.
- Never record photos, latents, typed inputs or raw error strings.
- Not ported: `src/Next/Contracts.fs` (101 lines), `Runtime.fs` (83), `Assets/ModelAssets.fs` (45) have no product consumer (`Index.fs` line 18 wires only `NextProduct.init/update/view`); their `BrowserWebGl`/`NativeCpu`/`NativeGpu` cases are retired anyway.

## Out of scope
- Other reducer cases (`migration.controller`); rendering.
- Static-names declared changes; many-face layout/Undo and seed/word validation changes beyond candidate behaviour (face controls).
- Fixing defects 12/16 and the `#debug-reporting` disclosure (diagnostics); host rebinding.

## Notes
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-migration (controller port; controller port versus the operation layer); #diagnostics-that-must-survive-the-move.

description:
## Background
On 20 October one Cloudflare edge returned HTTP 500 from static-asset storage for single encoder chunks for about ten minutes at a time. The candidate now retries and alternates with `models.facemorph.me` (classic `hosting/next-mirror/worker.mjs`, `worker.test.mjs`, `wrangler.jsonc`; R2 bucket `facemorph-runtime-mirror`; copies immutable runtime paths and is warmed by every deploy).

## Why
The second origin is part of serving, not an optional extra.

## Scope
Required MIME/CORS/embedding (COEP/CORP)/cache headers; immutable digest-addressed paths; the mirror Worker and its tests carried into the package; warm-on-deploy hook exposed for ws:deploy; no accidental Worker invocation on primary model requests.

## Out of scope
Client retry logic (manager acquisition).

## Considerations
Exactly one repository's workflow may publish a target at a time (classic keeps publishing until handover).

## Interface to application deploy (polish r1)
Expose two commands from the package for `deploy.ci-workflow`: deploy the mirror Worker (today `npx wrangler deploy --config hosting/next-mirror/wrangler.jsonc`) and warm it with every immutable runtime file of the staged manifest (today the candidate's "Warm the runtime mirror with every immutable runtime file" step). Both take the target as an explicit argument and publish only with `--publish`. Keep `worker.test.mjs` cases.

## Source and provenance of the mirror Worker (polish r2)
`ws:hosting` takes `hosting/next-mirror/{worker.mjs,worker.test.mjs,wrangler.jsonc}` from the frozen import revision recorded by `inventory.import-allowlist` (fm-hyw): the committed head of `candidate/next-delivery-20260916` at freeze, `6107f80` or later. Export it from Git objects (never a working tree) into `packages/cloudflare-model-host/`. Its digests must equal the `hosting/next-mirror/` row of fm-hyw's reviewed-delta path map. Record source repo, commit, per-file SHA-256 and destination paths in the package's provenance file. `ws:deploy` takes its deploy-and-warm step definitions from the same commit.

## Reusable shape (polish r2)
In classic the mirror Worker fills itself from `https://next.facemorph.me/`, hard-coded, through a service binding, and copies only the immutable `runtime/{assets,chunks,manifests,photo,encoder-stream}/` paths. In the package:
- The upstream origin, the R2 bucket name (`facemorph-runtime-mirror` for FaceMorph) and the copied path prefixes are configuration. External developers can run it with no FaceMorph hostname.
- FaceMorph's values live in the application's deploy configuration (`hosting/`).
- Keep every classic `worker.test.mjs` case. Add tests that a non-immutable path is refused and that a configured upstream is the only origin fetched.
- `warm` takes the staged manifest and the target origin and implements the classic warm semantics: every immutable path, `--retry 3` on transient errors, 8-way parallelism, failure on any non-200, held count reported.

- [ ] Mirror Worker tests pass; header check on a staged sample passes; request trace shows primary model requests not invoking a Worker.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic are listed in the destination test discovery (no unlisted test files) and pass in CI.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/hosting/serving.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Mirror Worker files in the package match the frozen-revision digests recorded by fm-hyw (provenance file committed); upstream origin, bucket and path prefixes are configuration with no literal `next.facemorph.me`/`models.facemorph.me` in package source (scan); classic `worker.test.mjs` cases plus refused-non-immutable-path and configured-upstream-only tests pass.
- [ ] `warm` command test against a local test mirror: one missing path -> non-zero exit naming it; complete -> exit 0 with held count equal to the manifest's immutable path count.

title: Research stage 2: drivers, recipes, workflows
description:
## Goal

Let new research rounds measure the new application and packages through the `build:next` / `deploy-next/` artifact contract: maintained copies of the built-UI paired driver and the morph-frame product harness that take an artifact by digest, worker recipes correct for this repository on the actual workers, and the research workflows re-homed with path filters over the new code roots and leased heavy steps. Control for future rounds is a pinned artifact by hash (the candidate artifact or an earlier new-app build), never F# source or a rebuilt candidate. It feeds the ORT Web evaluation, the deferred evaluator adapters and classic wind-down.

## Scope

**Drivers**
- Maintained, versioned copies of `autoresearch/candidates/direct-rgba-media-v1/built-ui-paired.mjs` and the morph-frame-pipeline product harness (`candidates/morph-frame-pipeline-v1/`); frozen originals stay byte-identical and are never edited.
- Each driver takes an artifact path/digest and origin, verifies the digest, and records artifact identity in its outputs; default control is the pinned control artifact by hash.
- Every run leased, with a fresh run label (no output overwrite); network claims through the request-interception helper; traces/screenshots kept on failure.
- Outputs copied to the durable output location named in the launch recipe (outside transient CI artifacts) and cited by the round record; private or local-only raw files labelled; a CI artifact is only a convenience copy.
- The built-UI driver auto-accepts consent and supplies files programmatically, so it cannot establish native chooser latency (that needs the evaluator's adapters).

**Worker recipes**
- `autoresearch/devices/<worker>/` maintained recipes for eris and TrueNAS updated as new revisions for this repository's paths and the absolute lease directory; remaining .NET/Fable assumptions flagged (new-app builds need neither); software adapters rejected. Verify actual remote paths, dependencies and adapters rather than assuming historical eris paths or Triton readiness.
- Recipes follow the stage-1 launch-recipe template (checkout/worker, readiness checks, exact command, device identity, absolute lease dir, fixtures, browser profile handling, durable outputs).

**Workflows**
- Re-home `research-built-ui-media-v1.yml` and `research-rgba-screen-v1.yml` using the maintained drivers; path filters over `apps/web/**`, `packages/**`, maintained `autoresearch/**`, `scripts/**`.
- Explicit artifact lookup via the shared action (source repo ID, workflow/run, commit, artifact); heavy steps via the lease wrapper; experimental jobs bounded, separate from product checks and never required.

**Smoke** — a bounded leased run of each maintained driver on its worker against the control artifact, journaled; recorded as a dated `log.md` entry and journal events, never a `results.tsv` row (smoke runs are not evaluated outcomes).

## Out of scope

Overlap/warming adapters and the evaluator (deferred bead); disabling classic copies (classic wind-down); new devices; performance claims.

## Notes

- "Workspace build" in the prerequisites means build milestone 1 (identity, CI, lease): stage-2 drivers consume `deploy-next/` (control artifact first) and do not need Vite targets.
- Research discipline: lease before every heavy step; never terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs first; append-only ledger and log rules; numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances before any performance acceptance; results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope; Simulator/desktop never stand in for physical phones; new opportunities are proposals with their next refuting test.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#autoresearch-re-homing, #research-evaluator, #development-workers-and-github-minute-use.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Each maintained driver runs a bounded leased smoke against the control artifact with the artifact digest in its output; a wrong digest is refused before the run.
- [x] Driver outputs land in the recipe's durable location and the log entry cites that path.
- [x] Each worker recipe is executed once on its worker under the lease, or the blocker is named; a software adapter is rejected by the recipe.
- [x] One recorded run per re-homed research workflow; a change under `packages/` triggers them; their heavy steps show a lease journal entry; they are not in the required-status list.
- [x] Smoke runs appear as `log.md` entries and journal events with artifact digests; `check-research-ledger.mjs` shows no new `results.tsv` row from them.
- [x] CI path filters for re-homed workflows at close need fm-7ge (with fm-7ge). If fm-7ge has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-7ge (`br update fm-7ge --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-7ge
- [x] leased CI workflows at close need fm-wzy (with fm-wzy). If fm-wzy has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-wzy (`br update fm-wzy --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-wzy

title: Run the debug-reporting built-UI checks against the configured collector
description:
## Background
Built-UI checks listed in PLAN.md#debug-reporting-control-and-consent.

## Why
Workstream acceptance.

## Scope
Saved On/Off/refusal; storage failure; keyboard/label/link focus; withdrawal during an active job; aborted/discarded
sends; no new debug traffic after Off without a separately approved one-shot; scoped reporting with unrelated staged slot
records; Off-only toast visibility; explicit ongoing opt-in and later withdrawal; the failure-toast consent fix; the
actual configured collector's retention and production host bindings.

## Out of scope
Integrated verification join.

## Considerations
-
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. This bead adds tests only and edits none of the three files. It is ordered after the morph pipeline through its prerequisites fm-ea3n and fm-b7mt, which edit the bridge.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Operated-UI rule: each acceptance step acts with real pointer input (touch tap at phone widths) at the control's visible position, asserts `document.elementFromPoint` at that point returns the control (or a descendant) and that the point lies inside the region a person would look in (named per control below); by-name/by-role clicks are used only to set up state, never as the acceptance step.
- [ ] Every case is checked at a phone width (390 px) and a desktop width (1,280 px) with one screenshot per case kept as evidence, in light and dark themes.
- [ ] Controls and regions used: **Debug reports: Off/On** summary and the checkbox **Send debug reports until I turn this off.** (region: `#debug-reporting`, directly after Help/FAQ); footer **Privacy & reports** link (region: page footer); the debug FAQ link (region: Help/FAQ); failure-toast **Send this report** and **Turn on debug reporting** (region: the single bottom toast, not covering any action); the error box's **Send this report** (region: inline in the owning tile/Morph status).
- [ ] Saved On / Off / No thanks each restore on reload with no intermediate false render (first-paint DOM snapshot and a 100 ms screenshot series).
- [ ] Storage failure (localStorage throwing): "Reporting is on for this tab; this choice could not be saved." shown; reload shows Off.
- [ ] Keyboard and label: Tab reaches the summary and checkbox in visual order; label click and Space toggle; footer and FAQ links expand and focus the checkbox.
- [ ] Withdrawal during an active job: pending send aborted, unsent batch and session-storage mirror discarded, grouping ID cleared; the job completes (network, storage and operation logs).
- [ ] After Off: zero requests to the collector host class for the rest of the session, except one separately approved one-shot whose payload holds only the owning attempt's records (unrelated staged slot records absent).
- [ ] Off-only toast: with standing reporting Off a failure shows one toast; with it On no toast offers opt-in; at 1,280 x 800 and 390 x 844 at most one prompt is visible and `elementFromPoint` at Create Morph and every face action centre returns the action.
- [ ] Explicit ongoing opt-in via **Turn on debug reporting** then withdrawal via the footer link works; **Send this report** leaves the stored preference unchanged.
- [ ] Against the actual configured collector: a consented report is stored (object found by the reference shown in the disclosure); the stored object carries no `expiresAt`; KV fallback writes carry no 30-day TTL; the production build posts to the production route from the host map.
- [ ] Each end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Every network claim is asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Every listed check passes on the built artifact; untested cells recorded.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Bounded acquisition grant and synthesis-first overlap
description:
26 October operator clarification: optional early preparation belongs beside the top Auto/CPU/WebGPU selector, above the first +. No per-card Prepare encoder or blank Encode source modal. Skipping early preparation still automatically opens explanatory consent on Generate/Morph/fresh-photo preparation when prerequisites are missing, after recovery inspection and before model acquisition. One modal explains separate synthesis/encoder purposes, missing bytes and ranges/unknowns; only approved scopes download. Changing provider alone authorizes nothing. Page-level preparation is independently owned and survives cancelling an unrelated card chooser. This supersedes conflicting placement and source-modal lifecycle prose; existing behavioral acceptance remains.

## Goal
Replace the candidate's broad `DownloadConsent`/`gateScope` with a bounded, owned acquisition grant, and schedule approved acquisition synthesis-first so it overlaps photo choosing and cropping. Approval must be a bounded scope with explicit owners so Cancel and later decisions are honest, and authorized downloads must not be serialized behind photo selection: the post-confirmation wait shrinks and seed/text generation is usable first.

## Scope
- **Defect being fixed.** Candidate `DownloadConsent` is a broad route/photo set; unknown inventory bypasses `gateScope`; the download gate lets work start when the size list cannot be built (audit defect 19, gate part; `Product.fs:365`, ~352-410; `model-inventory.mjs:5-8`).
- **Grant shape.** A grant covers manifest identity, route, purpose (generate / encode / detector / codec fallback), required asset digests and advertised remaining-byte scope, with explicit owner intents. Snapshot the requested route, permitted fallback scope and runtime/model identity at Download and continue. Uses the contracts milestone 2 consent state types and the model manager's acquisition/local-read/lease primitives through the operation service.
- **Unknowns.** Unknown cache/manifest status waits for a bounded inspection or settles with Retry; it is never permission to fetch. Unknown size means ask.
- **What approval covers.** Selected preparation during input selection, deferred stages and retry within unchanged scope. Not a new checkpoint/provider or an abandoned action. Cache revalidation never silently inflates scope; extra/replacement scope or a newly discovered material cost requires a revised Continue/Cancel decision.
- **No repeated asks.** A second Generate inside a still-valid approved scope, and any action whose assets are cached and verified, opens no consent decision. A photo request groups the known detector and encoder prerequisites in one decision. Only assets outside the authorized scope, or a newly discovered material cost, produce a new or revised decision.
- **Cancel.** Releases that intent's acquisition and speculative warm ownership; a shared fetch stops when its final authorized consumer leaves; verified chunks are kept; late continuations cannot restart abandoned work. Selecting both purposes is not perpetual consent after all owning intents are abandoned. Declined detector acquisition abandons its continuation; manual continuation is a new explicit request. Cancel is separate from Hide (the candidate prefetch toast offers Hide); the existing candidate download Cancel is a capability to retain and verify.
- **Synthesis-first overlap.** Start the selected acquisition right after approval; prioritize synthesis prerequisites so seed/text generation is usable first; acquire the small detector/alignment prerequisite promptly; overlap remaining encoder transfer with local inspection, choosing faces and adjusting crops.
- Crop OK freezes input/order and queues encoding without waiting for downloads; the selected generator's readiness permits a face while encoder assets are in flight.
- **Aggregate buffers.** One aggregate transfer budget with digest deduplication, bounded by the contracts' aggregate transfer/read-ahead/hash/write-buffer limits (the old two-chunk phone read-ahead is per-worker and does not bound several overlapping workers). Acquisition holds no heavyweight compute permit while waiting; foreground-required assets outrank optional preparation; lower-priority work pauses when a lockup or memory pressure requires. Overlap does not require simultaneous hydrated networks, all 108 encoder shards in RAM, or concurrent heavy inference.
- **Progress.** Overlapping work is counted once; action-owned setup progress sits in the card/crop status, then the owning tile; independently approved early preparation stays beside the top provider selector with its own Cancel setup.
- Any new diagnostics event is added to the diagnostics event registry with its allowlist and privacy-policy entry; no photos, latents, typed input or raw error strings.

## Out of scope
Modal UI and Prepare encoder (consent.modal); warming (consent.warming); model-manager internals; device estimates.

## Notes
- Edits none of `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (shared-file serialization, 16 Oct; mandatory ordering edges, 17 Oct). The grant lives in the ported TS controller and consent modules; scheduling lives in the operation controller and the manager's acquisition queue. Bridge `downloadModels`/`consentToDownload`/`pumpDownloads` are not changed here and consent does not wait for compute extraction. If an edit to a shared file turns out to be needed, add an ordering edge to the morph pipeline bead first.
- Needs the controller port (`migration.controller`, fm-v80g): the grant replaces `DownloadConsent` in the ported TS controller; the modal (consent.modal) also waits for the rendering milestone.
- Exposed waits are measured with no threshold. An overlap, warming or reuse opportunity found goes to the targeted research ledger and the operator/planner; it is never turned into a visitor setting.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#consented-downloads-useful-overlap-and-cached-model-warming, #gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design (operation/resource ownership, cold photo sequence), #acquisition-consent-overlap-and-warming.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Grant state-machine tests (the state machine is pure; events and timestamps are plain inputs): approve/cancel/resume; two owners sharing one fetch (first cancels, second continues; both cancel -> fetch aborted); cancel during inspection; unknown inventory -> ask; scope inflation -> revised decision required; late continuation after Cancel rejected; declined detector abandons its continuation.
- [x] No-repeated-ask tests: a second Generate in a valid scope and a cached-and-verified action open no decision; a photo request yields one grouped detector+encoder decision; only out-of-scope assets or a new material cost produce a revised decision (pure state-machine tests plus one built-app request-log run).
- [x] Type-level tests: a grant cannot be constructed without digests and byte scope.
- [x] Integration test with the real manager: verified chunks retained after Cancel and reused on re-approval without re-download (intercepted requests, bytes).
- [x] Scheduler tests against a real local model server with real timers and request logs: synthesis assets complete before encoder assets under contention; a seed request during encoder transfer starts synthesis as soon as generator assets verify; the aggregate buffer never exceeds the contract limit; acquisition holds no compute permit.
- [x] Built-app request-interception run (cold profile), asserting by host class and bytes: zero model-host requests before approval and after Cancel; approval -> generator requests first; photo choose and crop happen while encoder bytes transfer; OK queues encode; first useful face precedes encoder completion.
- [ ] Measured, no threshold (desktop CPU, desktop WebGPU, one phone-class cell where available; cold and warm cache): input latency during transfer; approval -> first model byte; approval -> first useful face; crop OK -> encode start; encode end -> face file ready; the full choose -> generate/encode -> export journey. Reported in the CI run output.
- [x] Unit tests run in CI (`npm test` workspace target) and pass.
- [x] quota interplay check at close needs fm-fy2.13 (with fm-fy2.13). If fm-fy2.13 has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-fy2.13 (`br update fm-fy2.13 --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-fy2.13
- [x] device-lab failure fixed and a later lab run passed (ticked by lab.py on that pass)

LilacGlen, 26 Oct, commit 699c541: apps/web/src/consent/grant-policy.ts, the app's grant policy. It is a pure state machine over the manager's grant primitives (scopeCovers, cancelOwner). Events: request, inspected, tick, approve, decline, cancel, continue, each with a plain 'at'. Effects returned: inspect, ask, proceed, fetch, stop, retry, abandon, refuse.
- Row 1 TICKED: grant-policy.test.ts covers approve/cancel/resume (a new press is a new owner and is asked again); two owners sharing one fetch (the first cancelling leaves it running, both cancelling stop it); cancel during inspection (the late result is ignored); unknown inventory -> inspect -> ask, or Retry when still unknown or past INSPECT_MS, never a fetch; scope inflation (an extra asset, a changed size, another route) -> a revised decision naming the grant it extends, with extraBytes; a late continuation after Cancel is refused; a declined detector abandons its continuation, and manual continuation is a new request.
- Row 3 TICKED: grant-policy.test-d.ts, six @ts-expect-error cases: no assets, an asset without bytes, an unchecked digest, a null size, no owner, a literal not made by makeGrant. Checked by src/consent/tsconfig.test.json; a probe proves an unused directive fails the check.

comments.author: cdilga
comments.text:
LilacGlen, 26 Oct: 95358ed fixes the fetch order. A photo's encoder is foreground-required, and the first ranking would have fetched it before the generator. The order is now synthesis, detector, the rest of what the action requires, optional, warming. The test asserts it with the encoder's real priority.
Wiring plan, for whoever continues (me next):
(1) Adapter src/consent/requests.ts. Build Requests from the pinned manifest with model-inventory.mjs routeAssets/photoAssets (per-asset sha256+size) and the manager's per-asset inventory. Priorities: route assets synthesis-prerequisite; landmarks/photo canaries detector-prerequisite; encoder descriptor and shards foreground-required.
(2) Open design point: before its descriptor is read, the streamed encoder's shards have no digests, only manifest.encoder.size (photoAssets 'estimated'). The decision must show that estimate, and the grant must let the shards found in the verified descriptor in, up to the shown bytes and no further; beyond that is a new material cost, so a revised decision. The manager's scopeCovers covers known digests only. So either the policy carries a per-grant 'discovered within advertised bytes' allowance tied to the descriptor digest, or the manager contract gains it. This is the bounded replacement for bridge-grant.mjs widenGrant.
(3) Controller: the DownloadConsent set and gateScope give way to the policy's ask/proceed/inspect/retry. The Gate modal shows Decision.bytes and extraBytes; Cancel maps to the policy's cancel(owner).
(4) Workers: per-worker shares of the policy's grants replace bridgeGrant's whole-manifest scope. That is an ort-worker.mjs edit, so the ordering edge to the morph pipeline bead comes first (bead notes).

comments.author: cdilga
comments.text: LilacGlen, 26 Oct, 6f91500: resolved design point (2) in the pure policy. A request may declare discovers {via: descriptor digest, bytes: advertised, priority}. The decision shows those bytes (Decision.discovers, included in bytes and extraBytes), and the approved grant keeps them as an allowance tied to the descriptor (makeGrant: an allowance must name a descriptor in the grant; remainingBytes = assets + allowances). A continuation whose shards carry via = that descriptor is covered while the allowance has room. The allowance is spent and never renewed, so the approved total never grows. A shard beyond it, or one named by another descriptor, gets a revised decision. Coverage is the policy's own cover(): same-size digests, or a descriptor allowance. Tests: 12/12, plus a type case (an allowance without bytes). Next: the src/consent/requests.ts adapter over model-inventory.mjs routeAssets/photoAssets, then the controller.

- It now asks whenever the inventory is unknown or the scope is not ready, unless already consented; a cached face still needs nothing.

title: Reuse the candidate runtime mirror and photo siblings with verified acquisition
description:
## Background
Frontend build alone supplies neither model/runtime bytes nor inference readiness. Two different things in classic are both loosely called "mirror"; this bead uses these names:
- **Runtime overlay/mirror inputs** (what this bead reuses): the digest-checked immutable runtime staged under `hosting/next-static/runtime-overlay/` with `manifest.json`, produced/refreshed by `hosting/next-static/mirror-runtime.py` and `restage-runtime.py`, plus the pinned photo module siblings (detector, landmark, codec WASM) and their notices. Full restaging can depend on ignored `experiment/`, installed ORT/FFmpeg packages and external `review-artifacts`, absent from a fresh clone; reuse must not.
- **Second runtime origin** `models.facemorph.me` (classic `hosting/next-mirror/`, added in `6107f80` on 21 October, after the planning reference): a Worker over R2 bucket `facemorph-runtime-mirror` that copies immutable `runtime/{assets,chunks,manifests,photo,encoder-stream}/` paths from `https://next.facemorph.me/` on first request and is warmed by CI after each site deploy. The page alternates chunk retries between the site and this origin only on `*.facemorph.me` pages. It is a serving surface owned by `ws:hosting` (with deploy/warm by `ws:deploy`), not an acquisition source for this bead; a clean destination must not depend on it.

## Why
Early checks and the port need real runtime bytes without waiting for converter or model-host extraction.

## Scope
- Acquisition/mirror commands (`scripts/runtime/acquire.mjs` or a documented wrapper around the classic procedure recorded by `inventory.build-inputs`) with sha256 checks against the runtime manifest and explicit model-term/download authorization for a clean destination (an explicit flag or env such as `ACCEPT_MODEL_TERMS=yes`; never defaulted).
- Acquired bytes land in an ignored cache directory (listed in `.gitignore`); nothing is committed.
- Track app-emitted workers separately from manifest-pinned runtime workers/modules (transitive imports, WASM/codec/photo siblings, URLs): two lists in `inventory.md`.
- `scripts/runtime/check-pins.mjs`: fails when emitted or staged runtime bytes change without matching pin updates; prints one JSON line per file (path, expected digest, actual digest, graph: emitted|pinned).

## Out of scope
Converter/model-host extraction; copying a private lab; deploying or changing `models.facemorph.me`.

## Considerations
No weights in Git; acquired bytes live in ignored caches. A local run never contacts `models.facemorph.me` (the page code only uses it on facemorph.me hosts); if acquisition ever needs that host, record it as a deviation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Clean clone acquires runtime bytes by the documented command; checksums verify; terms acknowledgement is explicit (run without it exits non-zero with the instruction; run with it succeeds).
- [ ] Interrupted acquisition resumes or restarts cleanly; a corrupted cached file is rejected by digest and re-fetched.
- [ ] Pin-drift check fails on a deliberately altered runtime file and on an emitted-worker change without a pin update; passes on the clean tree. Unit tests cover both graphs.
- [ ] Acquisition log (structured: step, ISO timestamp, file, bytes, host class, digest result) shows zero requests to `models.facemorph.me` and no committed bytes (`git status` clean apart from intended files).
- [ ] Receipt `docs/receipts/import-runtime-reuse.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime/model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Its structured event log is written with the emitter from `build.docs-decisions-receipts` (fm-ucl: `scripts/evidence/event-log.ts`, or `scripts/evidence/event_log.py` for Python harnesses) using the host classes in `scripts/evidence/host-classes.json`, and the log passes `node scripts/check-event-log.ts <log>`; the receipt passes `node scripts/check-receipts.ts` (polish r2).
