title: Sub-result 2 (platform and resource): degradation, responsive sweep, grid reflow
description:
## Goal
Sub-result 2 of integrated verification: platform and resource. Restriction and failure must surface before cost, in
the owning action, without disabling working routes; phones are first-class, so layout must hold across widths, not
only at endpoints; and every face's image, field, Generate and Remove must stay visible and reachable at any count
(no fixed face count; virtualised past about 100 faces). This bead exercises placement and degradation in the built UI, runs the responsive width sweep and
re-runs the many-face layout and removal matrix on the release artifact, then emits the sub-result 2 output combining
these cases with `verify.consent-device`'s (and warming's, if shipped).

## Scope
- **Placement and degradation (R03, R09, R14 fallback part, R16 storage/quota part, R34, R49; defect 15):** one visible
  home per state (selector above the first +, tile status, Morph status, consent modal, result action area, Help,
  `#debug-reporting`). Phone CPU and eligible phone GPU/photo paths; unavailable operations; null adapters,
  insufficient limits, failed canaries, slow admitted work, active device loss. Missing GPU triggers no GPU downloads
  and leaves qualified CPU generation; known-ineligible routes stop before detector/model network or crop; another
  supported operation stays usable. A full-model check failing after authorized acquisition: bounded CPU fallback,
  revised assets/cost consent, contextual Retry, never native fallback, no desktop-download recommendation. Research
  preservation items: adapter probing, visible-time watchdogs, worker-start/failure separation, constrained worker
  teardown, phone encoder limits, without the per-device lab encoder check at startup. Names, recovery-first file
  entry ("Open saved image" label), compatible playback and Save stay usable. Catalogue failure/offline uncached
  results; denied/quota-limited storage; known-unavailable MP4 preparation; post-inference export failure; lost photo
  retry pixels after reload. Whole visible output and decoded full-size face / complete video bytes including the
  disclosed 512 px fallback; reason/Retry/Help placement; no duplicated warning panels. Pick a name on a cold, slow or
  offline connection (R09): the face's action slot shows loading then Retry; the prepared result validates before
  Save or Morph; never a synthesis fallback. Offline with models cached (defect 15): the page states what works; if
  the planner proposal ships, a job whose files are all cached completes with zero network requests and the model
  manifest is not re-fetched per job, otherwise record the decision. Desktop-package recommendation retired (R49): no
  native build, update or download link or recommendation anywhere.
- **Responsive sweep:** `SWEEP_WIDTHS` (320, 360, 390, 480, 600, 768, 900, 1,024, 1,280, 1,920, 2,560 px) plus 1 px
  either side of each layout breakpoint read from the built CSS; touch emulation at or below the phone/tablet
  breakpoint. Continuous resize through transitions; portrait/landscape and window-height changes while the names,
  crop or download modal, keyboard focus, queue/progress and results are active; short viewports, long names/errors,
  browser zoom/text enlargement, touch virtual-keyboard occlusion where available. Face/crop geometry correct; menus,
  primary actions, progress and dismissal visible and reachable; no overlapping/clipped controls, page-wide overflow
  or lost focus. Sweep cells feed every operated row as its layout dimension (the matrix grader records a row as
  layout-untested where a width was not exercised). Record exact viewport/zoom/artifact and unsupported environments.
- **Grid and removal matrix (R26, R27, R28; defects 1, 2, 3; layout evidence for 7 and 18):** the same operated matrix
  `face.many` (fm-id4c) passes, with the same cell IDs: `GRID_COUNTS` 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 30, 64, 150 x `SWEEP_WIDTHS` plus
  breakpoint +/-1 px edges; faces set up by the controller fixture; touch taps at touch widths. Each cell: no page-level
  sideways scroll and no hidden scrolling surface; a visible scroll cue whenever any face is off screen; every face's
  image, field, Generate (or current slot action) and Remove (except on the last face) visible or reachable by normal
  scrolling; Remove inside its face image (or compact-row thumbnail), not overlapped, 44 x 44 px hit area at touch
  widths, checked with `elementFromPoint` at its four corners and centre; insertion + controls hittable (not under
  tiles, cue arrows or fades); Add face enabled at every count; past about 100 faces only tiles near the view render and the page stays responsive. Removal per cell: a real tap/click at Remove's
  visible position removes exactly that face without reload, focus moves to a neighbour, Undo restores it in place.
  Start over from 30, 64 and 150 faces returns to two empty faces; Undo reverses it. Page height at 30 faces on 390 px
  recorded (target a few phone screens, not the candidate's about 7,000 px for fourteen). Admission refusal (a real budget forced one over, message naming that limit) identical on
  the six entry paths (layout side; `verify.flows` grades defect 18 from batch cases).
- **Sub-result 2 output:** machine-readable result naming the source commit and artifact digest, covering this bead's,
  `verify.consent-device`'s and (if shipped) warming cases; warming listed as not shipped otherwise; unmeasured
  thresholds reported "measured, no threshold".

## Out of scope
Measured usability promises. Paired performance and reliability on physical phones (`verify.not-worse`). Direct face
reordering.

## Notes
- Capabilities are real (operator, 24 October): browsers launched with WebGPU disabled, real quotas, real devices, real server faults; a case no available browser or device can produce is reported untested, never mocked.
- Earlier feedback: intrinsic dimensions passed while the displayed face was clipped; the 18 October operated check at
  390, 1,024, 1,280 and 1,920 px found layout defects.
- Integrated verification checks the final integrated app (after the planned UI and package changes) against the Next baseline (`facemorph.me-classic` branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) plus the plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped. Not historic-API parity and not a shutdown-qualification campaign. Performance and reliability against the control, including control/control noise and the physical iPhone, are judged by the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27), not here. Correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found here are fixed in the owning bead and this bead re-runs. Wording says planned, experimental, implemented or deployed. No weights, secrets, photos or typed inputs in Git.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation, #integrated-verification (structure item 2,
  responsiveness acceptance), #face-controls-and-modals, #autoresearch-coverage-and-preservation-map; defects 1-3, 15.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each degradation state appears only in its specified home (screenshot per case at phone and desktop width); no GPU/model fetch for ineligible routes before refusal; R09, R34 (defect 15 or its decision) and R49 have operated cases.
- [ ] Sweep table: each width x state with screenshot and overflow/clipping/focus assertions; breakpoint list derived from the built CSS and each tested at +/-1 px; every width and edge listed as passed, failed or untested.
- [ ] Grid matrix: 7 counts x (11 widths + 2 per breakpoint) cells, one screenshot per cell, every cell listed as passed, failed or untested with reason; the script asserts the cell count.
- [ ] Cell IDs equal `face.many`'s; a diff against that bead's CI result is attached, and any cell that passed there and fails here is a blocking regression.
- [ ] Remove, insertion + and Add face hit at four corners and centre per cell at touch widths; real removal with Undo per cell; Start over from 30, 64 and 150 with Undo; 30-face phone height recorded; with a real budget forced one over, the refusal message (naming the limit) identical on the six entry paths.
- [ ] Repeating controls exercised at 0/1, 2, 3, many and, where a real budget exists, that budget and its degraded state (Morph over-budget message, virtualised strip past about 100 faces, blend scrolling slot panel).
- [ ] The sub-result 2 output names the same source commit and artifact digest as the release identity record, uses only the closed outcome set, and reports unmeasured thresholds as "measured, no threshold".
- [ ] Every UI step is operated through the `verify.harness` (fm-48bj) helpers: real pointer/touch at the control's visible position with an `elementFromPoint` assertion that the hit element is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role locators only for setup; phone-width and desktop-width screenshot per case.
- [ ] Every network or consent claim is asserted from intercepted requests by host class and bytes (the request-interception helper from `build.ci-site`, fm-aa8), never from a screenshot; traces and screenshots are kept on failure as privacy-filtered CI artifacts.
- [ ] Every case is listed in this bead's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix rows or defect numbers it grades; a case without a mapping fails manifest validation.
- [ ] All cases ran in the release-verification workflow against the named release artifact digest; a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded `failed` or `untested`, never `passed`.
- [ ] from fm-48bj (verify.harness): imports SWEEP_WIDTHS and GRID_COUNTS from apps/web/test/verify/harness.ts (no copy of the lists).
- [ ] verify.platform imports SWEEP_WIDTHS and GRID_COUNTS from apps/web/test/verify/harness.ts, defining no second list (with fm-48bj)

title: Automated grouped dependency updater that keeps every group at latest
description:
## Goal

Keep the new application, packages and tooling on latest stable dependencies without human calendar work or approval steps (operator, 16–17 October): grouped automated update changes merge when the existing gates pass and simply do not merge when they fail. Nothing stays below latest stable (no hold-backs), and a guard makes it impossible for "latest" to widen a numerical tolerance or remove a retained cell.

## Scope

**Updater**
- Platform built-in updater or Renovate, chosen at setup; the reason is stated in the config.
- Groups exactly: build tools; React and UI; ONNX Runtime (npm `onnxruntime-web` and the mirrored ORT runtime always move together); test tools. Grouped changes stay apart from behaviour changes.
- Required checks per group before merge: build tools → typecheck, lint, format, build and identity checks; React and UI → UI and visual-parity checks; ONNX Runtime → CPU and WebGPU numerical canaries at current tolerances plus the iOS Simulator and Android emulator lanes; test tools (Playwright, browser-harness) → all five desktop-matrix cells including WebKit and Firefox.
- Merge rule: gates pass → automatic merge; gates fail → not merged, left open with its failure visible and fixed in that change; never closed as a hold-back; no human approval step.
- Node and `engines` restricted to the active LTS line (24 today); a non-LTS major such as 26 while Current is rejected.
- Excludes classic and `self-host/` (frozen distribution).
- No exact pins and no hold-backs (operator, 24 October 2026): every group moves to latest; a latest release that fails a gate is a bug fixed in that update change, not a reason to hold back.

- CI check fails when a manifest declares an exact version instead of a caret range (lockfiles record exact resolutions; manifests do not pin).
- Lockfile check fails if any dependency outside the bleeding-edge lane resolves to a prerelease (`-dev`, `-canary`, `-alpha`, `-beta`, `-rc`, `-next`); a nightly is adopted only once stable.
- CI check fails when the lockfile's `onnxruntime-web` version differs from the ORT version and file digests in the runtime-mirror manifest.
- Updater changes may touch only package manifests, the lockfile and the runtime-mirror manifest.

**Tolerance and cell guard**
- Frozen manifest with digest of tolerance constants (RGB ≤ 1, sampled raw-float ≤ 0.002, e4e latent max abs 0.0001, from the milestone-1 `numerics.ts` constants file) and the required-cell/check list (named CI lanes and required statuses); research suites keep their own frozen tolerances.
- A required CI check fails a change that alters the manifest unless the same change is a declared plan revision (PLAN.md change backed by an operator decision in its dated table). This lane never changes tolerances.

## Out of scope

Bleeding-edge lane (separate bead); behaviour-changing major migrations (the port, ORT native EP).

## Notes

- No time box, no human approval step, no fallback or backport to the classic stack (operator, 17 and 18 October).
- Removal of a listed test is already guarded by the retired-tests check; this guard covers lanes/cells and tolerances.
- PLAN.md (24 Oct): no `docs/decisions/` entry for the updater choice and no receipts.
- Anchor: PLAN.md#dependency-currency-and-the-frozen-self-host-guarantee--16-october-2026, #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance (dependency currency lane).

- [x] Fixture test: an updater change editing a source file fails the manifests-only check.
- [x] Fixture test: mismatched `onnxruntime-web` lockfile version vs runtime-mirror manifest fails.
- [x] Fixture test: a prerelease resolved outside the bleeding-edge lane fails the lockfile check.
- [x] Guard unit tests: a changed tolerance constant and a removed cell/required check each fail; a declared plan revision passes.
- [x] Dry run: a synthetic grouped bump that widens one tolerance and another that removes one cell are both rejected by the gates and not merged (recorded CI runs).

title: Morph as a parent intent with dependency joins
description:
## Background
Settled (12 October): Create Morph automatically generates unfinished valid text/seed inputs before frames, as one accepted intent with shared consent/progress/Cancel. The candidate queues `Run "morph"` behind busy/preparing faces (`PendingMorph`).

## Why
Morph must not hold a heavyweight lease while waiting for its own prerequisite face jobs, nor duplicate inference.

## Scope
- Morph request snapshots ordered compatible input revisions and settings; unfinished words/seeds become dependency face jobs; pending selected-name/confirmed-photo results are dependencies; invalid/unconfirmed inputs block acceptance with a reason.
- Join an existing operation for the same slot/revision rather than enqueueing duplicates; dependencies admitted once.
- Release/yield compute admission before awaiting dependencies or download consent; request the frame-production lease through the same scheduler when ready.
- Join a dependency's compute-ready milestone (verified latent + usable endpoint) rather than its default-file completion; delayed/failed face-file preparation never duplicates inference or blocks ready inputs.
- Parent Cancel stops work owned solely by the parent, detaches from independently requested face jobs and leaves their results; failed/cancelled dependencies settle the parent with a specific recovery action (no permanently disabled Morph or dangling promise).
- Distinct encoder and generator capabilities stay explicit; synthesis eligibility does not imply encoder admission.

## Out of scope
Frame-budget estimate (4,096-frame limit), frame production, MP4 availability probe, identical-neighbour refusal (ws:morph).

## Considerations
A newer face edit abandons the old morph rather than exporting obsolete work.

## Named fake-clock tests (polish r1)
File `apps/web/src/operations/morph-parent.test.ts`: `morph yields its permit while awaiting dependency faces` (a face requested meanwhile is admitted before the Morph's frame lease); `morph holds no permit while awaiting download consent`; `explicit face request for a slot already being auto-generated joins the existing operation (one inference, two owners)`; `morph joins a dependency's compute-ready milestone, not its file`; `face-file preparation failure does not block morph`; `parent Cancel at each dependency boundary (queued, acquiring, loading, inferring, file prep) settles the parent and leaves independently requested faces running`; `capability loss while queued settles with a recovery action`; `photo -> queued Morph`; `no deadlock with sparse preview anchors`; `newer face edit abandons the old morph`.

## Frame budget does not hold other work (polish r2)
The frame-budget estimate itself is `ws:morph`'s (4,096-frame path limit). This leaf schedules around it:
- Independently requested photo encoding or face generation never waits for a future Morph's frame budget.
- A Morph that does not fit settles with its reduce-length reason before any Morph-owned acquisition or inference.
- Selected faces are never dropped to make it fit.
Tests in `morph-parent.test.ts`: `photo encode is not held by a pending morph's frame budget`, `over-budget morph settles before morph-owned acquisition`, `no face dropped to fit`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Fake-clock tests: photo -> queued Morph; Morph auto-generation -> explicit face request for the same slot joins rather than duplicates; capability loss while queued; Cancel at each dependency boundary; face-file failure does not block Morph; no deadlock with sparse preview anchors.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic are listed in the destination test discovery (no unlisted test files) and pass in CI.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/opctl/morph-parent.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Fake-clock tests: an independently requested photo encode proceeds while a Morph is over budget; an over-budget Morph settles before any Morph-owned acquisition request (event log); input face count unchanged after the refusal.
notes:
Plan anchor: PLAN.md#application-operation-controller; #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts; #gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design (Treat Morph as a parent intent).
Polish r2 (C): frame-budget scheduling rules from shared resource contracts.

title: Extend the check-migration inventory with research-preservation dispositions
description:
## Background

The research preservation map accounts for families: morph-frame pipeline; WGSL/direct engine (with
`manifest.webgl` coefficients also feeding direct WebGPU); OPFS shard cache; direct RGBA media;
compressed session; photo runtime; current media/video worker; native CUDA; v2 portfolio (10 synthesis,
15 e4e proposals); v3 design. Source invariants: keyed synthesis admission receipts (cold visitor runs
one canary first; others deferred; `fullQualify` runs all); `ort-worker.mjs` `warmMapping()` overlap in
direct and ORT WebGPU incl. mobile GPU; CPU loading sequential; CPU synthesis 1–4 threads; streamed e4e
bounded, unshared, single-threaded; dedicated cache-only worker; Firefox storage-permission timing;
no-third-party gate. Phone contract: adapter probe before GPU acquisition (`navigator.gpu` alone wasted
~180 MiB in Simulator), failure-only preference, visible-time watchdogs, worker-start vs route failure,
constrained worker teardown, 268,435,456-byte e4e WASM limit.

## Why

Each integrated optimisation must keep a destination check so the refactor does not silently drop performance work.

## Scope

- For each integrated path: current source, originating ledger row/report, retained behaviour,
  destination check, disposition (retained, deliberately replaced, historical, proposal, rejected,
  evidence unavailable).
- Map each source invariant and phone-contract item to a destination check or mark the gap with its owner.

## Retained performance evidence register

Carry every row below into the map as a "retained evidence" entry with its claim boundary and the
destination check or comparison that protects it. These are achieved results at their scope, not
absolute limits on a different browser, GPU, artifact, codec resolution or photo flow.

| Cell | Evidence | Claim boundary / destination |
| --- | --- | --- |
| eris RTX 2080 SUPER, Chromium 152 WebGPU, warm, 26-frame morph, ABBA×4 | pipeline 129.8→69.7 ms/frame; RGBA8 42.6→37.1 ms/frame; warm face 103.5→75.6 ms | worker/runtime boundary; protected by `migration.parity-perf`, `verify.artifact-no-regression` |
| eris, OPFS ABBA×4 | model loaded 1430→640 ms; first qualification synthesis 1685→859 ms; prepared-photo encode+reconstruct 17627→12093 ms | excludes upload/alignment/UI; later pairs contended |
| eris live `b322a26`, one built-UI observation | first face 8751 ms; continued 190.4/193.3/207.5 ms; post-reload face 2662.4 ms; 32-frame video 1834.8 ms | single observation, not a paired claim |
| Ubuntu 24.04 Chrome 155 CPU, ABBA×3 | repeat original 113.00→88.76 ms; repeat Save 100.72→66.49 ms; first Save 108.63→202.17 ms while 4.38 MB→117 KB; video 113043→113404 ms | keep repeat reuse; first-Save size/latency tradeoff acknowledged |
| Mac ARM64 WebGPU, Chrome/Brave 151 FP32 | ~254–300 ms/face, ledger v9 277.9 ms | historical full31 |
| Mac ARM64 CPU WASM | CPU4 25.7 s/face, 22.9 s/two faces; CPU1 v9 43.91 s | incompatible revisions; keep CPU/thread support |
| Windows x86_64 Chrome 153 WebGPU | 96.7 ms/face full31; MP4 2.6 s/26 chunks | browser evidence, separate from retired native |
| Physical S24 Ultra Brave WebGPU ORT 1.22 | full31 median 616.35 ms single, 682.39 ms/sequence face; CPU4 2582 ms, CPU1 5911 ms | historical, different providers |
| Android 10 Chrome 152 | CPU4 2300–2400 ms/face passed; CPU1 stalled; tiled GPU failed correctness | keep CPU route and failure recovery; failed GPU never qualifies |
| iPhone 16 Pro Simulator, iOS 18.5 | first full-1024 face 25287 ms; warm synthesis 4741.2 ms | Simulator only; `build.ci-mobile-ios-lane` product job |
| iOS 27 Simulator photo candidate | streamed e4e 32.5–41.8 s; full photo/reconstruction 71.1 s | historical reconstruction used WebGL |
| Physical iPhones; current Firefox/WebKit full performance; GTX 1050 inference | no complete current cell | evidence gap, recorded as untested, not a removal reason |

## No-regression comparison protocol (recorded in the map for every consumer)

Control = pinned candidate artifact by hash (or an explicitly qualified rebuild); same cell and workload
for the candidate. Record provider/model/runtime, resolution/FPS/frame count, cold/retained/resident/
restored state, visible-tab state and the same finish boundary. Protected metrics: first/nth face,
confirmed-photo work, complete video, first/repeated Save, restore, responsiveness, acquired/output bytes,
memory reservations, cancellation. Correctness/resource regressions fail their checks. A latency/bytes
regression is investigated only with compatible repeated evidence and a margin from control/control
variability (from `evaluator.noise-baseline` or the consuming bead's own control pairs); a single noisy
hosted-CI timing is not a speed verdict. Encoded-byte differences are size/cost, not image identity. No
compensation of phone CPU with desktop GPU gains, or 512 px video vs 1024 px.

## Out of scope

A new every-experiment benchmark campaign. Recovering missing historical raw reports.

## Considerations

Missing receipts constrain claims; not an automatic physical-phone cutover veto.

- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Every row of the retained performance evidence register (12 rows) appears in the map with its claim boundary and the destination comparison bead that protects it (`migration.parity-perf`, `verify.artifact-no-regression`, a CI lane, or "evidence gap").
- [ ] The no-regression comparison protocol is written once in the map and referenced by `migration.parity-perf`, `verify.artifact-no-regression` and `ortweb.desktop-perf` (report to their owners if their text diverges).

title: Verify cancel, retry, stale-completion and recovery journeys
description:
## Background
Candidate defect 17 (source): removing a generating face does not stop its job; a saved-MP4 drop can leave Morph queued forever and replaces every face; replacing a photo destroys the face before the new photo is checked; cancelling a queued re-generate can leave a broken image. Flow-matrix rows define Cancel/Retry, supersession and recovery outcomes.

## Why
Cancellation, recovery and stale-result rejection are retained candidate strengths and known defect areas; they must hold in the final app.

## Scope
- Cancel/fail text/seed generation then Retry the unchanged revision without editing.
- Edit/change mode/remove a queued or running tile: only that tile superseded, siblings preserved, late results rejected, Cancelling shown until settlement.
- Cancel/retry one confirmed photo encode in the same slot without recrop or duplicate keypoints.
- Morph cancel at each boundary; partial animation never exported as complete; completed faces survive Morph failure.
- Each defect-17 case as a stale-completion acceptance case.
- Background/reload/close during unfinished work: truthful interruption; completed records retained; lost photo retry pixels after reload need source selection again.
- Return with completed retained work: display/play/save without regeneration; reject late restore after user edits; reload after morph restores faces and result (words restored if the defect-9 proposal ships).
- Missing/damaged/incompatible still recovery: no silent fresh encoding; explicit use-as-photo; model mismatch keeps media viewable/saveable with compute disabled; unsupported video input reported without replacing work.
- Export-only Retry after file-preparation failure keeps pixels visible.
- Replacement commit points (R17): replacing a face with a photo keeps the previous target through a cancelled file picker, a cancelled crop and a rejected recovery; a failed replacement may leave a retryable or empty target while unrelated completed panels stay; the old face is never saved under a newly selected name and a late result never lands in a newer target.
- Morph settings/start/cancel/retry (R36): settings are snapshotted at start, duplicate starts are disabled while one runs, Cancel and Retry keep completed faces, progress never goes backwards.
- Saved-MP4 drop (defect 17): Morph is never left queued for good and faces are never all replaced without asking.
- Rows graded: R02, R06, R07, R17, R25, R33, R36, R43, R44; defects 9 (if the proposal ships, else `not-applicable-by-decision`) and 17.

## Out of scope
Whole-project transactions and elaborate rollback (accepted limit). External MP4 project opening.

## Considerations
- Commit points are accepted; old-face rollback desirable, not mandatory.
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each case scripted with the event log; log shows no inference after cancellation settles and no late result applied.
- [ ] Defect-17 cases each have a named passing case or a recorded failure.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome) through the shared emitter from `build.event-log-core` (fm-bd03) and passes `scripts/check-event-log.ts`; the log is kept as a CI artifact, privacy-filtered like diagnostics; screenshots kept on failure.
- [ ] Each case is listed in this leaf's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix row IDs or defect numbers it grades.
- [ ] UI steps are operated: real pointer/touch at the control's visible position with an `elementFromPoint` assertion that the hit element is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role clicks only for setup; phone-width and desktop-width screenshot per case.
- [ ] Ran against the named release-candidate artifact digest (the same digest the join report checks); a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded failed or untested, never passed.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Prepare and rename the GitHub organization to facemorph-me
description:
## Goal
Rename GitHub organization `check-face` to the selected login `facemorph-me` (brand FaceMorph.me) as an early, separately reviewable change, with concrete edits and a post-rename check prepared beforehand so the window of broken links is short and verifiable. Repository renames and backend archival are already done; their identities are preserved. A rename is not a deploy: the candidate publisher stays in classic and production domains stay unchanged.

## Scope
- **Prepare.** On the day, re-verify (read-only) that the `facemorph-me` login is available/valid and that the operator account has org-owner permission (`users/facemorph-me` returned 404 on 11 and 15 October; that is neither a reservation nor proof GitHub accepts the name; the operator had active admin membership on 11 October).
- From the classified org-link scan, prepare per-repository edit branches (not merged) for active links, remotes and workflow `uses`; candidate-source hits go to the candidate edit set.
- Post-rename check script (`scripts/identity/check-rename.mjs`): repo IDs, archive flag and default branch via API; `git ls-remote` on the new URLs; historical commit resolution (frontend pin `0abb215`, planning ref `b2d945a`); link checker over active docs. Dry-run it against the current org before the rename (pre-rename assertions).
- Native updater references (`desktop/scripts/prepare-release.mjs`, `desktop/tests/packaging.test.mjs`) get their retirement disposition; installed clients are never pointed at the fresh repository.
- **Rename.** Perform GitHub's supported organization rename (settings or API) under an owner account; immediately run the check script.
- Intended URLs: 1413979666 → `github.com/facemorph-me/facemorph.me`; 295956585 → `.../facemorph.me-classic`; 185985766 → `.../checkface` (archived); 348379171 → `.../facemorph-names`; 368806700 → `.../encoder4editing`.
- Update all five local `.git/config` origins, and any other local clone in the workspace carrying the org URL (e.g. `fm-control/`, `fm-direct/`), preserving each repository's identity.

## Out of scope
Merging the repair branches and integration repair (rename repair); domain, candidate branch, promotion or API changes; candidate-source edits.

## Notes
- If the login is refused, stop and add the refusal to the operator's items; never pick another login silently. Org-owner credentials are an execution prerequisite, not an approval step.
- Do not rename the classic checkout back to the monorepo name. Candidate `ISSUE_REPO` stays at its actual repository (new org prefix only).
- GitHub's docs: repository links normally redirect, but the old name can be reclaimed and redirects overridden; reusable action calls and Pages URLs are not redirected.
- Organization branding is not a prerequisite for domain handover, early promotion or API retirement.
- Plan: #organization-rename-execution, #organization-rename-first-known-reference-changes.

title: Reproduce production headers, integrity and static fallback in build and preview
description:
## Background

Production requires COOP/COEP/CORS, WASM/worker/runtime integrity, exact artifact hashing, static route
fallback and qualified-byte promotion. A simple Vite/static server does not supply production headers.

## Why

Threaded WASM and cross-origin isolation behave differently without the real headers; tests must run under them.

## Scope

- Header configuration consumed by both the local test/preview server and the deploy staging (shared
  source of truth with deploy re-homing).
- Checks: response headers on HTML, workers, WASM and runtime assets; `crossOriginIsolated` true where
  required; static route fallback; integrity of runtime assets against manifest digests.

## Out of scope

Domain/promotion changes (deploy re-homing and delivery).

## Considerations

- Shared-file serialisation: `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and
  `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited only in the mandated order (provider simplification, typed facade,
  compute extraction, confirmed-crop fix, morph pipeline, names picker/diagnostics); build items change
  tooling and CI, and add any shared file they touch to the check-migration map's conflict list.
- No worktrees, resets or cleans; preserve other sessions' uncommitted work.
- Hosted-minute economy: use capable workers where practical, but never weaken a required check or
  substitute Linux WebKit for Safari/iOS; never cancel a live publication halfway.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Automated header check passes against the local preview and against a staged (non-published) artifact; a missing COEP fails it.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script involved emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform and provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, retains the log as a CI artifact, and any network claim is asserted from that log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Unit tests for the header checker cover missing COOP, missing COEP, wrong CORS on a worker/WASM asset, a runtime asset whose digest differs from the manifest, and static route fallback; the local preview and staged artifact runs emit the structured event log with response headers per asset class.

title: Enforce decode and crop byte ceilings before large allocations
description:
## Background
The 120 x 1024^2-pixel source limit can represent 480 MiB for one RGBA buffer before decoder, canvas, crop and encoder copies; a compressed-file limit and a one-at-a-time e4e queue are insufficient memory admission. Contracts milestone 2 sets numeric ceilings per decode route from a measured protocol (peak transient bytes per representation on named workers); an unmeasured route has no ceiling and is not admitted.

## Why
Confirmed-crop encoding checks at/over those bounds before duplicate large allocations so phones and constrained devices fail with an actionable message instead of crashing.

## Scope
- Check declared ceilings (retained sources, crop buffers, transient decode, separately) before allocating; decode to a bounded working representation where supported while preserving the confirmed coordinate policy; otherwise report an actionable size limitation.
- Over-budget batch admission produces a reduce-selection/remove-retry-input message before any keypoint allocation; no truncation or hidden eviction.
- Tests at, just under and just over each ceiling per route.

## Out of scope
Setting the ceiling values (contracts milestone 2).

## Considerations
- Two-phase: thresholds are set at contracts milestone 2; until then report "measured, no threshold". This is an implementation contract, not a claim of browser RSS control.

## Relation to the single-input limits (polish r1)
The ceilings sit inside the preserved single-input limits from `photo/crop.mjs` (64 MiB compressed, 120 x 1024^2 pixels, 20,000 px edge); they may refuse inputs those limits allow on a constrained route, never relax them. The check runs after the header inspection and before any full-size decode or copy.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Ceiling values cited from the contracts milestone 2 measurement record; until available, tests report "measured, no threshold".
- [ ] At/over-boundary tests per decode route pass with actionable messages and no duplicate large allocation before the check (allocation spy).
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes: Position in the shared-file sequence: after crop.batch-encode, before media.split. Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Leaves that must not edit these three files: ws:crop.repro (failing tests and the failure analysis only), crop.policy, media.envelope-helpers, media.recovery-schema, morph.descriptor-geometry, compute.consumer-example, compute.names-equality, and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept leaf. They keep the module export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) and move logic behind them into the package. If such a leaf finds it must edit one of the three files, it records the file in the check-migration map conflict list and adds a needs edge to the latest leaf in the sequence that edits it; it never edits concurrently. Each sequenced leaf lists every file it edits in the check-migration map conflict list at claim time.

title: Switch next.facemorph.me to build from the monorepo
description:
## Goal
Handover (1): change next.facemorph.me's build source from classic `candidate/next-delivery-20260916` to the qualified monorepo, with exactly one publisher, a warmed rollback, the second-origin deploy-and-warm step taken over, and the served bug-report link pointing at the monorepo. Classic wind-down cannot start until no consumer points at classic. New-monorepo promotion to the candidate host needs the plan's correctness checks (integrated verification, fail-closed promotion with the research ledger, autoresearch stage 1) without another operator cutover decision; production promotion remains separate.

## Scope
- Authority (operator, 24 October 2026): no operator decision. This is the release bead: it becomes ready
when the release's beads are done; the agent taking it is the release manager, runs full release validation
(every plan flow, the strictly-not-worse gate, all six local CPU/WebGPU cells (eris Chrome, eris Firefox, Huawei Chrome), the available hosted CI matrix) on the
exact artifact and deploys if it passes. A real failure passes beads back instead. Unavailable hosted runners/simulators are recorded as untested with reasons and do not block forever. Missing required local P30 Pro/eris evidence keeps handover incomplete.
- Before state: publisher state for next.facemorph.me (classic `next-site.yml` deploy job enabled, monorepo publisher absent) and current artifact digest.
- Keep the prior candidate artifact as the rollback. Before switching, warm `models.facemorph.me` with every runtime path of the prior candidate artifact and of any artifact live on facemorph.me (the copy fills from next.facemorph.me, which stops serving the candidate's paths after this step); verify by HEAD list.
- Execute: enable the monorepo publisher for next.facemorph.me and disable classic `next-site.yml`'s deploy job for that target in the same step.
- The monorepo publisher takes over the second-origin deploy-and-warm step that classic `next-site.yml` runs after each site deploy (owned by deploy re-homing); verify it ran once after the first monorepo deploy.
- After the switch the served app's Report-error/issue link targets `facemorph-me/facemorph.me` and its `bug-report.yml` template (the candidate's `ISSUE_REPO` pointed at classic until this step).
- The workflow summary names repository ID, branch/commit, artifact and hostname.
- Changeover statistics: after the switch, post the cutover annotation with `scripts/delivery/annotate-cutover.mjs` (from `domain.actions`; tag `facemorph-cutover`, action `candidate-source-handover`, artifact digest). The prior candidate artifact stays the warmed rollback until `verify.field-not-worse` (fm-js8i) reports clean.

## Out of scope
facemorph.me promotion; classic wind-down.

title: Classic wind-down
description:
## Summary
Owns the end state: classic ends as a very clean repository serving the self-host Docker distribution plus its Git history. Starts only after candidate-source handover, autoresearch re-homing (both stages) and deploy re-homing are verified. Automated, no human approval step (operator, 18 October): stages run in order, each when its preconditions verify, each writing a receipt with the precondition check, the change, the reversal path and a post-check. A failed precondition means the stage does not run and is reported. Safety rules: Git history is never rewritten; no branch or tag is deleted; any path with uncommitted changes is skipped and reported; any path model staging or the distribution reads is kept or moved first. Nothing here deletes or archives the repository or personal production records. Terminal.

## Children
`winddown.runner`, `winddown.disable-publishers`, `winddown.clean-tree`, `winddown.forward-pointer`, `winddown.final-acceptance`.

title: Freeze app batch, progress, scheduler, preflight and export-identity types
description:
## Goal

Give the controller port, face controls, operation controller, morph pipeline, acquisition consent, device check and media/recovery one typed application state model: inputs and tile actions, ordered multi-file batches, whole-action progress, recovery classification, the scheduler's permits/leases/residency and Morph parent intent, preflight evidence and estimates, and stable export identity with collision-safe filenames. Discriminated unions make crop-confirm loops and invalid transitions visible at compile time. The candidate today has one slot per dropped file, `selectPhoto` admits one source at a time, and a single Busy/LastRun/Retry cannot represent independent slots.

## Scope

**Inputs and tiles** — `apps/web/src/contracts/inputs.ts`, `tiles.ts`:
- `InputMode` (`words` | `seed` | `selected-name` | `photo` | `restored-still`), `InputRevision`, `SEED_RANGE` (0–4,294,967,295), `WORDS_MAX_UTF8_BYTES = 512` (`browser/identity.mjs`), `WordsValidation` (rejects empty/whitespace; exact string semantics). Typing or changing a source creates a new revision and invalidates prepared file/morph immediately.
- `TileActionState`, one variant per action-table row: empty/invalid → no Generate; valid unfinished → Generate; verified result → result actions; static selection pending → loading/Retry; queued/active → Cancel; non-preemptible stopping → disabled Cancelling; failed/cancelled with retry pixels → Retry with new attempt ID; lost retry pixels → Encode image entry; pixels ready, file pending/failed → Preparing file / file-preparation Retry. `TileCommand` (Generate, Cancel, Retry, Encode image, file-preparation Retry); keyboard/Enter/IME rules as properties.

**Batch, progress, pixels, consent state** — `batch.ts`, `progress.ts`, `pixels.ts`, `consent-state.ts`:
- `BatchSelection`, `SelectionClick`, `GlobalClickOrder`: global cross-file selection-click order (deselect removes, reselect appends; never file/detector/completion order) that survives cancellation, retry and async completion; `KeypointAllocation` atomic first-target/additional-keypoint allocation only when source/target revision matches; mixed recovered-still/photo candidates in one batch.
- Tile Cancel is per slot; `BatchCancel` (modal Cancel) is pre-commit batch cancellation; Retry is one existing slot with a new attempt ID appended to the queue; pending siblings keep order; no implicit batch Cancel.
- `RetryPixelRef`: reference-counted pending/running/retryable pixel ownership, released on success/remove/replace/disposal; tab-only, never persisted.
- `WholeActionProgress` (monotonic per attempt, no stage resets, indeterminate when costs unknown, overlap counted once), `PerCropProgress`, `CompletionBoundary` per action (face/photo: default recovery-bearing file ready; Morph: playable default MP4 with project metadata; name selection: validated static result and prepared default file; persistence/diagnostics outside the boundary), `ComputeReadyVsFileComplete` (file-preparation failure keeps the verified face).
- `AppGrantState` (pending | approved | declined | cancelled, owner per intent).

**Recovery classification** — `recovery-classification.ts`: `RecoveryClassification` = `matching` | `missing` | `damaged` | `incompatible-schema` | `incompatible-model` | `unknown-model`; `classifyRecovery(parse, loadedModel)` from the engine's `parseRecoveryMetadata` result plus loaded model identity. `missing` enters photo encoding only through explicit Encode image / Use as photo; `damaged` is never silently re-encoded and offers Use as photo only when pixels decode; `incompatible-model` covers a known different checkpoint including equal-shaped latents; `matching` installs image and latent with no acquisition, detector or encoder. For `incompatible-*` and `unknown-model` the image is viewable, Save/Share returns the original bytes, the latent never reaches the engine and the face is excluded from Morph with a plain reason. The reader is implemented by media and recovery.

**Scheduler and residency** — `scheduler.ts`:
- `ComputePermit`, `ResidencyReservation` (sessions, shard buffers, WASM heaps, GPU allocations; reserved before allocating), `AssetLeaseRef` (wraps manager `AssetLease`), `MorphParentIntent`, `IntentSettlement` (with specific recovery action), `RouteSnapshot`, `FrameBudget`, `CapabilityStatus` (busy/unavailable from browser adapters), `ConstrainedTeardownPolicy`, `MAX_HEAVY_OPS_PER_PROVIDER_CONTEXT = 1`.
- One app scheduler governs photo encodes, face synthesis and morph production (per-slot queues cannot bound aggregate memory); one heavyweight op per shared provider context, with bounded internal frame pipelining and qualified warm reuse kept. Admission includes runtime init, model/session loading and canary execution; idle warm memory counts until released. Encoder-to-generator transition; constrained iPhone/unknown-memory paths terminate alignment/encoder workers before the next heavy phase (releasing an ONNX session does not shrink its WASM heap); waiting jobs hold no resources the active job needs; speculative warmup never evicts foreground live resources. The 120 × 1024² source limit is 480 MiB for one RGBA buffer.
- Morph parent intent: yields its permit while awaiting dependencies or consent; joins existing operations for the same slot/revision; frame-production lease through the same scheduler; parent Cancel detaches from independently requested face jobs; failed/cancelled inputs settle the parent with a specific recovery action; joins on compute-ready, not file-complete. Frame/slot budget estimated before Morph-owned work; frame budget from the contracts ceilings (classic 4,096-frame value until measured); no truncation of selected faces.
- `RouteSnapshot` at Start/Download approval: requested CPU/WebGPU route, bounded fallback scope, runtime/model identity; actual provider recorded later; selector changes affect new jobs only.

**Preflight** — `preflight.ts`:
- `PreflightEvidence`, `CapabilityFact` (`known` | `unknown` | `failed`), `SampleResult` (completion not submission time; warmup/compile separated), `PreflightOutcome` (`ok` | `skip` | `timeout` | `gpu-lost`; the last three → "no reliable estimate"), `RouteEligibility` ("eligible; model check pending"), `StageEstimate` (range per stage: photo preprocessing, e4e per confirmed crop, synthesis per output, model load/check, video export; with `CalibrationScope` = checkpoint/resolution, provider/runtime, thread mode, workload; and `EstimateSourceClass` = recent actual-device, calibrated local check, comparable device), `AdmissionSplit` (generator, encoder), `ConsentCostRow` (missing bytes, download range, use range or unknown; cold/warm), `MaterialCostChange` (requires revised consent).
- `PREFLIGHT_BUDGETS`: `samplingMs: 2000`, `uiDeadlineMs: 5000`, `scratchBytes: 16 MiB`, `checkerCodeBytesCompressed: 100 KiB`. Preflight is model-free (capabilities, WebGPU adapter/features/limits, WASM/SIMD/threading, coarse CPU/memory hints, short worker WASM and small WebGPU compute samples).

**Export identity** — `export-identity.ts` and `export-identity.vectors.json`:
- `ExportIdentityInput` (crops, ordered inputs, morph mode/settings, model, encoding options), `ExportIdentity`, `ExportKind` (`webp` | `png` | `mp4`) with MIME, `suggestFilename(identity, knownExportSet)`, `SanitizeRule` list, `NoClobberMode` (`browser-download` | `file-picker-no-clobber` | `file-picker-confirm-overwrite`), `ExportNameCollision`.
- `exportIdentityDigest(input)` = SHA-256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, UTF-8, no whitespace) of `{kind, crops[] (ConfirmedCrop identities), orderedInputs[], morph?: {mode, settings}, modelIdentity, format, encodingOptions}`; WebP and PNG of one result share the label with distinct suffixes.
- `SUFFIX_ALPHABET = "bcdfghjkmnpqrstvwxz23456789"` (27 symbols), digest read big-endian, most significant first, `SUFFIX_LENGTH = 6`. Collision = same suggested name, different identity in the session's known export set; extend one symbol at a time up to `SUFFIX_MAX_LENGTH = 16`, then `ExportNameCollision` (never silent overwrite, counter or timestamp).
- Basename (label, `-`, suffix) ≤ `FILENAME_MAX_STEM = 64` characters before the real extension; label truncated at a grapheme boundary; suffix never truncated; an edited name keeps `-<suffix>`. Strip source extension, path components, control/bidi and reserved characters/names; `face`/`morph` only when no label exists. Labels from result name, entered text, seed or source basename (operator examples `emma-k4p7s2.webp`, `seed-42-j8m3r6.png`, `holiday-face2-v9d2h5.webp`, `emma-noah-linear-c6q8t3.mp4`, `emma-noah-figure8-b7w4n2.mp4`).
- Repeated Save/Share of one prepared file reuses its name; identity survives restoration; extension and MIME match actual bytes (PNG fallback updates both). Ordinary downloads leave duplicates to the browser; file-picker writes use no-clobber naming or explicit overwrite confirmation. Filenames never authorise adding text/source names to recovery metadata or diagnostics. No cross-device uniqueness claim.
- Prepared-file cache: key (result revision, format, encoding options); superseded completions discarded; bounded only by bytes — `PREPARED_FILE_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`, named here, value set by the ceilings row from the measured per-tab memory budget (no fixed entry count; operator 24 October: only real resource limits). The current selection's file is pinned; others are evicted least-recently-used when the byte bound would be exceeded. Degraded state (typed): an evicted file shows "Preparing file…" and is re-prepared from retained pixels/frames on the next Save/Share with no new inference; a single file larger than the bound is prepared, handed off and not retained (`PreparedFileNotRetained`).

## Out of scope

Implementation and its tests (operation controller), checker and calibration (device check), filename/recovery implementation (media and recovery), UI rendering, additional export formats (deferred optional item), numeric byte ceilings (milestone 2).

## Notes

- The earlier `PREPARED_FILE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 4` proposal is withdrawn (24 October final pass): a fixed count is an artificial cap; the byte bound from measured memory is the real constraint.
- Additional scheduler concurrency only with measured aggregate memory and cancellation evidence. Device scores stay local under diagnostics consent; a synthetic check never establishes full-model success.
- PLAN.md (newer) drops `contracts.md`, the export index and `docs/decisions/` entries; frozen values live in the TS modules and vector files.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design, #confirmed-crop-and-ordered-multi-selection-flow, #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts, #lightweight-device-check-and-pre-download-guidance, #file-sharing-and-export-direction.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] A type test imports every listed export from `apps/web/src/contracts/*` and fails on a missing or renamed export; it runs in CI.
- [x] Type-level tests per union: every tile action-table row is a `TileActionState` variant with only its allowed `TileCommand`s; invalid transitions fail compilation.
- [x] Typed batch walkthrough tests: A1, B2, A2 across two files with a corrupt third; R → A2 → B1 with a corrupt fourth; click order survives cancel, retry and out-of-order completion.
- [x] Progress completion boundaries per action are type-level states; a test shows progress cannot decrease within an attempt.
- [x] `classifyRecovery` vector file maps each parse result × loaded-model case (same identity, different known identity, unknown identity, equal-shaped different checkpoint) to its classification and allowed actions (view, Save original bytes, Morph excluded, Use as photo); unit tests pass.
- [x] Scheduler typed walkthroughs: photo → queued Morph; Morph auto-generation → explicit face request; capability loss while queued; Cancel at each dependency boundary; idle retained encoder while generator load is requested; a second heavy request waiting without a residency reservation; competing provider-load requests for one context; constrained teardown and qualified warm reuse.
- [x] Preflight typed cases: unknown memory, no adapter, timeout and eligible GPU produce typed states with no model-asset reference; each budget is a named constant with unit.
- [x] `export-identity.vectors.json` covers long labels, bidi, reserved names, a forced collision (crafted digest values passed to the pure name allocator, plus a real 6-symbol prefix collision found by search) extending to 7 symbols, a 16-symbol exhaustion yielding `ExportNameCollision`, a 64-character boundary with a multi-codepoint grapheme at the cut, and WebP vs PNG of one result sharing the label with different suffixes; a reference `suggestFilename`/`exportIdentityDigest` test passes on it.
- [x] Validator fuzzing for untrusted app payloads runs in CI with a fixed seed; every rejection is a typed error.
- [x] Prepared-file cache type cases: byte-bounded with no entry-count constant; the pinned current selection is never evicted; least-recently-used eviction when the next file would exceed the bound; an evicted file's state is "Preparing file…" and re-preparation needs no inference; a file larger than the bound yields `PreparedFileNotRetained` after handoff. A type test fails if a `*_MAX_ENTRIES` constant is exported for this cache.

title: Confirmed-crop policy module: frozen ConfirmedCrop, single derivation and byte ceilings
description:
## Goal
Add the single frozen, versioned derivation from approved pixels to the encoder tensor, with a stable cache/provenance identity, and enforce decode and crop byte ceilings before large allocations. Pure policy code (no DOM/canvas display code) that edits no shared file. fm-6ib8 then rewires the bridge so detection only proposes a crop before OK.

## Scope
- Candidate: `photo/crop.mjs`, `photo/crop-view.mjs`, `photo/image-header.mjs` (EXIF), `photo/selection-worker.mjs`, photo-runtime preprocessing, e4e input `[1,3,256,256]`; crop policy types from the engine contracts (fm-z5wy).
- Frozen `ConfirmedCrop` record created at OK (readonly type plus `Object.freeze`): `{sourceRevision, sourceDigest, rect in oriented source pixels, rotationDegrees, exifOrientation (1-8) and whether applied, policyVersion, policyParams}`; identity = SHA-256 over a canonical encoding of every field.
- `deriveEncoderInput(sourcePixels, confirmedCrop) -> {tensor: Float32Array [1,3,256,256], tensorDigest, policyVersion}` covering all eight EXIF orientations, rotation, crop, resize, color and normalization; reads decoded source pixels, never a UI canvas.
- Single-input limits preserved: `CROP_MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024` ("Choose a photo smaller than 64 MB."), `CROP_MAX_PIXELS = 120 * 1024 * 1024`, `CROP_MAX_EDGE = 20000`, `CROP_OUTPUT = 1024`, `PREVIEW_MAX_EDGE = 4096`; 25 MB limit in `photo/align-photo.mjs` limits only the detector proposal (files between 25 MB and 64 MiB get "detector not run", keep manual crop) — planner rule listed in PLAN.md.
- Byte ceilings per decode route from contracts milestone 2 measurements (fm-2o8q, checked at close); until then tests report "measured, no threshold"; checks run after header inspection and before any full-size decode or copy; over-budget batch admission message before any keypoint allocation.

## Rules
- This bead edits NONE of the shared files (`apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs`). Code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today until the bridge's own turn in the shared-file sequence; the bridge rewiring is the original bead's job.
- Tests run against real models, real browsers and real files where stated; no mocks, fixtures or captures stand in for live proof. The original bead's real-bridge/built-app checks still have to pass before the feature counts as done.
- Split from the original bead in the parallelism pass (operator, 24 October 2026: more parallel work from the start).
- Original bead: fm-6ib8 (Confirmed-crop policy, byte ceilings and direct e4e without redetection); anchors as listed there.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Policy unit tests in Node and a real browser: `confirmed-crop.frozen`, `.identity-fields`, `.orientation-1..8`, `.rotation`, `.non-square`, `.alpha`, `.derive-once`, `.guides-not-burned`, `.limits` (64 MiB accepted, +1 byte rejected; 120 × 1024² pixels accepted, +1 rejected; 20,000 px accepted, 20,001 rejected; rejection raised before full decode), `.align-limit-proposal-only` (30 MB fixture), `.malformed`.
- [x] Policy tensor matches the candidate's qualified preprocessing on aligned fixtures (e4e W+ <= 0.0001 against `encoder-stream/qualification`).
- [x] A test fails if a single-input limit constant changes; import scan shows the policy module has no display/canvas code.

title: Carry over the desktop browser matrix lane
description:
## Background

Classic `next-matrix.yml` engines/summary: CPU product journeys on Ubuntu 24.04 Chromium/Firefox/WebKit
and macOS 14 WebKit/Firefox; manual deployed-origin matrix with pinned runtime/stage reports. macOS
Playwright WebKit is not Safari certification; Linux WebKit is not iOS. There is no dedicated Windows
web-browser job.

## Why

Keep the cells and repair the harness; a definition is not a passing result.

## Scope

- Destination workflow keeping every cell and the manual deployed-origin trigger.

- Artifact lookup, provenance (source repository ID, workflow, run, commit), digest verification,
  the shared path-filter list `scripts/ci/path-filters.json` (every new code root: `apps/web/**`,
  `packages/**`, `scripts/**`, relevant `hosting/**`, not only `src/Next`), concurrency and cache
  keys come from `build.ci-artifact-lookup` (`.github/actions/fetch-artifact`); inherited
  `context.repo` or a corrected org prefix is never used. This lane adapts its own paths, worker
  discovery and source assertions for `apps/web` and all four packages.
- Event log through `build.event-log-capture` (`cdp_capture.py` / `attachPlaywright`), validated by
  `check-event-log` and uploaded with `.github/actions/event-log-upload`.
- Retain the lane's protected behaviour, trigger coverage, required-check role and retained evidence;
  cancel superseded test builds; cache pinned dependencies and immutable runtime assets by identity.
- Every mapped check is listed in the check-migration map with its destination invocation.

## Destination workflow, platforms and pass thresholds

- File `.github/workflows/next-matrix.yml` ("New site browser matrix"), jobs `engines` and `summary`,
  `workflow_dispatch` against a deployed or staged origin input, `fail-fast: false`.
- Five cells, all kept: `ubuntu-24.04` × Chromium, Firefox, WebKit; `macos-14` × WebKit, Firefox.
  Runner installed from `scripts/matrix-tools` (pinned Playwright), driver `scripts/next-matrix.mjs <engine>`
  (repaired by `build.next-matrix-repair`), summary `scripts/next-matrix-summary.py` into the step summary;
  artifacts `next-matrix-<os>-<engine>` and `next-matrix-summary`.
- Pass thresholds: per cell, each stage reports pass/fail/incomplete-not-shipped with cause; the photo
  stage counts as passed only with real encoder events from an independent metadata-free photo; the
  summary lists per-cell outcomes and never shows a failed or incomplete cell as passing. macOS WebKit is
  labelled "Playwright WebKit, not Safari"; Linux WebKit "not iOS".

## Out of scope

Adding Windows or physical-phone qualification claims.

## Considerations

- A workflow definition is not a passing result: record actual run outcomes, and do not advertise cells
  as passing that fail (the 7 October manual matrix run 37555426933 failed; recent GPU evidence failed
  adapter admission).
- Classic's publisher stays live until the explicit source handover; this repository's lanes must not
  publish `next.facemorph.me` (exactly one repository may publish a target at a time).
- Native-package retirement does not retire desktop-browser, mobile or hardware-GPU checks.
- Required statuses and branch-protection bindings come from the inventory, not workflow filenames.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] One recorded run per cell with actual outcomes (failures recorded as failures with cause).
- [ ] Every end-to-end script involved emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform and provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, retains the log as a CI artifact, and any network claim is asserted from that log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] All five cells (ubuntu-24.04 Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, macos-14 WebKit/Firefox) appear in `next-matrix-summary` with per-stage outcomes; no failed or incomplete cell is shown as passing.

Anchor: PLAN.md#platform-ci-retention-and-performance-preservation.
Polish r2 (area B): shared artifact lookup, provenance, path filters, cache and concurrency now cited from build.ci-artifact-lookup (fm-z70g); event log via build.event-log-capture (fm-48ja).

title: Repair the stale next-matrix harness against declared controls
description:
## Background

`scripts/next-matrix.mjs` still targets older bulk Generate/post-result Crop controls and uploads a
previously saved result for `photoE4e`. Recovery-bearing files can now bypass e4e, so that fixture
cannot establish actual photo encoding.

## Why

Repair of a stale check, not permission to remove the browser cell.

## Scope

- Migrate selectors to the declared product/tester controls of the control artifact.
- Use an independent metadata-free photo fixture with actual encoder-event checks for `photoE4e`.
- Preserve stage coverage; label unavailable H.264/project controls as incomplete/not shipped, never
  fabricated passes.
- Emit the structured event log.

## Out of scope

Running the full deployed-origin matrix (ci-desktop-matrix-lane).

## Considerations

- Shared-file serialisation: `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and
  `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited only in the mandated order (provider simplification, typed facade,
  compute extraction, confirmed-crop fix, morph pipeline, names picker/diagnostics); build items change
  tooling and CI, and add any shared file they touch to the check-migration map's conflict list.
- No worktrees, resets or cleans; preserve other sessions' uncommitted work.
- Hosted-minute economy: use capable workers where practical, but never weaken a required check or
  substitute Linux WebKit for Safari/iOS; never cancel a live publication halfway.

- [ ] Every end-to-end script involved emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform and provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, retains the log as a CI artifact, and any network claim is asserted from that log, never from a screenshot.

A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Controller port: input, settings and names reducers
description:
## Background
`Product.fs` update cases at the pinned commit: `Edit`, `Mode` (~431-443), `AddAt` (64-face cap, ~573), `Remove` (~579, invalidates face, photo source and selections), `Kind`/`PinchToggle`/`Frames` (invalidate morph, ~580-582), `Provider` (only when not busy), `OverflowToggle`, `Compare`, `CachedFaceChecked`, `PreviewLoaded`, names `BrowseNames`/`NamesLoaded`/`SearchNames`/`ChooseName`/`CloseNames`/`MoreNames` (~717-734).

## Why
These are the bulk of everyday transitions; exact parity rows in the frozen matrix.

## Scope
Port each case as a pure reducer with transition tests against goldens: revision invalidation calls (`invalidateFace`, `invalidateMorph`, `invalidatePhotoSelections`) become operation-service/effect descriptions; names modal state as the candidate has it (search/Show more still present: their removal is static names' declared change).

## Out of scope
Static-names declared changes; many-face layout/Undo (face controls); seed/word validation changes (face controls) beyond candidate behaviour.

## Considerations
Pure typed reducers (no I/O); effects are returned as descriptions and executed by `migration.ctl-effects`. Calls to scheduling/cancellation/progress go through the operation-service interface (`opctl.interface`), backed by the retained bridge until `ws:opctl` lands. Do not copy candidate defects frozen as repair rows; keep the candidate behaviour for parity rows exactly.

## Source map (classic, read-only, classic `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (or the frozen import revision recorded in `inventory.md`; re-check line numbers there with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`))
`Product.fs` `updateCore` (371-744) cases: `Edit` 431-436 and `Mode` 437-443 (both via the local `change` helper 372-374, which calls `invalidateFace` and clears `CachedFaces`, the face, `VideoUrl` and `Status`); `AddAt` 573-578 (guard `Inputs.Length<64`; new id from `NextId`); `Remove` 579 (guard `Inputs.Length>1`; effects `invalidateFace`, `rememberSourcePhoto id null`, `invalidatePhotoSelections`; drops the face from Faces/PreparingFaces/CachedFaces/Inputs/PendingJobs/PendingFaces and clears `VideoUrl`); `Kind`/`PinchToggle`/`Frames` 580-582 (`invalidateMorph`, clear `VideoUrl` and `SliderFrames`); `Provider` 583 (only when not Busy); `OverflowToggle` 584; `Compare` 585; `BrowseNames` 717 (`openNamesFocus`, resets query/limit 48, loads names once via `loadNames`), `NamesLoaded` 718, `PreviewLoaded` 719-724, `SearchNames` 725, `ChooseName` 726-732, `CloseNames` 733 (`closeNamesFocus`), `MoreNames` 734 (+48). `previewCmd` 297-300 issues `publicPreview` (the per-keystroke request of defect 11 is a repair row owned by static names; port the candidate call for parity rows but do not assert it as required behaviour). The `update` wrapper (746-750) calls `rememberView` whenever Inputs/Kind/Frames/Pinch change: that effect is emitted by `migration.ctl-effects`, but this leaf's reducers must leave the fields so the wrapper rule fires identically.
Retained JS: `photo-selection.mjs` (`openNamesFocus`, `closeNamesFocus`, `invalidatePhotoSelections`), `product-bridge.mjs` (`invalidateFace`, `invalidateMorph`, `rememberSourcePhoto`, `loadNames`, `publicPreview`).

## Goldens replayed
Flow rows: First app visit (init/preview), Enter new words, Enter a numeric seed (0, 4,294,967,295, empty, negative, fractional, out of range), Edit/change mode/remove a queued or running tile, Open names from a face menu, Open/close fullscreen names modal Back/Escape, Find a particular known name (candidate search is a declared change), Add/remove controls, Remove down to one face, Select CPU/WebGPU (the `Provider` message only). Rows the freeze classes repair (defects 1, 5, 7, 8, 11, 18) or declared change are owner-graded, not asserted.

## Goldens and grading (polish r1)
- **Golden store.** Goldens are the recorder output chosen by `migration.golden-spike` (reducer transitions or journey-step DOM/state snapshots), committed under `apps/web/test/goldens/control/<flow-row-id>/` with a `goldens.json` index naming the control `deploy-next/` SHA-256, the recorder command and, per step, the freeze class of its row. Replays run `scripts/fetch-control.mjs` first and refuse to run if the index digest differs from `control-artifact.json`.
- **Parity rows** (freeze class *present and unchanged*): the port's transitions/DOM must equal the golden exactly (state fields, emitted effect descriptions, text, flow order, round-trip bytes). No tolerance, no "close enough".
- **Repair rows** (candidate defects 1-23) and **declared-change rows**: never parity. The recorder tags their steps `repair:<n>` or `declared:<section>` and the replay lists them as owner-graded instead of asserting them. No test in this repository may encode a candidate defect as expected output. Where the defect lives entirely in what this leaf writes (a string, a CSS rule order, a label), write the specification's version; where the repair needs the owner's design or copy, carry the nearest candidate behaviour without asserting it and leave the repair, and its grading against the plan specification, to the named owner.
- **Absent rows** are specification-graded by their owners after parity; this leaf adds no behaviour for them.
- A row the recorder cannot exercise is listed `untested` with the reason, never passed.
design: Files: `apps/web/src/controller/reducers/inputs.ts`, `names.ts`. Test files `inputs.test.ts`, `names.test.ts` replaying goldens, plus named unit cases: Remove of the last face is a no-op; Remove of a queued face drops its `RunFace` from PendingJobs and emits invalidateFace/rememberSourcePhoto(null)/invalidatePhotoSelections in that order; AddAt at 63 adds, at 64 is a no-op (candidate behaviour, repair row 18 not asserted beyond 'no state change'); Provider while Busy is ignored; Kind/Pinch/Frames emit invalidateMorph once and clear SliderFrames; MoreNames adds 48; BrowseNames loads names only when the list is empty. Replay/e2e runs emit the structured event log (step ID = `<flow-row-id>/<step>`, ISO timestamp, control and port artifact digests, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); the log is a CI artifact.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Transition tests per case pass against goldens recorded from the control (reducer- or step-level per the spike decision).
- [ ] Removing a face issues the invalidate/release effects the candidate issues.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic are listed in the destination test discovery (no unlisted test files) and pass in CI.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/migration/ctl-inputs.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: ProjectJson in TS with exact round trips; swap the bridge's Fable import
description:
## Split (parallelism pass, 24 October 2026)
The package/core work of this bead moved to fm-7s3a (ProjectJson in TypeScript: schema, validator and exact round-trip suite), which edits no shared file and starts as soon as its own inputs exist. This bead keeps: the one-line bridge import swap, emptying the unresolved-import allowlist, replacing the classic Fable CI step and skip-reason strings, and the bridge-loads-as-ES-module checks. The scope text below is kept for context; where it describes work now owned by fm-7s3a, that bead owns and accepts it and this bead consumes the result.

## Goal
Port `ProjectJson` to typed TS schema code with exact round-trip parity and swap the bridge's single Fable import to it, so the retained candidate bridge loads as an ES module with no Fable output and every unresolved import fails CI. Split from `migration.facade` (fm-pia9) in the 24 October final pass along the plan's own seam ("land ProjectJson before the bridge swap commit"): the typed facade's runtime harness can only load the bridge after this swap. Embedded MP4 project metadata and session recovery depend on these exact semantics.

## Scope
- ProjectJson: `src/Next/ProjectJson.fs` (266 lines, namespace `CheckFace.Next`, compiled by `src/App.fsproj`) defines the schema for embedded MP4 project metadata and session recovery; fixture `src/Next/project-v1.fixture.json`. Write `apps/web/src/project/project-json.ts` (decode/encode, typed errors replacing Fable's `tag === 1`) and `project-json.schema.ts` (validator for untrusted dropped files) with identical semantics: field names, version handling, rejection of unknown/invalid versions, numeric formatting.
- Round-trip goldens are exact parity: the fixture plus project JSON from control-exported MP4s and session records recorded by the golden recorder; byte-for-byte where textual, structural plus numeric identity otherwise. No repair rows inside ProjectJson; a freeze repair row is graded by media and recovery.
- Carry every classic `src/Next/verify-fable.mjs` (`6107f80`) assertion as a named case in `project-json.test.ts`: round trip (`decode` ok, `encode` ok, `JSON.parse(encode(decode(x)))` deep-equals `x`) for morph kinds `linear`, `pairwise-ellipse`, `pairwise-figure8`, `full-smooth-ellipse`, `full-smooth-figure8`; round trip with `bundle.version` = `quote" slash\ newline\n emoji 🙂` and `truncationPsi` = `0.12345678901234567`; rejection of 12 inputs: `{`, `null`, `[]`, duplicate `schemaVersion` key, `schemaVersion: 2`, unknown top-level `future: true`, morph kind `unrecognized`, `closed: "true"`, width `1e999`, `"schemaVersion":01`, valid JSON followed by `null`, 18-deep nested arrays; latent `space` `z`, `w`, `w-plus` accepted on every control; `space` missing, `q`, `d`, `unknown` rejected; mixed spaces (`z` and `w-plus`) rejected. Plus: unknown version, missing field, wrong types rejected; numeric formatting identical for 0, negative zero, 1e-7, 4,294,967,295.
- Bridge swap: `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` line 9 `import {decode,encode} from './ProjectJson.fs.js';` becomes an import of `apps/web/src/project/project-json.ts` (explicit `.ts` extension for Node 24 type stripping and the test runner), keeping the names `decode`/`encode`; nothing else in the bridge changes in that revision. That import was the single entry in the unresolved-import list (`unresolved-imports.mjs`, run by `import.checks`); after the swap its allowed-entries config is emptied so any unresolved specifier fails CI.
- Replace the classic Fable check `next-site.yml` step `node src/Next/verify-fable.mjs src/Next/ProjectJson.fs.js` with `project-json.test.ts`; `scripts/next-matrix.mjs` ~164-169 and `next-e2e-browser.py` (`projectSaveReopen`) reason strings now name `project-json.test.ts`.
- Bridge text-evaluating tests (`src/Next/fresh-review.test.mjs`, `src/Next/estimate.test.mjs`, which strip `import` lines with `plain()` and run under `node:vm`) and `scripts/check-progress-copy.mjs` keep passing unchanged.
- Project export and open stay hidden (`projectFilesVisible = false` at `Product.fs` 978, off since 21 September; no project toolbar); the schema serves embedded MP4 recovery and session records only.
- Detailed logging: the round-trip suite prints, per golden, the source (fixture, control MP4, session record), byte-equal or structural match, and the first differing path on failure.

## Out of scope
- The typed facade, its coverage checklist, the `check-bridge-imports.mjs` successor and the facade harness (`migration.facade`).
- Dynamic-shape recovery schema versioning (media and recovery). Raising `MaxControls` (`face.many`).

## Notes
- Shared-file order: the one-line bridge swap edits `product-bridge.mjs`, so this row follows `provider.route-admission` and precedes the typed facade. Nothing else in the bridge changes in that revision.
- A round-trip failure is a blocker fixed in TS, never by importing F#.
