title: renderMorph core in stylegan-js with descriptor-driven geometry
description:
## Goal
Move morph orchestration (geometry, infill, frame store and writer) behind one `renderMorph` in `stylegan-js` with bounded memory, and make morph geometry read latent shape from the model descriptor. fm-ioap then rewires the bridge's morph path to it.

## Scope
- Candidate sources (read, not edited): `src/Next/morph-frames.mjs`, `infill.mjs`, `media.mjs`, `video-worker.mjs` (WebCodecs 1024->512, FFmpeg 512, eight-frame raw segments, 4,096-frame path limit), `geometry/latent-path.mjs`.
- `renderMorph({endpoints, settings, descriptor, signal, onFrame, onProgress}) -> video result`; canonical indices and presentation order exposed; preserve bounded GPU submit/readback overlap, windows, ordered delivery and fallback resumption (morph-frame-pipeline-v1), sparse preview anchors that cannot deadlock ordered drain, direct RGBA input, eight-frame raw segments, bounded codec queues, stream-copy concatenation; distinct tested paths: cached frames, raw sparse anchors, blob stream, bounded sequential, retained-then-encode.
- Typed settle status `complete` | `cancelled` | `failed` | `export-failed`; only `complete` yields a shareable video; cancel at frame k returns no video.
- Geometry: lift the `latent-path-v1` 2–64 control-count check (operator, 24 October: no fixed face count; PLAN.md defect 18) with outputs for 2–64 unchanged so `GEOMETRY_VERSION` stays; keep 100,000-frame and fps 1–120 sanity bounds; read latent shape from the descriptor with the same per-layer rotation rules; reject unsupported shapes; all five modes unchanged for FFHQ; `geometry/verify.mjs` keeps passing.

## Rules
- This bead edits NONE of the shared files (`apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs`). Code moved out of the app keeps the export names the bridge imports today until the bridge's own turn in the shared-file sequence; the bridge rewiring is the original bead's job.
- Tests run against real models, real browsers and real files where stated; no mocks, fixtures or captures stand in for live proof. The original bead's real-bridge/built-app checks still have to pass before the feature counts as done.
- Split from the original bead in the parallelism pass (operator, 24 October 2026: more parallel work from the start).
- Original bead: fm-ioap (renderMorph in stylegan-js with descriptor-driven geometry); anchors as listed there.

- [ ] Raw frames equal the control's within the frozen synthesis tolerances (RGB <= 1/255, sampled raw float <= 0.002) on the 32-frame/16 FPS/1024 px workload where supported, in a package-level real-browser harness.
- [ ] `render-morph.cancel-at-frame-k-no-video` (first, middle, last frame and during finalize), `render-morph.writer-failure-export-failed`, `render-morph.complete-has-all-frames`, `render-morph.retention-skips-partial`.
- [ ] FFHQ geometry outputs byte-identical to `latent-path-v1` on the verify suite for all five modes.
- [ ] A non-FFHQ descriptor produces valid paths for all modes, and a morph of that reference model renders within its own declared tolerance.
- [ ] Unsupported shapes rejected with typed actionable errors.

title: Vite targets from the declared browser matrix, with the app shell
description:
## Goal

Make Vite the only bundler from the first app build, with explicit app and worker targets generated from a declared browser matrix taken from the retained CI lanes (Vite's defaults are not a CPU/WebGPU support policy), and port the React app shell every per-screen component mounts into: theme, header/topline/tagline, preview strip, footer and worker bundling. The matrix is a small declared cell list that the build reads for targets and the release summary (integrated verification) reports outcomes against; it carries no outcome states.

## Scope

**Declared browser matrix** (`apps/web/browser-matrix.json`, typed loader)
- One entry per cell: browser, version, OS, device class, provider/runtime, evidence class (static / Simulator / emulator / physical / desktop — kept distinct) and the CI lane that exercises it (or none). No outcome states, run links or rendered view: outcomes are generated into the release summary by integrated verification (`verify.join`).
- Cells: Ubuntu 24.04 Google Chrome (real-ui-cpu); Ubuntu 24.04 Chromium/Firefox/WebKit; macOS 14 WebKit/Firefox (Playwright, not Safari); Android API 35 Pixel 6 emulator Chrome (components, no inference); iOS Simulator Safari macOS 15 (components); iPhone 16 Pro Simulator (product CPU); self-hosted GTX 1050 WebGPU (Chrome for Testing 141.0.7390.54); the device lab on eris (`tools/device-lab/lab.py`): physical Huawei P30 Pro Chrome (`phone-webgpu`, `phone-cpu`) and desktop Chromium on the RTX 2080 SUPER (`eris-webgpu`, `eris-cpu`), run by the release manager and the deploy gate; physical iPhone declared with no lane until the Mac runner exists (reported untested).

**Vite targets and workers**
- Vite config for `apps/web` with explicit `build.target` and worker format/targets generated from the declared matrix, not hard-coded defaults; a matrix row without a version fails generation.
- Bundler-emitted app workers (`image-encoder-worker.mjs`, `video-worker.mjs`, bridge workers) bundled and inventoried separately from manifest-pinned hosted runtime workers/modules (WASM/codec/photo siblings), both hashed into identity. Every emitted worker loads in each matrix browser available in CI.
- `typecheck` stays separate from `vite build`. No bundler upgrade counts as a speed win until fixed first/nth-visit workloads measure it.

**App shell** (`apps/web` Vite + React entry)
- MUI theme equivalent to `ThemedApp`; header/topline/tagline; preview strip (`aside.next-preview-strip` with lead text and links Classic facemorph.me / Its server is retiring / Report an issue via `issueUrl`); faces area mount (`next-faces-area`, `data-next-faces`); footer `next-footer`/`-inner`/`-text`/`-version` (`sourceVersion`)/`-logo` with issue links; root `main.facemorph-page.next-product` with `data-next-busy` and background drag/drop handlers. `product-ux.scss` carried and compiled; `.next-*` DOM/class contract kept.
- Source map (classic, read-only, `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` or the frozen import revision; re-check lines with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`): `Product.fs` `view` 1193–1468 (root 1194–1199, preview strip ~1200–1208, `App.header` ~1223, tagline ~1224, faces area ~1236, footer 1454–1468); `src/App.fs` `header` (277) and `ThemedApp` (375); `src/Config.fs`, `src/FancyButton.fs`, `src/Logos.fs`; `src/Index.fs` (`withReactSynchronous "elmish-app"` mount id). `src/index.html`, styles and public assets come from the candidate import.
- Goldens: recorder output from the golden spike under `apps/web/test/goldens/control/<flow-row-id>/` with `goldens.json` naming the control `deploy-next/` SHA-256, recorder command and per-step freeze class; replays run `scripts/fetch-control.mjs` first and refuse if the digest differs from `control-artifact.json`. Parity rows (present and unchanged) must match exactly (state, effects, text, order, bytes). Repair rows (candidate defects 1–23) and declared-change rows are tagged `repair:<n>`/`declared:<section>` and owner-graded, never asserted; no test encodes a candidate defect as expected output. Rows the recorder cannot exercise are `untested` with reason.

## Out of scope

Porting per-screen UI (migration); production headers and `deploy-next/` replacement (build/deploy step); cell outcomes and the tested browser/OS list (release summary, integrated verification); final preview-strip wording (domain handover owns it — port as in the control).

## Notes

- MUI v4→v9 pixel differences are reviewed, not gated; anything that hides, overlaps or mislabels a control is a defect. Where carrying candidate CSS would reproduce a frozen defect (defect 1: MUI button style out-ranks the Remove close-button rule so it renders below the image, invisible, over the mode menu), carry the stylesheet's intended placement and leave the operated repair to face controls.
- Needs build milestone 1 and the migration facade.

title: Debug-report disclosure, toast labels and privacy text
description:
## Goal
Standing debug-report consent must be discoverable, restorable without a false state and withdrawable at once; a one-shot report must stay one-shot; no prompt may cover an action; and the privacy text must name every outside request and say what a saved file contains. Fixes defects 11 (text part: the FAQ says nothing leaves the device while previews go to a `workers.dev` host, a Cloudflare analytics beacon loads every visit, the name list is fetched on the first keystroke, and saved files carry the exact latent unmentioned), 12 (the failure toast's "Send report" calls `setDebug(true, "toast")`, turning standing reporting on for good, `Product.fs:738`, while the error box's "Send this report" sends once) and 16 (first visit stacks two bottom toasts; at 1,280x800 the first covers Create morph; on a phone it fills a third of the screen).

## Scope
- **Disclosure** at `#debug-reporting`, directly after Help/FAQ (candidate `.next-debug` area): summary **Debug reports: Off** / **Debug reports: On**; expanded: labelled checkbox **Send debug reports until I turn this off.**, copy "Timings, browser/device details and safe error codes. Never photos, typed words, seeds, faces or videos." plus true retention ("kept, with no deletion date" since 17 October; no "30 days" or deletion promise), sending status and report reference/copy access.
- FAQ and footer **Privacy & reports** links expand it and focus the checkbox. Nothing in face burgers, Morph options or output controls.
- Normal origins default Off; restore the actual saved choice (On, Off, No thanks) without briefly showing a false state; preserve the tester invitation and the separate disclosed `labs.*` policy. Persist failure: "Reporting is on for this tab; this choice could not be saved."
- **Off/withdrawal**: stop future uploads, abort pending sends where possible, discard unsent batches and their session-storage mirror, clear the consent-scoped random grouping ID; never cancel inference, remove results or evict models. No debug traffic after Off except a separately approved one-shot. Bounded safe diagnostics may stage in tab memory while Off; debug consent does not claim to disable analytics, which honours DNT/GPC/Save-Data and keeps its own disclosure.
- **Toast**: one contextual report toast while standing reporting is Off, at the bottom edge. **Send this report** sends only the owning failed attempt's bounded safe records (unrelated staged slot records excluded), never enables standing reporting or overrides a stored refusal. Any ongoing-consent action is labelled **Turn on debug reporting** and explains future sending. No opt-in request while On; reporting never blocks Retry; inline owning-error access (error box **Send this report** inline in the owning tile or Morph status) without duplicate prompts or focus stealing. At most one prompt visible at a time; no prompt covers an action.
- **Privacy text**: name every outside request (host class, purpose, trigger) from the names picker's outside-request list, the analytics configuration and the same-origin usage-statistics beacon (`/stats/v1`, carried from the candidate and switched by `diag.usage-stats`), and state that saved PNG/WebP/MP4 files embed the exact latent and model/provenance metadata (never photos, typed words or filenames). Keep the debug disclosure distinct from the analytics disclosure. Re-check whenever a workstream adds an outside request.

## Out of scope
Collector and host rebinding (diag.rebinding); Help page structure (provider workstream); usage-analytics policy changes.

## Notes
- **Shared file.** One-shot scoping needs the owning attempt's reference, but the bridge's `sendReportOnce()` takes no attempt argument and run scoping sits in its `photoStage`/`closePhotoRun`, so this bead changes `product-bridge.mjs` (that export's signature and run scoping) plus `reporting.mjs` and the toast UI; it follows the morph pipeline, in the diagnostics-edits position (ordering edge on `morph.guards`, fm-fy2.9). The disclosure itself calls `setDebug(enabled, basis)` unchanged.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#debug-reporting-control-and-consent, #clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation (standing consent row), #file-sharing-and-export-direction, #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026 (rows 11, 12, 16).
acceptance_criteria:
Operated rule: real pointer/touch at the visible position with `elementFromPoint` returning the control in its region (summary and checkbox in `#debug-reporting`; footer link in the page footer; toast at the bottom edge; error-box button inline in the owning status); by-name only for setup; 390 px and 1,280 px, light and dark, screenshot per case.
- [ ] Saved On / Off / No thanks each restore on reload with no intermediate false render (first-paint DOM snapshot and a 100 ms screenshot series).
- [ ] localStorage throwing: tab-only message shown; reload shows Off.
- [ ] Operated footer **Privacy & reports** and FAQ links expand and focus the checkbox; Tab order visual; label click and Space toggle.
- [ ] Withdrawal during an active job: pending send aborted, unsent batch and session mirror discarded, grouping ID cleared, job completes (intercepted requests, storage and operation trace).
- [ ] After Off: zero collector requests for the session except one approved one-shot whose payload holds only the owning attempt's records.
- [ ] Copy has no "30 days" or deletion promise; DOM scan finds no debug control in face burgers, Morph options or output controls.
- [ ] Operated **Send this report**: one upload with only the owning attempt's records; stored preference unchanged. Operated **Turn on debug reporting**: standing On; later withdrawal via the footer link works. While On no toast offers opt-in.
- [ ] First visit at 1,280x800 and 390x844, and with 1, 2, 3 and 8 faces: at most one prompt; `elementFromPoint` at Create Morph and every face action centre returns the action.
- [ ] Scripted comparison: every outside host class intercepted during a full journey (arrival; typing a seed and a word character by character; names picker open and pick; Generate with a model download; a photo encode; Morph; Save; Share; debug reporting On and Off; host classes site, model host, names/preview host, analytics beacon, usage-statistics beacon, diagnostics collector) appears in the privacy text; the text states file metadata contents.

title: Cached-only jobs need no network; state what works offline (defect 15)
description:

title: Keep the control artifact as a hash-verified release asset
description:
## Background
Candidate import pins the built `deploy-next/` control artifact by SHA-256 and exercises it locally. The classic CI artifact it came from (e.g. `next-site.yml` artifact runs) has limited retention, so it cannot be the only copy.

## Why
Every parity, golden and freeze step uses the control as the oracle. If its bytes disappear or drift, no port claim can be checked.

## Scope
- Upload the exact control `deploy-next/` bytes (and the runtime-manifest/catalogue identities it was exercised with) as a release asset of this repository.
- Record the SHA-256 and the source identity (classic repo ID, workflow/run, commit `b2d945a8...` or the frozen import revision, artifact name) in the repository (e.g. `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/control-artifact.json`).
- Add a script (e.g. `scripts/fetch-control.mjs`) that downloads the asset into a scratch location and re-verifies the digest; every parity/golden run calls it first and fails closed on mismatch.
- The control stays labelled as the control carrying classic's identity; it is never presented as this repository's build.

## Out of scope
Building the control (never rebuilt: no .NET). Populating `deploy-next/` for the interim `build:next` wrapper (candidate import).

## Considerations
Artifact lookup must name source repo ID, workflow/run, commit and artifact explicitly; inherited `context.repo` or a corrected org prefix cannot locate a classic artifact from the new repo. No weights in the asset (runtime bytes are acquired separately by the digest-checked mirror procedure).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Release asset exists; digest recorded in the repository matches a fresh download.
- [ ] Verification script fails closed on a tampered copy (test with a one-byte change).
- [ ] A scan of the asset finds no model weights, credentials or private provenance.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic are listed in the destination test discovery (no unlisted test files) and pass in CI.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/migration/control-custody.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] `scripts/fetch-control.mjs` logs the source identity, expected and actual SHA-256 and bytes, and exits non-zero on mismatch; every golden/parity/freeze script calls it first (grep test).
notes: Plan anchor: PLAN.md#application-migration (Control custody).

title: Post-delivery check script (app, retired, page, redirect, unchanged) and cutover annotation helper
description:
## Goal
Give every delivery action one reusable, read-only proving step: a Playwright post-delivery check parameterised by hostname, expected artifact identity and mode (app, retired, page, redirect, unchanged), plus a best-effort Grafana cutover annotation helper, so each action in `handover.md` (`domain.actions`, fm-5u9) ends with the same verifiable check. Needs no monorepo build.

## Scope
- **Post-delivery check** `scripts/delivery/post-delivery-check.mjs` (Playwright), parameterised by hostname, expected artifact identity and mode:
  - `app` (default): HTTP 200 with no console error; served artifact identity (build id / identity-file digest) equals expected; runtime manifest fetched; one model chunk verifies against its pin from the site origin **and** the same chunk directly from `models.facemorph.me`; names catalogue fetched and parses; a test diagnostics report (marked test, filterable; marker documented for the collector) is accepted; the same-origin changeover-statistics route `/stats/v1` is bound to the statistics Worker (a POST with a foreign `Origin` gets the Worker's documented refusal, identified by its response marker, never the site's 404), which proves the route without adding to any counter.
  - `retired`: DNS and HTTP probes of given hosts assert they no longer serve (NXDOMAIN, connection refused, or 4xx/5xx with no API body); 2xx or any 3xx is a failure (no replacement, GUID resolver, result-link redirect or proxy allowed). Probes `/`, `/api/face/?seed=0&dim=512` and one historic GUID-style path per host, redirects not followed; status, `Location` and body digest recorded per probe.

  - `unchanged`: compares each host's current artifact identity with a supplied before-identity.

- **Cutover annotation** `scripts/delivery/annotate-cutover.mjs`: posts one Grafana annotation to `metrics.facemorph.me` (tags `facemorph-cutover` plus the action name; text with hostname, artifact digest and run URL) through a Grafana service-account token held as a CI secret, best effort: a failure is logged and never fails or undoes the delivery. Only people read these annotations (the statistics check uses the `build` and `host` labels), so they carry no acceptance.

The retirement inventory, `handover.md`, names-host plan and runbook dry run (`domain.actions`, fm-5u9). Executing any delivery action; removing anything; integrated verification journeys; package registry checks; dashboards (the annotation is tag-scoped).

title: Exercise placement and useful degradation in the built UI
description:
## Background
The clean-placement table fixes one visible home per state (selector above first +, tile status, Morph status, consent modal, result action area, Help, `#debug-reporting`). Provider simplification removed WebGL execution and native routes; bounded CPU fallback remains.

## Why
Restriction and failure must surface before cost, in the owning action, without disabling working routes.

## Scope
- Phone CPU and eligible phone GPU/photo paths; unavailable operations; null adapters/insufficient limits; failed canaries; slow admitted work; active device loss.
- Missing GPU triggers no GPU downloads and leaves qualified CPU generation; known-ineligible routes stop before detector/model network or crop; another supported operation stays usable.
- Full-model check failing after authorized acquisition: bounded CPU fallback, revised assets/cost consent, contextual Retry, never native fallback; no desktop-download recommendation.
- Research preservation map items: adapter probing, visible-time watchdogs, worker-start/failure separation, constrained worker teardown, phone encoder limits, without the per-device lab encoder check at startup.
- Names, recovery-first file entry (Open saved image label), compatible playback and Save stay usable.
- Catalogue failure/offline uncached results; denied/quota-limited storage; known-unavailable MP4 preparation; post-inference export failure; lost photo retry pixels after reload; offline with cached models states what works.
- Whole visible output and decoded full-size face / complete video bytes incl. disclosed 512px fallback; reason/Retry/Help placement; no duplicated warning panels.
- Pick a name on a cold, slow or offline connection (R09): the face's action slot shows loading then Retry; the prepared result validates before Save or Morph; never a synthesis fallback.
- Offline with models cached (defect 15): the page states what works; if the planner proposal ships, a job whose files are all cached completes with zero network requests and the model manifest is not re-fetched per job (request log); otherwise record the decision.
- Desktop-package recommendation retired (R49): no native build, update or download link or recommendation anywhere.
- Rows graded: R03, R09, R14 (fallback part), R16 (storage/quota part), R34, R49; defect 15.

## Out of scope
Physical-phone inference qualification; measured usability promises.

## Considerations
- Mocked capabilities and available browsers are allowed for these UI/negative checks.
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each state appears only in its specified home (screenshot per case at phone and desktop width).
- [ ] Request log shows no GPU/model fetch for ineligible routes before refusal.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome) through the shared emitter from `build.event-log-core` (fm-bd03) and passes `scripts/check-event-log.ts`; the log is kept as a CI artifact, privacy-filtered like diagnostics; screenshots kept on failure.
- [ ] Each case is listed in this leaf's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix row IDs or defect numbers it grades.
- [ ] UI steps are operated: real pointer/touch at the control's visible position with an `elementFromPoint` assertion that the hit element is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role clicks only for setup; phone-width and desktop-width screenshot per case.
- [ ] Ran against the named release-candidate artifact digest (the same digest the join report checks); a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded failed or untested, never passed.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: stylegan-js README, API docs, runnable examples and acquisition guide; npm name check
description:
## Goal
Someone outside the project must be able to use the engine from public docs alone. This row writes the `stylegan-js` README, generated API reference, runnable examples (including the non-face example used by the joint proof) and model-acquisition guide, every code block executed by a docs test against the packed tarball, and settles the real npm names and scope by a registry availability check so docs, imports and the reviewer packet use the final names.

## Scope
**README (`packages/stylegan-js/README.md`)**
- What it is and is not; install; supported browsers/providers and build targets (worker bundling, WASM paths, COOP/COEP for threaded routes and single-thread behaviour); ownership/resource semantics (dispose, abort, errors); progress; first-use vs warm costs; descriptor and supported model shapes; numerical qualification statement with the frozen tolerances (RGB <= 1/255, sampled raw float <= 0.002, e4e W+ <= 0.0001, descriptor-specific tolerances for other models); recovery metadata contents and limits; troubleshooting.
- Near the top: "Using a new dataset means acquiring or training a compatible StyleGAN2 checkpoint first; this project does not train models." The main documented deployment is a browser app with static model assets; Node, headless and server inference are listed as unsupported unless a provider with its own evidence is documented.
- The FFHQ e4e limitation appears before any encoder acquisition snippet and any photo-upload example: photo-to-latent inversion needs a separately trained compatible encoder; the shipped FFHQ e4e is not generic; non-face generation and morph load no face detector and no e4e.
- Non-face label: until the joint non-face proof (`verify.packages`) passes, the README says non-face support is unqualified and names the blocker; it never calls package extraction "generic dataset support".
- Recovery semantics: the dynamic-shape schema version; schema-1 PNG and schema-2 PNG/WebP readers still supported; the typed error when equal-shaped latents from different checkpoints are combined; unknown models stay viewable as media without editable inference and without following metadata URLs.
- Lossless helpers are a library capability and do not change the FaceMorph app's lossy WebP 0.8 policy; exact model/latent/provenance values are separate from decoded-pixel quality.
- Supported model shapes equal the rows marked supported in the model-conv compatibility table.

**API reference and examples**
- Generated API reference from the emitted `.d.ts`, covering every public export.
- Runnable examples, no pseudocode: direct caller-loaded use (no manager), manager-loaded use, morph via `renderMorph`, PNG/lossless-WebP export and reopen, and the non-face example (manager-loaded and caller-loaded: load the converted non-face model, map, synthesize, morph, export/reopen PNG and lossless WebP, with the no-detector/no-e4e note).
- Model acquisition: NVlabs sources and terms, link to the compatibility table; no bundled weights.

**npm names**
- Working names `stylegan-js`, `browser-model-manager`, `cloudflare-model-host`. Read-only registry check (`npm view <name>`, scope existence) for each, working names first; if one is taken, use a scope the operator controls (organization login `facemorph-me`), never a confusingly similar unscoped name.
- The check is a script run in CI; the chosen names land in the `package.json` `name` fields and the docs; it re-runs immediately before publication (names can be taken in between), and the publication step uses the current result.

## Out of scope
Manager, host and converter docs (pkgdocs.others). Publishing and npm credentials (`gate.npm-creds`, delivery).

## Notes
- Newer PLAN.md (24 October) wins over the earlier text asking for a `docs/decisions/` names entry: the name fields plus the CI check output are the record.
- Edits no shared bridge/runtime/worker file.
- Needs `manager.quota` (edge added in the 24 October final pass): the manager-loaded examples run against the finished `browser-model-manager` tarball.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #stylegan-js, #external-developer-journey-and-non-face-models, #independent-published-package-acceptance (what publishes).

title: Sub-result 3 (packages and non-face): non-face joint proof
description:
## Goal
Sub-result 3 of integrated verification: packages and non-face. Only the non-face joint proof qualifies the
documented non-face capability; component completion or publication alone does not. Local packs allow the proof before
npm publication. This bead runs it from checkpoint to export and reopen in the clean consumer and emits the sub-result
3 output (clean consumers, conversion load, non-face proof), which feeds `pkgdocs.release` and the release summary.

## Scope
- Independently of the FaceMorph app, in the clean consumer from `verify.consumers` (fm-3pne; same tarballs, same
  integrity hashes).
- Input: the hand-off bundle from `conversion.qualify` (fm-fy2.15): checkpoint source, digest and terms; container
  and base-image digests and the exact commands; reference errors against the declared tolerance; descriptor and
  schema-valid manifests. Re-check every digest before use; a mismatch aborts the run. If the fixture was recorded
  blocked (converter or terms), record non-face support as unqualified with that blocker and run nothing else; this
  does not delay API retirement.
- Proposed fixture: NVlabs AFHQ cat 512 px, subject to converter compatibility and acquisition terms; not currently
  claimed supported. Generic code must not assume FFHQ's fixed 1024 px / 18x512; descriptors govern shapes.
- Trusted checkpoint acquisition (source/digest, terms recorded); pinned container conversion and independent
  reference checks with a declared small tolerance for this model; developer-controlled static hosting (no FaceMorph
  hostname, catalogue, alias or secret); manager-loaded and directly caller-loaded inference; seed mapping, synthesis,
  multi-input morph; PNG/lossless-WebP export and reopen with exact model/latent metadata; equal-shaped latents from
  different checkpoints never silently combined; no face detector or FFHQ e4e download (intercepted requests).
- **Sub-result 3 output:** machine-readable result naming the source commit, artifact digest and each pack's integrity
  hash, with the clean-consumer, conversion and non-face cells in the closed outcome set.

## Out of scope
Dataset training; a generic non-face photo encoder. Registry publication.

## Notes
- Integrated verification checks the final integrated app (after the planned UI and package changes) against the Next baseline (`facemorph.me-classic` branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) plus the plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped. Not historic-API parity and not a shutdown-qualification campaign. Performance and reliability against the control, including control/control noise and the physical iPhone, are judged by the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27), not here. Correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found here are fixed in the owning bead and this bead re-runs. Wording says planned, experimental, implemented or deployed. No weights, secrets, photos or typed inputs in Git.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #external-developer-journey-and-non-face-models, #integrated-verification (non-face paragraph,

title: Write the range, unknown and slow-work guidance copy used by consent and action areas
description:
## Background
Defect 20: the candidate's cold-device estimate text can never appear. `estimate.mjs` cold synthesis constants are
historical single-device priors.

## Why
Consent and slow-work guidance need honest ranges or honest unknowns.

## Scope
- Range strings for Generate (per face), Encode (per confirmed crop and batch), download time, and an optional compact
  Morph total beside Create Morph when reliable (including final video preparation or labelling the missing cost).
- Unknown copy ("Download time depends on your connection"; "No reliable estimate for this device").
- Slow-work nudge based on the affected workload range, never a phone label: "This may be slow here. For faster face
  generation and morphs, try a computer with WebGPU." with Continue/Cancel retained and **Using a computer** linking to
  Help; without a reliable range only general Help advice.
- Warnings that switching apps/tabs may pause work and closing/reloading can lose unfinished photo inputs.
- Relabel historical priors; never present `encodeMs` as photo encoding.

## Out of scope
Help page content (`ws:provider`).

## Considerations
Photo encoding also depends on CPU, so WebGPU is no promise of faster e4e.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** It is a copy/estimate-string module plus its rendering in the ported UI sources. If implementation finds it must edit one of them after all, it first runs `br dep add fm-tz5v fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph), adds the file to the conflict list in fm-bhw and records the change in its receipt (the plan's rule: an edge is added when an edit is discovered).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests over the copy builder: calibrated, comparable-device, uncalibrated and unknown inputs produce the specified strings; no range rendered without evidence; nudge triggers on range, not user agent.
- [ ] Rendered in the consent modal and Morph status at 390 px and 1,280 px (screenshots).
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic run in CI (`npm test` workspace target) and pass.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Make the self-host start with one command
description:
## Background
Classic self-host today: `self-host/compose.yml`, `compose.gpu.yml`, `setup.py`, `Dockerfile`, `legacy-route-inventory.json`, `verify.sh`, pinned frontend `0abb215` in `self-host/frontend-overlay/source.json`, `torch 2.9.1+cu128`, NVlabs StyleGAN2-ADA commit `d72cc7d`. Current self-host work is on `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`; the remote default `master` publishes legacy production through Vercel. Rot hazard 4: the quickstart is multi-step (clone, `cd`, export `COMPOSE_FILE`, build, separate setup run, `up`), says `cd facemorph.me/self-host` though the clone dir is `facemorph.me-classic`, and clones a feature branch. Target quickstart:
`git clone <canonical-url>` / `cd <repository>` / `ACCEPT_MODEL_TERMS=yes docker compose up`.

## Why
Operator direction: one-command, README-executed self-host.

## Scope
- Root `compose.yaml` that `include`s `self-host/compose.yml` (confirm minimum Compose v2 version; workstation has 5.5.1).
- Setup service downloads and checksum-verifies the three assets (dlib landmarks 64,040,097 B; StyleGAN2 checkpoint 381,673,535 B; e4e 1,201,649,680 B on Google Drive); API starts only after setup completes successfully; logs clickable `http://localhost:8080` once healthy.
- Missing terms acknowledgement: stop with where the terms are and the exact command, exit non-zero, never hang; never default acceptance.
- CUDA default; CPU an explicit documented override; no NVIDIA runtime → clear failure, no CPU fallback.
- Interrupted setup recovers on next `up`; corrupt/partial asset rejected by hash; verified files reused.
- README quickstart block marked for extraction with `<canonical-url>` as a variable.

## Out of scope
Mirrors or overrides for weight hosts (D6: none). Publishing a backend image (D5: never; the user builds it locally because it carries NVIDIA-licensed code and CUDA libraries).

## Considerations
Upstream hosts stated plainly in the README.

- [ ] Local runs (development, branch named) show: missing terms fails fast with instruction; kill during setup recovers; corrupted asset rejected; restart reuses volumes without re-download (the log shows zero weight bytes downloaded on restart).
- [ ] Unit tests for `setup.py` verification: wrong sha256 rejected; partial file resumed or replaced; verified file reused; missing acknowledgement exits non-zero with the terms location and exact command.
- [ ] Receipt `docs/receipts/classic-one-command.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime/model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Ship stylegan-js package surface, caller-loaded consumer example and the shared package-tarball-content-scan
description:
## Background
Contracts require a clean caller-loaded consumer that need not import the manager. The engine package must emit consumer-ready JS, public `.d.ts` and explicit worker exports without app aliases or React. The library's independent CPU/reference capabilities are distinct from the app's product routes.

## Why
Independent usability of the engine is a programme goal and a prerequisite of package publication and documentation and of the independent published-package acceptance.

## Scope
- `package.json` exports map (main, types, worker entry points), emitted `.d.ts`, no workspace aliases, `files` allowlist.
- `packages/stylegan-js/examples/caller-loaded/`: a minimal browser example that loads a model capability itself (no manager import), maps a seed, synthesizes, morphs a short sequence and disposes; shows progress, abort and errors.
- Document and qualify the library's independent CPU/reference capabilities (which providers, which browsers, what is unqualified), with no native distribution requirement.
- Tarball content scan: no weights, fixture blobs, host URLs, OPFS, UI, reporting transport, repository-only paths or secrets.

## Out of scope
Public README/API docs and quickstart (package publication and documentation). npm publication (delivery).

## Considerations
- Package construction and status/capability reads must start no acquisition.
- Node/headless inference is not implied; only documented provider support counts.

## Content scan as a named, reusable test (polish r1)
Create `scripts/packages/check-tarball-contents.mjs` (test ID `package-tarball-content-scan`) here, with profiles for all four packages (see Citable contract below), and run it in CI on every pack. `pkgdocs.consumer-smoke`, integrated verification, hosting and delivery run the same script rather than writing their own. Engine-specific rules on top of the shared ones: no host URLs, no OPFS or Cache Storage calls, no DOM/UI imports, no reporting transport.

## Citable contract: `package-tarball-content-scan` (polish r2)
This bead **creates** the one tarball content scan that every other bead cites by name: `scripts/packages/check-tarball-contents.mjs`, test ID `package-tarball-content-scan`. Created here (not in `pkgdocs.consumer-smoke`) so integrated verification (`verify.packages-clean-consumers` fm-3pne, `verify.packages-nonface` fm-9lt0), delivery's pack step, hosting's pack scan and the publication smoke all run the same script from the moment the first package exists, and none writes its own.
- Command: `node scripts/packages/check-tarball-contents.mjs --profile <stylegan-js|browser-model-manager|cloudflare-model-host|model-conv-context> --input <tarball.tgz | build-context dir> --report <out.json>`. Exit 0 = clean, 1 = findings, 2 = usage error or unknown profile (an unknown profile never passes silently).
- Profiles live in `scripts/packages/tarball-profiles/<profile>.json`. All four are created here, from the package boundaries the plan states, so later beads never wait to "extend" the scan; a profile change is a reviewed diff with its self-test fixture.
- JSON report: `{scanVersion, profile, input, inputSha256, files: [{path, bytes, sha256}], findings: [{rule, path, detail}], requiredMissing: [], outcome}`; kept as a CI artifact and cited by digest in receipts.
Shared rules (every profile). The script lists each tarball (`tar -tzf`) or build-context directory and fails on:
- weights or model blobs: extensions `.onnx`, `.ort`, `.bin`, `.pt`, `.pth`, `.pkl`, `.safetensors`, `.npy`, `.npz`, `.h5`, `.tflite`, and any file over a declared size limit (default 5 MiB) not on an allowlist of runtime WASM files;
- repository-only paths: `apps/`, `autoresearch/`, `docs/receipts/`, `docs/plans/`, `.beads/`, `deploy-next/`, `experiment/`, test fixtures, source maps pointing outside the package, and absolute or sibling paths (`/home/`, `../facemorph.me-classic`, `file://`) inside emitted JS, `.d.ts` or `package.json`;
- secrets: npm tokens (`npm_` prefix), Cloudflare API tokens, private keys (`-----BEGIN`), AWS-style keys, `.env` files, `.npmrc` with auth;
- private provenance: FaceMorph production hostnames or R2 bucket names in engine/manager code (host package docs may name them only as an example origin).
It also checks the required files are present: emitted JS, `.d.ts`, worker entry points named in `exports`, `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`, provenance record. Self-test: planted fixtures (a fake `.onnx`, an `apps/web/` path, a fake npm token, a missing `.d.ts`) must each make the scan fail; the scan writes a JSON report (file list with sizes and digests, findings) kept as a CI artifact.
- Profile-specific rules on top of the shared ones: `stylegan-js` has no host URLs, no OPFS or Cache Storage calls, no DOM/UI imports and no reporting transport; `browser-model-manager` has no engine/inference code and no FaceMorph catalogue or hostnames; `cloudflare-model-host` has no weights and names FaceMorph origins only in docs examples; `model-conv-context` (the converter's Docker build context) has no checkpoints, converted outputs, `.env` or credentials, and its `.dockerignore` excludes them.
- Self-test (`package-tarball-content-scan.self-test`): one planted fixture per rule class and per profile (a fake `.onnx`, an `apps/web/` path, a fake `npm_` token, a missing `.d.ts`, an OPFS call in the engine profile, a checkpoint in the converter context) must each fail with the expected rule ID; a clean fixture must pass.
- CI: runs on every `npm pack` of each package and on the converter build context.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `npm pack` tarball installed in a clean project outside the monorepo compiles against the emitted `.d.ts` and runs the example in a real browser (Chromium CPU at least; WebGPU where a real adapter exists).
- [ ] Network log: zero requests at construction/status reads; only caller-initiated model reads.
- [ ] Content scan passes (script committed, run in CI).
- [ ] Independent CPU/reference capability table committed with evidence per cell.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots are kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Network claims are asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] `package-tarball-content-scan` exists with a self-test and passes on the `stylegan-js` tarball in CI.
- [ ] All four profiles (stylegan-js, browser-model-manager, cloudflare-model-host, model-conv-context) exist and the self-test fails each planted fixture with the expected rule ID and passes the clean fixture; the command line, exit codes and JSON report match the Citable contract section.
notes: This leaf (compute.consumer-example) is outside the shared-file sequence and must not edit the three shared files. Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Leaves that must not edit these three files: ws:crop.repro (failing tests and the failure analysis only), crop.policy, media.envelope-helpers, media.recovery-schema, morph.descriptor-geometry, compute.consumer-example, compute.names-equality, and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept leaf. They keep the module export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) and move logic behind them into the package. If such a leaf finds it must edit one of the three files, it records the file in the check-migration map conflict list and adds a needs edge to the latest leaf in the sequence that edits it; it never edits concurrently. Each sequenced leaf lists every file it edits in the check-migration map conflict list at claim time.

title: Formalise docs/decisions and docs/receipts: READMEs, templates, receipt schema, writer and validator
description:
## Background

The plan: the decision log lives in `docs/decisions/` and receipts in `docs/receipts/`. Division of
work is fixed (not "whichever lands first"): source and repository identity (`identity.decision-log`,
fm-orh) runs first, **creates both directories**, writes the first dated decision entries (the ten
17/18 October decisions, D1-D7, cropper, serialization), the open entries Q1-Q4, the proposal
entries P1-P4, its own receipts (`docs/receipts/identity-*.md`) and the entry checker
`scripts/decisions/check-entries.mjs`. This bead runs after it and adds the READMEs, templates, the
receipt schema, writer and validator, and the CI job. It does not create the directories or enter
any decision.

Receipt schema (16 October): source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where
relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells;
evidence link. A receipt that omits one is incomplete, not passed.

The retained harnesses are mixed-language (Playwright/Node `scripts/next-matrix.mjs`; Python with
`browser-harness==0.1.8` in `scripts/next-e2e-browser.py`, `scripts/next-gpu-benchmark.py`,
`scripts/next-ios-sim.py`; the Python mobile runner `tests/mobile/run.py`), so the receipt writer
and validator exist in TypeScript and Python.

## Split (polish round 2)

The former single item is split into three reviewable leaves under `ws:build.m1`, all owned by
workspace build:
- **this bead** (`build.docs-decisions-receipts`): READMEs, decision and receipt templates, the
  receipt schema, writer, validator and the `receipts` CI job; the ownership statement.
- **`build.event-log-core`**: the e2e event-log schema, the TS and Python writers, host classes,
  privacy filter, `check-event-log` and the network query/assert primitives (no browser).
- **`build.event-log-capture`**: the Playwright attach helper, the Python CDP/browser-harness hook,
  the cross-language fixture journey and the CI artifact upload convention.
Beads that only write receipts need this bead; beads that emit or validate logs need the event-log
leaf they use (the core for validation and network assertions, capture for browser-driven runs).

## Ownership (single owner; other beads cite this)

Workspace build is the **only** owner of the receipt schema, receipt template, receipt writer and
receipt validator (this bead) and of the event-log schema, emitters, host classes, privacy filter,
log validator and network primitives (the two event-log leaves). Every other bead that writes a
receipt or runs an end-to-end script uses these and must not define its own schema or emitter.
Integrated verification's harness (`verify.harness`, fm-48bj) builds on top: it owns
release-artifact pinning by digest, operated-input helpers, width sweeps, case manifests, screenshot
conventions and journey assertions, and imports the receipt writer from here and the emitter, host
classes, privacy filter and network primitives from the event-log leaves.

## Why

Every acceptance in the plan writes a receipt. One schema and validator make incomplete receipts
detectable mechanically instead of by reading.

## Ordering

Needs only `ws:identity` (no workspace scaffold), so it lands before candidate import and before
every build.m1 CI lane. The modules are dependency-free: erasable-syntax-only TypeScript run directly
by Node 24 (the CI pin) through type stripping, and Python 3 standard library only. Once
`build.workspaces-ts` (fm-qja) lands, `scripts/evidence/**` joins the strict `typecheck` and
`npm test` (that bead's scope).

## Scope

### READMEs and decision template (directories already exist)
- `docs/decisions/README.md` and `docs/receipts/README.md`. Keep every entry identity wrote
  unchanged: its date, outcome, decider and status are never edited; only front-matter reformatting
  to the template is allowed, recorded in this bead's receipt.
- Decision entry template `docs/decisions/_template.md` with exactly the fields identity's entries
  use: date (ISO), title, outcome, decided-by (`operator` | `planner's call` | `automated gate` |
  `workstream`), status (`decided` | `open` | `proposal, operator may veto` | `superseded`),
  consequence, PLAN.md anchor, owner bead ids (open/proposal), supersedes (path, when an answer
  replaces an open entry), receipt links.
- The `receipts` CI job (below) also runs identity's `scripts/decisions/check-entries.mjs` on
  `docs/decisions/**`; this bead does not write a second decision checker. If the template adds a
  field, the checker gains it in the same revision with a fixture.

### Receipt schema, writer and validator
- `docs/schemas/receipt.v1.schema.json` (JSON Schema, for external tools) and
  `docs/receipts/_template.md`.
- Receipt file: Markdown with YAML front matter. Required keys: `schema: receipt/v1`, `receipt_id`,
  `bead` (tracker id and plan key), `workstream`, `date` (ISO 8601 with offset), `status_label`
  (`planned` | `experimental` | `implemented` | `deployed`), `source_commit` (full SHA plus
  repository ID), `artifact_digest` (sha256, or `not-applicable: <reason>`), `runtime_identity` and
  `model_identity` (digest/version, or `not-applicable: <reason>`; empty is invalid),
  `command_or_run` (exact command with working directory, or workflow name + run URL/ID), `platform`
  (OS, browser + version, device class, worker name), `provider` (requested and actual), `outcome`
  (`pass` | `fail` | `inconclusive` | `untested` | `blocked` | `measured-no-threshold`),
  `deviations` (list; `[]` allowed only explicitly), `untested_cells` (list; `[]` allowed only
  explicitly), `evidence` (links: CI artifact, event-log digest, report path), optional
  `decision_refs` (paths under `docs/decisions/`, required when the work implements an open or
  proposal entry or a delivery action).
- `scripts/evidence/receipt.ts`: `parseReceipt(text)`, `validateReceipt(obj) -> {ok, errors[]}`,
  `writeReceipt(path, fields)` (refuses to write an incomplete receipt), plus
  `scripts/evidence/receipt.py` with the same writer/validator for Python harnesses.
- `scripts/check-receipts.ts`: validates every file under `docs/receipts/**` (except README and
  template); exits non-zero with `file:key: message` lines and prints one JSON line per receipt
  (path, outcome, status_label, ok). CI job `receipts` in the static-checks workflow, triggered on

title: Package converters in a pinned container with the compatibility table
description:
## Goal
`packages/model-conv` turns supported pretrained StyleGAN2 checkpoints into the chunks, model descriptor and manifests the providers and manager need, starting from the existing classic exports and pinned upstream converter code, and runs them in a pinned Docker container with an opt-in Compose service so there is no host-specific virtualenv and the toolchain that produced each provider artifact is known. A published compatibility table states exactly what was qualified, so developers do not assume every StyleGAN checkpoint works. Generator, optional photo encoder and preprocessing identities stay separate throughout.

## Scope
**Converter package**
- Import the needed converters from classic into `packages/model-conv`: `experiment/onnx/export.py`, `phase1_export.py`, `e4e_export.py`, `block_export.py`, `precompute_demodulation.py`, `fold_resampling.py` and related tools (some under ignored `experiment/`), and `photo-runtime/encoder-stream/export.py` (writes `e4e-onnx-sequential-shards-v1` manifests: 108 steps, FP32, preprocessing SHA). Read classic in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the frozen import revision (planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`). Downstream consumers to keep compatible: `hosting/next-static/*.py`, `browser/stage-assets.py`.
- Pin upstream revisions (NVlabs stylegan2-ada-pytorch, e4e) with digests, licences and notices. Do not import the private lab or ignored caches; any upstream fetch is recorded with its checksum.
- One CLI entry with `convert` and `verify`, producing chunks, a model descriptor, manifests (digest/shape metadata valid against the contracts' host/converter manifest schema) and a reference/parity report.
- Architecture, resolution and operator limit declarations per supported model.
- Python/PyTorch stays in Python inside its owner; no JS rewrite. Python unit tests for manifest generation and shape declarations.
- Docs warn, before the command, that pickle loading requires a trusted checkpoint.

**Container**
- `packages/model-conv/Dockerfile`, base images pinned by digest, locked Python/PyTorch/export dependencies, a `.dockerignore` bounding the context, Compose conversion service behind an opt-in profile. Converter code, tools and notices in the image; no pretrained weights, credentials or large/generated artifacts in the build context or image.
- Caller-acquired checkpoints mounted read-only, outputs writable, optional tool/download caches as separate volumes; outputs owned by the invoking UID/GID.
- Documented clean-clone `build`, `convert`, `verify` commands (copyable, real). CPU reference conversion/verification where the exporter permits; optional documented NVIDIA profile (host driver + container toolkit, pinned CUDA/PyTorch stack) with no silent fallback and no arbitrary GPU claims.
- The report records image digest, tool/source versions, input checkpoint checksum and provenance, conversion flags and output manifest/digests.
- Empty-cache and repeat conversion; interrupted or failed runs leave no partial output labelled complete.
- Validated OS/architecture/provider matrix; absent hardware evidence shown as untested.
- Byte-reproducibility is claimed only if proven; otherwise list the nondeterministic fields and require numerical/identity parity.
- **Independent reference in `verify`:** the pinned upstream PyTorch implementation (stylegan2-ada-pytorch at the recorded revision; e4e for the encoder) loads the original checkpoint inside the container and produces raw outputs for a recorded seed/latent set with constant noise; the converted artifacts run under ONNX Runtime CPU on the same inputs. The report gives max absolute raw-float error, max RGB difference (0–255) and, for the encoder, max absolute W+ error, against the tolerance declared for that model before the run. FFHQ uses the frozen values; other models declare their own.

**Compatibility table**
- `packages/model-conv/docs/compatibility.md`: source serialization (which PyTorch/TF pickle variants are actually accepted), StyleGAN architecture, conditional/unconditional, resolution/channels, Z/W dimensions and W+ layer count, precision/operators and qualified providers; each cell qualified / unqualified / unsupported from actual runs; unsupported cells name the failure or an available conversion route; checkpoint source, digest and model-specific usage/redistribution terms.
- Acquisition docs for NVlabs and the linked catalogue without claiming every catalogue checkpoint works (the upstream list includes conditional models, which does not establish converter support).
- States, before a developer downloads an encoder or designs an upload UI, that photo-to-latent inversion needs a separately trained compatible encoder and FFHQ e4e is not a generic non-face encoder.
- Cells are updated as FFHQ and the non-face fixture qualify (conversion.qualify); unverified cells say so.

## Out of scope
Hosting/publishing chunks (model hosting). Registry image publication (none planned; any later push needs a licence check first). Conversion during app startup. Package READMEs (pkgdocs, which link this table). The classic API inference container, which is separate and unchanged.

## Notes
- Containerization grants no model rights; acquisition terms and acknowledgements stay explicit.
- The container's build context is scanned with `package-tarball-content-scan` profile `model-conv-context` (created by `compute.package-surface`); if this row lands first, run the equivalent rules on the context and adopt the shared script when it exists.
- Distribution (17 October): the converter ships as this Dockerfile and opt-in Compose service at a tagged public release, base images pinned by digest; no npm package and no registry image.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #model-conversion-container, #model-conv, #conversion-tooling, #external-developer-journey-and-non-face-models.

title: Build the README-is-the-test clean-clone harness
description:
## Background
Validation rule: a script extracts the README's marked quickstart block and runs it verbatim, never a hand-copied equivalent, into an empty directory with no existing images, volumes or build cache.

## Why
Guarantees the documented commands, not a prepared tree, are what works.

## Scope
- Extraction + runner script with assertions (healthy, URL logged, `/healthz` cuda, face image, frontend render, restart reuse, kill-during-setup recovery, corrupt asset rejection, missing-terms fast fail, no-NVIDIA clear failure, CPU override run).
- Pre-switch mode substitutes the branch explicitly and labels the run a development run.
- README: validated-matrix table (OS, Docker, driver, GPU, commit, date) claiming only cells that ran; measured first-run time and disk use; 'frozen, no feature updates'; upstream weight hosts (D6); 'Not guaranteed' list (pre-Volta GPUs, future Docker/driver behavior, third-party hosts).
- README also states what the default build reaches on the user's machine (D5: no published backend image): Docker Hub, Debian apt, PyPI, download.pytorch.org and GitHub (pinned NVlabs commit `d72cc7d`), and that dlib is compiled from source; and the minimum Compose v2 version that supports `include` (polish r2).

## Out of scope
The recorded post-switch run.

## Considerations
Runs on a GPU worker under the shared lease.

title: Move Browse Names into each face's burger menu bound to the stable face ID
description:
## Background
Candidate `Product.fs` `setpointField` renders Browse Names as a separate end adornment on the field (with
`tabIndex=-1`, defect 4). Historical `src/MorphForm.fs` is an additional field-menu reference. Static names owns the
modal and result consumption; face controls owns the menu entry and stable-ID capture (tie-break table).

## Why
Declared change "Move Browse Names into burger menu"; no page-wide selected-face mechanism.

## Scope
- Remove the adornment; add Browse Names to that face's existing burger/mode menu, keyboard reachable.
- Opening captures the face's stable ID and the originating focus; picking returns to that tile; dismissing leaves it
  intact; a removed/revised target invalidates the pending selection.
- No first-empty fallback, no implicit new slot, no `/names` navigation.

## Out of scope
The modal itself and static results (`ws:names.picker`).

## Considerations
Soft edge: the menu entry can land before the names modal; until then it opens the ported candidate modal.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** It edits the ported tile/menu UI (`setpointField` replacement) and calls `openNamesFocus`/`closeNamesFocus` (`photo-selection.mjs`, not a serialized file). If implementation finds it must edit one of them after all, it first runs `br dep add fm-uq8p fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph), adds the file to the conflict list in fm-bhw and records the change in its receipt (the plan's rule: an edge is added when an edit is discovered).

- [ ] Operated-UI rule: each acceptance step acts with real pointer input (touch tap at phone widths) at the control's visible position, asserts `document.elementFromPoint` at that point returns the control (or a descendant) and that the point lies inside the region a person would look in (named per control below); by-name/by-role clicks are used only to set up state, never as the acceptance step.
- [ ] Every case is checked at a phone width (390 px) and a desktop width (1,280 px) with one screenshot per case kept as evidence.
- [ ] Operated: open the burger at its visible position on face 2 of 3, choose Browse Names; the modal opens bound to face 2 (controller state); dismiss -> focus returns to face 2's burger.
- [ ] Remove face 2 while its picker is open (scripted) -> pending selection discarded, no write to another face.
- [ ] Keyboard: Tab reaches the burger, Enter opens, arrow keys reach Browse Names.

title: Declare the ledger handover point and add the classic forward pointer
description:
## Background

Record the final classic ledger prefix hash and last journal entry IDs; the first appended row here cites
them; keep the 11-column header; never initialise an empty ledger; corrections are new rows referencing
prior IDs. After handover classic receives no new rounds and only a forward pointer.

## Why

One canonical writable ledger and journal; no silent fork of two histories.

## Scope

- Compute and record the prefix hash (bytes of `results.tsv` at snapshot) and last journal IDs.
- Record the handover as a dated `log.md` entry and a `state/runs.jsonl` journal event citing them (never a `results.tsv` row: the ledger appends evaluated outcomes only). The first evaluated outcome row appended in this repository carries the prefix hash and last journal IDs in its notes/provenance cell.
- Classic forward pointer: one separately reviewable commit in classic adding a pointer in its research
  README, excluding other sessions' changes; skip and report paths with uncommitted edits.

## Append-only continuation checks

- `scripts/check-research-ledger.mjs` (CI on every change to `autoresearch/**`): `results.tsv` keeps the
  exact 11-column header; the file at HEAD starts with the file at the merge base byte for byte (rows only
  appended); the classic snapshot prefix hash recorded at handover still matches; every new row has a
  unique ID; corrections reference an existing prior ID; no unrun proposal is entered as an outcome
  (outcome column from the record standard's enum). `log.md` files in dated rounds only grow at EOF with
  unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps.
- Fork detection: the same script, given read access to classic, compares classic's
  `autoresearch/results.tsv` on its default and candidate branches with the recorded handover prefix and
  reports any row appended in classic after handover as a failure ("new round in classic"), so no second
  writable history appears silently.
- The forward pointer in classic's research README says: research moved to this repository at <commit>;
  canonical ledger and journal live at `autoresearch/results.tsv` / `autoresearch/state/runs.jsonl` here;
  start no new rounds in classic.

## Out of scope

Removing classic's research tree (classic wind-down).

## Considerations

No time box, no human approval step and no fallback or backport to the classic stack (operator rulings, 17 and 18 October 2026).

A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Promote the retained candidate to facemorph.me (early production promotion)
description:
## Goal
Let the operator put the existing working on-device candidate on facemorph.me before the monorepo, package and research work finishes, so the hosted API can be retired with a working on-device site in place. This uses the candidate's own ordinary functional and artifact evidence, not integrated verification, and does not mean the monorepo is complete. It is an operator option covered by the cutover decision.

## Scope
- Authority: before any change, read the operator's cutover decision (`gate:cutover`, recorded in PLAN.md's dated decisions) and confirm it names **early promotion of the retained candidate** and the artifact digest. Closing `gate:cutover` unblocks this bead but does not authorize it; if no decision names this action, make no change and report `blocked: no authorizing decision`.
- The promoted artifact is byte-identical to the one the candidate's ordinary qualification passed (classic `next-site.yml` `qualify` and `compiled-ui` green for that digest after the candidate edit-set merge), so its CPU/WebGPU/mobile routes are the qualified ones and native recommendations are already removed. title: Controller port: jobs, download gate and the typed effect runner
description:
## Goal
Complete the first part of the controller port (part of the TS/React milestone): job lifecycle, download gate, progress, save/share/import reducers and the typed effect runner that replaces Elmish `Cmd`, with their goldens replayed at controller level. This is where the UI meets the operation layer: reducers call a narrow operation-service interface rather than embedding scheduling, so the operation controller can replace the bridge-backed implementation without touching the UI. Photo and crop reducers and the full controller-level golden replay follow in `migration.ctl-photo` (split in the 24 October final pass so each part fits one reviewer sitting).

## Scope
- Source: classic `b2d945a8` or the frozen import revision (re-check lines with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`).
- Jobs/gate (`reducers/jobs.ts`, `gate.ts`, `schedule.ts`): helpers `noticeTask` 375 (Save/Share failure "Couldn't save or share this file. Try Save instead."), `schedule` 388-399 (builds `{kind:'face'|'morph'|'import'}` descriptors from `PendingJobs`, blocked faces from PreparingFaces/Crop/CropQueue/PhotoChoice; ported as a pure function that emits an operation-service `requestNext` description; the bridge-backed service from `opctl.interface` calls `scheduler.mjs` `nextScheduled(descriptors, {busy, blockedFaces, blockMorph})` so candidate ordering is exact); `CachedFaceChecked` 400-404; gate `RunFace` 405-408 (`checkCachedFace` first), `(RunFace|Run|Import)` gate 409-410, `GateAccept` 411-417 (`consentToDownload`; photo consent adds route), `GateCancel` 418, `DownloadsChanged` 419, `DownloadNow` 420-423 (`downloadModels`), `HideModelToast` 424; `CancelFace` 586-592 (`cancelQueuedFace`); `RunFace` while Busy/preparing 593-595 (`queueFace`); `Run "morph"` queued behind busy/preparing/PhotoChoice/Crop 596 (`PendingMorph`); `RunFace` 597-605 (snapshot `RunInputs`, `rememberView`, `execute`); `Run action` 606-618; `RestoredLast` 619-621 (only when JobId=0, RunInputs empty and the first input is still `hello`; abandoned after user edits); `Progressed` 622-650 (`frames-available`, `diagnostics-*`, `route-admitted`, `route-rejected`, `photo-acquisition`/`photo-tools-ready`, job progress gated by `jobId=state.JobId`); `Completed` 666-678 (photoChoices -> PhotoChoice; cropFace; normal with `displayMilestone`); `Failed` 683-686; `Cancel` 687 (`cancelWork`, Stage `cancelling`, "Cancelling…"); `Save`/`Share` 688-689; `Export` 690-692; `Import` 693-697 (pending while Busy); `Notice` 698; `Retry` 740-743 (re-dispatches `LastRun`). Job-ID gating of late events preserved.
- Candidate `DownloadConsent` is a broad route/photo set and unknown inventory bypasses `gateScope`; port as-is for parity (the bounded grant is acquisition consent's declared change).
- Retained JS: `scheduler.mjs` (+ `scheduler.test.mjs`); bridge `execute`, `cancel` (as `cancelWork`), `queueFace`, `cancelQueuedFace`, `checkCachedFace`, `consentToDownload`, `downloadModels`, `saveMedia`, `shareMedia`, `exportProject`, `importProject` (photo functions are wired in `migration.ctl-photo`).
- Effect runner (`controller/store.ts`, `effects.ts`, `subscriptions.ts`): typed effect descriptions and a runner (React `useReducer` + effect queue or an equivalent small store with `useSyncExternalStore`; no new state framework); single dispatch queue with synchronous drain, matching `src/Index.fs` 18-20 `Program.mkProgram ... |> Program.withReactSynchronous "elmish-app"` (one message fully processed and rendered before the next). Replaces `Cmd.OfPromise.either` (`previewCmd` 297-300, `noticeTask` 375, `dequeue` 383-387, `checkCachedFace` 405-408, `loadNames` 717), `Cmd.ofMsg` (`schedule`, `GateAccept`, `Retry`), `Cmd.ofSub` in `init` 311 (`subscribe (Progressed >> dispatch)`, `subscribeDownloads (DownloadsChanged >> dispatch)`), `Cmd.batch`. Subscriptions to bridge progress/download/report-status through the facade.
- Direct reducer side effects that become descriptions: `invalidateFace`, `invalidateMorph`, `rememberSourcePhoto`, `invalidatePhotoSelections`, `openNamesFocus`/`closeNamesFocus`/`focusCropArea`, `setDebug`, `consentToDownload`, `downloadModels`, `cancelWork`, `queueFace`/`cancelQueuedFace`, `rememberSlider`, and the `update` wrapper's `rememberView` (746-750, when Inputs/Kind/Frames/Pinch change, plus once in `RunFace` 602). Effect order: a reducer's effect list runs in emission order before any Cmd-derived dispatch (the candidate performs reducer side effects synchronously, then Elmish runs returned Cmds).
- View-side effects stay in components: `scheduleFill`/`flushFills` (771-787), `displayMilestone` on image load (888, 893), `dragStart` (753). No compute/model I/O or bridge singleton moves into React; the runner calls only facade/operation-service functions.
- Golden replay: `apps/web/test/controller/replay.test.ts` iterates `goldens.json`, runs each parity step through composed reducers + runner with the control's recorded events fed to the pure reducers as input data (no service double), diffs next state and emitted effects; prints a per-row result (`passed`/`failed`/`owner-graded`/`untested`) in the CI log. Replays run `scripts/fetch-control.mjs` first and refuse on digest mismatch with `control-artifact.json`. Parity rows exact; repair/declared rows owner-graded, never asserted; no test encodes a candidate defect; unexercisable rows `untested`. Failures are fixed, not skipped; no blanket disabled suite.
- Rows replayed: First app visit (no model prompt on arrival), Return with completed retained work (RestoredLast and abandonment), Cancel/fail text/seed generation and Retry unchanged input, Approve/refuse missing-model acquisition (candidate gate), Download/cache/quota failure, morph settings/start/cancel/retry, Save face WebP/PNG or morph MP4, Share/cancel share, Save repeatedly, `?testing` bulk Generate. Repair rows 10, 15, 17, 18, 19 and declared changes (bounded grant, Morph auto-generation, whole-action progress) are owner-graded. Photo and crop rows replay in `migration.ctl-photo`.
- Retire source-reading checks owned here: none beyond what `migration.project-json` (`verify-fable.mjs`, `next-matrix.mjs`/`next-e2e-browser.py` skip reasons) and `migration.facade` (`check-bridge-imports.mjs`) already replaced; the photo/crop source checks (`crop-queue.test.mjs`, the shared multiple-faces sentence) retire in `migration.ctl-photo`, which also runs the global no-`Product.fs`/`.fs.js` scan.
- Remaining candidate JS tests listed in `next-site.yml` (`scheduler`, `estimate`, `last-result`, `photo-selection` other cases, `fresh-review`, `route-choice`, `testing-link`, `logging`, `route-report`, `reporting`, `stage-labels`) keep running unchanged and stay listed in `check-tests-listed.mjs`.
- `scripts/check-progress-copy.mjs` reads `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` as text (`MORPH_SPOKEN_STAGES` = exactly `morph`,`export`; morph-only gate `if(jobCounts.framesTotal>1&&!MORPH_SPOKEN_STAGES.has(stage))return;`; `stage:'morph',text:` from `first.text`/`finished.text`; `stage:'export'` present) and drives `createFrameCounter`/`morphCounter` from `stage-labels.mjs`. It runs unchanged against the retained bridge and passes; if a matched line has moved into TS, re-point the regex with the same expectations. Replacing frame-only expectations is `opctl.progress`.

## Out of scope
- Scheduler/residency/intent/progress implementations (operation controller); consent modal redesign; photo/crop reducers (`migration.ctl-photo`); confirmed-crop repair (crop); batch proposal and crop modal redesign, paste entry (face controls); React components and rendering-level checks.

## Notes
- Pure typed reducers (no I/O); scheduling/cancellation/progress only through `opctl.interface`, bridge-backed until the operation controller lands.
- The controller port owns the UI state machine only; the operation layer is the operation controller's.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-migration (Controller port versus the operation layer); #application-operation-controller; #language-and-framework-direction; #workspace-build-and-artifact-identity (concrete seams).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] `jobs.test.ts` / `gate.test.ts` / `schedule.test.ts` replay goldens and named cases: stale `Completed`/`Failed`/`Progressed` for an old JobId leave state unchanged; `RestoredLast` after an edit is ignored; `Import` while Busy is queued once; `Run "morph"` while a crop is open sets PendingMorph and queues once; `GateAccept` for photo scope consents photo and route; `Retry` with no LastRun only clears the error; Cancel sets Stage `cancelling` and "Cancelling…"; `route-rejected` stores `Rejected`; `diagnostics-*` progress never changes Busy.

- [x] `effects.test.ts`: each description kind calls the matching facade function once; promise rejection maps to the candidate's Msg (`PreviewLoaded(...,"")`, `Notice "Couldn't save or share this file. Try Save instead."`, `CachedFaceChecked(item,false)`, `Notice e.Message`); teardown unsubscribes both subscriptions; effect lists run in emission order before Cmd-derived dispatch.
