title: Add main-field image paste, rename Upload image to Encode image, remove duplicate filename and hold-to-compare
description:
## Background
Candidate: per-face burger/file entry labelled Upload image, file/drop/recovery dispatch, a filename caption
repeated under the field and a Hold to compare control (all visible in locked `recovered image.png`). Image paste
exists only inside the historical `EncodeImageDialog.fs`; the candidate's main text field has no image paste.

## Why
Declared changes in PLAN.md#next-release-ui-and-photo-requirements: Encode image rename, paste equivalence, remove
the duplicate filename line, remove hold-to-compare.

## Scope
- Rename every photo-encoding label/entry point to **Encode image**; where photo encoding is genuinely unavailable,
  the same entry reads **Open saved image** (recovery-only), no duplicate control.
- Main-field paste: image clipboard data takes precedence over coincident text; a single image uses the same
  recovery-first/photo dispatch as the file chooser (same consent/crop/encoding flow); without image data ordinary text
  paste is unchanged; mixed/unsupported items give a contextual message and no unintended text replacement.
- Drop on a face binds that stable target; background drop uses the first empty face or appends one.
- File dispatch inspects recovery metadata first: a valid matching still installs without models; missing/damaged/
  incompatible metadata are distinguished; damaged/incompatible never silently re-encodes (explicit Use as photo in the
  existing error area); external MP4 input is reported unsupported without replacing work.
- Remove the separate filename caption (the field may show the filename).
- Remove hold-to-compare: button, pointer/keyboard gesture, instructions and stale state; no replacement gesture.

## Out of scope
Batch selection (batch leaves); the crop modal itself.

## Considerations
Replacement commit points: keep the previous target through a cancelled chooser or rejected recovery where simple;
never install a late import into a newer target. No new drop target or import toolbar.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** It edits the ported tile, field and menu UI and calls the existing recovery-first import and photo dispatch unchanged. Removing hold-to-compare leaves the bridge exports `rememberSourcePhoto`/`sourcePhotoUrl` unused; this bead removes their facade entries and UI calls, and records a conflict-list row in fm-bhw so the next bridge-editing bead in the order deletes the two exports (no bridge edit here). If implementation finds it must edit one of them after all, it first runs `br dep add fm-v8dw fm-fy2.9` (ws:morph), adds the file to the conflict list in fm-bhw and records the change in its receipt (the plan's rule: an edge is added when an edit is discovered).

- [ ] DOM scan: no hold-to-compare element, handler or copy; no duplicate filename caption.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic run in CI (`npm test` workspace target) and pass.
- [ ] Each end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Every network claim is asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.

title: Controller port: effect runner and subscriptions (Elmish Cmd replacement)
description:
## Background
Elmish `Cmd.OfPromise.either`, `Cmd.ofMsg`, subscriptions (`subscribe` progress callback, `subscribeDownloads`), the `schedule` helper, `requestAnimationFrame`-batched progress fills (`scheduleFill`/`flushFills`), `rememberView` and `displayMilestone` calls are the candidate's effect surface.

## Why
Reducers stay pure only if a small typed effect runner executes their effect descriptions; this is the store the React view subscribes to.

## Scope
- Typed effect descriptions and a runner (React `useReducer` + effect queue or an equivalent small store; no new state framework).
- Subscriptions to bridge progress/download/report-status events through the facade, dispatching typed messages.
- Ordering guarantees equal to Elmish (messages processed in dispatch order).
- Harness test running reducers + runner through the real bridge (facade harness) for one face and one morph.

## Out of scope
React components.

## Considerations
No compute/model I/O or bridge singleton moves into React; the runner only calls facade/operation-service functions.

## Source map (classic, read-only, classic `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (or the frozen import revision recorded in `inventory.md`; re-check line numbers there with `git show <rev>:src/Next/Product.fs`))
- Program wiring: `src/Index.fs` line 18-20 `Program.mkProgram NextProduct.init NextProduct.update NextProduct.view |> Program.withReactSynchronous "elmish-app"` (synchronous dispatch: one message fully processed, view rendered, before the next).

title: Whole-action progress, offline cached jobs, real-bridge trace
description:
## Goal
One honest progress bar per requested action, from acquisition to usable file, replacing the candidate's per-job stage progress (`Progress {jobId, stage, text, fraction, face}`) with stage resets and frame-only morph copy; cached-only jobs that need no network (defect 15); and the operation controller's gate-style acceptance: switch the operation service from bridge-backed to scheduler-backed and prove with one real-bridge run that the scheduler drives real runtime work in the expected order with correct settlement.

## Scope
- One progress contract (types from contracts milestone 2) spanning missing-model acquisition, local checks/load, confirmed input preparation, encoding/synthesis, morph frames and selected file preparation.
- Freeze known work and provider/model identity at the request boundary; phase weights from scoped measurements; overlap counted once; monotonic per attempt, no stage resets; never advance while waiting for a user decision; bytes and frame counts never mixed as one unit; indeterminate with bytes/count detail when costs are unknown (no race to 99%).
- Completion boundaries: face/photo when its default recovery-bearing file is ready; Morph when the playable default MP4 with project metadata is ready; name selection after the static result is validated and the default file prepared. Persistence and diagnostics are outside the boundary.
- Batch: the common acquisition prefix belongs to each affected slot; Morph composes prerequisites without double counting or restarting a completed tile's bar. Retry starts a new attempt; cancellation/failure settles the bar and keeps usable results.
- Replace `scripts/check-progress-copy.mjs` (source-text regexes over `product-bridge.mjs`/`stage-labels.mjs`) in the same revision with behavioural tests through the operation service (`apps/web/src/operations/progress-copy.test.ts`), at least as strict: one monotonic whole-action fraction per attempt for path order 26 frames, infill order 26 and 64 frames, a repeated frame (`[0,3,3,1,2]` of 4), and acquisition + face + frames + MP4 phases interleaved, never resetting on stage change; frame counter stays secondary detail worded exactly `Generating X / Y images` (X counts finished frames, never decreases in any order, final X equals Y; `Encoding` and `Generating images` never appear in it: the operator's 21 September release gate); non-morph stages never write the morph status line; MP4 preparation is reported (classic `stage:'export'` check) so the action never ends in silence; completion only at the playable default MP4 with project metadata; `morphCounter(3, 26)` still returns `Generating 3 / 26 images`. Delete the old script or reduce it to the counter cases. Rendering is `face.morph-output`.
- Offline (defect 15: with models cached and the network off, a new face failed with "The local generation engine stopped."; every job re-fetches the model manifest with no cache): jobs whose manifest and assets are verified locally run without network, with the manifest identity held per in-flight app (no re-fetch per job); offline messages in the owning action say what works (names' cached complete assets, completed files, cached-model generation); a genuinely missing asset gives a typed failure with Retry, never a generic engine-stopped error.
- Trace run: switch the service implementation to scheduler-backed; in the facade harness on CPU run two faces (one word, one seed), a Morph with one unfinished input, cancel one face mid-inference, Retry it (new attempt ID), file preparation for both and the MP4. Expected trace committed as `apps/web/test/harness/opctl-expected-trace.json`: ordered events with symbolic IDs (request, input revision, attempt), permit and reservation acquire/release, provider requested/actual, compute-ready, file-ready, cancelled, settled. Compare ignoring timestamps and mapping concrete IDs consistently; a mismatch prints the first divergent event. GPU cell under the shared device lease where available.

## Out of scope
- Rendering the bar (face controls); calibration data (device feeds measurements).
- Service worker/offline install (explicitly not promised). Integrated UI journeys (integrated verification).

## Notes
- Offline behaviour is partly a planner proposal (flow-matrix row "Use the page offline with models cached" is Planned); the operator may veto. If vetoed, drop the offline-message criterion; the zero-network cached job and typed missing-asset failure (defect 15 repair) stay.
- If the offline fix edits `product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` or `browser/ort-worker.mjs`, it follows the morph pipeline in the shared-file order (provider simplification -> typed facade -> compute extraction -> confirmed-crop fix -> morph pipeline -> static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics reporting rebinding); add that edge when discovered.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#application-operation-controller; #shared-resource-and-release-version-contracts (one immutable manifest identity per in-flight app); #gaps-with-reasonable-solutions-inside-the-accepted-design (Whole-action progress); #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026 (defect 15); #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance (Application operation controller).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Property tests: progress is monotonic for any event interleaving; completes only at the default-file boundary; unknown costs yield indeterminate; bytes and frames never share a unit.
- [ ] Tests: Retry starts a new attempt; cancellation/failure settles the bar and keeps usable results; a completed tile's bar never restarts inside a Morph.
- [ ] `progress-copy.test.ts` covers the four classic orderings (26 path, 26 infill, 64 infill, repeated frame) plus interleaved phases, the exact `Generating X / Y images` wording with `Encoding` banned, no stage reset, MP4 preparation reported, completion only at the default-file boundary; no regex over bridge source remains for these expectations; the retired script cases are listed in `tests/retired.txt` with the new test file.
- [ ] E2E in the facade harness (real bridge and runtime bytes): with models cached and the network blocked, a new face completes; intercepted requests show zero network requests for the job (by host class and bytes).
- [ ] E2E in the facade harness: the missing-asset offline case settles with a typed failure and Retry in the operation state, never "The local generation engine stopped." (rendering the message is face controls').
- [ ] Removable (operator may veto): offline message in the owning action names what works.
- [ ] Trace run passes on CPU in CI against the committed expected trace; a negative test with a deliberately swapped permit/reservation event fails; GPU cell run under lease or reported untested.
- [ ] Traces and screenshots kept on failure; unit tests listed in test discovery and pass locally with the CI command; CI verifies after push.

title: Make the P30 Pro faster on WebGPU without regressing the Samsung
description:
## Goal
The candidate's WebGPU path beats CPU on the operator's Samsung S24 Ultra, but on the P30 Pro's forced WebGPU path (Mali-G76, Bifrost) it is slower than CPU: cold face 94 s vs 72 s, warm 22 s vs 17 s, peak Chrome memory 6.5 GB vs 4.7 GB (device lab, 24 Oct 2026). Find and land engine changes that make phone-webgpu faster while keeping the Samsung's gains (PLAN.md 'Device lab, deploy gates and CI policy' > Optimisation target).

## Scope
- Profile the phone-webgpu cell (lab.py run --cell phone-webgpu) per stage; form hypotheses (workgroup sizes, f16 use, buffer sizes/memory pressure, readback path, Mali-specific limits) and test each with paired runs.
- Keep every change behind the same numerical tolerances; no device-name special cases unless capability-based.
- Each candidate change: paired phone-webgpu measurements plus eris-webgpu no-regression, and the operator's Samsung check in the qualified device round until a Samsung cell exists.

## Out of scope
Phone-specific UI changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Paired ABBA measurements on phone-webgpu show a gain beyond control noise for each landed change.
- [ ] eris-webgpu and phone-cpu show no regression beyond noise.
- [ ] Raw synthesis stays within the frozen tolerances.
- [ ] The operator reports no regression on the Samsung (qualified device round) before the change counts as kept.
- [ ] landing changes in stylegan-js needs fm-7f2o; prove no Samsung regression at close (with fm-7f2o). If fm-7f2o has not landed when this bead is otherwise done, add this check to fm-7f2o (`br update fm-7f2o --add-acceptance`), tick it here and close; never wait on fm-7f2o
notes: Edits the monorepo engine (`packages/stylegan-js` WGSL and the worker) after `compute.synthesis` (fm-7f2o), never the classic candidate; it follows the shared-file order for `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` and reserves them through Agent Mail. Noise comes from control/control pairs on the same lab cell under the lease. Until a Samsung cell exists, each kept change is provisional until the operator's device report confirms no Samsung regression (fm-n759).

title: Blend-view journey and numerical synthesis/export comparison on the release artifact
description:
## Goal
Architecture completion requires that the final app keeps existing features and that the planned additions work; a cleaner repository alone does not complete the plan. The candidate's `next-e2e.yml` real-ui-cpu job covers CPU name/seed, e4e, crop, original reuse, recovered still without inference, GPU refusal/fallback scope, playable/saved MP4 and face/video/slider restore; the final app adds the locked crop design, static names, paste, Share/Save/format/filename, many-face layout, Morph preparing unfinished inputs and the weighted blend view. This bead operates the weighted face blend view journey and runs the numerical synthesis and export comparison on the release artifact against the independent qualified reference. Its cases are part of sub-result 1 (app flows), collated by `verify.flows`.

## Scope
Operate on the release artifact with real models:
- **Weighted face blend view (X01):** open it by the **Blend faces** button in More options and by `#blend`; fill three slots (a word, a name, a confirmed photo) and five more from one multi-photo batch in click order; one blend synthesis per committed weight change; Reset, Make it 1 and Shuffle weights; Save a PNG of the full 1024 x 1024 frame and reopen it as a face on the main page with zero inference; Add to morph inserts "Blend of N faces"; Back to morph keeps the session; the blend job reaches the analytics and usage-statistics sinks as action `blend`. The blended latent equals the engine's `blend` over the slot latents and weights (exact) and its raw synthesis meets the frozen tolerances on each route.
- **Synthesis and export (R20, R38, R41):** compare pre-compression network output against the independent qualified reference (same model, latent, noise, preprocessing, workload) on CPU and each available qualified WebGPU route: max RGB difference <= 1 on 0-255, max sampled raw-float error <= 0.002; e4e latent max abs error <= 0.0001. Exports: face 1024x1024 model size, orientation, valid format/playback, practical quality under the retained policy; lossless helpers preserve supplied pixels on decode; exact model/latent/provenance recovery values; recovery envelope regenerated when a payload is re-encoded. MP4 contains the entire accepted path at the admitted, disclosed resolution (1024 WebCodecs, 512 WebCodecs or 512 FFmpeg fallback). Report compression quality, file size and latency as tradeoffs.
- Every case is operated through the `verify.harness` (fm-48bj) helpers, every network or consent claim is asserted from intercepted requests (the request-interception helper from `build.ci-site`, fm-aa8), and every case is listed in this bead's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix rows or defect numbers it grades.

## Out of scope
Input journeys (`verify.functional`, fm-ejwq); morph, session walk and result journeys (`verify.functional.results`). External MP4 project-open UI (deferred). Old GUID/share links. Server-pixel or legacy API comparison. Byte identity of image files across builds. Full-tensor coverage claims. The expensive encoder lab check on every visitor.

## Notes
- Inspect rendered crop/result bounds (all four corners) and decoded full-size output, not only intrinsic sizes (earlier feedback: intrinsic dimensions passed while the displayed face was clipped).
- Never widen tolerances, change precision or replace numerics with a visual spot-check. Other models need their own references (the non-face proof in `verify.packages`).
- Integrated verification checks the final integrated app (after the planned UI and package changes) against the Next baseline (`facemorph.me-classic` branch `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) plus the plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped. Not historic-API parity and not a shutdown-qualification campaign. Performance and reliability against the control, including control/control noise and the physical iPhone, are judged by the strictly-not-worse gate (`verify.not-worse`, fm-mc27), not here. Correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found here are fixed in the owning bead and this bead re-runs. Wording says planned, experimental, implemented or deployed. No weights, secrets, photos or typed inputs in Git.
- Split on 2026-10-24 for swarm size by journey family into three beads, all part of sub-result 1 (app flows) collated by `verify.flows` (fm-35zs): `verify.functional` (this ID, fm-ejwq: words, seeds, names, photo, remove down to one, retained tools), `verify.functional.results` (morph, session walk, results: play/scrub, Save/Share, reopen) and `verify.functional.synthesis` (weighted blend view and the numerical synthesis/export comparison). The harness, interception, manifest and release-artifact rules apply to each bead's own cases.
- Anchors: PLAN.md #integrated-verification, #end-to-end-experience-and-design-fidelity-check, #synthesis-correctness-and-export-quality, #file-sharing-and-export-direction, #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each journey above has a scripted operated case with pass/fail outcome, mapped to rows X01 (blend view), R20 (synthesis numerics), R38 and R41 (export checks).
- [ ] Raw synthesis report per route: max RGB diff <= 1, max raw-float error <= 0.002; e4e latent max abs error <= 0.0001.
- [ ] Export checks report dimensions, orientation, playback validity, exact recovery values and lossless decode equality, with no byte-equality gate; a re-encoded payload's envelope validates against the new payload.
- [ ] Every UI step is operated through the `verify.harness` (fm-48bj) helpers: real pointer/touch at the control's visible position with an `elementFromPoint` assertion that the hit element is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role locators only for setup; phone-width and desktop-width screenshot per case.
- [ ] Every network or consent claim is asserted from intercepted requests by host class and bytes (the request-interception helper from `build.ci-site`, fm-aa8), never from a screenshot; traces and screenshots are kept on failure as privacy-filtered CI artifacts.
- [ ] Every case is listed in this bead's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix rows or defect numbers it grades; a case without a mapping fails manifest validation.
- [ ] All cases ran in the release-verification workflow against the named release artifact digest; a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded `failed` or `untested`, never `passed`.

title: Verify composed scheduler dependencies, residency and whole-action progress in the real app
description:
## Background
One application scheduler admits one heavyweight operation per shared provider context; compute permit is separate from residency reservations; Morph is a parent intent that joins existing operations and yields its permit while waiting. Operation controller unit tests use a fake clock; this bead runs the composed real app.

## Why
Unit-level scheduler proofs do not show the integrated bridge, manager and media behave together.

## Scope
- Composed dependencies: photo -> queued Morph; Morph auto-generation -> explicit face request; capability loss while queued; Cancel at each dependency boundary.
- Runtime snapshots: requested route, fallback scope and model identity captured at approval stay with queued work.
- Shared-download ownership; whole-action progress through default file readiness (monotonic, never resets).
- Delay/fail face-file preparation while Morph consumes compute-ready inputs: bounded endpoint reuse, no duplicate inference, independent file-preparation Retry.
- Admission during provider/model loading and idle retained residency (idle encoder while generator loading), not just serial final calls; competing provider-load requests.
- 4,096-frame path limit; selected faces never truncated.
- Rows graded: R14 (route snapshot part), R35 (one intent joins existing operations), R36 (progress part).

## Out of scope
Additional concurrency beyond one heavyweight op (needs separate evidence).

## Considerations
- Completing inference does not imply memory reclaimed; check reservations until release.
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Operation event log compared against expected traces for each composed case.
- [ ] No duplicate inference events for a joined slot/revision.
- [ ] Progress values monotonic in every run.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome) through the shared emitter from `build.event-log-core` (fm-bd03) and passes `scripts/check-event-log.ts`; the log is kept as a CI artifact, privacy-filtered like diagnostics; screenshots kept on failure.
- [ ] Each case is listed in this leaf's case manifest with step IDs `<bead key>/<case id>/<step>` and the flow-matrix row IDs or defect numbers it grades.
- [ ] Ran against the named release-candidate artifact digest (the same digest the join report checks); a check that did not run on that artifact/platform, or missed its threshold, is recorded failed or untested, never passed.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Field bug: cold full-package downloads stall or fail (3 of 6 in the diagnostics)
description:
## Goal
Half of the cold full-package downloads seen in the field did not finish, so a first visitor can wait minutes and get nothing. Find out whether the live candidate still does this after its 21 October retry and mirror changes, and fix it where it lives. Source: the diagnostics learnings note (`docs/findings/diagnostics-learnings-2026-10-18.md`, finding 4), aggregates only.

## Background (field facts, 22 September to 17 October)
- A cold full package (1,040 MB planned) was attempted in 6 runs: 3 completed (download 92 s Linux, 243 s Windows, 286 s macOS) and 3 did not: stopped at 141 MB after 121 s; at 586 MB after 377 s with a failure; on an iPhone at 678 MB after 19 s with no terminal event.
- All failures carried the single code `operation_failed`, so the reports cannot say whether the network, storage or the page caused it.
- The candidate added chunk retries (`bacd6e5`) and the `models.facemorph.me` second origin (`6107f80`) on 21 October, after these reports.

## Scope
- Reproduce on the device lab (`tools/device-lab/lab.py`) against the live next.facemorph.me with an empty cache and real network: `phone-cpu`, `eris-cpu` and `eris-webgpu`, plus real interruptions (switching the phone's Wi-Fi off and on through adb mid-download; Chrome DevTools network throttling on eris). Record per run: bytes reached, elapsed time, which origin served each retried chunk, the terminal event and its stage.
- If a run fails or stalls, find the cause in the candidate's acquisition path (`src/Next/Assets/model-cache.mjs`, the download gate) and fix it as ordinary candidate work on a non-deploying classic branch, qualified and merged like `delivery.candidate-edits` (fm-ww4). The same behaviour is then required of the monorepo manager through `manager.acquisition` (fm-fr9s).
- If every run completes, close with the run evidence; the monorepo requirement in fm-fr9s stays.

## Out of scope
The monorepo manager implementation (fm-fr9s); typed failure causes in the new app (fm-imm9).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Device-lab runs (`phone-cpu`, `eris-cpu`, `eris-webgpu`, empty cache, real network, at least 3 per cell plus one with a real mid-download interruption each) against the live candidate are recorded with bytes, elapsed time, serving origin per retried chunk and terminal event.
- [x] Any failure or stall has a named cause; a candidate fix (if needed) is merged after the candidate's ordinary qualification and the same runs then complete on next.facemorph.me.
- [x] The requirement is present in `manager.acquisition` (fm-fr9s) acceptance.

title: Place milestone-1 contract types in packages with type tests, validators and a declaration consumer
description:
## Background

Milestone-1 design items write draft type files under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`. The workspace build scaffolds the
four package workspaces (`packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`,
`packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`) and `apps/web` as empty, building,
packable placeholders with strict TS (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`,
`exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `isolatedModules`, type-only imports).

## Why

The plan's contracts acceptance is type-level tests per union, validator fuzzing and an external consumer compiling against emitted declarations.

## Scope

- Move the milestone-1 draft types into `src/contracts/` of the owning package workspaces (engine,
  manager, host manifest) as public exported types; no runtime implementation beyond validators.
- Runtime validators for manifest/metadata/worker payloads (narrow, tested; no broad `any`, unchecked
  casts or silent defaults).
- Type-level tests per discriminated union (exhaustiveness, invalid states unrepresentable).
- Validator fuzzing with generated malformed inputs.
- External consumer: a fixture project outside the workspace graph installs the packed placeholders
  and compiles against emitted `.d.ts` only, with no repository path aliases; it constructs a
  caller-loaded consumer without importing the manager.

## Out of scope

Engine/manager implementation. App types (m2).

## Considerations

Shared contracts must not acquire accidental DOM/Node globals; scope type environments.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` and the contract type tests pass; a deliberately invalid state in a test fixture fails compilation.
- [ ] Fuzzing runs in CI with a fixed seed and a recorded case count; every rejection yields a typed error.
- [ ] The external consumer compiles against the packed tarballs' declarations.
- [ ] Unit tests cover this item's own logic and run in the workspace test command.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] A script (`scripts/check-contract-exports.ts`) resolves every milestone-1 row of the `contracts.md` export index to a real export of the named module (engine and manager packages) and fails on a missing or renamed export; it runs in CI.
notes: Anchor: PLAN.md#acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance (Package and operation contracts).

title: Implement the Prepare encoder action and pre-source setup ownership
description:
## Background
Before a source is chosen the plan offers one compact Prepare encoder action beside Choose image in the Encode image
modal, only when eligible required assets are missing. Face controls renders the entry (`face.prepare-encoder-entry`).

## Why
Lets approved photo setup overlap the native source chooser.

## Scope
- Prepare encoder opens the same bundle consent; after a fresh source is inspected, the consent is used automatically
  where prerequisites are missing.
- **Cancel setup** stops that setup owner's remaining acquisition/warming while keeping local source/crop work; later OK
  can use verified complete assets; missing assets require explicit resume/reapproval through the same flow, never a
  silent revival.
- Cancelling the initial native source chooser or closing/cancelling its source modal abandons the pre-source owner and
  its continuation; cancelling a later add-file chooser leaves the batch/setup intact; independent owners survive.
- If a result becomes ready before optional preparation finishes, its actions work while the compact status keeps
  cancellation.

## Out of scope
Rendering of the entry (face leaf).

## Considerations
Opening Encode image or the page alone authorizes nothing.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. **This bead edits none of the three shared files.** Setup-owner lifecycle lives in the consent and operation modules; acquisition goes through the manager. - [ ] Unit tests for owner lifecycle: chooser cancel abandons; add-file cancel keeps; Cancel setup then OK with missing assets -> reapproval prompt; independent owner survives.
- [ ] Request-log run: Prepare encoder -> approve -> encoder requests start before any file is chosen; Cancel setup -> no new encoder request after the declared bound.
- [ ] Unit tests for this item's own logic run in CI (`npm test` workspace target) and pass.
- [ ] Each end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. title: Wrap self-hosted heavy CI commands in the shared device lease
description:
## Background

All heavy local builds, self-hosted CI and benchmarks on one physical machine use the same
`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` lease identity and state directory. Default runner budget 600 s,
maximum 3600 s; busy exits 75 unless a bounded `--wait` is chosen. The runner journals execution and
owned process-group cleanup, not statistical validity. Stage 1 re-homing supplies `run.py` and the
absolute per-machine state directory here.

## Why

Prevents two leases for one GPU and keeps CI from colliding with research runs.

## Scope

- A reusable CI step/composite action that invokes `autoresearch/run.py --device <name> --state-dir
  <absolute machine dir> --timeout <bounded>` around a heavy command and uploads the journal entry.
- Busy handling: bounded `--wait` or explicit busy result (not a silent pass).
- Never nest a second lease for the same machine; never run a remote benchmark under only a local lease.

## Out of scope

The lease protocol itself (research.s1).

## Considerations

Exit zero is execution, not qualification.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A self-hosted job using the wrapper journals its run; a simultaneous local leased run is refused or waits within the bound.
- [ ] Unit tests cover this item's own logic and run in the workspace test command.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Unit and integration tests show: without `--wait` a busy device exits 75; with a bounded `--wait` it either acquires or exits non-zero at the bound; a wrapped command exceeding `--timeout` has its whole owned process group terminated (no surviving children, checked with `pgrep`), the journal records the timeout and the job fails; the wrapper refuses to start when a lease for the same device is already held by the calling process tree (no nested lease) and when the lease device differs from the host that will run the work (no remote benchmark under a local workstation lease).

title: Prove media round-trips and document format limits
description:
## Background
The media workstream's acceptance is a round-trip and identity matrix through the built app plus a documentation deliverable on format/metadata limits and corruption behaviour.

## Why
Recovery-bearing exports are the product's only durable result; each offered format must be shown to export and recover before it is labelled supported.

## Scope
- Built-app e2e: generate a face, Save (WebP default), Save again (reuse, same name), Save PNG, re-import each through the face file entry (installs without inference); morph, Save MP4, validate with the internal reader; check promise/object-URL cleanup after each.
- Documentation in `packages/stylegan-js` docs and app Help notes: formats, metadata carried and not carried, size/resolution limits, corruption behaviour, receiving apps that strip metadata (the untouched file remains the recovery source).
- Confirm product lossy compatibility policy (WebP 0.8, PNG lossless choice, unchanged MP4 settings, no quality slider) is written as explicit policy.

## Out of scope
Extra export formats (optional item). Share sheet UX acceptance (face controls).

## Considerations
- File-size/latency are reported as tradeoffs, not byte-equality gates (first Save 4.38 MB -> 117 KB tradeoff is known).

## Matrix additions (polish r1)
- Policy check on real files: default Save is WebP (lossy, quality 0.8 per `export-policy`), 1024 x 1024, exact recovery; PNG Save decodes pixel-exact to the prepared pixels; MP4 uses the unchanged settings and reports its resolution.
- Reopen each recovery class through the face file entry: `missing` (metadata-free image: no automatic encoding, explicit Encode image offered), `damaged` (truncated and bit-flipped copies: not re-encoded, explicit Use as photo only when decodable), `incompatible-schema`, `incompatible-model`/`unknown-model` (viewable, Save returns the original bytes, compute disabled, excluded from Morph).
- Repeat Save reuses name and bytes; a format switch prepares only that format with zero inference events; Share cancel triggers no download.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] E2E round-trip passes on Chromium CPU in CI and the retained engines where available; untested cells listed.
- [ ] No hidden additional encode or inference during Save/Share (event log).
- [ ] Docs committed and linked from Help.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots are kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Network claims are asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Built-app matrix covers WebP default, PNG lossless, MP4 unchanged settings, and reopening missing, damaged, incompatible-schema and model-mismatch files, each asserted from the event log (encoder/detector/inference counts, bytes equality where stated).
- [ ] Earlier candidate files still reopen (polish r2): the candidate's schema-1 PNG and schema-2 PNG/WebP still fixtures through the face file entry with exact latent and model identity, and earlier candidate MP4 project fixtures (including `project-v1.fixture.json`-shaped projects) through the internal reader with ordered controls and settings intact.
- [ ] Lossy and container checks follow the retained quality policy (polish r2): WebP and MP4 outputs are checked for dimensions (1024 x 1024 still; actual video resolution as reported), upright orientation, valid decode/playback to the last frame with the expected frame count, and practical visual quality under the retained quality policy (`../facemorph.me-classic/autoresearch/reviews/2026-10-10/quality-policy.md`, or its re-homed copy once research stage 1 lands); no byte or lossy-pixel equality gate is used. A re-encoded file carries a regenerated envelope whose integrity hash matches its own payload (an obsolete hash copied from the earlier file fails).
- [ ] Tradeoff fields recorded per format in the receipt, with no threshold (polish r2): file size, first-Save preparation latency and repeat-Save latency (repeat must reuse the prepared file: zero encode events), on each tested platform.

title: Candidate edit set on a non-deploying classic branch: copy, native links, names limitation, typos, capitalisation, Remove, hosts
description:
## Goal
Bring the working candidate to a state that can be promoted honestly and used today: retirement and FAQ copy that promises no GUID/link preservation or fixed date and links no retired host, no native desktop recommendations, an honest names-picker limitation, the one-rule and one-string defect repairs (Remove control, text-field capitalisation, copy and spacing typos), and per-host endpoints for the production origin, then qualify and merge them so next.facemorph.me carries the fixes and an early promotion has its artifact. Also remove the fixed retirement date from the legacy production notice. Candidate-source edits are ordinary work on the working candidate and need no separate approval (operator, 18 October).

## Scope
- **Flow.** Edits on a non-deploying classic branch (e.g. `delivery/candidate-edits`) from `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, commands run in `facemorph.me-classic` per its development guide; merged only after the candidate's ordinary qualification (`next-site.yml` artifact/qualify/compiled-ui/deploy), because the candidate branch publishes to next.facemorph.me on every qualified push. Preserve other sessions' work on the branch; no reset/clean/worktree.
- **Retirement/FAQ copy** from the copy inventory: preview strip, tester invite, "Use classic FaceMorph", "Preview version" footer, FAQ entries (next.facemorph.me, self-hostable API, Upload image, model sizes, support address), API FAQ links, GUID promises, fixed-date assurances. Retirement copy: old results/links not preserved, no share URLs, operator-controlled timing. `src/explain.md` (links `checkface.facemorph.me/api` and the archived backend as current): if the candidate build serves it (check `deploy-next/` for its rendered text) it gets the retirement copy; if only the historical app uses it, it stays unchanged with that evidence. If next.facemorph.me keeps a preview label, gate chrome by host config rather than forking source (state the choice in the PR).
- **Legacy notice date**: edit only the notice text on classic `master` (deploys via Vercel on push) to say the hosted service will retire on a date the operator sets (or the operator's date if PLAN.md records one); copy-only, no functional change to legacy production; verify the live page after deploy. If the operator rules not to touch `master`, this part is dropped.
- **Native links**: remove desktop-download/availability links and recommendations from candidate errors, slow-route guidance, Help and the desktop documentation link in `Product.fs`; replace with web requirements Help text. Native dispatch code and the CPU/WebGPU selector and mobile paths stay untouched.
- **Names limitation**: short text in the names modal/selection path that a picked name is generated on the device and needs the generator download (the picker still synthesizes, `ChooseName → RunFace`; preview pixels are not completed results; no promise of phone result selection or Save from a preview). The static-name contract is stated as not complete in the PR.
- **Typos** (defect 20 one-string parts): "about 1 seconds" pluralisation; "smaller than25 MB" and two further missing-space messages (found by search); seed placeholder "Just type anything". No new copy beyond the fixes.
- **Capitalisation** (defect 5): `autocapitalize="off"`, `autocorrect="off"`, `spellcheck="false"` (and `autocomplete="off"` if consistent with classic) on the main text field (in `Product.fs` if that is where it lives); text is never trimmed or normalised.
- **Remove control** (defect 1): one rule in `src/Next/product-ux.scss` nesting the Remove style under the image container so it sits top right inside the image (today the library button style wins: 32×32 at (201,611) under a 376×376 image at (206,229) at 1,280 px; a real click opens Change mode). The control stays 32 px; the 44 px size is a known limitation for face controls.
- **Host rebinding**: per-host endpoints via host config (not forked source) so collector, model asset/runtime hosts, names catalogue origin and analytics resolve for facemorph.me; collector routes accept the production origin; the retained static origins the artifact uses are listed in the PR; `runtimeMirror()` in `src/Next/Assets/model-cache.mjs` already maps any `*.facemorph.me` page to `https://models.facemorph.me` — confirm its CORS/CORP headers serve the production origin; its fill origin stays `https://next.facemorph.me/`. Production starts fresh, with no cross-origin storage transfer.
- **Merge** the batch (Remove, capitalisation, typos, retirement/FAQ copy, native links, host rebinding, names limitation) to `candidate/next-delivery-20260916`; CI deploys to next.facemorph.me. The org-link edit merges separately after the rename, so this batch and an early promotion never wait on it.

## Out of scope
Production promotion; monorepo face controls, text field and native retirement; static names; many-face layout, bulk remove, Undo/Start over, 44 px targets; disabled-looking Create morph and transparent light-mode crop panel; classic `desktop-*.yml` workflows; applying the diagnostics retention decision; DNS changes.

## Notes
- A production collector needs the retention decision applied with no expiry written (diagnostics learnings owns that).
- A download without a decision seen while operating the names picker is reported against defect 19 (consent), not fixed here.
- 24 October rules: no receipts, no `docs/decisions/` citations, no event-log emitter; network claims from intercepted requests by host class and bytes. Operated UI rules: PLAN.md "UI acceptance is operated, not queried".
- Plan: #delivery-and-publication, #known-candidate-defects-found-by-operating-the-live-candidate--18-october-2026, #domain-handover-and-retirement-preparation.

title: Inventory workers, wrap heavy CI in the lease, carry the GPU lane
description:
Operator 25 October supersession: correctness work shares compute, GPU timing alone uses --exclusive gpu-timing, and the physical phone keeps its own bounded lab lock. The original lease/journal scope below is historical; the acceptance checklist and fm-a7iz define the current implementation. Triton CPU/Docker capacity is available; browser/GPU capability there still needs qualification.

## Goal

Use capable development workers to save hosted GitHub minutes without dropping checks, and make every heavy self-hosted CI command share the same per-machine device lease that local agents and research use, so two leases never exist for one GPU. Carry classic's self-hosted WebGPU lane over under that lease, rejecting software adapters, so hardware-GPU evidence is retained.

## Scope

**Worker inventory** (dev guide section)
- Per worker: access path (SSH/runner labels), OS, Node/npm, Docker/CDI, browsers, actual WebGPU adapter captured from a real browser run (validated, not llvmpipe/SwiftShader — else the named failure "software adapter"), `nvidia-smi`/Vulkan ICD presence, cores/RAM/disk, runner registration, absolute lease state directory, and the lanes/tasks it can take.
- Known starting facts: eris (checked 15 October on the workstation): RTX 2080 SUPER, 12 cores, 31 GB RAM, Docker 29.7.2 with NVIDIA CDI devices and `nvidia-ctk`, Node 26.8.2 (CI pins differ), no usable .NET SDK (not needed: no F# here), no `wrangler`, `br` only via a borrowed binary. TrueNAS: self-hosted `truenas,gpu-vulkan` GTX 1050 lane; older `gpu-gtx1050` config may use llvmpipe (NVIDIA Vulkan ICD absent). Triton: GTX 1080 in the dated device lab, readiness/runner registration unknown; retiring Triton inference hosting does not retire the machine. Old physical-phone gate text in the device lab is superseded.
- Assign at least one non-required heavy job (a paired comparison or numerical suite) to a worker under the lease with its expected hosted-minute saving, or state in the inventory why none can be.

**Lease CI wrapper** (reusable composite action)
- Invokes `autoresearch/run.py --device <name> --state-dir <absolute machine dir> --timeout <bounded>` around a heavy command and uploads the journal entry. Runner defaults: budget 600 s, maximum 3600 s.
- Busy: exits 75 unless a bounded `--wait` is chosen; with `--wait` it acquires or exits non-zero at the bound; never a silent pass.
- Timeout terminates the whole owned process group; the journal records it and the job fails.
- Never nests a second lease for the same machine in the calling process tree; never runs a remote benchmark under only a local workstation lease (lease device must be the host doing the work).
- Exit zero is execution, not qualification.

**GPU lane** — `.github/workflows/next-gpu-lane.yml` ("GPU lane benchmark"), job `webgpu-benchmark`, `runs-on: [self-hosted, truenas, gpu-vulkan]` (GTX 1050), pinned Chrome for Testing 141.0.7390.54 (a version change goes through the currency lane), `browser-harness==0.1.8`, driver `scripts/next-gpu-benchmark.py` under a 2100 s watchdog, artifact `next-gpu-benchmark-<run_id>`; heavy command wrapped in the lease (the workflow's own concurrency group does not coordinate with local agents).
- Triggers: schedule `0 16 * * *`; workflow_dispatch with `url` (default the staged/qualified origin, never assumed production) and `faces` (default 6, first face reported cold); push path filter on WebGPU sources at new paths (`packages/stylegan-js/**` WebGPU engine/fused-resample files, `apps/web/**` route-priors/route-selection/runtime, `scripts/next-gpu-benchmark.py`, the workflow file).
- Pass: in-page adapter is hardware (adapter info names the NVIDIA GPU); llvmpipe, SwiftShader or any software/fallback adapter is the named failure "software adapter" with no timings; `nvidia-smi` recorded; synthesis canaries within RGB ≤ 1 / raw-float ≤ 0.002 before any timing is reported; per-face timings are evidence, no absolute limit. Not a promotion gate, not a required status.
- Shared lookup/provenance/path filters/caches and the interception helper from `build.ci-shared`; lane paths adapted for `apps/web` and packages. The GPU lane benchmarks a staged or qualified origin passed as input, so it does not wait for the site lane.

## Out of scope

The lease protocol itself (research stage 1); registering new runners beyond what lanes need; making the GPU lane a promotion gate.

## Notes

- An installed GPU or runner label is not inference evidence. A workflow definition is not a passing result (recent GPU evidence failed adapter admission). This repository must not publish `next.facemorph.me` before the source handover. Native-package retirement does not retire hardware-GPU checks.
- Needs research stage 1 for `run.py` and the absolute per-machine state directory; kept outside build milestone 1 so it does not hold the port.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#development-workers-and-github-minute-use, #platform-ci-retention-and-performance-preservation.

title: Run the static names acceptance journeys
description:
## Background
Static names acceptance (PLAN.md#static-names-and-picker).

## Why
Prove the inference-free contract end to end on the built app.

## Scope
- Gapless overlay-name grid, no search/header/x, explicit target, keyboard/touch dismissal.
- Cold/offline/corrupt/stale selection states; selection/Save/reopen with generator acquisition and inference disabled;
  Morph then acquires the generator only with consent.
- Catalogue/model consistency, bounded visible-preview fetching, modal Back/focus, selection-to-text editing, exact
  catalogue-versus-ordinary-text generation identity.
- Walk: select two names, morph, cancel/retry, play/scrub, save and reload; reopen a saved still.

## Out of scope
Integrated verification's join.

## Considerations
No claim of zero network latency or fully offline uncached browsing.
design: Shared-file order (polish r2; PLAN.md "Shared-file serialization", decided 16 October, and "Mandatory ordering edges", 17 October). The serialized files are `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` and `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs` (imported byte-identical under `apps/web/src/Next/`), plus any extracted equivalent the check-migration map conflict list (fm-bhw) names. This bead adds acceptance scripts only and edits none of the three files. It is ordered after the morph pipeline through fm-ntag.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Operated-UI rule: each acceptance step acts with real pointer input (touch tap at phone widths) at the control's visible position, asserts `document.elementFromPoint` at that point returns the control (or a descendant) and that the point lies inside the region a person would look in (named per control below); by-name/by-role clicks are used only to set up state, never as the acceptance step.
- [ ] Every case is checked at a phone width (390 px) and a desktop width (1,280 px) with one screenshot per case kept as evidence.
- [ ] Each end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Every network claim is asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Each journey listed passes; untested cells recorded.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Controls and regions: face burger -> Browse Names (region: the face field's burger), grid tile tap (region: the tapped name's tile), floating Back on touch (region: over the grid, not covering names), Loading/Retry in the target tile's action slot; picks into face 1 of 1, face 2 of 3 and face 64 of 64; the grid scrolled to the first, a middle and the last of the 5,055 names; Escape and history Back each dismiss once.

title: Names-catalogue pipeline runs without the hosted API
description:
## Background
`hosting/gallery/` (`materialize.py`, `wrangler.jsonc`, `names-wrangler.jsonc`, provenance notes). Tie-break: static names owns the generator (never calls the API); this workstream owns where the staging and publication workflow runs.

## Why
Static names publication needs a home that does not depend on the API being alive.

## Scope
Pipeline entry points and workflow in this repository; remove/replace any hosted-API dependency in staging; dry-run publication to a test target.

## Out of scope
The catalogue generator and its data shape (ws:names).

## Considerations
Explicit `--publish` only.

## Classic facts (candidate `6107f80`)
`hosting/gallery/materialize.py` takes `--output`, `--origin` (HTTPS static origin) and `--limit`; for a name whose image is not on disk it fetches `https://api.facemorph.me/api/face/?value=...&dim=1024` (line ~56): that is the hosted-API dependency to remove (inputs come from the verified local selection and the static-names generator instead). `wrangler.jsonc` and `names-wrangler.jsonc` deploy static-only Workers (no worker code, no upload endpoint). `hosting/next-static/catalogue.json` is the names index staged into the site by `stage.py --catalogue`. Home: the pipeline entry points and its workflow live in `hosting/gallery/` and `.github/workflows/` here; the generator and data shape stay with static names (`names.generator`, `ws:names.spike`) and publication order with `names.publish-pipeline`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Pipeline dry run with network access to API hosts blocked succeeds (request log shows no API host).
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, and the log is retained as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics). Network claims are asserted from the log, never from screenshots.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/deploy/catalogue-pipeline.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Unit test: the pipeline refuses to start when any configured input URL resolves to an API host; dry run log lists every request by host class with zero `api.facemorph.me`/`checkface` hosts.

title: Remove WebGL execution and migrate saved preferences
description:
## Goal
Remove the dead, slow WebGL execution route while keeping Auto (default), CPU and WebGPU with the fixed failure-only WebGPU -> CPU preference, and without touching the coefficients, descriptors or qualified WebGPU kernels that share the `webgl` name (`manifest.webgl` is the block-stream coefficient bundle used by the integrated direct WebGPU engine and its canary identity). Decided 17 October from the diagnostics read (791 objects, 300 runs, 22 devices, 22 Sep-16 Oct; WebGL in 23 runs on 6 devices, last 12 Oct; median synthesis 69 ms WebGPU / 1.28 s CPU / 7.9 s WebGL; WebGL 7 completed / 12 failed, 11 failures from one Win Chromium 109 device; the one advantage was an iPhone Safari case needing 158 MB versus the 1,040 MB CPU package; caveats: opt-in, few devices, GA4 not read).

## Scope
- First, inventory every WebGL touch with keep/remove/rename disposition in the PR: `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs` (route vocabulary `['auto','cpu','webgl','webgpu']` ~23 and `setPreferredRoute` ~367, `qualify` ~368 "Choose CPU, WebGL or WebGPU.", `webgl-only` detection ~124, provider mapping `webgl2` ~67/~249/~330, direct-engine selection reading `manifest?.webgl` ~176 (keep), `capability()`/`supportedRoutes()`/`orderedRoutes()` ~185-187); `route-selection.mjs` `rankedRoutes`; `route-priors.mjs`; `ort-worker.mjs`; `webgl-vector-v1.mjs`; `browser/evidence/webgl-smoke.json`; `reporting.mjs`/`analytics.mjs` allowlists (`provider`, `requestedProvider`); `scripts/check-next-artifact.sh`; saved route-preference storage key(s) read by the bridge; `Contracts.fs` `BrowserWebGl` (dead type, not ported).
- A `webgl` name alone does not make an asset removable. Shared coefficient assets and identities are kept; if a descriptor is renamed, keep compatible manifest/cache resolution and content identities. `webgl-vector-v1.mjs` is kept if it carries the coefficient format `manifest.webgl` / direct WebGPU need. Historical evidence files stay as history.
- Remove WebGL execution from `runtime.mjs`, `ort-worker.mjs`, route selection/priors and the bridge.
- Migrate saved `webgl` preferences to Auto on read (one-time, written back); saved `cpu`/`webgpu`/`auto` unchanged; `setPreferredRoute('webgl')` and `qualify('webgl')` reject with a typed error.
- Keep CPU/WebGPU selection, saved CPU preferences, CPU ordering, bounded GPU-failure CPU fallback, adapter probing, successful-slow preference, background watchdogs, worker start/failure separation.
- Choice semantics left in place and unit-tested: Auto with an admitted WebGPU adapter runs WebGPU; Auto with a null adapter runs CPU with zero GPU asset requests; Auto after a WebGPU admission/execution failure falls back to CPU once, records the reason, and does not retry GPU in the same intent. Explicit CPU never probes or acquires GPU assets. Explicit WebGPU on failure uses the bounded CPU fallback only within the approved asset/cost scope, otherwise settles with Retry or the existing revised decision. Worker start failure does not poison the route choice.
- Report allowlists still parse historical `webgl` values.
- Update WebGL-only test expectations in the same revision. Keep green with their coverage: `runtime.test.mjs` (GPU -> CPU retry), `route-priors.test.mjs` (CPU ordering), `route-choice.test.mjs` (existing cases unchanged, including "stored slow timings cannot demote successful routes across reloads" and "the operator route preference applies equally to Android and iOS"), `mobile-runtime.test.mjs`, `canary-qualification.test.mjs`, `webgpu-engine.test.mjs`.
- Repair `scripts/check-next-artifact.sh` (classic `6107f80` lines 46-48 open `.next-advanced` and assert options `{'auto','cpu','webgpu','webgl'}`): a helper finds the `Processing mode` select by accessible name, opens an enclosing closed `<details>` only if there is one, and records `providerLocation` in the JSON result (no location asserted here). The expected route set comes from the artifact label: `control` still reports `{auto,cpu,webgpu,webgl}` (a control fact); a destination-built artifact must report exactly `{auto,cpu,webgpu}`. The destination assertion first runs at `migration.rendering` (no destination UI artifact exists before the Vite build); here a unit test feeds both label cases a recorded DOM fixture. Tiles, Add/Remove face, Browse names Escape, width sweep 320/360/390/1280 and canvas fit in the script are untouched.

## Out of scope
- Selector placement and rendering (`face.selector-names`); per-operation admission (`provider.admission`).

## Notes
- Shared-file order step 1 (provider simplification -> typed facade -> compute extraction -> confirmed-crop fix -> morph pipeline -> static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics reporting rebinding). Soft preference: before compute extraction so dead WebGL execution is not extracted.
- Boundary: provider simplification owns route semantics (Auto = fixed failure-only WebGPU -> CPU filtered by real admission; explicit CPU/WebGPU stay meaningful; measured timings inform guidance, never automatic ranking; a healthy slow GPU route is never demoted). `face.selector-names` renders the selector and changes no semantics; until it lands, the ported Advanced selector (`migration.ren-tiles`) shows Auto/CPU/WebGPU with these semantics.
- The removal decision and its figures live in PLAN.md (#clean-ui-placement-and-useful-degradation, 17 October); no separate removal receipt.
- Plan anchors: PLAN.md#provider-simplification; #web-release-and-desktop-package-retirement--12-october-2026; #autoresearch-coverage-and-preservation-map (WGSL/direct engine row); #workspace-build-and-artifact-identity.

title: Ingest diagnostics learnings, then delete the old-wording reports
description:
## Goal
Keep the insights and keep the old promise. Verify that the 18 October learnings note is aggregates only and that the read wrote nothing, then delete every diagnostics report collected under the old "30 days" wording, unattended, with a receipt, repeating until nothing older than the boundary remains. Operator, 18 October: "I do want to delete the telemetry collected under the 30 days verbiage once we have mined it for insights. Keep the insights." P0: the earliest reports passed 30 days on 22 October, so the deletion is overdue. Needs only bucket access and the `cf` CLI, no monorepo prerequisite.

## Scope
- **Facts.** Read-only pass of 18 October over the whole `runs/` prefix of R2 bucket `facemorph-diagnostics`: 801 objects, 5.2 MB, uploaded 22 September to 17 October 08:02 UTC; 12,057 events, 309 runs, 22 devices. Note `docs/findings/diagnostics-learnings-2026-10-18.md` (commit `7875aaf`), key-list digest `c3833f1f056ae0700e82d997a592e9009114d014a7b1ce8ae21c45cd8c07e0fb` (SHA-256 of sorted keys, one per line, trailing newline). The read script was not committed; the note says the read used "a read-only listing and per-object get; nothing was written to the bucket". Findings already folded in: typed failure causes, iPhone cache capacity. Boundary: the corrected consent line went live **2026-10-17 20:28:59 UTC** (commit `40c63a9`, deploy job finish). A dry run on 18 October confirmed all 801 exist, none newer than the mined set, all before the boundary. KV fallback copies expire after 30 days by their own setting. Raw working copies from the 17 October WebGL read and 18 October mining sit in session scratch directories.
- **Identifier scan** `scripts/diagnostics/scan-learnings-note.mjs` (standalone Node 22, no workspace dependencies) with fixtures. Fails (non-zero exit, line numbers, matched text redacted) on: UUIDs; hex runs of 16+ characters other than the allowlisted key-list digest; base64/base64url runs of 20+; R2 keys (`runs/` + ID); IPv4/IPv6; email addresses; user-agent strings with build numbers; any current bucket run ID (optional `--keys-from-bucket` with a read-only token held in memory only). Run on the note at `7875aaf` and HEAD; if it finds an identifier, redact the note in a new commit and re-run.
- **Read-only and no-write evidence.** A fresh listing with a bucket-scoped R2 Object Read token (created with `cf user tokens create`, revoked after, token ID recorded) shows the objects uploaded at or before 2026-10-17 08:02:59 UTC number 801, hash to `c3833f1f…e0fb`, and none has an `uploaded` time on or after 18 October. Listings stay in memory.
- **Deletion script** `scripts/diagnostics/delete-old-wording-reports.mjs` (standalone Node 22; not a bucket rule), idempotent, each step logged with no keys or contents:
  1. Preconditions, any failure stops before any delete: (a) `7875aaf` is reachable from the remote default branch (`git fetch`, `git merge-base --is-ancestor 7875aaf origin/main`), so the only kept copy of the insights is durable; otherwise exit `precondition-a-unmet` with zero list/delete calls and no prompt; (b) the scan passes on the note at HEAD; (c) the ingest verification above passed; (d) a read-only token lists D = objects uploaded before the boundary; if D's digest is `c3833f1f…e0fb` (count 801) proceed; if D has objects not in the mined set (after 08:02, before the boundary), run the **mine-then-delete repeat**: aggregate them into a new dated section of the note (aggregates only, scan passes), commit, record the new digest, restart with the union as the mined set.
  2. Pre-delete receipt section: count and digest of D, boundary, mined-set upper bound, count and digest of set A (uploaded after the boundary, untouched).
  3. Delete exactly D's keys with a separate short-lived R2 Object Read & Write token scoped to the bucket, created through the logged-in `cf` CLI and revoked immediately after; batches with retry on transient errors; key list in memory only.
  4. Post-checks (read-only): D present = 0; objects before the boundary = 0; set A count and digest unchanged; lifecycle (S3 `GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration` on the bucket) has only the default multipart-abort rule and no expiration rule; bucket lock absent; KV fallback entry count and latest `expiration` recorded (no action; 30-day TTL).
  5. Working copies: search `/tmp`, `$TMPDIR`, `~/.cache`, `~/Work`, paths in `scripts/diagnostics/working-copy-paths.txt` and the 17/18 October scratch directories (from the session record) for files containing any D run ID or key (matched in memory); delete; re-scan to zero matches.
  6. Receipt completion.
- Never touch objects uploaded after the boundary. Add no expiration rule; make no deletion promise for later reports. Retention decided 17-18 October: kept with no deletion date going forward. Repeat the mine-then-delete pass until a listing finds nothing before the boundary.
- Tokens are never stored in Git or logs (IDs only).

## Out of scope
Re-mining beyond the repeat pass; collector code changes (diag.rebinding); the new app's retention copy (diag.disclosure).

## Notes
- **Kept receipt.** `docs/receipts/diagnostics/old-report-deletion-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` is one of the two full receipts the plan keeps because an irreversible action reads it. The ingest verification is recorded as that receipt's precondition section rather than a separate receipt.
- **Precondition (a) holds:** checked 24 October, `origin/main` (407a532) contains `7875aaf`, so the deletion can run now with no further input; the script still checks it on every run. The operator ordered the deletion on 18 October; PLAN.md's earlier "runs on the operator's go" is superseded by that ruling.
- Adds standalone scripts and the receipt only; no app source; stays unordered with respect to the shared-file chain.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#debug-reporting-control-and-consent (retention items 1-5), #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance (old-report deletion).
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Scan script unit tests over fixtures: each identifier class detected; the allowlisted digest not flagged; matched text redacted. Scan passes on the note at `7875aaf` and HEAD (or on a redaction commit).
- [x] Read-only re-listing: count at or before 2026-10-17 08:02:59 UTC = 801; sorted-key SHA-256 = `c3833f1f056ae0700e82d997a592e9009114d014a7b1ce8ae21c45cd8c07e0fb`; none uploaded on or after 2026-10-18; token revoked (a failing verify call confirms).
- [x] Deletion tests in CI against a real S3-compatible object store run locally (pinned SeaweedFS container `chrislusf/seaweedfs:3.97`, since MinIO no longer publishes public images; the script speaks the S3 API, so R2 is only its production endpoint) and a temp tree: each precondition failure (note not on the remote default branch, scan failing, ingest check failing, digest mismatch) stops before any delete; extra pre-boundary objects take the repeat path; post-boundary objects are never passed to delete; a post-check failure marks the receipt failed; the working-copy scan removes planted copies and leaves unrelated files.
- [x] Unit test: with `7875aaf` absent from the remote default branch (a real temp repository with a bare remote) the script exits `precondition-a-unmet` with zero list/delete calls and no prompt; with it present the same invocation proceeds with no flag, prompt or input.
- [x] Real run with no interactive prompt (log shows preconditions -> delete -> post-checks -> receipt).
- [x] Receipt records: scan results at `7875aaf` and HEAD, re-listing result, count deleted, key-list digest (or extended digest after a repeat), boundary 2026-10-17 20:28:59 UTC, mined-set upper bound, post-deletion count of the deleted set (0), objects before the boundary after the run (0), set-A count and digest before and after (equal), lifecycle rules (no expiration rule), bucket lock state, KV entry count and latest expiration, read- and write-token IDs with creation and revocation times, working-copy roots and files/bytes removed with a zero-match re-scan; plus the script's commit and blob SHA-256, the command or workflow run link, the outcome and any deviations.
- [x] The scan finds no key, run ID, token value or report content in the receipt, the committed files or the job log.
notes: 24 October, executed: the 801 old-wording reports are deleted and 807 raw working-copy files removed; the 129 post-boundary reports are untouched; receipt at docs/receipts/diagnostics/old-report-deletion-2026-10-24.md (deviations listed there, including the first run's crash before its receipt). Scripts and their 11 tests (real SeaweedFS and real temp Git repos) pass locally. Left before closing: commit the scripts and receipt, and a CI run of the tests on the merge commit.

title: Carry over the Android emulator component lane
description:
## Background

Classic `mobile-browser.yml` android: Android Chrome, API35 x86_64 Pixel6 emulator profile/SwiftShader
on Ubuntu 24.04; eight mandatory cache/worker/integrity/PNG/reload/portrait-EXIF-crop components; no
synthesis/e4e in this lane; scoped push/PR/manual runs.

## Why

Phones are first-class targets; existing Android CI is retained.

## Scope

- Destination job keeping the eight components and trigger scope.

- Artifact lookup, provenance (source repository ID, workflow, run, commit), digest verification,
  the shared path-filter list `scripts/ci/path-filters.json` (every new code root: `apps/web/**`,

title: Guard numerical tolerances and retained cells against dependency bumps
description:
## Background

Tolerances: RGB difference at most 1, sampled raw-float error at most 0.002, e4e latent maximum absolute error 0.0001; research suites keep their own frozen tolerances. Retained cells: the named CI lanes
and the check-migration map. A bump must never widen a tolerance or remove a cell.

## Why

The workstream acceptance requires that such a dry-run bump is rejected.

## Scope

- Freeze tolerance constants and the required-cell/check list in a manifest with a digest; a required CI
  check fails when a change alters them unless the change is a declared plan revision with a decision entry.
- Dry run: a synthetic grouped bump PR that widens one tolerance and another that removes one cell;
  both must be rejected by gates.

## Out of scope

Changing tolerances (never by this lane).

## Considerations

- Shared-file serialisation: `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and
  `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited only in the mandated order (provider simplification, typed facade,
  compute extraction, confirmed-crop fix, morph pipeline, names picker/diagnostics); build items change
  tooling and CI, and add any shared file they touch to the check-migration map's conflict list.
- No worktrees, resets or cleans; preserve other sessions' uncommitted work.
- Hosted-minute economy: use capable workers where practical, but never weaken a required check or
  substitute Linux WebKit for Safari/iOS; never cancel a live publication halfway.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Both dry-run PRs fail their gates (recorded runs) and are not merged.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Unit tests for the frozen tolerance/cell manifest check: changed tolerance constant, removed cell, removed check-migration row each fail; a declared plan revision with a decision entry passes.

title: Freeze manager acquisition lifecycle, verified-local reads and asset leases
description:
## Background

`browser-model-manager` owns manifest/chunk acquisition, checksum validation/recovery, OPFS/device
caching, cache reuse/eviction/quota and creation/disposal of loaded provider handles. Today
`model-cache.mjs` `acquire()` handles can fetch missing/corrupt assets through `bytes()`/`open()`;
`readOnly` and `has()`/`peek()` alone do not enforce a no-network boundary. Retained mechanisms:
per-read platform SHA, exact-length buffers, unit corruption repair, URL-independent pinned reuse,
Safari worker sync-handle support and Cache Storage fallback.

## Why

The manager milestone (loaded handles accepted), acquisition consent and warming all depend on a
frozen verified-local boundary and lease semantics.

## Scope

- Lifecycle: construct (no globals, no I/O), status/capability read (no acquisition), authorise,
  acquire, verify, load handle, lease, invalidate, dispose.
- Verified-local-only access (for example `allowRepair:false`) across both backends (OPFS and Cache
  Storage); typed cache-miss, corruption, eviction and invalidation errors; all-backend no-repair.
- Reference-counted leases on required verified local assets; manager eviction/deletion cannot remove
  leased assets; browser eviction, corruption, cross-tab deletion or device/worker loss invalidates
  the capability with a typed error; affected operations settle and release without network repair.
- Active operations cannot fetch replacement shards; reacquisition and re-admission happen outside
  engine execution through the application's consent policy.
- Keep candidate cache identities and on-origin result/session formats compatible; split model caches
  from application retention policy; model-cache eviction never deletes user exports or recovery records.
- Release-consistent sets: an in-flight app uses one immutable manifest identity.

## Typed outputs (citable)

Draft first under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`, then moved by the milestone type-test bead to the module below. Exported names are stable: downstream beads cite them; a rename needs a contract revision and an update of the `contracts.md` export index.

- `packages/browser-model-manager/src/contracts/lifecycle.ts`: `ModelManager` interface (construction without globals or I/O; `status()` and `capabilities()` acquisition-free; `authorize(grant)`, `acquire`, `verify`, `load` → handle wrapping `LoadedModelCapability`, `dispose`), `ManagerStatus`, `VerifiedLocalReader` (`allowRepair: false` across OPFS and Cache Storage).
- `packages/browser-model-manager/src/contracts/leases.ts`: `AssetLease` (reference-counted), `LeaseInvalidationCause` (`browser-eviction` | `corruption` | `cross-tab-deletion` | `device-loss` | `worker-loss`), `SettlementRule`.
- `packages/browser-model-manager/src/contracts/errors.ts`: `ManagerError` union (`cache-miss` | `corrupt` | `evicted` | `invalidated` | `quota` | `manifest-rejected` | `unknown-status` | `network`).
- Consumers: `manager.split`, `manager.loaded-handles`, `manager.local-only-reads`, `manager.acquisition`, `manager.quota-eviction`, `consent.grant-model`, `compute.provider-adapters`.

## Out of scope

The grant and budget types (contracts.acquisition-grant-budgets). Implementation.

## Considerations

Leases constrain manager behaviour, not the browser's ability to reclaim storage.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts.md` manager section and draft type file define the lifecycle, error union and lease API.
- [ ] A walkthrough shows warming and status reads issue zero network requests by construction of the types (no repair-capable handle reachable).
- [ ] Each invalidation cause maps to a typed error and a settlement rule.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Every name listed under "Typed outputs (citable)" exists in the draft type file and has a row in the `contracts.md` export index naming its consumers.
