title: Publish frozen classic, switch default branch, recorded acceptance
description:
## Goal
Make the frozen self-host distribution what a person gets from a plain `git clone <url>` plus one command: fill the final organization URL, tag the qualified release, publish the README on the distribution branch, switch `facemorph.me-classic`'s default branch to it (D4) without firing any publisher, then run the README-executed clean-clone acceptance verbatim on the GPU worker. This closes the frozen self-host guarantee. Not covered by the cutover decision; it waits only on rename repair and classic qualification.

## Scope
- Fill `<canonical-url>` with the renamed classic URL; tag the qualified release; publish the README on the distribution branch (working name `self-host`); never merge into `master`.
- Before state: default branch (`gh api repos/facemorph-me/facemorph.me-classic --jq .default_branch`), branch heads, latest Actions runs, latest Vercel production deployment id, and artifact identity of facemorph.me and next.facemorph.me (`post-delivery-check --mode unchanged` baseline).
- Switch the default branch (a setting change, not a push; the D4 pre-checks say whether it fires Vercel). If the switch fires the Vercel workflow despite the pre-checks, retire the Vercel publisher first (API retirement does that anyway) and say so.
- After state: default branch is the distribution branch; a fresh `git clone <canonical-url>` with no branch argument checks out the tagged commit; `post-delivery-check --mode unchanged` shows facemorph.me and next.facemorph.me unchanged; no new Actions run or Vercel deployment since the switch; the README quickstart block extracts.
- **Recorded acceptance**: run the README harness in verbatim mode (no substitution; plain `git clone <canonical-url>`) on the GPU worker under the lease, passing every harness assertion; update the README validated matrix with commit and date; restore any path the run shows to be needed.
- Confirm the scheduled rot check is registered from the new default branch (scheduled and dispatched workflows run only from default-branch files).

## Out of scope
Wind-down tree cleanup; any change to production or next.facemorph.me.

## Notes
- D4 (16 October, simplified 17 October): frozen distribution on its own branch, tagged, default switch on its pre-checks, never merged into `master`.
- 24 October rules: no receipts or `docs/decisions/` citations; the weight-download claims are asserted from captured requests by host class and bytes.
- Plan: #classic-distribution, #frozen-classic-distribution, #delivery-and-publication, #classic-distribution-acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Tag exists on the qualified commit; default branch is the distribution branch; a fresh default clone lands on the tagged commit; before/after state (default branch, heads, latest runs, Vercel deployment id, host identities) recorded.
- [ ] `post-delivery-check --mode unchanged` passes for facemorph.me and next.facemorph.me; the Actions run list and Vercel deployments show nothing ran on the switch.
- [ ] Verbatim harness run passes every assertion on the GPU worker; its output shows the plain `git clone <canonical-url>`; restart shows zero weight bytes downloaded (captured requests); README matrix updated with commit and date.
- [ ] The scheduled rot check is visible in Actions for the default branch.

title: Morph, session-walk and result journeys (play/scrub, Save/Share, filenames, reopen) on the release artifact
description:
## Goal
Architecture completion requires that the final app keeps existing features and that the planned additions work; a cleaner repository alone does not complete the plan. The candidate's `next-e2e.yml` real-ui-cpu job covers CPU name/seed, e4e, crop, original reuse, recovered still without inference, GPU refusal/fallback scope, playable/saved MP4 and face/video/slider restore; the final app adds the locked crop design, static names, paste, Share/Save/format/filename, many-face layout, Morph preparing unfinished inputs and the weighted blend view. This bead operates the morph, session and result journeys on the release artifact, where a person makes and keeps their work: Create Morph, the session walk, play/scrub, Save/Share, filenames and reopening saved stills. Its cases are part of sub-result 1 (app flows), collated by `verify.flows`.

## Scope
Operate on the release artifact with real models:
- **Morph (R30, R35):** Create Morph prepares unfinished valid words and seeds as one intent; repeated clicks do not queue duplicates; identical neighbours (same word twice; A, B, A under the closed-loop rule, a planner rule) are refused before any work with a plain message naming what to change (defect 6).
- **Session walk:** two names, morph, cancel and retry, play/scrub, save, reload; reopen a saved still; repeat with a confirmed photo and an ordered multi-selection.
- **Results (R37-R42):** play the morph, switch to the slider, scrub; absent scrub frames keep the video playable and regenerate nothing. Save face WebP/PNG and morph MP4: MIME, extension and dimensions match the choice; PNG fallback updates MIME and extension. Share by user gesture where file sharing exists; cancelled share keeps the prepared file and Save works; without file-share capability Save is primary; a share failure falls back to saving the same file. title: Build the evaluator core with normalised, scoped verdicts
description:
## Background

Keep `run.py` for budgets, cleanup and leases. Generic `passed` or exit zero is not product or release qualification. Frozen historical scripts/reports keep their bytes; new campaign code is versioned.

## Why

Prevents invalid or missing evidence from turning into speed wins.

## Scope

- Consume workload specs (shared schema); verify frozen digests before running.
- Verdict classes: execution, validity, correctness, non-regression, paired-benefit, architecture;
  expected-failure tests can pass cleanup/correctness without becoming timings; missing supported
  evidence is inconclusive; correctness failure rejects.
- Outputs append scoped outcomes to the ledger only for evaluated outcomes.

## Out of scope

Driver-specific adapters.

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests: invalid run, missing cell, expected failure, correctness failure each produce the right scoped verdict and never a benefit verdict.
- [ ] Unit tests cover this item's own logic and run in the workspace test command.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Unit tests: a frozen-digest mismatch on control, candidate or fixture yields `invalid`; a paired-benefit verdict requires confirmation samples whose identity is disjoint from screening, a complete screened-candidate list and an effect interval clearing the frozen margin, and a reused holdout, a missing screened record or a min-only (fastest-run) claim each yield no benefit; a numerical-correctness verdict from screening-only data without the applicable full31 suite is `inconclusive` and cannot yield `keep`.
- [ ] Evaluator output has no release-qualification field; a test shows the support-table generator and promotion reject evaluator output offered as qualification, and recording a `keep` creates no integration-commit or deployment record (they stay separate recorded facts). Every verdict reports effect uncertainty.

title: Probe MP4 preparation availability when Morph is accepted
description:
## Background
Clean-UI contract: check that a qualified MP4 preparation pipeline is available when accepting Morph; use an already qualified codec fallback only within the approved asset/resource scope (WebCodecs probes 1024 then 512, FFmpeg 512 fallback; the FFmpeg asset joins acquisition consent). If none exists, explain in Morph status before frame inference, keep ready faces saveable and do not imply an interactive preview is an exported video. A later codec failure retains usable pixels/frames and offers export-only Retry when feasible. Show a lower-resolution fallback beside format/result actions and before Morph when known.

## Why
Known degradation is discovered before expensive work; Morph completion means a playable default MP4 with project metadata.

## Scope
- Probe function (WebCodecs config support at 1024 and 512; FFmpeg fallback presence/consent state) returning available resolution or unavailable reason.
- Morph accept path uses it before frame inference; message in Morph status; disclosed 512 px fallback shown before Morph and with the result.
- Export-only Retry after a codec failure keeps frames and never re-runs inference.

## Out of scope
Consent for the FFmpeg asset (acquisition consent). Format controls (face controls).

## Considerations
- Mock capabilities are acceptable for unavailable-codec UI checks; they do not add physical-device qualification.

## Ordering and disclosure details (polish r1)
- Probe order is fixed: WebCodecs `avc1.42002A` at 1024, then at 512, then the FFmpeg 512 fallback only if its asset is already cached or inside the approved acquisition scope (acquisition consent owns asking for it). Settings are the unchanged ones from `export-policy` (media.split).
- The event log must show `mp4.probe` before the first `synthesis` event of the morph; with no route, zero `synthesis` events.
- Disclosure: when the probe chooses 512 (WebCodecs or FFmpeg), Morph status says the video will be 512 x 512 before frames start, and the result shows the actual resolution beside the format/result actions.
- An interactive preview is never described as an exported video when no MP4 route exists; ready faces stay saveable.

Named tests: `mp4-probe.1024`, `.512-webcodecs`, `.ffmpeg-cached`, `.ffmpeg-needs-consent`, `.none`, `.probe-before-synthesis`, `.disclosure-512`.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.

- [ ] Unit tests for probe outcomes (1024, 512, FFmpeg-only, none).
- [ ] E2E with WebCodecs disabled and no fallback: Morph explains before any frame inference (event log: zero synthesis events).
- [ ] E2E forced codec failure after frames: frames retained, export-only Retry produces the MP4 without inference.
- [ ] Operated UI acceptance: act with real pointer/touch input at the control's visible position and assert via `elementFromPoint` that the element there is the control and lies where a person would look; by-name/by-role clicks only to set up state; repeating controls exercised at 0/1, 2, 3, many and the cap; text inputs with an empty, a very long and a pasted value; a phone-width (390 px) and a desktop-width (1,280 px) screenshot per case.

Network claims are asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.

title: Wind-down stage precondition check and disabling superseded classic publishers
description:
## Goal
Automate classic wind-down without human approval steps (operator, 18 October): each stage is an ordinary commit on classic gated by its CI precondition, with Git as the reversal path and guards that protect other sessions' work and staging inputs. This bead writes the shared precondition check those stage commits run in CI and lands the first stage: disable classic's superseded publishers and moved workflows once their replacements are verified, so there is one publisher per target and classic can never overwrite the monorepo's deploys.

## Scope
- **Stage precondition check** (one script in the monorepo `scripts/`, not a stage-runner framework; each stage is an ordinary commit on classic whose CI job runs this check and the stage's own preconditions): compares refs (all branches/tags with SHAs) before and after; skips paths with uncommitted changes (`git status --porcelain`) and reports them, never overwriting; keeps or moves first every path in `inventory/protected-paths.json` (paths model staging or the distribution reads), never dropping one; fails the job when any precondition fails, so the stage does not land. Git (revert of the stage commit) is the reversal path; no per-stage receipt or report file.
- Safety rules (not approvals): Git history never rewritten; no branch or tag deleted; nothing deletes or archives the repository or any personal production record. No reset/clean/worktree; a separate clone is used for read-only checks only.
- **Publisher stage** (first stage commit). Preconditions: monorepo publisher live (post-delivery check passed); rollback artifact verified; consumers moved; the monorepo deploys and warms `models.facemorph.me` (classic `next-site.yml` does this today after each site deploy; disabling it stops that), shown by one monorepo run.
- Disable, on the default branch, classic's `next-site.yml` deploy job, the research workflows moved by re-homing (`research-built-ui-media-v1.yml`, `research-rgba-screen-v1.yml`), the three `desktop-*.yml` native workflows and any workflow whose consumer moved (GitHub workflow disable and/or removal); each with its re-enable command.
- Mark each classic GitHub Release from the native inventory historical: prepend one line to its notes ("Historical desktop build; native packages are retired; use https://facemorph.me in a browser"); assets, tags and update manifests untouched; the previous body is kept in the stage commit so reversal can restore it. Installed clients are never redirected into the fresh repository.
- Legacy production publisher `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` on `master` (Vercel) stays enabled while facemorph.me still serves legacy production (wind-down can start after the candidate-source handover alone); it is retired by promotion or API retirement, not here. The post-check reports its state and why it was or was not touched.
- Post-check: no classic workflow can publish next.facemorph.me.

## Out of scope
Deleting branches; removing workflows from non-default branches' history; tree cleanup and README pointer (next stage).

## Notes
- Candidate publisher and rollback material stay only until the handover is verified.
- Wind-down starts only after candidate-source handover, autoresearch re-homing (both stages) and deploy re-homing are verified.
- Newer PLAN.md "Acceptance receipts" (24 October: each stage is a commit gated by its CI precondition) wins over the older "Classic wind-down" text asking each stage to write a receipt: no receipt files and no stage runner with per-stage reports; the stage commit and its CI run are the evidence (sweep, 24 October).
- Plan: #classic-wind-down, #end-state-of-the-repositories, #acceptance-receipts-and-gate-style-acceptance.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Precondition-check fixture-repository tests: a dirty path is skipped and reported; a protected path is kept; refs unchanged except the default branch advancing; a failed precondition fails the job so the stage commit does not land.
- [ ] Publisher stage commit lands with its CI preconditions green; the commit lists each disabled workflow with its re-enable command, keeps the previous release bodies, and states the Vercel `deploy.yml` state with the reason.
- [ ] Post-check: no classic workflow can publish next.facemorph.me; ref snapshot shows no branch or tag deleted.

title: Compare raw synthesis within frozen tolerances and check export quality and recovery
description:
## Background
The candidate's product synthesis canaries require maximum RGB difference of 1 on 0-255 and maximum sampled raw-float error 0.002; the e4e latent tolerance is maximum absolute error 0.0001. Research/reference suites keep their own frozen coverage. Exported images need no byte identity between builds.

## Why
The operator ruled that network synthesis must stay virtually identical within existing small tolerances, including across qualified CPU/WebGPU routes, while compression/container bytes may differ.

## Scope
- Compare pre-compression network output against the independent qualified reference for the same model, latent, noise, preprocessing and workload, on CPU and each available qualified WebGPU route.
- e4e latent comparison within 0.0001.
- Exports: dimensions (face 1024x1024 model size), orientation, valid format/playback, practical visual quality under the retained quality policy; lossless helpers preserve supplied pixels on decode; exact model/latent/provenance recovery values; recovery envelope regenerated when a payload is re-encoded.
- MP4 contains the entire accepted path at admitted, disclosed resolution (1024 WebCodecs, 512 WebCodecs or 512 FFmpeg fallback).
- Report compression quality, file size and latency as tradeoffs.
- Rows supported: R20 (exact confirmed pixels), R38 and R41 (export validity and exact recovery values).

## Out of scope
Byte-identity of image files across builds. Full-tensor coverage claims. Legacy API pixel comparison. The expensive encoder lab check on every visitor.

## Considerations
- Never widen tolerances, change precision or replace numerics with a visual spot-check.
- Other models need their own references and declared tolerances (handled in the non-face proof).
- Integrated verification checks the **final integrated app** after the planned UI and package changes, against the identified Next branch baseline (`candidate/next-delivery-20260916`, reviewed commit `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3`, pinned control artifact) **plus** this plan's declared changes. Examples are representative; unlisted Next features are not dropped.
- Not historic-API parity, not a shutdown-qualification campaign, no physical-iPhone/physical-phone pass, no control/control performance report. Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a downgrade.
- Fix actual correctness, privacy, cancellation and resource errors found; record unsupported/untested cells. Fixes land in the owning workstream; this bead re-runs.
- Wording distinguishes planned, experimental, implemented and deployed. No weights or secrets in Git.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Raw synthesis comparison report per route: max RGB diff <= 1, max raw-float error <= 0.002; e4e latent max abs error <= 0.0001.
- [ ] Export checks report dims, orientation, playback validity, exact recovery values, lossless decode equality; no byte-equality gate.
- [ ] Re-encoded payload envelope validates against the new payload.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome) through the shared emitter from `build.event-log-core` (fm-bd03) and passes `scripts/check-event-log.ts`; the log is kept as a CI artifact, privacy-filtered like diagnostics; screenshots kept on failure.

title: Parity: preserved performance paths and retained CI cells, port versus control
description:
## Background
Retained lanes: `next-site.yml` (artifact/qualify/compiled-ui), `next-e2e.yml` real-ui-cpu (actual CPU name/seed and e4e, crop, original reuse, recovered still without inference, GPU refusal/fallback scope, playable/saved MP4, face/video/slider restore), `next-matrix.yml` (Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, macOS WebKit/Firefox), `mobile-browser.yml` (Android emulator 8 components, iOS Simulator components, ios-product), `next-gpu-lane.yml` (GTX1050 evidence, not a gate). Invariants: keyed synthesis admission receipts (one cold canary, deferred rest), `warmMapping()` overlap, bounded 1-4 CPU threads, single-threaded streamed e4e, cache-only worker, warm output hits need no inference, Firefox storage-permission timing, no-third-party gate.

## Why
Carry the actual candidate code forward: equal visual output is insufficient if warm reuse, bounded resources, restoration or export reuse are lost.

## Scope
Run the available cells with the pinned control and the TS/React milestone build on the same workload/cell; record provider/model/runtime, resolution/FPS/frame count, cache state, visible-tab state and finish boundary; protect first/nth face, confirmed photo, complete video, first/repeated Save, restore, bytes, memory reservations and cancellation. Investigate meaningful regressions with repeated evidence.

## Out of scope
New benchmark campaigns; physical-iPhone qualification.

## Considerations
A noisy single hosted-CI timing is not a speed verdict; correctness/resource regressions fail. Raw synthesis keeps frozen tolerances (RGB max diff 1, raw-float 0.002, e4e 0.0001); encoded bytes may differ.

## Comparison method: the shared no-regression protocol (polish r2)
This leaf uses the single protocol written once in the preservation map (`build.preservation-map-extension` fm-rqc, section "No-regression comparison protocol"), which `verify.artifact-no-regression` and `ortweb.desktop-perf` also use:
- Control = the pinned candidate artifact by hash (`migration.control-custody`), on the same cell and workload as the port build.
- Record provider/model/runtime, resolution/FPS/frame count, cold/retained/resident/restored state, visible-tab state and the same finish boundary.
- Protected metrics: first/nth face, confirmed-photo work, complete video, first/repeated Save, restore, responsiveness, acquired/output bytes, memory reservations, cancellation.
- Correctness and resource regressions fail. A latency or bytes regression is investigated only with compatible repeated evidence and a margin from control/control variability (`evaluator.noise-baseline` fm-a274 when it exists; it is research-terminal and this leaf does not wait for it, so otherwise this leaf's own control/control pairs on the cell). A single noisy hosted-CI timing is never a speed verdict.
- Encoded-byte differences are size/cost, not image identity. No compensating phone CPU with desktop GPU gains, or 512 px video with 1024 px.
If this text and fm-rqc's ever differ, fm-rqc's wins and the difference is reported.

## Evidence-register rows protected here (polish r2)
From fm-rqc's register:
- eris RTX 2080 SUPER, Chromium 152 WebGPU, warm 26-frame morph ABBA×4 (pipeline 129.8->69.7 ms/frame; RGBA8 42.6->37.1 ms/frame; warm face 103.5->75.6 ms). Re-run port vs control on that cell under the shared device lease. Record it untested if no lease is available.
- Ubuntu 24.04 Chrome CPU ABBA×3 repeat-reuse facts: repeat original 113.00->88.76 ms and repeat Save 100.72->66.49 ms must not regress. The first-Save size/latency tradeoff (108.63->202.17 ms while 4.38 MB->117 KB) is a known, accepted tradeoff, not a regression.
- iPhone 16 Pro Simulator iOS 18.5 product job (first full-1024 face 25,287 ms; warm synthesis 4,741.2 ms) through `build.ci-mobile-ios-lane`.
Rows marked evidence gap (physical iPhones, current Firefox/WebKit full performance, GTX 1050 inference) are listed untested, never passed.

## Baseline-note items checked by name (polish r2)
From the 11 October delivery note at classic `b2d945a8`, each gets a port-vs-control cell:
- Mobile controls and crop geometry fixes.
- Background WebP retention with PNG fallback.
- Bounded compressed multi-face/video/scrub session recovery (restore without repeated inference).
- Corrected asynchronous retention checks.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Per-cell comparison table (passed / failed / untested / inconclusive) with workload boundaries.
- [ ] No correctness/resource regression; any latency/bytes regression has an investigation note.
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome), keeps screenshots on failure, and the log is retained as a CI artifact (privacy-filtered like diagnostics). Network claims are asserted from the log, never from screenshots.
- [ ] Receipt committed under `docs/receipts/migration/parity-perf.md` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt missing a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Receipt cites the fm-rqc no-regression protocol by name, states control/control margins per compared metric (source: `evaluator.noise-baseline` or own control pairs), and lists the three register rows above plus the four baseline-note items with passed / failed / untested / inconclusive per cell; evidence-gap rows recorded untested.

title: Re-home research workflows with path filters and leased heavy steps
description:
## Background

Classic workflows `research-built-ui-media-v1.yml` and `research-rgba-screen-v1.yml` reference the tree.

## Why

Research CI must trigger on new code roots and use explicit artifact lookup.

## Scope

- Destination workflows using maintained drivers; path filters over `apps/web/**`, `packages/**`,
  `autoresearch/**` (maintained paths), `scripts/**`.
- Explicit artifact lookup (source repo ID, workflow/run, commit, artifact); heavy steps via the lease wrapper.
- Experimental jobs bounded and separate from product checks.

## Out of scope

Disabling classic copies (classic wind-down).

## Considerations

- Acquire the shared physical-device lease (`autoresearch/run.py --device <name>` with the machine's
  absolute state directory) before every heavy build, correctness run, warmup and measurement; never
  terminate another owner's work; inspect interrupted runs and other load before starting.
- Use a fresh run label (`A-Z`, `a-z`, digits, `_`/`-`) with no existing output directory; never overwrite
  earlier logs or measured source; new candidates get new directories.
- `results.tsv` keeps its 11-column header and only appends evaluated outcomes; corrections are new rows
  referencing prior IDs; `log.md` entries append at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps;
  `state/runs.jsonl` is the ignored execution journal.
- Numerical correctness at unchanged tolerances (RGB <= 1, sampled raw-float <= 0.002, e4e latent 0.0001)
  passes before any performance acceptance; architecture/parity without faster timings is not a `keep`.
- Results are experimental evidence at their recorded scope (machine, browser, build, cache state);
  Simulator or desktop results never stand in for physical-phone evidence.
- Raise newly found opportunities as proposals in the round record with the next refuting test; do not
  change product policy or tolerances.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] One recorded run per workflow; a change under `packages/` triggers them.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Refine the fullscreen names modal to the legacy gapless overlaid-name grid with accepted Back exit
description:
## Background
Legacy standalone names grid: sibling `facemorph-names/src/ImageGrid.svelte`, `LabelledImageButton.svelte`,
`VirtualList.svelte` (edge-to-edge faces, no gaps/borders, names over images). Candidate SCSS gives fullscreen/gapless
layout but the modal has header/search/Close/Show more and labels below faces. Defect 14 (operated): labels and Close
near-black on near-black (contrast 1.18:1, title 2.0:1); a failed name list leaves an empty dialog with the error behind
it. Legacy production's embedded picker has a dark "Select an Image" header and X (observed 11 October).

## Why
Gapless headerless picker is an original requirement; the touch Back exit is accepted.

## Scope
- Edge-to-edge gapless grid; names over images readable at 4.5:1 against a scrim/shadow on any face; no search,
  header, X or Show more.

  Back dismiss without page navigation or a history loop; small floating Back on touch browsers without visible Back,

- Only the topmost modal owns Escape/Back/focus; page beneath inert.
- Bounded preview window/cache (no accumulation of thousands of images); windowing preserves keyboard navigation;
  scroll preserved where inexpensive.
- Error/empty states show inside the dialog and stay dismissible.

Static-result fetching (next leaf); exact-name search (settled: not needed).

Copy the visual interaction, not the old iframe/API architecture. No `/names` route.

title: Crop editor per crop 2.png and the alignment-failure path
description:
## Goal
Build the "Crop your image" editor faithful to the locked `crop 2.png`, and the alignment-failure and detector-refusal path from `failed to align.png` with optional manual crop. Adjust Crop and the confirmed-crop loop repair are original requirements; the candidate's pan/zoom DOM (drag, zoom 1-8, 90° rotate, no guide) must not substitute for this design, and the candidate's outright refusal of unaligned photos is replaced by classic's accept-with-warning behaviour.

## Scope
- **Editor layout** (same modal element as face.encode; boxes/colours from `docs/design/legacy-encode-dialog-geometry.json`, cropper basis chosen by face.design (stated in `legacy-dialog-reference.ts`)): title **"Crop your image"**, logo top right; photo letterboxed in a wide frame; square stencil (thin light outline, eight white square handles); translucent light oval face guide with two dark round eye markers in its upper half; centred under the photo the crop-rotate icon and degree readout ("0°" at open); full-width slider (indigo track, round thumb); copy verbatim: bold "Cropping is generally not necessary, as faces are usually auto detected." then "Try to leave a bit above the top of the head and below the chin." and "Lining up the eyes is most important."; footer CANCEL left, USE CROP right.
- **Stencil.** Fixed 1:1; resizable from each of the eight handles (corners both axes, edges one axis with the square held); body drag moves it; stays within the photo unless the operator answers yes to crop-past-the-edge.
- Oval guide and eye markers are overlays inside the stencil, scaling with it, never burned into encoder pixels.
- **Rotation.** The crop-rotate icon is a button rotating 90° per press; the slider sets fine rotation; the readout shows the total angle in whole or half degrees with "°" ("0°", "90°", "17.5°"). Slider range and step as recorded in the inventory (legacy default -45° to 45° around the current quarter turn; use what `EncodeImageDialog.fs` used).
- USE CROP updates the proposal and returns to confirmation (no encoding); CANCEL / Escape / Back restore the prior proposal exactly and return to confirmation.
- **Batch.** Adjust Crop edits the focused/last-selected photo candidate only, identified in the editor (e.g. "Face 2 of 3" in the title row); never changes selection order; recovered candidates are not adjustable.
- Output rectangle/rotation in source-pixel coordinates after EXIF orientation, feeding the frozen preprocessing contract.
- **Keyboard**: Tab reaches the stencil, each handle, the rotate button, the slider, CANCEL and USE CROP in visual order; arrows move the stencil or focused handle (Shift for larger steps); slider keys rotate.
- **Touch**: each handle has a hit area >= 44 x 44 px at touch widths (drawn squares may be smaller); dragging a handle does not scroll the page. Stencil, guide, readout, slider and footer stay visible or reachable by the modal's own scroll at 320 px and a 568 px-high viewport.
- **Cropper extras** (wheel/pinch zoom, crop past the edge, posing tip): open operator question; candidate behaviour (none of the three) until answered.
- **Failure layout** per `failed to align.png` with the two renames: title **"Encode an image"**, logo top right, full-image preview (whole image at its aspect ratio), red filled button centred under it labelled **ADJUST CROP**, red line **"Unable to auto align face."**, guidance verbatim except the typo ("looking towards the camera" by default, per the inventory), CANCEL left, OK right.
- **Three distinct states**: (1) no face detected (detector ran): the failure layout; (2) detector assets refused/unavailable: same layout but the red line says detection did not run (e.g. "Face detection did not run."), never "Unable to auto align face."; an unrun detector is never a failure; (3) malformed/unsupported pixels: actionable terminal error (choose another image), no ADJUST CROP, no OK, no encoder request.
- From failure: ADJUST CROP opens the editor; USE CROP returns to confirmation with the manual crop; OK there encodes it. OK directly from failure continues with the eligible whole-image pixels (the default square proposal the inventory records) and reaches exactly one e4e attempt or an actionable error; detection failure after OK cannot reopen the crop prompt; repeated OK gives one attempt. Never force manual repair, never encode unconfirmed pixels automatically, never an automatic crop loop.
- Detector refusal abandons that acquisition only; OK/manual continuation is a new explicit request for remaining prerequisites, never a revival of the refused detector.
- No raw runtime exception text as visitor copy; one message owner per failed action.

## Out of scope
Encoding/fallback internals and typed detector failure kinds (crop workstream exposes them); consent grant; cropper extras unless the operator says yes.

## Notes
- Renders the typed detector failure kinds that the crop workstream exposes; detector/alignment calls go through the facade unchanged. Ported crop editor (cropper component or `photo/crop-view.mjs`); no shared bridge/runtime/worker file.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#supplied-ui-references, #confirmed-crop-and-ordered-multi-selection-flow, #crop-fidelity-and-export-flow-clarification, #locked-original-requirements-and-images, #next-release-ui-and-photo-requirements (repair confirmed-crop loop).

title: Engine contracts: capabilities, operations, worker messages, recovery metadata, crop policy, numerics
description:
## Goal

Freeze, as exported TypeScript in `packages/stylegan-js`, the engine-side contracts of contracts milestone 1: loaded model and encoder capabilities with their timing hooks, engine operations including `renderMorph` and the structured-clone-safe worker messages, the recovery-metadata reader result, the confirmed-crop preprocessing policy, and the synthesis numerical and export-quality rules. Types are derived from the real candidate adapters (the survey below), not guesses, so the port stays faithful and the bounded e4e stream stays viable on phones. Split out of contracts milestone 1 in the 24 October final pass so each half is reviewable in one sitting; the manager-side half (`contracts.m1`, fm-hwh) builds on these types and closes the milestone.

## Scope

**Adapter survey (input to the types, not a deliverable).** Read at the pinned import revision (classic until imported): `src/Next/browser/runtime.mjs`, `src/Next/browser/ort-worker.mjs`, `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs` (statically imports `desktop/runtime.mjs`), `Assets/model-cache.mjs`, `Assets/shard-store.mjs`, `photo/crop.mjs`, `media.mjs`, `video-worker.mjs`, `last-result.mjs`, `browser/identity.mjs`, `image-envelope.mjs`, `estimate.mjs`. Every exported function, worker message, callback, promise and owned resource gets a contract owner. Classify `desktop/runtime.mjs` as a retirement seam (provider simplification removes native dispatch), not a native contract. Identify every place a signal/callback/promise crosses a worker boundary and every network-repair-capable handle (`model-cache.mjs` `acquire()`, `bytes()`, `open()`). `estimate.mjs` cold synthesis constants are historical single-device priors and its `encodeMs` is video export, not photo encode: preflight types must not inherit them.

**Engine capability** — `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/capability.ts`, `timing.ts`:
- `ModelIdentity`, `LoadedModelCapability` (mapping, synthesis, optional encoder; dimensions and latent schema explicit), `LoadedEncoderCapability` (`encode`, `abort`, `dispose` only), `ProviderState` (requested, actual, admission, validation), `UnsupportedCapability`, `ResidencyTransition` (encoder → synthesis), `MemoryBoundName` (named placeholders; numeric values set in milestone 2).
- The engine accepts a caller-supplied, already-loaded capability; it has no model URLs, chunk downloader, OPFS cache, model-host dependency or UI/reporting policy. No URLs, OPFS handles or `acquireBytes` callbacks reach it; the network-repair-capable cache handle is never exposed as an offline loaded capability.
- Encoder baseline: the manager/provider adapter supplies a loaded encoder whose `encode` owns bounded sequential session creation/execution/release (today 108 sequential ORT sessions over FP32 shards); it may read verified local shards lazily; no engine-originated network acquisition during execution. Consent-authorised acquisition and verification of the encoder's shards finish before its admission; unrelated approved acquisition proceeds under its own budgets. "Loaded" means ready for offline execution, not all sessions resident.
- `StageTimingEvent`, `StageCompletionBoundary` (`inference-complete` | `readback-complete` | `map-async-complete`), `E4eTimings` (verifiedReadMs, sessionCreateMs, runMs, totalMs, wasmHeapBytes, maxLiveSessions). Hooks await real inference/readback completion (incl. GPU `mapAsync`), never submission time, a mock or whole bridge-call duration; engine events are reporting-transport-free.
- Dependency injection for loaded capabilities; unsupported capabilities and cleanup explicit.

**Engine operations** — `operations.ts`, `worker-messages.ts`, `recovery-metadata.ts`:
- `OperationIds` (requestId, inputRevision, attemptId); `MappingRequest/Result`, `SynthesisRequest/Result`, `EncodeRequest/Result`, `ExtractMetadataRequest/Result`, `RawImageEncodeRequest` (`png` | `webp-lossless`, with `RecoveryMetadata`), `RenderMorphRequest` (endpoints, `MorphSettings` with `MorphPathMode` covering every current selector mode incl. linear and figure-eight, frame count, FPS, resolution, display callbacks caller-side), `RenderMorphResult`, `ResultMilestone` (`compute-ready` | `file-complete`), `OperationSettlement` (`completed` | `cancelled` | `superseded` | `failed`), `MAX_MORPH_FRAMES` (the classic 4,096-frame path value as the starting frame budget; milestone 2's ceilings file replaces it with a per-route budget derived from measured memory, storage and time; never a face count). Actual provider recorded on every result.
- `ResultReadiness` = `{pixelsAvailable, fileReady, persisted, displayDecoded, videoPlayable}` (each boolean or `not-applicable`); `file-complete` never implies persistence or display readiness.
- Cancellation/disposal settles pending operations; late results cannot replace newer input.
- `EngineWorkerRequest`/`EngineWorkerResponse` unions are structured-clone safe: no functions, promises or AbortSignals; signals/callbacks stay caller-side; status/capability reads start no acquisition.
- Buffer/device ownership; retained frame, resource, cancellation and evidence contracts with named bounds. Media branch table, one row each for cached result, raw sparse preview anchors, blob stream, sequential, retained-then-encode, endpoint reuse: callback/drain type, buffer owner, and the anchor-ordering rule that stops sparse anchors deadlocking ordered video drain. Media path today: WebCodecs 1024→512, FFmpeg 512 fallback, eight-frame raw segments, bounded codec queues.
- `parseRecoveryMetadata(bytes)` returns exactly one of `{kind:'missing'}`, `{kind:'damaged', reason}` (parse, integrity hash or bounds failure), `{kind:'incompatible-schema', schemaVersion}`, `{kind:'parsed', metadata: RecoveryMetadataV1}`. Model comparison is the app's job. The reader never fetches a URL found in metadata. V1 does not hard-code 18×512 (shape comes from descriptor fields).

**Confirmed-crop preprocessing policy** — `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/crop-policy.ts`:
- `ConfirmedCrop` is readonly (`Readonly` plus `Object.freeze`), created once at crop OK and never edited; Adjust Crop or Encode image creates a new record with a new revision. Required fields exactly: `sourceRevision`, `sourceDigest` (SHA-256 of source bytes), `rect {left, top, width, height}` (integers, oriented source pixels), `rotationDegrees`, `exifOrientation` (1–8), `exifApplied`, `policyVersion`, `policyParams`; plus `confirmedCropId` = SHA-256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, UTF-8, integers as written) of those fields — the cache, provenance and export-identity key.
- `CropPreprocessingPolicyV1` (version, resize, colour, normalisation, encoder input size); `deriveEncoderInput(sourcePixels, crop) -> {tensor: Float32Array [1,3,256,256], tensorDigest, policyVersion}` is the only route to the encoder and runs once; `CropDerivationError`.
- Constants: `CROP_MAX_BYTES = 64*1024*1024`, `CROP_MAX_PIXELS = 120*1024*1024`, `CROP_MAX_EDGE = 20000`, `CROP_OUTPUT = 1024`, `PREVIEW_MAX_EDGE = 4096` (`SINGLE_INPUT_LIMITS`). The 25 MB `align-photo.mjs` limit bounds only the detector proposal and never rejects a confirmed crop.
- Testable properties: `noRedetectAfterConfirm`, `noRewarpAfterConfirm`, `guidesNotBurned`, `singleE4eAttemptPerConfirmedCrop`, `detectionFailureNeverReopensCrop`. Detector alignment/warp only shapes the proposal before confirmation; on detector failure or refusal a manual crop with eligible pixels may reach e4e; an eligible confirmed crop reaches one e4e attempt or an actionable error; optional post-confirmation validation cannot alter pixels or block encoding; malformed pixels fail clearly.

**Numerics and export rules** — `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/numerics.ts`:
- `PRODUCT_CANARY_TOLERANCE` (`maxRgbDiff: 1` on 0–255, `maxSampledRawFloatError: 0.002`), `E4E_LATENT_TOLERANCE` (`maxAbsError: 0.0001`), `NumericalCheckResult` (raw differences, not only pass/fail), `ExportQualityRule` list with `isGate` flags: gates are dimensions, orientation, valid format/playback, lossless decode equals supplied pixels, recovery envelope regenerated on re-encode (never copy an obsolete integrity hash); encoded-byte identity and decoded-lossy equality are `isGate: false`.
- Raw pre-compression synthesis is compared with the independent qualified reference (same model, latent, noise, preprocessing, workload) across qualified CPU/WebGPU routes. Research suites (full31 etc.) keep their own frozen tolerances. Encoder lab checks stay in lab/CI, not per visitor. Artifact/model/asset hashes bind inputs, manifests, packages, deployments; export-integrity hashes validate individual files only. Other models need their own references and tolerances. Each tolerance cites its candidate source file and suite. The constants file's digest feeds the currency tolerance guard.

**Placement and tests.** All types live directly in the packages scaffolded by the build workstream, as public exports; no runtime implementation beyond validators; contract type environments scoped so they gain no accidental DOM/Node globals.

## Out of scope

Manager lifecycle, leases, grant, budgets and manifest compatibility (`contracts.m1`); engine implementation; numeric byte ceilings and app batch/progress/scheduler/preflight types (milestone 2 rows); running canaries; non-face tolerances; MP4 project import UI (deferred by operator); any change to candidate adapters.

## Notes

## Notes

- PLAN.md (newer) says contracts are TS modules in the owning packages with type tests and a limits constants file and "there is no separate `contracts.md`". The absorbed beads' `contracts.md`, draft `docs/plans/.../contracts/` files and export-index table are dropped; the citable export names above are kept and checked by a type test instead.
- Stable exported names: downstream workstreams cite them; a rename is a contract revision.
- Any alternative encoder ownership needs equivalent independent-consumer, memory and acquisition-boundary evidence. Worker placement and GPU residency are measured implementation choices, not contract.
- Shared files: the facade and compute extraction later edit `product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs`, `browser/ort-worker.mjs`; this bead only defines types.
- Leases constrain manager behaviour, not the browser's ability to reclaim storage.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#package-and-operation-contracts, #stylegan-js, #browser-model-manager, #cloudflare-model-host, #model-conv, #synthesis-correctness-and-export-quality, #confirmed-crop-and-ordered-multi-selection-flow, #consented-downloads-useful-overlap-and-cached-model-warming.
- The survey's contract-owner list (every exported function, worker message, callback, promise and owned resource of the surveyed adapters, with its owning type or the manager half) is committed as a doc comment table in `capability.ts`, so the manager half and the typed facade read it.
- The decode measurement (`contracts.decode`) reads the `CROP_MAX_*` limits from this bead.

- [x] Type-level tests per discriminated union (exhaustiveness; invalid states unrepresentable); a deliberately invalid state in a fixture fails compilation; `npm run typecheck` passes.
- [x] Type test: a `file-complete` result does not type-check as `persisted` or `displayDecoded` without those `ResultReadiness` fields set.

- [x] Caller-loaded consumer test (types/stubs): seed→mapping→synthesis and confirmed crop→encode with a caller-loaded capability and no manager import.

title: Publish the checkpoint compatibility table and support boundary
description:
## Background
External developer journey step 1: choose a checkpoint using a compatibility table: source serialization (which PyTorch/TF pickle variants are actually accepted), StyleGAN architecture, conditional/unconditional inputs, resolution/channels, Z/W dimensions and W+ layer count, precision/operators and qualified providers; list unsupported cells and an available conversion route; record checkpoint source/digest and model-specific usage/redistribution terms. The upstream model list (NVlabs stylegan2-ada-pytorch) includes conditional models, which does not establish converter support.

## Why
Developers must not assume every StyleGAN checkpoint works; the table states exactly what was qualified.

## Scope
- `packages/model-conv/docs/compatibility.md` with the table filled from actual runs (qualified / unqualified / unsupported per cell), checkpoint sources, digests and terms.
- Acquisition docs for NVlabs and the linked catalogue without claiming every catalogue checkpoint works.
- Explain that photo-to-latent inversion needs a separately trained compatible encoder; FFHQ e4e is not a generic non-face encoder; say this before a developer downloads an encoder or designs an upload UI.

## Out of scope
Package READMEs (package publication and documentation, which links this table).

## Considerations
- Cells are updated as FFHQ and the non-face fixture qualify; unverified cells say so.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.

- [ ] Table committed; every "qualified" cell links a receipt; unsupported cells name the failure or missing route.
- [ ] Trusted-pickle warning and encoder limitation present.

title: Shared CI artifact lookup with explicit provenance, digest verification, path filters and cache keys
description:
## Background

Every carried-over lane (site, real-UI CPU, desktop matrix, Android, iOS components and product, GPU)
repeats the same adaptation in classic: find an artifact from another workflow run, prove where it
came from, verify its bytes, and run only when relevant paths change. Classic resolves artifacts with
the inherited `context.repo`; after the move, a corrected organisation prefix or inherited repository
alone cannot locate a classic artifact from this repository. Split out of the CI-lane carry-over
beads in polish round 2 so the shared part is written and reviewed once.

## Why

One tested lookup and one path-filter list stop each lane re-implementing provenance checks
slightly differently, and make "the artifact under test is the qualified bytes" a single assertion.

## Scope

- Composite action `.github/actions/fetch-artifact/action.yml` wrapping
  `scripts/ci/fetch-artifact.ts`. Required inputs, none inherited: `source_repo_id` (numeric GitHub
  repository ID, not owner/name), `workflow` (file name), `run_id`, `commit` (full SHA),
  `artifact_name`. Steps: query the run through the REST API with the job token (or a read-only
  token for a classic artifact), refuse when the run's `repository.id`, `head_sha` or workflow file
  differ from the inputs, download, then `sha256sum -c next-site-SHA256SUMS` (or the artifact's own
  sums file) and compare `next-site-source.txt` with the inputs. Outputs: `artifact_dir`,
  `artifact_digest` (the digest identity hashing defines, from `build.identity-hashing`),
  `provenance_json`.
- `scripts/ci/path-filters.json`: one list of code roots for all lanes (`apps/web/**`,
  `packages/**`, `scripts/**`, `hosting/**`, `photo-runtime/**` if imported, `tests/mobile/**`,
  `package*.json`, `tsconfig*.json`, `.oxlintrc.json`, `.oxfmtrc.json`, the lane's own workflow file
  and the actions it uses), plus per-lane narrowing; a test fails when a top-level code root exists
  that no lane filter covers.
- Concurrency convention: `<lane>-${{ github.ref }}` with cancel-in-progress for test builds only;
  never on a job that publishes or deploys.
- Cache convention: pinned dependency caches keyed by lockfile hash; immutable runtime/model assets
  keyed by their manifest digest, never by branch or date.
- Logging: every call writes one JSON line (inputs, resolved run, digest, verdict) and an event-log
  step through `scripts/evidence/event_log.py`/`event-log.ts`.

## Out of scope

The lanes' own jobs (site, e2e, matrix, mobile, GPU beads). Artifact fan-out to canonical bytes
(`build.artifact-fanout`, build.m2) — this action is what fan-out later points at the canonical
artifact.

## Considerations

- Fail closed: an API error, a missing sums file or a digest mismatch stops the lane with a named
  error; it never falls back to rebuilding silently.
- Classic artifacts expire (14-day retention); a lane that needs an expired classic artifact reports
  `blocked: artifact expired` rather than passing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit tests (`node --test scripts/ci/fetch-artifact.test.ts`, recorded API fixtures, no network) cover: wrong `repository.id`, wrong `head_sha`, wrong workflow file, missing sums file and one flipped byte each fail with a distinct named error; a correct fixture yields the expected `artifact_digest`; no input defaults to `context.repo`.
- [ ] A recorded workflow run in this repository fetches a classic `next-site-<sha>` artifact by explicit `source_repo_id`/`workflow`/`run_id`/`commit`/`artifact_name` and verifies it; a second run with the classic repository's owner/name in place of its numeric ID is refused.
- [ ] `scripts/ci/path-filters.json` covers every top-level code root; the coverage test fails on a fixture tree with an uncovered root.
- [ ] The JSON verdict line and the event-log step validate (`check-event-log`) for both the passing and the refused run.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.

title: Model-free preflight checker within its budgets
description:
## Goal
A small, model-free preflight check that runs before the first acquisition modal and gives evidence for download/compute estimates without downloading any model, detector, runtime or photo. It makes the download decision possible before bandwidth is spent, honestly, and never gates phones or reorders providers.

## Scope
- **Evidence read.** Browser capabilities; actual WebGPU adapter availability, features and limits (`GPU.requestAdapter`, not mere `navigator.gpu`); WASM/SIMD and permitted threading; coarse CPU/memory hints (`navigator.hardwareConcurrency`, `navigator.deviceMemory`; missing or rounded memory = unknown); and the storage quota/usage the browser reports (`navigator.storage.estimate()`) as evidence of what the page can keep (iOS reported a 1,000 MB quota with zero use in all 143 checks).
- **Samples.** On an eligible device, while visible and idle: a short worker-based WASM sample and, when available, a small WebGPU compute sample on generated buffers with representative arithmetic/memory access for the calibrated kernel families. Measure completed GPU work (`GPUQueue.onSubmittedWorkDone`), distinguishing warmup/compilation.
- **Budgets** (contracts milestone 2 freezes the evidence/estimate types and budgets): about 2 s sampling, 5 s UI deadline, <= 16 MiB explicitly allocated scratch, <= 100 KiB compressed checker code. Bounded chunks; deadline/cancel stops new submissions and ignores late callbacks; all resources released.
- Timeout, backgrounding, GPU loss or absent APIs -> broader estimate or "No reliable estimate for this device".
- Route label before real-model checks: "eligible; model check pending". Never demote a healthy route or reorder providers from timings; WebGPU synthesis says nothing about e4e speed. Generator and encoder admission stay separate.
- Reuse a compatible recent check; allow rerun; scores stay local under diagnostics consent.
- **Mobile safety.** The WebGPU sample runs only after `requestAdapter()` succeeds and the required limits fit; any validation error, device loss or timeout ends the sample with "No reliable estimate for this device", destroys its own device and never touches the inference device, the route choice or the CPU path. Phones keep working when the GPU sample fails.
- Any new diagnostics event gets its allowlist and privacy-policy entry; no photos, latents, typed input or raw error strings.

## Out of scope
UI placement and copy (device.ui); calibration mapping (device.calibration).

## Notes
- New small app module (worker with WASM-helper sample and optional WebGPU sample), not the inference runtime; edits none of the shared bridge/runtime/worker files.
- Tiny-buffer checks cannot predict memory exhaustion, thermal throttling, suspension or driver failures; never present them as qualification.
- Field data for context (findings note, 18 October): desktop WebGPU synthesis median 50 ms, Android WebGPU 738 ms, desktop CPU 1.28 s.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#lightweight-device-check-and-pre-download-guidance, #device-check-and-estimates, #provider-simplification.

title: Measure names data shapes and choose the smallest
description:
## Goal
Choose the smallest names data shape that meets the product's needs, by measurement, and set the numeric bars the generator, publication and picker are built to. `catalogue.json` is not a requirement (decided 16 October); the candidate's is 3.4 MB parsed, about 570 KB over the wire.

Generating results; UI.

title: Freeze stable export identity and collision-safe filename rules
description:
## Background

Operator ruling on filenames: short, informative defaults from the result's name, entered text, seed or
source-file basename (examples `emma-k4p7s2.webp`, `seed-42-j8m3r6.png`, `holiday-face2-v9d2h5.webp`,
`emma-noah-linear-c6q8t3.mp4`, `emma-noah-figure8-b7w4n2.mp4`; suffixes illustrative). At most 64
characters before the real extension; strip source extension, path components, control/bidi and
reserved characters/names; `face`/`morph` only when no label exists.

## Why

Media and recovery implements this and face controls renders it; both need one frozen identity definition.

## Scope

- Export identity inputs: crops, ordered inputs, morph mode/settings, model, encoding options; a short
  suffix derived from identity, extended on collision within the app's known export set (labels,
  timestamps or slot numbers alone are insufficient).
- Repeated Save/Share of the same prepared file reuses its name; identity survives restoration.
- Extension and MIME match actual WebP/PNG/MP4 bytes; PNG fallback updates both.
- Platform-specific no-clobber: ordinary downloads leave duplicates to the browser; optional file-picker
  writes use no-clobber naming or explicit overwrite confirmation.
- Filenames never authorise adding text/source names to embedded recovery metadata or diagnostics.

## Typed outputs (citable)

Draft first under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`, then moved by the milestone type-test bead to the module below. Exported names are stable: downstream beads cite them; a rename needs a contract revision and an update of the `contracts.md` export index.

- `apps/web/src/contracts/export-identity.ts`: `ExportIdentityInput` (crops, ordered inputs, morph mode/settings, model, encoding options), `ExportIdentity`, `ExportKind` (`webp` | `png` | `mp4`) with MIME, `suggestFilename(identity, knownExportSet)` signature, `FILENAME_MAX_STEM = 64`, `SanitizeRule` list, `NoClobberMode` (`browser-download` | `file-picker-no-clobber` | `file-picker-confirm-overwrite`).
- A golden table `apps/web/src/contracts/export-identity.vectors.json` (inputs → expected names, incl. long labels, bidi, reserved names, collisions) that `media.export-identity` tests consume.
- Consumers: `media.export-identity`, `face.share-save-export`, `contracts.ui-walkthrough`.

## Out of scope

Additional export formats (proposal only; deferred optional item owned by media and recovery).

## Considerations

No absolute cross-device uniqueness claim from a short suffix.

## Frozen values requested by media and recovery (polish r2)

`media.export-identity` (fm-9wy8) implements against these; they are frozen here, revised only by a
contract revision with a decision entry.
- **Identity digest.** `exportIdentityDigest(input)` = SHA-256 over a canonical JSON encoding (keys
  sorted, UTF-8, no whitespace) of `{kind, crops[] (ConfirmedCrop identities), orderedInputs[]
  (input identities in order), morph?: {mode, settings}, modelIdentity, format, encodingOptions}`.
  WebP and PNG of the same result therefore get distinct suffixes and share the label.
- **Suffix encoding.** `SUFFIX_ALPHABET = "bcdfghjkmnpqrstvwxz23456789"` (27 symbols: lowercase
  consonants without `l`, plus digits without `0`/`1`, so no vowels and no look-alikes; matches the
  operator examples' shape such as `k4p7s2`). The suffix is the digest read as a big-endian integer
  and written in this alphabet, most significant symbol first, taking the first `SUFFIX_LENGTH = 6`
  symbols.
- **Collision rule.** A collision is the same suggested name with a different identity inside the
  app's known export set (current session's prepared and saved names). Resolve by extending the
  suffix one symbol at a time from the same digest stream, up to `SUFFIX_MAX_LENGTH = 16`; a
  collision still present at 16 symbols is a typed error `ExportNameCollision` (never a silent
  overwrite, never a counter or timestamp).
- **Length.** The whole basename (label, `-`, suffix) is at most `FILENAME_MAX_STEM = 64` characters
  before the real extension. The label is truncated at a grapheme boundary to fit; the suffix is
  never truncated. An edited name keeps `-<suffix>` (the automatic disambiguator).
- **Prepared-file cache bound.** `PREPARED_FILE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 4` per tab: the current
  selection's prepared file (pinned, never evicted) plus up to 3 other (revision, format, options)
  entries, evicted oldest-first by last use. The byte bound `PREPARED_FILE_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` is a
  ceiling written by `contracts.byte-ceilings-freeze`; whichever bound is reached first evicts.
  Key = (result revision, format, encoding options); a completion for a superseded revision is
  discarded. The count of 4 is a planner's call (two still formats plus the current morph MP4 plus
  one spare) recorded as a decision entry.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts.md` export identity section with the derivation, sanitisation and truncation rules and a table of example inputs → names (including long labels, bidi characters, reserved names, collisions).
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
- [ ] Every name listed under "Typed outputs (citable)" exists in the draft type file and has a row in the `contracts.md` export index naming its consumers.
- [ ] `export-identity.ts` exports `SUFFIX_ALPHABET`, `SUFFIX_LENGTH = 6`, `SUFFIX_MAX_LENGTH = 16`, `FILENAME_MAX_STEM = 64`, `PREPARED_FILE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 4`, `exportIdentityDigest` and the `ExportNameCollision` error; `export-identity.vectors.json` includes a forced-collision vector (stubbed digest) that extends to 7 symbols, a 16-symbol exhaustion vector that yields `ExportNameCollision`, a 64-character boundary vector with a multi-codepoint grapheme at the cut, and WebP vs PNG of one result sharing the label with different suffixes.
- [ ] A decision entry under `docs/decisions/` records the suffix alphabet, length, collision rule and the cache count of 4 as a planner's call, and the receipt cites it.
notes: Anchor: PLAN.md#file-sharing-and-export-direction.

title: Rebind the app to stylegan-js and remove engine downloads
description:
## Background
After the engine operations exist in the package, the app (`product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs`, `browser/ort-worker.mjs` behind the typed facade) still owns copies of the moved code and engine-originated downloads/caches. The retained CI lanes: next-site.yml (artifact build/unit/import/geometry/integrity, `check-no-third-party.mjs`, exact CPU product qualification, Chromium compiled UI), next-e2e.yml real-ui-cpu, mobile-browser.yml android/ios eight components and ios-product lanes, next-gpu-lane.yml (non-gating GTX1050 WebGPU evidence), next-matrix.yml (manual cells, harness under repair).

## Why
Extraction is only done when the product actually runs on the package with its features, optimizations and cancellation intact; a cleaner package that loses Next behaviour fails the plan.

## Scope
- Replace the app's engine code paths with `stylegan-js` imports through the facade; delete the duplicated engine code and every engine-originated download/cache path.
- Keep app ownership of interaction, consent, input revisions, display URLs, retention and reporting transport.
- Run the applicable retained lanes against the rebuilt artifact and compare with the pinned control on the same cells (first/nth face, confirmed photo, complete video, first/repeat Save, restore, responsiveness, bytes, memory reservations, cancellation).
- Update stale harness assertions only in the revision that replaces the control they assert (check-migration map).

## Out of scope
Morph frame production (morph pipeline). Crop fix (confirmed-crop). New performance campaigns.

## Considerations
- A noisy single hosted-CI timing is not a speed verdict; investigate meaningful regressions with compatible repeated evidence.
- Missing physical-iPhone evidence is an evidence gap, not a reason to drop phone paths.
- Shared-file serialization (decided 16 October, mandatory edges 17 October): `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in the order provider simplification -> typed facade -> compute extraction -> confirmed-crop fix -> morph pipeline -> static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics reporting rebinding. Add every file this item edits to the check-migration map's conflict list. No worktrees; separate clones only for read-only runs.

Paths: the candidate is imported under `apps/web/` keeping `src/Next` structure (`apps/web/src/Next/...`); before import, read it in `../facemorph.me-classic/` at the planning reference `b2d945a8c7f0ff9f382fbfefaecc2651943077a3` (inventory freezes the actual import revision). Packages live at `packages/stylegan-js`, `packages/browser-model-manager`, `packages/cloudflare-model-host`, `packages/model-conv`.

Record planned, experimental, implemented and deployed results distinctly; no weights or secrets in Git; no fallback or backport to the old stack; no time box or human approval step.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Content scan: no engine code remains duplicated in `apps/web`; engine package has no host URLs/OPFS/UI/reporting.
- [ ] Retained lanes pass on the new artifact (next-site, next-e2e real-ui-cpu, mobile android/ios components, ios-product); next-gpu-lane evidence recorded (non-gating; software adapters rejected).
- [ ] Raw-synthesis tolerances met on each exercised route; e4e <= 0.0001.
- [ ] No-regression comparison against the control recorded per cell (untested cells listed, not passed).
- [ ] Every end-to-end script emits the structured event log (step ID, ISO timestamp, artifact digest, platform/provider, network requests by host class and bytes, console errors, outcome); screenshots are kept on failure; the log is retained as a CI artifact and privacy-filtered like diagnostics. Network claims are asserted from the log, never from a screenshot.
- [ ] Receipt committed in `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. A receipt that omits a field is incomplete, not passed.
notes: Position in the shared-file sequence: after compute.descriptor, before crop.fix. Shared-file order for area D (polish r2). `apps/web/src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited by area D leaves in one sequence, enforced by needs edges: typed facade (fm-pia9) -> compute.provider-adapters -> compute.mapping-synthesis -> compute.photo-orchestration -> compute.descriptor -> compute.app-rebind -> crop.fix -> crop.batch-encode -> crop.byte-ceilings -> media.split -> media.recovery-reader -> media.export-identity -> media.mp4-metadata -> morph.render-api -> morph.frame-budget -> morph.mp4-probe -> morph.scheduling -> morph.neighbour-rule -> then media.session-words and media.storage-clear (after the TS/React port) -> then the face, static-names picker and diagnostics edits. Leaves that must not edit these three files: ws:crop.repro (failing tests and the failure analysis only), crop.policy, media.envelope-helpers, media.recovery-schema, morph.descriptor-geometry, compute.consumer-example, compute.names-equality, and every conversion, pkgdocs and pkgaccept leaf. They keep the module export names the bridge imports today (`media.mjs` saveFile/shareFile/videoWriter; `recovery-metadata.mjs` decorateImage/downloadImage/recoverImage/decorateVideo/recoverVideoProject; `geometry/latent-path.mjs` createLatentPath/GEOMETRY_VERSION) and move logic behind them into the package. If such a leaf finds it must edit one of the three files, it records the file in the check-migration map conflict list and adds a needs edge to the latest leaf in the sequence that edits it; it never edits concurrently. Each sequenced leaf lists every file it edits in the check-migration map conflict list at claim time.

title: Freeze the versioned confirmed-crop preprocessing policy
description:
## Background

After crop OK, encoder pixels must derive once from the frozen confirmed crop (rectangle, rotation,
orientation, input revision) under a declared orientation/rotation/resize/color/normalization policy.
No redetection or rewarp may replace approved geometry; guides are not burned into pixels; optional
post-confirmation validation cannot alter pixels or block eligible direct-crop encoding. Existing
single-input limits in `src/Next/photo/crop.mjs`: 64 MiB compressed, 120 × 1024² pixels, 20,000 px edge.

## Why

Confirmed-crop encoding (its reproduction test and fix) and face controls build against this policy.

## Scope

- Versioned policy type: crop rectangle, rotation, EXIF orientation, resize, color, normalization,
  encoder input size; derivation happens once; detector-driven alignment/warp completes before
  confirmation and only shapes the proposal.
- Detector failure or refusal: manual crop with eligible pixels may reach e4e; an eligible confirmed
  crop reaches one e4e attempt or an actionable error; detection failure cannot reopen the crop prompt.
- Preserve existing single-input limits unless separately qualified.

## Typed outputs (citable)

Draft first under `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts/`, then moved by the milestone type-test bead to the module below. Exported names are stable: downstream beads cite them; a rename needs a contract revision and an update of the `contracts.md` export index.

- `packages/stylegan-js/src/contracts/crop-policy.ts`: `ConfirmedCrop` (rectangle, rotation, EXIF orientation, input revision), `CropPreprocessingPolicyV1` (version, resize, colour, normalisation, encoder input size), `deriveEncoderInput` signature (derivation happens once), `SINGLE_INPUT_LIMITS` (64 MiB compressed, 120 × 1024² pixels, 20,000 px edge), `CropDerivationError`.
- Testable properties (named for `crop.repro`/`crop.policy`/`crop.fix` tests): `noRedetectAfterConfirm`, `noRewarpAfterConfirm`, `guidesNotBurned`, `singleE4eAttemptPerConfirmedCrop`, `detectionFailureNeverReopensCrop`.
- Consumers: `crop.policy`, `crop.fix`, `crop.batch-encode`, `face.crop-confirm-modal`, `face.crop-editor-modal`.

## Out of scope

Batch/selection types (m2). Encoding implementation (confirmed-crop workstream).

## Considerations

Malformed/unsupported pixels still fail clearly. Only explicit Adjust Crop starts another adjustment.

## Frozen ConfirmedCrop field list (polish r2, requested by confirmed-crop and media)

`ConfirmedCrop` is a readonly record (TS `Readonly` plus `Object.freeze` at runtime), created once at
crop OK and never edited; Adjust Crop or Encode image creates a new record with a new source/input
revision. Fields, all required:
- `sourceRevision` (input revision of the source file) and `sourceDigest` (SHA-256 of the source bytes);
- `rect: {left, top, width, height}` in oriented source pixels (integers);
- `rotationDegrees` (number, the user's fine rotation plus any 90° steps);
- `exifOrientation` (1-8) and `exifApplied` (boolean);
- `policyVersion` and `policyParams` (the `CropPreprocessingPolicyV1` values used).
Identity: `confirmedCropId` = SHA-256 over a canonical JSON encoding (sorted keys, UTF-8, integers as
written) of every field above; it is the cache, provenance and export-identity key (cited by
`contracts.export-identity`). `deriveEncoderInput(sourcePixels, crop) -> {tensor: Float32Array
[1,3,256,256], tensorDigest, policyVersion}` is the only route from approved pixels to the encoder.
The candidate limits are exact constants: `CROP_MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024`,
`CROP_MAX_PIXELS = 120 * 1024 * 1024`, `CROP_MAX_EDGE = 20000`, `CROP_OUTPUT = 1024`,
`PREVIEW_MAX_EDGE = 4096`. The 25 MB `align-photo.mjs` limit bounds only the detector proposal and
never rejects a confirmed crop.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `docs/plans/repo-cleanup-and-architecture-refactor/contracts.md` preprocessing section with the versioned policy type and a worked example from source pixels to encoder tensor.
- [ ] The no-redetect/no-rewarp rule and the single-attempt rule are stated as testable properties for the confirmed-crop workstream.
- [ ] A receipt is written to `docs/receipts/` with every schema field: source commit; artifact digest; runtime and model identity where relevant; command or workflow run; platform and provider; outcome; deviations; untested cells; evidence link. title: Split last-result.mjs: UI preferences versus session retention
description:
## Background
`src/Next/last-result.mjs` (79 lines) mixes UI preference storage (`sliderPreference`, `sliderPosition`, `rememberSlider`) with completed-result/session retention (`rememberLast`, `readLast`, `rememberSession`, `readSession`) used by the bridge, plus the 4,096-frame path limit used with `video-worker.mjs`. The tie-break table assigns this split to the application migration's TS/React milestone (and the `media.mjs` split to media and recovery).

## Why
Application policy (slider preference, session selection) belongs to the app; retention formats must stay compatible for on-origin recovery.

## Scope
Move UI preferences into the app's TS store; keep session/result retention in a typed module with unchanged storage keys and formats; preserve bounded compressed session/video/scrub restoration.

## Out of scope
Dynamic-shape recovery schema (media and recovery); restore-words proposal (defect 9, media and recovery).

## Considerations
Do not edit `product-bridge.mjs` here; keep the retention module's exported names so the bridge import is unchanged (or defer the bridge-side rename to a later ordered revision). Shared-file serialization (decided 16/17 October): `src/Next/product-bridge.mjs`, `browser/runtime.mjs` and `browser/ort-worker.mjs` are edited in the order provider simplification -> typed facade -> compute extraction -> confirmed-crop fix -> morph pipeline -> static-names picker bridge edits and diagnostics reporting rebinding. Add any file this item edits to the check-migration map's conflict list.
