title: Research stage 1: guides, lease, ledger handover, provenance
description:
## Split (parallelism pass, 24 October 2026)
The **Lease** section below (per-machine state directory, `autoresearch/run.py` lease runner, runner and cross-repo concurrency tests) moved to fm-htbc (research lease), which has no prerequisites. This bead keeps the guides and protocol, the entry-command documentation, the ledger handover, the classic forward pointer and the clean-clone leased smoke, and uses fm-htbc's runner.

## Goal

Make the research system usable from this repository so new rounds optimise the new application and packages and classic receives no new rounds: maintained guides and protocol for this repository with one named entry command, one absolute lease state directory per machine shared by both repositories, a declared ledger handover with append-only and fork checks plus a classic forward pointer. It ends with a clean-clone leased smoke. It claims no performance result, needs only the application inventory and the imported tree, and is independent of release (an early candidate promotion from classic does not wait for it). It feeds the decode measurement, the lease CI wrapper, deploy re-homing (the promotion gate reads the canonical ledger), static names and classic wind-down.

## Scope

**Guides and protocol** — maintained `README.md` guide, `program.md` protocol, `records.md` standards, round and log-entry templates rewritten as new revisions (historical copies stay in Git history and frozen trees). State that PLAN.md governs release scope over older guide text. Rules carried: lease before every heavy build/correctness run/warmup/measurement; control/control noise first; discarded warmup + same-cell ABBA ×3; fresh confirmation separate from screening; append-only `log.md` at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps; `results.tsv` 11-column header, evaluated outcomes only, corrections as new rows; opportunity reporting; native evidence stays historical. Methodology boundaries (12 October check): no resets, no empty-ledger initialisation, no unbounded looping, no crash-as-zero metrics; a noisy minimum is not a gain.
- One entry command from the repository root: `python3 autoresearch/run.py --lane <lane> --device <machine> --state-dir "<absolute per-machine lease dir>" --timeout <s ≤ 3600> -- <driver command with quoted arguments>`; worked example (replacing classic's relative-state recipe): `python3 autoresearch/run.py --lane browser-gpu --device eris --state-dir "<ABS_LEASE_DIR>" --timeout 1800 -- autoresearch/devices/eris/gpu-bench.sh "UNIQUE_RUN_LABEL" "QUALIFIED_ORIGIN" 6`. The guide says this GPU screen is not the chooser-overlap benchmark and the evaluator/adapters do not exist merely because the wrapper exists.
- Round template: dated round, named journey/bottleneck, exclusions, one falsifiable mechanism per candidate, budget, new candidate directory; control/control noise before candidates; ABBA ×3; separate fresh confirmation; every screened candidate recorded; cohorts (empty cache, cached files/new browser, live resident session, cached output, restored result); finish boundaries (decoded/drawn face, useful scrub frame, playable video, prepared file, Save/share handoff).
- Opportunity fields: source/artifact, affected wait/journey/cache/device, bottleneck or hypothesis, mechanism, consent/asset/memory/cancellation costs, preserved invariants, platform cells, suitable worker, next refuting test; a proposal is not a ledger outcome or tracker authorisation.

**Lease** — one absolute state directory per physical machine (eris, TrueNAS, Triton when available) via machine-level config or environment variable read by `run.py`, documented; classic invocations on those machines use the same directory (machine config or documented `--state-dir`; any classic code change is a separately reviewable classic commit excluding other sessions' changes). The relative `autoresearch/state` gave two leases per GPU. `run.py`: budgets (default 600 s, max 3600 s), busy exit 75 or bounded `--wait`, owned process-group cleanup, `state/runs.jsonl` journal; refuses a nested second lease from the same process tree and a lease device differing from the host doing the work.

**Ledger handover**
- Record the prefix hash (bytes of `results.tsv` at snapshot) and last journal entry IDs as a dated `log.md` entry and a `state/runs.jsonl` event (never a `results.tsv` row); the first evaluated outcome row here cites them in its provenance cell. Keep the 11-column header; never initialise an empty ledger.
- `scripts/check-research-ledger.mjs` (CI on every `autoresearch/**` change): exact header; HEAD starts byte-for-byte with the merge-base file; snapshot prefix hash still matches; unique row IDs; corrections reference existing IDs; outcome column from the record standard's enum (no unrun proposal as outcome); dated `log.md` files only grow at EOF with unique IDs and timezone-aware timestamps. Fork detection: with read access to classic, any row appended to classic's `results.tsv` (default and candidate branches) after handover fails as "new round in classic".
- Classic forward pointer: one separately reviewable classic commit in its research README (skip and report paths with uncommitted edits) saying research moved here at <commit>, canonical ledger and journal are `autoresearch/results.tsv` / `autoresearch/state/runs.jsonl` here, start no new rounds in classic.
- Interim rule until this bead merges: the only executable research checkout is classic, under its append-only rules; no new optimisation round starts there.


**Smoke** — from a clean clone on a worker, one documented command runs a bounded smoke through the lease runner and journals it; digest and ledger-prefix checks re-run; a concurrent classic run is held off.

## Out of scope

Driver changes and workflows (stage 2); the CI lease wrapper (workspace build); removing classic's research tree (classic wind-down); re-qualifying any row; the evaluator.

## Notes

- No time box, no human approval step, no fallback or backport to the classic stack (operator, 17 and 18 October).
- PLAN.md (24 Oct): no receipts; the handover lives in the research log/journal, which is the research system's own record.
- Anchors: PLAN.md#autoresearch-re-homing, #targeted-autoresearch-launch-and-preserved-history, #autoresearch-coverage-and-preservation-map, #end-state-of-the-repositories.

# FaceMorph research

Research optimises the new application and packages in this repository: every wait a person sits
through, from first load to a saved or shared file, on the first visit and every later one. Since
24 October 2026 (fm-zxj) this is the research home. Classic
([facemorph.me-classic](https://github.com/check-face/facemorph.me-classic)) keeps its experiment
history read-only, and **no new round starts there**.

[PLAN.md](../PLAN.md) and the beads govern release scope; where this guide or an older research
document differs, they win. The [protocol](program.md) says how one experiment runs, and the
[record standards](records.md) say how it is written down.

## The one entry command

Every heavy build, correctness run, warmup or measurement runs under the machine's device lease,
from the repository root:

```sh
python3 autoresearch/run.py --lane <browser-cpu|browser-gpu|native-cpu|native-gpu|build> --device <machine> \
  --state-dir "<absolute per-machine lease dir>" --timeout <seconds, at most 3600> -- <driver command with quoted arguments>
```

Worked example on eris, which replaces classic's relative-state recipe:

```sh
python3 autoresearch/run.py --lane browser-gpu --device eris --state-dir "/home/cdilga/.local/state/facemorph/lease" \
  --timeout 1800 -- autoresearch/devices/eris/gpu-bench.sh "UNIQUE_RUN_LABEL" "QUALIFIED_ORIGIN" 6
```

- The lease is one per physical machine and shared with classic, the device lab and heavy CI. Its
  directory, config and refusals are in [ops/lease](../ops/lease/README.md). Busy exits 75; `--wait`
  is a bounded wait, not a queue.
- That GPU screen is a route benchmark. It is **not** the chooser-overlap benchmark, and the
  evaluator and its adapters do not exist just because the wrapper does. The eris drivers still call
  classic's `scripts/next-gpu-benchmark.py`; stage 2 (fm-qqh) re-homes the drivers onto this app.
- The runner journals every command to `<lease dir>/runs.jsonl` (one journal per machine, shared
  with classic). Exit zero means the command finished, never that it qualified.

## Where things are

| Record | Path |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical evaluation ledger (append-only, 11 columns) | [results.tsv](results.tsv) |
| New rounds, each with its README, experiments and append-only log | [rounds/](rounds/) ([templates](rounds/templates/)) |
| Research handover from classic | [rounds/2026-10-24-handover](rounds/2026-10-24-handover/README.md) |
| Device recipes and drivers | [devices/eris](devices/eris/README.md) |
| Frozen candidates and their reports | [candidates/](candidates/) |
| Frozen historical rounds and history | [reviews/](reviews/README.md), [history/](history/performance-through-2026-10-09/README.md), [benchmark campaign v2](benchmark-campaign-v2/README.md) |
| Proposed automation, not implemented | [loop-v3 proposal](loop-v3-proposal.md) |
| Import provenance of everything above | [docs/research-import](../docs/research-import/provenance.md) |

`reviews/`, `history/`, `candidates/`, `devices/`, `benchmark-campaign-v2/` and the old
`templates/` are the byte-identical import of classic at `b2d945a`; they are history, not current
instructions. Earlier versions of this guide, the protocol and the record standards are in classic's
Git history.

## Checks

`node scripts/check-research-ledger.mjs` runs in CI on every `autoresearch/**` change: the ledger
keeps its header and every earlier byte, including the handover snapshot; new rows record evaluated
outcomes only; round logs only grow at EOF; the links in these documents and in classic's forward
pointer resolve; and with `--classic` a row appended to classic's ledger after the handover fails as
a new round in classic. `node scripts/check-research-import.mjs` keeps the imported tree intact.

## Starting

Read Cass feedback (`cass search ... --robot`), `git status`, the ledger tail, the newest round log and
the machine's journal, and inspect any interrupted run before resuming. Then follow the
[protocol](program.md), one bounded experiment at a time. An agent session drives the research;
`run.py` is not a scheduler.

title: Rendering milestone and build milestone 2: headers, deploy-next, fan-out
description:
## Goal
Make the port a release candidate: its own Vite build fills `deploy-next/` with this repository's identity under real production headers, with integrity checks and static fallback, and one canonical artifact is built once and its exact bytes fanned out to every platform lane. Threaded WASM and cross-origin isolation behave differently without the real headers, so tests must run under them; exact-artifact identity across lanes also saves hosted minutes (the separate iOS product rebuild is a cost and identity limitation, not an invariant). Merging this bead completes the rendering port and workspace build milestone 2, and its merge commit is the TS/React milestone that every UI workstream waits for (face controls, acquisition consent, device check, static-names picker, diagnostics disclosure, provider Help copy), that `crop.ported-app` and `compute.ported-app` need for the built-UI acceptance of the extraction, crop and media chain, and that parity runs against.

## Scope
- Until now `deploy-next/` is populated from the pinned control artifact (labelled control, classic identity) via the root `build:next` wrapper from candidate import. Switch `build:next` to the Vite build; `deploy-next/` records this repository's source commit/build identity plus import provenance and never presents the classic commit as its deploy source.
- Header configuration as one source of truth consumed by the local test/preview server and deploy staging (shared with deploy re-homing). Match classic sources: `src/Next/browser/serve-local.py` and `hosting/next-static/wrangler.jsonc`/`worker.mjs` (entry Worker): COOP/COEP/CORP/CORS, MIME and cache headers. Verify with the test server, not a plain static server.

- Retained consumers (exact-artifact harness, research drivers, deploy re-homing) keep working against the new `deploy-next/`.

- First destination run of the repaired `scripts/check-next-artifact.sh` (from `provider.webgl`): label `destination`, route set exactly `{auto,cpu,webgpu}`, JSON result including `providerLocation` kept as a CI artifact.
- Fan-out: one build job produces the canonical artifact with identity; site, e2e, matrix, Android, iOS component and iOS product lanes download and verify the same digest (shared download-and-verify step) instead of rebuilding. Cache immutable runtime/model assets by a key derived from the runtime-mirror manifest digest and dependency caches by the lockfile hash (never branch or date); cancel superseded test builds; keep preview-deploy serialisation and qualified-artifact checks.
- Changed emitted runtime bytes require updated matching pins, never reuse of an unrelated digest.

## Out of scope
- Publishing and domain/promotion changes (deploy, delivery). Changing which checks run. Declared UX changes; the parity run.

title: CI: delete low-value gates, fix change base, unblock lanes; get main green
description:
Operator direction (27 Oct): CI slows the swarm needlessly; relax or remove gates that cost time without catching real defects, and make the rest reliable.

Evidence (last 100 main runs): no green since 40155218347 (25 Oct). 82 superseded, 16 failed. About 18 of ~50 job failures were infrastructure; about 18 were hash/golden/tracker gates; few were real.

Do, in order:
1. Delete the import-closure frozen per-file hash check (import-closure.yml, verify-closure.mjs). Move the network "real download" test in control.test.mjs to nightly or delete it. It caused 9 of 16 failures; exact-hash parity was already abandoned.
2. Delete the next-site "Destination parity smoke" DOM-golden step (next-site.yml ~193). It fails on intended UI changes while the Playwright flows pass.
3. Make `changes` diff against the previous main run's head, not the last green (03305f9 is 447 commits back, so every lane runs).
4. Split next-site into artifact and qualify; web-shell, mobile-browser and next-deploy need only artifact (main.yml ~290/352/427).
5. Move beads-check (closed-while-blocked) out of main CI into a br/pre-push guard.
6. Move mobile ios/android simulators, model-conv "Documented commands, verbatim", name-catalogue/publish and beads-site/publish off the push path (post-merge or nightly, or path-filtered after step 3).
7. Drop triton from linux-x64 or fix its setup-workspace (up to 334 s per job, versus 1 s on eris/tempcpu). Give next-site/artifact a reserved label.
Keep next-site/qualify/real-ui-cpu: it is catching a real fm-qrfz regression (faces render at 416 px and don't fill the tile; IndexError). That is fixed in the product, not here.
Done when main is green with these removals and the critical path is under 15 min.
